summary.en: Dnyaneshwar opens with invocations to Ganesha, Sharada and his guru Nivruttinath, and praises the Gita as the essence of the Vedas. He then describes the two armies assembled at Kurukshetra and Arjuna's growing despondency as he sees his kinsmen, teachers and friends arrayed for battle, until he sets down his bow in grief.
summary.hi: ज्ञानेश्वर गणेश, शारदा और अपने गुरु निवृत्तिनाथ की वंदना से आरंभ करते हैं और गीता को वेदों का सार बताकर उसकी स्तुति करते हैं। फिर वे कुरुक्षेत्र में खड़ी दोनों सेनाओं का वर्णन करते हैं और यह कि अपने स्वजनों, गुरुओं और मित्रों को युद्ध के लिए खड़ा देखकर अर्जुन कैसे शोक से भर जाता है और धनुष रख देता है।

summary.en: Krishna rebukes Arjuna's faint-heartedness and teaches that the Self is eternal and cannot be slain, while bodies come and go. He urges Arjuna to his duty as a warrior, introduces the yoga of equanimous action without attachment to its fruits, and closes with a portrait of the sthitaprajna, the person of steady wisdom.
summary.hi: कृष्ण अर्जुन की कायरता को फटकारते हैं और सिखाते हैं कि आत्मा नित्य और अवध्य है, केवल शरीर आते-जाते हैं। वे अर्जुन को क्षत्रिय धर्म की याद दिलाते हैं, फल की आसक्ति के बिना समबुद्धि से कर्म करने का योग बताते हैं और अंत में स्थितप्रज्ञ का वर्णन करते हैं।

summary.en: Arjuna asks why he should act at all if knowledge is higher than action. Krishna explains that no embodied being can escape action, that work done as an offering (yajna) does not bind, and that the wise must act to set an example for the world. He identifies desire and anger as the real enemies that cloud knowledge.
summary.hi: अर्जुन पूछता है कि यदि ज्ञान कर्म से श्रेष्ठ है तो उसे कर्म क्यों करना चाहिए। कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि कोई भी देहधारी कर्म से बच नहीं सकता, यज्ञ-भाव से किया गया कर्म बाँधता नहीं, और ज्ञानी को लोकसंग्रह के लिए कर्म करना चाहिए। वे काम और क्रोध को ज्ञान को ढकने वाले असली शत्रु बताते हैं।

summary.en: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this yoga and the purpose of his repeated incarnations to protect dharma. He explains how to see inaction in action, describes the many forms of sacrifice, and declares the sacrifice of knowledge supreme, to be gained through humility, inquiry and service to the guru.
summary.hi: कृष्ण इस योग की प्राचीन परंपरा और धर्म की रक्षा के लिए अपने बार-बार अवतार लेने का उद्देश्य प्रकट करते हैं। वे कर्म में अकर्म देखने की दृष्टि समझाते हैं, अनेक प्रकार के यज्ञों का वर्णन करते हैं और ज्ञानयज्ञ को सर्वश्रेष्ठ बताते हैं, जो नम्रता, जिज्ञासा और गुरु-सेवा से प्राप्त होता है।

summary.en: Krishna shows that renunciation and the yoga of action lead to the same goal, and that acting without attachment is the easier path. The one who acts while dedicating everything to Brahman remains untouched, like a lotus leaf in water, sees all beings with an equal eye, and attains the bliss of Brahman within.
summary.hi: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि संन्यास और कर्मयोग एक ही लक्ष्य तक ले जाते हैं, और अनासक्त कर्म अधिक सरल मार्ग है। जो सब कुछ ब्रह्म को अर्पित करके कर्म करता है, वह जल में कमल-पत्र की तरह अलिप्त रहता है, सब प्राणियों को समदृष्टि से देखता है और भीतर ब्रह्मानंद पाता है।

summary.en: Dnyaneshwar begins with his celebrated praise of Marathi, promising words sweeter than nectar. Krishna then teaches the yoga of meditation: the seat, posture and breath, the awakening of the Kundalini, and the stilling of the mind through practice and dispassion. He assures Arjuna that no seeker who strays midway is ever lost.
summary.hi: ज्ञानेश्वर मराठी भाषा की अपनी प्रसिद्ध प्रशंसा से आरंभ करते हैं और अमृत से भी मधुर शब्दों का वचन देते हैं। फिर कृष्ण ध्यानयोग सिखाते हैं: आसन, मुद्रा और प्राण, कुंडलिनी का जागरण, और अभ्यास तथा वैराग्य से मन को स्थिर करना। वे अर्जुन को आश्वस्त करते हैं कि मार्ग में भटका साधक कभी नष्ट नहीं होता।

summary.en: Krishna describes his lower nature of eight elements and his higher nature as the life of all beings, and explains how the world is deluded by Maya woven of the three gunas. He names four kinds of devotees and declares the one with knowledge the dearest, since he has become one with the Lord.
summary.hi: कृष्ण अपनी आठ तत्त्वों वाली अपरा प्रकृति और सब प्राणियों के जीवनरूप परा प्रकृति का वर्णन करते हैं, और समझाते हैं कि त्रिगुणमयी माया से संसार कैसे मोहित होता है। वे चार प्रकार के भक्त बताते हैं और ज्ञानी भक्त को सबसे प्रिय कहते हैं, क्योंकि वह भगवान से एकरूप हो गया है।

summary.en: Arjuna asks about Brahman, the Self, action and the ruling principles. Krishna explains that whatever one remembers at death, that one becomes, so the mind must be fixed on him always. He describes the imperishable Supreme, the cycles of creation, and the two paths by which departing souls either return or are freed.
summary.hi: अर्जुन ब्रह्म, अध्यात्म, कर्म और अधिभूत-अधिदैव के विषय में पूछता है। कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि मृत्यु के समय जिसका स्मरण होता है, मनुष्य वही बन जाता है, इसलिए मन को सदा उन्हीं में लगाना चाहिए। वे अविनाशी परमात्मा, सृष्टि के चक्र और उन दो मार्गों का वर्णन करते हैं जिनसे जीव लौटता है या मुक्त होता है।

summary.en: Krishna reveals the sovereign knowledge and sovereign secret: all beings rest in him, yet he is not contained in them. He declares that devotion is open to everyone, whatever their birth, and that he gladly accepts even a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water offered with love.
summary.hi: कृष्ण राजविद्या और राजगुह्य प्रकट करते हैं: सब प्राणी उनमें स्थित हैं, फिर भी वे उनमें सीमित नहीं हैं। वे घोषणा करते हैं कि भक्ति सबके लिए खुली है, चाहे जन्म कोई भी हो, और प्रेम से अर्पित एक पत्ता, फूल, फल या थोड़ा-सा जल भी वे प्रसन्नता से स्वीकार करते हैं।

summary.en: After a salutation to his guru, Dnyaneshwar presents Krishna's account of his divine glories. Krishna declares himself the source of all, and at Arjuna's request names his chief manifestations among gods, sages, rivers, mountains and all beings, concluding that the whole universe is supported by a mere fraction of him.
summary.hi: गुरु-वंदना के बाद ज्ञानेश्वर कृष्ण की दिव्य विभूतियों का वर्णन प्रस्तुत करते हैं। कृष्ण स्वयं को सबका मूल बताते हैं और अर्जुन के अनुरोध पर देवताओं, ऋषियों, नदियों, पर्वतों और सब प्राणियों में अपनी प्रमुख विभूतियाँ गिनाते हैं, और अंत में कहते हैं कि पूरा विश्व उनके एक अंश मात्र से टिका है।

summary.en: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's cosmic form, and Krishna grants him divine sight. Arjuna beholds the whole universe within the Lord, blazing with countless faces and swallowing the warriors of both armies. Overwhelmed with awe and fear, he begs forgiveness and asks Krishna to resume his gentle, familiar form.
summary.hi: अर्जुन कृष्ण का विश्वरूप देखने की इच्छा करता है और कृष्ण उसे दिव्य दृष्टि देते हैं। अर्जुन भगवान में समस्त ब्रह्मांड को देखता है, जो असंख्य मुखों से दहकता हुआ दोनों सेनाओं के योद्धाओं को निगल रहा है। विस्मय और भय से अभिभूत होकर वह क्षमा माँगता है और कृष्ण से उनका सौम्य, परिचित रूप धारण करने की प्रार्थना करता है।

summary.en: Arjuna asks whether devotion to the manifest Lord or to the unmanifest Absolute is better. Krishna praises devotion to his personal form as the easier path, offers a ladder of practices for those who find it hard, and describes in loving detail the qualities of the devotee who is dear to him.
summary.hi: अर्जुन पूछता है कि सगुण भगवान की भक्ति श्रेष्ठ है या निर्गुण ब्रह्म की उपासना। कृष्ण सगुण भक्ति को अधिक सरल मार्ग बताकर उसकी प्रशंसा करते हैं, कठिनाई अनुभव करने वालों के लिए साधनों की एक सीढ़ी देते हैं, और अपने प्रिय भक्त के गुणों का प्रेमपूर्वक विस्तार से वर्णन करते हैं।

summary.en: Krishna distinguishes the field (the body and nature) from the knower of the field (the Self). Dnyaneshwar expands at great length on the marks of true knowledge, such as humility, non-violence and steadfastness, and on their opposites, before explaining Prakriti and Purusha and the vision of the one Self in all.
summary.hi: कृष्ण क्षेत्र (शरीर और प्रकृति) और क्षेत्रज्ञ (आत्मा) का भेद बताते हैं। ज्ञानेश्वर अमानित्व, अहिंसा, स्थिरता जैसे सच्चे ज्ञान के लक्षणों और उनके विपरीत लक्षणों का बहुत विस्तार से वर्णन करते हैं, और फिर प्रकृति-पुरुष तथा सबमें एक ही आत्मा देखने की दृष्टि समझाते हैं।

summary.en: Krishna explains the three gunas, sattva, rajas and tamas, how each binds the embodied soul, and the signs by which each can be recognised. He then describes the one who has gone beyond the gunas, unmoved by pleasure and pain, and declares unwavering devotion the way to reach that state.
summary.hi: कृष्ण सत्त्व, रज और तम तीनों गुणों का, वे देहधारी जीव को कैसे बाँधते हैं और उन्हें किन लक्षणों से पहचाना जाता है, इसका वर्णन करते हैं। फिर वे सुख-दुःख से अविचल गुणातीत पुरुष का वर्णन करते हैं और अविचल भक्ति को उस अवस्था तक पहुँचने का मार्ग बताते हैं।

summary.en: Krishna describes worldly existence as an inverted ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below, to be cut down with the axe of detachment. He explains that the individual soul is his own eternal part, and reveals himself as Purushottama, the Supreme Person beyond both the perishable and the imperishable.
summary.hi: कृष्ण संसार को ऊपर जड़ और नीचे शाखाओं वाले उलटे अश्वत्थ वृक्ष के रूप में बताते हैं, जिसे वैराग्य की कुल्हाड़ी से काटना है। वे समझाते हैं कि जीव उनका ही सनातन अंश है, और स्वयं को क्षर और अक्षर दोनों से परे पुरुषोत्तम के रूप में प्रकट करते हैं।

summary.en: Krishna lists the divine qualities, such as fearlessness, purity, charity and compassion, that lead to liberation, and the demonic qualities, such as arrogance, anger and harshness, that lead to bondage. He describes how the demonic mind is driven by endless desire, and names lust, anger and greed as the three gates to hell.
summary.hi: कृष्ण अभय, शुद्धि, दान, दया जैसी दैवी संपदा बताते हैं जो मुक्ति की ओर ले जाती है, और दंभ, क्रोध, कठोरता जैसी आसुरी संपदा जो बंधन की ओर ले जाती है। वे बताते हैं कि आसुरी मन अंतहीन कामना से कैसे चलता है, और काम, क्रोध और लोभ को नरक के तीन द्वार कहते हैं।

summary.en: Krishna explains that faith takes three forms according to the gunas, and that the same threefold division applies to food, sacrifice, austerity and charity. He closes by explaining the sacred formula Om Tat Sat, which sanctifies every act done in the right spirit.
summary.hi: कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि गुणों के अनुसार श्रद्धा तीन प्रकार की होती है, और यही त्रिविध विभाजन आहार, यज्ञ, तप और दान पर भी लागू होता है। अंत में वे ॐ तत्सत् का अर्थ समझाते हैं, जो सही भाव से किए गए हर कर्म को पवित्र करता है।

summary.en: The final chapter draws together the whole teaching: the true meaning of renunciation and relinquishment, the threefold division of knowledge, action and doer, and the duties that arise from one's nature. Krishna gives his supreme counsel of complete surrender, Arjuna declares his delusion gone, and Dnyaneshwar closes the work with the Pasayadan, his prayer for the good of the whole world.
summary.hi: अंतिम अध्याय पूरी शिक्षा को समेटता है: संन्यास और त्याग का सच्चा अर्थ, ज्ञान, कर्म और कर्ता का त्रिविध विभाजन, और स्वभाव से उत्पन्न कर्तव्य। कृष्ण पूर्ण शरणागति का परम उपदेश देते हैं, अर्जुन कहता है कि उसका मोह नष्ट हो गया, और ज्ञानेश्वर संपूर्ण विश्व के कल्याण की प्रार्थना पसायदान के साथ ग्रंथ पूर्ण करते हैं।

verses.shloka_devanagari: श्रीगणेशाय नस: 3७ नमोजी आद्या । वेदप्रतिपाद्या। जय जय स्वसंवेद्या । आत्मरूपा ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: śrīgaṇeśāya nasa: 37 namojī ādyā | vedapratipādyā| jaya jaya svasaṃvedyā | ātmarūpā || 1||
verses.meaning: Salutations to the Primordial One, the essence of the Vedas, the self-evident, the very form of the Self, victory, victory!

verses.shloka_devanagari: देवा तूंचि गणेशु। सकलार्थमतिप्रकाशु। म्हणे निवृत्तिदासु| अबधारिजो जी॥२॥
verses.shloka_iast: devā tūṃci gaṇeśu| sakalārthamatiprakāśu| mhaṇe nivṛttidāsu| abadhārijo jī||2||
verses.meaning: O Lord, You are indeed Ganesha, the illuminator of all understanding. Nivruttidas says, please listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें शब्दब्रह्म अशेष। तेचि मूर्ति सुवेष। जेथ वर्णवपु निर्दोष। मिरवत असे॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ śabdabrahma aśeṣa| teci mūrti suveṣa| jetha varṇavapu nirdoṣa| miravata ase|| 3||
verses.meaning: This entire Shabda-Brahma (the Absolute as sound/word) is indeed a beautiful form, where the flawless body of letters shines forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्मृति तेचि अवयव। देखा आंगीक भाव। तेथ लावण्याची ठेव। अर्थशोभा॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: smṛti teci avayava| dekhā āṃgīka bhāva| tetha lāvaṇyācī ṭheva| arthaśobhā|| 4||
verses.meaning: Memory itself is like a limb, a part of the body, where the treasure of beauty and the splendor of meaning reside.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अष्टादश पुराणें । तींचि मणिभूषणें । 'पदपब्धति खेवणें । प्रमेयरत्नांचीं ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aṣṭādaśa purāṇeṃ | tīṃci maṇibhūṣaṇeṃ | 'padapabdhati khevaṇeṃ | prameyaratnāṃcīṃ || 5||
verses.meaning: The eighteen Puranas are indeed like jeweled ornaments, stringing together the gems of profound truths into a beautiful necklace of words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पदबंध नागर। तेंचि रंगाथिलें अंबर । जेथ साहित्य वाणें सपूर। उजाळाचें ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: padabaṃdha nāgara| teṃci raṃgāthileṃ aṃbara | jetha sāhitya vāṇeṃ sapūra| ujāḻāceṃ || 6||
verses.meaning: The arrangement of words is like a beautifully dyed cloth, where the literary embellishments shine with a complete and radiant splendor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखा काव्यनाटका । जे निर्धारितां सकौतुका । त्याचि रुणझुणती क्षुद्रघंटिका । अर्थध्वनि ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhā kāvyanāṭakā | je nirdhāritāṃ sakautukā | tyāci ruṇajhuṇatī kṣudraghaṃṭikā | arthadhvani || 7||
verses.meaning: Just as in a delightful play or poem, the tiny bells of meaning jingle with their subtle sounds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना प्रमेयांची परी । निपुणपणें पाहतां कुसरी । दिसती उचित पदें माझारीं । रत्ने भलीं ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā prameyāṃcī parī | nipuṇapaṇeṃ pāhatāṃ kusarī | disatī ucita padeṃ mājhārīṃ | ratne bhalīṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: When one skillfully examines the various profound truths, one finds appropriate words within them, like excellent jewels.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ व्यासादिकांच्या मती । तेचि मेखळा मिरवती । चोखाळपणें झळकती । 'पल्लवसडका ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha vyāsādikāṃcyā matī | teci mekhaḻā miravatī | cokhāḻapaṇeṃ jhaḻakatī | 'pallavasaḍakā || 9||
verses.meaning: There, the intellects of sages like Vyasa shine forth as a girdle, gleaming with their purity, like a path adorned with fresh sprouts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखा षड्दर्शनें म्हणिपती। तेचि भुजांची आकृति। म्हणौनि विसंवादें धरिती। आयुधें हातीं ॥ १०॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhā ṣaḍdarśaneṃ mhaṇipatī| teci bhujāṃcī ākṛti| mhaṇauni visaṃvādeṃ dharitī| āyudheṃ hātīṃ || 10||
verses.meaning: Behold, what are called the six systems of philosophy (Shaddarshanas) are like arms. Therefore, they hold weapons of disagreement in their hands.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तर्क तोचि फरशु। नीतिभेदु अंकुशु । वेदान्तु तो महारसु। मोदकु मिरवे॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tarka toci pharaśu| nītibhedu aṃkuśu | vedāntu to mahārasu| modaku mirave|| 11||
verses.meaning: Thus, logic is the axe, ethical discernment the goad, and Vedanta the great elixir, shining forth as a sweet delight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एके हातीं दंतु। जो स्वभावता खंडितु। तो बौद्धमतसंकेतु। वार्तिकांचा॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: eke hātīṃ daṃtu| jo svabhāvatā khaṃḍitu| to bauddhamatasaṃketu| vārtikāṃcā|| 92||
verses.meaning: In one hand, the tusk, which is naturally broken, is a symbol of Buddhist philosophy, according to the Vartikas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सहजें सत्कारवादु। तो पदाकरु वरदु । धर्मप्रतिष्ठा तो सिद्धु। अभयहस्तु॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sahajeṃ satkāravādu| to padākaru varadu | dharmapratiṣṭhā to siddhu| abhayahastu|| 13||
verses.meaning: Then naturally, the doctrine of existence, that giver of boons, the establisher of righteousness, is a hand bestowing fearlessness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखा विवेकवंतु सुविमळु। तोचि शुंडादंडु सरळु। जेथ परमानंदु केवळु । महासुखाचा॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhā vivekavaṃtu suvimaḻu| toci śuṃḍādaṃḍu saraḻu| jetha paramānaṃdu kevaḻu | mahāsukhācā|| 14||
verses.meaning: Behold, the discerning one, pure and clear, is like a straight trunk, from which springs the pure supreme bliss, of great joy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी संबादु तोचि दशनु। जो समता शुभ्रवर्णु। देवो उन्मेषसूक्ष्मेक्षणु। विघ्नराजु॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī saṃbādu toci daśanu| jo samatā śubhravarṇu| devo unmeṣasūkṣmekṣaṇu| vighnarāju|| 15||
verses.meaning: Therefore, that very dialogue is the tusk, which is of the pure white color of equanimity. The deity, Ganesha, with his subtle vision, is the king of obstacles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मज अवगमलिया दोनी । मीमांसा श्रवणस्थानीं । बोधमदामृत मुनी-। अली सेविती ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: maja avagamaliyā donī | mīmāṃsā śravaṇasthānīṃ | bodhamadāmṛta munī-| alī sevitī || 16||
verses.meaning: When I understood the two Mimamsas, the sages, like bees, partook of the nectar of enlightened bliss through listening.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रमेयप्रवाल सुप्रभ । ह्वैता द्वैत तेचि निकुंभ । सरिसेपणें एकवटत इभ-। मस्तकावरी ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: prameyapravāla suprabha | hvaitā dvaita teci nikuṃbha | sarisepaṇeṃ ekavaṭata ibha-| mastakāvarī || 17||
verses.meaning: The coral of the प्रमेय (that which is to be proven) shines brightly. The dualities of duality and non-duality, like two elephants, become one and stand united upon the head of the elephant of ultimate truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उपरि दशोपनिषदें । जियें उदारें ज्ञानमकरंदें। तियें कुसुमें मुगुटीं सुगंधें। शोभती भलीं ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: upari daśopaniṣadeṃ | jiyeṃ udāreṃ jñānamakaraṃdeṃ| tiyeṃ kusumeṃ muguṭīṃ sugaṃdheṃ| śobhatī bhalīṃ || 18||
verses.meaning: Above all, the ten Upanishads, which are generous with the nectar of knowledge, those flowers, as a crown, with their fragrance, shine beautifully.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अकार चरणयुगुल। उकार उदर विशाल। मकार महामंडल। मस्तकाकारें॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: akāra caraṇayugula| ukāra udara viśāla| makāra mahāmaṃḍala| mastakākāreṃ|| 19||
verses.meaning: The letter 'A' represents the two feet, 'U' the vast belly, and 'M' the great cosmic sphere, forming the head.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे तिन्ही एकवटळे। तेथ शब्दब्रह्म कवळलें। तें मियां श्रीगुरुकृपा नमिलें। आदिबीज॥ २०॥
verses.shloka_iast: he tinhī ekavaṭaḻe| tetha śabdabrahma kavaḻaleṃ| teṃ miyāṃ śrīgurukṛpā namileṃ| ādibīja|| 20||
verses.meaning: When these three unite, the sound-Brahman is embraced. I bow to that primal seed through the grace of my Guru.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अभिनव वाग्बिलासिनी। जे चातुर्यार्थकलाकामिनी। ते शारदा विश्‍्वमोहिनी । नमिली मियां॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ abhinava vāgbilāsinī| je cāturyārthakalākāminī| te śāradā viś‍vamohinī | namilī miyāṃ|| 29||
verses.meaning: Now, the innovative goddess of speech, the enchanting muse of wisdom and art, that world-bewitching Sharada, I have bowed to her.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मज हृदयीं सद्गुरु । जेणें तारिळों हा संसारपूरु । म्हणौनि वबिशेषें अत्यादरु । वबिवेकावरी ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maja hṛdayīṃ sadguru | jeṇeṃ tāriḻoṃ hā saṃsārapūru | mhaṇauni vabiśeṣeṃ atyādaru | vabivekāvarī || 22||
verses.meaning: My Guru resides in my heart, by whom I was carried across this flood of worldly existence. Therefore, I hold a special reverence for discrimination.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें डोळ्यां अंजन भेटे। ते वेळीं दृष्टीसी फांटा फुटे । मग वास पाहिजे तेथ प्रगटे। महानिधी॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ ḍoḻyāṃ aṃjana bheṭe| te veḻīṃ dṛṣṭīsī phāṃṭā phuṭe | maga vāsa pāhije tetha pragaṭe| mahānidhī|| 23||
verses.meaning: Just as when collyrium is applied to the eyes, the vision expands, and then wherever one looks, a great treasure is revealed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां चिंतामणि जालिया हातीं। सदा विजयवृत्ति मनोरथीं। तैसा मी पूर्णकाम श्रीनिवृत्ती। ज्ञानदेवो म्हणे ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ ciṃtāmaṇi jāliyā hātīṃ| sadā vijayavṛtti manorathīṃ| taisā mī pūrṇakāma śrīnivṛttī| jñānadevo mhaṇe || 24||
verses.meaning: Just as one who holds the Chintamani jewel always achieves their heart's desires, so too am I, Dnyandev, made complete in my aspirations by the grace of Shri Nivritti.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जाणतेनें गुरु भजिजे। तेणें कृतकार्य होईजे। जैसें मूळसिंचनें सहजें। शाखापल्लब संतोषती॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jāṇateneṃ guru bhajije| teṇeṃ kṛtakārya hoīje| jaiseṃ mūḻasiṃcaneṃ sahajeṃ| śākhāpallaba saṃtoṣatī|| 25||
verses.meaning: Therefore, a wise person should worship the Guru. By doing so, one achieves all their objectives, just as watering the root naturally satisfies the branches and leaves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां तीर्थे जियें त्रिभुवनी । तियें घडती समुद्रावगाहनीं। ना तरी अमृतरसास्वादनीं । रस सकळ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ tīrthe jiyeṃ tribhuvanī | tiyeṃ ghaḍatī samudrāvagāhanīṃ| nā tarī amṛtarasāsvādanīṃ | rasa sakaḻa|| 26||
verses.meaning: Or, all the holy places in the three worlds are attained by bathing in the ocean, or by tasting the nectar, all tastes are experienced.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा पुढतपुढती तोचि । मियां अभिवंदिला श्रीगुरुचि। जो अभिलषित मनोरुचि। पुरविता तो॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā puḍhatapuḍhatī toci | miyāṃ abhivaṃdilā śrīguruci| jo abhilaṣita manoruci| puravitā to|| 27||
verses.meaning: Again and again, I bow to that very Shri Guru, who fulfills all desired aspirations of the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अवधारा कथा गहन। जे सकळां कौतुकां जन्मस्थान । कौं अभिनव उद्यान । विवेकतरूचें ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ avadhārā kathā gahana| je sakaḻāṃ kautukāṃ janmasthāna | kauṃ abhinava udyāna | vivekatarūceṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Now, listen to this profound narrative, which is the birthplace of all wonders, like a new garden for the tree of discrimination.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी सर्व सुखाचि आदि । जे प्रमेयमहानिधि। नाना नवरससुधाब्धि । परिपूर्ण हे॥२९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī sarva sukhāci ādi | je prameyamahānidhi| nānā navarasasudhābdhi | paripūrṇa he||29||
verses.meaning: Or rather, it is the origin of all happiness, a great treasure of knowledge, or an ocean overflowing with the nectar of the nine rasas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं परमधाम प्रकट । सर्व विद्यांचें मूळपीठ । शास्त्रजाता बसौट । अशेषांचें॥३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ paramadhāma prakaṭa | sarva vidyāṃceṃ mūḻapīṭha | śāstrajātā basauṭa | aśeṣāṃceṃ||30||
verses.meaning: Or, it is the manifest supreme abode, the fundamental source of all knowledge, the very foundation of all scriptures, and the essence of everything.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी सकळ धर्माचें माहेर। सज्जनांचें जिव्हार। 'लावण्यरत्नभांडार। शारदेचें ॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī sakaḻa dharmāceṃ māhera| sajjanāṃceṃ jivhāra| 'lāvaṇyaratnabhāṃḍāra| śāradeceṃ || 31||
verses.meaning: Indeed, it is the birthplace of all righteousness, the very heart of the virtuous, a treasure trove of beauty, belonging to the Goddess Sharada.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना कथारूपें भारती । प्रकटली असे त्रिजगतीं । आविष्करोनि महामतीं। व्यासाचिये ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā kathārūpeṃ bhāratī | prakaṭalī ase trijagatīṃ | āviṣkaroni mahāmatīṃ| vyāsāciye || 32||
verses.meaning: The Mahabharata, in its various narratives, has manifested throughout the three worlds, brought forth by the great intellect of Vyasa.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि हा काव्यां- रावो । ग्रंथ गुरुवतीचा ठावो । एथूनि रसां झाला आवो । रसाळपणाचा॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni hā kāvyāṃ- rāvo | graṃtha guruvatīcā ṭhāvo | ethūni rasāṃ jhālā āvo | rasāḻapaṇācā|| 33||
verses.meaning: Therefore, this king of poetry, this scripture, is the abode of profound wisdom. From it, all sentiments have received their essence, their very sweetness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि आइका आणिक एक। एथूनि शब्दश्री सच्छास्त्रिक। आणि महाबोधीं कोंबळीक। दुणावली॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci āikā āṇika eka| ethūni śabdaśrī sacchāstrika| āṇi mahābodhīṃ koṃbaḻīka| duṇāvalī|| 34||
verses.meaning: Listen further to this one thing: from here, the glory of words, rooted in true scriptures, and the tenderness of great enlightenment, have doubled.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ चातुर्य शहाणें झालें। प्रमेय रुचीस आलें। आणि सौभाग्य पोखलें। सुखाचे एथ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha cāturya śahāṇeṃ jhāleṃ| prameya rucīsa āleṃ| āṇi saubhāgya pokhaleṃ| sukhāce etha|| 35||
verses.meaning: Here, cleverness becomes wise, the profound truth becomes palatable, and good fortune flourishes in happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: माधुर्यी मधुरता । श्रृंगारीं सुरेखता । रूढपण उचितां । दिसे भलें॥ ३६ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mādhuryī madhuratā | śrṛṃgārīṃ surekhatā | rūḍhapaṇa ucitāṃ | dise bhaleṃ|| 36 ||
verses.meaning: In sweetness, there is charm; in romance, beauty. Appropriateness, when established, appears good.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ कळाविदपण कळा। पुण्यासि प्रतापु आगळा । म्हणौनि जनमेजयाचे अवलीळा। दोष हरले॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha kaḻāvidapaṇa kaḻā| puṇyāsi pratāpu āgaḻā | mhaṇauni janamejayāce avalīḻā| doṣa harale|| 37||
verses.meaning: Here, the artistry of the narrative, coupled with the immense merit of the Punya (virtuous deeds), effortlessly removed the sins of Janamejaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पाहतां नावेक । रंगीं सुरंगतेची आगळीक । गुणां सगुणपणाचें बिक। बहुवस एथ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pāhatāṃ nāveka | raṃgīṃ suraṃgatecī āgaḻīka | guṇāṃ saguṇapaṇāceṃ bika| bahuvasa etha|| 38||
verses.meaning: And when one looks, the boat of devotion, in its colors, possesses an extraordinary beauty. The virtues here are abundant, giving substance to all good qualities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भानुचेनि तेजें धवळलें। जेसें त्रैलोक्य दिसे उजळलें। तैसें व्यासमति कवळलें। मिरवे विश्‍व ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhānuceni tejeṃ dhavaḻaleṃ| jeseṃ trailokya dise ujaḻaleṃ| taiseṃ vyāsamati kavaḻaleṃ| mirave viś‍va || 39||
verses.meaning: Just as the three worlds appear illuminated by the sun's radiance, so too does the universe shine, enveloped by the intellect of Vyasa.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां सुक्षेत्री बीज घातलें। तें आपुलियापरी विस्तारळें। तैसें भारतीं सुरवाडलें। अर्थजात॥ ४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ sukṣetrī bīja ghātaleṃ| teṃ āpuliyāparī vistāraḻeṃ| taiseṃ bhāratīṃ suravāḍaleṃ| arthajāta|| 40||
verses.meaning: Just as a seed sown in fertile ground expands according to its nature, so too do the meanings of the Vedas flourish in the Bharata (India).

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी नगरांतरीं वसिजे। तरी नागराचि होईजे। तेसें व्यासोक्तितेजें। धबळत सकळ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī nagarāṃtarīṃ vasije| tarī nāgarāci hoīje| teseṃ vyāsoktitejeṃ| dhabaḻata sakaḻa|| 49||
verses.meaning: Or, if one resides in a city, one becomes a citizen. Similarly, the entire world is illuminated by the brilliance of Vyasa's words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं प्रथम बयसाकाळीं । लावण्याची नव्हाळी । प्रगटे जैसी आगळी । अंगनाअंगीं ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ prathama bayasākāḻīṃ | lāvaṇyācī navhāḻī | pragaṭe jaisī āgaḻī | aṃganāaṃgīṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: Just as in the prime of youth, a woman's body blossoms with an extraordinary and fresh beauty.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी उद्यानीं माधवी घडे । तेथ वनशोभेची खाणी उघडे । आदिलापासौनि अपाडें। जियापरी ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī udyānīṃ mādhavī ghaḍe | tetha vanaśobhecī khāṇī ughaḍe | ādilāpāsauni apāḍeṃ| jiyāparī || 43||
verses.meaning: Or, when the spring season arrives in the garden, it unveils a mine of forest beauty, just as it has been from the very beginning, immeasurably so.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नानाघनीभूत सुवर्ण । जैसें न्याहाळितां साधारण । मग अलंकारीं बरवेपण । निवाडु दावी॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānāghanībhūta suvarṇa | jaiseṃ nyāhāḻitāṃ sādhāraṇa | maga alaṃkārīṃ baravepaṇa | nivāḍu dāvī|| 44||
verses.meaning: Just as gold, when examined, appears ordinary in its raw, solidified state, but then reveals its true beauty and distinction when crafted into ornaments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें व्यासोक्‍्ति अळंकारिलें। आवडे तें बरवेपण पातलें। तें जाणोनि काय आश्रयिलें। इतिहासीं ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ vyāsok‍ti aḻaṃkārileṃ| āvaḍe teṃ baravepaṇa pātaleṃ| teṃ jāṇoni kāya āśrayileṃ| itihāsīṃ || 45||
verses.meaning: Just as Vyasa's words are adorned, they attain beauty. Knowing this, what is it that history has taken refuge in?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना पुरतिये प्रतिष्ठेलागीं । सानीव धरूनि आंगीं। पुराणें आख्यानरूपें जगीं। भारता आलीं॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā puratiye pratiṣṭhelāgīṃ | sānīva dharūni āṃgīṃ| purāṇeṃ ākhyānarūpeṃ jagīṃ| bhāratā ālīṃ|| 46||
verses.meaning: To establish the many different paths of devotion, the ancient scriptures, in the form of narratives, came into the world through the Mahabharata.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि महाभारतीं नाहीं।॥ तें नोहेचि लोकीं तिहीं। येणें कारणें म्हणिपे पाहीं । व्यासोच्छिष्ट जगत्रय ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni mahābhāratīṃ nāhīṃ||| teṃ noheci lokīṃ tihīṃ| yeṇeṃ kāraṇeṃ mhaṇipe pāhīṃ | vyāsocchiṣṭa jagatraya || 47||
verses.meaning: Therefore, whatever is not found in the Mahabharata does not exist in any of the three worlds. For this reason, it is said that the three worlds are but the leavings of Vyasa's wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी जगीं सुरस कथा । जें जन्मभूमि परमार्था । मुनि सांगे नृपनाथा । जनमेजया ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī jagīṃ surasa kathā | jeṃ janmabhūmi paramārthā | muni sāṃge nṛpanāthā | janamejayā || 48||
verses.meaning: Thus, a delightful story in this world, which is the birthplace of the highest truth, was narrated by the sage to the king, Janamejaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें अद्वितीय उत्तम। पवित्रेक निरुपम। परम मंगलधाम। अवधारिजो॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ advitīya uttama| pavitreka nirupama| parama maṃgaladhāma| avadhārijo|| 49||
verses.meaning: That which is uniquely supreme, incomparably pure, the abode of ultimate auspiciousness, please listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां भारतकमळपरागु । गीताख्यु प्रसंगु। जो संवादला श्रीरंगु। अर्जूनेंसीं ॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ bhāratakamaḻaparāgu | gītākhyu prasaṃgu| jo saṃvādalā śrīraṃgu| arjūneṃsīṃ || 50||
verses.meaning: Now, the pollen of the lotus of Bharat (Mahabharata), which is the discourse named Gita, was spoken by Lord Vishnu to Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी शब्दब्रह्माब्धि। मथियला व्यासबुद्धि। निवडिलें निरवधि। नवनीत हें॥५९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī śabdabrahmābdhi| mathiyalā vyāsabuddhi| nivaḍileṃ niravadhi| navanīta heṃ||591||
verses.meaning: Or, Vyasa's intellect churned the ocean of the Word-Brahman, and from it, this endless butter (essence) was extracted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग ज्ञानाग्निसंपर्के। कडसिलेंनि विवेकें । पद आलें परिपाकें । आमोदासी ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga jñānāgnisaṃparke| kaḍasileṃni vivekeṃ | pada āleṃ paripākeṃ | āmodāsī || 52||
verses.meaning: Then, through the contact with the fire of knowledge, and purified by discrimination, the state of spiritual ripeness attained its fragrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें अपेक्षिजे विरक्‍तीं । सदा अनुभविजे संतीं । सोहंभावें पारंगतीं । रमिजे जेथ ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ apekṣije virak‍tīṃ | sadā anubhavije saṃtīṃ | sohaṃbhāveṃ pāraṃgatīṃ | ramije jetha || 53||
verses.meaning: That which is desired by the detached, always experienced by the saints, and where the perfected ones revel in the 'I am That' consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें आकर्णिजे भक्‍तीं। जें आदिवंद्य त्रिजगतीं । तें भीष्मपर्वी संगती । म्हिणितळी कथा ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ ākarṇije bhak‍tīṃ| jeṃ ādivaṃdya trijagatīṃ | teṃ bhīṣmaparvī saṃgatī | mhiṇitaḻī kathā || 54||
verses.meaning: That which is heard with devotion, that which is revered as the primal being in all three worlds, that is the story told in the Bhishma Parva.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें भगवद्गीता म्हणिजे । जें ब्रहोशांनीं प्रशंसिजे । जें सनकादिकीं सेविजे। आदेरेंसीं ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ bhagavadgītā mhaṇije | jeṃ brahośāṃnīṃ praśaṃsije | jeṃ sanakādikīṃ sevije| ādereṃsīṃ || 55 ||
verses.meaning: That which is called the Bhagavad Gita, that which is praised by Lord Brahma and other deities, that which is revered by Sanaka and other sages with great devotion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें शारदीचिये चंद्रकळे। माजि अमृतकण कोंवळे। ते वेंचिती मनें मवाळें। चकोरतलगें॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ śāradīciye caṃdrakaḻe| māji amṛtakaṇa koṃvaḻe| te veṃcitī maneṃ mavāḻeṃ| cakoratalageṃ|| 56||
verses.meaning: Just as the tender young chakora birds, with their gentle hearts, lovingly gather the drops of nectar from the autumnal moonbeams.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियापरी श्रोतां। अनुभवावी हे कथा । अतिहळुवारपण चित्ता । आणूनियां ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyāparī śrotāṃ| anubhavāvī he kathā | atihaḻuvārapaṇa cittā | āṇūniyāṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O listeners, experience this narrative with a very gentle and receptive mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें शब्देंबीण संबादिजे। इंद्रियां नेणतां भोगिजे। बोलाआधि झोंबिजे। प्रमेयासी ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ śabdeṃbīṇa saṃbādije| iṃdriyāṃ neṇatāṃ bhogije| bolāādhi jhoṃbije| prameyāsī || 58||
verses.meaning: This truth is communicated without words, experienced without the senses, and grasped by the intellect before any utterance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसे भ्रमर परागु नेती। परी कमळदळें नेणती । तैसी परी आहे सेविती । ग्रंथी इये॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaise bhramara parāgu netī| parī kamaḻadaḻeṃ neṇatī | taisī parī āhe sevitī | graṃthī iye|| 59||
verses.meaning: Just as a bee takes pollen without the lotus petals knowing, such is the way of partaking in this scripture.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां आपुला ठावो न सांडितां। आलिंगिजे चंद्रु प्रगटतां । हा अनुरागु भोगितां । कुमुदिनी जाणे ॥ ६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ āpulā ṭhāvo na sāṃḍitāṃ| āliṃgije caṃdru pragaṭatāṃ | hā anurāgu bhogitāṃ | kumudinī jāṇe || 60||
verses.meaning: Or, without leaving its own place, the kumudini (water lily) embraces the moon as it appears. Only the kumudini knows the joy of this love.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि गंभीरपणें । स्थिरावळेनि अंतःकरणें। आधथिला तोचि जाणे। मानूं इये॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni gaṃbhīrapaṇeṃ | sthirāvaḻeni aṃtaḥkaraṇeṃ| ādhathilā toci jāṇe| mānūṃ iye||61||
verses.meaning: Thus, with a profound and stable heart, only one who has meditated deeply knows this truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अहो अर्जुनाचिये पांती। जे परिसणया योग्य होती । तिहीं कृपा करूनि संतीं। अवधान द्यावें॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aho arjunāciye pāṃtī| je parisaṇayā yogya hotī | tihīṃ kṛpā karūni saṃtīṃ| avadhāna dyāveṃ|| 62||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, those who are worthy of hearing this, may those saints mercifully grant their attention.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें सलगी म्यां म्हणितळें। चरणां लागोनी विनविलें। प्रभू सखोल हृदय आपुलें। म्हणौनियां ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ salagī myāṃ mhaṇitaḻeṃ| caraṇāṃ lāgonī vinavileṃ| prabhū sakhola hṛdaya āpuleṃ| mhaṇauniyāṃ || 63 ||
verses.meaning: I have spoken this intimately, entreating at your feet, because, O Lord, your heart is profoundly compassionate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा स्वभावो मायबापांचा । अपत्य बोले जरी बोबडी वाचा । तरी अधिकचि तयाचा । संतोष आथी ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā svabhāvo māyabāpāṃcā | apatya bole jarī bobaḍī vācā | tarī adhikaci tayācā | saṃtoṣa āthī || 64||
verses.meaning: Just as parents, by their very nature, feel even greater joy when their child speaks in broken, lisping words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा तुम्हीं मी अंगिकारिला। सजनीं आपुला म्हणितला। तरी उणें सहजें उपसाहला । प्रार्थू कायी ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā tumhīṃ mī aṃgikārilā| sajanīṃ āpulā mhaṇitalā| tarī uṇeṃ sahajeṃ upasāhalā | prārthū kāyī || 65||
verses.meaning: Just as you have accepted me and called me your own, so too have I naturally endured my shortcomings. What more can I pray for?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी अपराधु तो आणिक आहे। जे मी गीतार्थु कबळूं पाहें । तें अवधारा विनवूं लाहें। म्हणौनियां ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī aparādhu to āṇika āhe| je mī gītārthu kabaḻūṃ pāheṃ | teṃ avadhārā vinavūṃ lāheṃ| mhaṇauniyāṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: But there is another transgression, that I attempt to explain the meaning of the Gita. Therefore, I implore you to listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें अनावर न विचारितां। वायांचि धिंवसा उपनला चित्ता। येऱ्हवीं भानुतेजीं काय खद्योता। शोभा आथी ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ anāvara na vicāritāṃ| vāyāṃci dhiṃvasā upanalā cittā| yeṟhavīṃ bhānutejīṃ kāya khadyotā| śobhā āthī || 67||
verses.meaning: This uncontrollable urge arose in my mind without being asked. Otherwise, what splendor can a firefly possess in the sun's brilliance?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं टिटिभू चांचुवरी । माप सूये सागरीं। मी नेणतु त्यापरी । प्रवर्ते येथ ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ ṭiṭibhū cāṃcuvarī | māpa sūye sāgarīṃ| mī neṇatu tyāparī | pravarte yetha || 68 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a tiny sandpiper tries to measure the ocean with its beak, so do I, unknowingly, attempt to describe the indescribable here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आइका आकाश गिंवसावें। तरी आणीक त्याहूनि थोर होआवें। म्हणौनि अपाडू हें आघवें। निर्धारितां॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āikā ākāśa giṃvasāveṃ| tarī āṇīka tyāhūni thora hoāveṃ| mhaṇauni apāḍū heṃ āghaveṃ| nirdhāritāṃ||69||
verses.meaning: Listen, if one were to try to grasp the sky, one would have to become greater than it. Therefore, all this is impossible to determine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या गीतार्थाची थोरी । स्वयें शंभू विवरी । जेथ भवानी प्रश्‍नु करी । चमत्कारौनी ॥ ७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā gītārthācī thorī | svayeṃ śaṃbhū vivarī | jetha bhavānī praś‍nu karī | camatkāraunī || 70||
verses.meaning: The greatness of the meaning of this Gita is such that Lord Shiva himself explains it, when Bhavani, astonished, questions him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ हरु म्हणे नेणिजे। देवी जैसें कां स्वरूप तुझें । तैसें हें नित्य नूतन देखिजे। गीतातत्त्व॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha haru mhaṇe neṇije| devī jaiseṃ kāṃ svarūpa tujheṃ | taiseṃ heṃ nitya nūtana dekhije| gītātattva|| 71||
verses.meaning: There, Shiva said, "O Devi, just as your true nature is unknowable, so too is this essence of the Gita, ever new and fresh, perceived."

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा वेदार्थसागरु। जया निद्रिताचा घोरू। तो स्वयें सर्वेश्‍वरू । प्रत्यक्ष अनुवादला॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā vedārthasāgaru| jayā nidritācā ghorū| to svayeṃ sarveś‍varū | pratyakṣa anuvādalā|| 72||
verses.meaning: He, from whose slumber emanates the ocean of Vedic wisdom, is the Lord of all, who has Himself manifested directly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जें अगाध। जेथ वेडावती वेद। तेथ अल्प मी मतिमंद। काई होये ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jeṃ agādha| jetha veḍāvatī veda| tetha alpa mī matimaṃda| kāī hoye || 73||
verses.meaning: Such is the unfathomable, where even the Vedas are bewildered. How then can I, of limited intellect, comprehend it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें अपार कैसेनि कवळावें। महातेज कवणें धवळावें। गगन मुठीं सुवावें । मशकें केवीं ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ apāra kaiseni kavaḻāveṃ| mahāteja kavaṇeṃ dhavaḻāveṃ| gagana muṭhīṃ suvāveṃ | maśakeṃ kevīṃ || 74||
verses.meaning: How can this immeasurable be grasped? By whom can this great effulgence be cleansed? How can the sky be held in a fist, or by a mosquito?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी एथ असे एकु आधारु । तेणेंचि बोलें मी सधरु । जे सानुकूळ श्रीगुरु । ज्ञानदेवो म्हणे ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī etha ase eku ādhāru | teṇeṃci boleṃ mī sadharu | je sānukūḻa śrīguru | jñānadevo mhaṇe || 75||
verses.meaning: But here there is one support, by which I am made capable, that is the benevolent Guru, says Dnyandev.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येऱ्हवीं तरी मी मूरर्खु । जरी जाहल्या अविवेकु । तऱही संतकृपादीपकु । सोज्वळु असे॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṟhavīṃ tarī mī mūrarkhu | jarī jāhalyā aviveku | taṟahī saṃtakṛpādīpaku | sojvaḻu ase|| 76||
verses.meaning: Even if I am foolish and ignorant, the lamp of the Guru's grace shines brightly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लोहाचें कनक होये । हें सामर्थ्य परिसींच आहे। कीं मृतही जीवित लाहे । अमृतसिऱ्दरि॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: lohāceṃ kanaka hoye | heṃ sāmarthya parisīṃca āhe| kīṃ mṛtahī jīvita lāhe | amṛtasiṟdari|| 77||
verses.meaning: Just as iron turns into gold by the touch of the philosopher's stone, or a dead person comes back to life by the touch of the elixir of immortality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी प्रकटे सिद्धसरस्वती । तरी मुकयाहि आथी भारती। एथ वस्तुसामर्थ्यशक्ति।) नबळ कायी ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī prakaṭe siddhasarasvatī | tarī mukayāhi āthī bhāratī| etha vastusāmarthyaśakti|) nabaḻa kāyī || 78||
verses.meaning: Even if the Goddess of eloquence, Saraswati, manifests, a mute person can still speak. Here, the power of the divine essence is such that nothing is weak.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयातें कामधेनु माये । तयासी अप्राप्य कांहीं आहे। म्हणौनि मी प्रवर्तो लाहें। ग्रंथी इये ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāteṃ kāmadhenu māye | tayāsī aprāpya kāṃhīṃ āhe| mhaṇauni mī pravarto lāheṃ| graṃthī iye || 79||
verses.meaning: For one who has the wish-fulfilling cow (Kamadhenu) as their mother, is there anything unattainable? Therefore, I am able to proceed with this scripture.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी न्यून तें पुरतें। अधिक तें सरतें। करूनि घेयावें हें तुमतें। विनवितु असें ॥ ८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī nyūna teṃ purateṃ| adhika teṃ sarateṃ| karūni gheyāveṃ heṃ tumateṃ| vinavitu aseṃ || 80||
verses.meaning: Therefore, I humbly request you to make up for what is lacking and to diminish what is excessive.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां देईजो अवधान । तुम्हीं बोलविल्या मी बोलेन । जैसें चेष्टे सूत्राधीन । दारूयंत्र ॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ deījo avadhāna | tumhīṃ bolavilyā mī bolena | jaiseṃ ceṣṭe sūtrādhīna | dārūyaṃtra || 81||
verses.meaning: Now, please pay attention. I will speak as you make me speak, just as a puppet is controlled by strings, or a firework mechanism.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा मी अनुग्रहीतु। साधूंचा निरूपितु। ते आपुलियापरी अलंकारितु। भलतयापरी ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā mī anugrahītu| sādhūṃcā nirūpitu| te āpuliyāparī alaṃkāritu| bhalatayāparī || 82||
verses.meaning: Just as I am the bestower of grace, the expounder for the saints, they adorn me in their own way, in whatever manner they please.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब श्रीगुरु म्हणती राहीं। हें तुज बोलावें नलगे कांहीं । आतां ग्रंथा चित्त देई । झडकरी वेगां॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba śrīguru mhaṇatī rāhīṃ| heṃ tuja bolāveṃ nalage kāṃhīṃ | ātāṃ graṃthā citta deī | jhaḍakarī vegāṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: Then Shri Guru says, "Stay here. You don't need to say anything. Now, quickly and swiftly, focus your mind on the scripture."

verses.shloka_devanagari: या बोला निवृत्तिदासु। पावूनि परम उल्हासु। म्हणे परियसा मना अवकाशु। देऊनियां॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā bolā nivṛttidāsu| pāvūni parama ulhāsu| mhaṇe pariyasā manā avakāśu| deūniyāṃ|| 84||
verses.meaning: Receiving these words, Nivrittidas, filled with supreme joy, said, "Listen attentively, giving your mind space."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी पुत्रस्नेहें मोहितु । धृतराष्ट्र असे पुसतु। म्हणे संजया सांगें मातु । कुरुक्षेत्रींची ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī putrasneheṃ mohitu | dhṛtarāṣṭra ase pusatu| mhaṇe saṃjayā sāṃgeṃ mātu | kurukṣetrīṃcī || 85||
verses.meaning: Yet, deluded by affection for his son, Dhritarashtra asked, "Sanjaya, tell me the news from Kurukshetra."

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें धर्मालय म्हणिजे। तेथ पांडब आणि माझे। गेले असती व्याजें। जुंझाचेनि॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ dharmālaya mhaṇije| tetha pāṃḍaba āṇi mājhe| gele asatī vyājeṃ| juṃjhāceni|| 86||
verses.meaning: Where the abode of Dharma is, there the Pandavas and my people have gone, under the pretext of war.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तेचि येतुला अवसरीं । काय किजत असे येरयेरीं। तें झडकरी कथन करीं । मजप्रती ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī teci yetulā avasarīṃ | kāya kijata ase yerayerīṃ| teṃ jhaḍakarī kathana karīṃ | majapratī || 87||
verses.meaning: Therefore, at this very moment, what is being done by each other? Quickly narrate that to me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये वेळीं तो संजय बोळे। म्हणे पांडवसैन्य उचललें। जैसें महाप्रळयीं पसरलें। कृतांतमुख॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye veḻīṃ to saṃjaya boḻe| mhaṇe pāṃḍavasainya ucalaleṃ| jaiseṃ mahāpraḻayīṃ pasaraleṃ| kṛtāṃtamukha|| 88||
verses.meaning: At that time, Sanjaya spoke, saying, "The Pandava army has risen, like the mouth of death spread wide at the time of the great dissolution."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें तें घनदाट। उठावलें एकवाट। जेसें उसळळलें काळकूट। धरी कवण॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ teṃ ghanadāṭa| uṭhāvaleṃ ekavāṭa| jeseṃ usaḻaḻaleṃ kāḻakūṭa| dharī kavaṇa|| 89||
verses.meaning: Just as that dense, unified darkness arose, like the surging poison of Kalakuta, who can contain it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी वडवानळु सादुकला। प्रळयवातें पोखला। सागरु शोषूनि उधवला। अंबरासी ॥ ९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī vaḍavānaḻu sādukalā| praḻayavāteṃ pokhalā| sāgaru śoṣūni udhavalā| aṃbarāsī || 90||
verses.meaning: Or, as the submarine fire, fanned by the winds of dissolution, dries up the ocean and scatters it into the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें दळ दुर्धर। नानाव्यूहीं परिकर। अवगमलळें भयासुर। तिये काळीं॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ daḻa durdhara| nānāvyūhīṃ parikara| avagamalaḻeṃ bhayāsura| tiye kāḻīṃ||91||
verses.meaning: At that time, the formidable army, arranged in various battle formations, appeared terrifying due to its sheer size and arrangement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें देखोनियां दुर्योधनें। अव्हेरिळें कवणें मानें। जैसें न गणिजे पंचाननें। गजघटांतें॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ dekhoniyāṃ duryodhaneṃ| avheriḻeṃ kavaṇeṃ māneṃ| jaiseṃ na gaṇije paṃcānaneṃ| gajaghaṭāṃteṃ||92||
verses.meaning: Seeing this, Duryodhana disregarded it, just as a lion does not count a herd of elephants.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग द्रोणापासी आला। तयांतें म्हणे हा देखिला। कैसा दळभारू उचलला । पांडवांचा ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga droṇāpāsī ālā| tayāṃteṃ mhaṇe hā dekhilā| kaisā daḻabhārū ucalalā | pāṃḍavāṃcā || 93||
verses.meaning: Then he came to Drona and said, "Look at this! How the Pandavas' army has risen!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: गिरिदुर्ग जैसे चालते । तैसे विविध व्यूह सभंवते । रचिले आथी बुद्धिमंतें । द्रुपदकुमरें ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: giridurga jaise cālate | taise vividha vyūha sabhaṃvate | racile āthī buddhimaṃteṃ | drupadakumareṃ || 94||
verses.meaning: Just as mountains and forts move, so too did the intelligent son of Drupada arrange various battle formations all around.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो कां तुम्हीं शिक्षापिला । विद्या देऊनि कुरुठा केला। तेणें हा सैन्यसिंहु पाखरिला। देख देख ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo kāṃ tumhīṃ śikṣāpilā | vidyā deūni kuruṭhā kelā| teṇeṃ hā sainyasiṃhu pākharilā| dekha dekha || 95||
verses.meaning: The one whom you educated and made a master of knowledge, he has now become a lion among armies. Behold, behold!

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिकही असाधारण । जे शस्त्रास्त्री प्रवीण । जे क्षात्रधर्मी निपुण । वीर आहाती ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇikahī asādhāraṇa | je śastrāstrī pravīṇa | je kṣātradharmī nipuṇa | vīra āhātī || 96||
verses.meaning: And also, those extraordinary ones, who are skilled in weapons and arms, who are adept in the warrior's dharma, those heroes are present.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे बळें प्रौढी पौरुषें। भीमार्जुनांसारिखे । ते सांगेन कौतुकें । प्रसंगेंची ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: je baḻeṃ prauḍhī pauruṣeṃ| bhīmārjunāṃsārikhe | te sāṃgena kautukeṃ | prasaṃgeṃcī || 97||
verses.meaning: I will now, with great delight, recount the prowess and valor of those like Bhima and Arjuna, as the occasion arises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ युयुधानु सुभटु। आला असे विराटु। महारथी श्रेष्ठु । द्रुपद वीरु॥९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha yuyudhānu subhaṭu| ālā ase virāṭu| mahārathī śreṣṭhu | drupada vīru||98||
verses.meaning: Here stands Yuyudhana, a great warrior, a giant among men, the supreme charioteer, and the hero Drupada.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चेकितान धृष्टकेतु। काशीराज वीर विक्रांतु। उत्तमौजा नृपनाथु । शैब्य देख॥९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: cekitāna dhṛṣṭaketu| kāśīrāja vīra vikrāṃtu| uttamaujā nṛpanāthu | śaibya dekha||99||
verses.meaning: Chekitana, Dhrishtaketu, the valiant King of Kashi, Uttamauja, and King Shaibya, behold them!

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा कुंतिभोज पाहें। एथ युधामन्यु आला आहे। आणि पुरुजितादि राय हे। सकळ देख ॥ १००॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā kuṃtibhoja pāheṃ| etha yudhāmanyu ālā āhe| āṇi purujitādi rāya he| sakaḻa dekha || 100||
verses.meaning: Behold Kuntibhoja! Here Yudhamanyu has arrived. And Purujit and other kings, all are seen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा सुभद्राहृदयनंदनु। जो अपरु नवार्जुनु| तो अभिमन्यु म्हणे दुर्योधनु। देखें द्रोणा॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā subhadrāhṛdayanaṃdanu| jo aparu navārjunu| to abhimanyu mhaṇe duryodhanu| dekheṃ droṇā|| 1||
verses.meaning: This son, who delights Subhadra's heart, who is a new Arjuna, that Abhimanyu, Duryodhana says, 'Behold, Drona!'

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणीकही द्रौपदीकुमर। हे सकळही महारथी वीर। मिती नेणिजे परी अपार। मीनले असती ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇīkahī draupadīkumara| he sakaḻahī mahārathī vīra| mitī neṇije parī apāra| mīnale asatī || 2||
verses.meaning: And also, the sons of Draupadi, all these great chariot-warriors, are assembled here in immeasurable numbers.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां आमुच्या दळीं नायक। जे रूढवीर सैनिक। ते प्रसंगें आइक । सांगिजती ॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ āmucyā daḻīṃ nāyaka| je rūḍhavīra sainika| te prasaṃgeṃ āika | sāṃgijatī || 3||
verses.meaning: Now, hear about the heroes in our army, those renowned and brave warriors, as they are mentioned in due course.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उद्देशें एक दोनी। जायिजती बोलोनी । तुम्ही आदिकरूनी। मुख्य जे जे॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: uddeśeṃ eka donī| jāyijatī bolonī | tumhī ādikarūnī| mukhya je je|| 4||
verses.meaning: With this intention, I will speak of one or two, starting with you, and all the other principal ones.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा भीष्म गंगानंदनु । जो प्रतापतेजस्वी भानु । रिपुगजपंचाननु । कर्णवीरु ॥५॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā bhīṣma gaṃgānaṃdanu | jo pratāpatejasvī bhānu | ripugajapaṃcānanu | karṇavīru ||5||
verses.meaning: This Bhishma, son of Ganga, is a sun of valor and radiance, a lion to the elephants of his enemies, and a hero like Karna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या एकेकाचेनी मनोव्यापारें। हें विश्व होय संहरे। हा कृपाचार्य न पुरे। एकलाचि॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā ekekācenī manovyāpāreṃ| heṃ viśva hoya saṃhare| hā kṛpācārya na pure| ekalāci|| 6||
verses.meaning: By the mental activity of each individual, this world comes into being and dissolves. Even a great teacher like Kripacharya is not enough, for this happens by itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ विकर्ण बीरु आहे। हा अश्वत्थामा पैल पाहें। याचा आडदरु सदां वाहे। कृतांतु मनीं ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha vikarṇa bīru āhe| hā aśvatthāmā paila pāheṃ| yācā āḍadaru sadāṃ vāhe| kṛtāṃtu manīṃ || 7||
verses.meaning: Here, there is a formidable warrior, Ashwatthama, who is visible there. The fear of him constantly flows in the mind of even Yama, the god of death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: समितिंजयो सौमदत्ती। ऐसे आणीकही बहुत आहाती । जयांचिया बळा मिती । धाताही नेणें॥८॥
verses.shloka_iast: samitiṃjayo saumadattī| aise āṇīkahī bahuta āhātī | jayāṃciyā baḻā mitī | dhātāhī neṇeṃ||8||
verses.meaning: There are many others like Somadatti, who are victorious in battle, whose strength even Brahma does not know.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे शस्त्रविद्यापारंगत। मंत्रावतार मूर्त। हो कां जें अस्त्रजात। एथूनि रूढ॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: je śastravidyāpāraṃgata| maṃtrāvatāra mūrta| ho kāṃ jeṃ astrajāta| ethūni rūḍha||9||
verses.meaning: He who is skilled in the science of weaponry, or who is the very embodiment of the mantra, or from whom all weapons originate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे अप्रतिमल्ल जगीं। पुरता प्रतापु अंगीं । परी सर्व प्राणें मजचिलागीं । आरायिळे असती ॥ ११०॥
verses.shloka_iast: he apratimalla jagīṃ| puratā pratāpu aṃgīṃ | parī sarva prāṇeṃ majacilāgīṃ | ārāyiḻe asatī || 110||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, though these warriors possess immense valor in this world, they have all come here to die for my sake.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पतित्रतेचें हृदय जैसें । पतिवांचूनि न स्पर्शे। मी सर्वस्व या तैसें । सुभटांसी ॥ ९११ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: patitrateceṃ hṛdaya jaiseṃ | pativāṃcūni na sparśe| mī sarvasva yā taiseṃ | subhaṭāṃsī || 911 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a chaste wife's heart is untouched by anyone but her husband, so too am I the everything for these brave warriors.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आमुचिया काजाचेनि पाडें । देखती आपुलें जीवित थोकडें। ऐसे निरवधि चोखडे । स्वामिभक्त ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āmuciyā kājāceni pāḍeṃ | dekhatī āpuleṃ jīvita thokaḍeṃ| aise niravadhi cokhaḍe | svāmibhakta || 12||
verses.meaning: Such are the pure and boundless devotees, who consider their own lives insignificant compared to the task of serving us.

verses.shloka_devanagari: झुंजती कुळकणी जाणती। कळे कौर्तीसी जिती । हे बहु असो क्षात्रनीति। 'एथोनियां ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jhuṃjatī kuḻakaṇī jāṇatī| kaḻe kaurtīsī jitī | he bahu aso kṣātranīti| 'ethoniyāṃ || 13||
verses.meaning: The family traditions are fought over by those who know them, and the glory of victory is understood. Let this be enough; the principles of Kshatriya dharma originate from here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे सर्वांपरि पुरते । बीर दळीं आमुतें। आतां काय गणू यांतें) अपार हे॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise sarvāṃpari purate | bīra daḻīṃ āmuteṃ| ātāṃ kāya gaṇū yāṃteṃ) apāra he|| 94||
verses.meaning: Thus, it is completely sufficient for all. Our strength is in the army. Now, what can we count in this? It is immeasurable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बरी क्षत्रियांमाजी श्रेष्ठु| जो जगजेठी जगीं सुभटु। तया दळवैपणाचा पाटु। भीष्मासि पैं॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: barī kṣatriyāṃmājī śreṣṭhu| jo jagajeṭhī jagīṃ subhaṭu| tayā daḻavaipaṇācā pāṭu| bhīṣmāsi paiṃ|| 15||
verses.meaning: Amongst the Kshatriyas, the greatest, the one who is the world's champion, the brave one in the world, the leadership of the army was given to Bhishma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां याचेनि बळें गवसलें। हें दुर्ग जैसें पन्नासिलें। येणें पाडें थेकुलें। लोकत्रय॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yāceni baḻeṃ gavasaleṃ| heṃ durga jaiseṃ pannāsileṃ| yeṇeṃ pāḍeṃ thekuleṃ| lokatraya|| 16||
verses.meaning: Now, by the strength of this, it has been attained. It is as if this fortress has been conquered, and in comparison, the three worlds appear insignificant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधींच समुद्र पाहीं। तेथ दुवाडपण कवणा नाहीं । मग वबडवानळु तैसेयाही । विरजा जैसा॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhīṃca samudra pāhīṃ| tetha duvāḍapaṇa kavaṇā nāhīṃ | maga vabaḍavānaḻu taiseyāhī | virajā jaisā|| 17||
verses.meaning: When one sees the ocean first, there is no difficulty for anyone. Then, even the submarine fire (vadavanala) becomes as calm as a river.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरीं प्रळयवन्ही महावातु। या दोघां जैसा सांघातु। तैसा हा गंगासुतु। सेनापति॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarīṃ praḻayavanhī mahāvātu| yā doghāṃ jaisā sāṃghātu| taisā hā gaṃgāsutu| senāpati|| 18||
verses.meaning: Or, just as the great wind and the fire of dissolution are united, so too is this son of Ganga, the commander of the army.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां येणेंसि कवण भिडे। हें पांडवसैन्य कीर थोकडें। वबरचिलेनि पाडें। दिसत असे॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yeṇeṃsi kavaṇa bhiḍe| heṃ pāṃḍavasainya kīra thokaḍeṃ| vabaracileni pāḍeṃ| disata ase|| 19||
verses.meaning: Now, why should one be afraid of this? This Pandava army, though small, appears to be well-arranged and prepared.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरी भीमसेनु बेथु। तो जाहला असे सेनानाथु। ऐसें बोलोनियां मातु । सांडिली तेणें॥१२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: varī bhīmasenu bethu| to jāhalā ase senānāthu| aiseṃ boloniyāṃ mātu | sāṃḍilī teṇeṃ||120||
verses.meaning: There, Bhimasena, having become the commander, spoke these words and then ceased.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग पुनरपि काय बोळे। सकळ सैनिकांतें म्हणितलें। आतां दळभार आपुलालळे। सरसे करा॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga punarapi kāya boḻe| sakaḻa sainikāṃteṃ mhaṇitaleṃ| ātāṃ daḻabhāra āpulālaḻe| sarase karā|| 21||
verses.meaning: Then, what more can be said? He addressed all the soldiers, saying, "Now, each of you, prepare your forces and be ready."

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया जिया अक्षौहिणी। तेणें तिया आरणी । 'बरगण कवणकवणी । महारथीया ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā jiyā akṣauhiṇī| teṇeṃ tiyā āraṇī | 'baragaṇa kavaṇakavaṇī | mahārathīyā || 22||
verses.meaning: In whichever army, whichever division, who are the great warriors?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें तिया आवरिजे। भीष्मातळीं राहिजे। द्रोणातें म्हणे पाहिजे । तुम्ही सकळ ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ tiyā āvarije| bhīṣmātaḻīṃ rāhije| droṇāteṃ mhaṇe pāhije | tumhī sakaḻa || 23||
verses.meaning: Thus, she was restrained, remaining under Bhishma, and said to Drona, "You are all needed."

verses.shloka_devanagari: हाचि एकु रक्षावा। मी तैसा हा देखावा । येणें दळभारु आघवा । साचु आमुचा॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāci eku rakṣāvā| mī taisā hā dekhāvā | yeṇeṃ daḻabhāru āghavā | sācu āmucā|| 24||
verses.meaning: Protecting this one (the self) is paramount. See others as you see yourself. By doing so, all your efforts will be truly fruitful.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या राजयाचिया बोला । सेनापति संतोषल्म । मग तेणें केला । सिंहनादु॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā rājayāciyā bolā | senāpati saṃtoṣalma | maga teṇeṃ kelā | siṃhanādu|| 25||
verses.meaning: The commander was pleased by the king's words. Then he roared like a lion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो गाजत असे अदभुतु। दोन्हीं सैन्यांआंतु। प्रतिध्वनि न समातु। उपजत असे॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to gājata ase adabhutu| donhīṃ sainyāṃāṃtu| pratidhvani na samātu| upajata ase|| 26||
verses.meaning: That wondrous sound resonated between both armies, and the echo, unable to be contained, arose.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचि तुलगासवें। वीरवृत्तीचेनि थावें। दिव्य शंख भीष्मदेवें। आस्फुरिला॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāci tulagāsaveṃ| vīravṛttīceni thāveṃ| divya śaṃkha bhīṣmadeveṃ| āsphurilā|| 27||
verses.meaning: At that very moment, with a surge of heroic spirit, Bhishmadeva blew his divine conch.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते दोन्ही नाद मीनले। तेथ त्रैलोक्य बधिरीभूत जाहलें। जैसें आकाश कां पडिलें। तुटोनियां॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: te donhī nāda mīnale| tetha trailokya badhirībhūta jāhaleṃ| jaiseṃ ākāśa kāṃ paḍileṃ| tuṭoniyāṃ|| 28||
verses.meaning: When those two sounds merged, the three worlds became deafened, as if the sky itself had fallen apart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: घडघडीत अंबर। उचंबळत सागर क्षोभलें चराचर । कांपत असे॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ghaḍaghaḍīta aṃbara| ucaṃbaḻata sāgara kṣobhaleṃ carācara | kāṃpata ase|| 29||
verses.meaning: The sky thunders, the ocean surges, the entire animate and inanimate creation trembles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें महाघोषगजरें। दुमदुमिताती गिरिकंदरें। तंव दळामाजीं रणतुरें। आस्फुरिलीं॥ १३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ mahāghoṣagajareṃ| dumadumitātī girikaṃdareṃ| taṃva daḻāmājīṃ raṇatureṃ| āsphurilīṃ|| 130||
verses.meaning: With that great resounding roar, the mountain caves echoed, and then, amidst the army, the war trumpets blared.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उदंड सैंघ वाजते । भयानकें खाखातें । महाप्रळयो जेथें । धाकडांसी ॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: udaṃḍa saiṃgha vājate | bhayānakeṃ khākhāteṃ | mahāpraḻayo jetheṃ | dhākaḍāṃsī || 31||
verses.meaning: Innumerable conch shells blare, terrifyingly resounding, where even the great dissolution trembles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भेरी निशाण मांदळ। शंख काहळ भोंगळ। आणि भयासुर रणकोल्हाळ। सुभटांचे॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: bherī niśāṇa māṃdaḻa| śaṃkha kāhaḻa bhoṃgaḻa| āṇi bhayāsura raṇakolhāḻa| subhaṭāṃce|| 32||
verses.meaning: The sounds of drums, banners, conches, and trumpets, along with the terrifying war cries of brave warriors, filled the battlefield.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आवेशें भुजा त्राहाटिती। विसणेले हांका देती। जेथ महामद भद्रजाती। आवरती ना॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āveśeṃ bhujā trāhāṭitī| visaṇele hāṃkā detī| jetha mahāmada bhadrajātī| āvaratī nā|| 33||
verses.meaning: In their fervor, they thrash their arms, and those who are weary cry out. Even the mighty elephants of noble lineage cannot be restrained there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ भेडांची कवण मातु। कांचया केर फिटतु। जेणें दचकला कृतांतु। आंग नेघे॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha bheḍāṃcī kavaṇa mātu| kāṃcayā kera phiṭatu| jeṇeṃ dacakalā kṛtāṃtu| āṃga neghe|| 34||
verses.meaning: What then is the power of such a devotee, by whose mere glance the dirt of worldly existence is cleansed, and even Death, startled, dares not approach?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एकां उभयाचि प्राण गेळे। चांगांचे दांत बैसळे। बिरुदाचे दादुले। हिंबताती ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ekāṃ ubhayāci prāṇa geḻe| cāṃgāṃce dāṃta baisaḻe| birudāce dādule| hiṃbatātī || 35 ||
verses.meaning: Some people lose their lives in this dualistic world, while others, like the good ones, have their teeth set firmly, and the brave ones, their moustaches, shiver in fear.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा अदभुत तूरबंबाळु। ऐकोनि ब्रह्मा व्याकुळु। देव म्हणती प्रळयकाळु। वबोढवला आजी ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā adabhuta tūrabaṃbāḻu| aikoni brahmā vyākuḻu| deva mhaṇatī praḻayakāḻu| vaboḍhavalā ājī || 36||
verses.meaning: Hearing such a wondrous and tumultuous sound, Brahma became distressed. The gods exclaimed, "The time of dissolution has arrived today!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी स्वर्गी मातु। देखोनि तो आकांतु। तंव पांडवदळाआंतु । वर्तले 'कायी॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī svargī mātu| dekhoni to ākāṃtu| taṃva pāṃḍavadaḻāāṃtu | vartale 'kāyī|| 37||
verses.meaning: Seeing such a great calamity in heaven, what happened then within the Pandava army?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हो कां निजसार विजयाचें। कीं तें भांडार महातेजाचें । जेथ गरुडाचिये जावळियेचे। कांतळे चाऱ्ही ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ho kāṃ nijasāra vijayāceṃ| kīṃ teṃ bhāṃḍāra mahātejāceṃ | jetha garuḍāciye jāvaḻiyece| kāṃtaḻe cāṟhī || 38||
verses.meaning: Or is it the very essence of victory, a treasury of immense splendor, where even the brilliance of Garuda's radiance pales in comparison?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं पाखांचा मेरु जैसा । रहंवरु मिरवतसे तैसा । तेजें कोंदाटलिया दिशा । जयाचेनि॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ pākhāṃcā meru jaisā | rahaṃvaru miravatase taisā | tejeṃ koṃdāṭaliyā diśā | jayāceni|| 39||
verses.meaning: Just as Mount Meru is adorned with wings, so too does the sun shine, its radiance illuminating all directions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ अश्ववाहकु आपण वैकुंठींचा राणा जाण। तया रथाचे गुण। काय वर्णू ॥ ९४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha aśvavāhaku āpaṇa vaikuṃṭhīṃcā rāṇā jāṇa| tayā rathāce guṇa| kāya varṇū || 940||
verses.meaning: Where the charioteer himself is the Lord of Vaikuntha, what can I say about the qualities of that chariot?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ध्वजस्तंभावरी वानरु । तो मूर्तिमंत शंकरु । सारथी शार्डुधरु । अर्जनेंसीं ॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: dhvajastaṃbhāvarī vānaru | to mūrtimaṃta śaṃkaru | sārathī śārḍudharu | arjaneṃsīṃ || 41||
verses.meaning: The monkey on the flagstaff is Lord Shankara incarnate, and the charioteer is Lord Krishna Himself, with Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखा नवल तया प्रभूचें। अदभुत प्रेम भक्‍ताचें। जें सारथ्यपण पार्थाचें। करितु असे॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhā navala tayā prabhūceṃ| adabhuta prema bhak‍tāceṃ| jeṃ sārathyapaṇa pārthāceṃ| karitu ase|| 42||
verses.meaning: Behold the wonder of that Lord, the amazing love for His devotee, that He performs the charioteering for Partha.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाइकु पाठीसी घातला । आपण पुढां राहिला । तेणें पांचजन्यु आस्फुरिळला। अवलीळाचि॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāiku pāṭhīsī ghātalā | āpaṇa puḍhāṃ rāhilā | teṇeṃ pāṃcajanyu āsphuriḻalā| avalīḻāci|| 43||
verses.meaning: Having placed Arjuna behind Him, and Himself standing in front, He effortlessly blew His conch, the Panchajanya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तो महाघोषु थोरु । गर्जतु असे गंहिरु । जैसा उदेला लोपी दिनकरु । नक्षत्रांतें ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī to mahāghoṣu thoru | garjatu ase gaṃhiru | jaisā udelā lopī dinakaru | nakṣatrāṃteṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: But that great, profound roar, like the rising sun eclipsing the stars, resounds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें तुरबंबाळु भवते । कौरवदळीं गाजत होते। ते हारपोनि नेणों केउते । गेले तेथ ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ turabaṃbāḻu bhavate | kauravadaḻīṃ gājata hote| te hāraponi neṇoṃ keute | gele tetha || 45||
verses.meaning: In the same way, the tumultuous roar that resounded in the Kaurava army, I know not where it vanished and disappeared.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसाचि देखें येरें। निनादें अति गहिरें। देवदत्त धनुर्धरें। आस्फुरिला॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisāci dekheṃ yereṃ| ninādeṃ ati gahireṃ| devadatta dhanurdhareṃ| āsphurilā|| 46||
verses.meaning: In the same manner, the conch named Devadatta, belonging to the archer Arjuna, was blown with a very deep and resounding sound.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते दोनी शब्द अचाट । मिनळे एकवट । तेथ ब्रह्मकटाह शतकूट। हों पाहत असे॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te donī śabda acāṭa | minaḻe ekavaṭa | tetha brahmakaṭāha śatakūṭa| hoṃ pāhata ase|| 47||
verses.meaning: When those two extraordinary words unite, the entire universe, with its myriad forms, seems to emerge from that oneness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब भीमसेनु विसणैला। जैसा महाकाळु खवळला । तेणें पौण्ड आस्फुरिला। महाशंख्त्रु ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba bhīmasenu visaṇailā| jaisā mahākāḻu khavaḻalā | teṇeṃ pauṇḍa āsphurilā| mahāśaṃkhtru || 48||
verses.meaning: Then Bhimasena blew his great conch, Paundra, like the enraged Mahakala (the great god of time and destruction).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो महाप्रलयजलधरु । जैसा घडघडिला गंहिरु । तंव अनंतविजयो युधिष्ठिर । आस्फुरित असे॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: to mahāpralayajaladharu | jaisā ghaḍaghaḍilā gaṃhiru | taṃva anaṃtavijayo yudhiṣṭhira | āsphurita ase|| 49||
verses.meaning: Just as a great cloud of the cosmic deluge rumbles with a deep roar, so too did Yudhishthira, the conqueror of countless foes, stand resolute and vibrant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नकुळें सुघोषु । सहदेवें मणिपुष्पकु । जेणें नादें अंतकु । गजबजल्म ठाके॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nakuḻeṃ sughoṣu | sahadeveṃ maṇipuṣpaku | jeṇeṃ nādeṃ aṃtaku | gajabajalma ṭhāke|| 150||
verses.meaning: Nakula blew the Sughosha conch, and Sahadeva blew the Manipushpaka, with a sound that made even the god of death, Yama, tremble and stand still.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ भूपति होते अनेक । द्रुपद द्रौपदेयादिक । हा काशीपति देख। महाबाहु ॥५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha bhūpati hote aneka | drupada draupadeyādika | hā kāśīpati dekha| mahābāhu ||51||
verses.meaning: There were many kings present, including Drupada and Drupadeya, and behold, there was also the mighty-armed King of Kashi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ अर्जुनाचा सुतु। सात्यकि अपराजितु। धृष्टदयुग्रु नृपनाथु। शिखंडी हन॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha arjunācā sutu| sātyaki aparājitu| dhṛṣṭadayugru nṛpanāthu| śikhaṃḍī hana|| 52||
verses.meaning: There were Arjuna's son (Abhimanyu), the unconquered Satyaki, the mighty Dhrishtadyumna, and King Drupada, along with Shikhandi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वबिराटादि नृपवर। जे सैनिक मुख्य वीर। तिहीं नाना शंख निरंतर। आस्फुरिळे॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: vabirāṭādi nṛpavara| je sainika mukhya vīra| tihīṃ nānā śaṃkha niraṃtara| āsphuriḻe|| 53||
verses.meaning: The great kings, starting with Virata, who were the chief warriors, continuously blew various conches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें महाघोषनिर्धातें। शेष कूर्म अवचितें।॥ गजबजोनि भूभारातें। सांडूं पाहती ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ mahāghoṣanirdhāteṃ| śeṣa kūrma avaciteṃ||| gajabajoni bhūbhārāteṃ| sāṃḍūṃ pāhatī || 54||
verses.meaning: With that great thunderous roar, Shesha and Kurma suddenly, agitated, seem to abandon the burden of the earth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ तिन्ही लोक डळमळित । मेरु मांदार आंदोळित । समुद्रजळ उसळत । कैळासवेरी ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha tinhī loka ḍaḻamaḻita | meru māṃdāra āṃdoḻita | samudrajaḻa usaḻata | kaiḻāsaverī || 55 ||
verses.meaning: There, the three worlds tremble, Mount Meru and Mandara sway, and the ocean waters surge even up to Kailasa.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पृथ्वीतळ उलथों पहात। आकाश असे आसुडत। तेथ सडा होत। नक्षत्रांचा ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: pṛthvītaḻa ulathoṃ pahāta| ākāśa ase āsuḍata| tetha saḍā hota| nakṣatrāṃcā || 56||
verses.meaning: The earth seems to turn upside down, the sky is being torn apart, and there, the stars are scattered like an offering.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सृष्टि गेली रे गेली । देवां मोकळवादी जाहली । ऐशी एक टाळी पिटली। सत्यलळोकीं ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: sṛṣṭi gelī re gelī | devāṃ mokaḻavādī jāhalī | aiśī eka ṭāḻī piṭalī| satyalaḻokīṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: The creation has vanished, O Lord, becoming empty. Such a clap resounded in Satyaloka.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दिहाचि दिन थोकला। जैसा प्रलयकाळ मांडला। तैसा हाहाकारु जाहला । तिन्हीं लोकीं ॥५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: dihāci dina thokalā| jaisā pralayakāḻa māṃḍalā| taisā hāhākāru jāhalā | tinhīṃ lokīṃ ||58||
verses.meaning: The day of the body was shortened, as if the time of dissolution had arrived. Such a great cry of distress arose in the three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें देखोनि आदिपुरुष विस्मितु । म्हणे झणें होय पां अंतु। मग लोपिला अदभुतु । संभ्रमु तो॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ dekhoni ādipuruṣa vismitu | mhaṇe jhaṇeṃ hoya pāṃ aṃtu| maga lopilā adabhutu | saṃbhramu to|| 59||
verses.meaning: Seeing this, the Primordial Being was astonished, thinking, "Lest this be the end!" Then that wondrous confusion vanished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि विश्व सांवरलें। एऱ्हवीं युगांत होतें बोडवलें। जें महाशंख आस्फुरिळे। कृष्णादिकीं ॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni viśva sāṃvaraleṃ| eṟhavīṃ yugāṃta hoteṃ boḍavaleṃ| jeṃ mahāśaṃkha āsphuriḻe| kṛṣṇādikīṃ || 160||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the universe was sustained; otherwise, it would have been destroyed in a great deluge, as the great conch shells were sounded by Krishna and others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो घोष तरी उपसंहरला। परि पडिसाद होता राहिला । तेणें दळभार विध्वंसिला । कौरवांचा ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: to ghoṣa tarī upasaṃharalā| pari paḍisāda hotā rāhilā | teṇeṃ daḻabhāra vidhvaṃsilā | kauravāṃcā || 61 ||
verses.meaning: Though that great roar had ceased, its echo lingered, and by that echo, the vast army of the Kauravas was utterly destroyed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा गजघटाआंतु । सिंह लीला विदारितु। तैसा ह॒दयातें भेदितु। कौरवांचिया॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā gajaghaṭāāṃtu | siṃha līlā vidāritu| taisā ha̱dayāteṃ bheditu| kauravāṃciyā|| 62||
verses.meaning: Just as a lion playfully tears apart a herd of elephants, so too did he pierce the hearts of the Kauravas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो गाजत जंब आइकती। तंव उभेचि हिये घालिती । एकमेकांतें म्हणती । सावध रे सावध॥ ६३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: to gājata jaṃba āikatī| taṃva ubheci hiye ghālitī | ekamekāṃteṃ mhaṇatī | sāvadha re sāvadha|| 63 ||
verses.meaning: When they heard that resounding roar, they stood still, their hearts pounding, and said to each other, "Beware! Be cautious!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ बळें प्रौढीपुरते। महारथी वीर होते। तिहीं पुनरपि दळातें । आवरिलें॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha baḻeṃ prauḍhīpurate| mahārathī vīra hote| tihīṃ punarapi daḻāteṃ | āvarileṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: There, with their might and valor, the great warriors and charioteers again restrained the army.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सरिसेपणें उठावळे। दुणबटोनि उचलले। तया दंडी क्षोभळें। लोकत्रय ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sarisepaṇeṃ uṭhāvaḻe| duṇabaṭoni ucalale| tayā daṃḍī kṣobhaḻeṃ| lokatraya || 65 ||
verses.meaning: Then, with equal force, they rose up, doubled in strength, and in that moment of fury, the three worlds were agitated.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ बाणवरी धनुर्धर। वर्षताती निरंतर । जैसे प्रळयांत जळधर। अनिवार कां॥६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha bāṇavarī dhanurdhara| varṣatātī niraṃtara | jaise praḻayāṃta jaḻadhara| anivāra kāṃ||66||
verses.meaning: There, the archers continuously showered arrows, like the incessant and uncontrollable rain clouds at the time of the cosmic dissolution.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते देखलिया अर्जूनें। संतोष घेऊनि मनें। मग संभ्रमें दिठी सेने। घालीतसे॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te dekhaliyā arjūneṃ| saṃtoṣa gheūni maneṃ| maga saṃbhrameṃ diṭhī sene| ghālītase|| 67||
verses.meaning: Seeing them, Arjuna's mind was filled with satisfaction. Then, with a gaze full of eagerness, he surveyed the army.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंव संग्रामीं सज जाहले। सकळ कौरव देखिळे। मग लीलाधनुष्य उचलिलें। पंडुकुमरें॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃva saṃgrāmīṃ saja jāhale| sakaḻa kaurava dekhiḻe| maga līlādhanuṣya ucalileṃ| paṃḍukumareṃ|| 68 ||
verses.meaning: Then, seeing all the Kauravas arrayed for battle, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) playfully lifted his bow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं अर्जुन म्हणतसे देवा । आतां झडकरी रथु पेलावा । नेऊनि मध्यें घालावा । दोहीं दळां॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ arjuna mhaṇatase devā | ātāṃ jhaḍakarī rathu pelāvā | neūni madhyeṃ ghālāvā | dohīṃ daḻāṃ||69||
verses.meaning: At that time, Arjuna said, "O Lord, quickly drive the chariot now. Take it and place it in the middle, between the two armies."

verses.shloka_devanagari: जंब मी नावेक। हे सकळ वीर सैनिक । न्याहाळीन अशेख। झुंजते जे॥ १९७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaṃba mī nāveka| he sakaḻa vīra sainika | nyāhāḻīna aśekha| jhuṃjate je|| 1970||
verses.meaning: When I am in the boat, I will observe all these brave warriors, the entire host, as they fight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ आले असती आघवे। परी 'कवणेंसीं म्यां झुंजावें । हें रणीं लागे पहावें । म्हणौनियां ॥ ७१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha āle asatī āghave| parī 'kavaṇeṃsīṃ myāṃ jhuṃjāveṃ | heṃ raṇīṃ lāge pahāveṃ | mhaṇauniyāṃ || 719||
verses.meaning: All have come here, but with whom should I fight? This needs to be seen on the battlefield, and so I have come.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बहुतकरूनि कौरवब। हे आतुर दुःस्वभाव। वांटिवेवीण हांव। बांधिती झुंजीं॥७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: bahutakarūni kauravaba| he ātura duḥsvabhāva| vāṃṭivevīṇa hāṃva| bāṃdhitī jhuṃjīṃ||72||
verses.meaning: The Kauravas, being very eager and of evil disposition, are tying themselves to battle without any reason.

verses.shloka_devanagari: झुंजाची आवडी धरिती । परी संग्रामीं धीर नव्हती। हें सांगोनि रायाप्रती । 'काय संजयो म्हणे ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jhuṃjācī āvaḍī dharitī | parī saṃgrāmīṃ dhīra navhatī| heṃ sāṃgoni rāyāpratī | 'kāya saṃjayo mhaṇe || 73||
verses.meaning: They desire to fight, but they lack courage in battle. Having said this to the King, what did Sanjaya say next?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्‌ । आइका अर्जुन इतुकें बोलिला। तंव श्रीकृष्णें रथु पेलिला। दोहीं सैन्यांमाजीं केला । उभा तेणें ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt‌ | āikā arjuna itukeṃ bolilā| taṃva śrīkṛṣṇeṃ rathu pelilā| dohīṃ sainyāṃmājīṃ kelā | ubhā teṇeṃ || 74||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, filled with compassion and sorrow, spoke these words. As Arjuna finished speaking, Shri Krishna positioned the chariot, placing it between the two armies.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ भौष्मद्रोणादिक। जवळिकेचि सन्मुख । पृथिवीपति आणिक । बहुत आहाती ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha bhauṣmadroṇādika| javaḻikeci sanmukha | pṛthivīpati āṇika | bahuta āhātī || 75||
verses.meaning: Where Bhishma, Drona, and others, along with many kings, are present in close proximity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ स्थिर करूनियां रथु। अर्जुन असे पाहातु। तो दळभार समस्तु । संभ्रमेंसीं ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha sthira karūniyāṃ rathu| arjuna ase pāhātu| to daḻabhāra samastu | saṃbhrameṃsīṃ || 76||
verses.meaning: Having steadied the chariot there, Arjuna looked upon the entire army with great agitation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग देवा म्हणे देख देख। हे गोत्रगुरु अशेख। तंब कृष्णमनीं नावेक । विस्मो जाहला ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga devā mhaṇe dekha dekha| he gotraguru aśekha| taṃba kṛṣṇamanīṃ nāveka | vismo jāhalā || 77||
verses.meaning: Then the Lord said, "Behold, behold! These are all the revered elders of the lineage." At that moment, Krishna felt a little wonder.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो आपणयां आपण म्हणे। एथ कायी कवण जाणे हें मनीं धरिलें येणें । परि कांहीं आश्चर्य असे ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: to āpaṇayāṃ āpaṇa mhaṇe| etha kāyī kavaṇa jāṇe heṃ manīṃ dharileṃ yeṇeṃ | pari kāṃhīṃ āścarya ase || 78||
verses.meaning: He says to Himself, "What is this? Who knows?" He held this in His mind, but there is some wonder in it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी पुढील से घेतु। तो सहजें जाणे हृदयस्थु। परि उगा असे निवांतु। तिये वेळीं ॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī puḍhīla se ghetu| to sahajeṃ jāṇe hṛdayasthu| pari ugā ase nivāṃtu| tiye veḻīṃ ||79||
verses.meaning: When such service is offered, the indwelling Lord naturally knows it, yet at that time, He remains silently peaceful.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब तेथ पार्थु सकळ । पितृ पितामह केवळ। गुरु बंधु मातुळ । देखता जाहला ॥ १८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba tetha pārthu sakaḻa | pitṛ pitāmaha kevaḻa| guru baṃdhu mātuḻa | dekhatā jāhalā || 180||
verses.meaning: There, Arjuna saw all his paternal ancestors, grandfathers, gurus, brothers, and maternal uncles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इष्ट मित्र आपुळे। कुमरजन देखिले। हे सकळ असती आले। तयांमाजी ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṣṭa mitra āpuḻe| kumarajana dekhile| he sakaḻa asatī āle| tayāṃmājī || 89||
verses.meaning: Among them were all his beloved friends and relatives, and his sons.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुहज्जन सासरे) आणीकही सखे सोडरे। कुमर पौत्र धनुर्धरे। देखिले तेथ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: suhajjana sāsare) āṇīkahī sakhe soḍare| kumara pautra dhanurdhare| dekhile tetha|| 82||
verses.meaning: There, he saw his good-hearted fathers-in-law, other friends and relatives, and his sons and grandsons, who were mighty archers.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयां उपकार होते केळे। कौं आपदीं जे रक्षिळे। हे असो वडील धाकुले। आदिकरूनि॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāṃ upakāra hote keḻe| kauṃ āpadīṃ je rakṣiḻe| he aso vaḍīla dhākule| ādikarūni|| 83||
verses.meaning: Those who have been helped, or those who have been protected in times of adversity—whether they are elders or younger ones, all of them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें गोत्रचि दोहीं दळीं। उदित जालें असे कळीं। हें अर्जुने तिये वेळीं। अवलोकिळें॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ gotraci dohīṃ daḻīṃ| udita jāleṃ ase kaḻīṃ| heṃ arjune tiye veḻīṃ| avalokiḻeṃ|| 84||
verses.meaning: Thus, Arjuna, at that time, observed that the lineage of both armies had arisen in this Kali Yuga.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ मनीं गजबज जाहली । आणि आपैसी कृपा आली । तेणें अपमानें निघाली । वीरवृत्ति॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha manīṃ gajabaja jāhalī | āṇi āpaisī kṛpā ālī | teṇeṃ apamāneṃ nighālī | vīravṛtti|| 85 ||
verses.meaning: Then, a commotion arose in the mind, and grace spontaneously descended. Through that perceived insult, the heroic spirit emerged.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिया उत्तम कुळींचिया होती। आणि गुणलावण्य आथी। तिया आणिकीतें न साहती । सुतेजपणें ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiyā uttama kuḻīṃciyā hotī| āṇi guṇalāvaṇya āthī| tiyā āṇikīteṃ na sāhatī | sutejapaṇeṃ || 86||
verses.meaning: Just as women of noble lineage, endowed with beauty and virtues, cannot tolerate the brilliance of others, so too is the nature of true spiritual light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नविये आवडीचेनि भरें। कामुक निजवनिता बिसरे। मग पाडेंबीण अनुसरे। भ्रमला जैसा ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: naviye āvaḍīceni bhareṃ| kāmuka nijavanitā bisare| maga pāḍeṃbīṇa anusare| bhramalā jaisā || 87||
verses.meaning: Just as a lustful man, captivated by a new desire, forgets his own wife and blindly follows it, so too is the deluded soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं तपोबळें त्रश्‍द्धी । 'पातलिया भ्रंशे बुद्धी। मग तया विरक्‍्ततासिद्धी। आठवेना॥ ८८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ tapobaḻeṃ traś‍ddhī | 'pātaliyā bhraṃśe buddhī| maga tayā virak‍tatāsiddhī| āṭhavenā|| 88 ||
verses.meaning: Or, by the power of penance, if the intellect becomes corrupted, then the attainment of detachment is not remembered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अर्जुना तेथ जाहलें) असतें पुरुषत्व गेळें। जे अंतःकरण दिधलें। 'कारुण्यासी॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ arjunā tetha jāhaleṃ) asateṃ puruṣatva geḻeṃ| je aṃtaḥkaraṇa didhaleṃ| 'kāruṇyāsī|| 89||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, that is what happened there; his masculinity was lost, as he surrendered his heart to compassion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखा मंत्रज्ञु बरळु जाय। मग तेथ कां जैसा संचार होय। तैसा तो धनुर्धर महामोहें । आकळिला॥ १९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhā maṃtrajñu baraḻu jāya| maga tetha kāṃ jaisā saṃcāra hoya| taisā to dhanurdhara mahāmoheṃ | ākaḻilā|| 190||
verses.meaning: Just as a person possessed by a spirit speaks incoherently, so too was that archer (Arjuna) overwhelmed by great delusion.
