verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अर्जुना तूं हें नेणसी। जरी तत्त्वता विचारिसी। तरी बधिता तूं नव्हेसी। हे वध्य नव्हती॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī arjunā tūṃ heṃ neṇasī| jarī tattvatā vicārisī| tarī badhitā tūṃ navhesī| he vadhya navhatī|| 38||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, if you do not know this, if you truly ponder, then you are not the slayer, nor are these the slain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें स्वप्नामाजीं देखिजे। तें स्वप्नींचि साच आपजे। मग चेऊनियां पाहिजे । तवं कांहीं नाहीं ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ svapnāmājīṃ dekhije| teṃ svapnīṃci sāca āpaje| maga ceūniyāṃ pāhije | tavaṃ kāṃhīṃ nāhīṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: Just as one sees something in a dream, and it seems real within that dream, but then upon waking, one finds that there is nothing there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी हे जाण माया। तूं भ्रमत आहासी वायां । शस्त्रें हाणितलिया छाया । जैसी आंगीं न रुपे॥ ९४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī he jāṇa māyā| tūṃ bhramata āhāsī vāyāṃ | śastreṃ hāṇitaliyā chāyā | jaisī āṃgīṃ na rupe|| 940||
verses.meaning: Similarly, know this illusion (Maya). You are wandering in vain. Just as a shadow, when struck by a weapon, does not pierce the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां पूर्ण कुंभ उलंडला। तेथ बिंबाकारु दिसे भ्रंशला। परी भानु नाहीं नासला। तयासवें॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ pūrṇa kuṃbha ulaṃḍalā| tetha biṃbākāru dise bhraṃśalā| parī bhānu nāhīṃ nāsalā| tayāsaveṃ|| 41||
verses.meaning: When a full pot overturns, the reflection within appears to be destroyed. But the sun itself is not destroyed along with it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी मठीं आकाश जेसें। मठाकृती अवतरलें असे। तो भंगळिया आपैसें॥ स्वरूपचि॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī maṭhīṃ ākāśa jeseṃ| maṭhākṛtī avataraleṃ ase| to bhaṃgaḻiyā āpaiseṃ|| svarūpaci|| 42||
verses.meaning: Just as the space within a monastery appears to take on the monastery's form, yet upon the monastery's destruction, it naturally reverts to its true, formless nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें शरीराच्या लोपीं। सर्वथा नाशु नाहीं स्वरूपीं। म्हणौनि तूं हें नारोपी । भ्रांति बापा॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ śarīrācyā lopīṃ| sarvathā nāśu nāhīṃ svarūpīṃ| mhaṇauni tūṃ heṃ nāropī | bhrāṃti bāpā|| 43||
verses.meaning: Just as the destruction of the body does not in any way destroy the true Self, so you should not entertain this illusion, my child.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें जीर्ण वस्त्र सांडिजे। मग नूतन वेढिजे । तैसें देहांतरातें स्वीकारिजे । चैतन्यनाथें ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ jīrṇa vastra sāṃḍije| maga nūtana veḍhije | taiseṃ dehāṃtarāteṃ svīkārije | caitanyanātheṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: Just as old clothes are discarded and new ones are worn, so too does the Lord of Consciousness accept a new body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा अनादि नित्यसिद्धु। निरुपाधि विशुद्धु । म्हणौनि शस्त्रादिकीं छेदु। न घडे यया॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā anādi nityasiddhu| nirupādhi viśuddhu | mhaṇauni śastrādikīṃ chedu| na ghaḍe yayā|| 45||
verses.meaning: This (Self) is beginningless, eternally perfect, and unconditioned, hence it cannot be cut by weapons or similar means.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा प्रळयोदकें नाप्लवे। अग्निदाहो न संभवे। एथ महाशोषु न प्रभवे। मारुताचा ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā praḻayodakeṃ nāplave| agnidāho na saṃbhave| etha mahāśoṣu na prabhave| mārutācā || 46||
verses.meaning: This (the Self) is not inundated by the waters of cosmic dissolution, nor is it consumed by fire. Even the great drying wind cannot affect it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना हा नित्यु| अचळु हा शाइवतु। सर्वत्र सदोदितु। परिपूर्णु हा ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā hā nityu| acaḻu hā śāivatu| sarvatra sadoditu| paripūrṇu hā || 47||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this (Self) is eternal, unmoving, constant, and ever-present everywhere, completely full and perfect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा तर्काचिये दिठी । गोचर नोहे किरीटी । ध्यान याचिये भेटी । उत्कंठा वाहे ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā tarkāciye diṭhī | gocara nohe kirīṭī | dhyāna yāciye bheṭī | utkaṃṭhā vāhe || 48||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, this cannot be perceived by the eye of logic; meditation yearns for its encounter.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा सदा दुर्लभु मना । आपु नोहे साधना । निःसीमु हा अर्जुना । पुरुषोत्तमु॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā sadā durlabhu manā | āpu nohe sādhanā | niḥsīmu hā arjunā | puruṣottamu|| 49||
verses.meaning: This Purushottama (Supreme Being) is always difficult to attain for the mind, not achievable through ordinary means, and is boundless, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा गुणत्रयरहितु। व्यक्‍्तीसी अतीतु। अनादि अविकृतु । सर्वरूप॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā guṇatrayarahitu| vyak‍tīsī atītu| anādi avikṛtu | sarvarūpa|| 150||
verses.meaning: He is beyond the three Gunas, transcendent to all manifestation, without beginning, unchanging, and the form of everything.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना ऐसा हा जाणावा । सकळात्मकु देखावा । मग सहजें शोकु आघवा । हरेल तुझा ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā aisā hā jāṇāvā | sakaḻātmaku dekhāvā | maga sahajeṃ śoku āghavā | harela tujhā || 51||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, know this: perceive the Self in all beings. Then, your sorrow will naturally vanish.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा ऐसा नेणसी। तूं अंतवंतचि मानिसी। तऱही शोचूं न पवसी। पंडुकुमरा ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā aisā neṇasī| tūṃ aṃtavaṃtaci mānisī| taṟahī śocūṃ na pavasī| paṃḍukumarā || 52||
verses.meaning: Or, if you do not understand this, and consider me to be finite, even then, O son of Pandu, you should not grieve.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो आदि स्थिति अंतु। हा निरंतर असे नित्यु। जैसा प्रवाहो अनुस्यूतु। गंगाजळाचा ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo ādi sthiti aṃtu| hā niraṃtara ase nityu| jaisā pravāho anusyūtu| gaṃgājaḻācā || 53||
verses.meaning: He who is the beginning, the state, and the end, remains eternal and continuous, like the uninterrupted flow of the Ganges water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें आदि नाहीं खंडलें। समुद्री तरी असे मिनलें। आणि जातचि मध्यें उरलें। दिसे जैसें ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ ādi nāhīṃ khaṃḍaleṃ| samudrī tarī ase minaleṃ| āṇi jātaci madhyeṃ uraleṃ| dise jaiseṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: That which was not broken in the beginning, is merged in the ocean, and remains in the middle, appears as it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इयें तिन्ही तयापरी । सरसींच सदा अवधारीं। भूतांसि कवणीं अवसरीं।॥ ठाकती ना॥५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: iyeṃ tinhī tayāparī | sarasīṃca sadā avadhārīṃ| bhūtāṃsi kavaṇīṃ avasarīṃ||| ṭhākatī nā||55||
verses.meaning: In these three states, always understand that they are equal. At no time do they hinder beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि हें आघवें। एथ तुज नलगे शोचावें। जे स्थितीचि हे स्वभावें । अनादि ऐसी॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni heṃ āghaveṃ| etha tuja nalage śocāveṃ| je sthitīci he svabhāveṃ | anādi aisī|| 56||
verses.meaning: Therefore, you need not grieve over this at all, for this state is inherently eternal and without beginning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी हें अर्जुना। न येचि तुझिया मना। जे देखोनि लोकु अधीना। जन्मक्षया ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī heṃ arjunā| na yeci tujhiyā manā| je dekhoni loku adhīnā| janmakṣayā || 57||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this truth does not enter your mind, that seeing this, people are subject to birth and death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी एथ कांहीं । तुज शोकासि कारण नाहीं। हे जन्ममृत्यु पाहीं । अपरिहर ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī etha kāṃhīṃ | tuja śokāsi kāraṇa nāhīṃ| he janmamṛtyu pāhīṃ | aparihara || 58||
verses.meaning: Therefore, there is no reason for you to grieve here. These cycles of birth and death, behold, are inevitable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उपजे तें नाशे। नाशलें पुनरपि दिसे। हें घटिकायंत्र तैसें । परिभ्रमे गा॥५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: upaje teṃ nāśe| nāśaleṃ punarapi dise| heṃ ghaṭikāyaṃtra taiseṃ | paribhrame gā||59||
verses.meaning: What is born perishes, and what perishes appears again. This cycle is like a water-clock, ever revolving.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी उदो अस्तु आपैसें। अखंडित होत जात जेसें। हें जन्ममरण तेैसें। अनिवार जगीं ॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī udo astu āpaiseṃ| akhaṃḍita hota jāta jeseṃ| heṃ janmamaraṇa teaiseṃ| anivāra jagīṃ || 160||
verses.meaning: Just as the rising and setting of the sun happen continuously and inevitably, so too are birth and death in this world, unavoidable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: महाप्रलयअवसरें। हें त्रैलोक्यहि संहरे। म्हणौनि हा न परिहरे। आदिअंतु ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mahāpralayaavasareṃ| heṃ trailokyahi saṃhare| mhaṇauni hā na parihare| ādiaṃtu || 61||
verses.meaning: Even at the time of the great dissolution, this entire universe perishes. Therefore, it does not abandon its beginning and end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं जरी हें ऐसें मानिसी । तरी खेदु कां करिसी। काय जाणतुचि नेणसी। धनुर्धरा ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ jarī heṃ aiseṃ mānisī | tarī khedu kāṃ karisī| kāya jāṇatuci neṇasī| dhanurdharā || 62||
verses.meaning: If you believe this to be true, then why do you grieve? Do you not know what you already know, O Arjuna?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ आणीकही एक पार्था) तुज बहुतीं परी पहातां। दुःख करावया सर्वथा । विषो नाहीं ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha āṇīkahī eka pārthā) tuja bahutīṃ parī pahātāṃ| duḥkha karāvayā sarvathā | viṣo nāhīṃ || 63||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, when you look at it in many ways, there is absolutely no reason for you to suffer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जियें समस्तें इयें भूतें। जन्माआदि अमूर्ते। मग पातलीं व्यक्‍तीतें । जन्मलेया ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiyeṃ samasteṃ iyeṃ bhūteṃ| janmāādi amūrte| maga pātalīṃ vyak‍tīteṃ | janmaleyā || 64||
verses.meaning: All these beings, which were formless before birth, then attained individuality upon being born.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियें क्षयासि जेथ जाती । तेथ निभ्रांत आने नव्हती । देखें पूर्वस्थितीच येती। आपुलिये॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyeṃ kṣayāsi jetha jātī | tetha nibhrāṃta āne navhatī | dekheṃ pūrvasthitīca yetī| āpuliye|| 65||
verses.meaning: When they reach that state of dissolution, they undoubtedly do not return to this world. Instead, they attain their original, true state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येर मध्यें जें प्रतिभासे। तें निद्रिता स्वप्न जैसें। तैसा आकारु हा मायावशें। सत्स्वरूपीं ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yera madhyeṃ jeṃ pratibhāse| teṃ nidritā svapna jaiseṃ| taisā ākāru hā māyāvaśeṃ| satsvarūpīṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: Whatever else appears in between is like a dream to one who is asleep. Similarly, this form, due to the power of Maya, appears within the true Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी पवनें स्पर्शिलें नीर। पठियासे तरंगाकार। कां परापेक्षा अळंकार-। व्यक्‍ती 'कनकीं॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī pavaneṃ sparśileṃ nīra| paṭhiyāse taraṃgākāra| kāṃ parāpekṣā aḻaṃkāra-| vyak‍tī 'kanakīṃ|| 67||
verses.meaning: Just as water touched by the wind forms waves, or as ornaments derive their form from gold, so too is the manifestation of the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सकळ हें मूर्त। जाण पां मायाकारित। जैसें आकाशीं बिंबत। अभ्रपटल॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sakaḻa heṃ mūrta| jāṇa pāṃ māyākārita| jaiseṃ ākāśīṃ biṃbata| abhrapaṭala|| 68||
verses.meaning: Understand that all this manifest world is a creation of Maya, just as clouds appear reflected in the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आदीचि जें नाहीं । तयालागीं तूं रुदसी कायी। तूं अवीट तें पाहीं । चैतन्य एक ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ādīci jeṃ nāhīṃ | tayālāgīṃ tūṃ rudasī kāyī| tūṃ avīṭa teṃ pāhīṃ | caitanya eka || 69||
verses.meaning: That which never existed in the first place, why do you weep for it? Behold that which is imperishable, the one Consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाची आर्तीचि भोगित। विषयीं त्यजिले संत । जयालागीं विरक्त । बनवासिये ॥ ९१७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayācī ārtīci bhogita| viṣayīṃ tyajile saṃta | jayālāgīṃ virakta | banavāsiye || 9170||
verses.meaning: Whose ardent desire is experienced by those saints who have renounced worldly pleasures, and for whom even hermits have become detached.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दिठी सूनि जयातें । ब्रह्मचर्यादि त्रतें। मुनीश्वर तपातें। आचरताती ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: diṭhī sūni jayāteṃ | brahmacaryādi trateṃ| munīśvara tapāteṃ| ācaratātī || 79||
verses.meaning: The one whom even great sages, through their austerities and vows of celibacy, strive to perceive with their inner vision.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक अंतरीं निश्चळ। जें निहाळितां केवळ। विसरळे सकळ। संसारजात ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka aṃtarīṃ niścaḻa| jeṃ nihāḻitāṃ kevaḻa| visaraḻe sakaḻa| saṃsārajāta || 72||
verses.meaning: When one contemplates that singular, unwavering reality within, the entire worldly existence is forgotten.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एकां गुणानुवादु करितां। उपरति होऊनि चित्ता । निरवधि तल्लीनता । निरंतर ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ekāṃ guṇānuvādu karitāṃ| uparati hoūni cittā | niravadhi tallīnatā | niraṃtara || 73||
verses.meaning: When one thus praises the divine qualities, the mind becomes detached from worldly concerns and remains continuously absorbed in that divine essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक ऐकतांचि निवाळे। ते देहभावीं सांडिळे। एक अनुभवें पातळे। तद्रूपता ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka aikatāṃci nivāḻe| te dehabhāvīṃ sāṃḍiḻe| eka anubhaveṃ pātaḻe| tadrūpatā || 74||
verses.meaning: Some attain liberation merely by hearing, abandoning their bodily identification. Others achieve oneness through direct experience.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसे सरिताओघ समस्त । समुद्रामाजीं मिळत। परी माघौते न समात। परतले नाहीं ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaise saritāogha samasta | samudrāmājīṃ miḻata| parī māghaute na samāta| paratale nāhīṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: Just as all rivers flow into the ocean, they never return from it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसिया योगीश्‍वरांचिया मती । मिळवणीसवें एकवटती। परी जे विचारूनि पुनरावृत्ति । भजतीचि ना॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisiyā yogīś‍varāṃciyā matī | miḻavaṇīsaveṃ ekavaṭatī| parī je vicārūni punarāvṛtti | bhajatīci nā|| 76||
verses.meaning: Thus, the minds of such great Yogis, upon attaining union, become one. But those who, after contemplation, do not return to worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें सर्वत्र सर्वही देहीं । जया करितांही घातु नाहीं। तें विश्वात्मक तूं पाहीं । चैतन्य एक ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ sarvatra sarvahī dehīṃ | jayā karitāṃhī ghātu nāhīṃ| teṃ viśvātmaka tūṃ pāhīṃ | caitanya eka || 77||
verses.meaning: That which is everywhere, in all bodies, and by which no harm is caused, know that to be the one universal consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचेनि स्वभावें। हें होत जात आघवें। तरी सांग काय शोचावें। एथ तुवां ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāceni svabhāveṃ| heṃ hota jāta āghaveṃ| tarī sāṃga kāya śocāveṃ| etha tuvāṃ || 78||
verses.meaning: By whose very nature all this comes into being and passes away, then tell me, what is there for you to grieve about here?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं तरी पार्था। तुज कां नेणों न मनें चित्ता। परी किडाळ हें शोचितां। बहुतीं परी ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ tarī pārthā| tuja kāṃ neṇoṃ na maneṃ cittā| parī kiḍāḻa heṃ śocitāṃ| bahutīṃ parī || 79||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, Arjuna, why should I not know you, or why should my mind not accept you? But this sorrow is a great defilement in many ways.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं अझुनी कां न विचारिसी। काय हें चिंतितु आहासी । स्वधर्मु तो वबिसरलासी । तरावें जेणें ॥ १८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ ajhunī kāṃ na vicārisī| kāya heṃ ciṃtitu āhāsī | svadharmu to vabisaralāsī | tarāveṃ jeṇeṃ || 180||
verses.meaning: Why do you not yet inquire? What is it that you are contemplating? You have forgotten your own dharma, by which you could have crossed over.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या कौरवां भलतें जाहलें। अथवा तुजचि कांहीं पातळें। कीं युगचि हें बुडालें। जऱ्ही एथ॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā kauravāṃ bhalateṃ jāhaleṃ| athavā tujaci kāṃhīṃ pātaḻeṃ| kīṃ yugaci heṃ buḍāleṃ| jaṟhī etha|| 81||
verses.meaning: Has something untoward happened to these Kauravas, or has something befallen you? Or has this very age come to an end, even here?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी स्वधर्मु एकु आहे। तो सर्वथा त्याज्य नोहे। मग तरिजेळ काय पाहें । कृपाळूपणें ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī svadharmu eku āhe| to sarvathā tyājya nohe| maga tarijeḻa kāya pāheṃ | kṛpāḻūpaṇeṃ || 82||
verses.meaning: Therefore, there is one's own Dharma. It is never to be abandoned. Then, one can see how it leads to liberation through compassion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना तुझे चित्त । जऱ्ही जाहलें द्रवीभूत । तऱही हें अनुचित । संग्रामसमयीं ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā tujhe citta | jaṟhī jāhaleṃ dravībhūta | taṟahī heṃ anucita | saṃgrāmasamayīṃ || 83||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, even if your heart has melted with compassion, such a state is inappropriate at the time of battle.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा गोक्षीर जरी जाहलें। तरी पथ्यासि नाहीं म्हणितळें। ऐसेनिहि विष होय सुदलें। नवज्वरीं देतां ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā gokṣīra jarī jāhaleṃ| tarī pathyāsi nāhīṃ mhaṇitaḻeṃ| aisenihi viṣa hoya sudaleṃ| navajvarīṃ detāṃ || 84||
verses.meaning: Even if cow's milk is considered a wholesome diet, it is not prescribed for a feverish patient. If given to someone with a new fever, it can turn into poison.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आनीं आन करितां। नाशु होईल हिता । म्हणौनि तूं आतां। सावध होई ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ānīṃ āna karitāṃ| nāśu hoīla hitā | mhaṇauni tūṃ ātāṃ| sāvadha hoī || 85||
verses.meaning: If you try to do something else, your true welfare will be destroyed. Therefore, you must now become alert.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वायांचि व्याकुळ कायी। आपुला निजधर्मु पाहीं। जो आचरितां बाधु नाहीं। कवणें काळीं॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāyāṃci vyākuḻa kāyī| āpulā nijadharmu pāhīṃ| jo ācaritāṃ bādhu nāhīṃ| kavaṇeṃ kāḻīṃ|| 86||
verses.meaning: Why are you needlessly distressed? Look to your own inherent duty, which, when performed, causes no hindrance at any time.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें मार्गेचि चालतां । अपावो न पवे सर्वथा । कां दीपाधारें वर्ततां। नाडळिजे ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ mārgeci cālatāṃ | apāvo na pave sarvathā | kāṃ dīpādhāreṃ vartatāṃ| nāḍaḻije || 87||
verses.meaning: Just as by walking on the right path, one never encounters danger, or by moving with the aid of a lamp, one does not stumble.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयापरी पार्था । स्वधर्मे राहाटतां। सकळ कामपूर्णता । सहजें होय॥ ८८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāparī pārthā | svadharme rāhāṭatāṃ| sakaḻa kāmapūrṇatā | sahajeṃ hoya|| 88 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, by adhering to one's own dharma, all desires are naturally fulfilled.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि यालागीं पाहीं । तुम्हां क्षत्रियां आणीक कांहीं । संग्रामावांचूनि नाहीं । ३८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी उचित जाणें ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni yālāgīṃ pāhīṃ | tumhāṃ kṣatriyāṃ āṇīka kāṃhīṃ | saṃgrāmāvāṃcūni nāhīṃ | 38 śrījñāneśvarī ucita jāṇeṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for you Kshatriyas, there is no other duty more appropriate than engaging in battle.

verses.shloka_devanagari: निष्कपटा होआवें । उसिणा घाई जुंझावें । हें असो काय सांगावें । प्रत्यक्षावरी ॥ १९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: niṣkapaṭā hoāveṃ | usiṇā ghāī juṃjhāveṃ | heṃ aso kāya sāṃgāveṃ | pratyakṣāvarī || 190||
verses.meaning: Be guileless. Fight with enthusiasm. Why should I say more about what is evident?

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना झुंज देखें आतांचें । हें हो कां जें दैव तुमचें । कीं निधान सकळ धर्माचें । प्रगटलें असे॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā jhuṃja dekheṃ ātāṃceṃ | heṃ ho kāṃ jeṃ daiva tumaceṃ | kīṃ nidhāna sakaḻa dharmāceṃ | pragaṭaleṃ ase|| 91||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this battle you see now, it is your destiny, for the treasure of all righteousness has manifested.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा संग्रामु काय म्हणिपे। कीं स्वर्गुचि येणें रूपें। मूर्त कां प्रतापें। उदो केला॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā saṃgrāmu kāya mhaṇipe| kīṃ svarguci yeṇeṃ rūpeṃ| mūrta kāṃ pratāpeṃ| udo kelā|| 92||
verses.meaning: What can this battle be called? Is it not heaven itself, manifested in this form, or perhaps the very glory that has arisen?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी गुणाचेनि पतिकरें। आर्तीचेनि पडिभरें। हें कौर्तीचि स्वयंबरें। आली तुज॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī guṇāceni patikareṃ| ārtīceni paḍibhareṃ| heṃ kaurtīci svayaṃbareṃ| ālī tuja|| 93||
verses.meaning: Or, perhaps, it is due to the power of your virtues, or the intensity of devotion, that this fame has come to you as if in a self-choice marriage.

verses.shloka_devanagari: क्षत्रियें बहुत पुण्य कौजे। तैं झुंज ऐसें लाहिजे। जैसें मार्गे जातां आडळिजे। चिंतामणि॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṣatriyeṃ bahuta puṇya kauje| taiṃ jhuṃja aiseṃ lāhije| jaiseṃ mārge jātāṃ āḍaḻije| ciṃtāmaṇi|| 94||
verses.meaning: When a Kshatriya accumulates great merit, they attain a battle like this, just as one might stumble upon a wish-fulfilling gem while walking along a path.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी जांभया पसरे मुख। तेथ अवचटें पडे पीयुख। तैसा संग्रामु हा देख। पातला असे॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī jāṃbhayā pasare mukha| tetha avacaṭeṃ paḍe pīyukha| taisā saṃgrāmu hā dekha| pātalā ase|| 95||
verses.meaning: Or, if one yawns and opens their mouth, and by chance nectar falls into it, such is this battle that has arrived.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां हा ऐसा अव्हेरिजे। मग नाथिलें शोचूं बैसिजे। तरी आपण आहाणा होईजे। आपणपेयां॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ hā aisā avherije| maga nāthileṃ śocūṃ baisije| tarī āpaṇa āhāṇā hoīje| āpaṇapeyāṃ|| 96||
verses.meaning: If one thus rejects this (the true Self), and then sits lamenting for what is not, then one becomes a stranger to oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पूर्वजांचे जोडलें आपणचि होय धाडिलें। जरी आजि शस्त्र सांडिळें। रणीं इये ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pūrvajāṃce joḍaleṃ āpaṇaci hoya dhāḍileṃ| jarī āji śastra sāṃḍiḻeṃ| raṇīṃ iye || 97||
verses.meaning: If I abandon my weapons today, it will be as if I myself have sent my ancestors to hell.

verses.shloka_devanagari: असती कौर्ति जाईल। जगचि अभिशापु देईल। आणि गिंवसित पावतीळ। महादोष॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: asatī kaurti jāīla| jagaci abhiśāpu deīla| āṇi giṃvasita pāvatīḻa| mahādoṣa|| 98||
verses.meaning: If there is fame, it will be lost. The world will curse. And great faults will be found.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी भातारेंहीन वनिता । उपहती पावे सर्वथा । तैशी दशा जीविता । स्वधर्मैवीण ॥९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī bhātāreṃhīna vanitā | upahatī pāve sarvathā | taiśī daśā jīvitā | svadharmaivīṇa ||99||
verses.meaning: Just as a woman without her husband is utterly disgraced, so too is life without one's own dharma (righteous duty or nature).

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी रणीं शव सांडिजे। तें चौमेरीं गिधीं विदारिजे। तैसें स्वधर्महीना अभिभविजे। महादोषीं ॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī raṇīṃ śava sāṃḍije| teṃ caumerīṃ gidhīṃ vidārije| taiseṃ svadharmahīnā abhibhavije| mahādoṣīṃ || 200||
verses.meaning: Just as a corpse abandoned on the battlefield is torn apart by vultures from all sides, so too is one who abandons their own dharma overwhelmed by great sins.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि स्वधर्मु हा सांडसीळ। पापा वरपडा होसील। आणि अपेश तें न वचेलळ। कल्पांतवरी॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni svadharmu hā sāṃḍasīḻa| pāpā varapaḍā hosīla| āṇi apeśa teṃ na vacelaḻa| kalpāṃtavarī|| 1||
verses.meaning: Therefore, if you abandon this inherent duty, you will become entangled in sin, and that disgrace will not depart even until the end of the eon.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जाणतेनि तंवचि जियावें। जंव अपकोर्ति आंगा न पवे। आणि सांग पां केवीं निगावें। एथोनियां ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāṇateni taṃvaci jiyāveṃ| jaṃva apakorti āṃgā na pave| āṇi sāṃga pāṃ kevīṃ nigāveṃ| ethoniyāṃ || 2||
verses.meaning: A wise person should live only as long as dishonor does not touch them. And tell me, how can one depart from here?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं निर्मत्सर सदयता। येथूनि निघसीळ कीर माघौता। परी ते गती समस्तां। न मनेल ययां॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ nirmatsara sadayatā| yethūni nighasīḻa kīra māghautā| parī te gatī samastāṃ| na manela yayāṃ||3||
verses.meaning: You are free from envy and full of compassion. You will indeed return from here, but this path will not be acceptable to all of them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे चहूंकडूनि वेढितील। बाणवरी घेतील। तेथ पार्था न सुटिजेळ। कृपाळुपणें ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: he cahūṃkaḍūni veḍhitīla| bāṇavarī ghetīla| tetha pārthā na suṭijeḻa| kṛpāḻupaṇeṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: They will surround you from all sides and shower you with arrows. There, O Partha, you cannot be saved by compassion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनिहि प्राणसंकटें। जरी विपायें पां निघणें घटे । तरी तें जियालेंही बोखटें । मरणाहुनी ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisenihi prāṇasaṃkaṭeṃ| jarī vipāyeṃ pāṃ nighaṇeṃ ghaṭe | tarī teṃ jiyāleṃhī bokhaṭeṃ | maraṇāhunī || 5||
verses.meaning: Even if one were to escape such a life-threatening situation by chance, that survival would be worse than death itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं आणीकही एक न विचारिसी। एथ संभ्रमें झुंजो आलासी । आणि सकणवपणें निघालासी। मागुता जरी ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ āṇīkahī eka na vicārisī| etha saṃbhrameṃ jhuṃjo ālāsī | āṇi sakaṇavapaṇeṃ nighālāsī| māgutā jarī || 6||
verses.meaning: You did not ask anything else; you came here confused and ready to fight, but then, out of compassion, you turned back.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तुझें तें अर्जुना । या वैरियां दुर्जनां। कां प्रत्यया येईल मना । सांगैं मज ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tujheṃ teṃ arjunā | yā vairiyāṃ durjanāṃ| kāṃ pratyayā yeīla manā | sāṃgaiṃ maja || 7||
verses.meaning: Then, Arjuna, how will your true nature be revealed to these wicked enemies? Tell me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे म्हणती गेला रे गेला। अर्जुन आम्हां बिहाला। हा सांगैं बोलु उरला । निका कायी॥८॥
verses.shloka_iast: he mhaṇatī gelā re gelā| arjuna āmhāṃ bihālā| hā sāṃgaiṃ bolu uralā | nikā kāyī||8||
verses.meaning: They say, "He is gone, he is gone! Arjuna has become afraid of us." What good is such talk remaining?

verses.shloka_devanagari: लोक सायासें करूनि बहुतें। कां वेंचिति आपुलीं जीवितें। परी वाढविती कौर्तीतें। धनुर्धरा ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: loka sāyāseṃ karūni bahuteṃ| kāṃ veṃciti āpulīṃ jīviteṃ| parī vāḍhavitī kaurtīteṃ| dhanurdharā || 9||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, people strive with great effort, even sacrificing their lives, to increase their fame.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते तुज अनायासे । अनकळित जोडिली असे। हें अद्वितीय जैसें । गगन आहे ॥ २१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: te tuja anāyāse | anakaḻita joḍilī ase| heṃ advitīya jaiseṃ | gagana āhe || 210||
verses.meaning: That (the Self) is effortlessly and unknowingly attained by you. It is unique, just like the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी कौर्ति निःसीम । तुझ्या ठायीं निरुपम। तुझे गुण उत्तम । तिहीं लोकीं ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī kaurti niḥsīma | tujhyā ṭhāyīṃ nirupama| tujhe guṇa uttama | tihīṃ lokīṃ || 19||
verses.meaning: Similarly, Your fame is boundless, incomparable within You. Your virtues are supreme in all three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दिगंतींचे भूपति। भाट होऊनि वाखाणिती । जे ऐकिलिया दचकती। कृतांतादिक॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: digaṃtīṃce bhūpati| bhāṭa hoūni vākhāṇitī | je aikiliyā dacakatī| kṛtāṃtādika|| 12||
verses.meaning: The kings of all directions, becoming bards, praise Him; even Yama and others are startled upon hearing of Him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा महिमा घनवट । गंगा जैसी चोखट। जया देखीं जगीं सुभट। वाट जाहली ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā mahimā ghanavaṭa | gaṃgā jaisī cokhaṭa| jayā dekhīṃ jagīṃ subhaṭa| vāṭa jāhalī || 13||
verses.meaning: Such is the profound glory, as pure as the Ganges, that wherever it is seen, a path is created for the valiant in this world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें पौरुष तुझें अदभुत। आइकोनियां हे समस्त । जाहले आधि विरक्‍्त। जीवितेंसीं ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ pauruṣa tujheṃ adabhuta| āikoniyāṃ he samasta | jāhale ādhi virak‍ta| jīviteṃsīṃ || 94||
verses.meaning: Hearing of your wondrous valor, all these (beings) became detached from life itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा सिंहाचिया हांका। युगांतु होय मदमुखा। तैसा कौरवां अशेखां। धाकु तुझा ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā siṃhāciyā hāṃkā| yugāṃtu hoya madamukhā| taisā kauravāṃ aśekhāṃ| dhāku tujhā || 15||
verses.meaning: Just as the roar of a lion at the end of an age causes elephants to lose their rut, so too does your terror strike all the Kauravas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसे पर्वत वज़ातें। ना तरी सर्प गरुडातें। तैसे अर्जुना हे तूंतें । मानिती सदा ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaise parvata vazāteṃ| nā tarī sarpa garuḍāteṃ| taise arjunā he tūṃteṃ | mānitī sadā || 16||
verses.meaning: Just as mountains consider a thunderbolt, or a snake considers an eagle, so too, Arjuna, do these (demons) always regard you.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें अगाधपण जाईल मग हीणावो अंगा येईल। जरी मागुता निघसील। न झुंजतुचि ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ agādhapaṇa jāīla maga hīṇāvo aṃgā yeīla| jarī māgutā nighasīla| na jhuṃjatuci || 97||
verses.meaning: That unfathomable greatness will then vanish, and disgrace will befall you. If you retreat again, without even fighting.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हे पळतां पळों नेदिती। धरूनि अवकळा करिती। न गणित कुटी बोलती । आइकतां तुज ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi he paḻatāṃ paḻoṃ neditī| dharūni avakaḻā karitī| na gaṇita kuṭī bolatī | āikatāṃ tuja || 18||
verses.meaning: And these (senses) do not allow the mind to run (towards God); they seize it and make it do evil deeds. They speak countless wicked words, even as you listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग ते वेळीं हियें फुटावें। आतां लाठेपणें कां न झुंजावें। हें जिंतळें तरी भोगावें। महीतळ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga te veḻīṃ hiyeṃ phuṭāveṃ| ātāṃ lāṭhepaṇeṃ kāṃ na jhuṃjāveṃ| heṃ jiṃtaḻeṃ tarī bhogāveṃ| mahītaḻa|| 19||
verses.meaning: At that time, the heart should burst. Why not fight with courage now? Even if this body is conquered, it will still experience the earthly realm.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ४० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी ना तरी रणीं एथ । झुंजतां वेंचळें जीवित । तरी स्वर्गसुख अनकळित। 'पावसील॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: 40 śrījñāneśvarī nā tarī raṇīṃ etha | jhuṃjatāṃ veṃcaḻeṃ jīvita | tarī svargasukha anakaḻita| 'pāvasīla|| 220||
verses.meaning: Or, if you die fighting in battle, you will attain unimaginable heavenly bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ये गोठी। विचारु न करीं किरीटी। आतां धनुष्य घेऊनि उठीं। झुंजे वेगीं ॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni ye goṭhī| vicāru na karīṃ kirīṭī| ātāṃ dhanuṣya gheūni uṭhīṃ| jhuṃje vegīṃ || 21||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Kiriti, do not dwell on these matters. Now, take up your bow and quickly prepare for battle.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें स्वधर्मु हा आचरतां । दोषु नाशे असता । तुज भ्रांति हे कवण चित्ता। एथ पातकाची ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ svadharmu hā ācaratāṃ | doṣu nāśe asatā | tuja bhrāṃti he kavaṇa cittā| etha pātakācī || 22||
verses.meaning: Behold, by practicing your own dharma, all sins are destroyed. What delusion is this in your mind, that there is any sin here?

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांगैं प्लवेंचि काय बुडिजे। कां मार्गी जातां आडळिजे। परी विपायें चालो नेणिजे। तरी तेंही घडे ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃgaiṃ plaveṃci kāya buḍije| kāṃ mārgī jātāṃ āḍaḻije| parī vipāyeṃ cālo neṇije| tarī teṃhī ghaḍe || 23||
verses.meaning: Tell me, does a boat inherently sink? Or does one stumble on a path? But if one does not know how to walk carefully, then even that can happen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अमृतें तरीच मरिजे। जरी विखेंसि सेविजे। तैसा स्वधर्मी दोषु पाविजे । हेतुकपणें ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: amṛteṃ tarīca marije| jarī vikheṃsi sevije| taisā svadharmī doṣu pāvije | hetukapaṇeṃ || 24||
verses.meaning: One can die even from nectar if it is consumed with poison. Similarly, one's own dharma (duty/nature) becomes flawed if performed with ulterior motives.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनियां पार्था । हेतु सांडोनि सर्वथा । तुज क्षात्रवृत्ति झुंजतां। पाप नाहीं ॥ २५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauniyāṃ pārthā | hetu sāṃḍoni sarvathā | tuja kṣātravṛtti jhuṃjatāṃ| pāpa nāhīṃ || 25 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, completely abandoning all attachment, there is no sin for you in fighting according to your Kshatriya duty.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुखीं संतोषा न यावें। दुःखीं विषादा न भजावें। आणि लाभालाभ न धरावे । मनामाजीं ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: sukhīṃ saṃtoṣā na yāveṃ| duḥkhīṃ viṣādā na bhajāveṃ| āṇi lābhālābha na dharāve | manāmājīṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: In happiness, do not be overjoyed; in sorrow, do not be disheartened. And do not hold onto gain or loss in your mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ विजयपण होईल। कां सर्वथा देह जाईल। हें आधींचि कांहीं पुढील। चिंतावें ना॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha vijayapaṇa hoīla| kāṃ sarvathā deha jāīla| heṃ ādhīṃci kāṃhīṃ puḍhīla| ciṃtāveṃ nā|| 27||
verses.meaning: Whether victory will be achieved here, or if the body will perish completely, why should one worry about this future outcome beforehand?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपणयां उचिता । स्वधर्म राहाटतां। जें पावे तें निवांता । साहोनि जावें ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaṇayāṃ ucitā | svadharma rāhāṭatāṃ| jeṃ pāve teṃ nivāṃtā | sāhoni jāveṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: When one lives according to their own dharma, whatever comes their way, they should calmly endure it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसियां मनें होआवें। तरी दोषु न घडे स्वभावें । म्हणौनि आतां झुंजावें। निश्रांत तुवां ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyāṃ maneṃ hoāveṃ| tarī doṣu na ghaḍe svabhāveṃ | mhaṇauni ātāṃ jhuṃjāveṃ| niśrāṃta tuvāṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: If the mind becomes like this, then naturally no fault occurs. Therefore, now you must fight without doubt.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे सांख्यस्थिति मुकुळित। सांगितळी तुज येथ। आतां बुब्दियोगु निश्चित । अवधारीं पां॥ २३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: he sāṃkhyasthiti mukuḻita| sāṃgitaḻī tuja yetha| ātāṃ bubdiyogu niścita | avadhārīṃ pāṃ|| 230||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, I have thus explained to you the path of Sankhya (knowledge) in a concise form. Now, listen carefully to the path of Buddhi Yoga (the yoga of intellect).

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया बुद्धियुक्‍्ता। जाहलिया पार्था । कर्मबंधु सर्वथा । बाधूं न पवे॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā buddhiyuk‍tā| jāhaliyā pārthā | karmabaṃdhu sarvathā | bādhūṃ na pave|| 39||
verses.meaning: O Partha, for those endowed with such intellect, the bonds of karma can never truly affect them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें वज़्रकवच लेइजे। मग शस्त्रांचा वर्षाबो साहिजे। परी जैतेसीं उरिजे। अचुंबित ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ vaj़rakavaca leije| maga śastrāṃcā varṣābo sāhije| parī jaitesīṃ urije| acuṃbita || 32||
verses.meaning: Just as one dons an armor of diamond, and then endures a shower of weapons, yet remains untouched and victorious.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ऐहिक तरी न नशे। आणि मोश्षु तो उरला असे। जेथ पुर्वानुक्रमु दिसे। चोखाळत॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ aihika tarī na naśe| āṇi mośṣu to uralā ase| jetha purvānukramu dise| cokhāḻata|| 33||
verses.meaning: Similarly, worldly life does not perish, and liberation remains, where the sequence of past actions is clearly seen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कर्माधारें राहाटिजे। परी कर्मफळ न निरीक्षिजे। जैसा मंत्रज्ञु न बाधिजे। भूतबाधा ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: karmādhāreṃ rāhāṭije| parī karmaphaḻa na nirīkṣije| jaisā maṃtrajñu na bādhije| bhūtabādhā || 34||
verses.meaning: One should act according to their karma, but not anticipate the fruits of those actions, just as a master of mantras is not afflicted by ghosts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियापरी जे सुबुट्धि । आपुलालिया निरवधि। हा असतांचि उपाधि) आकळूं न सके॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyāparī je subuṭdhi | āpulāliyā niravadhi| hā asatāṃci upādhi) ākaḻūṃ na sake|| 35||
verses.meaning: In the same way, those with good intellect, despite their endless efforts, cannot grasp this (the Self) while it is still associated with the limiting adjuncts (upadhis).

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ न संचरे पुण्यपाप। जें सूक्ष्म अति निष्कंप। गुणत्रयादि लेप। न लगती जेथ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha na saṃcare puṇyapāpa| jeṃ sūkṣma ati niṣkaṃpa| guṇatrayādi lepa| na lagatī jetha|| 36||
verses.meaning: Where there is no accumulation of merit or demerit, which is exceedingly subtle and unwavering, and where the stains of the three gunas and other impurities do not adhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना तें पुण्यबशें । जरी अल्पचि हृदयीं बुद्धि प्रकाशे । तरी अशेषही नाशे । संसारभय॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā teṃ puṇyabaśeṃ | jarī alpaci hṛdayīṃ buddhi prakāśe | tarī aśeṣahī nāśe | saṃsārabhaya|| 37||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, by the power of such merit, even if a small spark of wisdom illuminates the heart, all fear of worldly existence is destroyed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी दीपकळिका धाकुटी। परी बहु तेजातें प्रगटी । तैसी सदबुन्यि हे थेकुटी। म्हणों नये॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī dīpakaḻikā dhākuṭī| parī bahu tejāteṃ pragaṭī | taisī sadabunyi he thekuṭī| mhaṇoṃ naye|| 38||
verses.meaning: Just as a tiny lamp wick reveals immense light, so too, one should not dismiss a good intellect as insignificant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था बहुतीं परी। हे अपेक्षिजे विचारशूरीं । जे दुर्लभ चराचरीं । सद्ठासना ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā bahutīṃ parī| he apekṣije vicāraśūrīṃ | je durlabha carācarīṃ | sadṭhāsanā || 39 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this very seat of true existence is desired by the wise, for it is rare in all creation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिकासारिखा बहुवसु। जैसा न जोडे परिसु। कां अमृताचा लेशु। दैवगुणें ॥ २४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇikāsārikhā bahuvasu| jaisā na joḍe parisu| kāṃ amṛtācā leśu| daivaguṇeṃ || 240||
verses.meaning: Like a philosopher's stone, which is not easily found, or a drop of nectar, obtained by divine grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी दुर्लभ जे सदबुन्दि। जिये परमात्माचि अबधि। जैसा गंगेसी उदधि। निरंतर॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī durlabha je sadabundi| jiye paramātmāci abadhi| jaisā gaṃgesī udadhi| niraṃtara|| 49||
verses.meaning: Similarly, rare is good intellect, for which the Supreme Soul is the ultimate limit, just as the ocean is the continuous destination for the Ganges.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ईश्‍वरावांचुनी कांहीं । जिये आणीक लाणी नाहीं। ते एकचि बुद्धि पाहीं । अर्जुना जगीं ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ īś‍varāvāṃcunī kāṃhīṃ | jiye āṇīka lāṇī nāhīṃ| te ekaci buddhi pāhīṃ | arjunā jagīṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: Just as there is nothing else besides God, there is no other gain; that alone is the true understanding, Arjuna, in this world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरी ते दुर्मति।॥ जे बहुधा असे विकरती। तेथ निरंतर रमती। अविवेकिये॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerī te durmati||| je bahudhā ase vikaratī| tetha niraṃtara ramatī| avivekiye|| 43||
verses.meaning: On the other hand, those who are foolish constantly delight in such evil thoughts that are mostly distorted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तयां पार्था । स्वर्ग संसार नरकावस्था ( स्वर्गसंसारी आस्था )। आत्मसुख सर्वथा । दृष्ट नाहीं ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tayāṃ pārthā | svarga saṃsāra narakāvasthā ( svargasaṃsārī āsthā )| ātmasukha sarvathā | dṛṣṭa nāhīṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for them, O Partha, the states of heaven, worldly existence, or hell, and the bliss of the Self, are never perceived.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वेदाधारें बोळती। केवळ कर्म प्रतिष्ठिती। परी कर्मफळीं आसक्ती । धरूनियां ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: vedādhāreṃ boḻatī| kevaḻa karma pratiṣṭhitī| parī karmaphaḻīṃ āsaktī | dharūniyāṃ || 45||
verses.meaning: They speak based on the Vedas, establishing only action, but holding on to attachment to the fruits of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणती संसारीं जन्मिजे। यज्ञादिक कर्म कीजे ।॥ मग स्वर्गसुख भोगिजे। मनोहर॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇatī saṃsārīṃ janmije| yajñādika karma kīje ||| maga svargasukha bhogije| manohara|| 46||
verses.meaning: They say that one is born into the world, performs sacrifices and other rituals, and then enjoys the delightful pleasures of heaven.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ हेंबांचूनि कांहीं । आणिक सर्वथा सुखचि नाहीं। ऐसें अर्जुना बोलती पाहीं । दुर्बुद्धि ते॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha heṃbāṃcūni kāṃhīṃ | āṇika sarvathā sukhaci nāhīṃ| aiseṃ arjunā bolatī pāhīṃ | durbuddhi te|| 47||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, those with evil intellects say that there is no happiness at all in this world without sense objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें 'कामनाअभिभूत । होऊनि कर्मे आचरत । ते केवळ भोगीं चित्त । देऊनियां॥ ४८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ 'kāmanāabhibhūta | hoūni karme ācarata | te kevaḻa bhogīṃ citta | deūniyāṃ|| 48 ||
verses.meaning: Beholding this, those who are overwhelmed by desires perform actions, their minds solely focused on worldly enjoyments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ४२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी क्रियाविशेषें बहुतें। न लोपिती विधीतें। निपुण होऊन धर्मातें। अनुष्ठिती ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: 42 śrījñāneśvarī kriyāviśeṣeṃ bahuteṃ| na lopitī vidhīteṃ| nipuṇa hoūna dharmāteṃ| anuṣṭhitī || 49||
verses.meaning: The Dnyaneshwari states that those who are adept in performing actions, even many of them, do not neglect their prescribed duties. Instead, they skillfully and diligently follow the path of Dharma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी एकचि कुडें करिती। जे स्वर्गकामु मनीं धरिती । यज्ञपुर्षा चुकती । भोक्ता जो॥ २५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī ekaci kuḍeṃ karitī| je svargakāmu manīṃ dharitī | yajñapurṣā cukatī | bhoktā jo|| 250||
verses.meaning: But those who desire heaven in their minds perform only one kind of action, thereby missing the enjoyer of sacrifices.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा कर्पूराचा राशी कीजे। मग अग्नि लाऊन दीजे । कां मिष्टान्नीं संचरविजे। काळकूट ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā karpūrācā rāśī kīje| maga agni lāūna dīje | kāṃ miṣṭānnīṃ saṃcaravije| kāḻakūṭa || 51||
verses.meaning: Just as a heap of camphor is set ablaze, or a sweet dish is infused with deadly poison.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दैवें अमृतकुंभ जोडला । तो पायें हाणोनि उलंडिला। तैसा नासिती धर्मु निपजला। हेतुकपणें ॥५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: daiveṃ amṛtakuṃbha joḍalā | to pāyeṃ hāṇoni ulaṃḍilā| taisā nāsitī dharmu nipajalā| hetukapaṇeṃ ||52||
verses.meaning: It is like someone who, by fate, found a pot of ambrosia, but then kicked and overturned it. Similarly, they destroy the Dharma that has arisen, due to their self-serving motives.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सायासें पुण्य अर्जिजे। मग संसारु कां अपेक्षिजे। परी नेणती ते काय कौजे। अप्राप्य देखें ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāyāseṃ puṇya arjije| maga saṃsāru kāṃ apekṣije| parī neṇatī te kāya kauje| aprāpya dekheṃ || 53||
verses.meaning: If merit is accumulated with great effort, why then desire worldly existence? But those who do not know, what do they understand? They see it as unattainable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी रांधबणी रससोय निकी । करूनियां मोलें बिकी। तैसा भोगासाठीं अविवेकी । धाडिती धर्मु॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī rāṃdhabaṇī rasasoya nikī | karūniyāṃ moleṃ bikī| taisā bhogāsāṭhīṃ avivekī | dhāḍitī dharmu|| 54||
verses.meaning: Just as a skilled cook prepares delicious dishes and sells them for a price, so too do the unwise sacrifice dharma for the sake of enjoyment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि हे पार्था । दुर्बुद्धधि देख सर्वथा । तयां वेदवादरतां। मनीं वसे ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni he pārthā | durbuddhadhi dekha sarvathā | tayāṃ vedavādaratāṃ| manīṃ vase || 55||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Partha, this evil intellect always resides in the minds of those who are engrossed in the doctrines of the Vedas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिन्हीं गुणीं आवृत। हे वेद जाणें निश्रांत । म्हणोनि उपनिषदादि समस्त । सात्त्विक तें ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tinhīṃ guṇīṃ āvṛta| he veda jāṇeṃ niśrāṃta | mhaṇoni upaniṣadādi samasta | sāttvika teṃ || 56||
verses.meaning: The Vedas, being enveloped by the three Gunas, are understood to be entirely sattvic, as are all the Upanishads and other scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येर रजतमात्मक । जेथ निरूपिजे कर्मादिक। जे केवळ स्वर्गसूचक । धनुर्धरा ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yera rajatamātmaka | jetha nirūpije karmādika| je kevaḻa svargasūcaka | dhanurdharā || 57||
verses.meaning: The other path, which is of the nature of Rajas and Tamas, describes actions and their results, which merely point towards heavenly pleasures, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तूं जाण । हे सुखदुःखांसीच कारण । एथ झणें अंतःकरण रिगों देसी॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tūṃ jāṇa | he sukhaduḥkhāṃsīca kāraṇa | etha jhaṇeṃ aṃtaḥkaraṇa rigoṃ desī|| 58||
verses.meaning: Therefore, know this: these (pleasure and pain) are indeed the cause (of entanglement). Do not let your inner self get caught up in them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं गुणत्रयातें अव्हेरीं। मी माझें हें न करीं॥ एक आत्मसुख अंतरीं । विसंब झणीं॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ guṇatrayāteṃ avherīṃ| mī mājheṃ heṃ na karīṃ|| eka ātmasukha aṃtarīṃ | visaṃba jhaṇīṃ|| 59||
verses.meaning: Discard the three gunas. Do not claim 'I' and 'mine'. Rely solely on the inner bliss of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी वेदें बहुत बोलिलें। विविध भेद सूचिळे। तऱही आपण हित आपुलें। तेंचि घेपें॥ २६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī vedeṃ bahuta bolileṃ| vividha bheda sūciḻe| taṟahī āpaṇa hita āpuleṃ| teṃci ghepeṃ|| 260||
verses.meaning: Though the Vedas speak extensively and reveal various distinctions, one should still embrace that which is beneficial for oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा प्रगटलिया गभस्ती । अशेषही मार्ग दिसती । तरी तेतुलेही काय चालिजती। सांगैं मज॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā pragaṭaliyā gabhastī | aśeṣahī mārga disatī | tarī tetulehī kāya cālijatī| sāṃgaiṃ maja|| 61||
verses.meaning: Just as when the sun rises, countless paths become visible, but tell me, how many of them are actually walked upon?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां उदकमय सकळ। जऱ्ही जाहलें असे महीतळ। तरी आपण घेपें केवळ। आर्तीचिजोगें ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ udakamaya sakaḻa| jaṟhī jāhaleṃ ase mahītaḻa| tarī āpaṇa ghepeṃ kevaḻa| ārtīcijogeṃ || 62||
verses.meaning: Even if the entire earth were to become filled with water, one would only take as much as one needs to quench their thirst.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ज्ञानीये जे होती । ते वेदार्थातें विवरिती। मग अपेक्षित तें स्वीकारिती। शाश्‍वत जें॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jñānīye je hotī | te vedārthāteṃ vivaritī| maga apekṣita teṃ svīkāritī| śāś‍vata jeṃ|| 63||
verses.meaning: Just as the wise ones, they expound the meaning of the Vedas. Then they accept that which is desired, that which is eternal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आईकें पार्था । याचिपरी पाहातां। तुज उचित होय आतां|। स्वकर्म हें ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni āīkeṃ pārthā | yāciparī pāhātāṃ| tuja ucita hoya ātāṃ|| svakarma heṃ || 64||
verses.meaning: Therefore, listen, Partha, considering this, your own duty is now appropriate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आम्हीं समस्तही विचारिलें। तंव ऐसेंचि हें मना आलें। जें न सांडिजे तुवां आपुलें। विहित कर्म ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āmhīṃ samastahī vicārileṃ| taṃva aiseṃci heṃ manā āleṃ| jeṃ na sāṃḍije tuvāṃ āpuleṃ| vihita karma || 65||
verses.meaning: We have considered everything, and this is what came to mind: that you should not abandon your prescribed duties.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी कर्मफळीं आस न करावी) आणि कुकर्मी संगति न व्हावी। हे सत्क्रियाचि आचरावी। हेतूविण॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī karmaphaḻīṃ āsa na karāvī) āṇi kukarmī saṃgati na vhāvī| he satkriyāci ācarāvī| hetūviṇa|| 66||
verses.meaning: One should not desire the fruits of action, nor should one associate with evil deeds. One should perform good deeds without any ulterior motive.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं योगयुक्‍्त होऊनी। फळाचा संग टाकुनी । मग अर्जुना चित्त देउनी । करीं कर्मे ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ yogayuk‍ta hoūnī| phaḻācā saṃga ṭākunī | maga arjunā citta deunī | karīṃ karme || 67||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, being united with Yoga, abandoning attachment to the fruits of action, then with a focused mind, perform your actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी आदरिलें कर्म दैवें। जरी समाप्तीतें पावे। तरी विशेषें तेथ तोषावें। हेंही नको॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī ādarileṃ karma daiveṃ| jarī samāptīteṃ pāve| tarī viśeṣeṃ tetha toṣāveṃ| heṃhī nako|| 68||
verses.meaning: Even if a task undertaken by chance reaches completion, there is no need to be especially pleased by it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं निमित्ते कोणें एकें। तें सिद्धी न बचतां ठाके । तरी तेथिंचेनि अपरितोखें। क्षोभावें ना॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ nimitte koṇeṃ ekeṃ| teṃ siddhī na bacatāṃ ṭhāke | tarī tethiṃceni aparitokheṃ| kṣobhāveṃ nā|| 69||
verses.meaning: If, for some reason, that (action) does not come to fruition, then one should not be disturbed by that dissatisfaction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आचरतां सिद्धी गेलें तरी काजाची कीर आलें। परी ठेलियाही सगुण जहाळें। ऐसेंचि मानीं॥ २७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ācaratāṃ siddhī geleṃ tarī kājācī kīra āleṃ| parī ṭheliyāhī saguṇa jahāḻeṃ| aiseṃci mānīṃ|| 270||
verses.meaning: Even if one attains perfection through practice, it is indeed beneficial. But even if one remains in the realm of the manifest, consider it equally significant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें जेतुलालें कर्म निपजे। तेतुलें आदिपुरुषीं अर्पिजे। तरी परिपूर्ण सहजें । जहाळें जाणें ॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ jetulāleṃ karma nipaje| tetuleṃ ādipuruṣīṃ arpije| tarī paripūrṇa sahajeṃ | jahāḻeṃ jāṇeṃ || 71||
verses.meaning: Understand that whatever action is performed, if it is offered to the Primordial Being, then it naturally becomes complete.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें संतासंत कर्मी । हें जें सरिसेपण मनोधर्मी । तेचि योगस्थिति उत्तमीं। प्रशंसिजे ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ saṃtāsaṃta karmī | heṃ jeṃ sarisepaṇa manodharmī | teci yogasthiti uttamīṃ| praśaṃsije || 72||
verses.meaning: Behold, the equanimity of mind that perceives saints and sinners, or good and bad actions, as equal, that indeed is the highest state of Yoga, and is highly praised.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना समत्व चित्ताचें। तेंचि सार जाणें योगाचें।॥ जेथ मन आणि बुद्धीचें। ऐक्य आथी ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā samatva cittāceṃ| teṃci sāra jāṇeṃ yogāceṃ||| jetha mana āṇi buddhīceṃ| aikya āthī || 73||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, the equanimity of the mind is indeed the essence of Yoga, where the mind and intellect become one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो बुऱ्दियोग विवरितां। बहुतें पाडें पार्था । दिसे हा अरुता। कर्मयोगु॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: to buṟdiyoga vivaritāṃ| bahuteṃ pāḍeṃ pārthā | dise hā arutā| karmayogu|| 74||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, when that profound yoga is explained, this path of action (Karma Yoga) appears to be very easy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तेंचि कर्म आचरिजे। तरीच हा योगु पाविजे । जें कर्मशेष सहजें । योगस्थिति ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teṃci karma ācarije| tarīca hā yogu pāvije | jeṃ karmaśeṣa sahajeṃ | yogasthiti || 75 ||
verses.meaning: Only by performing such actions can one attain this yoga, where the residual effect of action naturally leads to the state of yoga.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि बुल्धियोगु सधरु । तेथ अर्जुना होई स्थिरु । मनें करीं अव्हेर । फलहेतूचा ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni buldhiyogu sadharu | tetha arjunā hoī sthiru | maneṃ karīṃ avhera | phalahetūcā || 76||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, be steadfast in the intellect of yoga. With your mind, reject the desire for the fruits of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे बुन्दियोगा योजिळे। तेचि पारंगत जाहले । इहीं उभयबंधीं सांडिले। पापपुण्यीं ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: je bundiyogā yojiḻe| teci pāraṃgata jāhale | ihīṃ ubhayabaṃdhīṃ sāṃḍile| pāpapuṇyīṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: Those who have engaged in the yoga of intellect have become adept. They have transcended both good and bad deeds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: डड श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी ते कर्मी तरी वर्तती। परी कर्मफळा नातळती। आणि यातायाति न 'लोपती । अर्जुना तयां ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ḍaḍa śrījñāneśvarī te karmī tarī vartatī| parī karmaphaḻā nātaḻatī| āṇi yātāyāti na 'lopatī | arjunā tayāṃ || 78||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, those who act in this way, though engaged in actions, are not touched by the fruits of their actions, nor do they become entangled in the cycle of birth and death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग निरामयभरित। पावती पद अच्युत ते बुन्दियोगयुक्‍्त । धनुर्धरा ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga nirāmayabharita| pāvatī pada acyuta te bundiyogayuk‍ta | dhanurdharā || 79||
verses.meaning: Then, filled with perfect health, they attain the imperishable state, those who are united with the intellect, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं ऐसा तैं होसी । जैं मोहातें यया सांडिसी। आणि वैराग्य मानसीं । संचरेलळ॥ २८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ aisā taiṃ hosī | jaiṃ mohāteṃ yayā sāṃḍisī| āṇi vairāgya mānasīṃ | saṃcarelaḻa|| 280||
verses.meaning: You will become such (realize your true nature) when you abandon this delusion, and detachment takes root in your mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग निष्कळंक गहन। उपजेल आत्मज्ञान। तेणें निचाडें होईल मन। अपैसें तुझें ॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga niṣkaḻaṃka gahana| upajela ātmajñāna| teṇeṃ nicāḍeṃ hoīla mana| apaiseṃ tujheṃ || 81||
verses.meaning: Then, a pure and profound self-knowledge will arise, by which your mind will naturally become steadfast.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ आणिक कांहीं जाणावें। कां मागिलातें स्मरावें। हें अर्जुना आघवें। पारुषेळ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha āṇika kāṃhīṃ jāṇāveṃ| kāṃ māgilāteṃ smarāveṃ| heṃ arjunā āghaveṃ| pāruṣeḻa|| 82||
verses.meaning: There, Arjuna, all other knowledge, or remembrance of the past, will cease.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियांचिया संगति। जिये पसरु होतसे मती । ते स्थिर होईल मागुती । आत्मस्वरूपीं ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyāṃciyā saṃgati| jiye pasaru hotase matī | te sthira hoīla māgutī | ātmasvarūpīṃ || 83||
verses.meaning: The intellect, which is dispersed by the company of the senses, will again become steady in the form of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: समाधिसुखीं केवळ। जें बुद्धि होईल निश्चळ] तैं पावसी तूं सकळ। योगस्थिति॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: samādhisukhīṃ kevaḻa| jeṃ buddhi hoīla niścaḻa] taiṃ pāvasī tūṃ sakaḻa| yogasthiti|| 84||
verses.meaning: When your intellect becomes completely steady in the bliss of samadhi, then you will attain the complete state of yoga.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ अर्जुन म्हणे देवा। हाचि अभिप्राबो आघवा। मी पुसेन आतां सांगावा । कृपानिधी ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha arjuna mhaṇe devā| hāci abhiprābo āghavā| mī pusena ātāṃ sāṃgāvā | kṛpānidhī || 85 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna then said, "O Lord, this is my entire intention. I will now ask, please tell me, O ocean of compassion."

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग अच्युत म्हणे सुखें । जें किरीटी तुज निकें । तें पूस पां उन्मेखें। मनाचेनि॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga acyuta mhaṇe sukheṃ | jeṃ kirīṭī tuja nikeṃ | teṃ pūsa pāṃ unmekheṃ| manāceni|| 86||
verses.meaning: Then Achyuta (Krishna) said, "O Kiriti (Arjuna), whatever is good for you, ask that with an awakened mind."

verses.shloka_devanagari: या बोला पार्थे । म्हणितलें सांग पां श्रीकृष्णातें। काय म्हणिपें स्थितप्रज्ञाते। बोळखों केवीं ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā bolā pārthe | mhaṇitaleṃ sāṃga pāṃ śrīkṛṣṇāteṃ| kāya mhaṇipeṃ sthitaprajñāte| boḻakhoṃ kevīṃ || 87||
verses.meaning: Upon hearing these words, Partha (Arjuna) asked Shri Krishna, "What is meant by a 'man of steady wisdom' (Sthitaprajna)? How can one recognize such a person?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि स्थिरबुट्धि जो म्हणिजे। तो कैसिया चिन्हीं जाणिजे। जो समाधिसुख भुंजे। अखंडित॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi sthirabuṭdhi jo mhaṇije| to kaisiyā cinhīṃ jāṇije| jo samādhisukha bhuṃje| akhaṃḍita|| 88||
verses.meaning: And how is one to recognize the person who is said to have a steady intellect? It is he who continuously enjoys the bliss of samadhi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो कवणें स्थिती असे। कैसेनि रूपीं विलसे। देवा सांगावें हें ऐसें । लक्ष्मीपती ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: to kavaṇeṃ sthitī ase| kaiseni rūpīṃ vilase| devā sāṃgāveṃ heṃ aiseṃ | lakṣmīpatī || 89 ||
verses.meaning: O Lord of Lakshmi, please tell me, in what state does He exist? In what form does He manifest?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब परब्रह्म अबतरणु | जो षड्गुणाधिकरणु । तो काय तेथ नारायणु। बोलतु असे॥ २९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba parabrahma abataraṇu | jo ṣaḍguṇādhikaraṇu | to kāya tetha nārāyaṇu| bolatu ase|| 290||
verses.meaning: The Supreme Brahman, who is the abode of the six divine attributes, has descended. What is it that Narayana speaks there?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे अर्जुना परियेसीं। जो हा अभिलाषु प्रौढ मानसीं । तो अंतराय स्वसुखेंसीं। करीतु असे॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe arjunā pariyesīṃ| jo hā abhilāṣu prauḍha mānasīṃ | to aṃtarāya svasukheṃsīṃ| karītu ase|| 91||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, listen. This strong desire in the mind creates an obstacle to one's own true happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो सर्वदा नित्यतृप्तु। अंतःकरण भरितु। परी विषयामाजीं पतितु। जेणें संगे कीजे॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo sarvadā nityatṛptu| aṃtaḥkaraṇa bharitu| parī viṣayāmājīṃ patitu| jeṇeṃ saṃge kīje|| 92||
verses.meaning: One who is ever content, whose inner being is full, yet falls into worldly attachments due to association.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो कामु सर्वथा जाये। जयाचें आत्मतोषीं मन राहे। तोचि स्थितप्रज्ञु होये । पुरुष जाणें ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: to kāmu sarvathā jāye| jayāceṃ ātmatoṣīṃ mana rāhe| toci sthitaprajñu hoye | puruṣa jāṇeṃ || 93||
verses.meaning: When one's mind finds contentment in the Self, all desires completely vanish. Such a person is indeed known as a man of steady wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना दुःखीं प्राप्तीं। जयासी उद्देगु नाहीं चित्तीं। आणि सुखाचिया आरती । अडपैजेना॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā duḥkhīṃ prāptīṃ| jayāsī uddegu nāhīṃ cittīṃ| āṇi sukhāciyā āratī | aḍapaijenā|| 94||
verses.meaning: One who, amidst various sorrows and adversities, does not feel agitation in their mind, and is not swayed by the allure of happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना तयाच्या ठायीं । कामक्रोधु सहजें नाहीं । आणि भवयातें नेणें कहीं । परिपूर्णु तो॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā tayācyā ṭhāyīṃ | kāmakrodhu sahajeṃ nāhīṃ | āṇi bhavayāteṃ neṇeṃ kahīṃ | paripūrṇu to|| 95||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, in such a person, desire and anger are naturally absent. And they do not know the cycle of birth and death anywhere; they are complete.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा जो निरवधि। तो जाण पां स्थिरबुद्धि।॥ जो निरसूनि उपाधि। भेदरहितु ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jo niravadhi| to jāṇa pāṃ sthirabuddhi||| jo nirasūni upādhi| bhedarahitu || 96||
verses.meaning: Know that one to be of steady intellect who, being boundless, transcends all limitations and is free from all distinctions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो सर्वत्र सदा सरिसा। परिपूर्णु चंद्रु कां जैसा । अधमोत्तम प्रकाशा-। माजीं न म्हणे॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo sarvatra sadā sarisā| paripūrṇu caṃdru kāṃ jaisā | adhamottama prakāśā-| mājīṃ na mhaṇe|| 97||
verses.meaning: Just as the full moon shines equally everywhere, without distinguishing between high and low, so too is the Divine, ever-present and impartial.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी अनवच्छिन्न समता । भूतमात्रीं सदयता। आणि 'पालटु नाहीं चित्ता। कवणें वेळे॥९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī anavacchinna samatā | bhūtamātrīṃ sadayatā| āṇi 'pālaṭu nāhīṃ cittā| kavaṇeṃ veḻe||98||
verses.meaning: Such unbroken equanimity, compassion towards all beings, and a mind that never changes at any time.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गोमटें कांहीं पावे। तरी संतोषें तेणें नाभिभवे। जो बोखटेनि नागवे। विषादासी॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: gomaṭeṃ kāṃhīṃ pāve| tarī saṃtoṣeṃ teṇeṃ nābhibhave| jo bokhaṭeni nāgave| viṣādāsī|| 99||
verses.meaning: If something good comes his way, he is not overwhelmed by that joy. And if something bad happens, he is not overcome by sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा 'हरिखशोकरहितु। जो आत्मबोधभरितु। तो जाण पां प्रज्ञायुक्‍्तु। धनुर्धरा ॥ ३०० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā 'harikhaśokarahitu| jo ātmabodhabharitu| to jāṇa pāṃ prajñāyuk‍tu| dhanurdharā || 300 ||
verses.meaning: Such a person, free from joy and sorrow, filled with self-realization, know him to be endowed with wisdom, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां कूर्म जियापरी। उबाइला अवेव पसरी। ना तरी इच्छावशें आवरी । आपुळे आपण॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ kūrma jiyāparī| ubāilā aveva pasarī| nā tarī icchāvaśeṃ āvarī | āpuḻe āpaṇa|| 1||
verses.meaning: Just as a tortoise, at its will, extends its limbs and then, by its own desire, withdraws them within itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं इंद्रियें आपैतीं होती । जयाचें म्हणितलें करिती । तयाची प्रज्ञा जाण स्थिति। पातळी असे॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ iṃdriyeṃ āpaitīṃ hotī | jayāceṃ mhaṇitaleṃ karitī | tayācī prajñā jāṇa sthiti| pātaḻī ase|| 2||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the senses come under the control of one whose commands they obey. Know that such a person's intellect has attained stability.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ४६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी अर्जुना आणिकही एक । सांगेन ऐकें कवतिक । या विषयांते साधक । त्यजिती नियमें ॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: 46 śrījñāneśvarī arjunā āṇikahī eka | sāṃgena aikeṃ kavatika | yā viṣayāṃte sādhaka | tyajitī niyameṃ || 3||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, listen to another wonder I will tell you. Ascetics renounce these worldly pleasures through discipline.

verses.shloka_devanagari: श्रोत्रादि इंद्रियें आवरिती। परि रसने नियमु न करिती । ते सहस्त्रधा कवळिजती। विषयीं इहीं ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: śrotrādi iṃdriyeṃ āvaritī| pari rasane niyamu na karitī | te sahastradhā kavaḻijatī| viṣayīṃ ihīṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: They control their senses like hearing, but they do not control their tongue. They are devoured a thousandfold by these worldly pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी वरिवरि पालवी खुडिजे। आणि मुळीं उदक घालिजे। तरी कैसेनि नाशु निपजे। तया वृक्षा॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī varivari pālavī khuḍije| āṇi muḻīṃ udaka ghālije| tarī kaiseni nāśu nipaje| tayā vṛkṣā|| 5||
verses.meaning: Just as a tree whose leaves are plucked from above, but whose roots are watered, how can such a tree be destroyed?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो उदकाचेनि बळें अधिकें। जैसा आडवेनि आंगें फांके। तैसा मानसीं विषो 'पोखे। रसनाद्वारें ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to udakāceni baḻeṃ adhikeṃ| jaisā āḍaveni āṃgeṃ phāṃke| taisā mānasīṃ viṣo 'pokhe| rasanādvāreṃ || 6||
verses.meaning: Just as water, with its increasing force, spreads out through a narrow opening, so too do worldly pleasures flourish in the mind through the gateway of the tongue.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरां इंद्रियां विषय तुटे। तैसा नियमूं न ये रस हटें। जे जीवन हें न घटे। येणेंबिण ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerāṃ iṃdriyāṃ viṣaya tuṭe| taisā niyamūṃ na ye rasa haṭeṃ| je jīvana heṃ na ghaṭe| yeṇeṃbiṇa || 7||
verses.meaning: While other senses may be restrained from their objects, the sense of taste cannot be forcibly controlled, for without it, life itself cannot be sustained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग अर्जुना स्वभावें। ऐसियाही नियमातें पावे। जैं परब्रह्म अनुभवें। होऊनि जाइजे॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga arjunā svabhāveṃ| aisiyāhī niyamāteṃ pāve| jaiṃ parabrahma anubhaveṃ| hoūni jāije|| 8||
verses.meaning: Then, Arjuna, by nature, one attains such a state of discipline when one becomes one with the experience of the Supreme Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें शरीरभाव नासती । इंद्रियें विषय विसरती। जें सोहंभावप्रतीति। प्रगट होय ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ śarīrabhāva nāsatī | iṃdriyeṃ viṣaya visaratī| jeṃ sohaṃbhāvapratīti| pragaṭa hoya || 9||
verses.meaning: Then the identification with the body ceases, the senses forget their objects, and the realization of "I am That" manifests.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येऱ्हबीं तरी अर्जुना। हें आया नये साधना। जे राहटताती जतना। निरंतर ॥ ३१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṟhabīṃ tarī arjunā| heṃ āyā naye sādhanā| je rāhaṭatātī jatanā| niraṃtara || 310||
verses.meaning: However, Arjuna, this (state) is not attained by those who are constantly striving with great effort.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयातें अभ्यासाची घरटी । यमनियमांची ताटी । जे मनातें सदा मुठी। धरूनि आहाती ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāteṃ abhyāsācī gharaṭī | yamaniyamāṃcī tāṭī | je manāteṃ sadā muṭhī| dharūni āhātī || 19||
verses.meaning: Those who have made a home in spiritual practice, who are protected by self-restraint and discipline, and who always hold their minds firmly in control.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेही किजती कासाविसी। या इंद्रियांची प्रौढी ऐसी । जैसी मंत्रज्ञातें बिवसी । भुलवी कां॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tehī kijatī kāsāvisī| yā iṃdriyāṃcī prauḍhī aisī | jaisī maṃtrajñāteṃ bivasī | bhulavī kāṃ|| 12||
verses.meaning: Even they (the wise) become distressed and agitated. Such is the power of these senses, just as a magician bewilders with his spells.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें विषय हे तैसे । पावती क्रस्द्विसि्धीचेनि मिषें। मग आकळिती स्पर्शे । इंद्रियांचेनी ॥ १३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ viṣaya he taise | pāvatī krasdvisidhīceni miṣeṃ| maga ākaḻitī sparśe | iṃdriyāṃcenī || 13 ||
verses.meaning: Just as these objects of the senses, through the pretext of the senses, are then grasped by touch, so too the spiritual experience is attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये संधीं मन जाये । मग अभ्यासीं ठोठावले ठाये। ऐसें बळकटपण आहे । इंद्रियांचे ॥९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye saṃdhīṃ mana jāye | maga abhyāsīṃ ṭhoṭhāvale ṭhāye| aiseṃ baḻakaṭapaṇa āhe | iṃdriyāṃce ||94||
verses.meaning: At such a juncture, the mind is drawn away, then it firmly settles in spiritual practice. Such is the strength of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आझकें पार्था । यांतें निर्टळी जो सर्वथा । सर्व विषयीं आस्था । सांडूनियां ॥ ९१५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni ājhakeṃ pārthā | yāṃteṃ nirṭaḻī jo sarvathā | sarva viṣayīṃ āsthā | sāṃḍūniyāṃ || 915||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Partha, whoever completely abandons all worldly desires and attachments, truly transcends them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोचि तूं जाण । योगनिष्ठेसी कारण । जयाचे विषयसुखें अंतःकरण । झकवेना॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: toci tūṃ jāṇa | yoganiṣṭhesī kāraṇa | jayāce viṣayasukheṃ aṃtaḥkaraṇa | jhakavenā|| 16||
verses.meaning: Know that such a person is indeed the cause of steadfastness in Yoga, one whose heart is not swayed by the pleasures of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो आत्मबोधयुक्‍्तु। होऊनि असे सततु। जो मातें हृदयाआंतु। विसंबेना॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo ātmabodhayuk‍tu| hoūni ase satatu| jo māteṃ hṛdayāāṃtu| visaṃbenā|| 17||
verses.meaning: One who is constantly united with the knowledge of the Self, and who never forgets Me within their heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येऱ्हवीं बाह्य विषय तरी नाहीं। परी मानसीं होईल जरी कांहीं । तरी साद्यंतुचि पाहीं । संसार असे॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṟhavīṃ bāhya viṣaya tarī nāhīṃ| parī mānasīṃ hoīla jarī kāṃhīṃ | tarī sādyaṃtuci pāhīṃ | saṃsāra ase|| 18||
verses.meaning: Even if external objects are not present, if they arise in the mind, then the entire worldly existence is present.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा कां विषाचा लेशु। घेतलियां होय बहुवसु। मग निभ्रांत करी नाशु। जीवितासी॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā kāṃ viṣācā leśu| ghetaliyāṃ hoya bahuvasu| maga nibhrāṃta karī nāśu| jīvitāsī|| 19||
verses.meaning: Just as a small trace of poison, when consumed, becomes abundant and then certainly destroys life.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी विषयाची शंका। मनीं वसती देखा। घातु करी अशेखा। विवेकजाता॥ ३२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī viṣayācī śaṃkā| manīṃ vasatī dekhā| ghātu karī aśekhā| vivekajātā|| 320||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the doubt of worldly pleasures, if it resides in the mind, destroys all spiritual wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी हृदयीं विषय स्मरती। तरी निसंगाही आपजे संगती । संगें प्रगटे मूर्ति। अभिलाषाची॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī hṛdayīṃ viṣaya smaratī| tarī nisaṃgāhī āpaje saṃgatī | saṃgeṃ pragaṭe mūrti| abhilāṣācī|| 21||
verses.meaning: Even if worldly desires are remembered in the heart, then even the detached one becomes associated with them. Through this association, the form of longing manifests.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ कामु उपजला । तेथ क्रोधु आधींचि आला । क्रोधीं असे ठेविला । संमोह जाणें ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha kāmu upajalā | tetha krodhu ādhīṃci ālā | krodhīṃ ase ṭhevilā | saṃmoha jāṇeṃ || 22||
verses.meaning: Where desire arises, anger has already arrived. Know that delusion is stored within that anger.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संमोहा जालिया व्यक्ति। तरी नाशु पावे स्मृति। चडवातें ज्योति। आहत जैसी॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃmohā jāliyā vyakti| tarī nāśu pāve smṛti| caḍavāteṃ jyoti| āhata jaisī|| 23||
verses.meaning: When delusion arises in a person, their memory is destroyed, just as a lamp's flame is extinguished by a strong wind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां अस्तमानीं निशी। जैसी सूर्य तेजातें ग्रासी। तैसी दशा स्मृतिभ्रंशीं । प्राणियांसी ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ astamānīṃ niśī| jaisī sūrya tejāteṃ grāsī| taisī daśā smṛtibhraṃśīṃ | prāṇiyāṃsī || 24||
verses.meaning: Just as night devours the sun's brilliance at dusk, so too does the loss of memory afflict living beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग अज्ञानांध केवळ। तेणें आप्लविजे सकळ। तेथ बुन्धि होय व्याकुळ । हृदयामाजीं ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ajñānāṃdha kevaḻa| teṇeṃ āplavije sakaḻa| tetha bundhi hoya vyākuḻa | hṛdayāmājīṃ || 25||
verses.meaning: Then, by that sheer darkness of ignorance, everything is enveloped. There, the intellect becomes distressed within the heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें जात्यंधा पळणीं पावे। मग ते काकुळती सैरा धांवे । तैसें बुद्धीसि होती भंवे। धनुर्धरा ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ jātyaṃdhā paḻaṇīṃ pāve| maga te kākuḻatī sairā dhāṃve | taiseṃ buddhīsi hotī bhaṃve| dhanurdharā || 26||
verses.meaning: Just as a person blind from birth, upon regaining sight, runs around frantically, so too does the intellect become bewildered, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा स्मृतिभ्रंशु घडे । मग सर्वथा बुद्धि अबघडे। तेथ समूळ हें उपडे। ज्ञानजात॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā smṛtibhraṃśu ghaḍe | maga sarvathā buddhi abaghaḍe| tetha samūḻa heṃ upaḍe| jñānajāta|| 27||
verses.meaning: When such a loss of memory occurs, then the intellect becomes completely impaired. There, this entire knowledge is uprooted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चैतन्याच्या भ्रंशीं। शरीरा दशा जैशी । तैसें पुरुषा बुऱ्धिनाशीं । होय देखें ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: caitanyācyā bhraṃśīṃ| śarīrā daśā jaiśī | taiseṃ puruṣā buṟdhināśīṃ | hoya dekheṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Just as the body becomes lifeless when consciousness departs, so too does a person become when their intellect is destroyed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आहकें अर्जुना। जैसा विस्फुलिंग लागे इंधना। मग तो प्रौढ जालिया त्रिभुवना। पुरों शके॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni āhakeṃ arjunā| jaisā visphuliṃga lāge iṃdhanā| maga to prauḍha jāliyā tribhuvanā| puroṃ śake|| 29||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, just as a spark ignites fuel, and then, when it grows, it can consume the three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें विषयांचें ध्यान। जरी विपायें वाहे मन । तरी येसणें हें पतन । गिंबवसित पावे॥ ३३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ viṣayāṃceṃ dhyāna| jarī vipāyeṃ vāhe mana | tarī yesaṇeṃ heṃ patana | giṃbavasita pāve|| 330||
verses.meaning: Similarly, if the mind happens to dwell on worldly pleasures, then such a downfall is certain to occur.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि विषय हे आघवे । सर्वथा मनौनि सांडावे । मग रागद्वेष स्वभावें । नाशतीळ॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni viṣaya he āghave | sarvathā manauni sāṃḍāve | maga rāgadveṣa svabhāveṃ | nāśatīḻa|| 31||
verses.meaning: Therefore, all these worldly objects should be completely abandoned from the mind. Then, attachment and aversion will naturally perish.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था आणिकही एक। जरी नाशले रागद्वेष। तरी इंद्रियां विषयीं बाधक । रमतां नाहीं॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā āṇikahī eka| jarī nāśale rāgadveṣa| tarī iṃdriyāṃ viṣayīṃ bādhaka | ramatāṃ nāhīṃ|| 32||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, there is yet another thing: even if attachment and aversion are destroyed, the senses are not harmed by indulging in their objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा सूर्य आकाशगतु। रश्मिकरें जगातें स्पर्शतु। तरी संगदोषें काय लिंपतु । तेथिचेनि ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā sūrya ākāśagatu| raśmikareṃ jagāteṃ sparśatu| tarī saṃgadoṣeṃ kāya liṃpatu | tethiceni || 33||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun, situated in the sky, touches the world with its rays, yet is not tainted by the contact, so too is the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा इंद्रियार्थी उदासीन । आत्मरसेंचि निर्थिन्न। जो कामक्रोधविहीन । होऊनि असे॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā iṃdriyārthī udāsīna | ātmaraseṃci nirthinna| jo kāmakrodhavihīna | hoūni ase|| 34||
verses.meaning: Just as one who is indifferent to sensory objects, being immersed in the bliss of the Self, becomes devoid of desire and anger.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी विषयां तयां कांहीं । आपणपेंवांचूनि नाहीं । मग विषय कवण कायी । ४८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी बाधितीळ कवणा ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī viṣayāṃ tayāṃ kāṃhīṃ | āpaṇapeṃvāṃcūni nāhīṃ | maga viṣaya kavaṇa kāyī | 48 śrījñāneśvarī bādhitīḻa kavaṇā || 35||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for them, there is nothing apart from their own Self. So, what objects of the senses could possibly trouble whom?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी उदकीं उदक बुडिजे। कां अग्नि आगी 'पोळिजे। तरी विषयसंगें आप्लविजे। परिपूर्णु तो॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī udakīṃ udaka buḍije| kāṃ agni āgī 'poḻije| tarī viṣayasaṃgeṃ āplavije| paripūrṇu to|| 36||
verses.meaning: Just as water cannot drown water, nor fire burn fire, so too the all-pervading, perfect Self cannot be affected by worldly attachments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा आपणचि केवळु। होऊनि असे निखळु। तयाची प्रज्ञा अचळु । निभ्रांत मानीं ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā āpaṇaci kevaḻu| hoūni ase nikhaḻu| tayācī prajñā acaḻu | nibhrāṃta mānīṃ || 37||
verses.meaning: Understand this for certain: one who becomes purely and completely one with the Self, their intellect becomes unwavering.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें अखंडित प्रसन्नता । आथी जेथ चित्ता । तेथ रिगणें नाहीं समस्तां । संसारदुःखां॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ akhaṃḍita prasannatā | āthī jetha cittā | tetha rigaṇeṃ nāhīṃ samastāṃ | saṃsāraduḥkhāṃ|| 38||
verses.meaning: Where the mind experiences unbroken joy, there is no entry for all worldly sorrows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा अमृताचा निर्झरु। प्रसवे जयाचा जठरु। तया क्षुधेतेषेचा अडदरु। कहींचि नाहीं ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā amṛtācā nirjharu| prasave jayācā jaṭharu| tayā kṣudheteṣecā aḍadaru| kahīṃci nāhīṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: Just as a spring of nectar, whose belly gives birth to it, never experiences the pangs of hunger.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें हृदय प्रसन्न होये। तरी दुःख कैचें कें आहे। तेथ आपैसी बुग्ि राहे । परमात्मरूपीं ॥ ३४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ hṛdaya prasanna hoye| tarī duḥkha kaiceṃ keṃ āhe| tetha āpaisī bugi rāhe | paramātmarūpīṃ || 340||
verses.meaning: When the heart becomes joyful, where then can sorrow exist? There, the intellect naturally abides in the form of the Supreme Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा निर्बातीचा दीपु। सर्वथा नेणे कंपु। तैसा स्थिरबुऱ्यि स्वस्वरूपु। योगयुक्तु ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā nirbātīcā dīpu| sarvathā neṇe kaṃpu| taisā sthirabuṟyi svasvarūpu| yogayuktu || 49 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a lamp in a windless place knows no flicker, so too is the yogi, whose intellect is steady in their true Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ये युक्‍्तीची कडसणी। नाहीं जयाच्या अंतःकरणीं। तो आकळिला जाण गुणीं। विषयादिकीं ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ye yuk‍tīcī kaḍasaṇī| nāhīṃ jayācyā aṃtaḥkaraṇīṃ| to ākaḻilā jāṇa guṇīṃ| viṣayādikīṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: One whose heart is devoid of this wisdom is known to be entangled in the qualities of worldly pleasures and the like.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया स्थिरबुऱ्दि पार्था। कहीं नाहीं सर्वथा। आणि स्थैर्याची आस्था । तेही नुपजे॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā sthirabuṟdi pārthā| kahīṃ nāhīṃ sarvathā| āṇi sthairyācī āsthā | tehī nupaje|| 43||
verses.meaning: O Partha, for such a person of steady intellect, there is absolutely nothing to be gained, nor does the desire for stability even arise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: निश्चळत्वाची भावना । जरी नव्हेचि देखें मना । तरी शांति केवीं अर्जुना। आपु होय ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: niścaḻatvācī bhāvanā | jarī navheci dekheṃ manā | tarī śāṃti kevīṃ arjunā| āpu hoya || 44||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, if the mind does not attain steadfastness, how can one achieve peace?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ शांतीचा जिव्हाळा नाहीं। तेथ सुख विसरोनि न रिगे कहीं। जैसा पापियाच्या ठायीं । मोक्षु न बसे ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha śāṃtīcā jivhāḻā nāhīṃ| tetha sukha visaroni na rige kahīṃ| jaisā pāpiyācyā ṭhāyīṃ | mokṣu na base || 45||
verses.meaning: Where there is no warmth of peace, happiness will never enter, just as liberation does not reside in a sinner.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें अग्निमाजीं घापती । तियें बीजें जरी विरूढती। तरी अशांता सुखप्राप्ती। घडो शके ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ agnimājīṃ ghāpatī | tiyeṃ bījeṃ jarī virūḍhatī| tarī aśāṃtā sukhaprāptī| ghaḍo śake || 46||
verses.meaning: If seeds cast into fire were to sprout, then an unpeaceful person might attain happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि अयुक्‍्तपण मनाचें। तेंचि सर्वस्व दुःखाचें। या कारणें इंद्रियांचें। दमन निकें ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni ayuk‍tapaṇa manāceṃ| teṃci sarvasva duḥkhāceṃ| yā kāraṇeṃ iṃdriyāṃceṃ| damana nikeṃ || 47||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the unruliness of the mind is the root cause of all suffering. For this reason, the control of the senses is excellent.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियें जें जें म्हणती । तें तेंचि जे पुरुष करिती। ते तरलेचि न तरती । विषयसिंधु ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyeṃ jeṃ jeṃ mhaṇatī | teṃ teṃci je puruṣa karitī| te taraleci na taratī | viṣayasiṃdhu || 48||
verses.meaning: Those who simply follow the dictates of their senses, whatever they may say, such individuals can never cross the ocean of worldly pleasures and attachments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी नाव थडिये ठाकितां। जरी वरपडी होय दुर्वाता । तरी चुकलाही मागौता। अपावो पावे॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī nāva thaḍiye ṭhākitāṃ| jarī varapaḍī hoya durvātā | tarī cukalāhī māgautā| apāvo pāve|| 49||
verses.meaning: Just as a boat, even if it reaches the shore, if it encounters a storm, it will again be thrown back into danger.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं प्राप्तेंही पुरुषें । इंद्रियें लाळिलीं जरी कौतुके । तरी आक्रमिला जाण दुःखें । संसारिके ॥ ३५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ prāpteṃhī puruṣeṃ | iṃdriyeṃ lāḻilīṃ jarī kautuke | tarī ākramilā jāṇa duḥkheṃ | saṃsārike || 350||
verses.meaning: Similarly, even if a person who has attained spiritual knowledge indulges their senses playfully, they will still be overcome by worldly suffering.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आपुलीं आपणपेया । जरी इंद्रियें येती आया। तरी अधिक कांहीं धनंजया। सार्थक असे॥५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni āpulīṃ āpaṇapeyā | jarī iṃdriyeṃ yetī āyā| tarī adhika kāṃhīṃ dhanaṃjayā| sārthaka ase||51||
verses.meaning: Therefore, if the senses come under one's own control, then, O Dhananjaya, there is nothing more meaningful than that.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें कूर्म जियापरी। उबाइला अवयव पसरी । ना तरी इच्छावशें आवरी । आपणपेंचि॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ kūrma jiyāparī| ubāilā avayava pasarī | nā tarī icchāvaśeṃ āvarī | āpaṇapeṃci|| 52||
verses.meaning: Just as a tortoise, by its own will, extends its limbs and then withdraws them into itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी इंद्रियें आपैतीं होती । जयाचें म्हणितलें करिती । तयाची प्रज्ञा जाण स्थिती । पातली असे॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī iṃdriyeṃ āpaitīṃ hotī | jayāceṃ mhaṇitaleṃ karitī | tayācī prajñā jāṇa sthitī | pātalī ase|| 53||
verses.meaning: When the senses come under one's control, and they act according to one's command, know that such a person's intellect has attained stability.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां आणिक एक गहन । पूर्णाचें चिन्ह। अर्जुना तुज सांगैन । परिस पां॥५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ āṇika eka gahana | pūrṇāceṃ cinha| arjunā tuja sāṃgaina | parisa pāṃ||54||
verses.meaning: Now, Arjuna, I will tell you another profound sign of the Complete One; listen carefully.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें भूतजात निदेलें। तेथेंचि जया पाहलें। आणि जीव जेथ चेइलें। तेथ निद्रितु जो॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ bhūtajāta nideleṃ| tetheṃci jayā pāhaleṃ| āṇi jīva jetha ceileṃ| tetha nidritu jo|| 55||
verses.meaning: When all beings are asleep, for Him it is dawn. And where beings are awake, there He is asleep.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोचि तो निरुपाधि। अर्जुना तो स्थिरबुऱ्दि। तोचि जाणें निरवधि। मुनीश्‍वर॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: toci to nirupādhi| arjunā to sthirabuṟdi| toci jāṇeṃ niravadhi| munīś‍vara|| 56||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, that very one is unconditioned, that one is of steady intellect. Know that one to be eternal, O chief among sages.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था आणीकही परी। तो जाणों येईल अवधारीं। जैसी अक्षोभता सागरीं। अखंडित ॥ ५७॥
