verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ sādukupaṇeṃ jvāḻā samṛtdhadhā | maga vāsanāṃtarāciyā samidhā | sneheṃsīṃ nānāvidhā | jāḻiḻiyā|| 36||
verses.meaning: With that purity, the flames of knowledge grew. Then, the diverse desires, like fuel sticks, along with their attachments, were consumed by the fire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ सोहंमंत्रे दीक्षितीं । इंद्रियकर्मांच्या आहुती । तियें ज्ञानानळीं प्रदीप्तीं। दिधळिया ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha sohaṃmaṃtre dīkṣitīṃ | iṃdriyakarmāṃcyā āhutī | tiyeṃ jñānānaḻīṃ pradīptīṃ| didhaḻiyā || 37||
verses.meaning: There, initiated by the 'Soham' mantra, the offerings of sensory actions are cast into the blazing fire of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं प्राणक्रियेचिये स्रुवेनिशीं । पूर्णाहुती पडली हुताशीं । तेथ अवभूथ समरसीं । सहजें जहाळें॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ prāṇakriyeciye sruveniśīṃ | pūrṇāhutī paḍalī hutāśīṃ | tetha avabhūtha samarasīṃ | sahajeṃ jahāḻeṃ|| 38||
verses.meaning: Then, with the ladle of the vital breath's action, the final offering was made into the fire. There, the concluding bath of the sacrifice naturally became one with the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आत्मबोधींचें सुख। जें संयमाग्नीचें हुतशेष। तोचि पुरोडाशु देख । घेतला तिहीं ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ātmabodhīṃceṃ sukha| jeṃ saṃyamāgnīceṃ hutaśeṣa| toci puroḍāśu dekha | ghetalā tihīṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: Then, the bliss of self-realization, which is the remnant of the fire of self-control, that very sacrificial offering was accepted by the three.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक ऐशिया इहीं यजनीं। मुक्‍त ते जाहले त्रिभुवनी । या यज्ञक्रिया तरी आनानीं। परि प्राप्य तें एक॥ १४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka aiśiyā ihīṃ yajanīṃ| muk‍ta te jāhale tribhuvanī | yā yajñakriyā tarī ānānīṃ| pari prāpya teṃ eka|| 140||
verses.meaning: Indeed, through these very sacrifices, they became liberated in all three worlds. Although the sacrificial rites may vary, the ultimate attainment remains one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक द्रव्ययजञु म्हिणिपती । एक तपसामग्रीया निपजविति। एक योगयागुही आहाती । जे सांगितले॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka dravyayajañu mhiṇipatī | eka tapasāmagrīyā nipajaviti| eka yogayāguhī āhātī | je sāṃgitale|| 41||
verses.meaning: Some perform the sacrifice of wealth, others engage in the practice of austerities, and still others are devoted to the sacrifice of yoga, as has been explained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एकीं शब्दीं शब्दु यजिजे। तो वाग्यजु म्हणिजे । ज्ञानें ज्ञेय गमिजे। तो ज्ञानयजु ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ekīṃ śabdīṃ śabdu yajije| to vāgyaju mhaṇije | jñāneṃ jñeya gamije| to jñānayaju || 42||
verses.meaning: When a word is offered to a word, it is called a sacrifice of speech. When the knowable is attained through knowledge, it is called a sacrifice of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें अर्जुना सकळ कुवाडें। जे अनुष्ठितां अतिसांकडें । परी जितेंद्रियासीचि घडे । योग्यतावशें ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ arjunā sakaḻa kuvāḍeṃ| je anuṣṭhitāṃ atisāṃkaḍeṃ | parī jiteṃdriyāsīci ghaḍe | yogyatāvaśeṃ || 43 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, all these difficult spiritual practices, which are extremely arduous to perform, are only accomplished by those who have conquered their senses, according to their worthiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते प्रवीण तेथ भले। आणि योगसमृव्दरि आथिले। म्हणौनि आपणपां तिहीं केलें) आत्महवन॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: te pravīṇa tetha bhale| āṇi yogasamṛvdari āthile| mhaṇauni āpaṇapāṃ tihīṃ keleṃ) ātmahavana|| 44||
verses.meaning: They were skilled and endowed with the abundance of Yoga, and thus, they performed the sacrifice of the self within themselves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग अपानाग्नीचेनि मुखीं। प्राणद्रव्यें देखीं। हवन केलें एकौं। अभ्यासयोगें ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga apānāgnīceni mukhīṃ| prāṇadravyeṃ dekhīṃ| havana keleṃ ekauṃ| abhyāsayogeṃ || 45 ||
verses.meaning: Then, through the practice of Yoga, the life-force is offered as an oblation into the fire of the self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक अपानु प्राणीं अर्पिती। एक दोहींतेंही निरुंधिती। ते प्राणायामी म्हणिपति। पंडुकुमरा।॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka apānu prāṇīṃ arpitī| eka dohīṃteṃhī niruṃdhitī| te prāṇāyāmī mhaṇipati| paṃḍukumarā||| 46||
verses.meaning: Some offer the apana into the prana, while others restrain both. These are known as practitioners of pranayama, O son of Pandu.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ७८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी 'एक वज्रयोगक्रमें। सर्वाहारसंयमें । प्राणी प्राणु संभ्रमें। हबन करिती ॥४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: 78 śrījñāneśvarī 'eka vajrayogakrameṃ| sarvāhārasaṃyameṃ | prāṇī prāṇu saṃbhrameṃ| habana karitī ||47||
verses.meaning: Some yogis, through the practice of Vajrayoga and by controlling all their intake, offer their life-breath as a sacrifice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें मोक्षकाम सकळ। समस्त हे यजनशीळ। जिहीं यज्ञद्वारां मनोमळ । क्षाळण केलळे॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ mokṣakāma sakaḻa| samasta he yajanaśīḻa| jihīṃ yajñadvārāṃ manomaḻa | kṣāḻaṇa kelaḻe|| 48||
verses.meaning: Thus, all those who desire liberation, who are devoted to sacrifice, have cleansed the impurities of their minds through the means of sacrifice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया अविद्याजात जाळितां। जें उरलें निजस्वभावता । जेथ अग्नि आणि होता । उरेचिना॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā avidyājāta jāḻitāṃ| jeṃ uraleṃ nijasvabhāvatā | jetha agni āṇi hotā | urecinā|| 49||
verses.meaning: When the entire realm of ignorance is consumed, what remains is the inherent nature of the Self, where even the fire that burned it ceases to exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ यजितयाचा कामु पुरे। यज्ञींचें विधान सरे। मागुतें जेथूनि बोसरें । क्रियाजात ॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha yajitayācā kāmu pure| yajñīṃceṃ vidhāna sare| māguteṃ jethūni bosareṃ | kriyājāta || 150||
verses.meaning: Where the purpose of the sacrificer is fulfilled, the rituals of the sacrifice conclude, and from where all actions cease.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विचार जेथ न रिगे। हेतु जेथ न निगे। जें द्वैतदोषसंगें । सिंपेचिना ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: vicāra jetha na rige| hetu jetha na nige| jeṃ dvaitadoṣasaṃgeṃ | siṃpecinā || 51||
verses.meaning: Where thought cannot enter, where intention cannot emerge, that which is untouched by the blemish of duality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें अनादिसिद्ध चोखट । जें ज्ञान यज्ञाबशिष्ट। तें सेविती ब्रह्मनिष्ठ । ब्रह्माहंमंत्रें ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ anādisiddha cokhaṭa | jeṃ jñāna yajñābaśiṣṭa| teṃ sevitī brahmaniṣṭha | brahmāhaṃmaṃtreṃ || 52||
verses.meaning: Such is the pure, eternally established remnant of the knowledge-sacrifice, which the steadfast in Brahman partake of with the mantra 'I am Brahman'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे शेषामृतें धाळे। कीं अमर्त्यभावा आळे। म्हणौनि ब्रह्म ते जहाले। अनायासें॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise śeṣāmṛteṃ dhāḻe| kīṃ amartyabhāvā āḻe| mhaṇauni brahma te jahāle| anāyāseṃ|| 53||
verses.meaning: Thus, by drinking the nectar of devotion, they attained immortality and effortlessly became one with Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरां विरक्ति माळ न घालीचि। जयां संयमाग्नीची सेवा न घडेचि । जे योगयागु न करितीचि। जन्मले सांते ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerāṃ virakti māḻa na ghālīci| jayāṃ saṃyamāgnīcī sevā na ghaḍeci | je yogayāgu na karitīci| janmale sāṃte || 54||
verses.meaning: Others do not wear the garland of detachment; they do not serve the fire of self-control; they do not perform yoga or sacrifices; they are born in vain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयांचें ऐहिक धड नाहीं । तयांचें परत्र पुससी काई । म्हणौनि असो हे गोठी पाहीं । पंडुकुमरा॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāṃceṃ aihika dhaḍa nāhīṃ | tayāṃceṃ paratra pusasī kāī | mhaṇauni aso he goṭhī pāhīṃ | paṃḍukumarā|| 55||
verses.meaning: Those whose worldly affairs are not in order, what can you ask about their afterlife? Therefore, let this discussion be, O son of Pandu.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें बहुतीं परी अनेग। जे सांगितले तुज कां याग। ते विस्तारूनि वेदेंचि चांग। म्हणितळे आहाती ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ bahutīṃ parī anega| je sāṃgitale tuja kāṃ yāga| te vistārūni vedeṃci cāṃga| mhaṇitaḻe āhātī || 56||
verses.meaning: In this way, many different types of sacrifices have been explained to you, which are well-described in the Vedas themselves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तेणें विस्तारें काय करावें । हेंचि कर्मसिद्ध जाणावें । येतुलेनि कर्मबंधु स्वभावें । पावेळ ना ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teṇeṃ vistāreṃ kāya karāveṃ | heṃci karmasiddha jāṇāveṃ | yetuleni karmabaṃdhu svabhāveṃ | pāveḻa nā || 57||
verses.meaning: But what is to be gained by such an elaborate explanation? Know this alone to be the perfection of action: by this much, the bondage of karma naturally ceases.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना वेदु जयांचें मूळ। जे क्रियाबिशेषें स्थूळ। जयां नव्हाळियेचें 'फळ। स्वर्गसुख ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā vedu jayāṃceṃ mūḻa| je kriyābiśeṣeṃ sthūḻa| jayāṃ navhāḻiyeceṃ 'phaḻa| svargasukha || 58||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, the Vedas are their root, and through specific actions, they manifest in the gross world. The fruit of their newness is the joy of heaven.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते द्रव्यादियागु कीर होती। परी ज्ञानयज्ञाची सरी न पवती । जैशी तारातेजसंपत्ती । दिनकरापाशीं ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: te dravyādiyāgu kīra hotī| parī jñānayajñācī sarī na pavatī | jaiśī tārātejasaṃpattī | dinakarāpāśīṃ || 59 ||
verses.meaning: Though these material sacrifices may be performed, they cannot compare to the sacrifice of knowledge, just as the brilliance of stars cannot compare to the sun.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें परमात्मसुखनिधान । साधावया योगीजन। जे न विसंब्िती अंजन उन्मेषनेत्रीं॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ paramātmasukhanidhāna | sādhāvayā yogījana| je na visaṃbitī aṃjana unmeṣanetrīṃ|| 160||
verses.meaning: Behold the treasure of supreme bliss, which yogis strive to attain, never forgetting it, like kohl applied to the eyes to enhance vision.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें धांबतया कर्माची लाणी । नेष्कर्म्यबोधाची खाणी। जें भुकेलिया धणी । साधनाची ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ dhāṃbatayā karmācī lāṇī | neṣkarmyabodhācī khāṇī| jeṃ bhukeliyā dhaṇī | sādhanācī || 61||
verses.meaning: It is the field where actions are sown, the mine of the knowledge of inaction, and the satisfaction for the hungry seeker of spiritual practice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ प्रवृत्ति पांगुळ जाहली। तर्काची दिठी गेली। जेणें इंद्रियें विसरलीं। विषयसंगु॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha pravṛtti pāṃguḻa jāhalī| tarkācī diṭhī gelī| jeṇeṃ iṃdriyeṃ visaralīṃ| viṣayasaṃgu|| 62||
verses.meaning: Where worldly activity becomes lame, the eye of logic is lost, and the senses forget their attachment to objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मनाचें मनपण गेलें। जेथ बोलाचें बोलकेपण ठेलें। जयामाजि सांपडलें। ज्ञेय दिसे॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: manāceṃ manapaṇa geleṃ| jetha bolāceṃ bolakepaṇa ṭheleṃ| jayāmāji sāṃpaḍaleṃ| jñeya dise|| 63||
verses.meaning: The mind's mental activity ceased, where the power of speech was stilled, and within that state, the knowable became manifest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ बैराग्याचा पांगु फिटे । विवेकाचाही सोसु तुटे । जेथ न पाहतां सहज भेटे । आपणपें॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha bairāgyācā pāṃgu phiṭe | vivekācāhī sosu tuṭe | jetha na pāhatāṃ sahaja bheṭe | āpaṇapeṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: Where the need for detachment ends, and the effort of discrimination ceases; where, without seeking, one effortlessly finds oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें ज्ञान पैं गा बरवें। जरी मनीं आधि आणावें। तरी संतां या भजावें। सर्वस्वेंसीं ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ jñāna paiṃ gā baraveṃ| jarī manīṃ ādhi āṇāveṃ| tarī saṃtāṃ yā bhajāveṃ| sarvasveṃsīṃ || 65 ||
verses.meaning: If you truly wish to attain that supreme knowledge in your heart, then you must serve these saints with your entire being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे ज्ञानाचा कुरुठा। तेथ सेवा हा दारवंटा। तो स्वाधीन करीं सुभटा । बोळगोनी ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: je jñānācā kuruṭhā| tetha sevā hā dāravaṃṭā| to svādhīna karīṃ subhaṭā | boḻagonī || 66||
verses.meaning: Service is the gateway to the abode of knowledge. O brave one, through service, make that abode your own, by humbly approaching it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तनुमनुजीवें । चरणासीं लागावें। आणि अगर्वता करावें। दास्य सकळ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tanumanujīveṃ | caraṇāsīṃ lāgāveṃ| āṇi agarvatā karāveṃ| dāsya sakaḻa|| 67||
verses.meaning: Therefore, with body, mind, and soul, surrender to His feet. And with humility, serve everyone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग अपेक्षित जें आपुलें। तेंही सांगती पुसिलें। जेणें अंतःकरण बोधलें। संकल्पा न ये॥६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga apekṣita jeṃ āpuleṃ| teṃhī sāṃgatī pusileṃ| jeṇeṃ aṃtaḥkaraṇa bodhaleṃ| saṃkalpā na ye||68||
verses.meaning: Then, what is desired by oneself, that too is told when asked, by which the inner self is enlightened and does not fall into mere संकल्प (mental resolve/desire).

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचेनि वाक्‍य उजिबडें। जाहलें चित्त निधडें। ब्रह्माचेनि पाडें। निःशंकु होय॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāceni vāk‍ya ujibaḍeṃ| jāhaleṃ citta nidhaḍeṃ| brahmāceni pāḍeṃ| niḥśaṃku hoya|| 69||
verses.meaning: By whose words, the mind becomes illuminated and fearless, attaining a state comparable to Brahman, free from all doubts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं आपणपेयांसहितें। इयें अशेषेंही भूतें । माझ्या स्वरूपी अखंडितें। देखसी तूं॥ १७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ āpaṇapeyāṃsahiteṃ| iyeṃ aśeṣeṃhī bhūteṃ | mājhyā svarūpī akhaṃḍiteṃ| dekhasī tūṃ|| 170||
verses.meaning: At that time, you will see all these beings, along with yourself, eternally abiding in My true nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें ज्ञानप्रकाशें पाहेल। तैं मोहांधकारु जाईल। जैं गुरुकृपा होईल। पार्था गा॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jñānaprakāśeṃ pāhela| taiṃ mohāṃdhakāru jāīla| jaiṃ gurukṛpā hoīla| pārthā gā|| 71||
verses.meaning: When one perceives through such a light of knowledge, then the darkness of delusion will vanish, O Partha, when the Guru's grace is received.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी कल्मषाचा आगरु । तूं भ्रांतीचा सागरु । व्यामोहाचा डोंगरु । होउनी अससी ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī kalmaṣācā āgaru | tūṃ bhrāṃtīcā sāgaru | vyāmohācā ḍoṃgaru | hounī asasī || 72||
verses.meaning: Even if you are a repository of impurities, an ocean of delusion, and a mountain of infatuation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तऱही ज्ञानशक्तिचेनि पाडें। हें आघवेंचि गा थोकडें। ऐसें सामर्थ्य असे चोखडें । ज्ञानीं इये ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṟahī jñānaśakticeni pāḍeṃ| heṃ āghaveṃci gā thokaḍeṃ| aiseṃ sāmarthya ase cokhaḍeṃ | jñānīṃ iye || 73||
verses.meaning: Compared to the power of spiritual knowledge, all this is indeed insignificant. Such pure power resides in this knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें विश्वभ्रमाऐसा। जो अमूर्ताचा कडवसा। तो जयाचिया प्रकाशा । पुरेचिना॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ viśvabhramāaisā| jo amūrtācā kaḍavasā| to jayāciyā prakāśā | purecinā|| 74||
verses.meaning: The entire universe, which is like a dream, and the formless (Brahman) which is like its seed, cannot be fully illuminated even by His (God's) light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया कायसे हे मनोमळु । हें बोलतांचि अति किडाळु। नाहीं येणें पाडें ढिसाळु । दुजें जगीं ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā kāyase he manomaḻu | heṃ bolatāṃci ati kiḍāḻu| nāhīṃ yeṇeṃ pāḍeṃ ḍhisāḻu | dujeṃ jagīṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: How can this mental impurity be described? Even speaking of it is utterly vile. There is nothing else in the world as loose and worthless as this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांगैं भुवनत्रयाची काजळी । जे गगनामाजि उधवली। तिये प्रळयींचे वाहटुळी। काय अशभ्र पुरे॥७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃgaiṃ bhuvanatrayācī kājaḻī | je gaganāmāji udhavalī| tiye praḻayīṃce vāhaṭuḻī| kāya aśabhra pure||76||
verses.meaning: The darkness that envelops the three worlds, rising into the sky during the cosmic dissolution, what inauspiciousness can it truly contain?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं पवनाचेनि कोपें। पाणियेंचि जो पळिपे। तो प्रळयानळु दडपे। तृणें काष्ठें काई ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ pavanāceni kopeṃ| pāṇiyeṃci jo paḻipe| to praḻayānaḻu daḍape| tṛṇeṃ kāṣṭheṃ kāī || 77||
verses.meaning: When the cosmic fire of dissolution (pralayanala) is ignited by the fury of the wind, it is extinguished by water itself. How then can mere grass and wood withstand it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि असो हें न घडे। तें विचारितांचि असंगडें। पुढती ज्ञानाचेनि पाडें। पवित्र न दिसे॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni aso heṃ na ghaḍe| teṃ vicāritāṃci asaṃgaḍeṃ| puḍhatī jñānāceni pāḍeṃ| pavitra na dise|| 78 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, let this not happen. When considered, it is incomparable. Furthermore, nothing appears as pure as knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ ज्ञान हें उत्तम होये। आणिकही एक तेसें कें आहे। जैसें चैतन्य कां नोहे। दुसरें गा ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha jñāna heṃ uttama hoye| āṇikahī eka teseṃ keṃ āhe| jaiseṃ caitanya kāṃ nohe| dusareṃ gā || 79||
verses.meaning: Here, knowledge is supreme. Is there anything else like it? Just as there is no second to consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या महातेजाचेनि कसें । जरी चोखाळु प्रतिबिंब दिसे। कां गिंबसिलें गिंवसे। आकाश हें॥ १८० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā mahātejāceni kaseṃ | jarī cokhāḻu pratibiṃba dise| kāṃ giṃbasileṃ giṃvase| ākāśa heṃ|| 180 ||
verses.meaning: How can the reflection be seen clearly in this great light? Or how can the sky be contained or grasped?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी पृथ्वीचेनि पाडें। कांटाळें जरी जोडे। तरी उपमा ज्ञानीं घडे । पंडुकुमरा॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī pṛthvīceni pāḍeṃ| kāṃṭāḻeṃ jarī joḍe| tarī upamā jñānīṃ ghaḍe | paṃḍukumarā|| 81||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, if a measure equal to the earth could be found, then that could be compared to the wise. Otherwise, no comparison is possible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि बहुतीं परीं पाहतां। पुढतपुढती निर्धारितां। हे ज्ञानाची पवित्रता । ज्ञानींचि आथि॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni bahutīṃ parīṃ pāhatāṃ| puḍhatapuḍhatī nirdhāritāṃ| he jñānācī pavitratā | jñānīṃci āthi|| 82||
verses.meaning: Therefore, when examined in many ways, and repeatedly ascertained, this purity of knowledge is found only in the knower of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी अमृताची चवी निवडिजे। तरी अमृताचिसारिखी म्हणिजे । तैसें ज्ञान हें उपमिजे। ज्ञानेंसींचि॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī amṛtācī cavī nivaḍije| tarī amṛtācisārikhī mhaṇije | taiseṃ jñāna heṃ upamije| jñāneṃsīṃci|| 83||
verses.meaning: Just as the taste of nectar is chosen, and it is said to be like nectar itself, so too is knowledge compared only to knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां यावरी जें बोलणें। तें वायांचि वेळु फेडणें। तंव साचचि हें पार्थ म्हणे। जें बोलत असां॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yāvarī jeṃ bolaṇeṃ| teṃ vāyāṃci veḻu pheḍaṇeṃ| taṃva sācaci heṃ pārtha mhaṇe| jeṃ bolata asāṃ|| 84||
verses.meaning: Now, whatever is said beyond this is merely a waste of time. To this, Arjuna truly said, "What you are saying is indeed true."

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तेंचि ज्ञान केवीं जाणावें । ऐसें अर्जूनें जंब पुसावें। तंव तें मनोगत देवें । जाणितलें॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teṃci jñāna kevīṃ jāṇāveṃ | aiseṃ arjūneṃ jaṃba pusāveṃ| taṃva teṃ manogata deveṃ | jāṇitaleṃ|| 85 ||
verses.meaning: But how is that knowledge to be known? As Arjuna was about to ask this, the Lord understood his unspoken thought.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणतसे किरीटी । आतां चित्त देई इये गोठी । सांगेन ज्ञानाचिये भेटी। उपावो तुज॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇatase kirīṭī | ātāṃ citta deī iye goṭhī | sāṃgena jñānāciye bheṭī| upāvo tuja|| 86||
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna said, "Now, pay attention to this matter. I will tell you the means to attain knowledge."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आत्मसुखाचिया गोडिया। विटे जो कां सकळ विषयां। जयाच्या ठायीं इंद्रियां। मानु नाहीं ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī ātmasukhāciyā goḍiyā| viṭe jo kāṃ sakaḻa viṣayāṃ| jayācyā ṭhāyīṃ iṃdriyāṃ| mānu nāhīṃ || 87||
verses.meaning: He who, for the joy of the Self, becomes detached from all worldly pleasures, and in whom the senses find no honor or sway.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो मनासीं चाड न सांगे। जो प्रकृतीचें केलें नेघे। जो श्रद्धेचेनि संभोगें। सुख्िया जाहला॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo manāsīṃ cāḍa na sāṃge| jo prakṛtīceṃ keleṃ neghe| jo śraddheceni saṃbhogeṃ| sukhiyā jāhalā|| 88||
verses.meaning: One who does not consult the mind, who does not accept what is done by nature, and who becomes blissful through the enjoyment of faith.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयातेंचि गिंवसित। तें ज्ञान पावे निशचित। जयामाजि अचुंबित। शांति असे॥८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāteṃci giṃvasita| teṃ jñāna pāve niśacita| jayāmāji acuṃbita| śāṃti ase||89||
verses.meaning: Searching for that, one certainly attains that knowledge, within which there is undisturbed peace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें ज्ञान हृदयीं प्रतिष्ठे। आणि शांतीचा अंकुर फुटे । मग विस्तार बहु प्रगटे । आत्मबोधाचा ( तत्क्षणी )॥ ९९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ jñāna hṛdayīṃ pratiṣṭhe| āṇi śāṃtīcā aṃkura phuṭe | maga vistāra bahu pragaṭe | ātmabodhācā ( tatkṣaṇī )|| 990||
verses.meaning: When that knowledge becomes established in the heart, then the sprout of peace emerges, and immediately, the vast expanse of self-realization manifests.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग जेउती वास पाहिजे। तेउती शांतीचि देखिजे। तेथ आपपरु नेणिजे। निर्धारितां॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga jeutī vāsa pāhije| teutī śāṃtīci dekhije| tetha āpaparu neṇije| nirdhāritāṃ||91||
verses.meaning: Then, wherever one seeks to go, there only peace is seen. There, the distinction of 'mine' and 'yours' is not known, upon reflection.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा हा उत्तरोत्तरु । ज्ञानबीजाचा विस्तारु । सांगतां असे अपारु । परि असो आतां॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā hā uttarottaru | jñānabījācā vistāru | sāṃgatāṃ ase apāru | pari aso ātāṃ|| 92||
verses.meaning: Such is the ever-expanding nature of the seed of knowledge. Its full description is boundless, but let it be for now.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐके जया प्राणियाच्या ठायीं । इया ज्ञानाची आवडी नाहीं। तयाचें जियालें म्हणों काई । वरी मरण चांग॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aike jayā prāṇiyācyā ṭhāyīṃ | iyā jñānācī āvaḍī nāhīṃ| tayāceṃ jiyāleṃ mhaṇoṃ kāī | varī maraṇa cāṃga|| 93||
verses.meaning: Listen, for the living being who has no love for this spiritual knowledge, what can we say about their life? Indeed, death is better.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शून्य जैसें कां गृह। कां चैतन्येंबीण देह । तैसें जीवित तें संमोह । ज्ञानहीन ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: śūnya jaiseṃ kāṃ gṛha| kāṃ caitanyeṃbīṇa deha | taiseṃ jīvita teṃ saṃmoha | jñānahīna || 94||
verses.meaning: Just as a house is empty, or a body without consciousness, so too is life without knowledge, mere delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा ज्ञान कीर आपु नोहे। परि ते चाड एकी जरी वाहे। तरी तेथ जिव्हाळा कांहीं आहे। प्राप्तीचा पैं ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā jñāna kīra āpu nohe| pari te cāḍa ekī jarī vāhe| tarī tetha jivhāḻā kāṃhīṃ āhe| prāptīcā paiṃ || 95||
verses.meaning: Or if one does not possess knowledge, but still cherishes a longing for it, then there is some affection for its attainment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि ज्ञानाची गोठी कायसी । परि ते आस्थाही न धरी मानसीं । तरी तो संशयरूप हुताशीं। पडिला जाण ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni jñānācī goṭhī kāyasī | pari te āsthāhī na dharī mānasīṃ | tarī to saṃśayarūpa hutāśīṃ| paḍilā jāṇa || 96||
verses.meaning: What is the point of talking about knowledge, if one does not even hold that aspiration in their mind? Know that such a person has fallen into the fire of doubt.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे अमृतही परि नावडे । ऐसें सावियाचीं अरोचकु जैं पडे । तें मरण आलें असे फुडें । जाणों ये कीं॥९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: je amṛtahī pari nāvaḍe | aiseṃ sāviyācīṃ arocaku jaiṃ paḍe | teṃ maraṇa āleṃ ase phuḍeṃ | jāṇoṃ ye kīṃ||97||
verses.meaning: When even nectar becomes unpalatable, and a complete aversion sets in, know that death is imminent.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा विषयसुखें रंजे। जो ज्ञानेंसींचि माजे। तो संशयें अंगीकारिजे। एथ भ्रांति नाहीं ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā viṣayasukheṃ raṃje| jo jñāneṃsīṃci māje| to saṃśayeṃ aṃgīkārije| etha bhrāṃti nāhīṃ || 98||
verses.meaning: Similarly, one who revels in worldly pleasures, even with knowledge, is embraced by doubt; there is no illusion in this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग संशयीं जरी पडला । तरी निशभ्नांत जाणें नासला। तो ऐहिकपरत्रा मुकला । सुखासि गा॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga saṃśayīṃ jarī paḍalā | tarī niśabhnāṃta jāṇeṃ nāsalā| to aihikaparatrā mukalā | sukhāsi gā|| 99||
verses.meaning: Then, if one falls into doubt, know that they are utterly ruined. They are deprived of happiness in this world and the next.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया काळज्वरु आंगीं बाणें। तो शीतोष्णें जैशीं नेणें आगी आणि चांदिणें। सरिसेंचि मानी॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā kāḻajvaru āṃgīṃ bāṇeṃ| to śītoṣṇeṃ jaiśīṃ neṇeṃ āgī āṇi cāṃdiṇeṃ| sariseṃci mānī|| 200||
verses.meaning: One whose body is afflicted by the fever of time, does not perceive cold and heat, and considers fire and moonlight to be the same.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें साच आणि लटिकें । विरुद्ध आणि निकें। संशयीं तो नोळखे। हिताहित॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sāca āṇi laṭikeṃ | viruddha āṇi nikeṃ| saṃśayīṃ to noḻakhe| hitāhita|| 1||
verses.meaning: Just as truth and falsehood, or good and bad, are not distinguished by a doubtful mind, so too it fails to discern what is beneficial and what is harmful.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा रात्रिदिवसु पाहीं । जैसा जात्यंधा ठाउवा नाहीं । तैसें संशयीं असतां कांहीं। मना न ये॥२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā rātridivasu pāhīṃ | jaisā jātyaṃdhā ṭhāuvā nāhīṃ | taiseṃ saṃśayīṃ asatāṃ kāṃhīṃ| manā na ye||2||
verses.meaning: Just as a person born blind does not perceive day and night, so too, when doubt persists, the mind does not grasp anything.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि संशयाहूनि थोर। आणिक नाहीं पाप घोर। हा विनाशाची वागुर। प्राणियासी॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni saṃśayāhūni thora| āṇika nāhīṃ pāpa ghora| hā vināśācī vāgura| prāṇiyāsī|| 3||
verses.meaning: Therefore, there is no greater or more terrible sin than doubt. It is a snare of destruction for all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणें कारणें तुवां त्यजावा । आधीं हाचि एकु जिणावा । जो ज्ञानाचिया अभावा-। माजि असे॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃ kāraṇeṃ tuvāṃ tyajāvā | ādhīṃ hāci eku jiṇāvā | jo jñānāciyā abhāvā-| māji ase|| 4||
verses.meaning: For this reason, you must first conquer this one thing: that which exists in the absence of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैं अज्ञानाचें गडद पडे । तैं हा बहुवस मनीं वाढे । म्हणोनि सर्वथा मार्गु मोडे । विश्वासाचा ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiṃ ajñānāceṃ gaḍada paḍe | taiṃ hā bahuvasa manīṃ vāḍhe | mhaṇoni sarvathā mārgu moḍe | viśvāsācā || 5||
verses.meaning: When the darkness of ignorance descends, this (doubt) greatly increases in the mind, and therefore, the path of faith is completely broken.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हृदयीं हाचि न समाये । बुद्धीतें गिंवसूनि ठाये। तेथ संशयात्मक होये । लोकत्रय ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: hṛdayīṃ hāci na samāye | buddhīteṃ giṃvasūni ṭhāye| tetha saṃśayātmaka hoye | lokatraya || 6||
verses.meaning: This (divine experience) does not fit in the heart; it encompasses and resides in the intellect, and then the three worlds become filled with doubt (as their reality is questioned).

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा जरी थोरावे । तरी उपायें एकें आंगवे। जरी हातीं होय बरवें । ज्ञानखडूग ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jarī thorāve | tarī upāyeṃ ekeṃ āṃgave| jarī hātīṃ hoya baraveṃ | jñānakhaḍūga || 7||
verses.meaning: Even if one were to achieve such greatness, it can only be attained through one means: if the excellent sword of knowledge is held in hand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तेणें ज्ञानशस्त्रे तिखटें । निखळु हा निवटे । मग निःशेष खता फिटे । मानसींचा ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī teṇeṃ jñānaśastre tikhaṭeṃ | nikhaḻu hā nivaṭe | maga niḥśeṣa khatā phiṭe | mānasīṃcā || 8||
verses.meaning: Then, with the sharp weapon of knowledge, this impurity is completely removed, and all mental anxieties are dispelled.

verses.shloka_devanagari: याकारणें पार्था । उठीं वेगीं वरौता । ८२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी नाशु करोनि हृदयस्था । संशयासी ॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yākāraṇeṃ pārthā | uṭhīṃ vegīṃ varautā | 82 śrījñāneśvarī nāśu karoni hṛdayasthā | saṃśayāsī ||9||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Partha, rise quickly and dispel the doubts residing in your heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें सर्वज्ञात बापु। जो श्रीकृष्णु ज्ञानदीपु) तो म्हणतसे सकृपु। ऐकें राया॥ २१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ sarvajñāta bāpu| jo śrīkṛṣṇu jñānadīpu) to mhaṇatase sakṛpu| aikeṃ rāyā|| 210||
verses.meaning: Thus, the universally known Shri Krishna, who is the lamp of knowledge, mercifully says, "Listen, O King."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब या पूर्वापर बोलाचा । विचारूनि कुमरु पंडूचा। कैसा प्रश्‍नु हन अवसरींचा। करिता होईल॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba yā pūrvāpara bolācā | vicārūni kumaru paṃḍūcā| kaisā praś‍nu hana avasarīṃcā| karitā hoīla|| 11||
verses.meaning: Considering the previous and subsequent words, how could Pandu's son (Arjuna) ask such a question at this opportune moment?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते कथेची संगति। भावाची संपत्ति) रसाची उन्नति। म्हणिपेल पुढा ॥ १२ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: te kathecī saṃgati| bhāvācī saṃpatti) rasācī unnati| mhaṇipela puḍhā || 12 ||
verses.meaning: The narrative's coherence, the wealth of emotion, and the elevation of its essence will be expounded further.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचिया बरवेपणीं। कीजे आठां रसांची बोबाळणी । जो सजनाचिये आयणी | विसांबा जगीं ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāciyā baravepaṇīṃ| kīje āṭhāṃ rasāṃcī bobāḻaṇī | jo sajanāciye āyaṇī | visāṃbā jagīṃ || 13||
verses.meaning: In whose goodness, the eight sentiments are celebrated; who is the resting place for the virtuous in the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो शांतुचि अभिनवेल। ते परियसा मऱ्हाटे बोळ। जे समुद्राहूनि सखोळ। अर्थभरित॥ ९१४॥
verses.shloka_iast: to śāṃtuci abhinavela| te pariyasā maṟhāṭe boḻa| je samudrāhūni sakhoḻa| arthabharita|| 914||
verses.meaning: That peace will be newly experienced. Listen to those Marathi words, which are deeper than the ocean, filled with meaning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें बिंब तरी बचकेंएवढें। परि प्रकाशा त्रैलोक्य थोकडें । शब्दाची व्याप्ति तेणें पाडें। अनुभवावी ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ biṃba tarī bacakeṃevaḍheṃ| pari prakāśā trailokya thokaḍeṃ | śabdācī vyāpti teṇeṃ pāḍeṃ| anubhavāvī || 15||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's disc, though small, illuminates the three worlds, so too is the pervasive reach of the Word; one should experience it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी कामितयाचिया इच्छा। फळे कल्पवृक्ष जैसा। बोलु व्यापकु होय तैसा। तरी अवधान द्यावें ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī kāmitayāciyā icchā| phaḻe kalpavṛkṣa jaisā| bolu vyāpaku hoya taisā| tarī avadhāna dyāveṃ || 16||
verses.meaning: Just as a wish-fulfilling tree grants the desires of those who seek its fruits, so too will my words be all-encompassing and fulfill your wishes, if you but pay attention.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो काय म्हणावें। सर्वज्ञु जाणती स्वभावें।॥ तरी निकें चित्त द्यावें। हे विनंती माझी॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso kāya mhaṇāveṃ| sarvajñu jāṇatī svabhāveṃ||| tarī nikeṃ citta dyāveṃ| he vinaṃtī mājhī|| 17||
verses.meaning: Let this be. What more can I say? The all-knowing naturally understand my disposition. Therefore, please give your full attention; this is my humble request.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ साहित्य आणि शांति । हे रेखा दिसे बोलती । जेसी 'लावण्यगुणकुळवती। आणि पतित्रता॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha sāhitya āṇi śāṃti | he rekhā dise bolatī | jesī 'lāvaṇyaguṇakuḻavatī| āṇi patitratā|| 18||
verses.meaning: Where literature and peace speak in unison, like a beautiful, virtuous, and chaste woman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधींच साखर आवडे । आणि तेचि जरी ओखदां जोडे । तरी सेवाबी ना कां कोडें । नावानाबा॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhīṃca sākhara āvaḍe | āṇi teci jarī okhadāṃ joḍe | tarī sevābī nā kāṃ koḍeṃ | nāvānābā|| 19||
verses.meaning: If one already likes sugar, and then it is also found to be a medicine, why would one not consume it with great delight?

verses.shloka_devanagari: सहजें मलयानिळु मंदु सुगंधु। तया अमृताचा होय स्वादु। आणि तेथेंचि जोडे नादु । जरी दैवगत्या॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: sahajeṃ malayāniḻu maṃdu sugaṃdhu| tayā amṛtācā hoya svādu| āṇi tetheṃci joḍe nādu | jarī daivagatyā|| 220||
verses.meaning: If by good fortune, the gentle, fragrant breeze from the Malaya mountains, which is like nectar in its taste, is accompanied by melodious sound.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी स्पर्शे सर्वांग निववी । स्वादें जिव्हेतें नाचवी । तेवींची कानांकरवीं म्हणवी। बापु माझा॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sparśe sarvāṃga nivavī | svādeṃ jivheteṃ nācavī | tevīṃcī kānāṃkaravīṃ mhaṇavī| bāpu mājhā|| 21||
verses.meaning: Just as touch cools the entire body, and taste makes the tongue dance, so too does it make my ears say, 'My dear father!'

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें कथेचें इये ऐकणें॥ एक श्रवणासी होय पारणें। आणि संसारदुःख मूळवणें। विकृतिविणें ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ katheceṃ iye aikaṇeṃ|| eka śravaṇāsī hoya pāraṇeṃ| āṇi saṃsāraduḥkha mūḻavaṇeṃ| vikṛtiviṇeṃ || 22||
verses.meaning: Listening to this discourse is a feast for the ears, and it uproots the suffering of worldly existence without any adverse effects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी मंत्रेंचि वैरी मरे। तरी वायां कां बांधावीं कटारें। रोग जाय दूधसाखरें। तरी निंब कां पियावा॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī maṃtreṃci vairī mare| tarī vāyāṃ kāṃ bāṃdhāvīṃ kaṭāreṃ| roga jāya dūdhasākhareṃ| tarī niṃba kāṃ piyāvā|| 23||
verses.meaning: If an enemy can be vanquished by a mere mantra, why bother to tie on a dagger? If a disease can be cured by milk and sugar, why should one drink bitter neem?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा मनाचा मारु न करितां। आणि इंद्रियां दुःख न देतां। एथ मोक्ष असे आयता। श्रवणाचिमाजी ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā manācā māru na karitāṃ| āṇi iṃdriyāṃ duḥkha na detāṃ| etha mokṣa ase āyatā| śravaṇācimājī || 24||
verses.meaning: Similarly, without afflicting the mind or causing distress to the senses, liberation is readily attained through listening alone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणोनि आथिलिया आराणुका। गीतार्थ्‌ हा निका। ज्ञानदेवो म्हणे आइका । निवृत्तिदासु॥ २२५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇoni āthiliyā ārāṇukā| gītārth‌ hā nikā| jñānadevo mhaṇe āikā | nivṛttidāsu|| 225 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, this profound meaning of the Gita, which is a great comfort, Dnyandev, the servant of Nivrutti, says, listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग पार्थ श्रीकृष्णातें म्हणे । हां हो हें कैसें तुमचें बोळणें । एक होय तरी अंतःकरणें। विचारू ये॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga pārtha śrīkṛṣṇāteṃ mhaṇe | hāṃ ho heṃ kaiseṃ tumaceṃ boḻaṇeṃ | eka hoya tarī aṃtaḥkaraṇeṃ| vicārū ye|| 1||
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna said to Shri Krishna, "Oh, how is this your teaching? If it were one, then it could be pondered in the heart."

verses.shloka_devanagari: मागां सकळ कर्मांचा संन्यासु। तुम्हींचि निरोपिला होता बहुवसु । तरी कर्मयोगी केवीं अतिरसु। पोखीतसां पुढती ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: māgāṃ sakaḻa karmāṃcā saṃnyāsu| tumhīṃci niropilā hotā bahuvasu | tarī karmayogī kevīṃ atirasu| pokhītasāṃ puḍhatī || 2||
verses.meaning: Earlier, you yourself had extensively expounded upon the renunciation of all actions. So, how is it that you are now again so enthusiastically nurturing the path of Karma Yoga?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें द्व्यर्थ हें बोलतां । आम्हां नेणतयांच्या चित्ता । आपुल्ियि चाडें श्रीअनंता । उमजु नोहे॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ dvyartha heṃ bolatāṃ | āmhāṃ neṇatayāṃcyā cittā | āpuliyi cāḍeṃ śrīanaṃtā | umaju nohe|| 3||
verses.meaning: When such ambiguous words are spoken, our ignorant minds, despite our longing, cannot comprehend the true meaning of the Infinite One.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐके एकसारातें बोधिजे। तरी एकनिष्ठचि बोलिजे । हें आणिकीं काय सांगिजे। तुम्हांप्रति॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aike ekasārāteṃ bodhije| tarī ekaniṣṭhaci bolije | heṃ āṇikīṃ kāya sāṃgije| tumhāṃprati|| 4||
verses.meaning: Listen, if one is to be taught the essence of truth, then only steadfast devotion should be spoken of. What more can I tell you about this?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी याचिलागीं तुमतें। म्यां राउळासि विनविलें होतें। जे हा परमार्थ ध्वनितें। न बोळावा॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī yācilāgīṃ tumateṃ| myāṃ rāuḻāsi vinavileṃ hoteṃ| je hā paramārtha dhvaniteṃ| na boḻāvā|| 5||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for this very reason, I had appealed to the temple (or the divine presence) that this spiritual truth should not be obscured.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मागील असो देवा । आतां प्रस्तुती उकलु देखावा । सांगें दोहींमाजि बरवा । मार्गु कवणु॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī māgīla aso devā | ātāṃ prastutī ukalu dekhāvā | sāṃgeṃ dohīṃmāji baravā | mārgu kavaṇu|| 6||
verses.meaning: But let the past be, O Lord. Now, let us see the present unfolding. Tell me, between the two, which is the better path?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो परिणामींचा निर्वाळा। अचुंबितु ये फळा। आणि अनुष्ठितां प्रांजळा । सावियाचि ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo pariṇāmīṃcā nirvāḻā| acuṃbitu ye phaḻā| āṇi anuṣṭhitāṃ prāṃjaḻā | sāviyāci || 7||
verses.meaning: The ultimate truth, when realized, yields its fruit effortlessly, and for those who sincerely practice, it comes naturally.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें निद्रेचें सुख न मोडे । आणि मार्गु तरी बहुसाल सांडे। तैसें सोहोकासन सांगडें । सोहपें होय ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ nidreceṃ sukha na moḍe | āṇi mārgu tarī bahusāla sāṃḍe| taiseṃ sohokāsana sāṃgaḍeṃ | sohapeṃ hoya || 8||
verses.meaning: Just as the bliss of sleep is not broken, and yet one travels a great distance, so too, the difficult practice of Soham becomes easy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणें अर्जुनाचेनि बोलें। देवो मनीं रिझळे। मग होईल ऐके म्हणितलें। संतोषोनियां ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃ arjunāceni boleṃ| devo manīṃ rijhaḻe| maga hoīla aike mhaṇitaleṃ| saṃtoṣoniyāṃ || 9||
verses.meaning: By these words of Arjuna, the Lord was pleased in His mind. Then, greatly satisfied, He said, "So be it."

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखा कामधेनु ऐसी माये। सदैवा जया होये। तो चंद्रही परी लाहे। खेळावया॥ १०॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhā kāmadhenu aisī māye| sadaivā jayā hoye| to caṃdrahī parī lāhe| kheḻāvayā|| 10||
verses.meaning: Behold, if one is fortunate enough to have a mother like the wish-fulfilling cow Kamadhenu, then even the moon becomes a plaything for them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहें पां श्रीशंभूची प्रसन्नता । तया उपमन्यूचिया आर्ता। काय क्लीराब्धि दूधभाता। देइजेचिना॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāheṃ pāṃ śrīśaṃbhūcī prasannatā | tayā upamanyūciyā ārtā| kāya klīrābdhi dūdhabhātā| deijecinā|| 11||
verses.meaning: Behold, through the grace of Lord Shambhu (Shiva), was not the distressed Upamanyu given the milk-ocean as his milk-rice?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा औदार्याचा कुरुठा। श्रीकृष्णु आपु जाहलिया सुभटा । कां सर्व सुखांचा बसौटा । तोचि नोहावा॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā audāryācā kuruṭhā| śrīkṛṣṇu āpu jāhaliyā subhaṭā | kāṃ sarva sukhāṃcā basauṭā | toci nohāvā|| 12||
verses.meaning: Similarly, if Lord Krishna Himself, the very abode of generosity, becomes your own, or if He, the source of all happiness, becomes yours, then why would He not be so?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ चमत्कारु कायसा । गोसावी श्रीलक्ष्मीकांताऐसा । आतां आपुलिया सवेसा। मागावा कीं ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha camatkāru kāyasā | gosāvī śrīlakṣmīkāṃtāaisā | ātāṃ āpuliyā savesā| māgāvā kīṃ || 13||
verses.meaning: What wonder is there in this, that the Lord, the consort of Shri Lakshmi, should now be sought for His companionship?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि अर्जुनें म्हणितलें। तें हांसोनि येरें दिधलें। तेंचि सांगेन बोलिलें। काय कृष्णे ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni arjuneṃ mhaṇitaleṃ| teṃ hāṃsoni yereṃ didhaleṃ| teṃci sāṃgena bolileṃ| kāya kṛṣṇe || 94||
verses.meaning: Therefore, what Arjuna said, Krishna, smiling, granted. I will now tell you what Krishna said in response.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो म्हणे गा कुंतीसुता। हे संन्यासयोगु विचारितां । मोक्षकरु तत्त्वता । दोनीही होती॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: to mhaṇe gā kuṃtīsutā| he saṃnyāsayogu vicāritāṃ | mokṣakaru tattvatā | donīhī hotī|| 15||
verses.meaning: He said, "O son of Kunti, when these two paths, renunciation and yoga, are considered, both are truly conducive to liberation."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी जाणां नेणां सकळां। हा कर्मयोगु कीर प्रांजळा । जैसी नाव स्त्रियां बाळां। तोयतरणी ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī jāṇāṃ neṇāṃ sakaḻāṃ| hā karmayogu kīra prāṃjaḻā | jaisī nāva striyāṃ bāḻāṃ| toyataraṇī || 16||
verses.meaning: Therefore, know that this Karma Yoga is indeed clear and straightforward for everyone, whether knowledgeable or ignorant, just as a boat is a means to cross water for women and children.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सारासार पाहिजे। तरी सोहपा हाचि देखिजे। येणें संन्यासफळ लाहिजे। अनायासे ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sārāsāra pāhije| tarī sohapā hāci dekhije| yeṇeṃ saṃnyāsaphaḻa lāhije| anāyāse || 97||
verses.meaning: Similarly, if one seeks the essence of truth, one will find it in the 'So'ham' (I am He) realization. Through this, the fruit of renunciation is effortlessly attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां याचिलागीं सांगेन । तुज संन्यासियाचें चिन्ह । मग सहजें हें अभिन्न । जाणसी तूं॥१८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yācilāgīṃ sāṃgena | tuja saṃnyāsiyāceṃ cinha | maga sahajeṃ heṃ abhinna | jāṇasī tūṃ||18||
verses.meaning: Now, for this very reason, I will tell you the characteristics of a renunciate. Then, you will naturally understand this non-duality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी गेलियाची से न करी। न पवतां चाड न धरी। जो सुनिश्‍चळु अंतरीं । मेरु जैसा॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī geliyācī se na karī| na pavatāṃ cāḍa na dharī| jo suniś‍caḻu aṃtarīṃ | meru jaisā|| 19||
verses.meaning: Therefore, one should not lament over what is lost, nor crave for what is not attained. Such a person is steadfast within, like Mount Meru.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मी माझें ऐसी आठवण । विसरलें जयाचें अंतःकरण । पार्था तो संन्यासी जाण । निरंतर ॥ २०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mī mājheṃ aisī āṭhavaṇa | visaraleṃ jayāceṃ aṃtaḥkaraṇa | pārthā to saṃnyāsī jāṇa | niraṃtara || 20||
verses.meaning: And the one whose heart has forgotten the thought of 'I' and 'mine', O Partha, know him to be a true renunciate, always.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो मनें ऐसा जाहला । संगीं तोचि सांडिला। म्हणोनि सुखें सुख पावला। अखंडित॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo maneṃ aisā jāhalā | saṃgīṃ toci sāṃḍilā| mhaṇoni sukheṃ sukha pāvalā| akhaṃḍita|| 21||
verses.meaning: One who becomes thus in mind, abandons attachment, and therefore attains unbroken happiness through joy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां गृहादिक आघवें। तें कांही नलगे त्यजावें। जें घेतें जाहलें स्वभावें । निःसंगु म्हणौनि॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ gṛhādika āghaveṃ| teṃ kāṃhī nalage tyajāveṃ| jeṃ gheteṃ jāhaleṃ svabhāveṃ | niḥsaṃgu mhaṇauni|| 22||
verses.meaning: Now, there is no need to abandon the home and everything else. For, by its very nature, it has become detached.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें अग्नि विझोनि जाये। मग जे राखोंडी केवळु होये । तैं ते कापुसें गिंवसूं ये । जियापरी ॥ २३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ agni vijhoni jāye| maga je rākhoṃḍī kevaḻu hoye | taiṃ te kāpuseṃ giṃvasūṃ ye | jiyāparī || 23 ||
verses.meaning: When a fire extinguishes, and only ashes remain, then those ashes can be gathered by cotton, just as it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा असतेनि उपाधी । नाकळिजे तो कर्मबंधीं। जयाचिये बुद्धी। संकल्पु नाहीं ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā asateni upādhī | nākaḻije to karmabaṃdhīṃ| jayāciye buddhī| saṃkalpu nāhīṃ || 24||
verses.meaning: Just as a person remains untouched by the bonds of karma, in whose intellect there is no संकल्प (resolve or intention).

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि कल्पना जें सांडे । तैंचि गा संन्यासु घडे । इयें कारणें दोनी सांगडे । संन्यासयोगु ॥ २५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni kalpanā jeṃ sāṃḍe | taiṃci gā saṃnyāsu ghaḍe | iyeṃ kāraṇeṃ donī sāṃgaḍe | saṃnyāsayogu || 25 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, when imagination (or mental constructs) is abandoned, only then does true renunciation occur. For these reasons, both renunciation and yoga (disciplined action) are intertwined.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं तरी पार्था । जे मूर्ख होती सर्वथा । ते सांख्ययोगुसंस्था । जाणती केवीं ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ tarī pārthā | je mūrkha hotī sarvathā | te sāṃkhyayogusaṃsthā | jāṇatī kevīṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, O Partha, how can those who are utterly foolish understand the principles of Sankhya Yoga?

verses.shloka_devanagari: सहजें ते अज्ञान । म्हणौनि म्हणती हे भिन्न । एऱ्हवीं दीपाप्रति काई आनान। प्रकाशु आहाती ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: sahajeṃ te ajñāna | mhaṇauni mhaṇatī he bhinna | eṟhavīṃ dīpāprati kāī ānāna| prakāśu āhātī || 27||
verses.meaning: It is simply ignorance that makes them say these are different. Otherwise, how can there be different lights for a lamp?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सम्यक्‌ येणें अनुभवें। जिहीं देखिलें तत्त्व आघवें। तें दोहींतेंही ऐक्यभावें। मानिती गा॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ samyak‌ yeṇeṃ anubhaveṃ| jihīṃ dekhileṃ tattva āghaveṃ| teṃ dohīṃteṃhī aikyabhāveṃ| mānitī gā|| 28||
verses.meaning: Indeed, those who have truly experienced and seen the entire truth, they perceive both as one, O listener.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि सांख्यीं जें पाविजे । तेंचि योगीं गमिजे। म्हणौनि ऐक्य दोहींतें सहजें । इयापरी ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi sāṃkhyīṃ jeṃ pāvije | teṃci yogīṃ gamije| mhaṇauni aikya dohīṃteṃ sahajeṃ | iyāparī || 29||
verses.meaning: And that which is attained by the path of knowledge (Sankhya), the same is reached by the path of action (Yoga). Therefore, the unity of both is natural, in this manner.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें आकाशा आणि अवकाशा । भेदु नाहीं जैसा । तैसें ऐक्य योगसंन्यासा। बोळखे जो॥ ३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ ākāśā āṇi avakāśā | bhedu nāhīṃ jaisā | taiseṃ aikya yogasaṃnyāsā| boḻakhe jo|| 30||
verses.meaning: Just as there is no difference between the sky and space, so too is the unity of Yoga and Sannyasa understood by one who realizes it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयासीचि जगीं पाहलें। आपणणपें तेणेंचि देखिलें। जया सांख्य-योग जाणवले भेदेंबिण॥ ३१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāsīci jagīṃ pāhaleṃ| āpaṇaṇapeṃ teṇeṃci dekhileṃ| jayā sāṃkhya-yoga jāṇavale bhedeṃbiṇa|| 319||
verses.meaning: The world dawned for them, and they saw their own true Self, those who understood Samkhya and Yoga without differentiation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो युक्तिपंथें पार्था । चढे मोक्षपर्वता । तो महासुखाचा निमथा । वहिला 'पावे॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo yuktipaṃtheṃ pārthā | caḍhe mokṣaparvatā | to mahāsukhācā nimathā | vahilā 'pāve|| 32||
verses.meaning: O Partha, whoever ascends the mountain of liberation through the path of wisdom quickly attains the ultimate abode of great bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरा योगस्थिति जया सांडे । तो वायांचि गा हव्यासीं पडे । परि प्राप्ति कहीं न घडे । संन्यासाची ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerā yogasthiti jayā sāṃḍe | to vāyāṃci gā havyāsīṃ paḍe | pari prāpti kahīṃ na ghaḍe | saṃnyāsācī || 33||
verses.meaning: One who loses this state of Yoga (union with the divine) falls into vain desires, and never truly attains the state of renunciation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेणें भ्रांतीपासूनि हिरतळें। गुरुवाक्यें मन धुतलें। मग आत्मस्वरूपीं घातलें। हारौनियां॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṇeṃ bhrāṃtīpāsūni hirataḻeṃ| guruvākyeṃ mana dhutaleṃ| maga ātmasvarūpīṃ ghātaleṃ| hārauniyāṃ|| 34||
verses.meaning: One whose mind, having been deluded, was cleansed by the Guru's words, and then, having dissolved, was placed in the Self's true nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें समुद्री लबण न पडे। तंब वेगळें अल्प आवडे । मग होय सिंधूचि एवढें। मिळे तेव्हां॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ samudrī labaṇa na paḍe| taṃba vegaḻeṃ alpa āvaḍe | maga hoya siṃdhūci evaḍheṃ| miḻe tevhāṃ|| 35||
verses.meaning: Just as a lump of salt, when it falls into the ocean, does not remain separate or appear small, but rather becomes one with the vast ocean when it merges.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें संकल्पोनि काढिलें। जयाचें मनचि चैतन्य जाहलें। तेणें एकदेशियें परी व्यापिलें। 'लोकत्रय ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ saṃkalponi kāḍhileṃ| jayāceṃ manaci caitanya jāhaleṃ| teṇeṃ ekadeśiyeṃ parī vyāpileṃ| 'lokatraya || 36||
verses.meaning: Thus, having resolved and brought forth, whose mind itself became consciousness, by that one-parted being, the three worlds were pervaded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां कर्ता कर्म करावें। हें खुंटले तया स्वभावें । आणि करी जऱ्ही आधवबें। तऱही अकर्ता तो॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ kartā karma karāveṃ| heṃ khuṃṭale tayā svabhāveṃ | āṇi karī jaṟhī ādhavabeṃ| taṟahī akartā to|| 37||
verses.meaning: Now, the very notion of the doer performing actions naturally ceases for such a one. And even if they appear to act, they are still considered a non-doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे पार्था तया देहीं । मी ऐसा आठऊ नाहीं । तरी कर्तृत्व कैंचें काई । उरे सांगैं ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: je pārthā tayā dehīṃ | mī aisā āṭhaū nāhīṃ | tarī kartṛtva kaiṃceṃ kāī | ure sāṃgaiṃ || 38||
verses.meaning: O Partha, if in that body there is no remembrance of Me, then how can there be any doership, what remains, tell me?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें तनुत्यागेंबीण। अमूर्ताचे गुण। दिसती संपूर्ण । योगयुक्‍्तां ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ tanutyāgeṃbīṇa| amūrtāce guṇa| disatī saṃpūrṇa | yogayuk‍tāṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: Thus, without the relinquishment of the body, the attributes of the formless become fully manifest to those who are united in yoga.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱहवी आणिकांचिये परी । तोही एक शरीरी । अशेषाही व्यापारीं। वर्ततु दिसे ॥ ४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟahavī āṇikāṃciye parī | tohī eka śarīrī | aśeṣāhī vyāpārīṃ| vartatu dise || 40||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, just like others, he too appears to be a body, engaged in all activities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोही नेत्रीं पाहे। श्रवणीं ऐकतु आहे। परि ८६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी तेथींचा सर्वथा नोहे । नवल देखें ॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tohī netrīṃ pāhe| śravaṇīṃ aikatu āhe| pari 86 śrījñāneśvarī tethīṃcā sarvathā nohe | navala dekheṃ || 41||
verses.meaning: He sees with His eyes, He hears with His ears, yet He is not of that place at all; behold this wonder!

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्पर्शासि तरी जाणे । परिमळु सेवी घ्राणें। अवसरोचित बोलणें । तयाहि आथी ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: sparśāsi tarī jāṇe | parimaḻu sevī ghrāṇeṃ| avasarocita bolaṇeṃ | tayāhi āthī || 42||
verses.meaning: The skin knows touch, the nose enjoys fragrance, and timely speech is also within its capacity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आहारातें स्वीकारी । त्यजावें तें परिहरी। निद्रेचिया अवसरीं। निदिजे सुखें ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āhārāteṃ svīkārī | tyajāveṃ teṃ pariharī| nidreciyā avasarīṃ| nidije sukheṃ || 43||
verses.meaning: Accept what is conducive to your well-being, reject what is not, and sleep peacefully when it is time to sleep.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपुलेनि इच्छावशें। तोही गा चालतु दिसे। पैं सकळ कर्म ऐसें। राहाटे कीर॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpuleni icchāvaśeṃ| tohī gā cālatu dise| paiṃ sakaḻa karma aiseṃ| rāhāṭe kīra|| 44||
verses.meaning: By His own will, He too is seen to move. Indeed, all actions proceed in this manner.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें सांगों काई एकैक। देखें स्वासोच्छासादिक । आणि निमिषोन्निमिष। आदिकरूनि॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ sāṃgoṃ kāī ekaika| dekheṃ svāsocchāsādika | āṇi nimiṣonnimiṣa| ādikarūni|| 45||
verses.meaning: Why should I explain each and every thing? Look, from breathing and blinking, and so on, everything is included.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था तयाचे ठायीं । हें आघवेंचि आथि पाहीं। परी तो कर्ता नव्हे कांहीं। प्रतीतिबळें ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā tayāce ṭhāyīṃ | heṃ āghaveṃci āthi pāhīṃ| parī to kartā navhe kāṃhīṃ| pratītibaḻeṃ || 46||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, all this indeed exists within him, yet he is not the doer of anything, by the power of direct experience.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें भ्रांतिसेजे सुतला। तै स्वप्नसुखें भुतला। मग तो ज्ञानोदयीं चेइला। म्हणौनियां ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ bhrāṃtiseje sutalā| tai svapnasukheṃ bhutalā| maga to jñānodayīṃ ceilā| mhaṇauniyāṃ || 47||
verses.meaning: When one sleeps on the bed of illusion, then one is deluded by the happiness of dreams. Then, upon the dawn of knowledge, one awakens.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अधिष्ठानसंगती। अशेषाही इंद्रियवृत्ती। आपुलालिया अर्थी । वर्तत आहाती ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ adhiṣṭhānasaṃgatī| aśeṣāhī iṃdriyavṛttī| āpulāliyā arthī | vartata āhātī || 48||
verses.meaning: Now, through the association with the substratum, all the senses are engaged in their respective objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दीपाचेनि प्रकाशें। गृहींचे व्यापार जैसे। देहीं कर्मजात तेसें। योगयुक्‍्ता॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: dīpāceni prakāśeṃ| gṛhīṃce vyāpāra jaise| dehīṃ karmajāta teseṃ| yogayuk‍tā|| 49||
verses.meaning: Just as the light of a lamp illuminates the activities within a house, so too does the yogi perform actions in the body, illuminated by spiritual wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो कर्मे करी सकळें। परी कर्मबंधा नाकळे। जैसें न सिंपे जळीं जळें। पद्ापत्र॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: to karme karī sakaḻeṃ| parī karmabaṃdhā nākaḻe| jaiseṃ na siṃpe jaḻīṃ jaḻeṃ| padāpatra|| 50||
verses.meaning: He performs all actions, yet is not entangled by the bonds of karma, just as a lotus leaf remains untouched by water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें बुद्धीची भाष नेणिजे। मनाचा अंकुर नुदैजे। ऐसा व्यापारु तो बोलिजे। शारीरु गा॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ buddhīcī bhāṣa neṇije| manācā aṃkura nudaije| aisā vyāpāru to bolije| śārīru gā|| 51||
verses.meaning: Where the intellect's language is unknown, and the sprout of the mind does not arise, such an activity is called 'bodily' (pertaining to the physical realm).

verses.shloka_devanagari: हेंच मराठें परियेशीं। तरी बाळकाची चेष्टा जैशी। योगिये कर्मे करिती तैशीं। केवळा तनु॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃca marāṭheṃ pariyeśīṃ| tarī bāḻakācī ceṣṭā jaiśī| yogiye karme karitī taiśīṃ| kevaḻā tanu|| 52||
verses.meaning: Listen to this Marathi explanation: Just as a child's actions are mere play, so too are the actions of yogis—they are merely of the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग पांचभौतिक संचलें। जेव्हां शरीर असे निदेलें। तेथ मनचि रहाटे एकलें। स्वप्नीं जेवीं ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga pāṃcabhautika saṃcaleṃ| jevhāṃ śarīra ase nideleṃ| tetha manaci rahāṭe ekaleṃ| svapnīṃ jevīṃ || 53||
verses.meaning: When the body, made of the five elements, is asleep, the mind alone wanders, just as in a dream.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नवल ऐकें धनुर्धरा। कैसा वासनेचा संसारा । देहा होऊं नेदी उजगरा। परी सुखदुःखें भोगी ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: navala aikeṃ dhanurdharā| kaisā vāsanecā saṃsārā | dehā hoūṃ nedī ujagarā| parī sukhaduḥkheṃ bhogī || 54||
verses.meaning: Listen to this wonder, O Arjuna, how the world of desires does not allow the body to awaken, yet it experiences joy and sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियांच्या गांबीं नेणिजे। ऐसा व्यापारु जो निपजे। तो केवळु गा म्हणिजे । मानसाचा ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyāṃcyā gāṃbīṃ neṇije| aisā vyāpāru jo nipaje| to kevaḻu gā mhaṇije | mānasācā || 55||
verses.meaning: That activity which is not perceived by the senses, but rather arises from within, is indeed said to be solely of the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: योगिये तोही करिती । परी कर्मे ते न बंधिजती । जे सांडिली आहे संगती । अहंभावाची ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yogiye tohī karitī | parī karme te na baṃdhijatī | je sāṃḍilī āhe saṃgatī | ahaṃbhāvācī || 56||
verses.meaning: Even yogis perform actions, yet they are not bound by them, for they have abandoned the association with ego.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां जाहालिया भ्रमहत। जैसें पिशाचाचें चित्त । मग इंद्रियांचे चेष्टित । बिकळु दिसे॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ jāhāliyā bhramahata| jaiseṃ piśācāceṃ citta | maga iṃdriyāṃce ceṣṭita | bikaḻu dise|| 57||
verses.meaning: Now, when delusion has taken hold, just as the mind of a madman becomes, then the actions of the senses appear distorted and ineffective.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्वरूप तरी देखे। आळविलें आइके। शब्दु बोले मुखें। परी ज्ञान नाहीं ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: svarūpa tarī dekhe| āḻavileṃ āike| śabdu bole mukheṃ| parī jñāna nāhīṃ || 58||
verses.meaning: One may see the form, hear when called, and speak words with the mouth, yet lack true knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो काजेंबिण। जें जें कांही करण तें केवळ कर्म जाण । इंद्रियांचे ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso kājeṃbiṇa| jeṃ jeṃ kāṃhī karaṇa teṃ kevaḻa karma jāṇa | iṃdriyāṃce || 59||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Whatever is done without purpose, know that it is merely the action of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सर्वत्र जें जाणतें। तें बुद्धीचे कर्म निरुतें। बोळख अर्जुनातें। म्हणे हरी ॥ ६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sarvatra jeṃ jāṇateṃ| teṃ buddhīce karma niruteṃ| boḻakha arjunāteṃ| mhaṇe harī || 60||
verses.meaning: Then, that which knows everything, that is the pure action of the intellect. Thus, Hari addressed Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते बुद्धि धुरे करुनी। कर्म करिती चित्त देऊनी। परि ते नैष्कर्म्यापासुनी । मुक्‍त दिसती ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: te buddhi dhure karunī| karma karitī citta deūnī| pari te naiṣkarmyāpāsunī | muk‍ta disatī || 61||
verses.meaning: They perform actions with their intellect as the guiding force, dedicating their minds to their work. Yet, they appear liberated from the bondage of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें बुद्धीचिये ठावूनि देहीं । तयां अहंकाराची सेचि नाहीं । म्हणौनि कर्म करितां पाहीं । चोखाळले॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ buddhīciye ṭhāvūni dehīṃ | tayāṃ ahaṃkārācī seci nāhīṃ | mhaṇauni karma karitāṃ pāhīṃ | cokhāḻale|| 62||
verses.meaning: Those who are established in the intellect, in their bodies, have no trace of ego. Therefore, when they perform actions, they are purified.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा करितेनवीण कर्म। तेंचि तें निष्कर्म। हें जाणती सवर्म। गुरुगम्य जें ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā karitenavīṇa karma| teṃci teṃ niṣkarma| heṃ jāṇatī savarma| gurugamya jeṃ || 63 ||
verses.meaning: Indeed, action performed without the sense of doership, that alone is true inaction. This profound secret is known to those who have received guidance from a Guru.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां शांतरसाचें भरितें। सांडीत आहे पात्रातें। जें बोलणें बोलापरौतें । बोलवलें॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ śāṃtarasāceṃ bhariteṃ| sāṃḍīta āhe pātrāteṃ| jeṃ bolaṇeṃ bolāparauteṃ | bolavaleṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: Now, the tide of tranquil bliss overflows its vessel, speaking that which is beyond words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ इंद्रियांचा पांगु। जया फिटला आहे चांगु। तयासीचि आथि लागु । परिसावया॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha iṃdriyāṃcā pāṃgu| jayā phiṭalā āhe cāṃgu| tayāsīci āthi lāgu | parisāvayā|| 65||
verses.meaning: Only those whose senses have been completely subdued and purified are truly capable of listening to this discourse.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा असो अतिप्रसंगु। न संडीं पां कथालागु । होईल एलोकसंगतिभंगु। म्हणौनियां ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā aso atiprasaṃgu| na saṃḍīṃ pāṃ kathālāgu | hoīla elokasaṃgatibhaṃgu| mhaṇauniyāṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: Let this be an extreme situation; I will not abandon the discourse. For if I do, the gathering of people will be disrupted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें मना आकळितां कुवाडें। घाघुसितां बुद्धी नातुडे । तें दैवाचेनि सुरवाडें । सांगवलें तुज ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ manā ākaḻitāṃ kuvāḍeṃ| ghāghusitāṃ buddhī nātuḍe | teṃ daivāceni suravāḍeṃ | sāṃgavaleṃ tuja || 67||
verses.meaning: That which is difficult for the mind to grasp, and which the intellect cannot comprehend even with great effort, has been revealed to you by divine grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें शब्दातीत स्वभावें। तें बोलींचि जरी फावे। तरी आणिकें काय करावें। कथा सांगैं॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ śabdātīta svabhāveṃ| teṃ bolīṃci jarī phāve| tarī āṇikeṃ kāya karāveṃ| kathā sāṃgaiṃ|| 68||
verses.meaning: If that which is by nature beyond words can be attained through mere speech, then what else is there to do? Tell me this story.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा आर्तिबिशेषु श्रोतयांचा । जाणोनि दास निवृत्तीचा । म्हणे संबादु दोघांचा । परिसोनि परिसा ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā ārtibiśeṣu śrotayāṃcā | jāṇoni dāsa nivṛttīcā | mhaṇe saṃbādu doghāṃcā | parisoni parisā || 69 ||
verses.meaning: Knowing this special longing of the listeners, Nivritti's servant (Dnyaneshwar) says: listen attentively to the dialogue of the two (Krishna and Arjuna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग श्रीकृष्ण म्हणे पार्थातें । आतां प्राप्ताचें चिन्ह पुरतें । सांगेन तुज निरुतें। चित्त देई ॥७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga śrīkṛṣṇa mhaṇe pārthāteṃ | ātāṃ prāptāceṃ cinha purateṃ | sāṃgena tuja niruteṃ| citta deī ||70||
verses.meaning: Then Shri Krishna said to Arjuna, "Now I will fully and truly explain to you the characteristics of one who has attained the Self. Pay attention."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आत्मयोगें आधथिला। जो कर्मफळाशीं विटला। तो घर रिघोनि वरिला। शांती जगीं ॥७१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī ātmayogeṃ ādhathilā| jo karmaphaḻāśīṃ viṭalā| to ghara righoni varilā| śāṃtī jagīṃ ||719||
verses.meaning: Therefore, one who is established in the yoga of the Self, and is detached from the fruits of action, enters the abode of peace and embraces it in this world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरु कर्मबंधें किरीटी। अभिलाषाचिया गांठीं। 'कळासला खुंटीं। फळभोगाच्या ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeru karmabaṃdheṃ kirīṭī| abhilāṣāciyā gāṃṭhīṃ| 'kaḻāsalā khuṃṭīṃ| phaḻabhogācyā || 72||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, bound by karma and entangled in desires, is tied to the post of experiencing the fruits of his actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा फळाचिये हांबें। तैसें कर्म करी आघवें। मग न कीजेचि येणें भावें। उपेक्षी जो॥७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā phaḻāciye hāṃbeṃ| taiseṃ karma karī āghaveṃ| maga na kījeci yeṇeṃ bhāveṃ| upekṣī jo||73||
verses.meaning: Just as a tree bears fruit, so too should one perform all actions. Then, with the understanding that one is not the doer, one should renounce the fruits of those actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो जयाकडे वासु पाहे। तेउती सुखाची सृष्टि होये। तो म्हणे तेथ राहे। महाबोधु॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: to jayākaḍe vāsu pāhe| teutī sukhācī sṛṣṭi hoye| to mhaṇe tetha rāhe| mahābodhu|| 74||
verses.meaning: Wherever He casts His gaze, a world of happiness manifests. What He declares, there abides the Great Knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नवद्वारें देहीं । तो असतुचि परि नाहीं। करितुचि न करी कांहीं । फलत्यागी ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: navadvāreṃ dehīṃ | to asatuci pari nāhīṃ| karituci na karī kāṃhīṃ | phalatyāgī || 75||
verses.meaning: Though present in the body with its nine gates, he is as if not there; though acting, he does nothing, for he has renounced the fruits of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा कां सर्वेश्‍वरु । पाहिजे तंब निर्व्यापारु । परि तोचि रची विस्तारु । त्रिभुबनाचा ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā kāṃ sarveś‍varu | pāhije taṃba nirvyāpāru | pari toci racī vistāru | tribhubanācā || 76 ||
verses.meaning: Just as the Supreme Lord, though desireless and inactive, Himself creates the expansion of the three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कर्ता ऐसें म्हणिपे। तरी कवणें कर्मी न शिंपे। जे हातुपावो न लिंपे। उदासवृत्तीचा ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kartā aiseṃ mhaṇipe| tarī kavaṇeṃ karmī na śiṃpe| je hātupāvo na liṃpe| udāsavṛttīcā || 77||
verses.meaning: And though He is called the doer, He is not tainted by any action, just as the hands and feet of one who is detached remain unsoiled.

verses.shloka_devanagari: योगनिद्रा तरी न मोडे । अकर्तेपणा सळु न पडे। परि महाभूतांचें दळवार्डे। उभारी भळें॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: yoganidrā tarī na moḍe | akartepaṇā saḻu na paḍe| pari mahābhūtāṃceṃ daḻavārḍe| ubhārī bhaḻeṃ|| 78||
verses.meaning: The sleep of Yoga (Yoganidra) does not break, nor does the state of non-doership (akartepana) falter. Yet, the army of the great elements (mahabhutas) continues to grow and expand with great force.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जगाच्या जीवीं आहे । परि कवणाचा कहीं नोहे । जगचि हें होय जाये। तो शुद्धीहि नेणे ॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jagācyā jīvīṃ āhe | pari kavaṇācā kahīṃ nohe | jagaci heṃ hoya jāye| to śuddhīhi neṇe ||79||
verses.meaning: He is the life of the world, yet belongs to no one. The world itself comes and goes, but He is not even aware of it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पापपुण्यें अशेषें। पासींचि असतु न देखे । आणि साक्षीही होऊं न ठके । येरी गोठी कायसी ॥ ८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāpapuṇyeṃ aśeṣeṃ| pāsīṃci asatu na dekhe | āṇi sākṣīhī hoūṃ na ṭhake | yerī goṭhī kāyasī || 80||
verses.meaning: Even if sins and merits are present, one does not perceive them. One cannot even be a witness to them, so what to speak of other matters?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं मूर्तीचेनि मेळें। तो मूर्तचि होऊनि खेळे । परि अमूर्तपण न मेळे । दादुलयाचें ॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ mūrtīceni meḻeṃ| to mūrtaci hoūni kheḻe | pari amūrtapaṇa na meḻe | dādulayāceṃ || 81||
verses.meaning: Just as a child, playing with a doll, becomes one with it in play, yet never loses its own formless, true nature, so too does the divine manifest in forms without losing its transcendent, formless essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो सृजी पाळी संहारी । ऐसें बोलती जे चराचरीं। तें अज्ञान गा अवधारीं। पंडुकुमरा॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: to sṛjī pāḻī saṃhārī | aiseṃ bolatī je carācarīṃ| teṃ ajñāna gā avadhārīṃ| paṃḍukumarā|| 82||
verses.meaning: He creates, sustains, and destroys; those who speak thus of the animate and inanimate world, that is ignorance, O son of Pandu.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें अज्ञान जैं समूळ तुटे । तैं भ्रांतीचें मसैरें फिटे । मग अकर्तृत्व प्रगटे । मज ईशवराचें ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ ajñāna jaiṃ samūḻa tuṭe | taiṃ bhrāṃtīceṃ masaireṃ phiṭe | maga akartṛtva pragaṭe | maja īśavarāceṃ || 83||
verses.meaning: When that ignorance is uprooted completely, then the illusion's veil is lifted. Then My non-doership, that of the Lord, is revealed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ ईश्वरु एकु अकर्ता । ऐसें मानळें जरी चित्ता । तरी तोचि मी हें स्वभावता। आदीचि आहे॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha īśvaru eku akartā | aiseṃ mānaḻeṃ jarī cittā | tarī toci mī heṃ svabhāvatā| ādīci āhe|| 84||
verses.meaning: If the mind accepts that God alone is the non-doer, then it naturally follows that "I am He" from the very beginning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि विवेकें उदो चित्तीं । तयासि भेदु कैंचा त्रिजगतीं। देखें आपुलिया प्रतीति। जगचि मुक्‍त ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni vivekeṃ udo cittīṃ | tayāsi bhedu kaiṃcā trijagatīṃ| dekheṃ āpuliyā pratīti| jagaci muk‍ta || 85 ||
verses.meaning: When such wisdom dawns in the mind, where is any division for them in the three worlds? Indeed, in their realization, the entire world is liberated.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैशी पूर्वदिशेच्या राउळीं। उदया येतांची सूर्य दिवाळी । कीं येरीही दिशां तियेचि काळीं । काळिमा नाहीं ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiśī pūrvadiśecyā rāuḻīṃ| udayā yetāṃcī sūrya divāḻī | kīṃ yerīhī diśāṃ tiyeci kāḻīṃ | kāḻimā nāhīṃ || 86||
verses.meaning: Just as when the sun rises in the eastern temple, it illuminates not only the east but also dispels darkness from all other directions at that very moment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बुद्धिनिशचयें आत्मज्ञान । ब्रह्मरूप भावी आपणा आपण । ब्रह्मनिष्ठा राखे पूर्ण । तत्परायण अहर्निशीं ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: buddhiniśacayeṃ ātmajñāna | brahmarūpa bhāvī āpaṇā āpaṇa | brahmaniṣṭhā rākhe pūrṇa | tatparāyaṇa aharniśīṃ || 87||
verses.meaning: Through the unwavering resolve of intellect, one perceives oneself as Brahman. This steadfast devotion to Brahman is maintained perfectly, day and night, with complete dedication.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें व्यापक ज्ञान भलें। जयांचिया हृदयातें गिंवसित आलें। तयांची समता दृष्टि बोलें। बिशेषूं काई ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ vyāpaka jñāna bhaleṃ| jayāṃciyā hṛdayāteṃ giṃvasita āleṃ| tayāṃcī samatā dṛṣṭi boleṃ| biśeṣūṃ kāī || 88||
verses.meaning: When such expansive knowledge has come to reside in their hearts, what more can be said about the equality of their vision?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक आपणपांचि जेसें। ते देखती विश्व तैसें । हें बोलणें कायसें। नवलु एथ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka āpaṇapāṃci jeseṃ| te dekhatī viśva taiseṃ | heṃ bolaṇeṃ kāyaseṃ| navalu etha|| 89||
verses.meaning: Just as they perceive themselves, so too do they perceive the universe. What wonder is there in such a statement?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी दैव जैसें कवतिकें। कहींचि दैन्य न देखे। कां विवेकु हा नोळखे। भ्रांतीतें जेवीं ॥ ९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī daiva jaiseṃ kavatikeṃ| kahīṃci dainya na dekhe| kāṃ viveku hā noḻakhe| bhrāṃtīteṃ jevīṃ || 90||
verses.meaning: Just as destiny, by its very nature, never perceives misery, or just as discrimination does not recognize illusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी अंधकाराची वानी । जैसा सूर्या न देखे स्वप्नीं। अमृत नायके कानीं । मृत्युकथा ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī aṃdhakārācī vānī | jaisā sūryā na dekhe svapnīṃ| amṛta nāyake kānīṃ | mṛtyukathā || 91||
verses.meaning: Just as darkness cannot even dream of seeing the sun, or as nectar cannot hear the tale of death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो संतापु कैसा । चंद्र न स्मरे जैसा। भूतीं भेदु नेणती तैसा । ज्ञानिये ते॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso saṃtāpu kaisā | caṃdra na smare jaisā| bhūtīṃ bhedu neṇatī taisā | jñāniye te|| 92||
verses.meaning: Let this be. How can there be anger? Just as the moon does not remember (or recognize) differences in beings, so too the wise do not perceive distinctions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग हा मशकु हा ग्जु। कीं हा श्‍वपचु हा द्विजु। पैल इतरु हा आत्मजु । हें उरेल कें ॥९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga hā maśaku hā gju| kīṃ hā ś‍vapacu hā dviju| paila itaru hā ātmaju | heṃ urela keṃ ||93||
verses.meaning: Then, how can one be a mosquito and another an elephant? How can one be an outcast and another a Brahmin? How can one be a stranger and another one's own child? Such distinctions will cease to exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तरी हे धेनु हें श्‍वान। एक गुरु एक हीन । हें असो कैचें स्वप्न। जागतया॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā tarī he dhenu heṃ ś‍vāna| eka guru eka hīna | heṃ aso kaiceṃ svapna| jāgatayā|| 94||
verses.meaning: How can a person who is awake perceive a dream where a cow and a dog are seen as one, or where one is superior and the other inferior?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ भेदु तरी कौों देखावा। जरी अहंभाव उरला होआवा। तो आधींचि नाहीं आघवा। आतां विषमु काई ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha bhedu tarī kauoṃ dekhāvā| jarī ahaṃbhāva uralā hoāvā| to ādhīṃci nāhīṃ āghavā| ātāṃ viṣamu kāī || 95||
verses.meaning: Where then can one perceive difference, if the sense of ego were to remain? But that is not there at all from the beginning; what then is there to be unequal?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि सर्वत्र सदा सम। तें आपणचि अद्वय ब्रह्म। हें संपूर्ण जाणे वर्म । समदृष्टीचें ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni sarvatra sadā sama| teṃ āpaṇaci advaya brahma| heṃ saṃpūrṇa jāṇe varma | samadṛṣṭīceṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: Therefore, one who is always and everywhere equanimous, truly knows the secret of equanimity, that they themselves are the non-dual Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिहीं विषयसंगु न सांडितां। इंद्रियांतें न दंडितां। परी भोगिली निसंगता। कामनेविण॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jihīṃ viṣayasaṃgu na sāṃḍitāṃ| iṃdriyāṃteṃ na daṃḍitāṃ| parī bhogilī nisaṃgatā| kāmaneviṇa|| 97||
verses.meaning: They, without abandoning attachment to worldly objects, and without punishing their senses, yet experienced detachment, free from desire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिहीं लोकांचेनि आधारें। लौकिकेंचि व्यापारें। परि सांडिलें निदसुरें लौकिकु हें ॥९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jihīṃ lokāṃceni ādhāreṃ| laukikeṃci vyāpāreṃ| pari sāṃḍileṃ nidasureṃ laukiku heṃ ||98||
verses.meaning: Those who, through the support of people, engage in worldly affairs, but have abandoned the worldly slumber.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा जनामाजि खेचरु । असतुचि जना नोहे गोचरु । तैसा शरीरीं परी संसारु । नोळखे तयांतें ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā janāmāji khecaru | asatuci janā nohe gocaru | taisā śarīrīṃ parī saṃsāru | noḻakhe tayāṃteṃ || 99||
verses.meaning: Just as a bird in the sky is not visible to people, so too is the world (samsara) within the body, yet it does not recognize itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो पवनाचेनि मेळें। जैसें जळींचि जळ लोळे। तें आणिकें म्हणती वेगळें। कल्लोळ हे॥ १००॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso pavanāceni meḻeṃ| jaiseṃ jaḻīṃci jaḻa loḻe| teṃ āṇikeṃ mhaṇatī vegaḻeṃ| kalloḻa he|| 100||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Just as water merges with water when stirred by the wind, others call these separate waves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें नाम रूप तयाचें । एऱ्हवीं ब्रह्मचि तो साचें । मन साम्या आलें जयाचें। सर्वत्र गा॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ nāma rūpa tayāceṃ | eṟhavīṃ brahmaci to sāceṃ | mana sāmyā āleṃ jayāceṃ| sarvatra gā|| 1||
verses.meaning: Just as His name and form are, so too is He truly Brahman. His mind has attained equanimity everywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि समदृष्टी जो होये। तया पुरुषा लक्षणही आहे । अर्जुना संक्षेपें सांगेन पाहें । अच्युत म्हणे॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni samadṛṣṭī jo hoye| tayā puruṣā lakṣaṇahī āhe | arjunā saṃkṣepeṃ sāṃgena pāheṃ | acyuta mhaṇe|| 2||
verses.meaning: Thus, for one who attains such equanimity, there are also specific characteristics. Arjuna, I will briefly explain them, says Achyuta.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी मृगजळाचेनि पूरें। जैसें न लोटिजे कां गिरिवरें। तैसा शुभाशुभीं न विकरे। पातलिया जो॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī mṛgajaḻāceni pūreṃ| jaiseṃ na loṭije kāṃ girivareṃ| taisā śubhāśubhīṃ na vikare| pātaliyā jo|| 3||
verses.meaning: Just as a great mountain is not swept away by the floodwaters of a mirage, so too is one who remains undisturbed by good and bad fortune.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोचि तो निरुता । समदृष्टि तत्त्वतां । हरि म्हणे पंडुसुता। तोचि ब्रह्म॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: toci to nirutā | samadṛṣṭi tattvatāṃ | hari mhaṇe paṃḍusutā| toci brahma|| 4||
verses.meaning: He alone, truly, is of equal vision, says Hari to the son of Pandu, He alone is Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया आपणणपें सांडूनि कहीं। इंद्रियग्रामावरी येणेंचि नाहीं । तो विषय न सेवी हें काई । विचित्र येथ ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā āpaṇaṇapeṃ sāṃḍūni kahīṃ| iṃdriyagrāmāvarī yeṇeṃci nāhīṃ | to viṣaya na sevī heṃ kāī | vicitra yetha || 5||
verses.meaning: One who has abandoned their ego and never comes under the sway of the senses, for them not to indulge in worldly pleasures is not at all surprising.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सहजें स्वसुखाचेनि अपारें। सुरवाडलेनि अंतरें। रचिला म्हणौनि बाहिरें। पाऊल न घाली ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: sahajeṃ svasukhāceni apāreṃ| suravāḍaleni aṃtareṃ| racilā mhaṇauni bāhireṃ| pāūla na ghālī || 6||
verses.meaning: Naturally, with immense inner contentment and joy, it is composed. Therefore, it does not step outside.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांगैं कुमुददळाचेनि ताटें। जो जेविला चंद्रकिरणें चोखटें। तो चकोरु काई वाळुवंटें । चुंबितु असे ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃgaiṃ kumudadaḻāceni tāṭeṃ| jo jevilā caṃdrakiraṇeṃ cokhaṭeṃ| to cakoru kāī vāḻuvaṃṭeṃ | cuṃbitu ase || 7||
verses.meaning: Tell me, if the chakor bird, which dines on pure moonbeams from a lotus petal, would ever peck at a desert wasteland?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आत्मसुख उपाइलें। जयासि आपणपेंचि फावलें। तया विषयो सहजें सांडवले। म्हणों काई ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ātmasukha upāileṃ| jayāsi āpaṇapeṃci phāvaleṃ| tayā viṣayo sahajeṃ sāṃḍavale| mhaṇoṃ kāī || 8||
verses.meaning: When the bliss of the Self has dawned, and one has attained their true Self, how can one then be entangled in worldly pleasures? They are naturally abandoned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हबीं तरी कौतुकें । विचारूनि पाहें पां निकें॥ या विषयांचेनि सुखें। झकवती कवण॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhabīṃ tarī kautukeṃ | vicārūni pāheṃ pāṃ nikeṃ|| yā viṣayāṃceni sukheṃ| jhakavatī kavaṇa|| 9||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, with curiosity, look closely and see: who is truly deluded by the pleasures of these worldly objects?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते। आद्यन्तवन्त: कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुध:॥२२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te| ādyantavanta: kaunteya na teṣu ramate budha:||22||
verses.meaning: Indeed, the pleasures born of contact with the senses are sources of sorrow. They have a beginning and an end, O Kaunteya; the wise do not delight in them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिहीं आपणपें नाहीं देखिळें। तेचि इहीं इंद्रियार्थी रंजळे। जैसें रंकु कां आळुकैलें। तुषांतें सेवी ॥ ११०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jihīṃ āpaṇapeṃ nāhīṃ dekhiḻeṃ| teci ihīṃ iṃdriyārthī raṃjaḻe| jaiseṃ raṃku kāṃ āḻukaileṃ| tuṣāṃteṃ sevī || 110||
verses.meaning: Those who have not realized their true Self are indeed deluded by these sense objects. It is like a poor, hungry person who consumes husks.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी मृगें तृषापीडितें। संभ्रमें विसरोनि जळातें॥ मग तोयबुद्धी बरडीतें। ठाकूनि येती ॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī mṛgeṃ tṛṣāpīḍiteṃ| saṃbhrameṃ visaroni jaḻāteṃ|| maga toyabuddhī baraḍīteṃ| ṭhākūni yetī || 11||
verses.meaning: Or, just as deer, tormented by thirst, forget the actual water in their confusion, and then, mistaking a barren land for water, rush towards it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आपणपें नाहीं दिठे। जयातें स्वसुखाचे सदा खरांटे। तयासीचि विषय हे गोमटे। आवडती ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ āpaṇapeṃ nāhīṃ diṭhe| jayāteṃ svasukhāce sadā kharāṃṭe| tayāsīci viṣaya he gomaṭe| āvaḍatī || 12||
verses.meaning: Just as one who has not seen their own self, and is always deprived of their own inner joy, finds external sense objects appealing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं विषयीं सुख आहे। हें बोलणेंचि सारिखें नोहे । तरी विद्युत्स्फुरणें कां न पाहे। जगामाजी ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ viṣayīṃ sukha āhe| heṃ bolaṇeṃci sārikheṃ nohe | tarī vidyutsphuraṇeṃ kāṃ na pāhe| jagāmājī || 13||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, to say that there is happiness in worldly pleasures is not at all appropriate. If that were true, why wouldn't the flash of lightning illuminate the entire world permanently?

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांगें वातवर्षआतपु धरे । ऐसें अभ्रच्छायाचि जरी सरे। तरी त्रिमाळिकें धवळारें। करावीं कां॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃgeṃ vātavarṣaātapu dhare | aiseṃ abhracchāyāci jarī sare| tarī trimāḻikeṃ dhavaḻāreṃ| karāvīṃ kāṃ|| 14||
verses.meaning: If a mere cloud's shadow could provide shelter from the wind, rain, and sun, then why would one bother to construct a three-storied palace?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि विषयसुख जें बोलिजे । तें नेणतां गा वायां जल्पिजे । जैसें महूर कां म्हणिजे। विषकंदातें ॥ ९१५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni viṣayasukha jeṃ bolije | teṃ neṇatāṃ gā vāyāṃ jalpije | jaiseṃ mahūra kāṃ mhaṇije| viṣakaṃdāteṃ || 915||
verses.meaning: Therefore, what is called the happiness of worldly pleasures, know that it is spoken of in vain, just as a poisonous root is called honey.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी भौमा नाम मंगळु। रोहिणीतें म्हणती जळु । तैसा सुखप्रवादु बरळु । विषयिकु हा॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī bhaumā nāma maṃgaḻu| rohiṇīteṃ mhaṇatī jaḻu | taisā sukhapravādu baraḻu | viṣayiku hā|| 16||
verses.meaning: Or, just as one might call Mars by the name 'Bhauma' or call the constellation Rohini 'Jal' (water), so too is the praise of worldly pleasures, which are inherently flawed, nothing but empty talk.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे असो आघवी बोली । सांग पां सर्पफणीची साउली । ते शीतळ होईल केतुली । मूषकासी॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: he aso āghavī bolī | sāṃga pāṃ sarpaphaṇīcī sāulī | te śītaḻa hoīla ketulī | mūṣakāsī|| 17||
verses.meaning: Let all this be. Tell me, how cool will the shadow of a serpent's hood be for a mouse?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा आमिषकवळु पांडवा। मीनु न सेवी तंवचि बरवा । तैसा विषयसंगु आघवा । निशभ्रांत जाणें॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā āmiṣakavaḻu pāṃḍavā| mīnu na sevī taṃvaci baravā | taisā viṣayasaṃgu āghavā | niśabhrāṃta jāṇeṃ|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as a fish does not touch the bait as long as it is well, so too, all attachment to worldly pleasures is certainly a delusion, O Pandava.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे विरक्‍्तांचिये दिठी। जैं न्याहाळिजे किरीटी । तैं पांडुरोगाचिये पुष्टी-। सारिखें दिसे ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: he virak‍tāṃciye diṭhī| jaiṃ nyāhāḻije kirīṭī | taiṃ pāṃḍurogāciye puṣṭī-| sārikheṃ dise || 19||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti (Arjuna), when this is seen by the eyes of the detached, it appears like the nourishment of jaundice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि विषयभोगीं जें सुख। तें साद्यंतचि जाण दुःख। परि काय कौजे मूर्ख । न सेवितां न सरे॥ १२०॥
