verses.shloka_devanagari: तेविं मृत्यूचेनि अवसरें एकें । जें येऊनि जीवासमोर ठाके । तें होणें मग न चुके । भलतयापरी ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: teviṃ mṛtyūceni avasareṃ ekeṃ | jeṃ yeūni jīvāsamora ṭhāke | teṃ hoṇeṃ maga na cuke | bhalatayāparī || 72||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when death arrives at its appointed time and stands before the soul, that destined event cannot be averted, no matter what.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जागता जंब असिजे। तंव जेणें ध्यानें भावना भाविजे। डोळां लागतखेंबो देखिजे। तेंचि स्वप्नीं ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jāgatā jaṃba asije| taṃva jeṇeṃ dhyāneṃ bhāvanā bhāvije| ḍoḻāṃ lāgatakheṃbo dekhije| teṃci svapnīṃ || 73||
verses.meaning: And as long as one is awake, whatever is meditated upon and contemplated, that very thing is seen in a dream as soon as one falls asleep.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेविं जितेनि अवसरें। जें आवडोनि जीवीं उरे। तेंचि मरणाचिये मेरे। फार हों लागे ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teviṃ jiteni avasareṃ| jeṃ āvaḍoni jīvīṃ ure| teṃci maraṇāciye mere| phāra hoṃ lāge || 74||
verses.meaning: Just as in life, whatever is cherished and remains in the heart, that very thing becomes prominent at the time of death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मरणीं जया जें आठवे। तो तेचि गतीतें पावे । तस्मात्सर्वेषे कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च। मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामिवैष्यस्यसंशयम्‌ ॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi maraṇīṃ jayā jeṃ āṭhave| to teci gatīteṃ pāve | tasmātsarveṣe kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca| mayyarpitamanobuddhirmāmivaiṣyasyasaṃśayam‌ ||7||
verses.meaning: And whatever one remembers at the time of death, that is the state one attains. Therefore, at all times, remember Me and fight. With your mind and intellect surrendered to Me, you will undoubtedly come to Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि सदा स्मरावें। मातेंचि तुवां ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni sadā smarāveṃ| māteṃci tuvāṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: Therefore, you should always remember Me.

verses.shloka_iast: ḍoḻāṃ jeṃ dekhāveṃ| kāṃ kānīṃ hana aikāveṃ| manīṃ jeṃ bhāvāveṃ| bolāveṃ vāce || 76||
verses.meaning: Whatever is seen by the eyes, or heard by the ears, or conceived in the mind, is spoken by the tongue.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें आंत बाहेरी आघवें। मीचि करूनि घालावें । मग सर्वी काळीं स्वभावें । मीचि आहें ॥७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ āṃta bāherī āghaveṃ| mīci karūni ghālāveṃ | maga sarvī kāḻīṃ svabhāveṃ | mīci āheṃ ||77||
verses.meaning: Then, I will make everything, inside and out, and then, in all times, naturally, I alone exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना ऐसें जाहालिया । मग न मरिजे देह गेलिया । मा संग्रामु केलिया । भय काय तुज॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā aiseṃ jāhāliyā | maga na marije deha geliyā | mā saṃgrāmu keliyā | bhaya kāya tuja|| 78||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, when this understanding is attained, then the body's passing does not mean death. So, what fear can there be for you in engaging in battle?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं मन बुद्धि सांचेंसीं । जरी माझिया स्वरूपीं अर्पिसी । तरी मातेंचि गा पावसी । हे माझी भाक॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ mana buddhi sāṃceṃsīṃ | jarī mājhiyā svarūpīṃ arpisī | tarī māteṃci gā pāvasī | he mājhī bhāka|| 79||
verses.meaning: If you truly dedicate your mind and intellect to My form, then you will surely attain Me; this is My promise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हेंच कायिसया होये। ऐसा जरी संदेहो वर्ततु आहे। तरी अभ्यासूनि आदीं पाहें।॥ मग नव्हे तरी कोपें॥८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃca kāyisayā hoye| aisā jarī saṃdeho vartatu āhe| tarī abhyāsūni ādīṃ pāheṃ||| maga navhe tarī kopeṃ||80||
verses.meaning: If you have a doubt as to how this can be, then first try it through practice. If it still doesn't happen, then you may be angry.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणेंचि अभ्यासेंसीं योगु। चित्तासि करी पां चांगु । अगा उपायबळें पंगु । 'पहाड़ ठाकी॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃci abhyāseṃsīṃ yogu| cittāsi karī pāṃ cāṃgu | agā upāyabaḻeṃ paṃgu | 'pahār̤a ṭhākī|| 81||
verses.meaning: Through this very practice, one can achieve a good state of Yoga for the mind. Just as a lame person, by the strength of a good plan, can conquer a mountain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेविं सदभ्यासें निरंतर । चित्तासि परमपुरुषाची मोहर । 'लावीं मग शरीर। राहो अथवा जावो॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: teviṃ sadabhyāseṃ niraṃtara | cittāsi paramapuruṣācī mohara | 'lāvīṃ maga śarīra| rāho athavā jāvo|| 82||
verses.meaning: Thus, through continuous good practice, imprint the Supreme Being upon your mind. Then, let the body remain or depart, as it may.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें नानागतीतें पाववितें। तें चित्त वरील आत्मयातें । मग कवण आठवी देहातें। गेलें कों आहे ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ nānāgatīteṃ pāvaviteṃ| teṃ citta varīla ātmayāteṃ | maga kavaṇa āṭhavī dehāteṃ| geleṃ koṃ āhe || 83||
verses.meaning: That which leads to various states of being, that mind then attains the Self. Then who remembers the body, whether it is gone or present?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सरितेचेनि ओघें। सिंधुजळा मीनलळें घोघें। तें काय वर्तत आहे मागें । म्हणौनि पाहों येती ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ sariteceni ogheṃ| siṃdhujaḻā mīnalaḻeṃ ghogheṃ| teṃ kāya vartata āhe māgeṃ | mhaṇauni pāhoṃ yetī || 84||
verses.meaning: Just as the river, flowing with its current, merges with the ocean's waters, does it then look back to see what it has left behind?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तें समुद्रचि होऊन ठेलें। तेविं चित्ताचें चैतन्य जाहालें। जेथ यातायात निमालें। घनानंद जे॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā teṃ samudraci hoūna ṭheleṃ| teviṃ cittāceṃ caitanya jāhāleṃ| jetha yātāyāta nimāleṃ| ghanānaṃda je|| 85 ||
verses.meaning: It became the very ocean itself, just as the mind became pure consciousness. There, all comings and goings ceased, becoming dense bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचें आकारावीण असणें। जया जन्म ना निमणें। जें आघवेंचि आधवबवेंपणें । देखत असे॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāceṃ ākārāvīṇa asaṇeṃ| jayā janma nā nimaṇeṃ| jeṃ āghaveṃci ādhavabaveṃpaṇeṃ | dekhata ase|| 86||
verses.meaning: That which exists without form, which has neither birth nor death, and which perceives everything with its inherent awareness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें गगनाहूनि जुनें। जें परमाणूहूनि सानें। जयाचेनि सन्निधानें। विश्व चळे॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ gaganāhūni juneṃ| jeṃ paramāṇūhūni sāneṃ| jayāceni sannidhāneṃ| viśva caḻe|| 87||
verses.meaning: That which is older than the sky, that which is smaller than an atom, by whose mere presence the universe moves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे सर्वातें यया विये। विश्व सर्व जेणें जिये। हेतु जया बिहे। अचिंत्य जें ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: je sarvāteṃ yayā viye| viśva sarva jeṇeṃ jiye| hetu jayā bihe| aciṃtya jeṃ || 88||
verses.meaning: That which gives birth to all, that by which the universe lives, that which even the cause fears, that which is inconceivable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखें बोळंबा इंगळु न चरे। तेजीं तिमिर न शिरे। जें दिहाचें अंधारें। चर्मचक्षूसीं ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekheṃ boḻaṃbā iṃgaḻu na care| tejīṃ timira na śire| jeṃ dihāceṃ aṃdhāreṃ| carmacakṣūsīṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Just as a snake cannot swallow a burning coal, and darkness cannot enter light, so too the darkness of ignorance cannot be perceived by the eyes of wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुसडा सूर्यकणांच्या राशी। जो नित्य उदो ज्ञानियांसी। अस्तमानाचें जयासी । आडनांव नाहीं ॥९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: susaḍā sūryakaṇāṃcyā rāśī| jo nitya udo jñāniyāṃsī| astamānāceṃ jayāsī | āḍanāṃva nāhīṃ ||90||
verses.meaning: He is the constant rising sun for the wise, a sun whose rays are ever-present, for whom the concept of setting or decline is entirely unknown.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया अव्यंगवाणेया ब्रह्मातें । प्रयाणकाले प्राप्ते। जो स्थिरावलेनि चित्तें । जाणोनि स्मरे॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā avyaṃgavāṇeyā brahmāteṃ | prayāṇakāle prāpte| jo sthirāvaleni citteṃ | jāṇoni smare|| 91||
verses.meaning: When the time of departure arrives, one who, with a steady mind, knows and remembers that flawless Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बाहेरी पद्यासन रचुनी। उत्तराभिमुख बैसोनि । जीवीं सुख सूनि। क्रमयोगाचें ॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: bāherī padyāsana racunī| uttarābhimukha baisoni | jīvīṃ sukha sūni| kramayogāceṃ || 92||
verses.meaning: Arranging the Padmasana outside, facing north, and experiencing the joy of the path of action within the soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आंतु मीनलेनि मनोधर्में । स्वरूपप्राप्तीचेनि प्रेमें। आपेंआप संभ्रमें, मिळावया॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṃtu mīnaleni manodharmeṃ | svarūpaprāptīceni premeṃ| āpeṃāpa saṃbhrameṃ, miḻāvayā|| 93||
verses.meaning: With the mind absorbed within, and with the love for attaining one's true nature, one spontaneously and eagerly merges with it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आकळलेनि योगें। मध्यमा- मध्यमार्गे। अग्निस्थानौनि निगे। ब्रह्मरंधा ॥९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ākaḻaleni yogeṃ| madhyamā- madhyamārge| agnisthānauni nige| brahmaraṃdhā ||94||
verses.meaning: Through the practice of Yoga, the Kundalini energy, rising from the Manipura chakra, ascends through the central channel (Sushumna Nadi) and reaches the Brahmarandhra.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ अचेत चित्ताचा सांगातु। आहाचवाणा दिसे मांडतु । तेथ प्राणु गगनाआंतु । संचरे कां॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha aceta cittācā sāṃgātu| āhācavāṇā dise māṃḍatu | tetha prāṇu gaganāāṃtu | saṃcare kāṃ|| 95||
verses.meaning: There, the company of the unconscious mind appears to be a sudden, unexpected display. How then can the life-breath move within the sky of consciousness?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मनाचेनि स्थैर्ये धरिला । भक्‍तीचिया भावना भरला । योगबळें आवरला । सज्ज होऊनि॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī manāceni sthairye dharilā | bhak‍tīciyā bhāvanā bharalā | yogabaḻeṃ āvaralā | sajja hoūni|| 96||
verses.meaning: But with the steadfastness of the mind, filled with the sentiment of devotion, and restrained by the power of yoga, one becomes ready.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो जडाजडातें विरवितु। भ्रूलतामाजीं संचरतु। जैसा घंटानाद लयस्तु। घंटेसीच होय॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: to jaḍājaḍāteṃ viravitu| bhrūlatāmājīṃ saṃcaratu| jaisā ghaṃṭānāda layastu| ghaṃṭesīca hoya|| 97||
verses.meaning: That (divine sound) dissolves the densest of matter, and moves within the eyebrows, just as the sound of a bell merges back into the bell itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां झांकलिया घटींचा दिवा । नेणिजे काय जाहला केव्हां। या रीतीं जो पांडवा । देह ठेवी॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ jhāṃkaliyā ghaṭīṃcā divā | neṇije kāya jāhalā kevhāṃ| yā rītīṃ jo pāṃḍavā | deha ṭhevī|| 98||
verses.meaning: Or, like a lamp hidden within a pot, one knows not when it was extinguished. In this manner, O Pandava, he casts off his body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो केवळ परब्रह्म जया परमपुरुष ऐसें नाम। तें माझें निजधाम। होऊनि ठाके ॥९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: to kevaḻa parabrahma jayā paramapuruṣa aiseṃ nāma| teṃ mājheṃ nijadhāma| hoūni ṭhāke ||99||
verses.meaning: That alone is the Supreme Brahman, known as the Supreme Being. That becomes my true abode.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सकळां जाणणेयां जे लाणी। तिये जाणिवेची जे खाणी । तयां ज्ञानियांचिये आयणी । जयातें अक्षरु म्हणिपे॥ ९००॥
verses.shloka_iast: sakaḻāṃ jāṇaṇeyāṃ je lāṇī| tiye jāṇivecī je khāṇī | tayāṃ jñāniyāṃciye āyaṇī | jayāteṃ akṣaru mhaṇipe|| 900||
verses.meaning: That which is the very essence of all knowledge, the mine of that knowing, the very abode of the wise, that indeed is called the Imperishable (Akshara).

verses.shloka_devanagari: चंडवातेंही न मोडे । तें गगनचि कीं फुडें। बांचूनि जरी होईल मेहुडें । तरी उरेल कैंचें ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: caṃḍavāteṃhī na moḍe | teṃ gaganaci kīṃ phuḍeṃ| bāṃcūni jarī hoīla mehuḍeṃ | tarī urela kaiṃceṃ || 1||
verses.meaning: The sky, indeed, cannot be broken even by a fierce storm. But if it were to become a cloud, how could it remain?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेविं जाणणेया जें आकळिलें। तें जाणिवळेपणेंचि उमाणलें। मग नेणवेचि तया म्हणितलें। अक्षर सहजे ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: teviṃ jāṇaṇeyā jeṃ ākaḻileṃ| teṃ jāṇivaḻepaṇeṃci umāṇaleṃ| maga neṇaveci tayā mhaṇitaleṃ| akṣara sahaje || 2||
verses.meaning: Thus, what is grasped by knowledge is also measured by that very knowing. Then, what is called the unknowable, the imperishable, naturally reveals itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणोनि वेदविद नर। म्हणती जयातें अक्षर । जें प्रकृतीसी पर। परमात्मरूप॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇoni vedavida nara| mhaṇatī jayāteṃ akṣara | jeṃ prakṛtīsī para| paramātmarūpa|| 3||
verses.meaning: Therefore, those who know the Vedas call that the Imperishable, which is beyond Prakriti, the form of the Supreme Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि विषयांचे विष उलंडूनि। जे सर्वेद्रियां प्रायश्चित्त देऊनि। आहाति देहाचिया बेसोनि। झाडातळीं ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi viṣayāṃce viṣa ulaṃḍūni| je sarvedriyāṃ prāyaścitta deūni| āhāti dehāciyā besoni| jhāḍātaḻīṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: And having overcome the poison of worldly pleasures, they have given penance to all their senses, and now sit under the tree of their body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते यापरी विरक्त । जयाची निरंतर वाट पाहात। निष्कामासि अभिप्रेत । सर्वदा जें ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: te yāparī virakta | jayācī niraṃtara vāṭa pāhāta| niṣkāmāsi abhipreta | sarvadā jeṃ || 5||
verses.meaning: That is how the detached ones, whose path is constantly awaited, always desire the state of desirelessness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचिया आवडी । न गणिती ब्रह्मचर्याचीं सांकडीं । निष्ठुर होऊनि बापुडीं । इंद्रियें करिती ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāciyā āvaḍī | na gaṇitī brahmacaryācīṃ sāṃkaḍīṃ | niṣṭhura hoūni bāpuḍīṃ | iṃdriyeṃ karitī || 6||
verses.meaning: Out of love for Him, they do not consider the hardships of celibacy; becoming resolute, the poor senses perform their duties.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जें पद। दुर्लभ आणि अगाध । जयाचिये थडिये वेद। चुबुकळिले ठेळे॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jeṃ pada| durlabha āṇi agādha | jayāciye thaḍiye veda| cubukaḻile ṭheḻe|| 7||
verses.meaning: Such is that state, rare and unfathomable, at whose shore even the Vedas stand bewildered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें ते पुरुष होती । जे यापरी लया जाती । तरी पार्था हेचि स्थिती। एक वेळ सांगों ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ te puruṣa hotī | je yāparī layā jātī | tarī pārthā heci sthitī| eka veḻa sāṃgoṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: Those who merge in this manner become that Purusha. Therefore, Arjuna, I will explain this state to you once more.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ अर्जुनें म्हणितलें स्वामी । हेंचि म्हणावया होतों पां मी । तंव सहजें कृपा केली तुम्ही । तरी बोलिजो कां ॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha arjuneṃ mhaṇitaleṃ svāmī | heṃci mhaṇāvayā hotoṃ pāṃ mī | taṃva sahajeṃ kṛpā kelī tumhī | tarī bolijo kāṃ ||9||
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna said, "Lord, I was just about to ask this very thing. And now, by your grace, you have spontaneously granted it. So please speak."

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि बोलावें तें अति सोहोपें। तेथें म्हणितलें त्रिभुवनदीपें। तुज काय नेणों संक्षेपें। सांगेन ऐक ॥ ९११०॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari bolāveṃ teṃ ati sohopeṃ| tetheṃ mhaṇitaleṃ tribhuvanadīpeṃ| tuja kāya neṇoṃ saṃkṣepeṃ| sāṃgena aika || 9110||
verses.meaning: But what is to be said is very simple. There, the lamp of the three worlds said, "What I do not know about you, I will tell you briefly, listen."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी मना या बाहेरिळीकडे । यावयाची साविया सवे मोडे । हें हृदयाचिया डोहीं बुडे । तैसें कौोजे॥११॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī manā yā bāheriḻīkaḍe | yāvayācī sāviyā save moḍe | heṃ hṛdayāciyā ḍohīṃ buḍe | taiseṃ kauoje||11||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the mind's habit of wandering outwards should be completely broken. It should be made to drown in the depths of the heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें तरीच घडे । जरी संयमाची अखंडे । सर्वद्वारी कवाडें। कळासती॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ tarīca ghaḍe | jarī saṃyamācī akhaṃḍe | sarvadvārī kavāḍeṃ| kaḻāsatī|| 12||
verses.meaning: However, this is only possible if the doors of all senses are continuously and firmly closed through self-control.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सहजें मन कोंडलें। हृदयींचि असेल उगलें। जैसें करचरणीं मोडलें। परिवरु न संडी॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sahajeṃ mana koṃḍaleṃ| hṛdayīṃci asela ugaleṃ| jaiseṃ karacaraṇīṃ moḍaleṃ| parivaru na saṃḍī|| 13||
verses.meaning: Even if the mind is naturally confined, it remains open in the heart, just as a broken hand or foot does not abandon its family.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें चित्त राहिलिया पांडवा । प्राणांचा प्रणवुचि करावा । मग अनुवृत्तिपंथें आणावा । मूर्धिववरी ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ citta rāhiliyā pāṃḍavā | prāṇāṃcā praṇavuci karāvā | maga anuvṛttipaṃtheṃ āṇāvā | mūrdhivavarī || 94||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, when the mind is thus steadied, one should then engage in the pranava (Om recitation) of the life-breath, and through the path of अनुवृत्ति (following the breath), bring it up to the crown of the head.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ आकाशीं मिळे न मिळे। तैसा धरावा धारणाबळें। जंब मात्रात्रय मावळे । अर्धबिंबीं ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha ākāśīṃ miḻe na miḻe| taisā dharāvā dhāraṇābaḻeṃ| jaṃba mātrātraya māvaḻe | ardhabiṃbīṃ || 15||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky seems to merge and yet not merge, so too, through the power of sustained concentration, one should hold the mind until the three measures (A, U, M) dissolve into the half-measure (the bindu).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंबबरी तो समीरु । निराळीं कीजे स्थिरु । मग लग्नीं जेविं ऊकारु । बिंबींच वबिलसे॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃbabarī to samīru | nirāḻīṃ kīje sthiru | maga lagnīṃ jeviṃ ūkāru | biṃbīṃca vabilase|| 16||
verses.meaning: Just as the wind is stilled within the tent, and then the 'U' sound appears in the reflection of the 'Om' symbol, so too is the divine manifested.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ७ हें स्मरों सरे। आणि तेथेंचि प्राणु पुरे। मग प्रणवांतीं उरे । पूर्णघन जें॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ 7 heṃ smaroṃ sare| āṇi tetheṃci prāṇu pure| maga praṇavāṃtīṃ ure | pūrṇaghana jeṃ|| 17||
verses.meaning: In the same way, when this remembrance ceases, and the life-breath merges there, then what remains at the end of the Pranava (Om) is the absolute, perfect fullness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि प्रणवैकनाम। हें एकाक्षर ब्रह्म। जो माझें स्वरूप परम । स्मरतसांता ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni praṇavaikanāma| heṃ ekākṣara brahma| jo mājheṃ svarūpa parama | smaratasāṃtā || 18||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the one name, Om, is the single-syllable Brahman, which is My supreme form, to be remembered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यापरी त्यजी देहातें। तो त्रिशुद्धी पावे मातें॥ जया पावणया परीतें । आणिक पावणें नाहीं ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yāparī tyajī dehāteṃ| to triśuddhī pāve māteṃ|| jayā pāvaṇayā parīteṃ | āṇika pāvaṇeṃ nāhīṃ || 19||
verses.meaning: In this way, one who abandons the body, truly attains Me. There is no other attainment like attaining Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ अर्जुना जरी विपायें। तुझ्या जीवीं हन ऐसें जाये। ना हें स्मरण मग होये। कायसयावरी अंतीं ॥ ९२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha arjunā jarī vipāyeṃ| tujhyā jīvīṃ hana aiseṃ jāye| nā heṃ smaraṇa maga hoye| kāyasayāvarī aṃtīṃ || 920||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, if by chance such a thought arises in your mind, 'How will I remember this at the end?'

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियां अनुघड पडलिया। जीविताचें सुख बुडालिया। आंतुबाहेरी उघडलिया । मृत्युचिन्हें ॥ २१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyāṃ anughaḍa paḍaliyā| jīvitāceṃ sukha buḍāliyā| āṃtubāherī ughaḍaliyā | mṛtyucinheṃ || 219||
verses.meaning: When the senses become unresponsive, the joy of life is lost, and the signs of death become evident both within and without.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं बैसावेंचि कवणें । मग कवण निरोधी करणें। तेथ काह्याचेनि अंतःकरणें। प्रणव स्मरावा ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ baisāveṃci kavaṇeṃ | maga kavaṇa nirodhī karaṇeṃ| tetha kāhyāceni aṃtaḥkaraṇeṃ| praṇava smarāvā || 22||
verses.meaning: At that time, who would even sit? Then who would give instructions? With whose inner being should one remember the Pranava (Om)?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरि गा ऐशिया हो ध्वनी । झणें थारा देशी हो मनीं। पैं नित्य सेविला मी निदानीं। सेवकु होय॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tari gā aiśiyā ho dhvanī | jhaṇeṃ thārā deśī ho manīṃ| paiṃ nitya sevilā mī nidānīṃ| sevaku hoya|| 23||
verses.meaning: Therefore, do not give place in your mind to such thoughts. For I am eternally served, and thus become a servant in the end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे विषयांसि तिळांजळी देउनी । प्रवृत्तीवरी निगड वाऊनि । मातें हृदयीं सूनि। भोगिताती ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: je viṣayāṃsi tiḻāṃjaḻī deunī | pravṛttīvarī nigaḍa vāūni | māteṃ hṛdayīṃ sūni| bhogitātī || 24||
verses.meaning: Those who offer a sesame seed oblation to worldly pleasures, bind their worldly inclinations, and place Me in their heart, thus experience true enjoyment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि भोगितया आराणुका । भेटणें नाहीं क्ष॒धादिकां । तेथ चक्षुरादि रंका। कवण पाडु॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari bhogitayā ārāṇukā | bheṭaṇeṃ nāhīṃ kṣa̱dhādikāṃ | tetha cakṣurādi raṃkā| kavaṇa pāḍu|| 25||
verses.meaning: When one experiences the ultimate bliss, there is no hunger or thirst. What then can the senses like the eyes do there?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे निरंतर एकवटले। जे अंतःकरणीं मजशीं लिंगटले । मीचि होऊनि आटले। उपासिती॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise niraṃtara ekavaṭale| je aṃtaḥkaraṇīṃ majaśīṃ liṃgaṭale | mīci hoūni āṭale| upāsitī|| 26||
verses.meaning: Those who are thus constantly united, who cling to Me in their hearts, becoming one with Me, they worship Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयां देहावसान जें पावे। तैं तिहीं मातें स्मरावें। मग म्यां जरी पावावें। तरि उपास्ति ते कायसी ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāṃ dehāvasāna jeṃ pāve| taiṃ tihīṃ māteṃ smarāveṃ| maga myāṃ jarī pāvāveṃ| tari upāsti te kāyasī || 27||
verses.meaning: When their bodies reach their end, then they should remember Me. If I am to be attained then, what is the purpose of devotion?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं रंक एक आडलेपणें। काकुळती धांव गा धांब म्हणे । तरि तयाचिये ग्लानि धांवणें। काय न घडे मज॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ raṃka eka āḍalepaṇeṃ| kākuḻatī dhāṃva gā dhāṃba mhaṇe | tari tayāciye glāni dhāṃvaṇeṃ| kāya na ghaḍe maja|| 28||
verses.meaning: If a poor, helpless person, in distress, cries out, "Run, run!" then why would I not run to alleviate their suffering?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि भक्तांही तेचि दशा। तरी भक्तीचा सोसु कायसा । म्हणौनि हा ध्वनि ऐसा। न वाखाणावा॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi bhaktāṃhī teci daśā| tarī bhaktīcā sosu kāyasā | mhaṇauni hā dhvani aisā| na vākhāṇāvā|| 29||
verses.meaning: And the same state applies to devotees. So what is the purpose of devotion? Therefore, this interpretation should not be expounded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिहीं जे वेळीं मी स्मरावा। ते वेळीं स्मरला कीं 'पाबावा। तो आभारुही जीवा। साहवेचि ना ॥१३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tihīṃ je veḻīṃ mī smarāvā| te veḻīṃ smaralā kīṃ 'pābāvā| to ābhāruhī jīvā| sāhaveci nā ||130||
verses.meaning: When they remember Me, and I am remembered, that very act of remembering becomes a burden to My soul, for I am bound to fulfill their wishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें क्रणवैपण देखोनि आंगीं। मी आपुलियाचि उत्तीर्णत्वालागीं। भक्‍तांचियां तनुत्यागीं। १४६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी परिचर्या करीं ॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ kraṇavaipaṇa dekhoni āṃgīṃ| mī āpuliyāci uttīrṇatvālāgīṃ| bhak‍tāṃciyāṃ tanutyāgīṃ| 146 śrījñāneśvarī paricaryā karīṃ || 31||
verses.meaning: Seeing that devotion, I, for the sake of my own transcendence, serve the devotees who sacrifice their bodies.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देहवैकल्याचा वारा। झणें लागेळ या सुकुमारा। म्हणौनि आत्मबोधाचिया पांजिरां। सूये तयातें ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: dehavaikalyācā vārā| jhaṇeṃ lāgeḻa yā sukumārā| mhaṇauni ātmabodhāciyā pāṃjirāṃ| sūye tayāteṃ || 32||
verses.meaning: Lest the wind of bodily infirmity should touch this tender one, he places him in the cage of self-knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरि आपुलिया स्मरणाची उवाइली । हींब ऐसी करीं साउली । ऐसेनि नित्यबुद्धी संचली। मी आणीं तयातें ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: vari āpuliyā smaraṇācī uvāilī | hīṃba aisī karīṃ sāulī | aiseni nityabuddhī saṃcalī| mī āṇīṃ tayāteṃ || 33||
verses.meaning: Above all, I bring to myself those who, with unwavering intellect, constantly remember Me, as if seeking shelter from the heat under the cool shade of My remembrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणोनि देहांतींचें सांकडें। माझिया कहींचि न पडे । मी आपुलियातें आपुलीकडे। सुखेंचि आणीं॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇoni dehāṃtīṃceṃ sāṃkaḍeṃ| mājhiyā kahīṃci na paḍe | mī āpuliyāteṃ āpulīkaḍe| sukheṃci āṇīṃ|| 34||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the distress of the end of the body never falls upon me. I easily draw my own unto myself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरचील देहाची गंबसणी फेडुनी। आहाच अहंकाराचे रज झाडुनी। शुद्ध वासना निवडुनी। आपणणपां मेळवीं ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: varacīla dehācī gaṃbasaṇī pheḍunī| āhāca ahaṃkārāce raja jhāḍunī| śuddha vāsanā nivaḍunī| āpaṇaṇapāṃ meḻavīṃ || 35 ||
verses.meaning: Shedding the outer garment of the body, sweeping away the dust of ego, and purifying the desires, one merges into the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि भक्तां तरी देहीं । विशेष एकवंकीचा ठावो नाहीं । म्हणौनि अव्हेरू करितां कांहीं । वियोगु ऐसा न वाटे ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi bhaktāṃ tarī dehīṃ | viśeṣa ekavaṃkīcā ṭhāvo nāhīṃ | mhaṇauni avherū karitāṃ kāṃhīṃ | viyogu aisā na vāṭe || 36||
verses.meaning: And for devotees, there is no special attachment to the body. Therefore, even if they renounce something, they do not feel separation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी देहांतींचि मियां यावें । मग आपणणपें यातें न्यावें। हेंही नाहीं स्वभावें। जे आधींचि मज मीनळे॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī dehāṃtīṃci miyāṃ yāveṃ | maga āpaṇaṇapeṃ yāteṃ nyāveṃ| heṃhī nāhīṃ svabhāveṃ| je ādhīṃci maja mīnaḻe|| 37||
verses.meaning: It is not that I come at the end of the body's life and then take them to myself. This is not my nature, for they are already merged with me from the very beginning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरी शरीराचिया सलिलीं। असतेपण हे साउली । वांचूनि चंद्रिका ते ठेली । चंद्रींच आहे॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerī śarīrāciyā salilīṃ| asatepaṇa he sāulī | vāṃcūni caṃdrikā te ṭhelī | caṃdrīṃca āhe|| 38||
verses.meaning: The existence of the body is like a shadow in water; the moonlight, however, remains in the moon itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे जे नित्ययुक्‍त । तयांसि सुलभ मी सतत। म्हणौनि देहांतीं निचित । मीचि होती ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise je nityayuk‍ta | tayāṃsi sulabha mī satata| mhaṇauni dehāṃtīṃ nicita | mīci hotī || 39||
verses.meaning: To those who are ever united with Me, I am easily attainable. Therefore, at the end of their lives, they certainly become Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग क्लेशतरूची वाडी। जे तापत्रयाग्नीची सगडी । जे मृत्युकाकासीं कुरोंडी । सांडिली आहे॥ १४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga kleśatarūcī vāḍī| je tāpatrayāgnīcī sagaḍī | je mṛtyukākāsīṃ kuroṃḍī | sāṃḍilī āhe|| 140||
verses.meaning: Then, the growth of the tree of suffering, which is the fuel for the fire of the three afflictions, and which is an offering left for the crow of death, is abandoned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें दैन्याचें दुभतें। जें महाभयातें वाढवितें। जें सकळ दुःखाचें पुरतें। भांडवल॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ dainyāceṃ dubhateṃ| jeṃ mahābhayāteṃ vāḍhaviteṃ| jeṃ sakaḻa duḥkhāceṃ purateṃ| bhāṃḍavala|| 41||
verses.meaning: That which is the milk of misery, that which increases great fear, that which is the complete capital of all sorrows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें दुर्मतीचें मूळ। जें कुकर्माचें 'फळ। जें व्यामोहाचें केवळ । स्वरूपचि॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ durmatīceṃ mūḻa| jeṃ kukarmāceṃ 'phaḻa| jeṃ vyāmohāceṃ kevaḻa | svarūpaci|| 42||
verses.meaning: That which is the root of evil thoughts, the fruit of wicked deeds, and the very embodiment of delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें संसाराचें बैसणें। जें विकारांचे उद्यानें ( उदाणें )। जें सकळ रोगांचें भाणें। वाढिळें आहे॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ saṃsārāceṃ baisaṇeṃ| jeṃ vikārāṃce udyāneṃ ( udāṇeṃ )| jeṃ sakaḻa rogāṃceṃ bhāṇeṃ| vāḍhiḻeṃ āhe|| 43||
verses.meaning: That which is the seat of worldly existence, that which is the origin of all afflictions, that which is the vessel of all diseases, has grown and expanded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें काळाचा खिचु उशिटा। जें आशेचा आंगवठा । जन्ममरणाचा वोलिंबटा । स्वभावें जें॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ kāḻācā khicu uśiṭā| jeṃ āśecā āṃgavaṭhā | janmamaraṇācā voliṃbaṭā | svabhāveṃ jeṃ|| 44||
verses.meaning: That which is the leftover of time, that which is the threshold of desire, that which is the entanglement of birth and death – such is its very nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें भुलीचें भरिव । विकल्पाचें बोतिंबव। किंबहुना पेंव । विंचुवांचें ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ bhulīceṃ bhariva | vikalpāceṃ botiṃbava| kiṃbahunā peṃva | viṃcuvāṃceṃ || 45 ||
verses.meaning: It is like a delusion, a seed of doubt, or rather, a nest of scorpions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें व्याघ्राचें क्षेत्र । जें पण्यांगनेचें मैत्र । जें विषयविज्ञानयंत्र । सुपूजित॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ vyāghrāceṃ kṣetra | jeṃ paṇyāṃganeceṃ maitra | jeṃ viṣayavijñānayaṃtra | supūjita|| 46||
verses.meaning: Like a tiger's territory, like the friendship of a courtesan, like a well-worshipped machine of worldly knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें लावेचा कळवळा । निवालिया विषोदकाचा गळाळा । जें बिश्‍वासु आंगवळा। संवबचोराचा ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ lāvecā kaḻavaḻā | nivāliyā viṣodakācā gaḻāḻā | jeṃ biś‍vāsu āṃgavaḻā| saṃvabacorācā || 47||
verses.meaning: It is like the tenderness of a creeper, the coolness of a stream of water that has lost its poison, or the natural trust of a thief in his accomplice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें कोढियाचें खेंब। जें काळसर्पाचें मार्दव। गोरियेचें स्वभाव। गायन जें॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ koḍhiyāceṃ kheṃba| jeṃ kāḻasarpāceṃ mārdava| goriyeceṃ svabhāva| gāyana jeṃ|| 48||
verses.meaning: Just as a leper's body is repulsive, just as a black serpent's nature is venomous, and just as a demoness's inherent disposition is to sing discordantly, so too is the nature of worldly attachments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें बैरियाचा पाहुणेरु । जें दुर्जञजाचा आदरु। हें असो जें सागरु। अनर्थांचा॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ bairiyācā pāhuṇeru | jeṃ durjañajācā ādaru| heṃ aso jeṃ sāgaru| anarthāṃcā|| 49||
verses.meaning: It is like a feast for an enemy, or respect shown to a wicked person. Let it be said, it is an ocean of calamities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें स्वणीं देखिलें स्वप्न। जें मृगजळें सासिन्नळलें वन। जें धूगम्ररजांचें गगन । ओतलें आहे॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ svaṇīṃ dekhileṃ svapna| jeṃ mṛgajaḻeṃ sāsinnaḻaleṃ vana| jeṃ dhūgamrarajāṃceṃ gagana | otaleṃ āhe|| 150||
verses.meaning: Like a dream seen in a dream, like a forest created by a mirage, like a sky formed by smoke and dust.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जें हें शरीर| तें ते न पवतीचि पुढती नर। जे होऊनि ठेळे अपार। स्वरूप माझें॥५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jeṃ heṃ śarīra| teṃ te na pavatīci puḍhatī nara| je hoūni ṭheḻe apāra| svarūpa mājheṃ||51||
verses.meaning: Such a body, they do not attain again, those who have become one with my boundless true nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं ब्रह्मपणाचिये भडसे। न चुकतीचि पुनरावृत्तीचे बळसे। परि निवटलियाचें जैसें। पोट न दुखे॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ brahmapaṇāciye bhaḍase| na cukatīci punarāvṛttīce baḻase| pari nivaṭaliyāceṃ jaiseṃ| poṭa na dukhe|| 52||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, even with the pretense of Brahmanhood, the cycle of rebirth is not escaped. But just as one who is satiated does not feel hunger pangs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी चेइलियानंतरें। न बुडिजे स्वपींचेनि महापूरें। तेवीं मातें पावळे ते संसारें। लिंपतीचि ना॥५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī ceiliyānaṃtareṃ| na buḍije svapīṃceni mahāpūreṃ| tevīṃ māteṃ pāvaḻe te saṃsāreṃ| liṃpatīci nā||53||
verses.meaning: Just as one is not drowned by the great flood of a dream after waking up, similarly, those who attain Me are not touched by the worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हबीं जगदाकाराचें सिरें। जें चिरस्थायीयांचे धुरे। ब्रह्मभुवन गा चबरें। लोकाचळाचें॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhabīṃ jagadākārāceṃ sireṃ| jeṃ cirasthāyīyāṃce dhure| brahmabhuvana gā cabareṃ| lokācaḻāceṃ|| 54||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, the very form of the universe, which is the foremost among the eternal, is indeed the abode of Brahman, the support of all worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिये गांबींचा पहारु दिवोबरी। एका अमरेंद्राचें आयुष्य न धरी। विळोनि पांतीं उठी एकीसरीं । चबदाजणांचीं ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiye gāṃbīṃcā pahāru divobarī| ekā amareṃdrāceṃ āyuṣya na dharī| viḻoni pāṃtīṃ uṭhī ekīsarīṃ | cabadājaṇāṃcīṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: The watch of whose womb, lasting for a day, does not even hold the lifespan of one Indra; but in a single moment, it gives rise to fourteen Indras.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैं चौकडिया सहस्त्र जाये। तें ठाये ठावो विळुचि होये । आणि तैसेंचि सहस्त्रवरिये पाहे। रात्री जेथ ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiṃ caukaḍiyā sahastra jāye| teṃ ṭhāye ṭhāvo viḻuci hoye | āṇi taiseṃci sahastravariye pāhe| rātrī jetha || 56||
verses.meaning: When a thousand ages pass, that place becomes a void. And similarly, where a thousand years of night exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येवढें अहोरात्र जेथिंचें । तेणें न लोटती जे भाग्याचे । देखती ते स्वर्गीचे। चिरंजीव ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yevaḍheṃ ahorātra jethiṃceṃ | teṇeṃ na loṭatī je bhāgyāce | dekhatī te svargīce| ciraṃjīva || 57||
verses.meaning: Even with such a long day and night, those fortunate ones who behold it do not find it passing; they are the immortals of heaven.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरां सुरगणांची नवाई । विशेष सांगावी येथ काई । मुद्दल इंद्राचीचि दशा पाहीं। जे दिहाचे चौदा ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerāṃ suragaṇāṃcī navāī | viśeṣa sāṃgāvī yetha kāī | muddala iṃdrācīci daśā pāhīṃ| je dihāce caudā || 58||
verses.meaning: What more is there to say about the novelty of other gods? Just look at the fundamental state of Indra, which changes fourteen times a day.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि ब्रह्मयाचियाहि आठां पाहारांतें। आपुलिया डोळां देखते । जे आहाति गा तयांतें। अहोरात्रविद म्हणिपे॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari brahmayāciyāhi āṭhāṃ pāhārāṃteṃ| āpuliyā ḍoḻāṃ dekhate | je āhāti gā tayāṃteṃ| ahorātravida mhaṇipe|| 59||
verses.meaning: Those who witness even Brahma's eight watches with their own eyes, they are called knowers of day and night.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तये ब्रह्मभुवनीं दिवसें पाहे। ते वेळीं गणना केहीं न समाये । ऐसें अव्यक्ताचें होये। व्यक्त विश्‍व ॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taye brahmabhuvanīṃ divaseṃ pāhe| te veḻīṃ gaṇanā kehīṃ na samāye | aiseṃ avyaktāceṃ hoye| vyakta viś‍va || 160||
verses.meaning: When the day of Brahma dawns, its duration cannot be calculated. Such is the manifestation of the unmanifest universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुढती दिहाची चौपाहारी फिटे। आणि हा आकारसमपुद्र आटे । पाठीं तैसाचि मग पाहांटे। भरों लागे॥ ६१ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: puḍhatī dihācī caupāhārī phiṭe| āṇi hā ākārasamapudra āṭe | pāṭhīṃ taisāci maga pāhāṃṭe| bharoṃ lāge|| 61 ||
verses.meaning: Again, the four watches of the day pass, and this ocean of forms recedes. Then, in the same way, at dawn, it begins to fill again.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शारदीयेचिये प्रवेशीं। अभ्रे जिरती आकाशीं । मग ग्रीष्मांतीं जैशीं । निगती पुढती ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: śāradīyeciye praveśīṃ| abhre jiratī ākāśīṃ | maga grīṣmāṃtīṃ jaiśīṃ | nigatī puḍhatī || 62||
verses.meaning: In the autumn season, clouds dissipate in the sky, only to reappear again after the summer, just as they were before.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैशी ब्रह्मदिनाचिये आदी। हे भूतसृष्टीची मांदी। मिळे जंब सहस्त्रावधी । निमित्त पुरे ( निमति युगें) ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiśī brahmadināciye ādī| he bhūtasṛṣṭīcī māṃdī| miḻe jaṃba sahastrāvadhī | nimitta pure ( nimati yugeṃ) || 63||
verses.meaning: Just as in the beginning of Brahma's day, this multitude of beings comes into existence, similarly, thousands of yugas (epochs) are created.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं रात्रींचा अवसरु होये। आणि विश्‍व अव्यक्तीं ल्या जाये। तोही युगसहस्त्र मोटका पाहे। आणि तेैसेंचि रचे॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ rātrīṃcā avasaru hoye| āṇi viś‍va avyaktīṃ lyā jāye| tohī yugasahastra moṭakā pāhe| āṇi teaiseṃci race|| 64||
verses.meaning: Then comes the night, and the universe merges into the unmanifest. This period, too, is a thousand ages long, and then creation begins anew.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें सांगावया काय उपपत्ती । जे जगाचा प्रळयो ९४८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी आणि संभूती। इये ब्रह्मभुवनींचिया होती । अहोरात्रामाजीं ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ sāṃgāvayā kāya upapattī | je jagācā praḻayo 948 śrījñāneśvarī āṇi saṃbhūtī| iye brahmabhuvanīṃciyā hotī | ahorātrāmājīṃ || 65||
verses.meaning: What is there to say about this, that the dissolution and creation of the world occur within a day and night of Brahma's abode?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कैसें थोरिवेचें मान पाहें पां। तो सृष्टिबीजाचा साटोपा । परि पुनरावृत्तीचिया मापा। शीग जाहाला॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kaiseṃ thoriveceṃ māna pāheṃ pāṃ| to sṛṣṭibījācā sāṭopā | pari punarāvṛttīciyā māpā| śīga jāhālā|| 66||
verses.meaning: Behold the measure of its greatness! Though it is the very seed of creation, it has become the pinnacle of the measure of non-return.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं त्रैलोक्य हें धनुर्धरा । तिये गांबींचा गा पसारा । तो हा दिनोदयीं एकसरां। मांडतु असे ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ trailokya heṃ dhanurdharā | tiye gāṃbīṃcā gā pasārā | to hā dinodayīṃ ekasarāṃ| māṃḍatu ase || 67||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, O Arjuna, this entire universe is but a manifestation of that very seed. It unfolds completely, all at once, with the dawn of day.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं रात्रींचा समो 'पावे। आणि अपैसाचि सांठवे। म्हणिये जेथिंचें तेथ स्वभावें । साम्यासी ये॥६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ rātrīṃcā samo 'pāve| āṇi apaisāci sāṃṭhave| mhaṇiye jethiṃceṃ tetha svabhāveṃ | sāmyāsī ye||68||
verses.meaning: Then, as night naturally follows day, everything spontaneously settles into its inherent balance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें वृक्षपण बीजासि आलें। कीं मेघ हें गगन जाहालें। तेसें अनेकत्व जेथ सामावलें। तें साम्य म्हणिपे॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ vṛkṣapaṇa bījāsi āleṃ| kīṃ megha heṃ gagana jāhāleṃ| teseṃ anekatva jetha sāmāvaleṃ| teṃ sāmya mhaṇipe|| 69||
verses.meaning: Just as the tree is contained within the seed, or the cloud is contained within the sky, so too is the oneness (Samya) where all diversity is encompassed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ समविषम न दिसे कांहीं । म्हणोनि भूतें हे भाष नाहीं । जेविं दूधचि जाहालिया दहीं।॥ नामरूप जाय॥ १७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha samaviṣama na dise kāṃhīṃ | mhaṇoni bhūteṃ he bhāṣa nāhīṃ | jeviṃ dūdhaci jāhāliyā dahīṃ||| nāmarūpa jāya|| 170||
verses.meaning: There, no distinction of sameness or difference is perceived; therefore, these beings have no separate identity, just as milk, having become yogurt, loses its original name and form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं आकारलोपासरिसें। जगाचें जगपण भ्रंशे। परि जेथें जाहाले तें जैसें । तैसेचि असे॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ ākāralopāsariseṃ| jagāceṃ jagapaṇa bhraṃśe| pari jetheṃ jāhāle teṃ jaiseṃ | taiseci ase|| 71||
verses.meaning: Similarly, with the dissolution of the form, the world's world-ness perishes. But that from which it arose remains just as it was.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैं तया नांव सहज अव्यक्त। आणि आकारावेळीं तेंचि व्यक्‍्त। हें एकास्तव एक सूचित । एऱ्हबीं दोनी नाहीं ॥७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiṃ tayā nāṃva sahaja avyakta| āṇi ākārāveḻīṃ teṃci vyak‍ta| heṃ ekāstava eka sūcita | eṟhabīṃ donī nāhīṃ ||72||
verses.meaning: That is called the unmanifest, and when it takes form, it becomes manifest. One indicates the other; otherwise, neither of them exists.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें आटलिया रुपें। आटलेपण ते खोटी म्हणिपे। पुढती तो घनाकारु हारपे। जे वेळीं अळंकार होती ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ āṭaliyā rupeṃ| āṭalepaṇa te khoṭī mhaṇipe| puḍhatī to ghanākāru hārape| je veḻīṃ aḻaṃkāra hotī || 73||
verses.meaning: Just as when silver is melted, its molten state is considered temporary, and that solid form disappears again when it is fashioned into ornaments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हीं दोहीं जैेशीं होणीं। एकीं साक्षिभूत सुवर्णी । तैसी व्यक्‍ताव्यक्‍ताची 'कडसणी। वस्तूच्या ठायीं ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: hīṃ dohīṃ jaieśīṃ hoṇīṃ| ekīṃ sākṣibhūta suvarṇī | taisī vyak‍tāvyak‍tācī 'kaḍasaṇī| vastūcyā ṭhāyīṃ || 74||
verses.meaning: Just as these two, the ornament and the gold, are formed, with the gold being the witness, similarly, the manifest and the unmanifest are but the 'boundary' or 'distinction' within the ultimate Reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें तरी व्यक्‍त ना अव्यक्त। नित्य ना नाशवंत। या दोहींभावां अतीत। अनादिसिद्ध॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ tarī vyak‍ta nā avyakta| nitya nā nāśavaṃta| yā dohīṃbhāvāṃ atīta| anādisiddha|| 75||
verses.meaning: That (Brahman) is neither manifest nor unmanifest; neither eternal nor perishable. It is beyond these two states, eternally established without beginning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें हें विश्‍वचि होऊनि असे। परि विश्‍वपण नासिलेनि न नासे। अक्षरें पुसिल्या न पुसे । अर्थ जैसा॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ heṃ viś‍vaci hoūni ase| pari viś‍vapaṇa nāsileni na nāse| akṣareṃ pusilyā na puse | artha jaisā|| 76||
verses.meaning: Just as this universe exists, yet its 'universeness' is not destroyed even if it seems to be, similarly, a word's meaning is not erased even if the letters are wiped away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहें पां तरंग तरी होत जात। परि तेथ उदक तें अखंड असत । तेवीं भूताभावीं न नाशत। अविनाश जें ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāheṃ pāṃ taraṃga tarī hota jāta| pari tetha udaka teṃ akhaṃḍa asata | tevīṃ bhūtābhāvīṃ na nāśata| avināśa jeṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: Behold, waves rise and fall, yet the water remains ever-present. Similarly, that which is imperishable does not perish with the coming and going of beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी आटतिये अळंकारीं। नाटतें कनक असे जयापरी। तेवीं मरतिये जीवाकारीं। अमर जें आहे ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī āṭatiye aḻaṃkārīṃ| nāṭateṃ kanaka ase jayāparī| tevīṃ maratiye jīvākārīṃ| amara jeṃ āhe || 78||
verses.meaning: Just as gold, though shaped into various ornaments, remains imperishable, so too the immortal Self resides within the perishable body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयातें अव्यक्त म्हणों ये कोडें । म्हणतां स्तुति हें ऐसें नावडे । जें मना- बुद्धी न सांपडे। म्हणौनियां॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāteṃ avyakta mhaṇoṃ ye koḍeṃ | mhaṇatāṃ stuti heṃ aiseṃ nāvaḍe | jeṃ manā- buddhī na sāṃpaḍe| mhaṇauniyāṃ|| 79||
verses.meaning: That which is called the Unmanifest out of sheer wonder, yet even this praise does not seem fitting. That which cannot be grasped by the mind or intellect, and therefore remains beyond description.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आकारा आलिया जयाचें। निराकारपण न वचे । आकारलेोपें न विसंचे । नित्यता गा॥ १८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ākārā āliyā jayāceṃ| nirākārapaṇa na vace | ākāraleopeṃ na visaṃce | nityatā gā|| 180||
verses.meaning: And that which, upon taking form, does not lose its formless nature; nor does it cease to be eternal even when the form dissolves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि अक्षर जें म्हणिजे। तेवींचि म्हणतां बोधुहि उपजे। जयापरौता पैसु न देखिजे। या नाम परमगती॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni akṣara jeṃ mhaṇije| tevīṃci mhaṇatāṃ bodhuhi upaje| jayāparautā paisu na dekhije| yā nāma paramagatī|| 81||
verses.meaning: Therefore, that which is called the Imperishable (Akshara), by merely uttering it, spiritual understanding arises. Beyond this, no further attainment is seen; this is indeed the Supreme State.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि आघवा इहीं देहपुरीं ॥ आहे निजेलियाचे परी। जे व्यापारु करवी ना करी । म्हणौनियां॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari āghavā ihīṃ dehapurīṃ || āhe nijeliyāce parī| je vyāpāru karavī nā karī | mhaṇauniyāṃ|| 82||
verses.meaning: But in all these bodies, it is as if it is asleep. It neither performs actions nor causes them to be performed. Therefore.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱहवी जे शारीरचेष्टा। त्यांमाजीं एकही न ठके गा सुभटा । दाहीं इंद्रियांचिया वाटा । वाहतचि आहाती॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟahavī je śārīraceṣṭā| tyāṃmājīṃ ekahī na ṭhake gā subhaṭā | dāhīṃ iṃdriyāṃciyā vāṭā | vāhataci āhātī|| 83||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, O brave one, not a single bodily action ceases; the paths of all ten senses continue to flow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उकळूनि विषयांचा पेटा। होत मनाचा चोहटा। तो सुखदुःखाचा राजवांटा। भीतराहि पावे॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ukaḻūni viṣayāṃcā peṭā| hota manācā cohaṭā| to sukhaduḥkhācā rājavāṃṭā| bhītarāhi pāve|| 84||
verses.meaning: When the mind becomes a marketplace of worldly desires, the inner self also receives its share of joy and sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि रावो पहुडलिया सुखें। जैसा देशींचा व्यापार न ठके। प्रजा आपुलालेनि अभिलाखें। करितचि असती ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari rāvo pahuḍaliyā sukheṃ| jaisā deśīṃcā vyāpāra na ṭhake| prajā āpulāleni abhilākheṃ| karitaci asatī || 85 ||
verses.meaning: Just as when a king sleeps peacefully, the affairs of his kingdom do not cease; the subjects, driven by their own desires, continue to carry out their activities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें बुद्धीचे हन जाणणें। कां मनाचें घेणें देणें । इंद्रियांचे करणें । स्फुरण वायूचें ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ buddhīce hana jāṇaṇeṃ| kāṃ manāceṃ gheṇeṃ deṇeṃ | iṃdriyāṃce karaṇeṃ | sphuraṇa vāyūceṃ || 86||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the intellect's knowing, the mind's giving and taking, the senses' actions, and the vital breath's pulsation—all these are but manifestations.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे देहक्रिया आघवी । न करवितां होय बरवी । जैसा न चलवितेनि रवी। लोकु चाळे॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: he dehakriyā āghavī | na karavitāṃ hoya baravī | jaisā na calaviteni ravī| loku cāḻe|| 87||
verses.meaning: All these bodily functions happen perfectly without anyone making them happen, just as the sun, without moving, makes the world move.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना तयापरी । सुतला ऐसा आहे शरीरीं । म्हणौनि पुरुषु गा अवधारीं । म्हणिपे जयातें ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā tayāparī | sutalā aisā āhe śarīrīṃ | mhaṇauni puruṣu gā avadhārīṃ | mhaṇipe jayāteṃ || 88 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, the Purusha (the Self) is like one who is asleep in the body. Therefore, listen, it is called Purusha.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि प्रकृति पतित्रते। पडिला एकपत्नीत्रतें । येणेंहि कारणें जयातें। पुरुषु म्हणों ये॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi prakṛti patitrate| paḍilā ekapatnītrateṃ | yeṇeṃhi kāraṇeṃ jayāteṃ| puruṣu mhaṇoṃ ye|| 89||
verses.meaning: And because of this, the one who is devoted to nature as his only wife, can truly be called a 'Purusha' (the Supreme Being or conscious principle).

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं वेदाचें बहुवसपण। देखेचिना जयाचें आंगण । हें गगनाचें पांघरूण । होय देखा ॥ १९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ vedāceṃ bahuvasapaṇa| dekhecinā jayāceṃ āṃgaṇa | heṃ gaganāceṃ pāṃgharūṇa | hoya dekhā || 190||
verses.meaning: The Vedas themselves cannot fully describe that which is beyond all measure, whose very being is the expanse of the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जाणूनि योगीश्वर । जयातें म्हणती परात्पर। जें अनन्यगतीचें घर। गिंबसीत ये॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jāṇūni yogīśvara | jayāteṃ mhaṇatī parātpara| jeṃ ananyagatīceṃ ghara| giṃbasīta ye||91||
verses.meaning: Knowing this, the great yogis call that which is beyond the highest, the very abode of ultimate refuge, and they seek it with great longing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे तनुवाचाचित्तें। नाइकती दुजिये गोष्टीतें। तयां एकनिष्ठेचें पिकतें। सुक्षेत्र जें॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je tanuvācācitteṃ| nāikatī dujiye goṣṭīteṃ| tayāṃ ekaniṣṭheceṃ pikateṃ| sukṣetra jeṃ||92||
verses.meaning: Those who, with body, speech, and mind, do not listen to anything else, for them, devotion blossoms like a fertile field.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें त्रैलोक्यचि पुरुषोत्तमु। ऐसा साच जयाचा मनोधर्मु। तया आस्तिकाचा आश्रमु। पांडवा गा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ trailokyaci puruṣottamu| aisā sāca jayācā manodharmu| tayā āstikācā āśramu| pāṃḍavā gā|| 93||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, the abode of such a believer, whose conviction is truly that this entire universe is the Supreme Being (Purushottama) himself, is indeed blessed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें निगर्वाचें गौरव । जें निर्गुणाची जाणिव । जें सुखाची राणिव । निराशांसी ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ nigarvāceṃ gaurava | jeṃ nirguṇācī jāṇiva | jeṃ sukhācī rāṇiva | nirāśāṃsī || 94||
verses.meaning: It is the glory of humility, the awareness of the attributeless, the sovereignty of joy for those without desire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें संतोषियां वाढिलें ताट । जें अचिंता अनाथांचें मायपोट । भक्‍तीसी उजू वाट। जया गांबा॥ ९५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ saṃtoṣiyāṃ vāḍhileṃ tāṭa | jeṃ aciṃtā anāthāṃceṃ māyapoṭa | bhak‍tīsī ujū vāṭa| jayā gāṃbā|| 95 ||
verses.meaning: It is like a feast served to the contented, a mother's womb for the unconcerned and the orphaned, and a straight path to devotion, for which this village is renowned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें 'एकैक सांगोनि वायां। काय फार करूं धनंजया। पैं गेलिया जया ठाया । तो ठावोचि होईजे॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ 'ekaika sāṃgoni vāyāṃ| kāya phāra karūṃ dhanaṃjayā| paiṃ geliyā jayā ṭhāyā | to ṭhāvoci hoīje|| 96||
verses.meaning: What is the point, Dhananjaya, of elaborating on each and every one of these? For upon reaching that state, one becomes that very state itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हिंबाचिया झुळुका । जैसें हिंवचि पडे उष्णोदका। कां समोर जालिया अर्का । तमचि प्रकाशु होय॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: hiṃbāciyā jhuḻukā | jaiseṃ hiṃvaci paḍe uṣṇodakā| kāṃ samora jāliyā arkā | tamaci prakāśu hoya|| 97||
verses.meaning: Just as a cold breeze makes hot water cold, or darkness turns into light when it faces the sun.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा संसारु जया गांवा । गेला सांता पांडवा । होऊनि ठाके आघवा । मोक्षाचाचि॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā saṃsāru jayā gāṃvā | gelā sāṃtā pāṃḍavā | hoūni ṭhāke āghavā | mokṣācāci|| 98||
verses.meaning: Just as the village where the Pandavas resided became entirely a village of liberation, so too does the world become for one who attains this state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अग्नीमाजीं आलें। जैसें इंधनचि अग्नि जहाळें। पाठीं न निवडेचि कांहीं १५० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी केलें। काष्ठपण ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī agnīmājīṃ āleṃ| jaiseṃ iṃdhanaci agni jahāḻeṃ| pāṭhīṃ na nivaḍeci kāṃhīṃ 150 śrījñāneśvarī keleṃ| kāṣṭhapaṇa || 99||
verses.meaning: Just as firewood, when it enters fire, becomes fire itself, and its wood-ness is no longer distinguishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी साखरेचा माघौता । बुद्धीमंतपणेंही करितां । परि ऊंस नव्हे पंडुसुता । जियापरी ॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī sākharecā māghautā | buddhīmaṃtapaṇeṃhī karitāṃ | pari ūṃsa navhe paṃḍusutā | jiyāparī || 200||
verses.meaning: Just as sugar, no matter how intelligently processed, cannot revert to being sugarcane, O son of Pandu, so it is with the soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लोहाचें कनक जाहलें। हें एकें परिसेंचि केलें। आतां आणिक कैंचें तें गेळें। लोहत्व आणी ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: lohāceṃ kanaka jāhaleṃ| heṃ ekeṃ pariseṃci keleṃ| ātāṃ āṇika kaiṃceṃ teṃ geḻeṃ| lohatva āṇī || 1||
verses.meaning: When iron is transformed into gold by the touch of the philosopher's stone, how can it ever revert to its former state of iron?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तूप होऊनि माघोतें। जेवीं दूधपणा न येचि निरुतें। तेवीं पावोनियां जयातें । पुनरावृत्ति नाहीं ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tūpa hoūni māghoteṃ| jevīṃ dūdhapaṇā na yeci niruteṃ| tevīṃ pāvoniyāṃ jayāteṃ | punarāvṛtti nāhīṃ || 2||
verses.meaning: Therefore, just as ghee, once formed, never truly returns to its state of milk, so too, having attained that (state), there is no return.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें माझें परम । साचोकारें निजधाम । हें आंतुबट तुज वर्म। दाविजत असे॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ mājheṃ parama | sācokāreṃ nijadhāma | heṃ āṃtubaṭa tuja varma| dāvijata ase|| 3||
verses.meaning: That supreme abode is truly mine, my own true dwelling. This secret, this profound truth, I reveal to you from within.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि आणिकेंही एके प्रकारें। हें जाणतां आहे सोपारें। तरि देह सांडितेनि अवसरें। जेथ मिळती योगी ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci āṇikeṃhī eke prakāreṃ| heṃ jāṇatāṃ āhe sopāreṃ| tari deha sāṃḍiteni avasareṃ| jetha miḻatī yogī || 4||
verses.meaning: In the same way, there is another simple method to understand this: the place where yogis merge at the time of leaving the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा अवच्टें ऐसें घडे । जे अनवसरें देह सांडे। तरि माघोतें येणें घडे। देहासीचि॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā avacṭeṃ aiseṃ ghaḍe | je anavasareṃ deha sāṃḍe| tari māghoteṃ yeṇeṃ ghaḍe| dehāsīci|| 5||
verses.meaning: Or if it so happens by chance that the body is abandoned untimely, then it is destined to return to a body again.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि 'काळणशुद्धी जरी देह ठेविती । तरी ठेवितखेंबीं ब्रह्मच होती । एऱ्हवीं अकाळीं तरी येती। संसारा पुढती॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni 'kāḻaṇaśuddhī jarī deha ṭhevitī | tarī ṭhevitakheṃbīṃ brahmaca hotī | eṟhavīṃ akāḻīṃ tarī yetī| saṃsārā puḍhatī|| 6||
verses.meaning: Therefore, if one gives up the body with a pure understanding of time, they immediately become Brahman upon leaving it. Otherwise, if they depart at an untimely moment, they return to the cycle of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सायुज्य आणि पुनरावृत्ती । ये दोन्ही अवसराआधीन आहाती । तोचि अवबसरु तुजप्रती । प्रसंगें सांगों ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sāyujya āṇi punarāvṛttī | ye donhī avasarāādhīna āhātī | toci avabasaru tujapratī | prasaṃgeṃ sāṃgoṃ || 7||
verses.meaning: Similarly, both liberation (sayujya) and rebirth are dependent on a particular opportune moment. I will now explain that very moment to you, as it arises in this context.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरि ऐकें गा सुभटा । पातलिया मरणाचा माजिवटा । पांचे आपुलालिया वाटा । निघती अंतीं ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tari aikeṃ gā subhaṭā | pātaliyā maraṇācā mājivaṭā | pāṃce āpulāliyā vāṭā | nighatī aṃtīṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: Listen, O brave warrior, when death's dominion arrives, the five elements depart, each to its own path, in the end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा वरिपडिला प्रयाणकाळीं। बुद्धीतें भ्रमु न गिळी । स्मृति नव्हे आंधळी । न मरे मन॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā varipaḍilā prayāṇakāḻīṃ| buddhīteṃ bhramu na giḻī | smṛti navhe āṃdhaḻī | na mare mana|| 9||
verses.meaning: When one is thus prepared, at the time of departure, delusion does not swallow the intellect, memory does not become blind, and the mind does not die.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा चेतनावर्गु आघवा । मरणीं दिसे टवटवा। परि अनुभविलिया ब्रह्मभावा। गंवसणी होऊनि॥ २१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā cetanāvargu āghavā | maraṇīṃ dise ṭavaṭavā| pari anubhaviliyā brahmabhāvā| gaṃvasaṇī hoūni|| 210||
verses.meaning: This entire conscious realm, though appearing vibrant and fresh at the time of death, ultimately becomes one with the realization of Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा सावध हा समवावो। आणि निर्वाणवेऱहीं निर्वाहो। हें तरीच घडे जरी सावावो। अग्नीचा आथी ॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā sāvadha hā samavāvo| āṇi nirvāṇaveṟahīṃ nirvāho| heṃ tarīca ghaḍe jarī sāvāvo| agnīcā āthī || 11||
verses.meaning: Such a vigilant and continuous effort, sustained until liberation, is only possible if it is supported by the fire of spiritual knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहां पां वारेनें कां उदकें । जें दिवियाचें दिवेपण झांके। तैं असतीच काय देखे। दिठी आपुली॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāhāṃ pāṃ vāreneṃ kāṃ udakeṃ | jeṃ diviyāceṃ divepaṇa jhāṃke| taiṃ asatīca kāya dekhe| diṭhī āpulī|| 12||
verses.meaning: See, how the wind or water extinguishes the lamp's light. What then does its own sight perceive?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें देहांतींचेनि विषमवातें। देह आंत बाहेरि शइलेष्माआंते। तें विझोनि जाय उजितें। अग्नीचें तें ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ dehāṃtīṃceni viṣamavāteṃ| deha āṃta bāheri śaileṣmāāṃte| teṃ vijhoni jāya ujiteṃ| agnīceṃ teṃ || 93||
verses.meaning: Just as the body, afflicted by the severe wind at the time of death, becomes filled with phlegm both inside and out, so too the fire of life, which was once burning brightly, is extinguished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं प्राणासि प्राणु नाहीं । तेथ बुद्धि असोनि करील काई । म्हणौनि अग्नीविण देहीं । चेतना न थारे॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ prāṇāsi prāṇu nāhīṃ | tetha buddhi asoni karīla kāī | mhaṇauni agnīviṇa dehīṃ | cetanā na thāre|| 94||
verses.meaning: At that time, there is no life in the life-breath; what can the intellect do even if it exists? Therefore, without the fire (of consciousness), awareness cannot sustain itself in the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा देहींचा अग्नि जरी गेला। तरी देह नव्हे चिखलु बोला । वायां आयुष्यवेळु आपला । आंधारें गिंवसी ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā dehīṃcā agni jarī gelā| tarī deha navhe cikhalu bolā | vāyāṃ āyuṣyaveḻu āpalā | āṃdhāreṃ giṃvasī || 15||
verses.meaning: Even if the fire of life leaves the body, the body does not become mere mud. Do not waste your precious lifespan by letting darkness engulf it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मागील स्मरण आघवें। तें तेणें अवसरें सांभाळावें। मग देह त्यजूनि मिळावें। स्वरूपी कीं॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi māgīla smaraṇa āghaveṃ| teṃ teṇeṃ avasareṃ sāṃbhāḻāveṃ| maga deha tyajūni miḻāveṃ| svarūpī kīṃ|| 16||
verses.meaning: And all the past memories, at that very moment, should be gathered and held. Then, abandoning the body, one merges into the true Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंव तया शलेष्माचे चिखलीं। चेतनाचि बुडोनि गेली। तेथ मागिली पुढिली हे ठेली । आठवण सहजें॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃva tayā śaleṣmāce cikhalīṃ| cetanāci buḍoni gelī| tetha māgilī puḍhilī he ṭhelī | āṭhavaṇa sahajeṃ|| 17||
verses.meaning: Then, in that mire of phlegm, consciousness itself drowned. There, all memory of past and future naturally ceased.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आधीं अभ्यासु जो केला। तो मरण न येतांचि निमोनि गेला । जैसें ठेवणें न दिसतां मालवला । दीपु हातींचा ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni ādhīṃ abhyāsu jo kelā| to maraṇa na yetāṃci nimoni gelā | jaiseṃ ṭhevaṇeṃ na disatāṃ mālavalā | dīpu hātīṃcā || 18||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the spiritual practice that was undertaken, it vanished even before death arrived. Just as a lamp held in hand extinguishes without its stored oil being seen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां असो हें सकळ जाण पां ज्ञानासि अग्नि मूळ । तया अग्नीचें प्रयाणीं बळ। संपूर्ण आथी ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ aso heṃ sakaḻa jāṇa pāṃ jñānāsi agni mūḻa | tayā agnīceṃ prayāṇīṃ baḻa| saṃpūrṇa āthī || 19||
verses.meaning: Now, let this be known: knowledge has its origin in fire. And in the journey of that fire, there is complete strength.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आंत अग्नीज्योतीचा प्रकाशु । बाहेरी शुक्‍्लपक्षु आणि दिवसु। आणि सामासांमाजीं मासु। उत्तरयण॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṃta agnījyotīcā prakāśu | bāherī śuk‍lapakṣu āṇi divasu| āṇi sāmāsāṃmājīṃ māsu| uttarayaṇa|| 220||
verses.meaning: Within, there is the light of the fire's flame; outside, there is the bright fortnight and the day; and among the months, it is the auspicious month of Uttarayana.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐशिया समयोगाची निरुती। 'लाहोनि जे देह ठेविती । ते ब्रह्मच होती। ब्रह्मविद॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiśiyā samayogācī nirutī| 'lāhoni je deha ṭhevitī | te brahmaca hotī| brahmavida|| 21||
verses.meaning: Those who, having attained such a perfect union, give up their bodies, verily become Brahman, the knowers of Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अवधारीं गा धनुर्धग। येथवरी सामर्थ्य यया अवसरा। तेवींचि हा उजू मार्ग स्वपुरा । यावया पैं॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: avadhārīṃ gā dhanurdhaga| yethavarī sāmarthya yayā avasarā| tevīṃci hā ujū mārga svapurā | yāvayā paiṃ|| 22||
verses.meaning: Listen, O Arjuna, such is the power of this opportune moment, and this is indeed the direct path to one's true abode.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ अग्नी हें पहिलें पायतरें। ज्योतिर्मय हें दुसरें। दिवस जाणें तिसरें। चौथें शुक्लपक्ष ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha agnī heṃ pahileṃ pāyatareṃ| jyotirmaya heṃ dusareṃ| divasa jāṇeṃ tisareṃ| cautheṃ śuklapakṣa || 23||
verses.meaning: Here, fire is the first step. Light-filled is the second. Day is known as the third. The fourth is the bright fortnight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि सामास उत्तरायण तें वरचील गा सोपान । येणें सायुज्यसिन्द्विसदन। पावती योगी ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi sāmāsa uttarāyaṇa teṃ varacīla gā sopāna | yeṇeṃ sāyujyasindvisadana| pāvatī yogī || 24||
verses.meaning: And the path of Uttarayana, that is the upward ascent, by this, yogis attain the abode of complete union (with the Divine).

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा उत्तम काळु जाणिजे । यातें अर्चिरा मार्गु म्हणिजे। आतां अकाळु तोही सहजें । सांगेन आईक ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā uttama kāḻu jāṇije | yāteṃ arcirā mārgu mhaṇije| ātāṃ akāḻu tohī sahajeṃ | sāṃgena āīka || 25||
verses.meaning: This is known as the auspicious time; it is called the path of light. Now, I will easily tell you about the inauspicious time, so listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी प्रयाणाचिया अवसरें। बातशलेष्मां सुभरें। तेणें अंतःकरणीं आंधारें। कोंदलें ठाके ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī prayāṇāciyā avasareṃ| bātaśaleṣmāṃ subhareṃ| teṇeṃ aṃtaḥkaraṇīṃ āṃdhāreṃ| koṃdaleṃ ṭhāke || 26||
verses.meaning: However, at the time of departure, when the body is filled with wind and phlegm, the inner consciousness becomes enveloped in darkness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सवेंद्रियां लांकुड पडे । स्मृति भ्रमामाजीं बुडे । मन होय वेडें। कोंडे प्राण ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: saveṃdriyāṃ lāṃkuḍa paḍe | smṛti bhramāmājīṃ buḍe | mana hoya veḍeṃ| koṃḍe prāṇa || 27||
verses.meaning: The senses become like wood, memory drowns in delusion, the mind becomes mad, and life is trapped.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अग्नीचें अग्निपण जाये। मग तो धूमचि अवघा होये। तेणें चेतना गिंबसिली ठाये। शरीरींची॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: agnīceṃ agnipaṇa jāye| maga to dhūmaci avaghā hoye| teṇeṃ cetanā giṃbasilī ṭhāye| śarīrīṃcī|| 28||
verses.meaning: The fire loses its fiery nature, then it becomes all smoke. In the same way, the consciousness residing in the body is obscured.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें चंद्राआड आभाळ । सदट दाटे सजळ । मग गडद ना उजाळ । ऐसें झांवळें होय॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ caṃdrāāḍa ābhāḻa | sadaṭa dāṭe sajaḻa | maga gaḍada nā ujāḻa | aiseṃ jhāṃvaḻeṃ hoya|| 29||
verses.meaning: Just as when the moon is obscured by dense, water-laden clouds, it becomes neither dark nor bright, but rather a hazy, indistinct glow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां मरे ना सावध। ऐसें जीवितासि पडे स्तब्ध। आयुष्य मरणाची मर्याद। वेळु ठाकी॥ २३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ mare nā sāvadha| aiseṃ jīvitāsi paḍe stabdha| āyuṣya maraṇācī maryāda| veḻu ṭhākī|| 230||
verses.meaning: Why does life not become alert and realize that it is stunned by death? Life itself is the limit of death, and time is its boundary.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी मनबुन्दिकरणीं। सभोंबतीं धूमाकुळाची कोंडणी । तेथ जन्में जोडलिये वाहणीं। युगचि बुडे॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī manabundikaraṇīṃ| sabhoṃbatīṃ dhūmākuḻācī koṃḍaṇī | tetha janmeṃ joḍaliye vāhaṇīṃ| yugaci buḍe|| 31||
verses.meaning: Thus, in the mind, intellect, and senses, a dense cloud of delusion surrounds, and in that very state, the accumulated karma of many births leads to the drowning of an entire eon.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा हातींचे जे वेळीं जाये। ते वेळीं आणिका लाभाची गोठी कें आहे । म्हणौनि प्रयाणीं तंव होये । येतुली दशा॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā hātīṃce je veḻīṃ jāye| te veḻīṃ āṇikā lābhācī goṭhī keṃ āhe | mhaṇauni prayāṇīṃ taṃva hoye | yetulī daśā|| 32||
verses.meaning: Indeed, when what is in hand is lost, where then is the talk of any other gain? Therefore, at the time of departure, such a state of being occurs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐशी देहाआंतु स्थिती । बाहेरी कृष्णपक्षु वरि राती । १५२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी आणि सामासही बोडवती । दक्षिणायन॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiśī dehāāṃtu sthitī | bāherī kṛṣṇapakṣu vari rātī | 152 śrījñāneśvarī āṇi sāmāsahī boḍavatī | dakṣiṇāyana|| 33||
verses.meaning: Such is the state within the body, and outside, the dark fortnight and the night prevail. The Dnyaneshwari and the Sama Veda are also nourished, and it is the period of Dakshinayana (the sun's southward journey).

verses.shloka_devanagari: इये पुनरावृत्तीचीं घराणीं । आघवीं एकवटती जयाचिया प्रयाणीं। तो स्वरूपसिव्धीची काहाणी । कैसेनि आडके ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: iye punarāvṛttīcīṃ gharāṇīṃ | āghavīṃ ekavaṭatī jayāciyā prayāṇīṃ| to svarūpasivdhīcī kāhāṇī | kaiseni āḍake || 34||
verses.meaning: All the cycles of rebirth converge at the journey of one who has attained self-realization. How can such a one be hindered?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा जयाचा देह पडे । तया योगी म्हणोनि चंद्रवरी जाणें घडे । मग तेथूनि मागुता बहुडे। संसारा ये॥ ३५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jayācā deha paḍe | tayā yogī mhaṇoni caṃdravarī jāṇeṃ ghaḍe | maga tethūni māgutā bahuḍe| saṃsārā ye|| 35 ||
verses.meaning: When such a body falls, that yogi is said to ascend to the moon. From there, he returns to the cycle of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आम्हीं अकाळु जो पांडवा। म्हणितळला तो हा जाणावा। आणि हाचि धूग्रमार्गु गांवा । पुनरावृत्तीचिया ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āmhīṃ akāḻu jo pāṃḍavā| mhaṇitaḻalā to hā jāṇāvā| āṇi hāci dhūgramārgu gāṃvā | punarāvṛttīciyā || 36||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, know that what we call untimely death is indeed this very path of smoke, which leads to rebirth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येर तो अर्चिरा मार्ग) तो बसता आणि असलगु । साविया स्वस्त चांगु । निवृत्तीवरी ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yera to arcirā mārga) to basatā āṇi asalagu | sāviyā svasta cāṃgu | nivṛttīvarī || 37||
verses.meaning: The other path, the Arciradi Marga, is easy to attain, effortless, and truly auspicious, leading to the state of Nivritti (cessation of worldly activity).

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐशिया अनादि या दोन्ही वाटा। एकी उजू एकी अव्हांटा। म्हणौनि बुद्धिपूर्वक सुभटा । दाविलिया तुज ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiśiyā anādi yā donhī vāṭā| ekī ujū ekī avhāṃṭā| mhaṇauni buddhipūrvaka subhaṭā | dāviliyā tuja || 38||
verses.meaning: These two paths, which are beginningless, one is straight and the other is crooked. Therefore, O good warrior, I have shown them to you with deliberate wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां जे मार्गामार्ग देखावे। साच लटिकें बोळखावें। हिताहित जाणावें । हिताचिलागीं ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ je mārgāmārga dekhāve| sāca laṭikeṃ boḻakhāveṃ| hitāhita jāṇāveṃ | hitācilāgīṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: Just as one discerns the right and wrong paths, distinguishes truth from falsehood, and recognizes what is beneficial and what is harmful, all for the sake of one's own good.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहें पां नाव देखतां बरवी । कोणी आड घाली काय अथावीं। कां सुपंथ जाणौनियां अडवीं। रिगवत असे॥ २४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāheṃ pāṃ nāva dekhatāṃ baravī | koṇī āḍa ghālī kāya athāvīṃ| kāṃ supaṃtha jāṇauniyāṃ aḍavīṃ| rigavata ase|| 240||
verses.meaning: Behold, when one sees a beautiful boat, does anyone obstruct its path in the water? Or, knowing a good path, does one enter a thorny thicket?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो विष अमृत बोळखे। तो अमृत काय सांडूं शके। तेविं जो उजू वाट देखे। तो अव्हांटा न बचे॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo viṣa amṛta boḻakhe| to amṛta kāya sāṃḍūṃ śake| teviṃ jo ujū vāṭa dekhe| to avhāṃṭā na bace|| 41||
verses.meaning: One who recognizes poison as nectar, how can they discard that nectar? Similarly, one who sees the straight path will not stray onto a wrong one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि फुडें। पारखावें खरें कुडें। पारखिलें तरी न पडे। अनवसरें कहीं ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni phuḍeṃ| pārakhāveṃ khareṃ kuḍeṃ| pārakhileṃ tarī na paḍe| anavasareṃ kahīṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: Therefore, one should discern what is true and what is false. If one discerns, one will never fall into an inappropriate situation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं देहांतीं थोर विषम । या मार्गाचे आहे संभ्रम । जन्मे अभ्यासिलियाचें हन काम। जाईल वायां॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ dehāṃtīṃ thora viṣama | yā mārgāce āhe saṃbhrama | janme abhyāsiliyāceṃ hana kāma| jāīla vāyāṃ|| 43||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, at the end of life, there is great difficulty. This path is confusing. The efforts of a lifetime of practice will go in vain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी अर्चिरा मार्ग चुकलिया। अवचटें धूम्रपंथें पडलिया । तरी संसारपांथी जुंतलिया । भंबवतचि असावें॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī arcirā mārga cukaliyā| avacaṭeṃ dhūmrapaṃtheṃ paḍaliyā | tarī saṃsārapāṃthī juṃtaliyā | bhaṃbavataci asāveṃ|| 44||
verses.meaning: Even if one misses the path of light (Archi-ra marga) and accidentally falls onto the path of smoke (Dhuma-pantha), one should still remain steadfast and unwavering, like a bull yoked to the path of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे सायास देखोनि मोठे। आतां कैसेनि पां एकवेळ फिटे । म्हणौनि योगमार्ग गोमटे। शोधिले दोन्ही ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: he sāyāsa dekhoni moṭhe| ātāṃ kaiseni pāṃ ekaveḻa phiṭe | mhaṇauni yogamārga gomaṭe| śodhile donhī || 45||
verses.meaning: Witnessing these great efforts, how can one be freed from them at once? Therefore, both paths of Yoga were beautifully explored.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब एके ब्रह्मत्वा जाइजे। आणि एके पुनरावृत्ति येईजे। परि दैवगत्या जो लाहिजे। देहांतीं जेणें ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba eke brahmatvā jāije| āṇi eke punarāvṛtti yeīje| pari daivagatyā jo lāhije| dehāṃtīṃ jeṇeṃ || 46||
verses.meaning: By one path, one attains Brahmanhood; by another, one returns to this world. But that which is attained by divine grace at the end of the body's existence is the true path.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं म्हणितलें हें नव्हें।॥ वायां अवचटें काय पावे । देह त्यजूनि वस्तु होआवें। मार्गच कीं ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ mhaṇitaleṃ heṃ navheṃ||| vāyāṃ avacaṭeṃ kāya pāve | deha tyajūni vastu hoāveṃ| mārgaca kīṃ || 47||
verses.meaning: At that time, it was said, "This is not it." What is gained by useless, sudden efforts? The path is indeed to abandon the body and become the true essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आतां देह असो अथवा जावो । आम्ही तों केवळ वस्तूचि आहों। कां जे दोरीं सर्पत्व बाबो। दोराचिकडुनी॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī ātāṃ deha aso athavā jāvo | āmhī toṃ kevaḻa vastūci āhoṃ| kāṃ je dorīṃ sarpatva bābo| dorācikaḍunī|| 48||
verses.meaning: So now, whether the body remains or perishes, we are indeed only the Absolute Reality. Just as the snake-ness in a rope is nothing but the rope itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मज तरंगपण असे कीं नसे। ऐसें हें उदकासी कहीं प्रतिभासे। तें भलतेव्हां जैसें तैसें। उदकचि कौं॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maja taraṃgapaṇa ase kīṃ nase| aiseṃ heṃ udakāsī kahīṃ pratibhāse| teṃ bhalatevhāṃ jaiseṃ taiseṃ| udakaci kauṃ|| 49||
verses.meaning: Does a wave ever question its existence as separate from water? No, because whether it appears as a wave or not, it is always water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरंगाकारें न जन्मेचि। ना तरंगलोपें न निमेचि। तेविं देहीं जे देहेंचि। वस्तु जाहळे॥ २५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taraṃgākāreṃ na janmeci| nā taraṃgalopeṃ na nimeci| teviṃ dehīṃ je deheṃci| vastu jāhaḻe|| 250||
verses.meaning: Just as waves are not born from the water, nor do they truly cease to exist when they disappear into the water, similarly, the true essence (the Self) within the body is not born with the body, nor does it perish with the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां शरीराचें 'तयाचिया ठाई । आडनांबही उरलें नाहीं । तरी कोणें काळें काई । निमे तें पाहें पां॥५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ śarīrāceṃ 'tayāciyā ṭhāī | āḍanāṃbahī uraleṃ nāhīṃ | tarī koṇeṃ kāḻeṃ kāī | nime teṃ pāheṃ pāṃ||51||
verses.meaning: Now, even the name of the body has not remained in that (Self). So, when and how will it perish? See!

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग मार्गातें कासया शोधावे। कोणें कोठूनि कें जावें। जरी देशकालादि आघवें। आपणचि असे॥५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mārgāteṃ kāsayā śodhāve| koṇeṃ koṭhūni keṃ jāveṃ| jarī deśakālādi āghaveṃ| āpaṇaci ase||52||
verses.meaning: Then why search for a path? Who should go where and when? If all of space and time are oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हां गा घटु जे वेळीं फुटे। ते वेळीं तेथिंचें आकाश लागे नीट वाटे । वाटा लागे तरि गगना भेटे । एऱ्हवीं चुके ॥५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi hāṃ gā ghaṭu je veḻīṃ phuṭe| te veḻīṃ tethiṃceṃ ākāśa lāge nīṭa vāṭe | vāṭā lāge tari gaganā bheṭe | eṟhavīṃ cuke ||53||
verses.meaning: And when this pot breaks, then the space within it merges perfectly with the universal space. Only then does it meet the sky; otherwise, it remains separate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहें पां ऐसें हन आहे। कीं तो आकारुचि जाये । येर गगन तें गगनींचि आहे। घटत्वाहि आधीं॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāheṃ pāṃ aiseṃ hana āhe| kīṃ to ākāruci jāye | yera gagana teṃ gaganīṃci āhe| ghaṭatvāhi ādhīṃ|| 54||
verses.meaning: See, it is like this: the form itself disappears, but the sky remains as the sky, even before the pot-ness came into being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसिया बोधाचेनि सुरवाडे । मार्गामार्गाचें सांकडें । तया सोहंसिद्धां न पडे । योगियांसी ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyā bodhāceni suravāḍe | mārgāmārgāceṃ sāṃkaḍeṃ | tayā sohaṃsiddhāṃ na paḍe | yogiyāṃsī || 55 ||
verses.meaning: Such is the delight of this spiritual knowledge, that the difficulties of various paths do not trouble those yogis who have realized their oneness with the Divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: याकारणें पंडुसुता । तुवां होआवें योगयुक्‍ता। येतुळलेनि सर्वकाळीं साम्यता । आपैसया होईल॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yākāraṇeṃ paṃḍusutā | tuvāṃ hoāveṃ yogayuk‍tā| yetuḻaleni sarvakāḻīṃ sāmyatā | āpaisayā hoīla|| 56||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O son of Pandu, you should become united with Yoga. By this, equanimity will naturally arise in you at all times.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग भलतेथ भलतेव्हां। देहे असो अथवा जावा । परि अबंधा नित्य ब्रह्ममावा। विघडु नाहीं ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga bhalatetha bhalatevhāṃ| dehe aso athavā jāvā | pari abaṃdhā nitya brahmamāvā| vighaḍu nāhīṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: Then, at any place, at any time, whether the body remains or perishes, the unconditioned, eternal Brahman-state remains unbroken.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो कल्पादि जन्मा नागवे । कल्पांती मरणें नाप्लवे । माजि स्वर्गसंसाराचेनि लाघवें। झकवेना ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: to kalpādi janmā nāgave | kalpāṃtī maraṇeṃ nāplave | māji svargasaṃsārāceni lāghaveṃ| jhakavenā || 58||
verses.meaning: He is not born at the beginning of a kalpa (cosmic cycle), nor does He die at its end. He is not deluded by the allure of heaven or worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणें बोधें जो योगी होये। तयासीचि या बोधाचें नीटपण आहे। कां जे भोगातें पेळूनि पायें। निजरूपा ये॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃ bodheṃ jo yogī hoye| tayāsīci yā bodhāceṃ nīṭapaṇa āhe| kāṃ je bhogāteṃ peḻūni pāyeṃ| nijarūpā ye|| 59||
verses.meaning: The yogi who becomes enlightened by this knowledge, only for him is the true essence of this knowledge. Because, trampling over worldly pleasures, he attains his true self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं गा इंद्रादिकां देवां। जयां सर्वस्वें गाजती राणिवा। तें सांडणें मानूनि पांडवा । डावळी जो॥ २६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ gā iṃdrādikāṃ devāṃ| jayāṃ sarvasveṃ gājatī rāṇivā| teṃ sāṃḍaṇeṃ mānūni pāṃḍavā | ḍāvaḻī jo|| 260||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, even the gods like Indra, whose sovereignty is proclaimed everywhere, consider it a loss to abandon their positions, but the yogi abandons them as if they were mere trifles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी वेदाध्ययनाचें जालें। अथवा यज्ञाचे शेतचि पिकलें। कां तपोदानांचें जोडलें। सर्वस्व हन जें॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī vedādhyayanāceṃ jāleṃ| athavā yajñāce śetaci pikaleṃ| kāṃ tapodānāṃceṃ joḍaleṃ| sarvasva hana jeṃ|| 61||
verses.meaning: Even if the study of the Vedas has been accomplished, or the field of sacrifices has yielded its harvest, or the entirety of penance and charity has been accumulated—all of this is but a fraction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया आघवयाचि पुण्याचा मळा । भारु १५ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी आंतौनि जया ये फळा। जें परब्रह्मा निर्मळा । सांटि न सरे॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā āghavayāci puṇyācā maḻā | bhāru 15 śrījñāneśvarī āṃtauni jayā ye phaḻā| jeṃ parabrahmā nirmaḻā | sāṃṭi na sare||62||
verses.meaning: The entire garden of merit, from within which this Dnyaneshwari bears fruit, is that pure Supreme Brahman, which is inexhaustible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें नित्यानंदाचेनि मानें। उपमेचा कांटाळा न दिसे सानें।॥ पाहा पां वेदयज्ञादि साधनें॥ जया सुखा ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ nityānaṃdāceni māneṃ| upamecā kāṃṭāḻā na dise sāneṃ||| pāhā pāṃ vedayajñādi sādhaneṃ|| jayā sukhā || 63||
verses.meaning: That which, by the measure of eternal bliss, shows no trace of comparison, however small. Behold, the means like Vedic sacrifices lead to that very happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें बिटे ना सरे। भोगी तयाचेनि पवाडें पुरे। पुढती महासुखाचें सोयरें। भावंडचि॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ biṭe nā sare| bhogī tayāceni pavāḍeṃ pure| puḍhatī mahāsukhāceṃ soyareṃ| bhāvaṃḍaci|| 64||
verses.meaning: That which does not diminish or end, but rather, through its experience, brings complete fulfillment, is then a sibling to great joy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें दृष्टीचेनि सुखपणें । जयासी अदृष्टाचें बैसणें। जें शतमखींही आंगवणें । नोहेचि एका॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ dṛṣṭīceni sukhapaṇeṃ | jayāsī adṛṣṭāceṃ baisaṇeṃ| jeṃ śatamakhīṃhī āṃgavaṇeṃ | noheci ekā|| 65 ||
verses.meaning: Such is the joy of this vision, that the unseen resides within it, and even a hundred sacrifices cannot attain it alone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयातें योगीश्वर अलौकिकें । दिठीचेनि हाततुकें । अनुमानती कौतुकें । तंव हळुवट आवडे ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāteṃ yogīśvara alaukikeṃ | diṭhīceni hātatukeṃ | anumānatī kautukeṃ | taṃva haḻuvaṭa āvaḍe || 66||
verses.meaning: The great yogis, with their extraordinary vision, try to gauge its wonder with their mind's eye, but it appears exceedingly subtle.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तया सुखाची किरीटी। करूनियां गा पाउटी । परब्रह्माचिये पाठीं। आरूढती ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga tayā sukhācī kirīṭī| karūniyāṃ gā pāuṭī | parabrahmāciye pāṭhīṃ| ārūḍhatī || 67||
verses.meaning: Then, O Kiriti (Arjuna), making that bliss their very footstool, they ascend to the very essence of the Supreme Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें चराचरैकभाग्य। जें ब्रहोशां आराधनायोग्य । योगियांचें भोग्य। भोगधन जें ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ carācaraikabhāgya| jeṃ brahośāṃ ārādhanāyogya | yogiyāṃceṃ bhogya| bhogadhana jeṃ || 68||
verses.meaning: Such is the singular fortune of all creation, worthy of adoration by Brahma and Shiva, the very essence enjoyed by yogis, the wealth of their experience.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो सकळ कळांची कळा । जो परमानंदाचा पुतळा । जो जिवाचा जिव्हाळा । विश्वाचिया ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo sakaḻa kaḻāṃcī kaḻā | jo paramānaṃdācā putaḻā | jo jivācā jivhāḻā | viśvāciyā || 69 ||
verses.meaning: He is the art of all arts, the very embodiment of supreme bliss, the life-force of all beings in the universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो सर्वज्ञतेचा बोळावा। जो यादवकुळींचा कुळदिवा। तो श्रीकृष्णजी 'पांडवा-। प्रती बोलिला ॥ २७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo sarvajñatecā boḻāvā| jo yādavakuḻīṃcā kuḻadivā| to śrīkṛṣṇajī 'pāṃḍavā-| pratī bolilā || 270||
verses.meaning: Lord Krishna, who is the embodiment of all knowledge, the lamp of the Yadava clan, thus spoke to Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा कुरुक्षेत्रींचा वृत्तांतु| संजयो रायासी असे सांगतु। तेचि परियेसा पुढारी मातु। ज्ञानदेव म्हणे॥ २७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā kurukṣetrīṃcā vṛttāṃtu| saṃjayo rāyāsī ase sāṃgatu| teci pariyesā puḍhārī mātu| jñānadeva mhaṇe|| 271||
verses.meaning: Dnyandev says, "Listen to that very account of the events at Kurukshetra, which Sanjaya narrated to the King."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अवधान एकलें दीजे। मग सर्वसुखासि पात्र होइजे । हें प्रतिज्ञोत्तर माझें। उघड ऐका ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī avadhāna ekaleṃ dīje| maga sarvasukhāsi pātra hoije | heṃ pratijñottara mājheṃ| ughaḍa aikā || 1||
verses.meaning: Therefore, pay singular attention, and you shall become worthy of all happiness. This is my open promise to you, so listen carefully.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी प्रौढी न बोलें हो जी। तुम्हां सर्वज्ञांच्या समाजीं। देयावें अवधान हे माझी। विनवणी सलगीची॥२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī prauḍhī na boleṃ ho jī| tumhāṃ sarvajñāṃcyā samājīṃ| deyāveṃ avadhāna he mājhī| vinavaṇī salagīcī||2||
verses.meaning: But I do not speak with arrogance, O Lord, in the assembly of you all-knowing ones. Please grant your attention; this is my intimate plea.
