verses.shloka_iast: diso paratattva ḍoḻāṃ| pāho sukhācā sohaḻā | righo mahābodhasukāḻā-| mājīṃ viś‍va|| 62||
verses.meaning: May the Supreme Reality be seen by the eyes. May the celebration of bliss be witnessed. May the universe enter into the auspicious time of great enlightenment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें निफजेळ आतां आघवें। ऐसें बोलिजेळ बरवें। जें अधिष्ठिळा असें परमदेवें। श्रीनिवृत्तीं मी ॥६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ niphajeḻa ātāṃ āghaveṃ| aiseṃ bolijeḻa baraveṃ| jeṃ adhiṣṭhiḻā aseṃ paramadeveṃ| śrīnivṛttīṃ mī ||63||
verses.meaning: All this will now come to fruition, so it is beautifully said, that I am established in the Supreme Being, by the grace of Shri Nivrutti.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि अक्षरीं सुभेदीं। उपमा शलोक कोंदाकोंदी। झाडा देईन प्रतिपदीं। ग्रंथार्थासी ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni akṣarīṃ subhedīṃ| upamā śaloka koṃdākoṃdī| jhāḍā deīna pratipadīṃ| graṃthārthāsī || 64||
verses.meaning: Therefore, through clear and distinct words, and with an abundance of similes and verses, I will illuminate the meaning of this scripture, step by step.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा ठावोवरीं मातें । पुरतया सारस्वतें। केलें असे श्रीमंतें । श्रीगुरुरायें ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā ṭhāvovarīṃ māteṃ | puratayā sārasvateṃ| keleṃ ase śrīmaṃteṃ | śrīgururāyeṃ || 65||
verses.meaning: My Guru, the King of Gurus, has made me rich with the complete Saraswati (knowledge/eloquence) up to this point.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें जी कृपासावायें। मी बोलें तेतुलें सामाये। आणि मी तुमचिये सभे लाहें। गीता म्हणों ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ jī kṛpāsāvāyeṃ| mī boleṃ tetuleṃ sāmāye| āṇi mī tumaciye sabhe lāheṃ| gītā mhaṇoṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: By that grace and assistance, whatever I speak is contained within it. And in your assembly, I am able to recite the Gita.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरी तुम्हां संतांचे पाये । आजि मी लाधलो आहें। म्हणौनि जी नोहे। अटकु कांहीं ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: varī tumhāṃ saṃtāṃce pāye | āji mī lādhalo āheṃ| mhaṇauni jī nohe| aṭaku kāṃhīṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: Today, I have attained the feet of you, the saints. Therefore, there is no obstacle whatsoever.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रभु काश्मिरी मुकें। नुपजे हें काय कौतुकें । नाहीं उणीं सामुद्रिके । लक्ष्मीयेसी ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: prabhu kāśmirī mukeṃ| nupaje heṃ kāya kautukeṃ | nāhīṃ uṇīṃ sāmudrike | lakṣmīyesī || 68||
verses.meaning: The Lord's Kashmiri-like mouth is not a wonder. There is no lack of auspicious marks in Lakshmi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी तुम्हां संतांपासीं । अज्ञानाची गोठी कायसी । यालागीं नवरसीं। वरुषेन मी॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī tumhāṃ saṃtāṃpāsīṃ | ajñānācī goṭhī kāyasī | yālāgīṃ navarasīṃ| varuṣena mī||69||
verses.meaning: Amongst you saints, what place has ignorance? Therefore, I shall shower you with the nine rasas (sentiments).

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना आतां देवा। अवसरु मज देयावा। ज्ञानदेव म्हणे बरवा । सांगेन ग्रंथु॥ ११७० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā ātāṃ devā| avasaru maja deyāvā| jñānadeva mhaṇe baravā | sāṃgena graṃthu|| 1170 ||
verses.meaning: Indeed, now, O Lord, grant me this opportunity. Dnyandev says, I will beautifully narrate this scripture.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जय जय अआचार्या। समस्तसुरवर्या । प्रज्ञाप्रभासूर्या। सुखोदया॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaya jaya aācāryā| samastasuravaryā | prajñāprabhāsūryā| sukhodayā|| 9||
verses.meaning: Victory, victory to the Guru, the foremost among all gods, the sun of wisdom's light, the dawn of bliss!

verses.shloka_devanagari: जय जय सर्व विसांवया । सो5हंभावसुहावया। नाना लोक हेलावया । समुद्रा तूं॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaya jaya sarva visāṃvayā | so5haṃbhāvasuhāvayā| nānā loka helāvayā | samudrā tūṃ|| 2||
verses.meaning: Victory, victory to the one who is the resting place for all, who is the beauty of the 'I am That' realization, and who is like the ocean for the various worlds to surge and sway.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आइकें गा आर्तबंधू । निरंतरकारुण्यसिंधू । विशदविद्यावधू-। वल्लभा जी॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āikeṃ gā ārtabaṃdhū | niraṃtarakāruṇyasiṃdhū | viśadavidyāvadhū-| vallabhā jī||3||
verses.meaning: Listen, O Friend of the distressed, O Ocean of eternal compassion, O Beloved of the pure bride of knowledge!

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं जयांप्रति लपसी। तयां विश्‍व हें दाविसी । प्रकट तैं करिसी। आधवेंचि तूं ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ jayāṃprati lapasī| tayāṃ viś‍va heṃ dāvisī | prakaṭa taiṃ karisī| ādhaveṃci tūṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: You hide from those to whom you reveal this universe. When you manifest, you do so completely.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं पुढिलाची दृष्टि चोरिजे। हा दृष्टिबंधु निफजे। परी नवल लाघव तुझें। जें आपणपें चोरें॥५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ puḍhilācī dṛṣṭi corije| hā dṛṣṭibaṃdhu niphaje| parī navala lāghava tujheṃ| jeṃ āpaṇapeṃ coreṃ||5||
verses.meaning: Or, one's vision is stolen away, a trick of the eye is performed. But your wondrous skill is such that you steal yourself away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी तूंचि तूं सर्वा यया। मा कोणा बोधु कोणा माया । ऐसिया आपेंआप लाघविया। नमो तुज॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī tūṃci tūṃ sarvā yayā| mā koṇā bodhu koṇā māyā | aisiyā āpeṃāpa lāghaviyā| namo tuja|| 6||
verses.meaning: You alone are everything. Then who is to be enlightened and who is to be deluded? To such a one, who is effortlessly self-manifest, I bow to You.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जाणों जगीं आप वबोलें। तें तुझिया बोला सुरस जालें। तुझेनि क्षमत्व आलें। पृथ्वीयेसी ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāṇoṃ jagīṃ āpa vaboleṃ| teṃ tujhiyā bolā surasa jāleṃ| tujheni kṣamatva āleṃ| pṛthvīyesī || 7||
verses.meaning: Just as the earth's forbearance is due to your forgiveness, so too has my speech become eloquent and delightful because of your words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रविचंद्रादि शुक्‍्ती। उदय करिती त्रिजगतीं। तें तुझिया दीप्ती। तेज तेजां॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ravicaṃdrādi śuk‍tī| udaya karitī trijagatīṃ| teṃ tujhiyā dīptī| teja tejāṃ|| 8||
verses.meaning: The sun and moon, and other luminaries, illuminate the three worlds; but their light is merely a reflection of Your inherent brilliance, O Lord.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें चळवळिजे अनिळें। तें दैविकेनि जी निजबळें। नभ तुजमाजीं खेळें। लपीथपी॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ caḻavaḻije aniḻeṃ| teṃ daivikeni jī nijabaḻeṃ| nabha tujamājīṃ kheḻeṃ| lapīthapī|| 9||
verses.meaning: Just as the wind moves, so too, by its own inherent divine power, the sky plays hide-and-seek within you.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना माया असोस। ज्ञान जी तुझेनि डोळस। असो वानणें सायास श्रुतीसि हें॥ १०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā māyā asosa| jñāna jī tujheni ḍoḻasa| aso vānaṇeṃ sāyāsa śrutīsi heṃ|| 10||
verses.meaning: Indeed, Maya (the illusory power) exists, but it is through Your knowledge that it becomes perceptible. Even the Vedas struggle to describe this, so why should I attempt such a difficult task?

verses.shloka_devanagari: वेद वानूनि तंवचि चांग। जंब न दिसे तुझें आंग। मग आम्हां तया मूग) एके पांती॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: veda vānūni taṃvaci cāṃga| jaṃba na dise tujheṃ āṃga| maga āmhāṃ tayā mūga) eke pāṃtī|| 11||
verses.meaning: The Vedas are good only until your form is not seen. Once your form is revealed, then we and the Vedas are all in the same row, equal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी एकार्णवाचे ठाई । पाहतां थेंबाचा पाडु नाहीं । मा महानदी काई। जाणिजती॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī ekārṇavāce ṭhāī | pāhatāṃ theṃbācā pāḍu nāhīṃ | mā mahānadī kāī| jāṇijatī|| 12||
verses.meaning: Where even a drop of water cannot be discerned in the great ocean, how can mighty rivers be recognized?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां उदयलिया भास्वतु। चंद्र जैसा खद्योतु। आम्हां श्रुति तुजआंतु। तो पाडु असे॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ udayaliyā bhāsvatu| caṃdra jaisā khadyotu| āmhāṃ śruti tujaāṃtu| to pāḍu ase|| 13||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon is but a glow-worm before the rising sun, so too is the knowledge of the Vedas (scriptures) insignificant before You, O Lord. Such is Your glory.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि दुजया थांबो मोडे । जेथ परेशीं वैखरी बुडे। तो तूं मा कोणें तोंडें । बानावासी ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi dujayā thāṃbo moḍe | jetha pareśīṃ vaikharī buḍe| to tūṃ mā koṇeṃ toṃḍeṃ | bānāvāsī || 94||
verses.meaning: Where the second (duality) ceases and the very speech (Vaikhari) dissolves into the Supreme Being, by what words then can You be described?

verses.shloka_devanagari: यालागीं आतां । स्तुति सांडूनि निवांता । चरणीं ठेविजे माथा । हेंचि भलें॥ ९१५॥
verses.shloka_iast: yālāgīṃ ātāṃ | stuti sāṃḍūni nivāṃtā | caraṇīṃ ṭhevije māthā | heṃci bhaleṃ|| 915||
verses.meaning: Therefore, now, setting aside praise and becoming tranquil, it is best to place one's head at the feet (of the Lord).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तूं जैसा आहासि तैसिया। नमो जी श्रीगुरुराया । मज ग्रंथोद्यमु फळावया । वेव्हारा होई ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tūṃ jaisā āhāsi taisiyā| namo jī śrīgururāyā | maja graṃthodyamu phaḻāvayā | vevhārā hoī || 16||
verses.meaning: Therefore, just as you are, O revered Guru, I bow to you. So that my endeavor of writing this scripture may bear fruit, please be my support.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां कृपाभांडवल सोडीं। भरीं मति माझी पोतडी । करीं ज्ञानपद्यजोडी । थोरा मातें ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ kṛpābhāṃḍavala soḍīṃ| bharīṃ mati mājhī potaḍī | karīṃ jñānapadyajoḍī | thorā māteṃ || 17||
verses.meaning: Now, release the capital of your grace; fill my intellect's purse. Grant me the pair of knowledge-feet, O great one!

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग मी संसरे न तेणें । करीन संतांसी कर्णभूषणे । लेबवीन सुलक्षणें । विवेकाची ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mī saṃsare na teṇeṃ | karīna saṃtāṃsī karṇabhūṣaṇe | lebavīna sulakṣaṇeṃ | vivekācī || 18||
verses.meaning: Then, I will not be born again; instead, I will adorn the saints with the earrings of wisdom, making them beautiful with auspicious signs of discernment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी गीतार्थनिधान। काढू माझें मन। सुयीं स्नेहांजन। आपुलें तूं५८& १९॥ हे वाकसृष्टि एके वेळे। देखतु माझे बुद्धीचे डोळे। तैसा उदैजो जी निर्मळें। कारुण्यबिंबें॥ २०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī gītārthanidhāna| kāḍhū mājheṃ mana| suyīṃ snehāṃjana| āpuleṃ tūṃ58& 19|| he vākasṛṣṭi eke veḻe| dekhatu mājhe buddhīce ḍoḻe| taisā udaijo jī nirmaḻeṃ| kāruṇyabiṃbeṃ|| 20||
verses.meaning: Oh, the treasure of the Gita's meaning! Draw out my mind, anoint it with the collyrium of your love. May the eyes of my intellect behold the entire creation of words at once, just as the pure orb of your compassion rises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ३२४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी माझी प्रज्ञावेली वेल्हाळ। काव्यें होय सफळ। तो वसंतु होई स्नेहाळ- । शिरोमणी ॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: 324 śrījñāneśvarī mājhī prajñāvelī velhāḻa| kāvyeṃ hoya saphaḻa| to vasaṃtu hoī snehāḻa- | śiromaṇī || 21||
verses.meaning: My Dnyaneshwari, a creeper of wisdom, becomes fruitful through its poetry. May that spring of affection, the crest-jewel, be with us.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रमेयमहापूरें। हे मतिगंगा ये थोरें। तैसा वरिष उदारें। दिठीवेनी ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: prameyamahāpūreṃ| he matigaṃgā ye thoreṃ| taisā variṣa udāreṃ| diṭhīvenī || 22||
verses.meaning: Just as the great Ganges of knowledge flows in a mighty flood, so too does the generous rain of spiritual insight pour forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा विश्‍वैकधामा। तुझा प्रसाद चंद्रमा। करू मज पूर्णिमा । स्फूर्तीची जी॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā viś‍vaikadhāmā| tujhā prasāda caṃdramā| karū maja pūrṇimā | sphūrtīcī jī|| 23||
verses.meaning: Oh, the sole abode of the universe! May the moon of your grace make me full, like a full moon of inspiration.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी अवलोकिलिया मातें। उन्मेषसागरीं भरितें। बोसंडेल स्फूर्तीतें। रसवृत्तीचें ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī avalokiliyā māteṃ| unmeṣasāgarīṃ bhariteṃ| bosaṃḍela sphūrtīteṃ| rasavṛttīceṃ || 24||
verses.meaning: When I behold myself, I am filled with an ocean of inspiration, overflowing with the essence of poetic expression.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब संतोषोनि श्रीगुरुराजें। म्हणितलें विनतिव्याजें। मांडिलें देखोनि दुजें। स्तवनमिषें ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba saṃtoṣoni śrīgururājeṃ| mhaṇitaleṃ vinativyājeṃ| māṃḍileṃ dekhoni dujeṃ| stavanamiṣeṃ || 25||
verses.meaning: Then, the revered Guru, pleased with the devotion, spoke as if in humble supplication, seeing the praise offered to him as a separate entity, though it was truly a form of worship.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो आतां वांजटा। तो ज्ञानार्थ करूनि गोमटा। ग्रंथु दावीं उत्कंठा । भंगों नेदीं॥२६॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso ātāṃ vāṃjaṭā| to jñānārtha karūni gomaṭā| graṃthu dāvīṃ utkaṃṭhā | bhaṃgoṃ nedīṃ||26||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Now, by making this knowledge beautiful, I shall reveal the scripture, and not let the eagerness diminish.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हो कां जी स्वामी । हेंचि पाहत होतों मी। जे श्रीमुखें म्हणा तुम्ही । ग्रंथु सांग ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ho kāṃ jī svāmī | heṃci pāhata hotoṃ mī| je śrīmukheṃ mhaṇā tumhī | graṃthu sāṃga || 27||
verses.meaning: Oh, revered Master, I was indeed waiting for this very moment, that you yourself would narrate the scripture from your divine lips.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सहजें दुर्वेचा डिरु। आंगेंचि तंव अमरु। बरी आला पूरु। पीयुषाचा॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: sahajeṃ durvecā ḍiru| āṃgeṃci taṃva amaru| barī ālā pūru| pīyuṣācā|| 28||
verses.meaning: Naturally, the sprout of the Durva grass is inherently immortal. It is as if a flood of nectar has arrived.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आतां येणें प्रसादें। विन्यासें विदग्थें । मूळशास्त्रपदें। वाखाणीन॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī ātāṃ yeṇeṃ prasādeṃ| vinyāseṃ vidagtheṃ | mūḻaśāstrapadeṃ| vākhāṇīna|| 29||
verses.meaning: Therefore, by the grace of this divine gift, I shall now expound upon the fundamental principles of the scripture with skillful arrangement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी जीवा आंतुलीकडे । जैसी संदेहाची डोणी बुडे। ना श्रवणीं तरी चाडे । वाढी दिसे॥ ३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī jīvā āṃtulīkaḍe | jaisī saṃdehācī ḍoṇī buḍe| nā śravaṇīṃ tarī cāḍe | vāḍhī dise|| 30||
verses.meaning: But within the soul, just as the boat of doubt sinks, so too, the eagerness to listen (to spiritual teachings) is seen to grow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी बोली साचारी। अवतरो माझी माधुरी । माळे मागूनि घरीं । गुरुकृपेच्या॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī bolī sācārī| avataro mājhī mādhurī | māḻe māgūni gharīṃ | gurukṛpecyā|| 31||
verses.meaning: In the same way, may my words, imbued with sweetness, emerge from the garland of my Guru's grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी मागां त्रयोदशीं । अध्यायीं गोठी ऐसी । श्रीकृष्ण अर्जुनेंसी। चावळलळे॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī māgāṃ trayodaśīṃ | adhyāyīṃ goṭhī aisī | śrīkṛṣṇa arjuneṃsī| cāvaḻalaḻe|| 32||
verses.meaning: So, in the thirteenth chapter, such a discourse unfolded, where Shri Krishna conversed with Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोगें । होईजे येणें जगें। आत्मा गुणसंगें । संसारिया ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: je kṣetrakṣetrajñayogeṃ | hoīje yeṇeṃ jageṃ| ātmā guṇasaṃgeṃ | saṃsāriyā || 33||
verses.meaning: Through the union of the field (body) and the knower of the field (soul), this world comes into being, and the soul, through its association with the gunas (qualities of nature), becomes a worldly being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हाचि प्रकृतिगतु। सुखदुःखभोगीं हेतु) अथवा गुणातीतु। केवळु हा॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi hāci prakṛtigatu| sukhaduḥkhabhogīṃ hetu) athavā guṇātītu| kevaḻu hā|| 34||
verses.meaning: And this very nature is the cause of experiencing joy and sorrow, or it is beyond all qualities, pure and absolute.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कैसा पां असंगा संगु। कोण तो क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञा योगु। सुखदुःखादि भोगु । केवीं तया॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī kaisā pāṃ asaṃgā saṃgu| koṇa to kṣetrakṣetrajñā yogu| sukhaduḥkhādi bhogu | kevīṃ tayā|| 35||
verses.meaning: Then how can there be association with the unassociated? What is that union of the field and the knower of the field? How can there be experiences of pleasure and pain for that (unassociated one)?

verses.shloka_devanagari: गुण ते कैसे किती। बांधती कवणे रीती । नातरी गुणातीतीं। चिन्हें काई॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: guṇa te kaise kitī| bāṃdhatī kavaṇe rītī | nātarī guṇātītīṃ| cinheṃ kāī|| 36||
verses.meaning: What are these qualities, and how do they bind? Or what are the signs of one who transcends qualities?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं इया आघवेया। अर्था रूप करावया । विषो एथ चौदाविया। अध्यायासि॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ iyā āghaveyā| arthā rūpa karāvayā | viṣo etha caudāviyā| adhyāyāsi|| 37||
verses.meaning: Thus, to give form to the entire meaning, this fourteenth chapter is dedicated.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरि तो आतां ऐसा। प्रस्तुत परियेसा । अभिप्रायो विश्वेशा । वैकुंठाचा ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tari to ātāṃ aisā| prastuta pariyesā | abhiprāyo viśveśā | vaikuṃṭhācā || 38||
verses.meaning: So, listen now to this, the intention of the Lord of the universe, of Vaikuntha, as it is presented.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो म्हणे गा अर्जुना । अवधानाची सर्व सेना। मेळऊनि इया ज्ञाना। झोंबावें हो॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: to mhaṇe gā arjunā | avadhānācī sarva senā| meḻaūni iyā jñānā| jhoṃbāveṃ ho|| 39||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, he says, gather all the army of attention and engage with this knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आम्हीं मागां तुज बहुतीं। दाविलें हें उपपत्तीं। तरी आझुनी प्रतीती-। कुशीं न निघे॥ ४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āmhīṃ māgāṃ tuja bahutīṃ| dāvileṃ heṃ upapattīṃ| tarī ājhunī pratītī-| kuśīṃ na nighe|| 40||
verses.meaning: Earlier, I explained this to you in many ways, with many examples. Yet, it still doesn't emerge from the womb of your understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि गा पुढती । सांगिजैळ तुजप्रती। पर म्हण म्हणौनि श्रुतीं। डाहारिलें जें॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni gā puḍhatī | sāṃgijaiḻa tujapratī| para mhaṇa mhaṇauni śrutīṃ| ḍāhārileṃ jeṃ|| 41||
verses.meaning: Therefore, I will tell you again, that which the Vedas have declared as 'but, but'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं ज्ञान हें आपुलें परी पर ऐसेनि जालें। जे आवडोनि घेतलें। भवस्वर्गादिक॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ jñāna heṃ āpuleṃ parī para aiseni jāleṃ| je āvaḍoni ghetaleṃ| bhavasvargādika|| 42||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, this knowledge, though inherently ours, has become alien, as if it has been taken up with fondness for worldly existence and heavenly pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा याचि कारणें। हें उत्तम सर्वांपरी मी म्हणें। जे वन्हि हें तृणें। येरें ज्ञानें ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā yāci kāraṇeṃ| heṃ uttama sarvāṃparī mī mhaṇeṃ| je vanhi heṃ tṛṇeṃ| yereṃ jñāneṃ || 43||
verses.meaning: For this very reason, I say that this knowledge is supreme above all else, just as fire consumes grass, so does this knowledge consume all other forms of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जियें भवस्वर्गातें जाणती । यागचि चांग म्हणती । पारखी फुडी आथी । भेदीं जया॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiyeṃ bhavasvargāteṃ jāṇatī | yāgaci cāṃga mhaṇatī | pārakhī phuḍī āthī | bhedīṃ jayā|| 44||
verses.meaning: Those who understand the nature of worldly existence and heavenly pleasures, truly consider sacrificial rites to be good, for they are the discerning ones who grasp the profound truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियें आधघवींचि ज्ञानें। केलीं येणें स्वप्नें। जैशा वातोर्मी गगनें। गिळिजती अंतीं ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyeṃ ādhaghavīṃci jñāneṃ| kelīṃ yeṇeṃ svapneṃ| jaiśā vātormī gaganeṃ| giḻijatī aṃtīṃ || 45||
verses.meaning: By that very knowledge, this dream (of the world) is consumed, just as the sky ultimately swallows the waves of the wind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां उदितें रश्मिराजें। लोपिली चंद्रादि तेजें । नाना प्रळयांबुमाजें । नदी नद॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ uditeṃ raśmirājeṃ| lopilī caṃdrādi tejeṃ | nānā praḻayāṃbumājeṃ | nadī nada|| 46||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's rising obscures the moon and other celestial lights, or as the waters of the great deluge engulf all rivers and streams.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें येणें पाहळेया । ज्ञानजात जाय लया । म्हणौनियां धनंजया । उत्तम हें ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ yeṇeṃ pāhaḻeyā | jñānajāta jāya layā | mhaṇauniyāṃ dhanaṃjayā | uttama heṃ || 47||
verses.meaning: Just as the dawn dispels the darkness, so too does this knowledge dissolve ignorance. Therefore, Arjuna, this is supreme.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अनादि जे मुक्‍तता। आपुली असे पंडुसुता । तो मोक्षु हातां येता । होय जेणें ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: anādi je muk‍tatā| āpulī ase paṃḍusutā | to mokṣu hātāṃ yetā | hoya jeṇeṃ || 48||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, that liberation which is beginningless and inherently yours, the means by which that liberation comes into your hands.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचिया प्रतीती । विचारवीरीं समस्तीं। नेदिजेचि संसृती। माथां उधऊं ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāciyā pratītī | vicāravīrīṃ samastīṃ| nedijeci saṃsṛtī| māthāṃ udhaūṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: By the realization of which, the entire cycle of worldly existence does not arise in the minds of those who contemplate it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मनें मन घाळूनि मागें। विश्रांति जालिया आंगें। ते देहीं देहाजोगे। होतीचि ना॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maneṃ mana ghāḻūni māgeṃ| viśrāṃti jāliyā āṃgeṃ| te dehīṃ dehājoge| hotīci nā|| 50||
verses.meaning: When the mind, having abandoned its past, finds rest within itself, then the body, even while existing, does not act according to its own nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तें देहाचें बेळें । बोलांडूनि एकेचि वेळे। संवतुकी कांटाळें। माझें जालें॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga teṃ dehāceṃ beḻeṃ | bolāṃḍūni ekeci veḻe| saṃvatukī kāṃṭāḻeṃ| mājheṃ jāleṃ|| 51||
verses.meaning: Then, having crossed the body's boundary in a single moment, I became weary of worldly attachments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे माझिया नित्यता। तेणें नित्य तें पंडुसुता । परिपूर्ण पूर्णता । माझियाचि ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je mājhiyā nityatā| teṇeṃ nitya teṃ paṃḍusutā | paripūrṇa pūrṇatā | mājhiyāci || 52||
verses.meaning: That which is My eternality, by that, O son of Pandu, is the eternal. My fullness is complete and perfect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मी जैसा अनंतानंदु । जैसाचि सत्यसिंधु। तैसेचि ते भेदु । उरेचि ना॥५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mī jaisā anaṃtānaṃdu | jaisāci satyasiṃdhu| taiseci te bhedu | ureci nā||53||
verses.meaning: I am infinite bliss, just as I am the ocean of truth; in the same way, no difference remains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें मी जेवढें जैसें । तेंचि ते जाले तैसें । घटभंगीं घटाकाशें । आकाश जेबीं॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ mī jevaḍheṃ jaiseṃ | teṃci te jāle taiseṃ | ghaṭabhaṃgīṃ ghaṭākāśeṃ | ākāśa jebīṃ|| 54||
verses.meaning: Whatever I am, to whatever extent, in whatever form, they too became exactly like that. Just as when a pot breaks, the space within the pot merges into the universal space.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी दीपमूळकीं। दीपशिखा अनेकीं । मीनलिया अवलोकोौं। होय जेसें ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī dīpamūḻakīṃ| dīpaśikhā anekīṃ | mīnaliyā avalokoauṃ| hoya jeseṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: Just as many lamps are lit from a single lamp, so too is the universe illuminated by the divine light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना तयापरी । सरली ह्वैताची वारी । नांदे नामार्थ एकाहारीं। मीतूंबिण॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā tayāparī | saralī hvaitācī vārī | nāṃde nāmārtha ekāhārīṃ| mītūṃbiṇa|| 56||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, in that manner, the journey of duality ends. The meaning of the Name resides in unity, without 'I' and 'you'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणेंचि पैं कारणें । जें पहिलें सृष्टीचें जुंपणें । तेंही तया होणें । पडेचिना ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃci paiṃ kāraṇeṃ | jeṃ pahileṃ sṛṣṭīceṃ juṃpaṇeṃ | teṃhī tayā hoṇeṃ | paḍecinā || 57||
verses.meaning: For this very reason, the initial creation of the universe does not even fall upon Him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सृष्टीचिये सर्वादी। जयां देहाची नाहीं बांधी । ते कैचें प्रळयाबधी । निमतील पां ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: sṛṣṭīciye sarvādī| jayāṃ dehācī nāhīṃ bāṃdhī | te kaiceṃ praḻayābadhī | nimatīla pāṃ || 58||
verses.meaning: Those who were not bound by a body at the very beginning of creation, how can they be destroyed even at the time of the great dissolution?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जन्मक्षयां-। अतीत ते धनंजया । मी जालें ज्ञाना इया। अनुसरोनी ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni janmakṣayāṃ-| atīta te dhanaṃjayā | mī jāleṃ jñānā iyā| anusaronī || 59||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Dhananjaya, I have become that which transcends birth and decay, by following this knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी ज्ञानाची वाढी। वानिली देवें आवडी । तेवबींचि पार्थाही गोडी। ळावावया॥ ६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī jñānācī vāḍhī| vānilī deveṃ āvaḍī | tevabīṃci pārthāhī goḍī| ḻāvāvayā|| 60||
verses.meaning: Thus, the growth of knowledge was lovingly described by the Lord, and to that, Partha's delight was also added.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंव तया जाळें आन। सर्वांगी निघाळे कान। सपाई अवधान। आतला पां॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃva tayā jāḻeṃ āna| sarvāṃgī nighāḻe kāna| sapāī avadhāna| ātalā pāṃ||61||
verses.meaning: Then, as if a net of ears, his entire body became attentive, and his inner awareness became fully absorbed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां देवाचिया ऐसें। जाकळीजत असे वोरसें। जें निरूपण आकाशें। वेंटाळेना॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ devāciyā aiseṃ| jākaḻījata ase voraseṃ| jeṃ nirūpaṇa ākāśeṃ| veṃṭāḻenā|| 62||
verses.meaning: Now, the divine discourse is so profound and expansive that even the vast sky cannot encompass it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणे गा प्रज्ञाकांता। उजबली आजि वक्तृत्वता। जे बोलायेवढा श्रोता। जोडलासी॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇe gā prajñākāṃtā| ujabalī āji vaktṛtvatā| je bolāyevaḍhā śrotā| joḍalāsī|| 63||
verses.meaning: Then, O beloved of wisdom, today my eloquence has blossomed, for I have found a listener worthy of such words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी एकु मी ३२६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी अनेकीं। गोंबिजे देहपाशकीं। त्रिगुणीं लुब्धकीं। कवणेपरी ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī eku mī 326 śrījñāneśvarī anekīṃ| goṃbije dehapāśakīṃ| triguṇīṃ lubdhakīṃ| kavaṇeparī || 64||
verses.meaning: How can the one 'I' (the Self) be entangled in the many bodily attachments, ensnared by the three Gunas (qualities of nature) like a hunter's snare?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कैसा क्षेत्रयोगें । वियें इयें जगें। तें परिस सांगें। कवणेपरी ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kaisā kṣetrayogeṃ | viyeṃ iyeṃ jageṃ| teṃ parisa sāṃgeṃ| kavaṇeparī || 65 ||
verses.meaning: How, through the union of the field and the knower of the field, are these worlds born? Please tell me how this happens.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं क्षेत्र येणें व्याजें। यालागीं हें बोलिजे। जें मत्संगबीजें। भूतीं पिके ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ kṣetra yeṇeṃ vyājeṃ| yālāgīṃ heṃ bolije| jeṃ matsaṃgabījeṃ| bhūtīṃ pike || 66||
verses.meaning: Indeed, it is called a 'field' for this reason: because the seed of My company yields a harvest in all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं तरी महट्रहया। यालागीं हें ऐसें नाम। जे महदादिविश्राम-। शालिका हें ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ tarī mahaṭrahayā| yālāgīṃ heṃ aiseṃ nāma| je mahadādiviśrāma-| śālikā heṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, it is called 'Mahat' (the Great Principle) because it is the resting place for the 'Mahat-adi' (the Great Principle and all that follows from it).

verses.shloka_devanagari: विकारां बहुवस थोरी । अर्जुना हेंचि करी। म्हणौनि अवधारीं । महट्रह्म ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: vikārāṃ bahuvasa thorī | arjunā heṃci karī| mhaṇauni avadhārīṃ | mahaṭrahma || 68 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this is the greatness of the many transformations; therefore, listen to the Mahat-Brahma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अव्यक्‍्तवादमतीं । अव्यक्त ऐसी वदंती । सांख्याचिया प्रतीती । प्रकृति हेचि ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: avyak‍tavādamatīṃ | avyakta aisī vadaṃtī | sāṃkhyāciyā pratītī | prakṛti heci || 69||
verses.meaning: To those who believe in the unmanifest, it is indeed unmanifest. But for the Sankhya philosophers, it is simply Prakriti (primordial nature).

verses.shloka_devanagari: वेदांती इयेतें माया । ऐसें म्हणिजे प्राज्ञराया । असो किती बोलों वायां। अज्ञान हें ॥ ७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: vedāṃtī iyeteṃ māyā | aiseṃ mhaṇije prājñarāyā | aso kitī boloṃ vāyāṃ| ajñāna heṃ || 70||
verses.meaning: In Vedanta, this is called Maya, O King of the wise. Why speak in vain? This is ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपला आपणपेयां। विसरु जो धनंजया । तेंचि रूप यया। अज्ञानासी॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpalā āpaṇapeyāṃ| visaru jo dhanaṃjayā | teṃci rūpa yayā| ajñānāsī|| 71||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, the forgetfulness of one's own true Self is precisely the form of this ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिकही एक असे। जें विचारावेळे न दिसे। वातीं पाहतां जैसें । अंधारे कां ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇikahī eka ase| jeṃ vicārāveḻe na dise| vātīṃ pāhatāṃ jaiseṃ | aṃdhāre kāṃ || 72||
verses.meaning: There is yet another thing, which is not seen when one tries to contemplate it, just as darkness is not seen when one looks for it with a lamp.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हाळविलिया जाय। निश्चळीं तरी होय । दुधीं जैसी साय । दुधाची ते॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāḻaviliyā jāya| niścaḻīṃ tarī hoya | dudhīṃ jaisī sāya | dudhācī te|| 73||
verses.meaning: When stirred, it becomes disturbed. But when still, it becomes like the cream on milk, which is of the milk itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं जागरु ना स्वप्न। ना स्वरूप अवस्थान। ते सुषुप्ति कां घन। जैसी होय ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ jāgaru nā svapna| nā svarūpa avasthāna| te suṣupti kāṃ ghana| jaisī hoya || 74||
verses.meaning: Neither wakefulness nor dream, nor the state of being established in one's true nature—it is like deep sleep, or a dense cloud.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां न वियतां वायूतें। वांझें आकाश रितें। तयाऐसें निरुतें। अज्ञान गा॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ na viyatāṃ vāyūteṃ| vāṃjheṃ ākāśa riteṃ| tayāaiseṃ niruteṃ| ajñāna gā|| 75||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky, without giving birth, remains empty and barren, so too is ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैल खांबु कां पुरुखु । ऐसा निश्चयो नाहीं एकु । परी काय नेणों आलोकु । दिसत असे॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paila khāṃbu kāṃ purukhu | aisā niścayo nāhīṃ eku | parī kāya neṇoṃ āloku | disata ase|| 76||
verses.meaning: There is no certainty whether it is a pillar or a man. But I do not know what kind of light is seen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं वस्तु जैसी असे। तैसी कौर न दिसे। परी कांहीं अनारिसें। देखिजेना॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ vastu jaisī ase| taisī kaura na dise| parī kāṃhīṃ anāriseṃ| dekhijenā|| 77||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the true nature of reality, though not directly perceived, is also not seen as something different or other.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना राती ना तेज। ते संधि जेवीं सांज। तेवीं विरुद्ध ना निज। ज्ञान आथी ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā rātī nā teja| te saṃdhi jevīṃ sāṃja| tevīṃ viruddha nā nija| jñāna āthī || 78 ||
verses.meaning: Neither night nor light, but like the twilight where they meet; similarly, neither opposition nor inherent knowledge exists.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी कोण्ही एकी दशा । तिये बादु अज्ञान ऐसा । तया गुंडलिया प्रकाशा । क्षेत्रजु नाम ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī koṇhī ekī daśā | tiye bādu ajñāna aisā | tayā guṃḍaliyā prakāśā | kṣetraju nāma || 79||
verses.meaning: There is a certain state, beyond which lies ignorance. When that light is enveloped, it is called the 'knower of the field' (Kshetrajna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: अज्ञान थोरिये आणिजे। आपणपें तरी नेणिजे। तें रूप जाणिजे । क्षेत्रज्ञाचे ॥ ८० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ajñāna thoriye āṇije| āpaṇapeṃ tarī neṇije| teṃ rūpa jāṇije | kṣetrajñāce || 80 ||
verses.meaning: That which is called great ignorance, yet does not know itself, that form should be understood as the Knower of the Field (Kshetrajna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: हाचि उभय योगु। बुझें बापा चांगु । सत्तेचा नैसर्गु। स्वभावो हा॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāci ubhaya yogu| bujheṃ bāpā cāṃgu | sattecā naisargu| svabhāvo hā|| 81||
verses.meaning: Understand, my child, that this dual yoga is indeed good. It is the natural disposition of the Self's inherent power.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अज्ञानासारिखें। वस्तु आपणपांचि देखे। परी रूपें अनेकें । नेणों कोणें ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ ajñānāsārikheṃ| vastu āpaṇapāṃci dekhe| parī rūpeṃ anekeṃ | neṇoṃ koṇeṃ || 82||
verses.meaning: Now, like ignorance, the Self sees itself in many forms, yet does not know which is its true form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा रंकु भ्रमला । म्हणे जारे मी रावो आला । कां मूछितु गेला । स्वर्गळोकां॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā raṃku bhramalā | mhaṇe jāre mī rāvo ālā | kāṃ mūchitu gelā | svargaḻokāṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: Just as a pauper, deluded, might exclaim, "Behold, I am a king!" or as one who has fainted might believe they have gone to heaven.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं लचकलिया दिठी। मग देखणें जें जें उठी । तया नाम सृष्टी) मीचि वियें पैं गा॥८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ lacakaliyā diṭhī| maga dekhaṇeṃ jeṃ jeṃ uṭhī | tayā nāma sṛṣṭī) mīci viyeṃ paiṃ gā||84||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the sight is opened, whatever arises to be seen, that creation, know that I alone give birth to it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें कां स्वप्नममोहा। तो एकाकी देखे बहुवा। तोचि पाडु आत्मया। स्मरणेंबीण असे॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ kāṃ svapnamamohā| to ekākī dekhe bahuvā| toci pāḍu ātmayā| smaraṇeṃbīṇa ase|| 85 ||
verses.meaning: Just as in a dream's delusion, a single person sees many, so too is the soul's state without remembrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हेंचि आनीभ्रांति। प्रमेय उपलबूं पुढती । परी तूं प्रतीती। याचि घे पां॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃci ānībhrāṃti| prameya upalabūṃ puḍhatī | parī tūṃ pratītī| yāci ghe pāṃ|| 86||
verses.meaning: This is another illusion, a concept to be understood later; but you should experience this now.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी माझी हे गृहिणी । अनादि तरुणी । अनिर्वाच्यगुणी । अविद्या हे ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī mājhī he gṛhiṇī | anādi taruṇī | anirvācyaguṇī | avidyā he || 87||
verses.meaning: My dear housewife, this primordial, ever-youthful, indescribably virtuous Avidya (ignorance) is truly mine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इये नाहीं हेंचि रूप। ठाणें हें अति उमप। हें निद्रितां समीप । चेतां दुरी॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: iye nāhīṃ heṃci rūpa| ṭhāṇeṃ heṃ ati umapa| heṃ nidritāṃ samīpa | cetāṃ durī|| 88||
verses.meaning: This 'no' is not its true form; this 'place' is exceedingly vast. It is near when one is asleep, but far when one is awake.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं माझेनिचि आंगें। पहुडल्या हे जागे। आणि सत्तासंभोगें। गुर्विणी होय॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ mājhenici āṃgeṃ| pahuḍalyā he jāge| āṇi sattāsaṃbhogeṃ| gurviṇī hoya|| 89||
verses.meaning: Indeed, through My very being, this world awakens, and through the enjoyment of My power, it becomes pregnant (with creation).

verses.shloka_devanagari: महद्रह्मउदरीं। प्राकृतीं आठे विकारीं। गर्भाची करी। पेलोवेली ॥ ९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mahadrahmaudarīṃ| prākṛtīṃ āṭhe vikārīṃ| garbhācī karī| pelovelī || 90||
verses.meaning: Within the womb of the great Brahman, nature, in its eightfold modifications, creates the embryo, causing it to swell and grow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उभयसंगु पहिलें। बुद्धितत्त्व प्रसवलें। बुऱ्दितत्त्वें भारेलें। होय मन॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ubhayasaṃgu pahileṃ| buddhitattva prasavaleṃ| buṟditattveṃ bhāreleṃ| hoya mana|| 91||
verses.meaning: First, from the union of the two (Purusha and Prakriti), the intellect principle (Buddhi) was born. When this intellect principle becomes burdened (with thoughts and desires), it becomes the mind (Manas).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरुणी ममता मनाची। ते अहंकार तत्त्व रची। तेणें महाभूतांची । अभिव्यक्ति होय॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taruṇī mamatā manācī| te ahaṃkāra tattva racī| teṇeṃ mahābhūtāṃcī | abhivyakti hoya|| 92||
verses.meaning: The youthful affection of the mind creates the principle of ego, through which the great elements manifest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि विषषयेंद्रियां गौसी । स्वभावें तंव भूतांसी । म्हणौनि येती सरिसीं । तियेंही रूपा ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi viṣaṣayeṃdriyāṃ gausī | svabhāveṃ taṃva bhūtāṃsī | mhaṇauni yetī sarisīṃ | tiyeṃhī rūpā || 93 ||
verses.meaning: And the senses are naturally drawn to their objects, just as all beings are drawn to their forms.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जालेनि विकारक्षोभें। पाठीं त्रिगुणाचें उभें। तेव्हां ये वासनागर्भे । ठायेंठावों ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāleni vikārakṣobheṃ| pāṭhīṃ triguṇāceṃ ubheṃ| tevhāṃ ye vāsanāgarbhe | ṭhāyeṃṭhāvoṃ || 94||
verses.meaning: Then, agitated by the modifications of nature, and subsequently by the three gunas, the womb of desires is formed, taking root everywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रुखाचा आवांका। जैसी बीजकणिका। जीवीं बांधे उदका। भेटतखेंबो॥ ९५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: rukhācā āvāṃkā| jaisī bījakaṇikā| jīvīṃ bāṃdhe udakā| bheṭatakheṃbo|| 95 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a tiny seed holds within itself the potential for a mighty tree, and upon meeting water, it sprouts forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी माझेनि संगें । अविद्या नाना जगें। आर घेवों लागे। आणियाची ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī mājheni saṃgeṃ | avidyā nānā jageṃ| āra ghevoṃ lāge| āṇiyācī || 96||
verses.meaning: In the same way, through My association, ignorance begins to assume various forms of the world, as if taking on another's identity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग गर्भगोळा तया । कैसें रूप तैं ये आया । तें परियेसें राया । सुजनांचिया ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga garbhagoḻā tayā | kaiseṃ rūpa taiṃ ye āyā | teṃ pariyeseṃ rāyā | sujanāṃciyā || 97||
verses.meaning: Then, how does the embryo take form? Listen to that, O King, among the good people.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं मणिज स्वेदज। उद्िभिज जारज। उमटती सहज। अवयव हे॥९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ maṇija svedaja| udibhija jāraja| umaṭatī sahaja| avayava he||98||
verses.meaning: Thus, from sweat, from eggs, from seeds, and from the womb, these bodies naturally emerge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्योमवायुवशें । वाढलेनि गर्भरसें। मणिजु उससे। अवयव तो॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vyomavāyuvaśeṃ | vāḍhaleni garbharaseṃ| maṇiju usase| avayava to|| 99||
verses.meaning: Just as a gem grows from the essence within the womb, nourished by the sky and wind, so too do the limbs develop.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पोटीं सूनि तमरजें। आगळिकां तोय तेजें। उठितां निपजे। स्वेदजु गा॥ १००॥
verses.shloka_iast: poṭīṃ sūni tamarajeṃ| āgaḻikāṃ toya tejeṃ| uṭhitāṃ nipaje| svedaju gā|| 100||
verses.meaning: From the womb of darkness, with the power of water and light, when it arises, the sweat-born are produced.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपपृथ्वी उत्कटें। आणि तमोमात्रें निकृष्टें। स्थावरु उमटे। उद्‌भिजु हा॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpapṛthvī utkaṭeṃ| āṇi tamomātreṃ nikṛṣṭeṃ| sthāvaru umaṭe| ud‌bhiju hā|| 1||
verses.meaning: From the intense earth element and the inferior quality of tamas, the stationary (plants) emerge; this is the 'udbhija' (sprouting from the earth) category.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पांचां पांचही विरजीं । होती मनबुल्धयादि साजीं। हीं हेतु जारजीं। ऐसें जाण॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṃcāṃ pāṃcahī virajīṃ | hotī manabuldhayādi sājīṃ| hīṃ hetu jārajīṃ| aiseṃ jāṇa|| 2||
verses.meaning: The five senses, along with the mind and intellect, are all born of desire. Know this to be true.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे चारी हे सरळ । करचरणतळ।। महाप्रकृति स्थूळ । तेंचि शिर॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise cārī he saraḻa | karacaraṇataḻa|| mahāprakṛti sthūḻa | teṃci śira|| 3||
verses.meaning: Thus, these four are straight: the hands and feet. The great, manifest nature itself is the head.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रवृत्ति पेळळें पोट । निवृत्ति ते पाठी नीट । सुरयोनी आंगें आठ । ऊर्ध्वाचीं ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: pravṛtti peḻaḻeṃ poṭa | nivṛtti te pāṭhī nīṭa | surayonī āṃgeṃ āṭha | ūrdhvācīṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: The path of worldly engagement is like a soft belly, while the path of renunciation is a straight back. These are the eight divine forms, ascending upwards.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कंठु उल्हासता स्वर्गु। मृत्युलोकु मध्यभागु। अधोदेशु चांगु । नितंबु तो॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kaṃṭhu ulhāsatā svargu| mṛtyuloku madhyabhāgu| adhodeśu cāṃgu | nitaṃbu to|| 5||
verses.meaning: The heavens are the joyful neck, the mortal world is the middle part, and the nether regions are the beautiful hips.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें लेकरू एक । प्रसवली हें देख। जयाचें तिन्ही लोक । बाळसें गा॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ lekarū eka | prasavalī heṃ dekha| jayāceṃ tinhī loka | bāḻaseṃ gā|| 6||
verses.meaning: Behold, she gave birth to such a child, whose infancy encompasses all three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चौऱ्यांयशीं लक्ष योनी। तिये कांडां पेरां सांदणी । वाढे प्रतिदिनीं। बाळक हें॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: cauṟyāṃyaśīṃ lakṣa yonī| tiye kāṃḍāṃ perāṃ sāṃdaṇī | vāḍhe pratidinīṃ| bāḻaka heṃ||7||
verses.meaning: In the eighty-four lakh species, the child grows day by day, like joints in a sugarcane stalk.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना देहअवयवीं। नामाचीं लेणीं लेववी। मोहस्तन्यें बाढवी। नित्य नवें॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā dehaavayavīṃ| nāmācīṃ leṇīṃ levavī| mohastanyeṃ bāḍhavī| nitya naveṃ|| 8||
verses.meaning: In various bodily forms, it adorns them with the ornaments of the Divine Name, nourishing them with the milk of delusion, ever new.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सृष्टी वेगवेगळीया। तिया करांघ्रीं आंगोळियां। भिन्नाभिमान सूदलिया। मुदिया तेथें॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: sṛṣṭī vegavegaḻīyā| tiyā karāṃghrīṃ āṃgoḻiyāṃ| bhinnābhimāna sūdaliyā| mudiyā tetheṃ||9||
verses.meaning: The diverse creation, with its various hands and feet, and distinct identities, is but a manifestation of the same fundamental essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें एकलोतें चराचर। अविचारित सुंदर। प्रसबोनि थोर। थोरावली॥ ११०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ ekaloteṃ carācara| avicārita suṃdara| prasaboni thora| thorāvalī|| 110||
verses.meaning: This singular universe, beautiful beyond conception, was brought forth, and thus she (the primordial energy) became great.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं ब्रह्मा प्रातःकाळु । विष्णु तो माध्यान्ह वेळु। सदाशिव सायंकाळु | बाळा यया॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ brahmā prātaḥkāḻu | viṣṇu to mādhyānha veḻu| sadāśiva sāyaṃkāḻu | bāḻā yayā|| 11||
verses.meaning: Brahma is the morning, Vishnu is the midday, and Sadashiva is the evening, my child.

verses.shloka_devanagari: महाप्रळयसेजे। खेळोनि निवांत निजे । विषमज्ञानें उमजें । कल्पोदयीं ॥ ९१२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mahāpraḻayaseje| kheḻoni nivāṃta nije | viṣamajñāneṃ umajeṃ | kalpodayīṃ || 912||
verses.meaning: Having played upon the bed of the great dissolution, it rests peacefully. With the dawn of creation, it awakens through the knowledge of differentiation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ३२८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी अर्जुना इयापरी । मिथ्यादृष्टीच्या घरीं । युगानुवृत्तीचीं करी । चोज पाउलें॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: 328 śrījñāneśvarī arjunā iyāparī | mithyādṛṣṭīcyā gharīṃ | yugānuvṛttīcīṃ karī | coja pāuleṃ|| 13||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, in this way, in the abode of false perception, the footsteps of the ages leave their marks.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संकल्पु जयाचा इष्टु। अहंकारु तो विनटु। ऐसिया होय शेवटु । ज्ञानें यया॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃkalpu jayācā iṣṭu| ahaṃkāru to vinaṭu| aisiyā hoya śevaṭu | jñāneṃ yayā|| 14||
verses.meaning: The one whose resolve is for the desired, and whose ego is adorned, such a one reaches the end through this knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां असो हे बहु बोली । ऐसें विश्व माया व्याली । तेथ साह्य जाली । माझी सत्ता॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ aso he bahu bolī | aiseṃ viśva māyā vyālī | tetha sāhya jālī | mājhī sattā|| 15||
verses.meaning: Let's not dwell on this much. The universe was born from Maya, and my power became its support.

verses.shloka_devanagari: याकारणें मी पिता । महद्रह्म हे माता । अपत्य पंडुसुता । जगडंबरु ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yākāraṇeṃ mī pitā | mahadrahma he mātā | apatya paṃḍusutā | jagaḍaṃbaru || 16||
verses.meaning: Therefore, I am the father, and the great Brahman is the mother. O son of Pandu, the entire universe is our offspring.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां शरीरें बहुतें। देखोनि न भेदें हो चित्तें। जें मनबुद्धयादि भूतें । एकेंचि येथें॥१७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ śarīreṃ bahuteṃ| dekhoni na bhedeṃ ho citteṃ| jeṃ manabuddhayādi bhūteṃ | ekeṃci yetheṃ||17||
verses.meaning: Now, seeing many bodies, the mind is not differentiated, for here, mind, intellect, and other elements are all one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा एकाचि देहीं। काय अनारिसें अवयव नाहीं। तेवीं विचित्र विश्‍व पाहीं। एकचि हें॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā ekāci dehīṃ| kāya anāriseṃ avayava nāhīṃ| tevīṃ vicitra viś‍va pāhīṃ| ekaci heṃ|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as in a single body there are no separate or distinct limbs, so too, behold, this wondrous universe is but one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं उंचा नीचा डाहाळिया। विषमा वेगळालिया। येकाचि जेवीं जालिया। बीजाचिया॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ uṃcā nīcā ḍāhāḻiyā| viṣamā vegaḻāliyā| yekāci jevīṃ jāliyā| bījāciyā|| 19||
verses.meaning: Just as branches, some high and some low, though distinct and varied, all originate from a single seed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि संबंधु तोही ऐसा । मृत्तिके घटु लेंकु जैसा । कां पटत्व कापुसा । नातू होय ॥ १२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi saṃbaṃdhu tohī aisā | mṛttike ghaṭu leṃku jaisā | kāṃ paṭatva kāpusā | nātū hoya || 120||
verses.meaning: And that relationship is like the pot to the clay, or the cloth to the cotton, which is its grandchild.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना कल्लोळपरंपरा। संतती जैसी सागरा । आम्हां आणि चराचरा। संबंधु तैसा ॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā kalloḻaparaṃparā| saṃtatī jaisī sāgarā | āmhāṃ āṇi carācarā| saṃbaṃdhu taisā || 21||
verses.meaning: Just as countless waves are born from the ocean, so too is our relationship with all animate and inanimate creation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि वन्हि आणि ज्वाळ। दोन्ही वन्हीचि केवळ तेवीं मी गा सकळ संबंधु वाबो॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni vanhi āṇi jvāḻa| donhī vanhīci kevaḻa tevīṃ mī gā sakaḻa saṃbaṃdhu vābo|| 22||
verses.meaning: Therefore, fire and its flame are both nothing but fire. Similarly, I am the entirety of all relationships.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जालेंनि जगें मी झांकें । तरी जगत्वें कोण 'फांके। किळेवरी माणिकें । लोपिजे काई ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāleṃni jageṃ mī jhāṃkeṃ | tarī jagatveṃ koṇa 'phāṃke| kiḻevarī māṇikeṃ | lopije kāī || 23||
verses.meaning: If the world covers me, then who reveals the world? Can jewels be hidden by dirt?

verses.shloka_devanagari: अळंकारातें आलें। तरी सोनेंपण काइ गेलें कौं कमळ फांकळलें। कमळत्वा मुके ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aḻaṃkārāteṃ āleṃ| tarī soneṃpaṇa kāi geleṃ kauṃ kamaḻa phāṃkaḻaleṃ| kamaḻatvā muke || 24||
verses.meaning: If an ornament is made, does its goldness cease? Or if a lotus blossoms, does it lose its lotus-ness?

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांग पां धनंजया । अवयवीं अवयविया। आच्छादिजे कीं तया। तेंचि रूप॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃga pāṃ dhanaṃjayā | avayavīṃ avayaviyā| ācchādije kīṃ tayā| teṃci rūpa|| 25||
verses.meaning: Tell me, O Dhananjaya, can a limb cover the whole body, which is its very form?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौं विरूढलिया जोंधळा। कणिसाचा निर्वाळा। वेंचळा कीं आगळा । दिसतसे॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauṃ virūḍhaliyā joṃdhaḻā| kaṇisācā nirvāḻā| veṃcaḻā kīṃ āgaḻā | disatase|| 26||
verses.meaning: When the jowar plant sprouts, the ear of corn, whether it is small or large, becomes visible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जग परोतें। सारूनि पाहिजे मातें। तैसा नोहें उखितें। आघवें मीचि॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jaga paroteṃ| sārūni pāhije māteṃ| taisā noheṃ ukhiteṃ| āghaveṃ mīci|| 27||
verses.meaning: Therefore, if one were to set aside the world and seek Me, it would not be like that; rather, everything is Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा तूं साचोकारा । निश्चयाचा खरा । गांठी बांध वीरा। जीवाचिये ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā tūṃ sācokārā | niścayācā kharā | gāṃṭhī bāṃdha vīrā| jīvāciye || 28||
verses.meaning: You are indeed the true essence of certainty. Tie this truth firmly, O brave one, to your very life.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां मियां मज दाविला । शरीरीं वेगळाला । गुणीं मीचि बांधिला । ऐसा आवडें ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ miyāṃ maja dāvilā | śarīrīṃ vegaḻālā | guṇīṃ mīci bāṃdhilā | aisā āvaḍeṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: Now I have shown myself to myself, distinct from the body. It seems as if I am bound by the qualities (gunas).

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें स्वप्नीं आपण । उठूनियां आत्ममरण। भोगिजे गा जाण। कपिध्वजा॥ १३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ svapnīṃ āpaṇa | uṭhūniyāṃ ātmamaraṇa| bhogije gā jāṇa| kapidhvajā|| 130||
verses.meaning: Just as in a dream, one experiences one's own death after rising, know this, O Kapidhwaja.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां कवळांतें डोळे । प्रकाशूनि पिंवळें । देखती तेंही कळे। तयांसीचि॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ kavaḻāṃteṃ ḍoḻe | prakāśūni piṃvaḻeṃ | dekhatī teṃhī kaḻe| tayāṃsīci|| 31||
verses.meaning: Or, just as those with jaundice see everything yellow, so too do they understand it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना सूर्यप्रकाशें । प्रकटी तैं अभ्र भासे। तो लोपला हेंही दिसे। सूर्येचे कों५८€३२॥ पैं आपणपेनि जालिया। छाया गा आपुलिया । ब्रिहोनी बिहाळिया। आन आहे॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā sūryaprakāśeṃ | prakaṭī taiṃ abhra bhāse| to lopalā heṃhī dise| sūryece koṃ58€32|| paiṃ āpaṇapeni jāliyā| chāyā gā āpuliyā | brihonī bihāḻiyā| āna āhe|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as clouds appear due to the sun's light, and their disappearance is also perceived because of the sun, similarly, the shadow that appears from oneself, is it truly separate from oneself?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसीं इयें नाना देहें। दाऊनि मी नाना होयें। तेथ ऐसा जो बंधु आहे। तेंही देखें॥३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tesīṃ iyeṃ nānā deheṃ| dāūni mī nānā hoyeṃ| tetha aisā jo baṃdhu āhe| teṃhī dekheṃ||34||
verses.meaning: Thus, by manifesting in various bodies, I appear as many. Even in that state, I perceive this bond (of multiplicity).

verses.shloka_devanagari: बंधु कां न बंधिजे। हें जाणणें मज माझें । नेणणेनि उपजे। आपलेनि॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: baṃdhu kāṃ na baṃdhije| heṃ jāṇaṇeṃ maja mājheṃ | neṇaṇeni upaje| āpaleni|| 35||
verses.meaning: Why am I not bound? This knowing is mine, and from not knowing, my own self arises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कोणें गुणें कैसा। मजचि मी बंधु ऐसा । आवडे तें परियेसा । अर्जुनदेवा॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī koṇeṃ guṇeṃ kaisā| majaci mī baṃdhu aisā | āvaḍe teṃ pariyesā | arjunadevā|| 36||
verses.meaning: Therefore, by what qualities and in what manner do I, as a brother, become pleasing to myself? Listen to this, Arjuna, O divine one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गुण ते किती किंधर्म। कायि ययां रूपनाम। कें जालें हें वर्म। अवधारीं पां॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: guṇa te kitī kiṃdharma| kāyi yayāṃ rūpanāma| keṃ jāleṃ heṃ varma| avadhārīṃ pāṃ|| 37||
verses.meaning: How many are these qualities, and what are their forms and names? How did this secret come to be? Listen carefully.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सत्त्वरजतम। तिघांसि हें नाम। आणि प्रकृति जन्म-। भूमिका ययां॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sattvarajatama| tighāṃsi heṃ nāma| āṇi prakṛti janma-| bhūmikā yayāṃ|| 38||
verses.meaning: Thus, Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas – these three are given this name. And Prakriti is the birthplace of these.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ सत्त्व तें उत्तम । रज तें मध्यम । तिहींमाजीं तम । साविया- धारें॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha sattva teṃ uttama | raja teṃ madhyama | tihīṃmājīṃ tama | sāviyā- dhāreṃ|| 39||
verses.meaning: Among these, Sattva is the best, Rajas is the mediocre, and Tamas is the lowest of the three.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें एकेचि वृत्तीच्या ठायीं । त्रिगुणत्व आवडे पाहीं । वयसात्रय देहीं । येकीं जेवीं ॥ १४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ ekeci vṛttīcyā ṭhāyīṃ | triguṇatva āvaḍe pāhīṃ | vayasātraya dehīṃ | yekīṃ jevīṃ || 140||
verses.meaning: Just as the three stages of life (childhood, youth, old age) are experienced within a single body, so too do the three Gunas (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas) manifest within a single state of mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां मीनळेनि कोडें । जंबजंब तूक वाढे । तंवतंव सोनें हीन पडे। पांचिका कसीं॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ mīnaḻeni koḍeṃ | jaṃbajaṃba tūka vāḍhe | taṃvataṃva soneṃ hīna paḍe| pāṃcikā kasīṃ|| 41||
verses.meaning: Just as the more the fish is weighed, the more the gold loses its value in the assay, so too does the spiritual seeker's ego diminish as their devotion grows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सावधपण जेसें। वाहविलें आळसें। सुषुप्ति बेसे। घणावोनी ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ sāvadhapaṇa jeseṃ| vāhavileṃ āḻaseṃ| suṣupti bese| ghaṇāvonī || 42||
verses.meaning: Just as wakefulness is overcome by laziness, so too is deep sleep (sushupti) overcome by a profound, dense slumber.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी अज्ञानांगीकारें। निघाली वृत्ति विखुरे। ते सत्त्वरजद्वारें। तमही होये ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī ajñānāṃgīkāreṃ| nighālī vṛtti vikhure| te sattvarajadvāreṃ| tamahī hoye || 43||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the mind accepts ignorance, its tendencies become scattered. Through the doors of sattva and rajas, it also becomes tamas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना गा जाण। ययां नाम गुण। आतां दाखऊं खुण। बांधिती ते॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā gā jāṇa| yayāṃ nāma guṇa| ātāṃ dākhaūṃ khuṇa| bāṃdhitī te|| 44||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, know that I will now show you the signs by which these (actions) bind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी क्षेत्रज्नदशे । आत्मा मोटका पैसे। हें देह मी ऐसें। मुहूर्त करी ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī kṣetrajnadaśe | ātmā moṭakā paise| heṃ deha mī aiseṃ| muhūrta karī || 45 ||
verses.meaning: Then, in the state of the knower of the field (the individual soul), the Self becomes limited, and it begins to identify itself with the body, thinking, "This body is I."

verses.shloka_devanagari: आजन्ममरणांतीं । देहधर्मी समस्तीं। ममत्वाची सूती। घे ना जंब॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ājanmamaraṇāṃtīṃ | dehadharmī samastīṃ| mamatvācī sūtī| ghe nā jaṃba|| 46||
verses.meaning: From birth until death, in all bodily functions, do not hold onto the thread of possessiveness, O Jambu.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी मीनाच्या तोंडीं । पडेना जंब उंडी। तंव गळ आसुडी। जळपारधी ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī mīnācyā toṃḍīṃ | paḍenā jaṃba uṃḍī| taṃva gaḻa āsuḍī| jaḻapāradhī || 47||
verses.meaning: Just as a fish does not fall into the hook until it bites the bait, so the fisherman waits patiently.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं सत्त्वे लुब्धकें । सुखज्ञानाचीं पाशकें । बोढिजती मग खुडके । मृगु जैसा॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ sattve lubdhakeṃ | sukhajñānācīṃ pāśakeṃ | boḍhijatī maga khuḍake | mṛgu jaisā|| 48||
verses.meaning: Similarly, with the bait of the joy of spiritual knowledge, the senses, like hunters, ensnare the mind, just as a deer is trapped.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग ज्ञानें चडफडी। जाणिवेचे खुर खोडी। स्वयंसुख हें धाडी । हातींचें गा॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga jñāneṃ caḍaphaḍī| jāṇivece khura khoḍī| svayaṃsukha heṃ dhāḍī | hātīṃceṃ gā|| 49||
verses.meaning: Then, through knowledge, the roots of all knowing are severed, and this inherent bliss is attained, as if it were already in one's hand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां विद्यमानें तोखे। लाभमात्रें हरिखे। मी संतुष्ट हेंही देखे। एलाघों लागे॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ vidyamāneṃ tokhe| lābhamātreṃ harikhe| mī saṃtuṣṭa heṃhī dekhe| elāghoṃ lāge|| 150||
verses.meaning: Then, by its very existence, it rejoices; by mere gain, it is delighted. It sees, "I am content," and begins to exult.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे भाग्य ना माझें। आजि सुखियें नाहीं दुजें। विकाराष्टर्के फुंजे। सात्त्विकाचेनि॥ ५९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe bhāgya nā mājheṃ| āji sukhiyeṃ nāhīṃ dujeṃ| vikārāṣṭarke phuṃje| sāttvikāceni|| 591||
verses.meaning: My fortune, it is said, is unparalleled today; no other joy compares, for it swells with the eight sattvic emotions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि येणेंही न सरे। लांकण लागे दुसरें। जें विद्वत्तेचें भरे। भूत आंगीं ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi yeṇeṃhī na sare| lāṃkaṇa lāge dusareṃ| jeṃ vidvatteceṃ bhare| bhūta āṃgīṃ || 52||
verses.meaning: And even with this, it is not enough; another affliction arises, that of the ghost of scholarship possessing one's being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपणचि ज्ञानस्वरूप आहे तें गेलें हें दुःख न वाहे। कीं विषयज्ञानें होये । गगनायेवढा॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaṇaci jñānasvarūpa āhe teṃ geleṃ heṃ duḥkha na vāhe| kīṃ viṣayajñāneṃ hoye | gaganāyevaḍhā|| 53||
verses.meaning: One does not grieve over the loss of one's true nature, which is pure knowledge itself. Instead, through the knowledge of worldly objects, one becomes as vast as the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रावो जैसा स्वप्नीं । रंकपणें रिघे धानीं। तो दों दाणां मानी । इंद्रु ना मी॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: rāvo jaisā svapnīṃ | raṃkapaṇeṃ righe dhānīṃ| to doṃ dāṇāṃ mānī | iṃdru nā mī|| 54||
verses.meaning: Just as a king, in a dream, may assume the state of a pauper and enter a grain field, and then believe that he is not Indra, but merely two grains of rice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें गा देहातीता। जाळेया देहवंता। हों लागे ३३० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी पंडुसुता । बाह्यज्ञानें ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ gā dehātītā| jāḻeyā dehavaṃtā| hoṃ lāge 330 śrījñāneśvarī paṃḍusutā | bāhyajñāneṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: Thus, O Pandu's son, the embodied soul, though beyond the body, begins to experience external knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रवृत्तिशास्त्र बुझे। यज्ञविद्या उमजे। किंबहुना सुझे। स्वर्गवरी ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: pravṛttiśāstra bujhe| yajñavidyā umaje| kiṃbahunā sujhe| svargavarī || 56||
verses.meaning: One understands the science of action, comprehends the knowledge of sacrifice, and indeed, attains up to heaven.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि म्हणे आजि आन। मीवांचूनि नाहीं सज्ञान । चातुर्यचंद्रा गगन। चित्त माझें ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mhaṇe āji āna| mīvāṃcūni nāhīṃ sajñāna | cāturyacaṃdrā gagana| citta mājheṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: And he says, "Today, besides me, there is no one wise. My mind is the sky for the moon of cleverness."

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें सत्त्व सुखज्ञानी। जीवासि लावूनि कानी। बैलाची करी वानी । पांगुळाचिया॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ sattva sukhajñānī| jīvāsi lāvūni kānī| bailācī karī vānī | pāṃguḻāciyā|| 58||
verses.meaning: Thus, the pure knowledge, by whispering into the ear of the soul, makes it like a bull for the lame.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां हाचि शरीरीं । रजें जियापरी। बांधिजे तें अवधारीं। सांगिजैल ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ hāci śarīrīṃ | rajeṃ jiyāparī| bāṃdhije teṃ avadhārīṃ| sāṃgijaila || 59||
verses.meaning: Now, listen, I will explain how the soul is bound in this very body by the quality of 'rajas'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें रज याचि कारणें । जीवातें रंजऊं जाणे। हें अभिलाखार्चे तरुणें। सदाचि गा॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ raja yāci kāraṇeṃ | jīvāteṃ raṃjaūṃ jāṇe| heṃ abhilākhārce taruṇeṃ| sadāci gā|| 160||
verses.meaning: This 'rajas' (passion) exists for this very reason: to delight living beings. It is the ever-youthful spring of desires.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें जीवीं मोटकें रिगे। आणि कामाच्या मदीं लागे । मग वारया वळघे। तृष्णेचिया॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ jīvīṃ moṭakeṃ rige| āṇi kāmācyā madīṃ lāge | maga vārayā vaḻaghe| tṛṣṇeciyā|| 61||
verses.meaning: When this (desire) enters the heart, it becomes entangled in worldly pleasures, and then it is embraced by the wind of craving.

verses.shloka_devanagari: घृतें आंबुखूनि आगियाळें । वज़्ाग्नीचें सादुकलें। आतां बहु थेंकुलें। आहे तेथ ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ghṛteṃ āṃbukhūni āgiyāḻeṃ | vaj़āgnīceṃ sādukaleṃ| ātāṃ bahu theṃkuleṃ| āhe tetha || 62||
verses.meaning: The fire, fueled by ghee, which was once a small spark of the cosmic fire, has now grown immensely there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी खवळे चाड। होय दुःखासकट गोड । इंद्रश्नीहि सांकड। गमों लागे॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī khavaḻe cāḍa| hoya duḥkhāsakaṭa goḍa | iṃdraśnīhi sāṃkaḍa| gamoṃ lāge|| 63||
verses.meaning: Similarly, desire becomes agitated, and even sorrow becomes sweet. Even Indra's glory seems like a burden.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी तृष्णा वाढिनळिया। मेरुही हाता आलिया । तऱही म्हणे एखादिया। दारुणा बळघो॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī tṛṣṇā vāḍhinaḻiyā| meruhī hātā āliyā | taṟahī mhaṇe ekhādiyā| dāruṇā baḻagho|| 64||
verses.meaning: Just as insatiable desire, even after acquiring a mountain of gold, still yearns for more, saying, "Give me something else, something even greater!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: जीविताची कुरोंडी। बोंबाळूं लागे कवडी । मानी तृणाचिये जोडी । कृतकृत्यता ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jīvitācī kuroṃḍī| boṃbāḻūṃ lāge kavaḍī | mānī tṛṇāciye joḍī | kṛtakṛtyatā || 65 ||
verses.meaning: Life becomes a mere trifle, and one starts to value even a blade of grass as a great achievement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आजि असतें वेंचिजेळ। परी पाहे काय कीजेल। ऐसा पांगीं बडील। व्यवसाय मांडी ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āji asateṃ veṃcijeḻa| parī pāhe kāya kījela| aisā pāṃgīṃ baḍīla| vyavasāya māṃḍī || 66||
verses.meaning: Today, I will spend my life in this way. What else can be done? With such a resolve, he began his endeavor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे स्वर्गा हन जावें। तरी काय तेथें खावें। इयालागीं धांवे । याग करूं ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe svargā hana jāveṃ| tarī kāya tetheṃ khāveṃ| iyālāgīṃ dhāṃve | yāga karūṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: He thinks, "If I go to heaven, what will I eat there?" For this reason, he rushes to perform sacrifices.

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्रतापाठीं व्रतें। आचरे इष्टापूर्ते। काम्यावाचूनि हातें । शिवणें नाहीं ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: vratāpāṭhīṃ vrateṃ| ācare iṣṭāpūrte| kāmyāvācūni hāteṃ | śivaṇeṃ nāhīṃ || 68 ||
verses.meaning: He performs vows upon vows, and acts of charity and sacrifice, but his hands are untouched by any desire for their fruits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं ग्रीष्मांतींचा वारा । विसांबो नेणें बीरा। तैसा न म्हणे व्यापारा। रात्र दिवस ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ grīṣmāṃtīṃcā vārā | visāṃbo neṇeṃ bīrā| taisā na mhaṇe vyāpārā| rātra divasa || 69||
verses.meaning: Just as the wind at the end of summer knows no rest, so too does he not cease his activities day and night.

verses.shloka_devanagari: काय चंचळु मासा। कामिनीकटाक्षु जैसा । लबलाहो तैसा । विजूही नाहीं ॥ १७० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāya caṃcaḻu māsā| kāminīkaṭākṣu jaisā | labalāho taisā | vijūhī nāhīṃ || 170 ||
verses.meaning: What is as fleeting as a fish, or as a flirtatious glance from a beautiful woman? Even lightning is not as swift and transient.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेतुळेनि गा वेगें। स्वर्गसंसारपांगें । आगीमाजीं रिगे। क्रियांचिये ॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetuḻeni gā vegeṃ| svargasaṃsārapāṃgeṃ | āgīmājīṃ rige| kriyāṃciye ||79||
verses.meaning: Due to that, one quickly enters the fire of actions, which are the shackles of heaven and worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा देहीं देहावेगळा। ले तृष्णेचिया सांखळा। खटाटोपु वाहे गळां|। व्यापाराचा ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā dehīṃ dehāvegaḻā| le tṛṣṇeciyā sāṃkhaḻā| khaṭāṭopu vāhe gaḻāṃ|| vyāpārācā || 72||
verses.meaning: Thus, though separate from the body, he wears the shackles of desire, carrying the burden of worldly affairs around his neck.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें रजोगुणाचें दारुण। देहीं देहियासी बंधन। परिस आतां विंदाण। तमाचें तें ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ rajoguṇāceṃ dāruṇa| dehīṃ dehiyāsī baṃdhana| parisa ātāṃ viṃdāṇa| tamāceṃ teṃ || 73||
verses.meaning: This terrible quality of passion (rajas) binds the embodied soul to the body. Now listen to the nature of darkness (tamas).

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्यवहाराचेहि डोळे। मंद जेणें पडळें। मोहरात्रीचें काळें। मेहुडें जें॥७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: vyavahārācehi ḍoḻe| maṃda jeṇeṃ paḍaḻeṃ| moharātrīceṃ kāḻeṃ| mehuḍeṃ jeṃ||74||
verses.meaning: The darkness of delusion, like a dense cloud of ignorance, blinds the eyes of worldly affairs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अज्ञानाचें जियाळें। जया एका लागलें। जेणें विश्‍व भुललें। नाचत असे॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ajñānāceṃ jiyāḻeṃ| jayā ekā lāgaleṃ| jeṇeṃ viś‍va bhulaleṃ| nācata ase|| 75||
verses.meaning: The entire universe, deluded by the poison of ignorance, dances to its tune.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अविवेकमहामंत्र। जें मोढ्यमद्याचें पात्र। हें असो मोहनास्त्र। जीवांसि जें ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: avivekamahāmaṃtra| jeṃ moḍhyamadyāceṃ pātra| heṃ aso mohanāstra| jīvāṃsi jeṃ || 76||
verses.meaning: This great mantra of indiscretion, which is a vessel of the wine of ignorance, is indeed a weapon of delusion for all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था तें गा तम । रचूनि ऐसें वर्म। चौखुरी देहात्म-। मानियातें ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā teṃ gā tama | racūni aiseṃ varma| caukhurī dehātma-| māniyāteṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, it is this darkness that creates such a secret, causing those who identify with the body to be deluded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें एकचि कौर शरीरीं। माजों लागे चराचरीं। आणि तेथ दुसरी । गोठी नाहीं ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ ekaci kaura śarīrīṃ| mājoṃ lāge carācarīṃ| āṇi tetha dusarī | goṭhī nāhīṃ || 78||
verses.meaning: This one body of the Kauravas, when it begins to spread throughout the animate and inanimate world, there is no other discourse.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सर्वेद्रियां जाड्य । मनामाजीं मौढ्य । माल्हाती जे दार्ढ्य। आलस्याचें ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: sarvedriyāṃ jāḍya | manāmājīṃ mauḍhya | mālhātī je dārḍhya| ālasyāceṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: All senses become dull, the mind becomes foolish, and the body is gripped by the firmness of laziness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आंगें आंग मोडामोडी । कार्यजातीं अनावडी। नुसती परवडी । जांभयांची ॥ ९८० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṃgeṃ āṃga moḍāmoḍī | kāryajātīṃ anāvaḍī| nusatī paravaḍī | jāṃbhayāṃcī || 980 ||
verses.meaning: The body is breaking down, the senses are out of control, and there is nothing but a continuous stream of yawns.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उघडियाची दिठी । देखणें नाहीं किरीटी । नाळवितांचि उठी । बो म्हणौनि॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ughaḍiyācī diṭhī | dekhaṇeṃ nāhīṃ kirīṭī | nāḻavitāṃci uṭhī | bo mhaṇauni|| 81||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, the one who is awake does not need to see; without being called, he rises, saying 'Bo'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पडल्यि धोंडी । नेणें कानी मुरडी। तयाचि परी मुरकुंडी। उकल नेणें॥८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: paḍalyi dhoṃḍī | neṇeṃ kānī muraḍī| tayāci parī murakuṃḍī| ukala neṇeṃ||82||
verses.meaning: Just as a stone, once fallen, knows no turning back, so too does the entangled mind not know how to unravel itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पृथ्वी पाताळीं जावो । कां आकाशही वरी येवो। परी उठणें हा भावो। उपजों नेणें॥८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: pṛthvī pātāḻīṃ jāvo | kāṃ ākāśahī varī yevo| parī uṭhaṇeṃ hā bhāvo| upajoṃ neṇeṃ||83||
verses.meaning: Let the earth go to the netherworld, or the sky come down; but the thought of rising (from meditation) does not arise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उचितानुचित आधवें। झांसुरतां नाठवे जीवें । जेथींचा तेथ लोळावें। ऐसी मेधा॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ucitānucita ādhaveṃ| jhāṃsuratāṃ nāṭhave jīveṃ | jethīṃcā tetha loḻāveṃ| aisī medhā|| 84||
verses.meaning: The intellect that, when faced with what is proper and improper, becomes so bewildered that it cannot discern, and simply rolls along wherever it finds itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उभऊनि करतळें। पडिघाये कपोळें । पायाचे शिरियाळें। मांडू लागे॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ubhaūni karataḻeṃ| paḍighāye kapoḻeṃ | pāyāce śiriyāḻeṃ| māṃḍū lāge|| 85||
verses.meaning: He would raise his hands and strike his cheeks, then begin to massage his feet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि निद्रेविषयीं चांगु जीवीं आधि लागु। झोंपीं जातां स्वर्गु। वाबो म्हणे ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi nidreviṣayīṃ cāṃgu jīvīṃ ādhi lāgu| jhoṃpīṃ jātāṃ svargu| vābo mhaṇe || 86||
verses.meaning: And regarding sleep, he would first feel a good longing in his heart, saying, "Going to sleep is like going to heaven."

verses.shloka_devanagari: ब्रह्मायु होईजे। मा निजेलियाचि असिजे। हें वांचूनि दुजें। व्यसन नाहीं ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: brahmāyu hoīje| mā nijeliyāci asije| heṃ vāṃcūni dujeṃ| vyasana nāhīṃ || 87||
verses.meaning: Even if one were to live for the duration of Brahma's life, one would remain in a state of slumber. There is no other addiction than this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वाटें जातां बोघें। कल्हातांही डोळा लागे। अमृतही परी नेघे। जरी नीद आली ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vāṭeṃ jātāṃ bogheṃ| kalhātāṃhī ḍoḻā lāge| amṛtahī parī neghe| jarī nīda ālī || 88||
verses.meaning: Even if one is walking on a path, or arguing, if sleep comes, the eyes close. Similarly, even if nectar is offered, one will not take it if sleep has overcome them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि आक्रोशबळें । व्यापारे कोणे एके वेळे। निगालें तरी आंधळें। रोषें जैसें॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci ākrośabaḻeṃ | vyāpāre koṇe eke veḻe| nigāleṃ tarī āṃdhaḻeṃ| roṣeṃ jaiseṃ|| 89||
verses.meaning: Just as a blind person, driven by the force of anger, might rush out at some point, so too does the mind act.

verses.shloka_iast: kedhavāṃ kaiseṃ rāhāṭāveṃ| koṇesīṃ kāya bolāveṃ| heṃ ṭhākateṃ kauoṃ nāgaveṃ| heṃhī neṇeṃ|| 9190||
verses.meaning: When and how to behave, what to speak with whom—this understanding, too, I do not possess.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वणवा मियां आघवा । पांखें पुसोनि घेयावा । पतंगु पां हांवा । घाली जेवीं ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: vaṇavā miyāṃ āghavā | pāṃkheṃ pusoni gheyāvā | pataṃgu pāṃ hāṃvā | ghālī jevīṃ || 91||
verses.meaning: Just as a moth, with great eagerness, throws itself into a blazing fire, so too should one, with complete devotion, surrender themselves to the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा वळघे साहसा। अकरणींच धिंवसा। किंबहुना ऐसा । प्रमादु रुचे॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā vaḻaghe sāhasā| akaraṇīṃca dhiṃvasā| kiṃbahunā aisā | pramādu ruce|| 92||
verses.meaning: Similarly, one embraces recklessness, a daring spirit in inaction; in short, such delusion is appealing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं निद्रालस्यप्रमादीं। तम इया त्रिबंधीं। बांधे निरुपाधी। चोखटातें ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ nidrālasyapramādīṃ| tama iyā tribaṃdhīṃ| bāṃdhe nirupādhī| cokhaṭāteṃ || 93||
verses.meaning: Thus, through sleep, laziness, and negligence, Tamas binds even the purest, who is beyond all attributes, with these three ties.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा वन्ही काष्ठीं भरे। तें दिसे काष्ठाकारें। व्योम घटें आवरे। तें घटाकाश॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā vanhī kāṣṭhīṃ bhare| teṃ dise kāṣṭhākāreṃ| vyoma ghaṭeṃ āvare| teṃ ghaṭākāśa|| 94||
verses.meaning: Just as fire, when it enters wood, appears in the form of the wood; and space, when enclosed by a pot, becomes the space within the pot.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना सरोवर भरलें। तैं चंद्रत्व तेथें बिंबलें। तैसें गुणाभासीं बांधलें। आत्मत्व गमे॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā sarovara bharaleṃ| taiṃ caṃdratva tetheṃ biṃbaleṃ| taiseṃ guṇābhāsīṃ bāṃdhaleṃ| ātmatva game|| 95||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon's reflection appears in many lakes, so too does the Self seem to be bound by the reflections of the gunas (qualities).

verses.shloka_devanagari: ३३२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी पै हरूनि कफवात। जेैं देहीं आटोपे पित्त। तें करी संतप्त। देह जेबीं॥९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: 332 śrījñāneśvarī pai harūni kaphavāta| jeaiṃ dehīṃ āṭope pitta| teṃ karī saṃtapta| deha jebīṃ||96||
verses.meaning: Just as when phlegm and wind are removed, the bile in the body becomes dominant and afflicts the body, so too does the mind become afflicted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वरिष आतप जेैसें। जिणौनि शीतचि दिसे। तेव्हां होय हिंब ऐसें। आकाश हें ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ variṣa ātapa jeaiseṃ| jiṇauni śītaci dise| tevhāṃ hoya hiṃba aiseṃ| ākāśa heṃ || 97||
verses.meaning: Or just as the heat of the sun, having conquered the cold, makes the sky appear like ice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना स्वप्न जागृती । लोपूनि ये सुषुप्ती । तैं क्षणु एक चित्तवृत्ती । तेचि होय ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā svapna jāgṛtī | lopūni ye suṣuptī | taiṃ kṣaṇu eka cittavṛttī | teci hoya || 98||
verses.meaning: When the many dreams of the waking state dissolve into deep sleep, for a moment, the mind's activity becomes that very state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं रजतमें हारवी । जैं सत्त्व माजु मिरवी । तैं जीवाकरवीं म्हणवी। सुखिया ना मी॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ rajatameṃ hāravī | jaiṃ sattva māju miravī | taiṃ jīvākaravīṃ mhaṇavī| sukhiyā nā mī|| 99||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the qualities of Rajas and Tamas are overcome, and Sattva predominates, then the individual soul declares, "I am truly happy."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंचि सत्त्व रज। लोपूनि तमाचें भोज। वळघें तैं सहज। प्रमादीं होय॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃci sattva raja| lopūni tamāceṃ bhoja| vaḻagheṃ taiṃ sahaja| pramādīṃ hoya|| 200||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when sattva and rajas are suppressed, and tamas takes over, then naturally, one becomes prone to error and delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचि गा परिपाठीं । सत्त्व तमातें पोटीं । घाळूनि जेव्हां उठी। रजोगुण॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāci gā paripāṭhīṃ | sattva tamāteṃ poṭīṃ | ghāḻūni jevhāṃ uṭhī| rajoguṇa|| 1||
verses.meaning: However, when the quality of Rajas (activity and passion) arises, it subsumes both Sattva (goodness and purity) and Tamas (ignorance and inertia) within itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां कर्मावांचूनि कांहीं । आन गोमटें नाहीं। ऐसें मानी देहीं । देहराजु॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ karmāvāṃcūni kāṃhīṃ | āna gomaṭeṃ nāhīṃ| aiseṃ mānī dehīṃ | deharāju|| 2||
verses.meaning: Then, the king of the body (the embodied soul) believes that there is nothing better than action (karma) for the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: त्रिगुणवृद्दविनिरूपण। तीं एलोकीं सांगितलें जाण । आतां सत्त्वादिवृन्दिलक्षण । सादर परियेसीं॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: triguṇavṛddavinirūpaṇa| tīṃ elokīṃ sāṃgitaleṃ jāṇa | ātāṃ sattvādivṛndilakṣaṇa | sādara pariyesīṃ|| 3||
verses.meaning: The description of the growth of the three Gunas has been given in those chapters. Now, listen attentively to the characteristics of the growth of Sattva and the others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं रजतमविजयें। सत्त्व गा देहीं इयें। वाढतां चिन्हें तियें। ऐसीं होती॥४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ rajatamavijayeṃ| sattva gā dehīṃ iyeṃ| vāḍhatāṃ cinheṃ tiyeṃ| aisīṃ hotī||4||
verses.meaning: Just as the signs of silver appear when it increases, so too do the signs of Sattva (goodness) manifest in the body when it grows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे प्रज्ञा आंतुलीकडे। न समाती बाहेरी बोसंडे। बसंती 'पदाखंडें । दृती जैसी ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: je prajñā āṃtulīkaḍe| na samātī bāherī bosaṃḍe| basaṃtī 'padākhaṃḍeṃ | dṛtī jaisī || 5||
verses.meaning: Just as the earth, though vast, is contained within the seed, so too does wisdom, though boundless, reside within the heart, not overflowing outwardly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सर्वेद्रियांच्या आंगणीं। विवेक करी राबणी। साचचि करचरणीं। होती डोळे ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: sarvedriyāṃcyā āṃgaṇīṃ| viveka karī rābaṇī| sācaci karacaraṇīṃ| hotī ḍoḻe || 6||
verses.meaning: In the courtyard of all senses, discrimination works diligently, and truly, hands and feet become eyes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: राजहंसापुढें । चांचूचें आगरडें । तोडी जेवीं झगडे । क्षीरनीराचे ॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: rājahaṃsāpuḍheṃ | cāṃcūceṃ āgaraḍeṃ | toḍī jevīṃ jhagaḍe | kṣīranīrāce ||7||
verses.meaning: Just as a royal swan, with its beak, separates milk from water, so too does the discerning intellect distinguish between the real and the unreal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं दोषादोषविवेकीं। इंद्रियेंचि होती 'पारखीं। नियमु बा रे पायिकी । बोळगे तैं ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ doṣādoṣavivekīṃ| iṃdriyeṃci hotī 'pārakhīṃ| niyamu bā re pāyikī | boḻage taiṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: Similarly, in discerning right from wrong, the senses themselves become the discerning judges. Then, O child, discipline becomes a mere servant, following their lead.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाइकणें तें कानचि वाळी । न पाहाणें तें दिठीचि गाळी । अवाच्य तें टाळी । जीभचि गा॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nāikaṇeṃ teṃ kānaci vāḻī | na pāhāṇeṃ teṃ diṭhīci gāḻī | avācya teṃ ṭāḻī | jībhaci gā|| 9||
verses.meaning: That which should not be heard, the ears themselves should avoid; that which should not be seen, the sight itself should reject; that which is unspeakable, the tongue itself should shun.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वातीपुढां जैसें। पळों लागे काळवसें। निषिद्ध इंद्रियां तेसें। समोर नोहे॥ २९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: vātīpuḍhāṃ jaiseṃ| paḻoṃ lāge kāḻavaseṃ| niṣiddha iṃdriyāṃ teseṃ| samora nohe|| 290||
verses.meaning: Just as darkness flees before a lamp, so too do forbidden things not stand before the senses of a yogi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: धाराधरकाळें । महानदी उचंबळे। तैसी बुद्धि पघळे। शास्त्रजातीं ॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: dhārādharakāḻeṃ | mahānadī ucaṃbaḻe| taisī buddhi paghaḻe| śāstrajātīṃ || 11||
verses.meaning: Just as a great river swells with the monsoon rains, so too does the intellect expand and flow through the study of scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा पुनवेच्या दिवशीं । चंद्रप्रभा धांवे आकाशीं । ज्ञानी वृत्ति तैसी । फांके सैंघ ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā punavecyā divaśīṃ | caṃdraprabhā dhāṃve ākāśīṃ | jñānī vṛtti taisī | phāṃke saiṃgha || 12||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon's light spreads across the sky on a full moon night, so too does the intellect of a wise person expand in all directions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वासना एकवटे । प्रवृत्ति बोहटे । मानस विटे । विषयांवरी ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāsanā ekavaṭe | pravṛtti bohaṭe | mānasa viṭe | viṣayāṃvarī || 13||
verses.meaning: Desires converge, worldly inclinations cease, and the mind detaches from sensory objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं सत्त्व वाढे। तैं हें चिन्ह फुडें। आणि निधनही घडे । तेव्हांच जरी॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ sattva vāḍhe| taiṃ heṃ cinha phuḍeṃ| āṇi nidhanahī ghaḍe | tevhāṃca jarī|| 14||
verses.meaning: Thus, when goodness (sattva) increases, these signs become evident. And even if death occurs at that very moment, it is still auspicious.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां पाहालेनि सुयाणें। जाल्या परगुणें। पढियंतें पाहुणें। स्वर्गौनियां ।॥। १५ ॥ तरी जैसीचि घरींची संपत्ती । आणि तैसीच औदार्यधेर्यवृत्ती । मा परत्रा आणि कौर्ती। कां नोहावें ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ pāhāleni suyāṇeṃ| jālyā paraguṇeṃ| paḍhiyaṃteṃ pāhuṇeṃ| svargauniyāṃ |||| 15 || tarī jaisīci gharīṃcī saṃpattī | āṇi taisīca audāryadheryavṛttī | mā paratrā āṇi kaurtī| kāṃ nohāveṃ || 16||
verses.meaning: When a wise person sees someone with good qualities, it's like a beloved guest arriving from heaven. If one has both inner wealth and a generous, courageous disposition, why wouldn't they achieve both the afterlife and fame?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग गोमटेया तया। जावळी असे धनंजया । तेवीं सत्त्वीं जाणे देहा। कें आधि गा॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga gomaṭeyā tayā| jāvaḻī ase dhanaṃjayā | tevīṃ sattvīṃ jāṇe dehā| keṃ ādhi gā|| 17||
verses.meaning: Then, O Dhananjaya, just as a beautiful twin is born, so too does the body arise from Sattva. Where then is its origin?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे स्वगुणीं उद्‌भट। घेऊनि सत्त्व चोखट । निगे सांडूनि कोपट। भोगक्षम हें ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: je svaguṇīṃ ud‌bhaṭa| gheūni sattva cokhaṭa | nige sāṃḍūni kopaṭa| bhogakṣama heṃ || 18||
verses.meaning: That which, endowed with its own inherent qualities and pure sattva, emerges, abandoning this perishable body, becomes capable of experiencing the fruits of actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अवचटें ऐसा जो जाये। तो सत्त्वाचाचि नवा होये। किंबहुना जन्म लाहे। ज्ञानियांमाजीं ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: avacaṭeṃ aisā jo jāye| to sattvācāci navā hoye| kiṃbahunā janma lāhe| jñāniyāṃmājīṃ || 99||
verses.meaning: One who unexpectedly attains such a state is indeed reborn into pure goodness, or rather, takes birth among the wise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांग पां धनुर्धगा। रावो रायपणें डोंगरा । गेलिया अपुरा। होय काई॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃga pāṃ dhanurdhagā| rāvo rāyapaṇeṃ ḍoṃgarā | geliyā apurā| hoya kāī|| 220||
verses.meaning: Tell me, O Arjuna, if a king, due to his kingship, goes to a mountain and is unable to return, what good is that kingship?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी येथिंचा दिवा । नेलिया सेजिया गांवा । तो तेथें तरी पांडवा। दीपच्ि कों॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī yethiṃcā divā | neliyā sejiyā gāṃvā | to tetheṃ tarī pāṃḍavā| dīpaci koṃ|| 21||
verses.meaning: Just as a lamp from here, taken to a neighboring village, illuminates that place as well, O Pandava, so too is the light of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी ते सत्त्वशुद्धी। आगळी ज्ञानेंसी वृद्धी। तरंगाबो लागे बुद्धी। विवेकावरी ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī te sattvaśuddhī| āgaḻī jñāneṃsī vṛddhī| taraṃgābo lāge buddhī| vivekāvarī || 22||
