verses.meaning: Just as a person with good eyesight can perceive the light of many suns, so too does knowledge alone provide the delight of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तया ज्ञानालागीं । कवणा पां योग्यता आंगीं । हें पाहतां जगीं । देखिला एकु ॥३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tayā jñānālāgīṃ | kavaṇā pāṃ yogyatā āṃgīṃ | heṃ pāhatāṃ jagīṃ | dekhilā eku ||33||
verses.meaning: Then, who indeed possesses the inherent qualification for that knowledge? When I looked for such a one in the world, I found only one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें पाताळींचेंही निधान। दाबीळ कौर अंजन। परी होआवे लोचन । 'पायाळाचे ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ pātāḻīṃceṃhī nidhāna| dābīḻa kaura aṃjana| parī hoāve locana | 'pāyāḻāce || 34||
verses.meaning: Even if the treasure of the netherworld is revealed by applying collyrium, one must still possess the eyes of a subterranean being to perceive it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें मोक्ष देईल ज्ञान। येथें कौर नाहीं आन । परी तेंचि थारे ऐसें मन। शुद्ध होआवे ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ mokṣa deīla jñāna| yetheṃ kaura nāhīṃ āna | parī teṃci thāre aiseṃ mana| śuddha hoāve || 35||
verses.meaning: Just as knowledge grants liberation, there is no doubt about this. But for that knowledge to take root, the mind must be purified.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी विरक्‍्तीवांचूनि कहीं । ज्ञानासि 'तगणेंचि नाहीं। हें विचारूनि ठाई । ठेविलें देवें ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī virak‍tīvāṃcūni kahīṃ | jñānāsi 'tagaṇeṃci nāhīṃ| heṃ vicārūni ṭhāī | ṭhevileṃ deveṃ || 36||
verses.meaning: Therefore, without detachment, knowledge cannot truly manifest. The Lord has firmly established this truth after careful consideration.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां विरक्‍्तीची 'कवण परी । जे येऊनि मनातें वरी । हेंही सर्वज्ञें श्रीहरी । देखिलें असे ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ virak‍tīcī 'kavaṇa parī | je yeūni manāteṃ varī | heṃhī sarvajñeṃ śrīharī | dekhileṃ ase || 37||
verses.meaning: Now, how does detachment come to embrace the mind? The all-knowing Shri Hari has also seen this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे विषें रांधिलळी रससोये। जैं जेवणारा ठाउवी होये। तैं तो ताटचि सांडूनि जाये। जयापरी॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: je viṣeṃ rāṃdhilaḻī rasasoye| jaiṃ jevaṇārā ṭhāuvī hoye| taiṃ to tāṭaci sāṃḍūni jāye| jayāparī|| 38||
verses.meaning: Just as a person, knowing that the food prepared with great care is poisoned, abandons the plate, so too should one abandon worldly pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी संसारा या समस्ता। जाणिजे जैं अनित्यता। तैं वैराग्य दवडितां। पाठी लागे॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī saṃsārā yā samastā| jāṇije jaiṃ anityatā| taiṃ vairāgya davaḍitāṃ| pāṭhī lāge|| 39||
verses.meaning: In the same way, when one truly understands the impermanence of this entire worldly existence, then dispassion (vairagya) pursues them, even if they try to push it away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अनित्यत्व या कैसें। तेंचि वृक्षाकारमिषें । सांगिजत असे विशवेशें । पंचदशीं ॥ ४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ anityatva yā kaiseṃ| teṃci vṛkṣākāramiṣeṃ | sāṃgijata ase viśaveśeṃ | paṃcadaśīṃ || 40||
verses.meaning: Now, how is this impermanence? That very thing is explained in the Panchadashi, through the analogy of a tree, with great clarity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उपडिलें कवतिके । झाड येरी मोहरा ठाके। तें वेगें जैसें सुके । तैसें हें नोहे॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: upaḍileṃ kavatike | jhāḍa yerī moharā ṭhāke| teṃ vegeṃ jaiseṃ suke | taiseṃ heṃ nohe|| 49||
verses.meaning: If a tree is uprooted playfully, it might appear to blossom, but it quickly withers. This (spiritual experience) is not like that.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यातें 'एकेपरी । रूपकाचिया कुसरी । सारीतसे वारी । संसाराची ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yāteṃ 'ekeparī | rūpakāciyā kusarī | sārītase vārī | saṃsārācī || 42||
verses.meaning: In this way, through the art of allegory, the cycle of worldly existence is brought to an end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: करूनि संसार वावो । स्वरूपीं अहंते ठावो । होआवया अध्याबो । पंधरावा हा॥ ४३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: karūni saṃsāra vāvo | svarūpīṃ ahaṃte ṭhāvo | hoāvayā adhyābo | paṃdharāvā hā|| 43 ||
verses.meaning: Having made the worldly life futile, and the ego established in the Self, this fifteenth chapter is for the purpose of understanding this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां हेंचि आघवें। ग्रंथगर्भींचें चांगावें। उपलविजेळ जीवें । आकर्णिजे॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ heṃci āghaveṃ| graṃthagarbhīṃceṃ cāṃgāveṃ| upalavijeḻa jīveṃ | ākarṇije|| 44||
verses.meaning: Now, all that is good within the essence of this scripture will be revealed to you. Listen with your very life.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी महानंदसमुद्र । जो पूर्ण पूर्णिमाचंद्र । तो द्वारकेचा नरेंद्र । ऐसें म्हणे ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī mahānaṃdasamudra | jo pūrṇa pūrṇimācaṃdra | to dvārakecā nareṃdra | aiseṃ mhaṇe || 45 ||
verses.meaning: He, who is the ocean of supreme bliss, the full moon, the king of Dwarka, thus it is said.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा पैं पंडुकुमरा । येतां स्वरूपाचिया घरा । करीतसे आडवारा । विश्वाभासु जो॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā paiṃ paṃḍukumarā | yetāṃ svarūpāciyā gharā | karītase āḍavārā | viśvābhāsu jo|| 46||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, the illusion of the universe obstructs the path to the abode of the true Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो हा जगडंबरु। नोहे येथ संसारु। हा जाणिजे महातरु । थांबला असे॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: to hā jagaḍaṃbaru| nohe yetha saṃsāru| hā jāṇije mahātaru | thāṃbalā ase|| 47||
verses.meaning: This entire universe is not a mere worldly existence. Know that it is a great tree, standing still.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी येरां रुखांसारिखा। हा तळीं मूळें वरी शाखा । तैसा नोहे म्हणोनि लेखा । नयेचि कवणा ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī yerāṃ rukhāṃsārikhā| hā taḻīṃ mūḻeṃ varī śākhā | taisā nohe mhaṇoni lekhā | nayeci kavaṇā || 48||
verses.meaning: But this tree is not like other trees, with roots below and branches above. Therefore, it cannot be comprehended by anyone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आगी कां कुऱ्हाडी । होय रिगावा जरी बुडीं। तरी हो कां भलतेवढी। वरिचीळ वाढी॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āgī kāṃ kuṟhāḍī | hoya rigāvā jarī buḍīṃ| tarī ho kāṃ bhalatevaḍhī| varicīḻa vāḍhī|| 49||
verses.meaning: Even if fire or an axe were to strike at its roots, a tree would still grow upwards, no matter how large it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे तुटलिया मूळापाशीं । उलंडेल कां शाखांशीं । परी तैशी गोठी कायशी । हा सोपा नव्हे ॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: je tuṭaliyā mūḻāpāśīṃ | ulaṃḍela kāṃ śākhāṃśīṃ | parī taiśī goṭhī kāyaśī | hā sopā navhe || 50||
verses.meaning: If the root is severed, will the branches remain? But such a thing is not easy to understand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना हें कवतिक । सांगतां असे अलौकिक । जे वाढी अधोमुख । रुखा यया॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā heṃ kavatika | sāṃgatāṃ ase alaukika | je vāḍhī adhomukha | rukhā yayā|| 51||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this wonder I speak of is extraordinary, for this tree grows downwards.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा भानू उंची नेणों कें । रश्मिजाळ तळीं 'फांके । संसार हें कावरुखें। झाड तैसें ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā bhānū uṃcī neṇoṃ keṃ | raśmijāḻa taḻīṃ 'phāṃke | saṃsāra heṃ kāvarukheṃ| jhāḍa taiseṃ || 52||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's height is unknown, yet its rays spread below, so too is the tree of worldly existence, with its roots above and branches below.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आधी नाथी तितुकें । रुंधलें असें येणेंचि एकें। कल्पांतींचेनि उदकें । व्योम जेसें॥५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ādhī nāthī titukeṃ | ruṃdhaleṃ aseṃ yeṇeṃci ekeṃ| kalpāṃtīṃceni udakeṃ | vyoma jeseṃ||53||
verses.meaning: And before that, all that was not, was obstructed by this one, just as the sky is by the waters of the deluge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां रवीच्या अस्तमानीं। आंधारेनि कोंदे रजनी। तैसा हाचि गगनीं। मांडला असे॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ ravīcyā astamānīṃ| āṃdhāreni koṃde rajanī| taisā hāci gaganīṃ| māṃḍalā ase|| 54||
verses.meaning: Just as darkness engulfs the night at the setting of the sun, so too does this (illusion) prevail in the sky (of consciousness).

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया फळ ना चुंबितां। फूल ना तुरंबितां। जें कांहीं पंडुसुता । तें रुखुचि हा॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā phaḻa nā cuṃbitāṃ| phūla nā turaṃbitāṃ| jeṃ kāṃhīṃ paṃḍusutā | teṃ rukhuci hā|| 55||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, without tasting the fruit or adorning oneself with the flower, whatever it is, it is the tree itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा उर्ध्वभूळ आहे। परी उन्मूळिला नोहे। येणेंचि हा होये । शाडूवळू गा॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā urdhvabhūḻa āhe| parī unmūḻilā nohe| yeṇeṃci hā hoye | śāḍūvaḻū gā|| 56||
verses.meaning: This tree has its roots above, yet it is not uprooted. Because of this, it is indeed a tree that provides shade and shelter.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि उर्ध्वमूळ ऐसें । निगदिलें कीर असे । परी अधींही असोसें। मूळें यया ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi urdhvamūḻa aiseṃ | nigadileṃ kīra ase | parī adhīṃhī asoseṃ| mūḻeṃ yayā || 57||
verses.meaning: And it is indeed said that its roots are above, but it also has countless roots below.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रबळला चौमेरी । पिंपळा कां वडाचिया परी। जे पारंबियांमाझारीं । डहाळिया असती ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: prabaḻalā caumerī | piṃpaḻā kāṃ vaḍāciyā parī| je pāraṃbiyāṃmājhārīṃ | ḍahāḻiyā asatī || 58||
verses.meaning: Like a mighty banyan or peepal tree, whose branches are supported by aerial roots.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि गा धनंजया । संसारतरु यया । अधींचि आथी खांदिया । हेंही नाहीं ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci gā dhanaṃjayā | saṃsārataru yayā | adhīṃci āthī khāṃdiyā | heṃhī nāhīṃ || 59||
verses.meaning: Thus, O Dhananjaya, this tree of worldly existence does not even have branches from the very beginning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी उर्ध्वाहीकडे । शाखांचे मांदोडे। दिसताति अपाडें। सासिन्नळे॥ ६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī urdhvāhīkaḍe | śākhāṃce māṃdoḍe| disatāti apāḍeṃ| sāsinnaḻe|| 60||
verses.meaning: Yet, above, the branches appear immensely dense and intertwined.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जालें गगनचि पां वेलिये। कां वारा मांडला रुखाचेनि आयें। नाना अवस्थात्रयें। उदयला असे॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāleṃ gaganaci pāṃ veliye| kāṃ vārā māṃḍalā rukhāceni āyeṃ| nānā avasthātrayeṃ| udayalā ase||61||
verses.meaning: It is as if the sky itself has become a creeper, or the wind has manifested through the trees, or the three states of consciousness have arisen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा हा एकु । विश्‍वाकार विटंकु। उदयला जाण रुखु। ऊर्ध्वमूळु॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā hā eku | viś‍vākāra viṭaṃku| udayalā jāṇa rukhu| ūrdhvamūḻu||62||
verses.meaning: Thus, this entire universe, like a grand tree, has emerged, with its roots above.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ऊर्ध्व या कवण। येथें मूळ तें किंलक्षण। कां अधोमुखपण। शाखा कैसिया॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ ūrdhva yā kavaṇa| yetheṃ mūḻa teṃ kiṃlakṣaṇa| kāṃ adhomukhapaṇa| śākhā kaisiyā|| 63||
verses.meaning: Now, what is this upward direction? What is the nature of its root here? And how are its branches facing downwards?

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा द्रुमा यया। अधीं जिया मुळिया। तिया कोण कैसिया। ऊर्ध्व शाखा॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā drumā yayā| adhīṃ jiyā muḻiyā| tiyā koṇa kaisiyā| ūrdhva śākhā|| 64||
verses.meaning: Or, if the roots of a tree are not known, how can one understand its upward-growing branches?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अशवत्धु हा ऐसी । प्रसित्दि कायसी। आत्मविदविलासीं। निर्णयो केला ॥६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi aśavatdhu hā aisī | prasitdi kāyasī| ātmavidavilāsīṃ| nirṇayo kelā ||65||
verses.meaning: And what is this fame of the Ashvattha tree? It has been decided in the glorious play of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें आधवेंचि बरवें। तुझिये प्रतीतीसि फावे। तेसेनि सांगो सोलिंवे । ३४६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी विन्यासें गा॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ ādhaveṃci baraveṃ| tujhiye pratītīsi phāve| teseni sāṃgo soliṃve | 346 śrījñāneśvarī vinyāseṃ gā|| 66||
verses.meaning: This entire discourse, which is pleasing to your understanding, I will explain in a simple manner, O Dnyaneshwari, with its full exposition.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ऐकें गा सुभगा। हा प्रसंगु असे तुजचिजोगा। कानचि करीं हो सर्वांगा। हियें आधिलिया॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī aikeṃ gā subhagā| hā prasaṃgu ase tujacijogā| kānaci karīṃ ho sarvāṃgā| hiyeṃ ādhiliyā|| 67||
verses.meaning: Listen, O fortunate one, this occasion is truly meant for you. Let your ears become your entire body, and let your heart be fully attentive.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें प्रेमरसें सुरफुरें। बोलिलें जंब यादववीरें। तंव अवधान अर्जुनाकारें। मूर्त जालें ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ premaraseṃ suraphureṃ| bolileṃ jaṃba yādavavīreṃ| taṃva avadhāna arjunākāreṃ| mūrta jāleṃ || 68 ||
verses.meaning: As the valiant Krishna spoke thus, overflowing with the nectar of love, Arjuna's attention became a tangible form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देव निरूपिती तें थेंकुलें। येवढें श्रोतेपण फांकलें। जैसें आकाशा खेंव पसरिळें। दाही दिशीं ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: deva nirūpitī teṃ theṃkuleṃ| yevaḍheṃ śrotepaṇa phāṃkaleṃ| jaiseṃ ākāśā kheṃva pasariḻeṃ| dāhī diśīṃ || 69||
verses.meaning: The divine discourse is but a small drop, yet its audience has expanded so vastly, like the sky stretching its embrace in all ten directions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: श्रीकृष्णोक्तिसागरा। हा अगस्तीचि दुसरा । म्हणौनि घोंटु भरों पाहे एकसरा। अवघेयाचा ॥ ७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: śrīkṛṣṇoktisāgarā| hā agastīci dusarā | mhaṇauni ghoṃṭu bharoṃ pāhe ekasarā| avagheyācā || 70||
verses.meaning: O ocean of Shri Krishna's words! This is like a second Agasti, who seeks to drink it all in one gulp.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी सोय सांडूनि खवळिली । आवडी अर्जुनी देवें देखिली । तेथ जालेनि सुखें केली । कुरवंडी तया ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī soya sāṃḍūni khavaḻilī | āvaḍī arjunī deveṃ dekhilī | tetha jāleni sukheṃ kelī | kuravaṃḍī tayā || 79||
verses.meaning: Seeing Arjuna's intense longing, the Lord, overflowing with joy, offered himself as a sacrifice to him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणे धनंजया तें ऊर्ध्व गा तरू यया । येणें रुखेंचि कां जयां। ऊर्ध्वता गमे॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇe dhanaṃjayā teṃ ūrdhva gā tarū yayā | yeṇeṃ rukheṃci kāṃ jayāṃ| ūrdhvatā game|| 72||
verses.meaning: Then, Arjuna, he says, that which is above, that tree, by what means does its upwardness appear to be so?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं मध्योर्ध्व अध। हे नाहीं जेथ भेद। अद्दयासीं एकवद। जया ठायीं ॥७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ madhyordhva adha| he nāhīṃ jetha bheda| addayāsīṃ ekavada| jayā ṭhāyīṃ ||73||
verses.meaning: Where there is no distinction of middle, upper, or lower, where the indivisible becomes one with itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो नाइकिजतां नादु। जो असौरभ्य मकरंदु । जो आंगाथिला आनंदु । सुरतेंबिण ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo nāikijatāṃ nādu| jo asaurabhya makaraṃdu | jo āṃgāthilā ānaṃdu | surateṃbiṇa || 74||
verses.meaning: That sound which is heard without being heard, that fragrance which is without scent, that joy which is experienced without any union.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया जें आच्हां परौतें। जया जें पुढें मागौतें। दिसतेनविण दिसतें। अदृश्य जें ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā jeṃ āchāṃ parauteṃ| jayā jeṃ puḍheṃ māgauteṃ| disatenaviṇa disateṃ| adṛśya jeṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: That which is beyond all that is seen, that which is before and behind, that which is seen without being seen, that which is invisible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उपाधीचा दुसरा। घालितां बोपसरा । नामरूपाचा संसारा । होय जयातें ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: upādhīcā dusarā| ghālitāṃ bopasarā | nāmarūpācā saṃsārā | hoya jayāteṃ || 76||
verses.meaning: When the covering of limiting adjuncts is removed, the world of names and forms comes into being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ज्ञातृज्ञेयाविहीन । नुसधेंचि जें ज्ञान। सुखा भरलें गगन। गाळींब जें॥७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jñātṛjñeyāvihīna | nusadheṃci jeṃ jñāna| sukhā bharaleṃ gagana| gāḻīṃba jeṃ||77||
verses.meaning: That which is pure knowledge, devoid of the knower and the known, a sky filled with bliss, that is the essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें कार्य ना 'कारण। जया दुजें ना एकपण । आपणयां जें जाण। आपणचि ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ kārya nā 'kāraṇa| jayā dujeṃ nā ekapaṇa | āpaṇayāṃ jeṃ jāṇa| āpaṇaci || 78||
verses.meaning: That which has no cause, nor any duality or singularity; that which knows itself by itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें वस्तु जें साचें। तें ऊर्ध्व गा यया तरूचें। तेथ आर घेणें मूळाचें। तें ऐसें असे॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ vastu jeṃ sāceṃ| teṃ ūrdhva gā yayā tarūceṃ| tetha āra gheṇeṃ mūḻāceṃ| teṃ aiseṃ ase|| 79||
verses.meaning: Such is the true nature of that Reality, which is the root of this tree of existence. Therefore, one must take refuge in its root, which is indeed like this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी माया ऐसी ख्याती। नसतीच यया आथी। कां वांझेची संतती । वानणें जैशी॥ ८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī māyā aisī khyātī| nasatīca yayā āthī| kāṃ vāṃjhecī saṃtatī | vānaṇeṃ jaiśī|| 80||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Maya is renowned in such a way, though it has no real existence, just like describing the children of a barren woman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी सत्‌ ना असत्‌ होये। जे विचाराचें नाम न साहे । ऐसेया परीची आहे । अनादि म्हणती ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī sat‌ nā asat‌ hoye| je vicārāceṃ nāma na sāhe | aiseyā parīcī āhe | anādi mhaṇatī || 89||
verses.meaning: Similarly, it is neither existent nor non-existent, it cannot be grasped by thought or inquiry. Such is its nature, and it is called beginningless.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे भवद्रुमबीजिका । जे प्रपंचचित्र भूमिका। विपरीतज्ञानदीपिका। सांचली जे॥८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je bhavadrumabījikā | je prapaṃcacitra bhūmikā| viparītajñānadīpikā| sāṃcalī je||82||
verses.meaning: She is the seed of the tree of worldly existence, the stage for the drama of life, and the lamp that illuminates perverse knowledge, all accumulated within her.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे नानातत्त्वांची मांदुस । जे जगदभ्राचें आकाश । जे आकारजाताचें दुस। घडी केलें॥८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: je nānātattvāṃcī māṃdusa | je jagadabhrāceṃ ākāśa | je ākārajātāceṃ dusa| ghaḍī keleṃ||83||
verses.meaning: Which is the treasure chest of diverse principles, which is the sky for the illusion of the world, which is the very foundation for all forms, created in an instant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते माया वस्तूच्या ठायीं । असे जैसेनि नाहीं । मग वस्तुप्रभाचि पाही । प्रगट होये ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: te māyā vastūcyā ṭhāyīṃ | ase jaiseni nāhīṃ | maga vastuprabhāci pāhī | pragaṭa hoye || 84||
verses.meaning: That illusion does not exist in the reality itself. Rather, it is only the brilliance of the reality that manifests.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेव्हां आपणया आली निद। करी आपणणपें जेवीं मुग्ध॥ कां काजळी आणि मंद। प्रभा दीपीं ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jevhāṃ āpaṇayā ālī nida| karī āpaṇaṇapeṃ jevīṃ mugdha|| kāṃ kājaḻī āṇi maṃda| prabhā dīpīṃ || 85||
verses.meaning: Just as when sleep comes, one becomes oblivious to oneself, or like the dim light of a lamp obscured by soot.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्वप्नीं प्रियापुढें तरुणांगी। निदेली चेववूनि वेगीं। आलिंगिलेनिवीण आलिंगी। सकामु करी ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: svapnīṃ priyāpuḍheṃ taruṇāṃgī| nidelī cevavūni vegīṃ| āliṃgilenivīṇa āliṃgī| sakāmu karī || 86||
verses.meaning: In a dream, a young woman, awakened quickly, lies before her beloved. She embraces him without actually embracing, fulfilling her desire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी स्वरूपीं जाली माया । आणी स्वरूप नेणे धनंजया । तेंचि रुखा यया। मूळ पहिलें॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī svarūpīṃ jālī māyā | āṇī svarūpa neṇe dhanaṃjayā | teṃci rukhā yayā| mūḻa pahileṃ|| 87||
verses.meaning: Just as illusion (Maya) arises from the Self (Swaroop) yet the Self does not know it, that very illusion is the primordial root of this tree of worldly existence, O Dhananjaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वस्तूसी आपुला जो अबोधु । तो ऊर्ध्वी आठुळैजे कंदु। वेदांती हाचि प्रसिद्धु। बीजभावो ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: vastūsī āpulā jo abodhu | to ūrdhvī āṭhuḻaije kaṃdu| vedāṃtī hāci prasiddhu| bījabhāvo || 88 ||
verses.meaning: That ignorance of the true nature of the Self, which is the root cause of all, is known in Vedanta as the seed-state or primal ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: घनअज्ञानसुषुप्ती । तो बीजांकुरभावो म्हणती । येर स्वप्न हन जागृती । हा फळभावो तियाचा॥ ८९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ghanaajñānasuṣuptī | to bījāṃkurabhāvo mhaṇatī | yera svapna hana jāgṛtī | hā phaḻabhāvo tiyācā|| 89 ||
verses.meaning: Deep ignorance is called the state of a seed or sprout. And the states of dream and wakefulness are its fruit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी यया वेदांतीं। निरूपणभाषाप्रतीती। परी तें असो प्रस्तुतीं। अज्ञान मूळ॥९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī yayā vedāṃtīṃ| nirūpaṇabhāṣāpratītī| parī teṃ aso prastutīṃ| ajñāna mūḻa||90||
verses.meaning: Such is the understanding of the Vedantic discourse. But for now, let that be; ignorance is the root cause.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते ऊर्ध्व आत्मा निर्मळें। अधोर्ध्व सूचिती मूळें। बळिया बांधोनि आळें । मायायोगाचें ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: te ūrdhva ātmā nirmaḻeṃ| adhordhva sūcitī mūḻeṃ| baḻiyā bāṃdhoni āḻeṃ | māyāyogāceṃ || 91||
verses.meaning: That pure Supreme Soul, through the roots of Maya's yoga, binds the powerful (individual soul) with its downward and upward indications.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आधिलीं सदेहांतरें। उठती जियें अपारें। तें चौपासी घेऊनि आगारें। खोलावती॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ādhilīṃ sadehāṃtareṃ| uṭhatī jiyeṃ apāreṃ| teṃ caupāsī gheūni āgāreṃ| kholāvatī|| 92||
verses.meaning: Then, the innumerable previous bodies, which were the abodes of doubt, rise up and surround one, deepening the illusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें भवद्रुमाचें मूळ । हें ऊर्ध्वी करी बळ। मग आणियांचें बेंचळ। अधीं दावी॥९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ bhavadrumāceṃ mūḻa | heṃ ūrdhvī karī baḻa| maga āṇiyāṃceṃ beṃcaḻa| adhīṃ dāvī||93||
verses.meaning: Thus, the root of the tree of worldly existence, which is the upward force, first reveals its branches below.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ चिदवूत्तीं पहिलें। महत्तत्त्व उमललें। तें पान वाल्हेंदुल्हें। एक निघे॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha cidavūttīṃ pahileṃ| mahattattva umalaleṃ| teṃ pāna vālheṃdulheṃ| eka nighe|| 94||
verses.meaning: There, from the primal stir of consciousness, the great principle (Mahat-tattva) blossomed forth. From that single leaf, a sprout emerged.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सत्त्वरजतमात्मकु । त्रिविध अहंकारु जो एकु । तो तिवणा अधोमुखु । डिरु फुटे॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sattvarajatamātmaku | trividha ahaṃkāru jo eku | to tivaṇā adhomukhu | ḍiru phuṭe|| 95||
verses.meaning: Then, the ego, which is one but threefold in nature (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas), splits into three downward-facing branches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो बुद्धीची घेऊनि आगारी । भेदाची वृन्दि करी । तेथ मनाचे डाळ धरी । साजेपणें ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to buddhīcī gheūni āgārī | bhedācī vṛndi karī | tetha manāce ḍāḻa dharī | sājepaṇeṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: Taking hold of the intellect, it creates the garden of distinctions, and there, it gracefully holds the branches of the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा मूळाचिया गाढिका । विकल्परस कोंबळिका। चित्तचतुष्टय डाहाळिका। कोंभेजे तो॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā mūḻāciyā gāḍhikā | vikalparasa koṃbaḻikā| cittacatuṣṭaya ḍāhāḻikā| koṃbheje to|| 97||
verses.meaning: Thus, from the root of the primordial, the sprout of thought emerges. The fourfold inner instrument (mind, intellect, consciousness, ego) becomes its branches, and it flourishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आकाश वायु द्योतक । आप पृथ्वी हे पांच फोंक। महाभूतांचें सरोख। सरळे होती॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ākāśa vāyu dyotaka | āpa pṛthvī he pāṃca phoṃka| mahābhūtāṃceṃ sarokha| saraḻe hotī|| 98||
verses.meaning: Then the sky, air, and fire, along with earth and water, these five elements, which are the great elements, become simple and straightforward.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं श्रोत्रादि तन्मात्रें। तियें अंगवसां गर्भपत्रें। लुळलुळितें विचित्रें। उमळती गा॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ śrotrādi tanmātreṃ| tiyeṃ aṃgavasāṃ garbhapatreṃ| luḻaluḻiteṃ vicitreṃ| umaḻatī gā|| 99||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the subtle elements of sound and others, like tender leaves, unfold in wondrous ways, as if emerging from the very essence of the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ शब्दांकुर वरिपडी। श्रोत्रा बाढी देव्हडी । होता करित कांडीं । आकांक्षेचीं ॥ १०० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha śabdāṃkura varipaḍī| śrotrā bāḍhī devhaḍī | hotā karita kāṃḍīṃ | ākāṃkṣecīṃ || 100 ||
verses.meaning: There, the sprout of words falls upon the ears, growing manifold, as if making a ladder of longing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अंगत्वचेचे वेळपल्लव । स्पर्शांकुरीं घेती धांब। तेथ बांबळ पडे अभिनव विकारांचे ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: aṃgatvacece veḻapallava | sparśāṃkurīṃ ghetī dhāṃba| tetha bāṃbaḻa paḍe abhinava vikārāṃce || 1||
verses.meaning: The hairs on the skin, like tender sprouts, respond to touch, and there, a new kind of emotional upheaval arises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं रूपपत्र 'पालोवेलीं। चक्षु लांब तें कांडें घाली । ते वेळीं व्यामोहता भली । पाहाळीं जाय॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ rūpapatra 'pālovelīṃ| cakṣu lāṃba teṃ kāṃḍeṃ ghālī | te veḻīṃ vyāmohatā bhalī | pāhāḻīṃ jāya|| 2||
verses.meaning: When the form of the body, like a leaf, withers and the eyes, like a stalk, grow long and weak, then the delusion that binds one to the world completely vanishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि रसाचें आंगवसें। वाढतां वेगें बहुवसें। जिव्हे आरतीची असोसें। निघती बेंचें ॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi rasāceṃ āṃgavaseṃ| vāḍhatāṃ vegeṃ bahuvaseṃ| jivhe āratīcī asoseṃ| nighatī beṃceṃ || 3||
verses.meaning: And as the essence of devotion grows with great speed, the ardent longing of the tongue for the Aarti emerges with intense eagerness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंचि कोंभेलेनि गंधें। प्राणाची डिरी थांबु बांधे। तेथ तळु घे स्वानंदें। प्रलोभाचा॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃci koṃbheleni gaṃdheṃ| prāṇācī ḍirī thāṃbu bāṃdhe| tetha taḻu ghe svānaṃdeṃ| pralobhācā|| 4||
verses.meaning: Similarly, with the fragrance of the blossoming spiritual experience, the life-force is bound and held firm. There, in that state of self-joy, the allure of spiritual bliss takes root.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं महदहंबुद्धी। मनें महाभूतसमृद्धी। इये संसाराचिया अवधी । सासनिजे॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ mahadahaṃbuddhī| maneṃ mahābhūtasamṛddhī| iye saṃsārāciyā avadhī | sāsanije|| 5||
verses.meaning: Thus, from the great intellect and ego, and from the mind and the abundance of the great elements, this entire cycle of worldly existence is established.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना इहीं आठें। आंगीं हा अधिक फांटे। परी शिंपीचियेवढें उमटे। रुपें जेवीं ॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā ihīṃ āṭheṃ| āṃgīṃ hā adhika phāṃṭe| parī śiṃpīciyevaḍheṃ umaṭe| rupeṃ jevīṃ ||6||
verses.meaning: Indeed, from these eight, the body expands further, yet it appears as silver, just as much as an oyster shell.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां समुद्राचेनि पैसारें। वरी तरंगता आसारे। तैसें ब्रह्मच होय वृक्षाकारें। ३४८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी अज्ञानमूळ ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ samudrāceni paisāreṃ| varī taraṃgatā āsāre| taiseṃ brahmaca hoya vṛkṣākāreṃ| 348 śrījñāneśvarī ajñānamūḻa || 7||
verses.meaning: Just as waves surge upon the vastness of the ocean, so too does Brahman manifest as the form of a tree.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां याचा हाचि विस्तारु। हाचि यया पैसारु। जैसा आपणणपें स्वप्नीं परिवारु । येकाकिया॥८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yācā hāci vistāru| hāci yayā paisāru| jaisā āpaṇaṇapeṃ svapnīṃ parivāru | yekākiyā||8||
verses.meaning: Now, this is its expansion, this is its vastness, just as in a dream, one's own family appears to oneself, though one is alone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तें असो हें ऐसें। कावरें झाड उससे। यया महदादि आरवसें। अधोशाखा ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teṃ aso heṃ aiseṃ| kāvareṃ jhāḍa usase| yayā mahadādi āravaseṃ| adhośākhā || 9||
verses.meaning: Let that be. This tree, bewildered and uprooted, with its branches extending downwards, is like the Mahat and other principles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अशवत्थु ऐसें ययातें। म्हणती जे जाणते । तेंही परिस हो येथें ।॥ सांगिजेळ॥ ११०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi aśavatthu aiseṃ yayāteṃ| mhaṇatī je jāṇate | teṃhī parisa ho yetheṃ ||| sāṃgijeḻa|| 110||
verses.meaning: And those who are wise call this the Ashwattha (Pipal tree). Listen here, I will explain that too.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी इव: म्हणिजे उखा। तोंबरी एकसारिखा। नाहीं निर्वाहो यया रुखा। प्रपंचरूपा ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī iva: mhaṇije ukhā| toṃbarī ekasārikhā| nāhīṃ nirvāho yayā rukhā| prapaṃcarūpā || 19||
verses.meaning: Therefore, this tree of worldly existence, though appearing as a single entity, is not sustained by a single root.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा न लोटतां क्षणु। मेघु होय नानावर्णु। कां विजु नसे संपूर्णु। निमेषभरी॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā na loṭatāṃ kṣaṇu| meghu hoya nānāvarṇu| kāṃ viju nase saṃpūrṇu| nimeṣabharī|| 12||
verses.meaning: Just as in an instant, a cloud takes on various colors, or lightning flashes incompletely for a moment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना कांपतया पद्यदळा। वरीलिया बैसका नाहीं जळा। कां चित्त जैसें व्याकुळा । माणुसाचें ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā kāṃpatayā padyadaḻā| varīliyā baisakā nāhīṃ jaḻā| kāṃ citta jaiseṃ vyākuḻā | māṇusāceṃ || 13||
verses.meaning: Just as a trembling lotus leaf cannot hold water, or a restless mind cannot find peace, so too is the state of a distressed person.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीचि ययाची स्थिती । नासत जाय क्षणक्षणाप्रती । म्हणौनि ययातें म्हणती । अश्वत्थु हा॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīci yayācī sthitī | nāsata jāya kṣaṇakṣaṇāpratī | mhaṇauni yayāteṃ mhaṇatī | aśvatthu hā|| 14||
verses.meaning: Similarly, this world is constantly perishing moment by moment. Therefore, it is called Ashwattha (the impermanent fig tree).

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अशवत्थु येणें नांवें । पिंपळु म्हणती स्वभावें।॥ परी तो अभिप्राय नव्हे । श्रीहरीचा ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi aśavatthu yeṇeṃ nāṃveṃ | piṃpaḻu mhaṇatī svabhāveṃ||| parī to abhiprāya navhe | śrīharīcā || 15||
verses.meaning: And by the name 'Ashwatthu', naturally, it is called a fig tree. But that is not the intention of Shri Hari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं पिंपळु म्हणतां विखीं। मियां गति देखिली असे निकी । परी तें असो काय लौकिकीं। हेतु काज॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ piṃpaḻu mhaṇatāṃ vikhīṃ| miyāṃ gati dekhilī ase nikī | parī teṃ aso kāya laukikīṃ| hetu kāja|| 16||
verses.meaning: Indeed, when one speaks of the fig tree, I have seen a good path. But let that be, what is the purpose of worldly concerns?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि हा प्रस्तुतु । अलौकिकु परियेसा ग्रंथु। तरी क्षणिकत्वेंचि अश्वत्थु । बोलिजे हा॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni hā prastutu | alaukiku pariyesā graṃthu| tarī kṣaṇikatveṃci aśvatthu | bolije hā|| 97||
verses.meaning: Therefore, listen to this extraordinary scripture, which is called the Ashwattha (Pipal tree) because of its momentary nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिकही येकु थोरु । यया अव्ययत्वाचा डगरु। आथी परी तो भीतरु । ऐसा आहे ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇikahī yeku thoru | yayā avyayatvācā ḍagaru| āthī parī to bhītaru | aisā āhe || 18||
verses.meaning: And there is yet another great secret to this imperishability, but it is hidden within.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा मेघांचेनि तोंडें । सिंधु एके आंगें काढे। आणि नदी येरीकडे । भरितीच असती॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā meghāṃceni toṃḍeṃ | siṃdhu eke āṃgeṃ kāḍhe| āṇi nadī yerīkaḍe | bharitīca asatī|| 19||
verses.meaning: Just as the ocean, through the mouth of the clouds, draws water from one side, and rivers from the other side keep filling it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ वोहटे ना चढे। ऐसा परिपूर्णुचि आवडे । परी ते फुली जंब नुघडे। मेघानदींची॥ १२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha vohaṭe nā caḍhe| aisā paripūrṇuci āvaḍe | parī te phulī jaṃba nughaḍe| meghānadīṃcī|| 120||
verses.meaning: There, it neither recedes nor overflows; it always appears full and complete. Yet, it is not like the swelling of rivers during the monsoon season.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें या रुखाचें होणें जाणें । न तर्के होतेनि बहिलेपणें । म्हणौनि ययातें लोकु म्हणे । अव्ययु हा॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ yā rukhāceṃ hoṇeṃ jāṇeṃ | na tarke hoteni bahilepaṇeṃ | mhaṇauni yayāteṃ loku mhaṇe | avyayu hā|| 21||
verses.meaning: The coming and going of this tree cannot be comprehended by external perception. Therefore, people call it imperishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हबीं दानशीळु पुरुषु। वेंचकपणेंचि संचकु । तैसा व्ययेंचि हा रुखु। अव्ययो गमे॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhabīṃ dānaśīḻu puruṣu| veṃcakapaṇeṃci saṃcaku | taisā vyayeṃci hā rukhu| avyayo game|| 22||
verses.meaning: Just as a generous person, though spending, is truly accumulating, so too this tree, through its giving, appears imperishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जातां वेगें बहुवसें। न वचे कां भूमीं रुतलें असे। रथाचें चक्र दिसे। जियापरी॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jātāṃ vegeṃ bahuvaseṃ| na vace kāṃ bhūmīṃ rutaleṃ ase| rathāceṃ cakra dise| jiyāparī|| 23||
verses.meaning: Just as a chariot wheel, stuck in the mud, cannot move forward swiftly, so too the mind, entangled in worldly attachments, cannot progress on the spiritual path.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें काळातिक्रमें जे वाळे । ते भूतशाखा जेथ गळे। तेथ कोडीवरी उमाळे। उठती आणिक ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ kāḻātikrameṃ je vāḻe | te bhūtaśākhā jetha gaḻe| tetha koḍīvarī umāḻe| uṭhatī āṇika || 24||
verses.meaning: Just as branches that wither over time and fall away, from that very spot, countless new shoots sprout forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी येकी केधवां गेली । शाखाकोडी केधवां जाली । हें नेणवे जेवीं उमलली । आषाढअभ्रें ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī yekī kedhavāṃ gelī | śākhākoḍī kedhavāṃ jālī | heṃ neṇave jevīṃ umalalī | āṣāḍhaabhreṃ || 25||
verses.meaning: Just as one cannot tell when a single cloud appeared or when it branched into many, so too is the origin of the universe unknowable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: महाकल्पाच्या शेवटीं । उदेलिया उमळती सृष्टी । तैसेंचि आणिखीचें दांग उठी । सासिन्नलें॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mahākalpācyā śevaṭīṃ | udeliyā umaḻatī sṛṣṭī | taiseṃci āṇikhīceṃ dāṃga uṭhī | sāsinnaleṃ|| 26||
verses.meaning: At the end of the great cosmic cycle, when the creation unfolds, similarly, another great manifestation arises, fully formed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संहारवातें प्रचंडें। पडती प्रळयांतींचीं सालडें। तंब कल्पादीचीं जुंबाडें। पाल्हेजती ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃhāravāteṃ pracaṃḍeṃ| paḍatī praḻayāṃtīṃcīṃ sālaḍeṃ| taṃba kalpādīcīṃ juṃbāḍeṃ| pālhejatī || 27||
verses.meaning: Like the mighty winds of destruction that tear down the very foundations of the universe at the end of a cosmic cycle, so too do the ancient structures of creation, from the very beginning of time, crumble and fall.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रिगे मन्वंतर मनुपुढें । वंशाबरी वंशांचें मांडे। जैसी इक्षुवृद्धी कांडेंनकांडें। जिंके जेवीं ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: rige manvaṃtara manupuḍheṃ | vaṃśābarī vaṃśāṃceṃ māṃḍe| jaisī ikṣuvṛddhī kāṃḍeṃnakāṃḍeṃ| jiṃke jevīṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Just as a sugarcane grows joint by joint, so too do ages and lineages unfold, one after another, in an unbroken succession.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कल्युगांतीं कोरडी। चहूं युगांची सालें सांडी। तंव कृतयुगाची पेली देव्हडी। पडे पुढती॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kalyugāṃtīṃ koraḍī| cahūṃ yugāṃcī sāleṃ sāṃḍī| taṃva kṛtayugācī pelī devhaḍī| paḍe puḍhatī|| 29||
verses.meaning: At the end of Kali Yuga, when the layers of the four yugas are shed, then the golden age of Krita Yuga will again manifest itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वर्ततें वर्ष जाये। तें पुढिळला मुळहारी होये । जैसा दिवसु जात कीं येत आहे। हें चोजवेना॥ १३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: vartateṃ varṣa jāye| teṃ puḍhiḻalā muḻahārī hoye | jaisā divasu jāta kīṃ yeta āhe| heṃ cojavenā|| 130||
verses.meaning: The passing year becomes the root of the next, just as it is difficult to discern whether the day is going or coming.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैशा वारियाचां झुळकां। सांदा ठाउवा नव्हे देखा। तैसिया उठती पडती शाखा। नेणों किती॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiśā vāriyācāṃ jhuḻakāṃ| sāṃdā ṭhāuvā navhe dekhā| taisiyā uṭhatī paḍatī śākhā| neṇoṃ kitī|| 31||
verses.meaning: Just as the origin of a gust of wind is unknown, so too are the countless branches that rise and fall, their source unseen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एकी देहाची डिरी तुटे। तंब देहांकुरीं बहुवी फुटे। ऐसेनि भवतरु हा वाटे । अव्ययो ऐसा॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ekī dehācī ḍirī tuṭe| taṃba dehāṃkurīṃ bahuvī phuṭe| aiseni bhavataru hā vāṭe | avyayo aisā|| 32||
verses.meaning: When the cord of one body breaks, many new bodies sprout forth. Thus, this tree of worldly existence appears imperishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें वाहतें पाणी जाय वेगें । तैसेंचि आणिक मिळे मागें । तेवीं असंतचि असिजे जगें। मानिजे संत॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ vāhateṃ pāṇī jāya vegeṃ | taiseṃci āṇika miḻe māgeṃ | tevīṃ asaṃtaci asije jageṃ| mānije saṃta|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as flowing water moves swiftly, and more water joins it from behind, so too, the world, though transient, is considered eternal by the saints.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां 'लागोनि डोळा उघडे । तंव कोडीवरी घडे मोडे । नेणतया तरंगु आवडे । नित्यु ऐसा॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ 'lāgoni ḍoḻā ughaḍe | taṃva koḍīvarī ghaḍe moḍe | neṇatayā taraṃgu āvaḍe | nityu aisā|| 34||
verses.meaning: Just as when the eye opens, countless things appear and disappear, so too, the ignorant person finds the transient wave appealing, believing it to be eternal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वायसा एके बुबुळें दोहींकडे। डोळा चाळितां अपाडें । दोन्हीं आथी ऐसा पडे । भ्रम जेवीं जगा॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāyasā eke bubuḻeṃ dohīṃkaḍe| ḍoḻā cāḻitāṃ apāḍeṃ | donhīṃ āthī aisā paḍe | bhrama jevīṃ jagā|| 35||
verses.meaning: Just as a crow, with its single eye, moves it from side to side, creating the illusion for the world that it has two eyes, so too is this illusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं भिंगोरी निधिये पडली । ते गमे भूमीसी जैसी जडली । ऐसा वेगातिशयो भुली । हेतु होय॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ bhiṃgorī nidhiye paḍalī | te game bhūmīsī jaisī jaḍalī | aisā vegātiśayo bhulī | hetu hoya|| 36||
verses.meaning: When a spinning top falls to the ground, it appears as if it has become stuck to the earth. Such is the illusion created by excessive speed, causing one to forget the true nature of things.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें बहु असो झडती । आंधारें भोवंडितां कोलती। ते दिसे जैसी आयती। चक्राकार॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ bahu aso jhaḍatī | āṃdhāreṃ bhovaṃḍitāṃ kolatī| te dise jaisī āyatī| cakrākāra|| 37||
verses.meaning: Let this be enough; when a burning brand is whirled around in the darkness, it appears like a circular form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा संसारवृक्षु तैसा। मोडतु मांडतु सहसा। न देखोनि 'लोकु पिसा। अव्ययो मानी॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā saṃsāravṛkṣu taisā| moḍatu māṃḍatu sahasā| na dekhoni 'loku pisā| avyayo mānī|| 38||
verses.meaning: This tree of worldly existence, though it is constantly being broken down and rebuilt, people, being deluded, do not perceive this and consider it eternal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ययाचा वेगु देखे। जो हा क्षणिक ऐसा बोळखे । जाणे कोडिवेळां निमिखें। होत जात ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī yayācā vegu dekhe| jo hā kṣaṇika aisā boḻakhe | jāṇe koḍiveḻāṃ nimikheṃ| hota jāta || 39||
verses.meaning: But one who perceives its swiftness, recognizing it as momentary, knows that in an instant it comes into being and passes away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाहीं अज्ञानाबांचूनि मूळ | ययाचें असिलेंपण टवाळ। ऐसें झाडचि सिनसाळ । देखिलें जेणें ॥ ९४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nāhīṃ ajñānābāṃcūni mūḻa | yayāceṃ asileṃpaṇa ṭavāḻa| aiseṃ jhāḍaci sinasāḻa | dekhileṃ jeṇeṃ || 940||
verses.meaning: There is no root other than ignorance; its very existence is a mere illusion. Whoever has seen this tree of illusion for what it is, has seen it truly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयातें गा पंडुसुता। मी सर्वजुुही म्हणें जाणता । पैं वाग्ब्रह्म सिद्धांता । वंद्यु तोचि ॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāteṃ gā paṃḍusutā| mī sarvajuuhī mhaṇeṃ jāṇatā | paiṃ vāgbrahma siddhāṃtā | vaṃdyu toci || 41||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, I declare that among all beings, the one who knows the essence of speech (Vagbrahma) is truly worthy of reverence, for that is the ultimate truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: योगजाताचें जोडलें। तया एकासीचि उपेगा गेलें। किंबहुना जियालें। ज्ञानही त्याचेनी ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yogajātāceṃ joḍaleṃ| tayā ekāsīci upegā geleṃ| kiṃbahunā jiyāleṃ| jñānahī tyācenī || 42||
verses.meaning: The union of Yoga, that is, the knowledge that arises from it, is useful only to that one (the Yogi). In fact, even knowledge itself comes alive through him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: असो बहु हें बोलणें । बानिजेळ तो कवणें। जो भवरुखु जाणे। उखि ऐसा॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aso bahu heṃ bolaṇeṃ | bānijeḻa to kavaṇeṃ| jo bhavarukhu jāṇe| ukhi aisā|| 43||
verses.meaning: Enough of this extensive talk. Who can truly understand the nature of this worldly tree (samsara) and uproot it like this?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग ययाचि प्रपंचरूपा। अधोशाखिया पादपा। डाहाळिया जाती उमपा। ऊर्ध्वाही उजू॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga yayāci prapaṃcarūpā| adhośākhiyā pādapā| ḍāhāḻiyā jātī umapā| ūrdhvāhī ujū|| 44||
verses.meaning: Then, from this tree of worldly existence, with its downward branches, countless twigs emerge, extending upwards.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अधीं फांकली डाळें। तियें होती मूळें । तयांही तळीं पघळे । वेळ पालवु ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi adhīṃ phāṃkalī ḍāḻeṃ| tiyeṃ hotī mūḻeṃ | tayāṃhī taḻīṃ paghaḻe | veḻa pālavu || 45 ||
verses.meaning: And the branches that had spread earlier, they became roots. And beneath those, the creeper of time spread further.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जें आम्हीं । म्हणितलें उपक्रमीं । ३५० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी तेंही परिसें सुगमीं । बोलीं सांगो ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jeṃ āmhīṃ | mhaṇitaleṃ upakramīṃ | 350 śrījñāneśvarī teṃhī pariseṃ sugamīṃ | bolīṃ sāṃgo || 46||
verses.meaning: Listen, I will now explain in simple language what I said in the beginning of this Dnyaneshwari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी बक्धमूळें अज्ञानें। महदादिकीं सासिनें। वेदांची थोरवनें । घेऊनियां ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī bakdhamūḻeṃ ajñāneṃ| mahadādikīṃ sāsineṃ| vedāṃcī thoravaneṃ | gheūniyāṃ || 47||
verses.meaning: Therefore, due to the deeply rooted ignorance, the Vedas, with their great authority, have taken hold of the Mahat and other principles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि आधीं तंब स्वेदज। जारज उदिभज अंडज हे बुडौनि महाभुज। उठती चारी ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari ādhīṃ taṃba svedaja| jāraja udibhaja aṃḍaja he buḍauni mahābhuja| uṭhatī cārī || 48||
verses.meaning: First, the four types of beings—sweat-born, illegitimate, sprout-born, and egg-born—all perish, O mighty-armed one, and then arise again.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया एकैकाचेनि आंगवटें। चौऱर्‍यांशीं लक्षधा फुटे। ते वेळीं जीवशाखीं फाटें। सैंघचि होती ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā ekaikāceni āṃgavaṭeṃ| cauṟar‍yāṃśīṃ lakṣadhā phuṭe| te veḻīṃ jīvaśākhīṃ phāṭeṃ| saiṃghaci hotī || 49||
verses.meaning: From each individual's body, eighty-four lakh (8.4 million) species emerge. At that time, the branches of life spread everywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रसवती शाखा सरळिया। नानासृष्टि डाहाळिया। आड फुटती माळिया। जातिचिया॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: prasavatī śākhā saraḻiyā| nānāsṛṣṭi ḍāhāḻiyā| āḍa phuṭatī māḻiyā| jāticiyā|| 150||
verses.meaning: From it, straight branches emerge, and various creations are like its offshoots. From these, new shoots of different species sprout forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्त्री पुरुष नपुंसकें । हे व्यक्तिभेदांचे टके। आंदोळती आंगिकें। विकारभारें॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: strī puruṣa napuṃsakeṃ | he vyaktibhedāṃce ṭake| āṃdoḻatī āṃgikeṃ| vikārabhāreṃ|| 51||
verses.meaning: Men, women, and eunuchs—these distinctions of individuals—are tossed about by the physical burdens of their own bodies and their inherent defects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा वर्षाकाळु गगनीं। पाल्हेजे नवघनीं। तैसें आकारजात अज्ञानीं। वेळीं जाय॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā varṣākāḻu gaganīṃ| pālheje navaghanīṃ| taiseṃ ākārajāta ajñānīṃ| veḻīṃ jāya|| 52||
verses.meaning: Just as the monsoon clouds gather in the sky, so too do all forms of ignorance dissipate with time.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग शाखांचेनि आंगभारें। लबोनि गुंफिती परस्परें। गुणक्षोभाचे वारे। उदयजती॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga śākhāṃceni āṃgabhāreṃ| laboni guṃphitī paraspareṃ| guṇakṣobhāce vāre| udayajatī|| 53||
verses.meaning: Then, by the weight of their branches, they intertwine with each other, and the winds of agitated qualities arise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ तेणें अचाटें । गुणांचेनि झडझडाटें । तिहीं ठायीं हा फांटे। ऊर्ध्वमपूळ ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha teṇeṃ acāṭeṃ | guṇāṃceni jhaḍajhaḍāṭeṃ | tihīṃ ṭhāyīṃ hā phāṃṭe| ūrdhvamapūḻa || 54||
verses.meaning: There, by that immense power, with the swiftness of the Gunas, it branches out in three places, its roots extending upwards.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा रजाचिया झुळुका । झडाडितां आगळिका । मनुष्यजाती शाखा। थोरावती॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā rajāciyā jhuḻukā | jhaḍāḍitāṃ āgaḻikā | manuṣyajātī śākhā| thorāvatī|| 55||
verses.meaning: Just as a gentle breeze makes the branches of a tree sway, so too does the divine grace of the Lord cause the human race to flourish and grow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिया ऊर्ध्वी ना अधीं। माझारींचि कोंदाकोंदी। आड फुटती खांदी । चतुर्वर्णांच्या॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyā ūrdhvī nā adhīṃ| mājhārīṃci koṃdākoṃdī| āḍa phuṭatī khāṃdī | caturvarṇāṃcyā|| 56||
verses.meaning: Neither above nor below, but in the very midst, branches of the four varnas sprout forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ विधिनिषेध सपल्लवब । वेदवाक्यांचे अभिनव । पालव डोलती बरव। नीच नवे॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha vidhiniṣedha sapallavaba | vedavākyāṃce abhinava | pālava ḍolatī barava| nīca nave|| 57||
verses.meaning: There, the do's and don'ts, with their fresh shoots, the novel branches of Vedic statements, sway beautifully, ever new.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्थ कामु पसरे । अग्रवनें घेती थारे। तेथ क्षणिकें पदांतरें। इहभोगाचीं ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: artha kāmu pasare | agravaneṃ ghetī thāre| tetha kṣaṇikeṃ padāṃtareṃ| ihabhogācīṃ || 58||
verses.meaning: When the desires for worldly pleasures spread, they take root in the mind, and then the fleeting enjoyments of this world become the only goal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ प्रवृत्तीचेनि वृद्धिलो भें। खांकरेजती शुभाशुभें। नानाकर्मांचे खांबे । नेणों किती ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha pravṛttīceni vṛddhilo bheṃ| khāṃkarejatī śubhāśubheṃ| nānākarmāṃce khāṃbe | neṇoṃ kitī || 59||
verses.meaning: There, with the growth of worldly inclinations, good and bad deeds multiply like countless pillars of various actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि भोगक्षीणें मागिळें। पडती देहांतींची बुडसळें। तंव पुढां वाढी पेळे। नवेया देहांची ॥ ९६० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci bhogakṣīṇeṃ māgiḻeṃ| paḍatī dehāṃtīṃcī buḍasaḻeṃ| taṃva puḍhāṃ vāḍhī peḻe| naveyā dehāṃcī || 960 ||
verses.meaning: In the same way, as the old karmic debts are exhausted, the impurities of the past bodies fall away. Meanwhile, new bodies are prepared and grow for the future.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि शब्दादिक सुहावें। सहज रंगे हवावे। विषयपल्लव नवे। नित्य होती ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi śabdādika suhāveṃ| sahaja raṃge havāve| viṣayapallava nave| nitya hotī || 61||
verses.meaning: And with the delight of words and other sensory pleasures, the mind naturally gets colored and swayed. New sprouts of worldly objects constantly emerge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे रजोवातें प्रचंडें । मनुष्यशाखांचे मांदोडे। वाढती तो एथ रूढे। मनुष्यलोकु ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise rajovāteṃ pracaṃḍeṃ | manuṣyaśākhāṃce māṃdoḍe| vāḍhatī to etha rūḍhe| manuṣyaloku || 62||
verses.meaning: Thus, by the mighty winds of Rajas, the groves of human branches grow, and this is how the human world flourishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसाचि तो रजाचा वारा । नावेक धरी बोसरा। मग वाजों लागे घोरा। तमाचा तो॥६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisāci to rajācā vārā | nāveka dharī bosarā| maga vājoṃ lāge ghorā| tamācā to||63||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the wind of 'rajas' (passion) blows for a while, and then the fierce wind of 'tamas' (ignorance) begins to rage.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेधवां याचि मनुष्यशाखा। नीच वासना अधीं देखा । पाल्हेजती डाहाळिका। कुकर्माचिया॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tedhavāṃ yāci manuṣyaśākhā| nīca vāsanā adhīṃ dekhā | pālhejatī ḍāhāḻikā| kukarmāciyā|| 64||
verses.meaning: Then, in this human branch, first, the lowly desires, the offshoots of evil deeds, sprout forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अप्रवृत्तींचे खणुवाळे। कोंभ निघती सरळे। घेत पान पालव डाळें। प्रमादाचीं ॥६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: apravṛttīṃce khaṇuvāḻe| koṃbha nighatī saraḻe| gheta pāna pālava ḍāḻeṃ| pramādācīṃ ||65||
verses.meaning: The sprouts of non-action emerge straight, bearing leaves, tender shoots, and branches of diligence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बोलती निषेधनियमें। जिया क्रच्चा यजुःसामें। तो पाला तया घुमें। टकेयावरी ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: bolatī niṣedhaniyameṃ| jiyā kraccā yajuḥsāmeṃ| to pālā tayā ghumeṃ| ṭakeyāvarī || 66||
verses.meaning: The one who speaks of the forbidden actions and the prescribed rituals of Yajur and Sama Vedas, that person is like a coin that has lost its value.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रतिपादिती अभिचार। आगम जे परमार तिहीं पानीं घेती प्रसर। वासना वेली ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pratipāditī abhicāra| āgama je paramāra tihīṃ pānīṃ ghetī prasara| vāsanā velī || 67||
verses.meaning: The tantric rituals, which are considered supreme, spread their desires like a creeper, taking root in those who practice them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब तंव होतीं थोराडें । अकर्मांचीं तळबुडे । आणि जन्मशाखा पुढें पुढें । घेती धांब॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba taṃva hotīṃ thorāḍeṃ | akarmāṃcīṃ taḻabuḍe | āṇi janmaśākhā puḍheṃ puḍheṃ | ghetī dhāṃba|| 68||
verses.meaning: The great ones were then like the bottom of a deep well of inaction, and the branches of birth continued to grow further and further.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ चांडाळादि निकृष्टा। दोषजातीचा थोर फांटा । जाळ पडे कर्मभ्रष्टां। भुलोनियां॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha cāṃḍāḻādi nikṛṣṭā| doṣajātīcā thora phāṃṭā | jāḻa paḍe karmabhraṣṭāṃ| bhuloniyāṃ|| 69||
verses.meaning: There, even the lowest of the low, like a Chandala, and those who have fallen from their duties due to delusion, are caught in the great snare of various faults.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पशु पक्षी सूकर। व्याघ्र वृश्चिक विखार। हे आडशाखानिकर। पैसु घेती॥ १७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paśu pakṣī sūkara| vyāghra vṛścika vikhāra| he āḍaśākhānikara| paisu ghetī|| 170||
verses.meaning: Animals, birds, pigs, tigers, scorpions, and other venomous creatures—all these take refuge in the shade of the tree of the universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ऐशा शाखा पांडवा । सर्वांगींही नित्य नवा। निरयभोग यावा। फळाचा तो॥७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī aiśā śākhā pāṃḍavā | sarvāṃgīṃhī nitya navā| nirayabhoga yāvā| phaḻācā to||71||
verses.meaning: But O Pandava, such branches, though ever new in every part, will yield the fruit of suffering in hell.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हिंसाविषयपुढारी। कुकर्मसंगें धुर धुरी। जन्मवबरी आगारी। वाढतीचि असे॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi hiṃsāviṣayapuḍhārī| kukarmasaṃgeṃ dhura dhurī| janmavabarī āgārī| vāḍhatīci ase|| 72||
verses.meaning: And the leaders of violence and worldly pleasures, through their association with evil deeds, accumulate a great burden of sins, which continues to grow throughout their lives.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे होती तरु तृण। लोह लोष्ट पाषाण। इया खांदिया तेवीं जाण। फळेंही हेंची ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise hotī taru tṛṇa| loha loṣṭa pāṣāṇa| iyā khāṃdiyā tevīṃ jāṇa| phaḻeṃhī heṃcī || 73||
verses.meaning: Thus, trees and grass, iron, stone, and rocks, are all of the same nature, and their fruits are also the same.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना गा अवधारीं। मनुष्याळागोनि इया परी । वृद्दि स्थावरांतवरी । अधोशाखांची ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā gā avadhārīṃ| manuṣyāḻāgoni iyā parī | vṛddi sthāvarāṃtavarī | adhośākhāṃcī || 74||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, listen! In this way, from humans to the immovable, the branches extend downwards.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जीं मनुष्यडाळें । तियें जाणावीं अधींचि मूळें। जे एथूनि मग पघळे। संसारतरु ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jīṃ manuṣyaḍāḻeṃ | tiyeṃ jāṇāvīṃ adhīṃci mūḻeṃ| je ethūni maga paghaḻe| saṃsārataru || 75||
verses.meaning: Therefore, know that these human beings are the very roots, from which the tree of worldly existence then spreads forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱहवी ऊर्ध्वींचें पार्था । मुद्दल मूळ पाहतां । अधींचिया मध्यस्था । शाखा इया ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟahavī ūrdhvīṃceṃ pārthā | muddala mūḻa pāhatāṃ | adhīṃciyā madhyasthā | śākhā iyā || 76||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, O Partha, if you look at the fundamental root of what is above, these branches are merely intermediaries of what came before.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तामसी सात्त्विकी। सुकृतदुष्कृतात्मकी। विरूढती या शाखीं। अधोध्वींचिया॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī tāmasī sāttvikī| sukṛtaduṣkṛtātmakī| virūḍhatī yā śākhīṃ| adhodhvīṃciyā|| 77||
verses.meaning: But on these branches, which grow downwards and upwards, sprout actions that are either sattvic (good) or tamasic (bad), embodying both good and evil.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि वेदत्रयाचिया पाना। नये अन्यत्र लागों अर्जुना। जे मनुष्यावांचूनि विधाना। विषय नाहीं ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi vedatrayāciyā pānā| naye anyatra lāgoṃ arjunā| je manuṣyāvāṃcūni vidhānā| viṣaya nāhīṃ || 78||
verses.meaning: And the leaves of the three Vedas, Arjuna, do not apply elsewhere, for their injunctions are not meant for anything other than humans.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तनु मानुषा। इया ऊर्ध्वमूळौनि जरी शाखा । तरी कर्मवृद्धीसि देखा। इयेंचि मूळें॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tanu mānuṣā| iyā ūrdhvamūḻauni jarī śākhā | tarī karmavṛddhīsi dekhā| iyeṃci mūḻeṃ|| 79||
verses.meaning: Therefore, though the human body is like a tree with roots above and branches below, yet these very roots are the cause of the growth of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आनीं तरी झाडीं। शाखा वाढतां मूळें गाढीं। मूळ गाढे तंव वाढी । पैस आथी॥ १८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ānīṃ tarī jhāḍīṃ| śākhā vāḍhatāṃ mūḻeṃ gāḍhīṃ| mūḻa gāḍhe taṃva vāḍhī | paisa āthī|| 180||
verses.meaning: And just as a tree, as its branches grow, strengthens its roots, so too, as the roots deepen, its expanse grows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंचि इया शरीरा । कर्म तंव देहा संसारा । आणि देह तंव व्यापारा। ना म्हणोंचि नये॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃci iyā śarīrā | karma taṃva dehā saṃsārā | āṇi deha taṃva vyāpārā| nā mhaṇoṃci naye|| 81||
verses.meaning: Similarly, for this body, action is indeed for the worldly existence, and the body is for activity; this cannot be denied.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि देहें मानुषें। इयें मुळें होती न चुके । ऐसें जगज्जनर्के । बोलिलें तेणें ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni deheṃ mānuṣeṃ| iyeṃ muḻeṃ hotī na cuke | aiseṃ jagajjanarke | bolileṃ teṇeṃ || 82||
verses.meaning: Therefore, these human bodies are fundamentally rooted in the divine, this truth is undeniable. Thus spoke the Creator of the universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तमाचे तें दारुण। स्थिरावळेया वाउधाण। सत्त्वाची सुटे सत्राण। बाहुटळी॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga tamāce teṃ dāruṇa| sthirāvaḻeyā vāudhāṇa| sattvācī suṭe satrāṇa| bāhuṭaḻī|| 83||
verses.meaning: Then, the terrible darkness, having settled in its wildness, the power of Sattva (goodness) is released, and it becomes strong.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैं याचि मनुष्याकारा । मूळीं सुवबासना निघती आरा । घेऊनी फुटती कोंबारा । सुकृतांकुरीं ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiṃ yāci manuṣyākārā | mūḻīṃ suvabāsanā nighatī ārā | gheūnī phuṭatī koṃbārā | sukṛtāṃkurīṃ || 84||
verses.meaning: From this very human form, good inclinations originally emerge like sprouts. Taking root, they burst forth as tender shoots of virtuous deeds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उकलतेनि उन्मेखें। प्रज्ञाकुशलतेंची तिखें। डिरिया निघती निमिखें । बांबळेजुनी ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ukalateni unmekheṃ| prajñākuśalateṃcī tikheṃ| ḍiriyā nighatī nimikheṃ | bāṃbaḻejunī || 85 ||
verses.meaning: With the unfolding of insight, and the sharpness of wisdom, the knots of ignorance are untied in an instant, like a bamboo joint.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मतीचे सोट वांवे। घालिती स्फूर्तीचेनि थांबें। बुद्धि प्रकाश घे धांवे। विवेकावरी॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: matīce soṭa vāṃve| ghālitī sphūrtīceni thāṃbeṃ| buddhi prakāśa ghe dhāṃve| vivekāvarī|| 86||
verses.meaning: The dull intellect, spurred by inspiration, rushes to grasp the light of wisdom through discrimination.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ मेधारसें सगर्भ । आस्थापत्रीं सबोंब। सरळ निघती कोंभ। सदवृत्तीचे ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha medhāraseṃ sagarbha | āsthāpatrīṃ saboṃba| saraḻa nighatī koṃbha| sadavṛttīce || 87||
verses.meaning: There, with the sap of intelligence, on the leaves of faith, sprouts of good conduct emerge straight and strong.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सदाचाराचिया सहसा। टका उठती बहुवसा। घुमघुमिती घोषा। वेदपद्याच्या॥ ८८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: sadācārāciyā sahasā| ṭakā uṭhatī bahuvasā| ghumaghumitī ghoṣā| vedapadyācyā|| 88 ||
verses.meaning: From such virtuous conduct, the resounding echoes of Vedic hymns spontaneously arise and reverberate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ३५२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी शिष्टागमविधानें । विविधयागवितानें । इयें पानाबरी पानें । पाळेजती ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: 352 śrījñāneśvarī śiṣṭāgamavidhāneṃ | vividhayāgavitāneṃ | iyeṃ pānābarī pāneṃ | pāḻejatī || 89||
verses.meaning: Just as leaves grow upon leaves, so too do the established traditions and various sacrificial rituals described in the Dnyaneshwari proliferate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा यमदमीं घोंसाळिया। उठती तपाचिया डाहाळिया। देती वैराग्यशाखा 'कोंबळिया । वेल्हाळपणें ॥ १९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā yamadamīṃ ghoṃsāḻiyā| uṭhatī tapāciyā ḍāhāḻiyā| detī vairāgyaśākhā 'koṃbaḻiyā | velhāḻapaṇeṃ || 190||
verses.meaning: When the mind is thus purified by self-restraint, branches of penance sprout forth, and tender shoots of dispassion emerge with grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विशिष्टां व्रतांचे फोक । धीराच्या अणगटीं तिख। जन्मवेगें ऊर्ध्वमुख। उंचावती॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: viśiṣṭāṃ vratāṃce phoka | dhīrācyā aṇagaṭīṃ tikha| janmavegeṃ ūrdhvamukha| uṃcāvatī|| 91||
verses.meaning: The fruits of excellent vows, sharpened by the anvil of patience, rise upwards with the force of birth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: माजीं वेदांचा पाला दाट। तो करी सुविद्येचा झडझडाट। जंब वाजे अचाट । सत्त्वानिळु तो॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mājīṃ vedāṃcā pālā dāṭa| to karī suvidyecā jhaḍajhaḍāṭa| jaṃba vāje acāṭa | sattvāniḻu to|| 92||
verses.meaning: When the dense foliage of my Vedas rustles, it creates a powerful surge of true knowledge, like an extraordinary wind of sattva (purity) that blows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ धर्मडाळ बाहाळी। दिसती जन्मशाखा सरळी। तिया आड फुटती फळीं। स्वर्गादिकीं ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha dharmaḍāḻa bāhāḻī| disatī janmaśākhā saraḻī| tiyā āḍa phuṭatī phaḻīṃ| svargādikīṃ || 93||
verses.meaning: There, the branches of Dharma flourish, and the straight paths of birth are seen. From these, fruits like heaven emerge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुढां उपरति रागें लोहिवी । धर्ममोक्षाची शाखा पालवी । 'पाल्हाजत नित्य नवी। वाढतीचि असे॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: puḍhāṃ uparati rāgeṃ lohivī | dharmamokṣācī śākhā pālavī | 'pālhājata nitya navī| vāḍhatīci ase|| 94||
verses.meaning: Further, with the cessation of worldly desires, the branch of Dharma and Moksha (liberation) sprouts anew, ever flourishing and continuously growing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं रविचंद्रादि ग्रहवर। पितृ क्रषि विद्याधर हे आडशाखा प्रकार। पैसु घेती॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ ravicaṃdrādi grahavara| pitṛ kraṣi vidyādhara he āḍaśākhā prakāra| paisu ghetī|| 95||
verses.meaning: The sun, moon, and other planets, along with the ancestors and Vidyadharas, are like branches that receive their share.

verses.shloka_devanagari: याहीपासून उंचबडें। गुढले फळाचेनि बुडें। इंद्रादिक ते मांदोडे। थोर शाखांचे ॥९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yāhīpāsūna uṃcabaḍeṃ| guḍhale phaḻāceni buḍeṃ| iṃdrādika te māṃdoḍe| thora śākhāṃce ||96||
verses.meaning: Even higher than this, hidden at the root of the fruit, are Indra and other deities, who are like the great branches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तयांही उपरी डाहाळिया। तपोज्ञानीं उंचावलिया। मरीचि कश्यपादि इया। उपरी शाखा॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga tayāṃhī uparī ḍāhāḻiyā| tapojñānīṃ uṃcāvaliyā| marīci kaśyapādi iyā| uparī śākhā|| 97||
verses.meaning: Above them are the branches, elevated by their penance and knowledge, like Marichi and Kashyapa, who are further branches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं माळोवाळी उत्तरोत्तरु। ऊर्ध्वशाखांचा पैसारु। बुडीं साना अग्रीं थोरु। फलाढ्यपणें ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ māḻovāḻī uttarottaru| ūrdhvaśākhāṃcā paisāru| buḍīṃ sānā agrīṃ thoru| phalāḍhyapaṇeṃ || 98||
verses.meaning: Thus, like a garland, one after another, the branches spread upwards. Small at the root, large at the top, laden with fruits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरी उपरिशाखाही पाठीं । येती फळभार जे किरीटी । ते ब्रह्मेशांत अणगटीं। कोंभ निघती ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: varī upariśākhāhī pāṭhīṃ | yetī phaḻabhāra je kirīṭī | te brahmeśāṃta aṇagaṭīṃ| koṃbha nighatī || 99 ||
verses.meaning: And on the upper branches, O Kiriti, the fruits that bear heavy, from them sprout the shoots of Brahma and Shiva.

verses.shloka_devanagari: फळाचेनि बोझेपणें। ऊर्ध्वीं बोबांडें दुणें। जंब माघोतें बैसणें । मूळींचि होय॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: phaḻāceni bojhepaṇeṃ| ūrdhvīṃ bobāṃḍeṃ duṇeṃ| jaṃba māghoteṃ baisaṇeṃ | mūḻīṃci hoya|| 200||
verses.meaning: When the fruit-laden branches bend downwards, they return to their origin, the root, with double the burden.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्राकृताही तरी रुखा। जें फळें दाटली होय शाखा। ते बोबांडली देखा । बुडासि ये॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: prākṛtāhī tarī rukhā| jeṃ phaḻeṃ dāṭalī hoya śākhā| te bobāṃḍalī dekhā | buḍāsi ye|| 1||
verses.meaning: Even a common tree, when its branches are laden with fruit, bends down to its roots.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें जेथूनि हा आघवा । संसारतरूचा उठावा । तियें मूळीं टेंकती पांडवा । वाढतेनि ज्ञानें ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jethūni hā āghavā | saṃsāratarūcā uṭhāvā | tiyeṃ mūḻīṃ ṭeṃkatī pāṃḍavā | vāḍhateni jñāneṃ || 2||
verses.meaning: Just as the entire tree of worldly existence originates from its roots, so too, O Pandava, do those roots become firmly established through the growth of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ब्रह्मेशानापरोतें । वाढणें नाहीं जीवातें। तेथूनि मग वरोतें। ब्रह्मचि कीं ॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni brahmeśānāparoteṃ | vāḍhaṇeṃ nāhīṃ jīvāteṃ| tethūni maga varoteṃ| brahmaci kīṃ ||3||
verses.meaning: Therefore, there is no growth for the individual soul beyond Brahma and Ishana. From that point onwards, it is indeed Brahman itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें असो ऐसे। ब्रह्मादिक ते आंगवसें। ऊर्ध्वमूळासरिसें। न तुकती गा॥४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ aso aise| brahmādika te āṃgavaseṃ| ūrdhvamūḻāsariseṃ| na tukatī gā||4||
verses.meaning: But let this be. Even Brahma and others, with all their greatness, cannot compare to the root of this cosmic tree.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणीकही शाखा उपरता | जिया सनकादिक नामें विख्याता। तिया फळीं मूळीं नाडळता। भरल्या ब्रह्मीं॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇīkahī śākhā uparatā | jiyā sanakādika nāmeṃ vikhyātā| tiyā phaḻīṃ mūḻīṃ nāḍaḻatā| bharalyā brahmīṃ|| 5||
verses.meaning: And other branches too, known by names like Sanaka and others, which, without being attached to fruits or roots, are filled with Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी मनुष्यापासूनि जाणावी । ऊ्ध्वी ब्रह्मादिशेष पालळवी। शाखांची वाढी बरवी । उंचावे पैं॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī manuṣyāpāsūni jāṇāvī | ūdhvī brahmādiśeṣa pālaḻavī| śākhāṃcī vāḍhī baravī | uṃcāve paiṃ||6||
verses.meaning: Thus, know that from humanity, the upward growth of Brahma and the remaining branches flourishes beautifully, rising high.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था ऊर्ध्वींचिया ब्रह्मादि। मनुष्यत्वचि होय आदि । म्हणौनि इयें अधीं । म्हणितलीं मूळें॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā ūrdhvīṃciyā brahmādi| manuṣyatvaci hoya ādi | mhaṇauni iyeṃ adhīṃ | mhaṇitalīṃ mūḻeṃ||7||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, the root of all beings, from Brahma down to humans, is considered to be their human form. Therefore, these are called the roots.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं तुज अलौकिकु। हा अधोर्ध्वशाखु। सांगितला भवरुखु। ऊर्ध्वमूळु॥८॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ tuja alaukiku| hā adhordhvaśākhu| sāṃgitalā bhavarukhu| ūrdhvamūḻu||8||
verses.meaning: Thus, I have described to you this extraordinary tree of worldly existence, with its roots above and branches below.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अधींची हीं मूळें। उपरती परिसविलळी सविवळे। आतां परिस उन्मूळे। कैसेनि हा॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: adhīṃcī hīṃ mūḻeṃ| uparatī parisavilaḻī savivaḻe| ātāṃ parisa unmūḻe| kaiseni hā||9||
verses.meaning: These roots were already loosened by detachment. Now, how can this tree be uprooted?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तुझ्या हन पोटीं । ऐसें गमेल किरीटी । जे येवढें झाड उत्पाटी । ऐसें कायि असे॥२१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī tujhyā hana poṭīṃ | aiseṃ gamela kirīṭī | je yevaḍheṃ jhāḍa utpāṭī | aiseṃ kāyi ase||210||
verses.meaning: But within your heart, O Kiriti, it may seem that what could uproot such a large tree?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं ब्रह्मयाच्या शेबटवरी। ऊर्ध्व शाखांची थोरी । आणि मूळ तंब निराकारीं। ऊर्ध्वी असे॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ brahmayācyā śebaṭavarī| ūrdhva śākhāṃcī thorī | āṇi mūḻa taṃba nirākārīṃ| ūrdhvī ase|| 11||
verses.meaning: Or, like a tree whose branches extend upwards to the very realm of Brahma, yet whose root remains formless and unseen, abiding in the transcendent above.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा स्थावराही तळीं । फांकत असे अधींच्या डाळीं। माजीं धांबतसे दुजां मूळीं । मनुष्यरूपीं ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā sthāvarāhī taḻīṃ | phāṃkata ase adhīṃcyā ḍāḻīṃ| mājīṃ dhāṃbatase dujāṃ mūḻīṃ | manuṣyarūpīṃ || 12||
verses.meaning: This (divine essence) spreads through the roots of the immovable, and through the branches of the earlier ones. It also runs through the secondary roots, in the form of humans.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा गाढा आणि अफाटु । आतां कोण करी यया शेवटु। तरी झणीं हा हळुवटु । धरिसी भावो॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā gāḍhā āṇi aphāṭu | ātāṃ koṇa karī yayā śevaṭu| tarī jhaṇīṃ hā haḻuvaṭu | dharisī bhāvo|| 13||
verses.meaning: Such a profound and boundless experience, who can truly grasp its end? Do not, however, let this thought lead you to a shallow understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हा उन्मूळावया दोषें। येथ सायासचि कायिसे। काय बाळा बागुल देशें। दवडावा आहे॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī hā unmūḻāvayā doṣeṃ| yetha sāyāsaci kāyise| kāya bāḻā bāgula deśeṃ| davaḍāvā āhe|| 14||
verses.meaning: To uproot this fault, what efforts are needed? Is a child to be scared away by a bogeyman?

verses.shloka_devanagari: गंधर्वदुर्ग कायी पाडावे । 'काय शशविषाण मोडावें। होआवें मग तोडावें। खपुष्प कौं ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: gaṃdharvadurga kāyī pāḍāve | 'kāya śaśaviṣāṇa moḍāveṃ| hoāveṃ maga toḍāveṃ| khapuṣpa kauṃ || 15||
verses.meaning: Why should one demolish a city of Gandharvas (a mirage)? Why should one break the horns of a rabbit? How can one cut a sky-flower after it has bloomed?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा संसारु हा वीरा । रुख नाहीं साचोकारा। मा उन्मूळणीं दरारा। कायिसा तरी॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā saṃsāru hā vīrā | rukha nāhīṃ sācokārā| mā unmūḻaṇīṃ darārā| kāyisā tarī|| 16||
verses.meaning: O brave one, this worldly existence is not a true tree. So, what fear can there be in uprooting it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आम्हीं सांगितली जे परी। मूळडाळांची उजरी। ते वांझेचीं घरभरीं। लेंकुरें जैशीं ॥ ९१७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āmhīṃ sāṃgitalī je parī| mūḻaḍāḻāṃcī ujarī| te vāṃjhecīṃ gharabharīṃ| leṃkureṃ jaiśīṃ || 917||
verses.meaning: The way we have described the root and branches, it is like the children filling the house of a barren woman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: काय कोजती चेइलेपणीं। स्वपींचीं तियें बोलणीं। तैशी जाण ते काहाणी । दुगळींचि ते॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāya kojatī ceilepaṇīṃ| svapīṃcīṃ tiyeṃ bolaṇīṃ| taiśī jāṇa te kāhāṇī | dugaḻīṃci te|| 18||
verses.meaning: What is the use of words spoken in a dream when one is awake? Similarly, know that such a story is indeed false.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि आम्हीं निरूपिलें जैसें ।॥ ययाचें अचळ मूळ असे तैसें। आणि तैसाचि जरी हा असे। साचोकारा॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni āmhīṃ nirūpileṃ jaiseṃ ||| yayāceṃ acaḻa mūḻa ase taiseṃ| āṇi taisāci jarī hā ase| sācokārā|| 19||
verses.meaning: If what we have expounded is true, then this (the universe) has an unmoving root, and if it is indeed so, then it is truly real.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कोणाचेनि संतानें। निपजती तया उन्मूळणें । काय फुंकिलिया गगनें। जाइजेळ गा॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī koṇāceni saṃtāneṃ| nipajatī tayā unmūḻaṇeṃ | kāya phuṃkiliyā gaganeṃ| jāijeḻa gā|| 220||
verses.meaning: By whose progeny then, are they uprooted? Does the sky get blown away by mere breath?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि पैं धनंजया । आम्हीं वानिळें रूप तें माया। कासवीचेनि तुपें राया। बोगरिलें जैसें॥२९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni paiṃ dhanaṃjayā | āmhīṃ vāniḻeṃ rūpa teṃ māyā| kāsavīceni tupeṃ rāyā| bogarileṃ jaiseṃ||29||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Dhananjaya, the form we have described is Maya, just as a tortoise's ghee is used to anoint a king.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मृगजळाचीं गा तळीं। तियें दिठी दुरूनि न्याहाळीं। वांचूनि तेणें पाणियें साळी केळी । लाविसी काई॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mṛgajaḻācīṃ gā taḻīṃ| tiyeṃ diṭhī durūni nyāhāḻīṃ| vāṃcūni teṇeṃ pāṇiyeṃ sāḻī keḻī | lāvisī kāī|| 22||
verses.meaning: You see ponds of mirage water from afar. But will you plant banana and rice crops with that water?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मूळ अज्ञानचि तंव लटिकें। मा तयाचें कार्य हें केतुकें। म्हणौनि संसाररूख सतुकें। वाबोचि गा॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mūḻa ajñānaci taṃva laṭikeṃ| mā tayāceṃ kārya heṃ ketukeṃ| mhaṇauni saṃsārarūkha satukeṃ| vāboci gā|| 23||
verses.meaning: The root ignorance itself is false; how much then is its effect? Therefore, the tree of worldly existence is truly vain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अंतु यया नाहीं। ऐसें बोलिजे जें कांहीं। तेंही साचचि पाहीं। येकें परी॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi aṃtu yayā nāhīṃ| aiseṃ bolije jeṃ kāṃhīṃ| teṃhī sācaci pāhīṃ| yekeṃ parī|| 24||
verses.meaning: And that which is said to be without end, know that too is truly one in a certain way.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी प्रबोधु जंव नोहे। तंव निद्रे काय अंतु आहे। कीं रात्री न सरे तंव न पाहे। तया आरीतें ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī prabodhu jaṃva nohe| taṃva nidre kāya aṃtu āhe| kīṃ rātrī na sare taṃva na pāhe| tayā ārīteṃ || 25||
verses.meaning: As long as true awakening does not occur, how can the sleep of ignorance end? Just as one cannot see the sun until the night passes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा जंब पार्था । विवेकु नुधवी ३५४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी माथा। तंव अंतु नाहीं अशश्‍वत्था। भवरूपा या॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā jaṃba pārthā | viveku nudhavī 354 śrījñāneśvarī māthā| taṃva aṃtu nāhīṃ aśaś‍vatthā| bhavarūpā yā|| 26||
verses.meaning: Just as, O Partha, discrimination does not arise, so too, there is no end to this worldly fig tree (samsara) until the head of Shri Dnyaneshwari (the ultimate wisdom) is attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वाजतें वारें निवांत । जंब न राहे जेथिंचें तेथ। तंव तरंगतां अनंत । म्हणाबीचि कौं॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: vājateṃ vāreṃ nivāṃta | jaṃba na rāhe jethiṃceṃ tetha| taṃva taraṃgatāṃ anaṃta | mhaṇābīci kauṃ|| 27||
verses.meaning: The wind, though it blows, remains still; it does not move from its place. Similarly, the infinite waves are said to be in constant motion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि सूर्य जें हारपे। तैं मृगजळाभासु लोपे। कां प्रभा जाय दीपें। मालवलेनि॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni sūrya jeṃ hārape| taiṃ mṛgajaḻābhāsu lope| kāṃ prabhā jāya dīpeṃ| mālavaleni|| 28||
verses.meaning: Therefore, when the sun disappears, the illusion of a mirage vanishes. Or, when a lamp is extinguished, its light is gone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें मूळ अविद्या खाये। तें ज्ञान जैं उभें होये। तैचि यया अंतु आहे। एऱ्हवीं नाहीं ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ mūḻa avidyā khāye| teṃ jñāna jaiṃ ubheṃ hoye| taici yayā aṃtu āhe| eṟhavīṃ nāhīṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: Just as the root of ignorance is consumed, when knowledge arises, then alone does this (ignorance) come to an end; otherwise, it does not.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि हा अनादी। ऐसीही आथी शाब्दी। तो आळु नोहे अनुरोधी। बोलातें या॥ २३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci hā anādī| aisīhī āthī śābdī| to āḻu nohe anurodhī| bolāteṃ yā|| 230||
verses.meaning: Similarly, this (Brahman) is beginningless, as declared by the scriptures. This is not a mere accusation or a statement that contradicts the words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें संसारवृक्षाच्या ठायीं । साचोकार तंव नाहीं । मा नाहीं तया आदि काई । कोण होईल ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ saṃsāravṛkṣācyā ṭhāyīṃ | sācokāra taṃva nāhīṃ | mā nāhīṃ tayā ādi kāī | koṇa hoīla || 39||
verses.meaning: That which is truly non-existent in the tree of worldly existence, how can it have a beginning?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो साच जेथूनि उपजे । तयातें आदि हें साजे। आतां नाहींचि तो म्हणिजे । कोठूनियां॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo sāca jethūni upaje | tayāteṃ ādi heṃ sāje| ātāṃ nāhīṃci to mhaṇije | koṭhūniyāṃ|| 32||
verses.meaning: That which is truly born from something, that is fittingly called its origin. Now, if that origin itself is said not to exist, then from where could anything arise?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जन्मे ना आहे। तैसिया सांगों कवण माये। यालागीं नाहींपणेंचि होये। अनादि हा॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni janme nā āhe| taisiyā sāṃgoṃ kavaṇa māye| yālāgīṃ nāhīṃpaṇeṃci hoye| anādi hā|| 33||
verses.meaning: Therefore, there is no birth, nor is there a mother to speak of. For this reason, He is without beginning, existing in His non-existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांझेचिया लेंका। कैंची जन्मपत्रिका । नभीं निळी भूमिका। कें कल्पूं पां॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃjheciyā leṃkā| kaiṃcī janmapatrikā | nabhīṃ niḻī bhūmikā| keṃ kalpūṃ pāṃ|| 34||
verses.meaning: How can a barren woman's child have a birth chart? How can we imagine a blue color in the sky?

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्योमकुसुमांचा पांडवा। कवणें देंठु तोडावा । म्हणौनि नाहीं ऐसिया भवा। आदि कैंची ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: vyomakusumāṃcā pāṃḍavā| kavaṇeṃ deṃṭhu toḍāvā | mhaṇauni nāhīṃ aisiyā bhavā| ādi kaiṃcī || 35||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, who can pluck the stem of a sky-flower? Therefore, how can there be a beginning for that which does not exist?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें घटाचें नाहींपण। असतचि असे केळेनिवीण। तैसा समूळ वृक्षु जाण । अनादि हा॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ ghaṭāceṃ nāhīṃpaṇa| asataci ase keḻenivīṇa| taisā samūḻa vṛkṣu jāṇa | anādi hā|| 36||
verses.meaning: Just as the non-existence of a pot is inherent even without its destruction, so too, know this entire tree of samsara to be without beginning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना ऐसेनि पाहीं । आद्यंतु ययासि नाहीं । माजीं स्थिती आभासे कांही । परी टवाळ ते॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā aiseni pāhīṃ | ādyaṃtu yayāsi nāhīṃ | mājīṃ sthitī ābhāse kāṃhī | parī ṭavāḻa te|| 37||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, behold, this (world) has neither beginning nor end. Whatever existence it seems to have in between is merely an illusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ब्रह्मगिरीहूनि न निगे। आणि समुद्रींहीं कीर न रिगे। माजीं दिसे वाउगें। मृगांबु जैसें ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: brahmagirīhūni na nige| āṇi samudrīṃhīṃ kīra na rige| mājīṃ dise vāugeṃ| mṛgāṃbu jaiseṃ || 38||
verses.meaning: It does not originate from the Brahmagiri mountain, nor does it enter the ocean; yet, in between, it appears as a mirage.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा आद्यंतीं कौर नाहीं। आणि साचही नोहे कहीं। परी लटिकेपणाची नवाई । पडिभासे गा॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā ādyaṃtīṃ kaura nāhīṃ| āṇi sācahī nohe kahīṃ| parī laṭikepaṇācī navāī | paḍibhāse gā|| 39||
verses.meaning: Similarly, it has no beginning or end, nor is it ever real. Yet, the wonder of its falsity appears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना रंगीं गजबजे । जैसें इंद्रधनुष्य देखिजे। तैसा नेणतया आपजे। आहे ऐसा॥ २४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā raṃgīṃ gajabaje | jaiseṃ iṃdradhanuṣya dekhije| taisā neṇatayā āpaje| āhe aisā|| 240||
verses.meaning: Just as a rainbow appears in various vibrant colors, so too does the ignorant person perceive the world as truly existing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि स्थितीचिये वेळे। भुलवी अज्ञानाचे डोळे। लाघवी हरी मेखळे। लोकु जैसा ॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni sthitīciye veḻe| bhulavī ajñānāce ḍoḻe| lāghavī harī mekhaḻe| loku jaisā || 41||
verses.meaning: At such a time, the enchanting Hari, like a magician, blinds the eyes of ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि नसतीचि श्यामिका । व्योमीं दिसे तैसी दिसो कां। तरी दिसणेंही क्षणा एका । होय जाय॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi nasatīci śyāmikā | vyomīṃ dise taisī diso kāṃ| tarī disaṇeṃhī kṣaṇā ekā | hoya jāya|| 42||
verses.meaning: And just as a non-existent darkness appears in the sky, so too does this appearance. Yet, even this appearance lasts but a moment, coming and going.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्वप्नींही मानिळें लटिकें । तरी निर्वाहो कां एकसारिखें। तेवीं आभासु हा क्षणिकें । रिताचि गा॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: svapnīṃhī māniḻeṃ laṭikeṃ | tarī nirvāho kāṃ ekasārikheṃ| tevīṃ ābhāsu hā kṣaṇikeṃ | ritāci gā|| 43||
verses.meaning: Even if one considers a dream to be false, how can it still appear so real? Similarly, this illusion is momentary and empty.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखतां आहे आवडे । घेऊं जाइजे तरी नातुडे । जैसा टिकु कोजे माकडें। जळामाजीं ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhatāṃ āhe āvaḍe | gheūṃ jāije tarī nātuḍe | jaisā ṭiku koje mākaḍeṃ| jaḻāmājīṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: It is pleasing to behold, but if one tries to grasp it, it eludes, like a monkey trying to catch the reflection of the moon in water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरंगभंगु सांडीं पडे । विजूही न पुरे होडे। आभासासि तेणें पाडें। होणें जाणें गा॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taraṃgabhaṃgu sāṃḍīṃ paḍe | vijūhī na pure hoḍe| ābhāsāsi teṇeṃ pāḍeṃ| hoṇeṃ jāṇeṃ gā|| 45||
verses.meaning: Just as waves rise and fall, and lightning flashes and disappears, so too does the illusory world appear and vanish.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा ग्रीष्मशेषींचा वारा । नेणिजे समोर कीं पाठीमोरा। तैसी स्थिती नाहीं तरुवरा। भवरूपा यया ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā grīṣmaśeṣīṃcā vārā | neṇije samora kīṃ pāṭhīmorā| taisī sthitī nāhīṃ taruvarā| bhavarūpā yayā || 46||
verses.meaning: Just as a tree does not know whether the wind at the end of summer is coming from the front or the back, so too, this tree of worldly existence has no such state of knowing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं आदि ना अंतु स्थिती । ना रूप ययासि आथी । आतां कायसी कुंथाकुंथी । उन्मूळणीं गा ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ ādi nā aṃtu sthitī | nā rūpa yayāsi āthī | ātāṃ kāyasī kuṃthākuṃthī | unmūḻaṇīṃ gā || 47||
verses.meaning: Thus, that which has neither beginning nor end, nor any form or state, why then this struggle and effort to uproot it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपुलिया अज्ञानासाठीं । नव्हता थांबला किरीटी। तरि आतां आत्मज्ञानाच्या लोटीं। खांडेनि गा॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpuliyā ajñānāsāṭhīṃ | navhatā thāṃbalā kirīṭī| tari ātāṃ ātmajñānācyā loṭīṃ| khāṃḍeni gā|| 48||
verses.meaning: Due to his own ignorance, Arjuna was not able to stop the war. But now, in the flood of self-knowledge, he will be cut down.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि ज्ञानेंबीण एकें। उपाय करिसी जितुके । तिहीं गुंफसि अधिकें । रुखीं इये॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni jñāneṃbīṇa ekeṃ| upāya karisī jituke | tihīṃ guṃphasi adhikeṃ | rukhīṃ iye|| 49||
verses.meaning: Without knowledge, whatever other efforts you make, they will entangle you further in this tree of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग किती खांदोखांदीं । यया हिंडावें ऊर्ध्वी अधीं। म्हणौनि मूळचि अज्ञान छेदीं । सम्यक्ज्ञानें ॥ २५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga kitī khāṃdokhāṃdīṃ | yayā hiṃḍāveṃ ūrdhvī adhīṃ| mhaṇauni mūḻaci ajñāna chedīṃ | samyakjñāneṃ || 250||
verses.meaning: Then, how long will it wander up and down, from shoulder to shoulder? Therefore, cut off ignorance at its very root with perfect knowledge.
