verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं दोरीचिया उरगा। डांगा मेळवितां पैं गा। तो शिणुचि वाउगा। केला होय ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ dorīciyā uragā| ḍāṃgā meḻavitāṃ paiṃ gā| to śiṇuci vāugā| kelā hoya || 51||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, if one were to strike at a rope, mistaking it for a snake, all that effort would be in vain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरावया मृगजळाची गंगा । डोणीलागीं धांबतां दांगा-। माजीं बोहळें बुडिजे पै गा। साच जेवीं ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarāvayā mṛgajaḻācī gaṃgā | ḍoṇīlāgīṃ dhāṃbatāṃ dāṃgā-| mājīṃ bohaḻeṃ buḍije pai gā| sāca jevīṃ || 52||
verses.meaning: Just as one who tries to cross a mirage-river, thinking it to be real, will surely drown in the illusion, so too is the fate of those who chase after worldly desires.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं नाथिलिया संसारा । उपा्ईड जाचतया वीरा । आपणपें लोपे वारा। विकोपीं जाय ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ nāthiliyā saṃsārā | upāīḍa jācatayā vīrā | āpaṇapeṃ lope vārā| vikopīṃ jāya || 53||
verses.meaning: Similarly, in this worldly existence, which is like a tangled knot, the brave and virtuous are tormented. Their true self is lost, and they are consumed by distress.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि स्वप्नींचिया घाया । ओखद चेबवोचि धनंजया । तेवीं अज्ञानमूळा यया । ज्ञानचि खडूग ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni svapnīṃciyā ghāyā | okhada cebavoci dhanaṃjayā | tevīṃ ajñānamūḻā yayā | jñānaci khaḍūga || 54||
verses.meaning: Therefore, just as a wound seen in a dream is healed by medicine in that dream, so too, for this root of ignorance, knowledge alone is the sword, O Dhananjaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तेचि लीला परजवे। तैसें वैराग्याचें नवें। अभंगबळ होआवें। बुद्धीसी गा॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teci līlā parajave| taiseṃ vairāgyāceṃ naveṃ| abhaṃgabaḻa hoāveṃ| buddhīsī gā|| 55||
verses.meaning: But that very divine play should be manifested. Similarly, the new, unwavering strength of detachment should come to the intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उठिलेनि वैराग्यें जेणें । हा त्रिवर्गु ऐसा सांडणें । जैसें बमुनियां सुणें। आतांचि गेलें॥५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: uṭhileni vairāgyeṃ jeṇeṃ | hā trivargu aisā sāṃḍaṇeṃ | jaiseṃ bamuniyāṃ suṇeṃ| ātāṃci geleṃ||56||
verses.meaning: With the rise of detachment, one abandons the three pursuits of life (dharma, artha, kama) as if a dog, having just barked, has now gone away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा ठायवरी पांडवा । पदार्थजातीं आघवा । बिटवी तो होआवा। वैराग्यलाठु ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā ṭhāyavarī pāṃḍavā | padārthajātīṃ āghavā | biṭavī to hoāvā| vairāgyalāṭhu || 57||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, for all the worldly objects, let detachment be the axe that fells them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग देहाहंतेचें दळें। सांडूनि एकेचि वेळे । प्रत्यकबुद्धी करतळें । हातवसावें ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga dehāhaṃteceṃ daḻeṃ| sāṃḍūni ekeci veḻe | pratyakabuddhī karataḻeṃ | hātavasāveṃ || 58 ||
verses.meaning: Then, casting aside the delusion of body-consciousness all at once, one should grasp the inner wisdom as if it were a treasure held in the palm of the hand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: निसळें विवेकसाहणें । जे ब्रह्मास्मिबोधें सणाणें । मग पुरतेनि बोधें उटणें। एकलेंचि॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nisaḻeṃ vivekasāhaṇeṃ | je brahmāsmibodheṃ saṇāṇeṃ | maga purateni bodheṃ uṭaṇeṃ| ekaleṃci|| 59||
verses.meaning: With the pure whetstone of discrimination, sharpened by the realization 'I am Brahman,' and then cleansed by perfect knowledge, one becomes truly unique.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी निश्‍चयाचें मुष्टिबळ। पाहावें एकदोनी वेळ। मग तुळावें अति चोखाळ। मननवरी ॥ २६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī niś‍cayāceṃ muṣṭibaḻa| pāhāveṃ ekadonī veḻa| maga tuḻāveṃ ati cokhāḻa| mananavarī || 260||
verses.meaning: But the strength of conviction should be tested once or twice, and then, after careful contemplation, it should be weighed with utmost purity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं हतियेरां आपणयां । निदिध्यासें एक जालिया । पुढें दुजें नुरेल घाया-। पुरतें गा॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ hatiyerāṃ āpaṇayāṃ | nididhyāseṃ eka jāliyā | puḍheṃ dujeṃ nurela ghāyā-| purateṃ gā|| 61||
verses.meaning: When one becomes completely absorbed in the contemplation of the Self, the distinction between the Self and the instruments of action, and even the very notion of a 'second' entity, vanishes entirely, leaving no room for any wound or separation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें आत्मज्ञानाचे खांडें । अह्वैतप्रभेचेनि वाडें । नेदील उरों कवणेकडे। भववृक्षासी ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ ātmajñānāce khāṃḍeṃ | ahvaitaprabheceni vāḍeṃ | nedīla uroṃ kavaṇekaḍe| bhavavṛkṣāsī || 62||
verses.meaning: That sword of self-knowledge, with the great light of non-duality, will not allow the tree of worldly existence to remain anywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शरदागमींचा वारा । जैसा केरु फेडी अंबरा। कां उदयला रवी आंधारा । घोंटु भरी ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: śaradāgamīṃcā vārā | jaisā keru pheḍī aṃbarā| kāṃ udayalā ravī āṃdhārā | ghoṃṭu bharī || 63||
verses.meaning: Just as the autumn wind clears the sky of clouds, or the rising sun dispels darkness completely.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना उपवढ होतां खेंबो। नुरे स्वणसंभ्रमाचा ठावो। स्वप्रतीतिधारेचा वाहो। करील तैसें ॥६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā upavaḍha hotāṃ kheṃbo| nure svaṇasaṃbhramācā ṭhāvo| svapratītidhārecā vāho| karīla taiseṃ ||64||
verses.meaning: When various obstacles arise, the place of self-delusion does not remain. The flow of self-realization will then accomplish its purpose.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां ऊर्ध्वींचें मूळ। कां अधींचें हन शाखाजाळ] तें कांहींचि न दिसे मृगजळ । चांदिणां जेवीं ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ ūrdhvīṃceṃ mūḻa| kāṃ adhīṃceṃ hana śākhājāḻa] teṃ kāṃhīṃci na dise mṛgajaḻa | cāṃdiṇāṃ jevīṃ || 65||
verses.meaning: Then, neither the root above nor the network of branches below is seen, just as a mirage or moonlight is not truly seen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि गा वीरनाथा । आत्मज्ञानाचिया खडूगलता । छेदूनियां भवाश्वत्था। ऊर्ध्वमूळातें ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni gā vīranāthā | ātmajñānāciyā khaḍūgalatā | chedūniyāṃ bhavāśvatthā| ūrdhvamūḻāteṃ || 66 ||
verses.meaning: O great hero, with the sword of self-knowledge, having cut down the worldly fig tree, whose roots are above.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग इदंतेसि वाळलें। जें मीपणेंबीण डाहारलें। तें रूप पाहिजे आपलें। आपणचि ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga idaṃtesi vāḻaleṃ| jeṃ mīpaṇeṃbīṇa ḍāhāraleṃ| teṃ rūpa pāhije āpaleṃ| āpaṇaci || 67||
verses.meaning: Then, having shed the sense of 'this-ness,' that which blossomed without the ego, one should behold that form as one's own self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि दर्पणाचेनि आधारें। एकचि करून दुसरें। मुख पाहाती गव्हारें। तैसें नको हो॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari darpaṇāceni ādhāreṃ| ekaci karūna dusareṃ| mukha pāhātī gavhāreṃ| taiseṃ nako ho|| 68||
verses.meaning: Just as a foolish person, using a mirror as a support, makes one face into two and then looks at it, do not be like that.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें पाहाणें ऐसें असे वीरा। जैसा न बोडलिया विहिरा । मग आपलिया उगमीं झरा । भरोनि ठाके ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ pāhāṇeṃ aiseṃ ase vīrā| jaisā na boḍaliyā vihirā | maga āpaliyā ugamīṃ jharā | bharoni ṭhāke || 69||
verses.meaning: Behold, this seeing is like a well that has not been dug; then, from its own source, a spring overflows and stands full.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी आटल्या अंभ । निजबिंबीं प्रतिबिंब । निहटे कां नभीं नभ । घटाभावीं ॥ २७० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī āṭalyā aṃbha | nijabiṃbīṃ pratibiṃba | nihaṭe kāṃ nabhīṃ nabha | ghaṭābhāvīṃ || 270 ||
verses.meaning: Or, just as the reflection in water disappears when the water dries up, or the sky within a pot merges with the vast sky when the pot breaks, so too does the individual self merge with the Supreme Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना इंधनांशु सरळेया। वन्हि परते जेवी आपणपयां। तैसें आपेंआप धनंजया । न्याहाळणें जें गा ॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā iṃdhanāṃśu saraḻeyā| vanhi parate jevī āpaṇapayāṃ| taiseṃ āpeṃāpa dhanaṃjayā | nyāhāḻaṇeṃ jeṃ gā || 71||
verses.meaning: Just as fire, having consumed various fuels, returns to its own nature, so too, O Dhananjaya, is the self-realization that happens spontaneously.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिव्हें आपली चवी चाखणें। चक्षु निज बुबुळ देखणें । आहे तया ऐसें निरीक्षणें। आपुलें पैं ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jivheṃ āpalī cavī cākhaṇeṃ| cakṣu nija bubuḻa dekhaṇeṃ | āhe tayā aiseṃ nirīkṣaṇeṃ| āpuleṃ paiṃ || 72||
verses.meaning: Just as the tongue tastes its own flavor, and the eye sees its own pupil, so too is the observation of one's own self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां प्रभेसि प्रभा मिळे । गगन गगनावरी लोळे । नाना पाणी भरलें खोळे। पाणियाचिये ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ prabhesi prabhā miḻe | gagana gaganāvarī loḻe | nānā pāṇī bharaleṃ khoḻe| pāṇiyāciye || 73||
verses.meaning: Just as light merges with light, the sky merges with the sky, or water fills a vessel and becomes one with the water within it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपणचि आपणयातें। पाहिजें जें अद्वैतें। तें ऐसें होय निरुतें। बोलिजतु असे॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaṇaci āpaṇayāteṃ| pāhijeṃ jeṃ advaiteṃ| teṃ aiseṃ hoya niruteṃ| bolijatu ase|| 74||
verses.meaning: That which is to be seen by oneself in oneself, that non-dual reality, is indeed spoken of in this manner.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें पाहिजतेनवीण पाहिजे । कांहीं नेणणाचि जाणिजे । आद्यपुरुष कां म्हणिजे। जया ठायातें ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ pāhijatenavīṇa pāhije | kāṃhīṃ neṇaṇāci jāṇije | ādyapuruṣa kāṃ mhaṇije| jayā ṭhāyāteṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: That which is desired without desiring, that which is known without knowing anything, why is it called the Primal Being? That very abode.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथही उपाधीचा बोथंबा। घेऊनि श्रुति उभविती जिभा। मग नामरूपाचा वडंबा। करिती वायां॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tethahī upādhīcā bothaṃbā| gheūni śruti ubhavitī jibhā| maga nāmarūpācā vaḍaṃbā| karitī vāyāṃ|| 76||
verses.meaning: Even there, taking the support of limiting adjuncts, the Vedas raise their voices, and then they needlessly create the illusion of names and forms.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं भवस्वर्गा उबगले। मुमुक्षु योगज्ञाना वळघले। पुढती न यों इया निगाले। पैजा जेथ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ bhavasvargā ubagale| mumukṣu yogajñānā vaḻaghale| puḍhatī na yoṃ iyā nigāle| paijā jetha|| 77||
verses.meaning: Indeed, those who are weary of the cycles of birth and heavenly abodes, the seekers of liberation, have embraced the path of Yoga and knowledge, departing to a place from which they never return.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संसाराचिया पायां पुढां। पळती बीतराग होडा। ओलांडोनि ब्रह्मपदाचा कर्मकडा। घालिती मागां॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃsārāciyā pāyāṃ puḍhāṃ| paḻatī bītarāga hoḍā| olāṃḍoni brahmapadācā karmakaḍā| ghālitī māgāṃ|| 78||
verses.meaning: Before the feet of worldly existence, even the dispassionate flee, leaping over the precipice of Brahman's state, leaving it behind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अहंतादिभावां आपुलियां। झाडा देऊनि आघवेयां। पत्र घेती ज्ञानिये जया। मूळघरासी॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ahaṃtādibhāvāṃ āpuliyāṃ| jhāḍā deūni āghaveyāṃ| patra ghetī jñāniye jayā| mūḻagharāsī|| 79||
verses.meaning: The wise, having uprooted all their ego and other attachments, take refuge in the very source, the root of all existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं जेथुनी हे एवढी । विशवपरंपरेची वेलांडी। वाढती आशा जैसी कोरडी । निदैवाची ॥ २८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ jethunī he evaḍhī | viśavaparaṃparecī velāṃḍī| vāḍhatī āśā jaisī koraḍī | nidaivācī || 280||
verses.meaning: From where this vast lineage of the universe originates, it grows like the dry hope of the unfortunate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिये कां वस्तूचें नेणणें। आणिळें थोर जगा जाणणें । नाहीं तें नांदविलें जेणें । मीं तूं जगीं ॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiye kāṃ vastūceṃ neṇaṇeṃ| āṇiḻeṃ thora jagā jāṇaṇeṃ | nāhīṃ teṃ nāṃdavileṃ jeṇeṃ | mīṃ tūṃ jagīṃ || 81||
verses.meaning: That which is unknowable, yet made known to the world; that which does not exist, yet was made to exist as 'I' and 'you' in the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था तें वस्तु पहिलें। आपणपें आपुलें। पाहिजे जैसें हिंवलें। हिंब हिंबें॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā teṃ vastu pahileṃ| āpaṇapeṃ āpuleṃ| pāhije jaiseṃ hiṃvaleṃ| hiṃba hiṃbeṃ|| 82||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, that original essence, one's own true self, should be experienced just as ice is experienced by ice itself, in its own nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणीकही एक तया । 'बोळखण असे धनंजया। तरी जया कां भेटलिया। येणेंचि नाहीं॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇīkahī eka tayā | 'boḻakhaṇa ase dhanaṃjayā| tarī jayā kāṃ bheṭaliyā| yeṇeṃci nāhīṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: And another sign of him, O Dhananjaya, is that upon meeting him, there is no return (to the cycle of birth and death).

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तया भेटती ऐसें। जे ज्ञानें सर्वत्र सरिसे। महाप्रळयांबूचें जैसें। भरळेपण॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī tayā bheṭatī aiseṃ| je jñāneṃ sarvatra sarise| mahāpraḻayāṃbūceṃ jaiseṃ| bharaḻepaṇa|| 84||
verses.meaning: But they meet in such a way, those who are equal everywhere in knowledge, just like the vastness of the waters of the great dissolution.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया पुरुषांचें कां मन। सांडोनि गेलें मोह मान। वर्षांतीं जैसें घन । आकाशातें॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā puruṣāṃceṃ kāṃ mana| sāṃḍoni geleṃ moha māna| varṣāṃtīṃ jaiseṃ ghana | ākāśāteṃ|| 85||
verses.meaning: The minds of those men, having shed their delusion and pride, are like clouds that depart from the sky at the end of the rainy season.

verses.shloka_devanagari: निकवड्या निष्ठुरा । उबगिजे जेवीं सोयरा । तैसें नागवती बिकारां । वेटाळूं जे॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nikavaḍyā niṣṭhurā | ubagije jevīṃ soyarā | taiseṃ nāgavatī bikārāṃ | veṭāḻūṃ je|| 86||
verses.meaning: Just as a cruel and heartless relative is shunned, so too are vices to be avoided and not allowed to cling to oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: फळली केळी उन्मूळे। तैसी आत्मलाभें प्रबळे । तयाची क्रिया ढाळेंढाळें। गळती आहे॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: phaḻalī keḻī unmūḻe| taisī ātmalābheṃ prabaḻe | tayācī kriyā ḍhāḻeṃḍhāḻeṃ| gaḻatī āhe|| 87||
verses.meaning: Just as a banana tree, having borne fruit, uproots itself, so too, when one attains self-realization, their actions naturally fall away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आगी लागलिया रुखीं। देखोनि सैरा पळती पक्षी। तैसें सांडिळें अशेखीं। विकल्पीं जे॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āgī lāgaliyā rukhīṃ| dekhoni sairā paḻatī pakṣī| taiseṃ sāṃḍiḻeṃ aśekhīṃ| vikalpīṃ je|| 88||
verses.meaning: Just as birds scatter wildly when they see a tree catch fire, so too do all doubts and dualities abandon one who has attained this state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आइकें सकळ दोषतृणीं। अंकुरिजती जिये मेदिनी। तिये भेदबुद्धीची काहाणी । नाहीं जयातें ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āikeṃ sakaḻa doṣatṛṇīṃ| aṃkurijatī jiye medinī| tiye bhedabuddhīcī kāhāṇī | nāhīṃ jayāteṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Listen, the land where all faults sprout, that is the story of the intellect of division, which is not in him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सूर्योदयासरिसी । रात्री पळोनि जाय अपैसी । गेली देहअहंता तैसी । अविद्येसवें ॥ २९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: sūryodayāsarisī | rātrī paḻoni jāya apaisī | gelī dehaahaṃtā taisī | avidyesaveṃ || 290||
verses.meaning: Just as night automatically flees with the sunrise, so too does the ego of the body vanish along with ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आयुष्यहीना जीवातें। शरीर सांडी जेवीं अवचितें। तेवीं निदसुरें द्वैतें। सांडिले जे॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ āyuṣyahīnā jīvāteṃ| śarīra sāṃḍī jevīṃ avaciteṃ| tevīṃ nidasureṃ dvaiteṃ| sāṃḍile je|| 91||
verses.meaning: Just as a body suddenly abandons a lifeless being, so too, duality is abandoned by the one who is awakened.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लोहाचें सांकडें परिसा। न जोडे अंधारु रवि जैसा। द्वैतबुद्धीचा तैसा। सदा दुकाळ जया॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: lohāceṃ sāṃkaḍeṃ parisā| na joḍe aṃdhāru ravi jaisā| dvaitabuddhīcā taisā| sadā dukāḻa jayā|| 92||
verses.meaning: Just as iron cannot bind the philosopher's stone, and darkness cannot approach the sun, so too is there perpetual scarcity for one with a dualistic mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा सुखदुःखाकारें। दृंद्रें देहीं जियें गोचरें। तियें जयां कां समोरें। होतीचिना॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā sukhaduḥkhākāreṃ| dṛṃdreṃ dehīṃ jiyeṃ gocareṃ| tiyeṃ jayāṃ kāṃ samoreṃ| hotīcinā|| 93||
verses.meaning: Indeed, the dualities of joy and sorrow, which are perceptible in the body, do not confront him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्वप्नींचें राज्य कां मरण। नोहे हर्षशोकांसि 'कारण । उपवढलिया जाण। जियापरी॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: svapnīṃceṃ rājya kāṃ maraṇa| nohe harṣaśokāṃsi 'kāraṇa | upavaḍhaliyā jāṇa| jiyāparī|| 94||
verses.meaning: Just as a kingdom or death experienced in a dream does not cause joy or sorrow upon waking, so too are the experiences of this world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सुखदुःखरूपीं । दृवंद्री जे पुण्यपापीं। न घेपिजती सर्पी। गरुड जैसें ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sukhaduḥkharūpīṃ | dṛvaṃdrī je puṇyapāpīṃ| na ghepijatī sarpī| garuḍa jaiseṃ || 95||
verses.meaning: Just as a serpent is not affected by the duality of joy and sorrow, which are like good and bad deeds, similarly, a Garuda (mythical bird, vehicle of Vishnu) is not affected by these dualities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अनात्मवर्गनीर। सांडूनि आत्मरसाचें क्षीर। चरताति जे सविचार। राजहंसु॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi anātmavarganīra| sāṃḍūni ātmarasāceṃ kṣīra| caratāti je savicāra| rājahaṃsu|| 96||
verses.meaning: And those discerning ones, like royal swans, abandon the water of non-self and partake of the milk of the Self's essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा वर्षोनि भूतळीं। आपला रसु अंशुमाळी । मागौता आणी रश्मिजाळीं। बिंबासीचि ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā varṣoni bhūtaḻīṃ| āpalā rasu aṃśumāḻī | māgautā āṇī raśmijāḻīṃ| biṃbāsīci || 97||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun, having poured its essence onto the earth through rain, draws it back into itself through its rays.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आत्मभ्रांतीसाठीं । वस्तु विखुरली बारावाटीं। ते एकवटिती ज्ञानदृष्टी। अखंड जे॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ātmabhrāṃtīsāṭhīṃ | vastu vikhuralī bārāvāṭīṃ| te ekavaṭitī jñānadṛṣṭī| akhaṃḍa je|| 98||
verses.meaning: Just as due to the delusion of the self, the true reality is scattered in twelve directions, so too, through the unbroken vision of knowledge, all these scattered parts are unified.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना आत्मयाचा । निर्धारी बिवेकु जयांचा । बुडाला बोघु गंगेचा । सिंधूमाजीं जैसा॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā ātmayācā | nirdhārī biveku jayāṃcā | buḍālā boghu gaṃgecā | siṃdhūmājīṃ jaisā|| 99||
verses.meaning: Indeed, those whose discriminative intellect regarding the Self is completely submerged, like the sacred waters of the Ganga merging into the ocean.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आधवेंचि आपलेंपणें । नुरेचि जया अभिलाषणें । जैसें येथूनि पऱ्हां जाणें । आकाशा नाहीं ॥ ३००॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ ādhaveṃci āpaleṃpaṇeṃ | nureci jayā abhilāṣaṇeṃ | jaiseṃ yethūni paṟhāṃ jāṇeṃ | ākāśā nāhīṃ || 300||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky has no desire to move from its place, so too, one who has realized their true self has no desires left.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा अग्नीचा डोंगरु । नेघे कोणी बीजअंकुरु । तैसा मनीं जयां विकारु । उदैजेना॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā agnīcā ḍoṃgaru | neghe koṇī bījaaṃkuru | taisā manīṃ jayāṃ vikāru | udaijenā|| 1||
verses.meaning: Just as a mountain of fire does not allow any seed to sprout, similarly, no evil thoughts arise in the minds of such people.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा काढिलिया मंदराचळु । राहे क्षीराब्धि निश्चळु। तैसा नुठी जयां सळू। कामोर्मीचा॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā kāḍhiliyā maṃdarācaḻu | rāhe kṣīrābdhi niścaḻu| taisā nuṭhī jayāṃ saḻū| kāmormīcā|| 2||
verses.meaning: Just as the ocean of milk remains undisturbed after the Mandarachal mountain is removed, so too, the waves of desire do not arise in one whose mind is steady.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चंद्रमा कळीं धाला । ३५८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी न दिसे कोणें आंगीं बोसावला । तेवीं अपेक्षेचा अबखळा। न पडे जयां॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: caṃdramā kaḻīṃ dhālā | 358 śrījñāneśvarī na dise koṇeṃ āṃgīṃ bosāvalā | tevīṃ apekṣecā abakhaḻā| na paḍe jayāṃ||3||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon, though full of phases, shows no sign of being worn away, so too, those who are free from desire leave no trace of longing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें किती बोलूं असांगडें। जेवीं परमाणु नुरे वायूपुढें। तैसें विषयांचें नावडे । नांबचि जयां॥४॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ kitī bolūṃ asāṃgaḍeṃ| jevīṃ paramāṇu nure vāyūpuḍheṃ| taiseṃ viṣayāṃceṃ nāvaḍe | nāṃbaci jayāṃ||4||
verses.meaning: How much more can I say? Just as an atom cannot remain before the wind, so too, the very name of worldly pleasures is not liked by them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं जे जे कोणी ऐसे। केले ज्ञानाख्यहुताशें । ते तेथ मिळती जेसें। हेमीं हेम ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ je je koṇī aise| kele jñānākhyahutāśeṃ | te tetha miḻatī jeseṃ| hemīṃ hema || 5||
verses.meaning: Thus, all those who, through the fire of knowledge, have purified themselves, merge into that Supreme Being, just as gold merges with gold.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ म्हणिजे कवणें ठाई । ऐसेंही पुससी कांहीं । तरी तें पद गा नाहीं । वेंचु जया ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha mhaṇije kavaṇeṃ ṭhāī | aiseṃhī pusasī kāṃhīṃ | tarī teṃ pada gā nāhīṃ | veṃcu jayā || 6||
verses.meaning: If you ask, "Where then is that place?" know that it is not a state that can be exhausted or diminished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दृश्यपणें देखिजे। कां ज्ञेयत्वें जाणिजे। अमुकें ऐसें म्हणिजे। तें जें नव्हे ॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: dṛśyapaṇeṃ dekhije| kāṃ jñeyatveṃ jāṇije| amukeṃ aiseṃ mhaṇije| teṃ jeṃ navhe ||7||
verses.meaning: That which cannot be seen, known, or described as 'this' or 'that'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं दीपाचिया बंबाळीं। कां चंद्र हन जें उजळी। हें काय बोलों अंशुमाळी । प्रकाशी जें ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ dīpāciyā baṃbāḻīṃ| kāṃ caṃdra hana jeṃ ujaḻī| heṃ kāya boloṃ aṃśumāḻī | prakāśī jeṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: What can I say about the sun, which illuminates everything, when even a lamp or the moon shines? The sun is the ultimate source of light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें आधवेंचि दिसणें। जयातें कां न देखणें। बिश्व भासतसे जेणें । लपालेनी ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ ādhaveṃci disaṇeṃ| jayāteṃ kāṃ na dekhaṇeṃ| biśva bhāsatase jeṇeṃ | lapālenī || 9||
verses.meaning: That very seeing, which is not seeing, by which the universe appears, yet remains hidden.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें शिंपीपण हारपे। तंब तंव खरें होय रुपें। कां दोरी लोपतां सापें। फार होइजे॥ ३१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ śiṃpīpaṇa hārape| taṃba taṃva khareṃ hoya rupeṃ| kāṃ dorī lopatāṃ sāpeṃ| phāra hoije|| 310||
verses.meaning: Just as the shell-like appearance vanishes, the silver becomes real. Or, when the rope disappears, the snake becomes prominent.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं चंद्रसूर्यादि थोरें। इयें तेजें जियें फारें। तियें जयाचेनि आधारें। प्रकाशती॥ १९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ caṃdrasūryādi thoreṃ| iyeṃ tejeṃ jiyeṃ phāreṃ| tiyeṃ jayāceni ādhāreṃ| prakāśatī|| 191||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the great luminaries like the sun and moon, which possess immense brilliance, shine forth only by His support.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वस्तु कौं तेजोराशी । सर्वभूतात्मक सरिसी। चंद्रसूर्याच्या मानसीं । प्रकाशे जे॥९१२॥
verses.shloka_iast: te vastu kauṃ tejorāśī | sarvabhūtātmaka sarisī| caṃdrasūryācyā mānasīṃ | prakāśe je||912||
verses.meaning: That very essence, a radiant mass of light, resides equally within all beings, illuminating the minds of the moon and the sun.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि चंद्रसूर्य कडवसां। पडती वस्तूच्या प्रकाशा । यालागीं तेज जें तेजसा। तें बस्तूचें आंग॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni caṃdrasūrya kaḍavasāṃ| paḍatī vastūcyā prakāśā | yālāgīṃ teja jeṃ tejasā| teṃ bastūceṃ āṃga|| 13||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the sun and moon are but reflections of the light of the Self. Hence, the light that illuminates all is the very essence of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जयाच्या प्रकाशीं। जग हारपे चंद्रार्केसीं । सचंद्र नक्षत्रे जैसीं । दिनोदयीं ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jayācyā prakāśīṃ| jaga hārape caṃdrārkesīṃ | sacaṃdra nakṣatre jaisīṃ | dinodayīṃ || 94||
verses.meaning: And in whose light the world, along with the moon and sun, disappears, just as the moon and stars vanish at the break of day.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी प्रबोधल्िये वेळे। ते स्वप्नींची डिंडिमा मावळे । कां नुरेचि सांजवेळे । मृगतृष्णिका ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī prabodhaliye veḻe| te svapnīṃcī ḍiṃḍimā māvaḻe | kāṃ nureci sāṃjaveḻe | mṛgatṛṣṇikā || 95 ||
verses.meaning: Or, when true knowledge dawns, the illusory drumbeats of a dream vanish. Similarly, at dusk, the mirage disappears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा जिये वस्तूच्या ठायीं । कोण्हीच कां आभासु नाहीं। तें माझें निजधाम पाहीं । पाटाचें गा॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā jiye vastūcyā ṭhāyīṃ | koṇhīca kāṃ ābhāsu nāhīṃ| teṃ mājheṃ nijadhāma pāhīṃ | pāṭāceṃ gā|| 16||
verses.meaning: Just as there is no illusion whatsoever in that Reality, that is My true abode, understand, the original, fundamental state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुढती जे तेथ गेळे। ते न घेतीचि माघौतीं पाउलें। महोदधीं कां मिनले। स्त्रोत जैसे ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: puḍhatī je tetha geḻe| te na ghetīci māghautīṃ pāuleṃ| mahodadhīṃ kāṃ minale| strota jaise || 17||
verses.meaning: Those who have gone there do not take a single step back, just as streams that have merged into the great ocean do not return.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां लवणाची कुंजरी। सूदलिया 'लवणसागरीं । होयच्ि ना माघारी। परती जैसी॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ lavaṇācī kuṃjarī| sūdaliyā 'lavaṇasāgarīṃ | hoyaci nā māghārī| paratī jaisī|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as a lump of salt, once dissolved in the ocean, can never return to its original form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना गेलिया अंतराळा। न येतीचि वन्हिज्वाळा। नाहीं तप्तळोहौनि जळा । निघणें जेबीं॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā geliyā aṃtarāḻā| na yetīci vanhijvāḻā| nāhīṃ taptaḻohauni jaḻā | nighaṇeṃ jebīṃ|| 19||
verses.meaning: Just as flames do not return to the sky after ascending, and water does not emerge from a red-hot iron, so too is the nature of the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं मजसीं एकवट । जे जाले ज्ञानें चोखट । तयां पुनरावृत्तीची वाट। मोडली गा॥ ३२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ majasīṃ ekavaṭa | je jāle jñāneṃ cokhaṭa | tayāṃ punarāvṛttīcī vāṭa| moḍalī gā|| 320||
verses.meaning: Thus, those who have become pure through knowledge and have united with Me, for them, the path of rebirth is broken.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ प्रज्ञापूथ्वीचा रावो। पार्थु म्हणे जी जी 'पसावो। परी विनंती एकी देवो । चित्त देतु॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha prajñāpūthvīcā rāvo| pārthu mhaṇe jī jī 'pasāvo| parī vinaṃtī ekī devo | citta detu|| 21||
verses.meaning: There, the king of the earth of wisdom, Arjuna, said, "O Lord, be gracious! But please, listen to one request."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी देवेंसि स्वयें एक होती। मग माघौते जे न येती। ते देवेंसि भिन्न आथी। कौं अभिन्न जी॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī deveṃsi svayeṃ eka hotī| maga māghaute je na yetī| te deveṃsi bhinna āthī| kauṃ abhinna jī|| 22||
verses.meaning: If they become one with God, then they do not return. Are they different from God, or non-different?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी भिन्नचि अनादिसिद्ध। तरी न येती हें असंबद्ध । जे फुलां गेळे षट्पद। ते फुलेंचि होती पां॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī bhinnaci anādisiddha| tarī na yetī heṃ asaṃbaddha | je phulāṃ geḻe ṣaṭpada| te phuleṃci hotī pāṃ|| 23||
verses.meaning: Though distinct and eternally established, they are not unrelated. Just as bees are drawn to flowers, they become one with the flowers.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं लह््याहुनि अनारिसें। बाण लह्ष्यीं शिवोनि जैसे। मागुते पडती तैसे। येतीचि ते॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ lahyāhuni anāriseṃ| bāṇa lahṣyīṃ śivoni jaise| māgute paḍatī taise| yetīci te|| 24||
verses.meaning: Just as arrows, having struck their target, return, so too do these (beings) come back, but in a way that is even more extraordinary than the waves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी तूंचि ते स्वभावें । तरी कोणें कोणासि मिळावें । आपणयासी आपण रुपावें। शस्त्रें केवीं ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī tūṃci te svabhāveṃ | tarī koṇeṃ koṇāsi miḻāveṃ | āpaṇayāsī āpaṇa rupāveṃ| śastreṃ kevīṃ || 25||
verses.meaning: If you are naturally everything, then who is to meet whom? How can one's own form be cut by weapons?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तुजसी अभिन्नां जीवां । तुझा संयोगवियोगु देवा। न ये बोलो अवयवां। शरीरेंसीं ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tujasī abhinnāṃ jīvāṃ | tujhā saṃyogaviyogu devā| na ye bolo avayavāṃ| śarīreṃsīṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for those souls who are inseparable from You, O Lord, it is not possible to speak of Your union or separation, just as it is not possible for the limbs to be separate from the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जे सदा वेगळे तुजसीं। तयां मिळणीं नाहीं कोणे दिवशीं।॥ मा येती न येती हे कायसी । वायबुन्दि॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi je sadā vegaḻe tujasīṃ| tayāṃ miḻaṇīṃ nāhīṃ koṇe divaśīṃ||| mā yetī na yetī he kāyasī | vāyabundi|| 27||
verses.meaning: And those who are always separate from You, they will never unite with You on any day. So, what is this talk of coming and not coming? It is all empty words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कोण गा तूंतें । पाबोनि न येती माघौते। हे विश्‍्वतोमुखा मातें । बुझावीं जी॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī koṇa gā tūṃteṃ | pāboni na yetī māghaute| he viś‍vatomukhā māteṃ | bujhāvīṃ jī|| 28||
verses.meaning: Then who are You, that having drunk of You, they do not return? O Universal-faced One, please explain this to me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इये आक्षेपीं अर्जुनाच्या। तो शिरोमणी सर्वज्ञांचा। तोषला बोध शिष्याचा । देखोनियां॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: iye ākṣepīṃ arjunācyā| to śiromaṇī sarvajñāṃcā| toṣalā bodha śiṣyācā | dekhoniyāṃ|| 29||
verses.meaning: Upon Arjuna's inquiry, the crest-jewel of all-knowing ones was pleased, seeing the disciple's understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणे गा महामती । मातें पावोनि न येती पुढती। ते भिन्नाभिन्न रीती। आहाती दोनी॥ ३३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇe gā mahāmatī | māteṃ pāvoni na yetī puḍhatī| te bhinnābhinna rītī| āhātī donī|| 330||
verses.meaning: Then, O great-minded one, those who attain Me do not return again. They are of two kinds, distinct and non-distinct.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें विवेकें खोलें पाहिजे) तरी मी तेचि ते सहजें। ना आहाचवाहाच तरी दुजे। ऐसेही गमती ॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ vivekeṃ kholeṃ pāhije) tarī mī teci te sahajeṃ| nā āhācavāhāca tarī duje| aisehī gamatī || 31||
verses.meaning: If one seeks with discrimination, then I am indeed that very same Self, effortlessly. If one does not seek with such discrimination, then the duality of 'other' also appears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसे पाणियावरी वेगळ। तळपतां दिसती कल्लोळ। येऱ्हवीं तरी निखिळ। पाणीचि तें ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaise pāṇiyāvarī vegaḻa| taḻapatāṃ disatī kalloḻa| yeṟhavīṃ tarī nikhiḻa| pāṇīci teṃ || 32||
verses.meaning: Just as waves appear distinct and shimmering on the surface of water, yet in reality, they are nothing but water itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां सुवर्णाहुनि आनें। लेणीं गमती भिन्नें। मग पाहिजे तंब सोनें। अवघेंचि तें॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ suvarṇāhuni āneṃ| leṇīṃ gamatī bhinneṃ| maga pāhije taṃba soneṃ| avagheṃci teṃ|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as ornaments, though appearing different from gold, are ultimately nothing but gold itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ज्ञानाचिये दिठी। मजसीं अभिन्नचि ते किरीटी। येर भिन्नपण तें उठी। अज्ञानास्तव ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jñānāciye diṭhī| majasīṃ abhinnaci te kirīṭī| yera bhinnapaṇa teṃ uṭhī| ajñānāstava || 34||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, through the eye of knowledge, I am seen as non-different from you. Any perception of difference arises only from ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि साचोकारेनि वस्तुविचारें। कैचे मज एकासि दुसरें। जें भिन्नाभिन्नव्यवहारें। उमसिजेळ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi sācokāreni vastuvicāreṃ| kaice maja ekāsi dusareṃ| jeṃ bhinnābhinnavyavahāreṃ| umasijeḻa|| 35||
verses.meaning: And truly, upon contemplating the ultimate reality, how can there be a second to me, such that the distinctions of difference and non-difference could arise?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधघवेंचि आकाश सूनि पोटीं । बिंबचि जें आते खोटी । तैं प्रतिबिंब कें उठी। कें रश्मि शिरे॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhaghaveṃci ākāśa sūni poṭīṃ | biṃbaci jeṃ āte khoṭī | taiṃ pratibiṃba keṃ uṭhī| keṃ raśmi śire|| 36||
verses.meaning: When the sky itself is empty within the sun, and the sun itself is a false appearance, then how can a reflection arise? How can rays enter?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां कल्पांतींचिया पाणिया । 'काय बोत भरिती धनंजया। म्हणौनि कैंचे अंश अविक्रिया। एका मज॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ kalpāṃtīṃciyā pāṇiyā | 'kāya bota bharitī dhanaṃjayā| mhaṇauni kaiṃce aṃśa avikriyā| ekā maja|| 37||
verses.meaning: Just as the waters of the deluge cannot fill a single palm, how can the immutable and indivisible me be divided into parts, O Dhananjaya?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ओघाचेनि मेळें। पाणी उजू परी वांकुडें जालें। रवी दुजेपण आलें। तोयबगें ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī oghāceni meḻeṃ| pāṇī ujū parī vāṃkuḍeṃ jāleṃ| ravī dujepaṇa āleṃ| toyabageṃ || 38||
verses.meaning: Just as water, though straight in itself, appears crooked due to the flow of the stream, and the sun, though one, appears multiple when reflected in different bodies of water, so too does the singular divine appear diversified through the illusion of Maya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्योम चौफळें कीं वाटोळें। हें ऐसें 'कायिसयाही मिळे। परी घटमठीं वेंटाळें। तैसेंही आथी॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vyoma cauphaḻeṃ kīṃ vāṭoḻeṃ| heṃ aiseṃ 'kāyisayāhī miḻe| parī ghaṭamaṭhīṃ veṃṭāḻeṃ| taiseṃhī āthī|| 39||
verses.meaning: Is the sky square or round? It is neither. Yet, it appears to take the shape of the pot or the monastery it encompasses. So too is the divine reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा निद्रेचेनि आधारें। काय एकलेनि जग न भरे। स्वप्नींचेनि जें अवतरें। रायपणें ॥ ३४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā nidreceni ādhāreṃ| kāya ekaleni jaga na bhare| svapnīṃceni jeṃ avatareṃ| rāyapaṇeṃ || 340||
verses.meaning: Indeed, does the world not become full by the support of sleep alone? What appears in a dream as kingship?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां मिनलळेनि किडाळें। वानिभेदासि ये सोळें। तैसा स्वमायें वेंटाळें। शुद्ध जें मी॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ minalaḻeni kiḍāḻeṃ| vānibhedāsi ye soḻeṃ| taisā svamāyeṃ veṃṭāḻeṃ| śuddha jeṃ mī|| 41||
verses.meaning: Just as a speck of gold dust, when mixed with an alloy, appears to change its color, so too am I, the pure Self, entangled by My own Maya (illusory power).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैं अज्ञान एक रूढे। तेणें को$हं विकल्पाचें मांडें। मग विवरूनि कौजे फुडें। देहो मी ऐसें॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiṃ ajñāna eka rūḍhe| teṇeṃ ko$haṃ vikalpāceṃ māṃḍeṃ| maga vivarūni kauje phuḍeṃ| deho mī aiseṃ|| 42||
verses.meaning: Ignorance is deeply rooted, giving rise to the notion of "who am I?" From this, the illusion that "I am the body" then clearly manifests.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें शरीराचि येवढें। जें आत्मज्ञान वेगळें पडे। तैं माझा अंशु आवडे । थोडेपणें ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ śarīrāci yevaḍheṃ| jeṃ ātmajñāna vegaḻeṃ paḍe| taiṃ mājhā aṃśu āvaḍe | thoḍepaṇeṃ || 43||
verses.meaning: When the body, which is so vast, becomes separate from Self-knowledge, then my essence, though diminished, becomes dear.

verses.shloka_devanagari: समुद्र कां वायुवशें। तरंगाकार उल्लसे। तो समुद्रांशु ऐसा दिसे। सानिवा जेवीं ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: samudra kāṃ vāyuvaśeṃ| taraṃgākāra ullase| to samudrāṃśu aisā dise| sānivā jevīṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: Just as the ocean, swayed by the wind, manifests as waves, appearing as if they are parts of the ocean itself, so too is the divine presence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं जडातें जीवविता । देहअहंता उपजविता । मी जीव गमें पंडुसुता । जीवलोकीं ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ jaḍāteṃ jīvavitā | dehaahaṃtā upajavitā | mī jīva gameṃ paṃḍusutā | jīvalokīṃ || 45||
verses.meaning: Similarly, it enlivens the inert, gives rise to the ego of the body, and makes one feel "I am a living being" in the world of mortals, O son of Pandu.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं जीवाचिया बोधा। गोचरु जो हा धांदा। तो जीवलोकशब्दा। अभिप्राबो ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ jīvāciyā bodhā| gocaru jo hā dhāṃdā| to jīvalokaśabdā| abhiprābo || 46||
verses.meaning: The entire realm of worldly activities, which is perceptible to the intellect of the embodied soul, is what is meant by the term 'Jeevaloka' (the world of living beings).

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा उपजणें निमणें। हें साचचि जें कां मानणें। तो जीवबलोकु मी म्हणें। संसारु हन॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā upajaṇeṃ nimaṇeṃ| heṃ sācaci jeṃ kāṃ mānaṇeṃ| to jīvabaloku mī mhaṇeṃ| saṃsāru hana|| 47||
verses.meaning: Indeed, this belief in birth and death, that is what I call the world of transmigration, the cycle of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवंबिध जीवलोकीं। तूं मातें ऐसा अवलोकीं। जैसा चंद्रु कां उदकौं। उदकातीत॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃbidha jīvalokīṃ| tūṃ māteṃ aisā avalokīṃ| jaisā caṃdru kāṃ udakauṃ| udakātīta|| 48||
verses.meaning: In this world of living beings, you should perceive Me just as the moon is seen in water, yet remains beyond the water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं काश्मीराचा रवा। कुंकुमावरी पांडवा। आणिका गमे 'लोहिवा। तो तरी नव्हे॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ kāśmīrācā ravā| kuṃkumāvarī pāṃḍavā| āṇikā game 'lohivā| to tarī navhe|| 49||
verses.meaning: Just as the saffron powder, when mixed with kumkum, appears red to others, but is not truly red itself, so too is the nature of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अनादिपण न मोडे । माझें अक्रियत्व न खंडे। परी कर्ता भोक्ता ऐसें आवडे । ते जाण गा भ्रांती॥ ३५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ anādipaṇa na moḍe | mājheṃ akriyatva na khaṃḍe| parī kartā bhoktā aiseṃ āvaḍe | te jāṇa gā bhrāṃtī|| 350||
verses.meaning: My eternality is not broken, nor is My inaction hindered; yet, to perceive Me as an doer and enjoyer—know that to be an illusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना आत्मा चोखटु । होऊनि प्रकृतीसी एकवट । बांधे प्रकृतिधर्माचा पाटु। आपणपयां॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā ātmā cokhaṭu | hoūni prakṛtīsī ekavaṭa | bāṃdhe prakṛtidharmācā pāṭu| āpaṇapayāṃ|| 51||
verses.meaning: Indeed, the pure Self, becoming one with Prakriti (primordial nature), binds itself with the attributes of Prakriti.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं मनादि साही इंद्रियें। श्रोत्रादि प्रकृतिकार्ये । तिये माझीं म्हणौनि होये । व्यापारारूढ ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ manādi sāhī iṃdriyeṃ| śrotrādi prakṛtikārye | tiye mājhīṃ mhaṇauni hoye | vyāpārārūḍha || 52||
verses.meaning: The mind and the six senses, such as the ears, are products of Prakriti (nature). Because they are considered 'mine,' they become engaged in their respective activities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें स्वप्नीं परित्राजें। आपणपयां आपण कुटुंब होईजे । मग तयाचेनि धांविजे। मोहें सैरा॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ svapnīṃ paritrājeṃ| āpaṇapayāṃ āpaṇa kuṭuṃba hoīje | maga tayāceni dhāṃvije| moheṃ sairā|| 53||
verses.meaning: Just as in a dream, a renunciate himself becomes a family man, and then, driven by that delusion, he runs wildly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा आपलिया विस्मृती। आत्मा आपणचि प्रकृती-। सारिखा गमोनि पुढती । तियेसीचि भजे॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā āpaliyā vismṛtī| ātmā āpaṇaci prakṛtī-| sārikhā gamoni puḍhatī | tiyesīci bhaje|| 54||
verses.meaning: Similarly, due to its own forgetfulness, the Self itself appears like nature, and then worships that very nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मनाच्या रथीं वळघे। श्रवणाच्या द्वारें निघे । मग शब्दाचिया रिघे। रानामाजीं ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: manācyā rathīṃ vaḻaghe| śravaṇācyā dvāreṃ nighe | maga śabdāciyā righe| rānāmājīṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: It enters the chariot of the mind, emerges through the gate of hearing, and then penetrates the forest of words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोचि प्रकृतीचा वागोरा। करी त्वचेचिया मोहरा । आणि स्पर्शाचिया घोरा। बना जाय ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: toci prakṛtīcā vāgorā| karī tvaceciyā moharā | āṇi sparśāciyā ghorā| banā jāya || 56||
verses.meaning: That very (Brahman) becomes the expanse of Prakriti, creating the forms of skin and entering into the dense forest of touch.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कोणे एके अवसरीं । रिघोनि नेत्राच्या द्वारीं । मग रूपाच्या डोंगरीं। सैरा हिंडे॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: koṇe eke avasarīṃ | righoni netrācyā dvārīṃ | maga rūpācyā ḍoṃgarīṃ| sairā hiṃḍe|| 57||
verses.meaning: At some opportune moment, entering through the gateway of the eyes, it then wanders freely on the mountain of forms.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां रसनेचिया वाटा। निघोनि गा सुभटा । रसाचा दरकुटा। भरोंचि लागे॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ rasaneciyā vāṭā| nighoni gā subhaṭā | rasācā darakuṭā| bharoṃci lāge|| 58||
verses.meaning: Or, O valiant one, through the path of the tongue, the very essence of taste begins to fill up.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी येणेंचि घराणें।॥ जैं देहांशु करी निघणें। मग गंधाचीं दारुणें। आडवें ल॑घी॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī yeṇeṃci gharāṇeṃ||| jaiṃ dehāṃśu karī nighaṇeṃ| maga gaṃdhācīṃ dāruṇeṃ| āḍaveṃ la̭ghī|| 59||
verses.meaning: Or, when the subtle body departs from the physical body, it then crosses the formidable gates of smell.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि देहेंद्रियनायकें । धरूनि मन जवळिकें । भोगिजती शब्दादिकें । विषयभरणें ॥ ३६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni deheṃdriyanāyakeṃ | dharūni mana javaḻikeṃ | bhogijatī śabdādikeṃ | viṣayabharaṇeṃ || 360||
verses.meaning: In this way, the master of the body and senses, holding the mind close, experiences sound and other sense objects, which are like sustenance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी कर्ता भोक्ता ऐसें। हें जीवाचें तैचि दिसे। जें शरीरीं कां पैसे। एकाधिये॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī kartā bhoktā aiseṃ| heṃ jīvāceṃ taici dise| jeṃ śarīrīṃ kāṃ paise| ekādhiye|| 61||
verses.meaning: The doer and enjoyer, such is the nature of the soul, which is seen only when it enters a body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा आधिलळा आणि विलासिया। तैंचि वबोळखों ये धनंजया । जैं राजसेव्या ठाया। वस्तीसि ये॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā ādhilaḻā āṇi vilāsiyā| taiṃci vaboḻakhoṃ ye dhanaṃjayā | jaiṃ rājasevyā ṭhāyā| vastīsi ye||62||
verses.meaning: Just as a person who is already wealthy and enjoys luxury, O Dhananjaya, becomes even more prominent when they come to reside in a place of royal service.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा अहंकर्तृत्वाचा वाढु । कां विषयेंद्रियांचा धुमाडु। हा जाणिजे तैं निवाडु। जैं देह पाविजे॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā ahaṃkartṛtvācā vāḍhu | kāṃ viṣayeṃdriyāṃcā dhumāḍu| hā jāṇije taiṃ nivāḍu| jaiṃ deha pāvije|| 63||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the growth of ego-driven actions, or the tumultuous pursuit of sensory pleasures, is truly understood only when one attains the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा शरीरातें सांडी । तऱही इंद्रियांची तांडी। हे आपणयांसवें काढी । घेऊनि जाय॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā śarīrāteṃ sāṃḍī | taṟahī iṃdriyāṃcī tāṃḍī| he āpaṇayāṃsaveṃ kāḍhī | gheūni jāya|| 64||
verses.meaning: Or, even if the body is abandoned, the senses' stubbornness, this too, it takes with itself and carries away.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा अपमानिला अतिथी । ने सुकृताची संपत्ति । कां साइखडेयाची गती । सूत्रतंतू॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā apamānilā atithī | ne sukṛtācī saṃpatti | kāṃ sāikhaḍeyācī gatī | sūtrataṃtū|| 65 ||
verses.meaning: Just as an insulted guest takes away the host's accumulated good deeds, or as a thread is the ultimate fate of a silkworm's efforts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना मावळतेनि तपनें। नेइजती लोकांचीं दर्शनें । हें असो द्रुती पवनें। नेईजे जैसी ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā māvaḻateni tapaneṃ| neijatī lokāṃcīṃ darśaneṃ | heṃ aso drutī pavaneṃ| neīje jaisī || 66||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's setting does not take away the sight of people, or as the wind does not take away the light, so too is the nature of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं मनःषष्ठां ययां। इंद्रियांतें धनंजया । देहराजु ने देहा-। पासूनि गेला ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ manaḥṣaṣṭhāṃ yayāṃ| iṃdriyāṃteṃ dhanaṃjayā | deharāju ne dehā-| pāsūni gelā || 67||
verses.meaning: Just as the king of the body, the soul, leaves the body, so too, O Dhananjaya, the mind, along with the other five senses, departs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग येथ अथवा स्वर्गी । जेथ जें देह आपंगी । तेथ तैसेंचि पुढती पांगी । मनादिक॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga yetha athavā svargī | jetha jeṃ deha āpaṃgī | tetha taiseṃci puḍhatī pāṃgī | manādika|| 68||
verses.meaning: Then, whether here (on Earth) or in heaven, whatever body one assumes, there again, the mind and other faculties follow accordingly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा मालवलिया दिवा। प्रभेसि जाय पांडवा। मग उजळिजे तेथ तेधवां। तैसाचि फांके॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā mālavaliyā divā| prabhesi jāya pāṃḍavā| maga ujaḻije tetha tedhavāṃ| taisāci phāṃke||69||
verses.meaning: Just as a lamp, though extinguished, can be rekindled, so too does the divine light manifest itself, O Pandava.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ऐसैसिया राहाटी । अविवेकियांचे दिठी। येतुलें हें किरीटी। गमेंचि गा। ३७०॥ जे आत्मा देहासि आला। आणि विषयो येणेंचि भोगिला । अथवा देहोनि गेला । हें साचचि मानिती ॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī aisaisiyā rāhāṭī | avivekiyāṃce diṭhī| yetuleṃ heṃ kirīṭī| gameṃci gā| 370|| je ātmā dehāsi ālā| āṇi viṣayo yeṇeṃci bhogilā | athavā dehoni gelā | heṃ sācaci mānitī || 71||
verses.meaning: But in such a way of life, to the eyes of the undiscerning, this much, O Kiriti, seems to be true. They truly believe that the soul came into the body and enjoyed worldly pleasures, or that it departed from the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं येणें आणि जाणें । कां करणें हन भोगणे । हें प्रकृतीचें तेणें । मानियेलें॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ yeṇeṃ āṇi jāṇeṃ | kāṃ karaṇeṃ hana bhogaṇe | heṃ prakṛtīceṃ teṇeṃ | māniyeleṃ|| 72||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, this coming and going, or doing and experiencing, is considered by Prakriti (nature) to be its own.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी देहाचें मोटकें उभे। आणि चेतना तेथ उपलभे । तिये चळवळेचेनि लोभें।॥ आला म्हणती ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī dehāceṃ moṭakeṃ ubhe| āṇi cetanā tetha upalabhe | tiye caḻavaḻeceni lobheṃ||| ālā mhaṇatī || 73||
verses.meaning: When a body stands up, and consciousness is perceived within it, then due to the desire for its movement, people say it has come.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंचि तयां संगतीं । इंद्रियें आपुलाल्या अर्थी वर्तती। तया नांव सुभद्रापती। भोगणें जया॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃci tayāṃ saṃgatīṃ | iṃdriyeṃ āpulālyā arthī vartatī| tayā nāṃva subhadrāpatī| bhogaṇeṃ jayā|| 74||
verses.meaning: Similarly, in their company, the senses engage in their respective objects. This is called the 'husband of Subhadra' (a metaphor for the enjoyer), for whom there is enjoyment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं भोगक्षीण आपैसें। देह गेलिया तें न दिसे। तेथें गेला गेळा ऐसें। बोभाती गा॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ bhogakṣīṇa āpaiseṃ| deha geliyā teṃ na dise| tetheṃ gelā geḻā aiseṃ| bobhātī gā|| 75 ||
verses.meaning: When the body, weakened by experiencing its karmic fruits, naturally perishes, it is no longer seen. Then people lament, "He is gone, he is gone!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं रुखु डोलतु देखावा । तरी वारा बाजतु मानावा । रुख नसे तेथें पांडवा । ३६२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी नाहीं तो गा॥७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ rukhu ḍolatu dekhāvā | tarī vārā bājatu mānāvā | rukha nase tetheṃ pāṃḍavā | 362 śrījñāneśvarī nāhīṃ to gā||76||
verses.meaning: When you see a tree swaying, you should understand that the wind is blowing. O Pandava, where there is no tree, there is no wind either, says Shri Dnyaneshwari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां आरिसा समोर ठेविजे। आणि आपणपें तेथ देखिजे। तरी तेधवांचि जालें मानिजे। काय आधीं नाहीं ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ ārisā samora ṭhevije| āṇi āpaṇapeṃ tetha dekhije| tarī tedhavāṃci jāleṃ mānije| kāya ādhīṃ nāhīṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: When a mirror is placed before oneself, and one sees oneself in it, does that mean one did not exist before?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां परता केलिया आरिसा। लोपु जाळा तया आभासा । तरी आपणपें नाहीं ऐसा । निश्चयो करावा ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ paratā keliyā ārisā| lopu jāḻā tayā ābhāsā | tarī āpaṇapeṃ nāhīṃ aisā | niścayo karāvā || 78||
verses.meaning: Or, if one turns away from the mirror, the reflection vanishes. In the same way, one should be certain that the self does not exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शब्द तरी आकाशाचा । परी कपाळीं पिटे मेघाचा । कां चंद्रीं वेगु अभ्राचा। आरोपिजे॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: śabda tarī ākāśācā | parī kapāḻīṃ piṭe meghācā | kāṃ caṃdrīṃ vegu abhrācā| āropije|| 79||
verses.meaning: Just as the sound is of the sky, yet it is attributed to the cloud, or the movement of the clouds is attributed to the moon.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें होइजे जाइजे वेहें। तें आत्मसत्ते अविक्रिये। निष्टंकिती गा मोहें। आंधळे ते॥ ३८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ hoije jāije veheṃ| teṃ ātmasatte avikriye| niṣṭaṃkitī gā moheṃ| āṃdhaḻe te|| 380||
verses.meaning: In the same way, coming and going, which are actions, are attributed to the unchanging power of the Self due to delusion, just as a blind person might stumble.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ आत्मा आत्मयाच्या ठायीं । देखिजे देहींचा धर्मु देहीं । ऐसें देखणें तें पाहीं । आन आहाती ॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha ātmā ātmayācyā ṭhāyīṃ | dekhije dehīṃcā dharmu dehīṃ | aiseṃ dekhaṇeṃ teṃ pāhīṃ | āna āhātī || 81||
verses.meaning: Here, the Self is seen within the Self, and the nature of the body is seen within the body. Such a vision, behold, is unique.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ज्ञानें कां जयाचे डोळे। देखोनि न राहाती देहींचे खोळे । सूर्यरश्‍्मी आणियाळे । ग्रीष्मीं जैसें ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jñāneṃ kāṃ jayāce ḍoḻe| dekhoni na rāhātī dehīṃce khoḻe | sūryaraś‍mī āṇiyāḻe | grīṣmīṃ jaiseṃ || 82||
verses.meaning: Just as the sharp rays of the sun in summer do not allow the body's coverings to remain, so too, knowledge, for those whose eyes are opened by it, does not allow them to remain confined to the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें विवेकाचेनि पैसें। जयांची स्फूर्ती स्वरूपीं बैसे। ते ज्ञानिये देखती ऐसें॥ आत्मयातें॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ vivekāceni paiseṃ| jayāṃcī sphūrtī svarūpīṃ baise| te jñāniye dekhatī aiseṃ|| ātmayāteṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: Just as those whose spiritual inspiration settles in the Self through the expanse of discrimination, such enlightened ones perceive the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें तारागणीं भरलें। गगन समुद्री बिंबलें। परी तें तुटोनि नाहीं पडिलें। ऐसें निवडे। ८४॥ गगन गगनींचि आहे। हें आभासे तें वाये । तैसा आत्मा देखती देहें॥। गंवसिलाही ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ tārāgaṇīṃ bharaleṃ| gagana samudrī biṃbaleṃ| parī teṃ tuṭoni nāhīṃ paḍileṃ| aiseṃ nivaḍe| 84|| gagana gaganīṃci āhe| heṃ ābhāse teṃ vāye | taisā ātmā dekhatī deheṃ||| gaṃvasilāhī || 85||
verses.meaning: Just as the stars are filled in the sky, and the sky is reflected in the ocean, yet it has not fallen or broken away; such is the discernment. The sky remains in the sky; what appears is an illusion. Similarly, the Self is seen as if caught within the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: खळाळाच्या लगबगीं। फेडूनि खळाळाच्या भागीं। देखिजे चंद्रिका कां उगी । चंद्री जेवीं ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: khaḻāḻācyā lagabagīṃ| pheḍūni khaḻāḻācyā bhāgīṃ| dekhije caṃdrikā kāṃ ugī | caṃdrī jevīṃ || 86||
verses.meaning: Just as the moonlight, though appearing to rush and spread, is inherently one with the moon, so too is the true nature of reality. It is not separate from its source, even in its apparent manifestation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां नाडरचि भरे शोषे। सूर्यु तो जैसा तैसाचि असे। देह होतां जातां तैसें । देखती मातें ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ nāḍaraci bhare śoṣe| sūryu to jaisā taisāci ase| deha hotāṃ jātāṃ taiseṃ | dekhatī māteṃ || 87||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun remains as it is, whether the water in a mirage appears or disappears, so too do people perceive Me, even as bodies come and go.

verses.shloka_devanagari: घटु मठु घडले। तेचि पाठीं मोडले) परी आकाश तें संचलें। असतचि असे॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ghaṭu maṭhu ghaḍale| teci pāṭhīṃ moḍale) parī ākāśa teṃ saṃcaleṃ| asataci ase|| 88||
verses.meaning: Pots and monasteries are formed and then destroyed, but the sky remains ever-present and unchanged.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अखंडे आत्मसत्ते। अज्ञानदृष्टिकल्पितें। हें देहचि होतें जातें। जाणती फुडें॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ akhaṃḍe ātmasatte| ajñānadṛṣṭikalpiteṃ| heṃ dehaci hoteṃ jāteṃ| jāṇatī phuḍeṃ|| 89||
verses.meaning: Similarly, by the unbroken power of the Self, what is imagined by the vision of ignorance as this body, is truly understood to be that which comes and goes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चैतन्य चढे ना वोहटे। चेष्टवी ना चेष्टे । ऐसें आत्मज्ञानें चोखटें । जाणती ते॥ ३९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: caitanya caḍhe nā vohaṭe| ceṣṭavī nā ceṣṭe | aiseṃ ātmajñāneṃ cokhaṭeṃ | jāṇatī te|| 390||
verses.meaning: That pure self-knowledge, which neither rises nor falls, and neither acts nor causes action, is understood by those who truly know.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि ज्ञानही आपेतें होईल प्रज्ञा 'परमाणुही उगाणा घेईल। सकळ शास्त्रांचे येईल। सर्वस्व हातां ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jñānahī āpeteṃ hoīla prajñā 'paramāṇuhī ugāṇā gheīla| sakaḻa śāstrāṃce yeīla| sarvasva hātāṃ || 91||
verses.meaning: And knowledge itself will become one's own; wisdom will take even the smallest particle into account. The essence of all scriptures will come into one's hands.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ते व्युत्पत्ति ऐसी। जरी विरक्ति न रिगे मानसीं । तरी सर्वात्मका मजसीं। नव्हेचि भेटी॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī te vyutpatti aisī| jarī virakti na rige mānasīṃ | tarī sarvātmakā majasīṃ| navheci bheṭī||92||
verses.meaning: But such erudition, if detachment does not enter the mind, then there can be no union with Me, the All-Pervading Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं तोंड भरो कां विचारा। आणि अंतःकरणी विषयांसि थारा । तरी नातुर्डे धनुर्धरा । त्रिशुद्धी मी ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ toṃḍa bharo kāṃ vicārā| āṇi aṃtaḥkaraṇī viṣayāṃsi thārā | tarī nāturḍe dhanurdharā | triśuddhī mī || 93||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, if one's mouth is full of contemplation, but their heart still harbors worldly desires, then truly, they will not find Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा बोसणतयाच्या ग्रंथी । काइ तुटती संसारगुंती । कीं परिवसिळिया पोथी । वाचिळी होय ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā bosaṇatayācyā graṃthī | kāi tuṭatī saṃsāraguṃtī | kīṃ parivasiḻiyā pothī | vāciḻī hoya || 94||
verses.meaning: Can the knots of worldly entanglement be untied by merely sitting and reading scriptures? Or does a book become truly read just by being turned over?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना बांधोनियां डोळे। प्राणीं लाविजती मुक्‍ताफळें। तरी तयांचें काय 'कळे । मोल मान ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā bāṃdhoniyāṃ ḍoḻe| prāṇīṃ lāvijatī muk‍tāphaḻeṃ| tarī tayāṃceṃ kāya 'kaḻe | mola māna || 95||
verses.meaning: When pearls are tied to the eyes of creatures, how can they understand their value or worth?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसा चित्तीं अहंते ठावो । आणि जिभे सकळणशास्त्रांचा सराबो। ऐसेनि कोडी एक जन्म जावो) परी न पबिजे मातें॥९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tesā cittīṃ ahaṃte ṭhāvo | āṇi jibhe sakaḻaṇaśāstrāṃcā sarābo| aiseni koḍī eka janma jāvo) parī na pabije māteṃ||96||
verses.meaning: If one's mind is filled with ego, and their tongue is skilled in all scriptures, even if they take countless births, they will not attain Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो एक मी कां समस्तीं। व्यापकु असें भूतजातीं। ऐक तिये व्याप्ती। रूप करूं॥९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo eka mī kāṃ samastīṃ| vyāpaku aseṃ bhūtajātīṃ| aika tiye vyāptī| rūpa karūṃ||97||
verses.meaning: Listen, I shall now describe the form of that pervasiveness, by which I alone pervade all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सूर्यासकट आघवी । हे विश्वरचना जे दावी। ते दीप्ति माझी जाणावी । आद्यंती आहे॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sūryāsakaṭa āghavī | he viśvaracanā je dāvī| te dīpti mājhī jāṇāvī | ādyaṃtī āhe|| 98||
verses.meaning: Know that the entire universe, along with the sun, which is revealed, is my radiance, existing from beginning to end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जळ शोषूनि गेलिया सविता। ओलांश पुरवीतसे जे माघौता। ते चंद्रीं पंडुसुता । ज्योत्स्ना माझी ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaḻa śoṣūni geliyā savitā| olāṃśa puravītase je māghautā| te caṃdrīṃ paṃḍusutā | jyotsnā mājhī || 99||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, just as the sun dries up water, and the moon then replenishes that moisture, so too is my divine light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि 'दहन-पाचनसिद्धी। करीतसे जे निरवधी। ते हुताशीं तेजोवृष्धी । माझीचि गा॥४००॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi 'dahana-pācanasiddhī| karītase je niravadhī| te hutāśīṃ tejovṛṣdhī | mājhīci gā||400||
verses.meaning: And the fire that continuously performs the acts of burning and digesting, in that fire, the increase of its brilliance is also My own manifestation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मी रिगालो असें भूतळीं । म्हणौनि समुद्रमहाजळीं। हे पांसूचि ढेंपुळी । वबिरेचिना॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: mī rigālo aseṃ bhūtaḻīṃ | mhaṇauni samudramahājaḻīṃ| he pāṃsūci ḍheṃpuḻī | vabirecinā|| 1||
verses.meaning: I have entered the world, and therefore, in the great waters of the ocean, these clods of dust do not dissolve.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि भूतेंही चराचरें। हे धरितसे जियें अपारें। तियें मीचि धरीं धरे। रिगोनियां ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi bhūteṃhī carācareṃ| he dharitase jiyeṃ apāreṃ| tiyeṃ mīci dharīṃ dhare| rigoniyāṃ || 2||
verses.meaning: And all beings, moving and unmoving, which are held in countless ways, I alone hold them, having entered into them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गगनीं मी पंडुसुता । चंद्राचेनि मिसें अमृता । भरला जालों चालता । सरोवरु॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: gaganīṃ mī paṃḍusutā | caṃdrāceni miseṃ amṛtā | bharalā jāloṃ cālatā | sarovaru|| 3||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, I have become a moving lake, filled with the nectar of the moon in the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथूनि फांकती रश्मिकर। ते पाट पेळूनि अपार । सर्वौषधींचे आगर। भरित असें मी॥४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tethūni phāṃkatī raśmikara| te pāṭa peḻūni apāra | sarvauṣadhīṃce āgara| bharita aseṃ mī||4||
verses.meaning: From there, rays of light spread out, and those abundant streams, the very source of all medicinal herbs, are filled by me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि सस्यादिकां सकळां। करीं धान्यजाती सुकाळा। हें अन्नद्वारां जिव्हाळा । भूतजातां॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni sasyādikāṃ sakaḻāṃ| karīṃ dhānyajātī sukāḻā| heṃ annadvārāṃ jivhāḻā | bhūtajātāṃ|| 5||
verses.meaning: In this way, the sun makes all kinds of grains, including barley, ripen. Through this food, it becomes the life-force for all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि निपजविलें अन्न। तरी तैसें कैचें दीपन। जेणें जिरूनि समाधान । भोगिती जीव ॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi nipajavileṃ anna| tarī taiseṃ kaiceṃ dīpana| jeṇeṃ jirūni samādhāna | bhogitī jīva ||6||
verses.meaning: And even if food is produced, how can there be such a digestive fire, by which living beings, having digested it, experience contentment?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि प्राणिजातांच्या घटीं । करूनि कंदावरी आगिठी। दीप्ति जठरींही किरीटी । मीचि जालों ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni prāṇijātāṃcyā ghaṭīṃ | karūni kaṃdāvarī āgiṭhī| dīpti jaṭharīṃhī kirīṭī | mīci jāloṃ || 7||
verses.meaning: Therefore, in the bodies of all living beings, by placing the fire of hunger above the root (of sustenance), I alone have become the light within their stomachs, O Kiriti (Arjuna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्राणापानाच्या जोडभातीं। फुंकफुंकोनियां अहोराती । आटीतसें नेणों किती । उदरामाजीं॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: prāṇāpānācyā joḍabhātīṃ| phuṃkaphuṃkoniyāṃ ahorātī | āṭītaseṃ neṇoṃ kitī | udarāmājīṃ|| 8||
verses.meaning: Through the bellows of prana and apana, blowing day and night, I know not how much is being consumed within the belly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शुष्कें अथवा स्निग्धें। सुपक्वें कां विदग्धें। परी मीचि गा चतुर्विधें। अन्ने पचीं ॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: śuṣkeṃ athavā snigdheṃ| supakveṃ kāṃ vidagdheṃ| parī mīci gā caturvidheṃ| anne pacīṃ ||9||
verses.meaning: Whether dry or oily, well-cooked or burnt, I alone digest all four kinds of food.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं मीचि आधवबें जन। जना निरवितें मीचि जीवन। जीवनीं मुख्य साधन। वन्हिही मीचि॥ ४१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ mīci ādhavabeṃ jana| janā niraviteṃ mīci jīvana| jīvanīṃ mukhya sādhana| vanhihī mīci|| 410||
verses.meaning: Thus, I am indeed the support for all people, and I am the life that sustains them. I am the primary means within that life, and I am also the fire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ऐसियाहीवरी काई । सांगों व्याप्तीची नवाई । येथ दुजें ३६४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी नाहींचि घेई । सर्वत्र मी गा॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ aisiyāhīvarī kāī | sāṃgoṃ vyāptīcī navāī | yetha dujeṃ 364 śrījñāneśvarī nāhīṃci gheī | sarvatra mī gā|| 11||
verses.meaning: Now, what more can I say about the pervasiveness (of the Self)? Understand that there is no other here; I am indeed everywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कैसेनि पां वेखें। सदा सुखियें एकें । एकें तियें बहुदुःखें। क्रांत भूतें ॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī kaiseni pāṃ vekheṃ| sadā sukhiyeṃ ekeṃ | ekeṃ tiyeṃ bahuduḥkheṃ| krāṃta bhūteṃ || 92||
verses.meaning: How is it then that some beings are always happy, while others are afflicted by much sorrow?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी सगळिये पाटणीं । एकेंचि दीपें दिवेळलावणी। जालिया कां न देखणीं। उरलीं एकें॥१३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī sagaḻiye pāṭaṇīṃ | ekeṃci dīpeṃ diveḻalāvaṇī| jāliyā kāṃ na dekhaṇīṃ| uralīṃ ekeṃ||13||
verses.meaning: Just as in an entire city, when one lamp is lit, all other lamps are not needed, for they are already illuminated by that single light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी हन उखिविखी। करित आहासी मानसीं कौं। तरी परिस तेही निकी। शंका फेडू॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī hana ukhivikhī| karita āhāsī mānasīṃ kauṃ| tarī parisa tehī nikī| śaṃkā pheḍū|| 14||
verses.meaning: Are you, then, thus pondering in your mind? If so, listen carefully, and I shall resolve that doubt as well.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आघवा मीचि असें। येथ नाहीं कौर अनारिसें। परी प्राणियांचिया उल्लासें। बुद्धि ऐसा॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ āghavā mīci aseṃ| yetha nāhīṃ kaura anāriseṃ| parī prāṇiyāṃciyā ullāseṃ| buddhi aisā|| 15||
verses.meaning: Indeed, I alone am everything. There is nothing here that is different. But for the joy of beings, I appear as intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें एकच्चि आकाशध्वनी। वाद्यविशेषीं आनानीं । वाजावें पडे भिन्नीं । नादांतरीं ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ ekacci ākāśadhvanī| vādyaviśeṣīṃ ānānīṃ | vājāveṃ paḍe bhinnīṃ | nādāṃtarīṃ || 16||
verses.meaning: Just as a single sound from the sky, through various musical instruments, must be played in different tunes and melodies.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां लोकचेष्टीं वेगळाला । जो हा एकुचि भानु उदेला । तो आनानी परी गेला । उपयोगासी ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ lokaceṣṭīṃ vegaḻālā | jo hā ekuci bhānu udelā | to ānānī parī gelā | upayogāsī || 17||
verses.meaning: Just as the one sun, having risen, serves various purposes for people's different activities, so too is the divine light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना बीजधर्मानुरूप। झाडीं उपजविलें आप। तैसें परिणमलें स्वरूप । माझें जीवां॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā bījadharmānurūpa| jhāḍīṃ upajavileṃ āpa| taiseṃ pariṇamaleṃ svarūpa | mājheṃ jīvāṃ|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as a forest is born from various seeds according to their nature, so too has My form manifested in all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा नेणा आणि चतुरा । पुढां निळयांचा दुसरा । नेणा सर्पत्वें जाला येरा। सुखालागीं॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā neṇā āṇi caturā | puḍhāṃ niḻayāṃcā dusarā | neṇā sarpatveṃ jālā yerā| sukhālāgīṃ|| 19||
verses.meaning: Oh, ignorant and wise! The second of the blue-throated ones (Lord Shiva) became a serpent for the sake of bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो स्वातीचें उदक। शुक्तीं मोतीं व्याळीं विख। तैसा सज्ञानांसी मी सुख। दुःख तों अज्ञानांसी॥ ४२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso svātīceṃ udaka| śuktīṃ motīṃ vyāḻīṃ vikha| taisā sajñānāṃsī mī sukha| duḥkha toṃ ajñānāṃsī|| 420||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Just as the Swati nakshatra's rainwater becomes a pearl in an oyster and poison in a snake, so too am I happiness for the wise and sorrow for the ignorant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं सर्वांच्या हृदयदेशीं। मी अमुका आहें ऐसी । जे बुद्धि स्फुरे अहर्निशीं। ते वस्तु गा मी॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ sarvāṃcyā hṛdayadeśīṃ| mī amukā āheṃ aisī | je buddhi sphure aharniśīṃ| te vastu gā mī|| 21||
verses.meaning: Indeed, that very essence which continuously manifests as 'I am this' in the hearts of all beings, that indeed am I.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी संतांसवें वसतां। योगज्ञानीं पैसतां । गुरुचरण उपासितां। वैराग्येंसी ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī saṃtāṃsaveṃ vasatāṃ| yogajñānīṃ paisatāṃ | gurucaraṇa upāsitāṃ| vairāgyeṃsī || 22||
verses.meaning: By residing with saints, by entering into the knowledge of Yoga, and by serving the Guru's feet, one attains dispassion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणेंचि सत्कर्मे। अशेषही अज्ञान विरमे। जयांचें अहं विश्रामे। आत्मरूपीं ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃci satkarme| aśeṣahī ajñāna virame| jayāṃceṃ ahaṃ viśrāme| ātmarūpīṃ || 23||
verses.meaning: Through such good deeds, all ignorance ceases, and their ego finds rest in the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते आपेआप देखोनि देखीं। मियां आत्मेनि सदा सुखी । येथें मीवांचून अवलोकीं। आन हेतु असे॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: te āpeāpa dekhoni dekhīṃ| miyāṃ ātmeni sadā sukhī | yetheṃ mīvāṃcūna avalokīṃ| āna hetu ase|| 24||
verses.meaning: Seeing myself, I am always happy in my soul. Is there any other purpose here besides me?

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा सूर्योदयो जालिया । सूर्ये सूर्यचचि पहावा धनंजया । तेवीं मातें मियां जाणावया। मीचि हेतु॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā sūryodayo jāliyā | sūrye sūryacaci pahāvā dhanaṃjayā | tevīṃ māteṃ miyāṃ jāṇāvayā| mīci hetu|| 25||
verses.meaning: Just as when the sun rises, the sun itself is the means by which the sun is seen, so too, to know Me, I alone am the means, O Dhananjaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना शरीरपरातें सेवितां। संसारगौरवचि ऐकतां। देहीं जयांची अहंता । बुडोनि ठेळी॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā śarīraparāteṃ sevitāṃ| saṃsāragauravaci aikatāṃ| dehīṃ jayāṃcī ahaṃtā | buḍoni ṭheḻī|| 26||
verses.meaning: They do not serve the body, nor do they listen to worldly glories. Their ego, rooted in the body, remains submerged.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते स्वर्गसंसारालागीं। धांवतां कर्ममार्गी । दुःखाच्या सेळभागीं । विभागी होती ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te svargasaṃsārālāgīṃ| dhāṃvatāṃ karmamārgī | duḥkhācyā seḻabhāgīṃ | vibhāgī hotī || 27||
verses.meaning: They, who run on the path of karma for the sake of heavenly pleasures, become partakers in the sorrowful consequences.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हेंही होणें अर्जुना । मजचिस्तव तया अज्ञाना । जैसा जागताचि हेतु स्वप्ना । निद्रेतें होय॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃhī hoṇeṃ arjunā | majacistava tayā ajñānā | jaisā jāgatāci hetu svapnā | nidreteṃ hoya|| 28||
verses.meaning: But Arjuna, even this ignorance arises from Me, just as the waking state is the cause of a dream in sleep.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं अभ्रे दिवसु हरपला । तोहि दिवसेंचि जाणों आला । तेवीं मी नेणोनि विषयो देखिला । मजचिस्तव भूती ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ abhre divasu harapalā | tohi divaseṃci jāṇoṃ ālā | tevīṃ mī neṇoni viṣayo dekhilā | majacistava bhūtī || 29||
verses.meaning: Just as the clouds obscure the day, yet the day itself reveals them, so too, I, unknowingly, perceived the world of objects, which exists only because of me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं निद्रा कां जागणिया । प्रबोधुचि हेतु धनंजया । तेवीं ज्ञाना अज्ञाना जीवांचिया। मीचि मूळ ॥ ४३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ nidrā kāṃ jāgaṇiyā | prabodhuci hetu dhanaṃjayā | tevīṃ jñānā ajñānā jīvāṃciyā| mīci mūḻa || 430||
verses.meaning: Just as sleep and waking are both rooted in consciousness, so too am I the origin of both knowledge and ignorance in all beings, O Dhananjaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें सर्पत्वा कां दोरा। दोरुूचि मूळ धनुर्धरा। तैसा ज्ञाना अज्ञानाचिया संसारा । मियांचि सिऱ्धु॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ sarpatvā kāṃ dorā| doruūci mūḻa dhanurdharā| taisā jñānā ajñānāciyā saṃsārā | miyāṃci siṟdhu|| 31||
verses.meaning: Just as the snake is merely a rope, O Arjuna, so too am I the root of both knowledge and ignorance in this world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जैसा असें तैसया । मातें नेणोनि धनंजया । वेदु जाणों गेला तंव तया । जालिया शाखा॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jaisā aseṃ taisayā | māteṃ neṇoni dhanaṃjayā | vedu jāṇoṃ gelā taṃva tayā | jāliyā śākhā|| 32||
verses.meaning: Therefore, just as I am, not knowing Me, O Dhananjaya, when the Vedas tried to know Me, they became My branches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तिहीं शाखाभेदीं । मीचि जाणिजे त्रिशुद्धी । जैसा पूर्वापरा नदी । समुद्रचि ठी॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tihīṃ śākhābhedīṃ | mīci jāṇije triśuddhī | jaisā pūrvāparā nadī | samudraci ṭhī|| 33||
verses.meaning: Yet, in all three branches, know that I alone am the pure truth. Just as all rivers, from east to west, ultimately merge into the ocean.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि महासिद्धांतापासीं। श्रुति हारपती शब्देंसीं । जैसिया सगंधा आकाशीं। वातलहरी॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mahāsiddhāṃtāpāsīṃ| śruti hārapatī śabdeṃsīṃ | jaisiyā sagaṃdhā ākāśīṃ| vātalaharī|| 34||
verses.meaning: And at the ultimate truth, the Vedas themselves lose their words, just as fragrant breezes dissolve into the vast sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें समस्तही श्रृतिजात। ठाके लाजिलें ऐसें निवांत। तें मीचि करीं यथावत। प्रकटोनियां॥ ३५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ samastahī śrṛtijāta| ṭhāke lājileṃ aiseṃ nivāṃta| teṃ mīci karīṃ yathāvata| prakaṭoniyāṃ|| 35 ||
verses.meaning: In the same way, all the scriptures, as if ashamed, remain silent. I myself reveal them perfectly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं श्रुतीसहित अशेष। जग हारपे जेथ निःशेष। तें निजज्ञानही चोख । जाणता मीचि ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ śrutīsahita aśeṣa| jaga hārape jetha niḥśeṣa| teṃ nijajñānahī cokha | jāṇatā mīci || 36||
verses.meaning: Where all the worlds, along with the Vedas, completely dissolve, know that I alone am that pure Self-knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें निदेलिया जागिजे । तेव्हां स्वप्नींचें कीर नाहीं दुजें । परी 'एकत्वही देखों पाविजे। आपलेंचि॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ nideliyā jāgije | tevhāṃ svapnīṃceṃ kīra nāhīṃ dujeṃ | parī 'ekatvahī dekhoṃ pāvije| āpaleṃci|| 37||
verses.meaning: Just as when one awakens from sleep, the dream world ceases to exist as a separate entity, yet one realizes their own oneness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें आपलें अट्ठयपण। मी जाणतसें दुजेनवीण। तयाही बोधाकारण | जाणता मीचि॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ āpaleṃ aṭṭhayapaṇa| mī jāṇataseṃ dujenavīṇa| tayāhī bodhākāraṇa | jāṇatā mīci|| 38||
verses.meaning: Just as my own inherent nature, I know without any duality. And for the very understanding of that nature, I am the knower.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आगी 'लागलिया कापुरा। ना काजळी ना वैश्वानरा । उरणें नाहीं वीरा । जयापरी ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga āgī 'lāgaliyā kāpurā| nā kājaḻī nā vaiśvānarā | uraṇeṃ nāhīṃ vīrā | jayāparī || 39||
verses.meaning: Just as camphor, once ignited, leaves no soot nor any remnant of the fire itself, so too is the complete annihilation of the ego.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं समूळ अविद्या खाये। तें ज्ञानही जैं बुडोनि जाये। तऱही नाहीं कौर नोहे । आणि न साहे असणेंही ॥ ४४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ samūḻa avidyā khāye| teṃ jñānahī jaiṃ buḍoni jāye| taṟahī nāhīṃ kaura nohe | āṇi na sāhe asaṇeṃhī || 440||
verses.meaning: In the same way, when ignorance is completely consumed, and even that knowledge itself dissolves, then there is no 'is' or 'is not,' nor can there be any 'being.'

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं विश्‍व घेऊनि गेला मागेंसीं । तया चोरातें कवण कें गिवसी। जे कोणी एकी दशा ऐसी शुद्ध ते मी॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ viś‍va gheūni gelā māgeṃsīṃ | tayā corāteṃ kavaṇa keṃ givasī| je koṇī ekī daśā aisī śuddha te mī|| 41||
verses.meaning: When the universe is taken away, who can find that thief? For I am that pure, singular state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी जडाजडव्याप्ती। रूप करितां कैवल्यपती। ठी केली निरुपहितीं। आपुल्या रूपीं ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī jaḍājaḍavyāptī| rūpa karitāṃ kaivalyapatī| ṭhī kelī nirupahitīṃ| āpulyā rūpīṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: Thus, the Lord of Kaivalya, by assuming a form that pervades both the inert and the conscious, established His unconditioned nature within His own being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो आघवाचि बोधु सहसा । अर्जुनी उमटला कैसा । व्योमींचा चंद्रोदयो जैसा । क्षीरार्णवीं॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: to āghavāci bodhu sahasā | arjunī umaṭalā kaisā | vyomīṃcā caṃdrodayo jaisā | kṣīrārṇavīṃ|| 43||
verses.meaning: Suddenly, all that knowledge manifested in Arjuna, like the moonrise in the ocean of milk.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां प्रतिभिंतीं चोखटें । समोरील चित्र उमटे । तैसा अर्जुनें आणि वैकुंठें। नांदतसे बोधु॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ pratibhiṃtīṃ cokhaṭeṃ | samorīla citra umaṭe | taisā arjuneṃ āṇi vaikuṃṭheṃ| nāṃdatase bodhu|| 44||
verses.meaning: Just as a clear image is reflected on a clean wall, so too does the spiritual wisdom (bodha) reside between Arjuna and the Lord of Vaikuntha (Krishna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी बाप वस्तुस्वभावो। फावे तंब तंव गोडिये थांवो। म्हणौनि अनुभवियांचा रावो । अर्जुन म्हणे ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī bāpa vastusvabhāvo| phāve taṃba taṃva goḍiye thāṃvo| mhaṇauni anubhaviyāṃcā rāvo | arjuna mhaṇe || 45||
verses.meaning: However, the very nature of the thing is such that the more one experiences it, the sweeter it becomes. Therefore, Arjuna, the king among experiencers, said.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी व्यापकपण बोलतां । निरुपाधिक जें आतां। स्वरूप प्रसंगता। बोलिले देवो॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī vyāpakapaṇa bolatāṃ | nirupādhika jeṃ ātāṃ| svarūpa prasaṃgatā| bolile devo|| 46||
verses.meaning: That which is spoken of as all-pervading, that which is now unconditioned, that very nature was spoken of by the Lord in this context.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें एक वेळ अव्यंगवाणें। कौजो कां मज कारणें । तेथ द्वारकेचा नाथु म्हणे। भलें केलें॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ eka veḻa avyaṃgavāṇeṃ| kaujo kāṃ maja kāraṇeṃ | tetha dvārakecā nāthu mhaṇe| bhaleṃ keleṃ|| 47||
verses.meaning: Then, at one point, with flawless words, he said, "Why do you trouble yourself for my sake?" There, the Lord of Dwarka said, "You have done well."

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं अर्जुना आम्हांहि वाडेकोडें। अखंड बोलो आवडे | परी काय कौजे न जोडे । पुसतें ऐसें ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ arjunā āmhāṃhi vāḍekoḍeṃ| akhaṃḍa bolo āvaḍe | parī kāya kauje na joḍe | pusateṃ aiseṃ || 48||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, it would please Me greatly to speak endlessly, but what is the use if there is no one to ask such questions?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आजि मनोरथांसि फळ। जोडलासि तूं केवळ। जे तोंड भरूनि ३६६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी निखळ । आलासि पुसों॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āji manorathāṃsi phaḻa| joḍalāsi tūṃ kevaḻa| je toṃḍa bharūni 366 śrījñāneśvarī nikhaḻa | ālāsi pusoṃ|| 49||
verses.meaning: Today, the fruit of my desires has been attained, for you have come to inquire, with a full heart, about the pure Dnyaneshwari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें अद्वैतावरीही भोगिजे। तें अनुभवींच तूं बिरजें। पुसोनि मज माझें । देतासि सुख॥ ४५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ advaitāvarīhī bhogije| teṃ anubhavīṃca tūṃ birajeṃ| pusoni maja mājheṃ | detāsi sukha|| 450||
verses.meaning: That which is experienced even beyond non-duality, you yourself experience that. By asking me, you give me joy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा आरिसा आलिया जवळां। दिसे आपणपे आपला डोळा । तैसा संवादिया तूं निर्मळा । शिरोमणी ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā ārisā āliyā javaḻāṃ| dise āpaṇape āpalā ḍoḻā | taisā saṃvādiyā tūṃ nirmaḻā | śiromaṇī || 51||
verses.meaning: Just as one's own eye sees itself when it comes near a mirror, so too are you, the pure speaker, a crest-jewel.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तुवां नेणोनि पुसावे । मग आम्ही परिसऊं बैसावें। तो गा हा पाडु नव्हे। सोयरेया॥५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tuvāṃ neṇoni pusāve | maga āmhī parisaūṃ baisāveṃ| to gā hā pāḍu navhe| soyareyā||52||
verses.meaning: You should not ask out of ignorance, and then we should sit and listen. O friend, this is not the proper way.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें म्हणौनि आलिंगिळें। कृपादृष्टी अवबलोकिलें। मग देवो काय बोलिले। अर्जुनेंसीं ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ mhaṇauni āliṃgiḻeṃ| kṛpādṛṣṭī avabalokileṃ| maga devo kāya bolile| arjuneṃsīṃ || 53||
verses.meaning: Having said this, He embraced him and looked upon him with a compassionate gaze. Then what did the Lord say to Arjuna?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं दोहीं बोठीं एक बोलणें । दोहीं चरणीं एक चालणें । तैसें पुसणें सांगणें । तुझें माझें ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ dohīṃ boṭhīṃ eka bolaṇeṃ | dohīṃ caraṇīṃ eka cālaṇeṃ | taiseṃ pusaṇeṃ sāṃgaṇeṃ | tujheṃ mājheṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: Just as two lips speak as one, and two feet walk as one, so too is our questioning and answering, yours and mine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं आम्हीं तुम्हीं येथें । देखावे एका अर्थातें। सांगतें पुसतें येथें । दोन्हीं एक ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ āmhīṃ tumhīṃ yetheṃ | dekhāve ekā arthāteṃ| sāṃgateṃ pusateṃ yetheṃ | donhīṃ eka || 55||
verses.meaning: Thus, you and I here, perceive a single meaning. The speaker and the listener here are both one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा बोलत देवो भुलला मोहें। अर्जुनातें आलिंगूनि ठाये । मग बिहाला म्हणे नोहें। आवडी हे ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā bolata devo bhulalā moheṃ| arjunāteṃ āliṃgūni ṭhāye | maga bihālā mhaṇe noheṃ| āvaḍī he || 56||
verses.meaning: Speaking thus, the Lord was overcome with affection. He embraced Arjuna and then, realizing the intensity of His love, He became somewhat apprehensive, thinking, "This is not merely affection, but profound love."

verses.shloka_devanagari: जाले इक्षुरसाचें ढाळ। तरी लवण देणें किडाळ। जे संवादसुखाचें रसाळ। नासेल थितें ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāle ikṣurasāceṃ ḍhāḻa| tarī lavaṇa deṇeṃ kiḍāḻa| je saṃvādasukhāceṃ rasāḻa| nāsela thiteṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: If sugarcane juice is poured, adding salt to it would be detrimental. Similarly, adding anything that spoils the sweet essence of spiritual discourse would be destructive to its very foundation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधींच आम्हां यया कांहीं । नरनारायणासी भिन्न नाहीं। परी आतां जिरो माझ्या ठाई। वेगु हा माझा॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhīṃca āmhāṃ yayā kāṃhīṃ | naranārāyaṇāsī bhinna nāhīṃ| parī ātāṃ jiro mājhyā ṭhāī| vegu hā mājhā|| 58||
verses.meaning: Indeed, there is no difference between us and Narayana. But now, let this separation of mine dissolve within me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इया बुद्धी सहसा । श्रीकृष्ण म्हणे वीरेशा । पैं गा तो तुवां कैसा । प्रश्‍नु केला ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: iyā buddhī sahasā | śrīkṛṣṇa mhaṇe vīreśā | paiṃ gā to tuvāṃ kaisā | praś‍nu kelā || 59||
verses.meaning: Lord Krishna said, "O Arjuna, how did such a question arise in your mind?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो अर्जुन श्रीकृष्णीं विरत होता । तो परतोनि मागुता । प्रश्‍नाबळीची कथा । ऐको आला॥ ४६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo arjuna śrīkṛṣṇīṃ virata hotā | to paratoni māgutā | praś‍nābaḻīcī kathā | aiko ālā|| 460||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, who was absorbed in Krishna, returned to listen to the story of the questions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ सद्गदें बोलें। अर्जुनें जी जी म्हणितलें। निरुपाधिक आपुलें। रूप सांगा ॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha sadgadeṃ boleṃ| arjuneṃ jī jī mhaṇitaleṃ| nirupādhika āpuleṃ| rūpa sāṃgā ||61||
verses.meaning: Here, with a choked voice, Arjuna pleaded, "Please reveal Your true, unconditioned form."

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया बोला तो शार्डी। तेंचि सांगावयालागीं। उपाधी दोहीं भागीं। निरूपीत असे ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā bolā to śārḍī| teṃci sāṃgāvayālāgīṃ| upādhī dohīṃ bhāgīṃ| nirūpīta ase || 62||
verses.meaning: To explain this very point, He (the Lord) describes the limiting adjuncts (upadhis) in both aspects (the individual and the universal).

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुसिलिया निरुपहित । उपाधि कां सांगे येथ । हें कोण्हाही प्रस्तुत । गमे जरी॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: pusiliyā nirupahita | upādhi kāṃ sāṃge yetha | heṃ koṇhāhī prastuta | game jarī|| 63||
