verses.meaning: If it is said that the unconditioned is pure, then what is the need to speak of conditions here? Even if this seems to anyone to be the case.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी ताकाचें अंश फेडणें। याची नांव लोणी काढणें। चोखाचिये शुद्धी तोडणें। किडचि जेवीं ॥६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tākāceṃ aṃśa pheḍaṇeṃ| yācī nāṃva loṇī kāḍhaṇeṃ| cokhāciye śuddhī toḍaṇeṃ| kiḍaci jevīṃ ||64||
verses.meaning: Just as removing the watery part from buttermilk is called churning butter, and purifying gold means removing its impurities, so too is the process of spiritual refinement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बाबुळीचि सारावी हातें । परी पाणी तंव असे आइतें। अभ्रचि जावें गगन तें। सिद्धचि कों॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: bābuḻīci sārāvī hāteṃ | parī pāṇī taṃva ase āiteṃ| abhraci jāveṃ gagana teṃ| siddhaci koṃ|| 65||
verses.meaning: One may clear away the moss from the water with their hands, but the water itself is already there, ready. Similarly, the clouds may depart, but the sky remains, inherently perfect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरील कोंडियाचा गुंडाळा। झाडूनि केलिया वेगळा । कणु घेतां विरंगोळा। असे काई ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: varīla koṃḍiyācā guṃḍāḻā| jhāḍūni keliyā vegaḻā | kaṇu ghetāṃ viraṃgoḻā| ase kāī || 66||
verses.meaning: When the husk is separated from the grain, does the grain then feel any separation anxiety?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा उपाधि उपहितां। शेवटु जेथ विचारितां। तें कोणातेंही न पुसतां। निरुपाधिक ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā upādhi upahitāṃ| śevaṭu jetha vicāritāṃ| teṃ koṇāteṃhī na pusatāṃ| nirupādhika || 67||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when one inquires into the ultimate end of the conditioned self, it is found to be unconditioned, without needing to ask anyone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें न सांगणेवरी। बाळा पतीसी रूप करी। बोल निमालेपणें विवरी। अचर्चातें॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ na sāṃgaṇevarī| bāḻā patīsī rūpa karī| bola nimālepaṇeṃ vivarī| acarcāteṃ|| 68||
verses.meaning: Just as a child, without being told, assumes the form of its father, so too does the inexpressible truth reveal itself when words cease, contemplating the inconceivable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सांगणेया जोगें नव्हे। तेथिंचें सांगणें ऐसें आहे। म्हणौनि उपाधि लक्ष्मीनाहे। बोलिजे आदीं ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ sāṃgaṇeyā jogeṃ navhe| tethiṃceṃ sāṃgaṇeṃ aiseṃ āhe| mhaṇauni upādhi lakṣmīnāhe| bolije ādīṃ || 69||
verses.meaning: That which is beyond description, its nature is such that it cannot be spoken of. Therefore, the primordial cause, the source of all manifestation, is spoken of as the consort of Lakshmi, the divine energy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाडिव्याची चंद्रेरेखा । निरुती दाबावया शाखा । दाविजे तेवीं औपाधिका। बोली इया॥ ४७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāḍivyācī caṃdrerekhā | nirutī dābāvayā śākhā | dāvije tevīṃ aupādhikā| bolī iyā|| 470||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon's crescent is shown by pointing to a branch, similarly, the Absolute Truth is indicated through these conditional words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तो म्हणे गा सव्यसाची । पैं इये संसारपाटणींची । बस्ती साविया टांची । दुपुरुषीं ॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga to mhaṇe gā savyasācī | paiṃ iye saṃsārapāṭaṇīṃcī | bastī sāviyā ṭāṃcī | dupuruṣīṃ || 71||
verses.meaning: Then he said, O Arjuna, this worldly town is populated by two kinds of people, the good and the bad.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी आघवांचि गगनीं। नांदत दिवोरात्री दोन्ही । तैसे संसार राजधानीं । दोन्हीचि हे ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī āghavāṃci gaganīṃ| nāṃdata divorātrī donhī | taise saṃsāra rājadhānīṃ | donhīci he || 72||
verses.meaning: Just as day and night both exist throughout the entire sky, so too are these two (joy and sorrow) present in the capital city of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिकही तिजा पुरुषु आहे। परी तो या दोहींचें नांव न साहे। जो उदेला गांबेंसीं खाये। दोहींतें ययां॥७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇikahī tijā puruṣu āhe| parī to yā dohīṃceṃ nāṃva na sāhe| jo udelā gāṃbeṃsīṃ khāye| dohīṃteṃ yayāṃ||73||
verses.meaning: There is yet a third Purusha, but He does not bear the names of these two. He arises and consumes both of them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी ते तंव गोठी असो। आधीं दोन्हींची हे परियेसों। जें संसारग्रामा वसो । आळे असती ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī te taṃva goṭhī aso| ādhīṃ donhīṃcī he pariyesoṃ| jeṃ saṃsāragrāmā vaso | āḻe asatī || 74||
verses.meaning: But let that discussion be for later. First, let us understand the nature of both, which are the boundaries of the village of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक आंधळा वेडा पंगु । येर सर्वागें पुरता चांगु । परी ग्रामगुणें संगु।| घडला दोघां ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka āṃdhaḻā veḍā paṃgu | yera sarvāgeṃ puratā cāṃgu | parī grāmaguṇeṃ saṃgu|| ghaḍalā doghāṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: One blind, one mad, one lame; the other, though perfect in every limb, yet due to the village's nature, companionship arose between the two.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया एका नाम क्षरु । येरातें म्हणती अक्षरु। इहीं दोहींचि परी संसारु। कोंदला असे॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā ekā nāma kṣaru | yerāteṃ mhaṇatī akṣaru| ihīṃ dohīṃci parī saṃsāru| koṃdalā ase|| 76||
verses.meaning: That one name is called perishable, and the other imperishable. The entire world is filled with these two.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां क्षर तो कवणु । अक्षरु तो किंलक्षणु। हा अभिप्रायो संपूर्ण । विवंचूं गा॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ kṣara to kavaṇu | akṣaru to kiṃlakṣaṇu| hā abhiprāyo saṃpūrṇa | vivaṃcūṃ gā|| 77||
verses.meaning: Now, what is this 'Kshara' (perishable)? And what are the characteristics of 'Akshara' (imperishable)? Let us thoroughly deliberate on this profound subject.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी महदहंकारा-। लागुनियां धनुर्धरा । तृणांतींचा पांगोरा-। वरी पैं गा॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī mahadahaṃkārā-| lāguniyāṃ dhanurdharā | tṛṇāṃtīṃcā pāṃgorā-| varī paiṃ gā|| 78||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, the great ego, like a tiny speck of dust, is carried away by the wind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें कांहीं सानें थोर। चालतें अथवा स्थिर। किंबहुना गोचर । मनबुद्धींसि जें॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ kāṃhīṃ sāneṃ thora| cālateṃ athavā sthira| kiṃbahunā gocara | manabuddhīṃsi jeṃ|| 79||
verses.meaning: Whatever is small or large, moving or still, or rather, whatever is perceptible to the mind and intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेतुलें पांचभौतिक घडतें। जें नामरूपा सांपडतें । गुणत्रयाच्या पडतें। कामठां जें ॥ ४८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetuleṃ pāṃcabhautika ghaḍateṃ| jeṃ nāmarūpā sāṃpaḍateṃ | guṇatrayācyā paḍateṃ| kāmaṭhāṃ jeṃ || 480||
verses.meaning: That which is formed from the five elements, that which is caught in name and form, and that which falls under the sway of the three Gunas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भूताकृतीचें नाणें। घडत भांगारें जेणें काळासि जूं खेळणें। जिहीं कवडां॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhūtākṛtīceṃ nāṇeṃ| ghaḍata bhāṃgāreṃ jeṇeṃ kāḻāsi jūṃ kheḻaṇeṃ| jihīṃ kavaḍāṃ|| 81||
verses.meaning: The coin of all beings, made from the gold of time, with which the game of dice is played, these are the cowries.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जाणणेंचि विपरितें। जें जें कांहीं जाणिजेतें। जें प्रतिक्षणीं निमतें । होऊनियां ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jāṇaṇeṃci vipariteṃ| jeṃ jeṃ kāṃhīṃ jāṇijeteṃ| jeṃ pratikṣaṇīṃ nimateṃ | hoūniyāṃ || 82||
verses.meaning: Whatever is known, that which is known to be contrary, that which perishes every moment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा काढूनि भ्रांतीचें दांग। उभवी सृष्टीचें आंग । हें असो बहु जग। जया नाम॥८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā kāḍhūni bhrāṃtīceṃ dāṃga| ubhavī sṛṣṭīceṃ āṃga | heṃ aso bahu jaga| jayā nāma||83||
verses.meaning: Indeed, by removing the illusion's veil, the body of creation is established. Let this be the vast world, to which He is the name.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं अष्टधा भिन्न ऐसें। जें दाविलें प्रकृतिमिसें । जें क्षेत्रद्वारां छत्तिसें। भागी केलें॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ aṣṭadhā bhinna aiseṃ| jeṃ dāvileṃ prakṛtimiseṃ | jeṃ kṣetradvārāṃ chattiseṃ| bhāgī keleṃ|| 84||
verses.meaning: Thus, the eightfold differentiated nature, which was revealed through the guise of Prakriti, was divided into thirty-six parts through the gateway of the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें मागील सांगों किती। अगा आतांचि जें प्रस्तुती । वृक्षाकार रूपाकृती। निरूपिलें॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ māgīla sāṃgoṃ kitī| agā ātāṃci jeṃ prastutī | vṛkṣākāra rūpākṛtī| nirūpileṃ|| 85||
verses.meaning: Why should I elaborate on what has been said before? Just now, I have described the form of the tree.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें आधवेंचि साकारें। कल्पुनी आपणपयां पुरे। जाळें असें तदनुसारें। चैतन्यचि ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ ādhaveṃci sākāreṃ| kalpunī āpaṇapayāṃ pure| jāḻeṃ aseṃ tadanusāreṃ| caitanyaci || 86||
verses.meaning: That very primal, formless consciousness, by imagining itself, becomes sufficient unto itself, and accordingly, it is a net of pure consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा कुहां आपणचि बिंबे। सिंह प्रतिबिंब पाहतां क्षोभे। मग क्षोभला समारंभें। घाली तेथ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā kuhāṃ āpaṇaci biṃbe| siṃha pratibiṃba pāhatāṃ kṣobhe| maga kṣobhalā samāraṃbheṃ| ghālī tetha|| 87||
verses.meaning: Just as a lion, seeing its own reflection in a well, becomes enraged, and in its fury, attacks the image there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां सलिलीं असतचि असे। व्योमावरी व्योम बिंबे जेसें। अद्वैत होऊनि तैसें। ह्वैते घेपे ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ salilīṃ asataci ase| vyomāvarī vyoma biṃbe jeseṃ| advaita hoūni taiseṃ| hvaite ghepe || 88||
verses.meaning: Just as water exists within water, and the sky is reflected in the sky, so too is the non-dual (Advaita) embraced and absorbed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना गा यापरी । साकार कल्पूनि पुरीं। आत्मा विस्मृतीची करी। निद्रा तेथ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā gā yāparī | sākāra kalpūni purīṃ| ātmā vismṛtīcī karī| nidrā tetha|| 89||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, in this way, by conceiving a complete form, the Self (Atman) enters into a sleep of forgetfulness there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं स्वप्नीं सेजार देखिजे। मग पहुडणें जैसें तेथ कौजे। तैसें पुरी शयन देखिजे। आत्मयासी ॥ ४९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ svapnīṃ sejāra dekhije| maga pahuḍaṇeṃ jaiseṃ tetha kauje| taiseṃ purī śayana dekhije| ātmayāsī || 490||
verses.meaning: Just as one sees a bed in a dream and then lies down on it, so too does the soul perceive the body as its resting place.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं तिये निद्रेचेनि ३६८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी भरें। मी सुखी दुःखी म्हणत घोरें। अहंममतेचेनि थोरें। बोसणायें सादें॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ tiye nidreceni 368 śrījñāneśvarī bhareṃ| mī sukhī duḥkhī mhaṇata ghoreṃ| ahaṃmamateceni thoreṃ| bosaṇāyeṃ sādeṃ||91||
verses.meaning: In the grip of that sleep, I snore, saying 'I am happy, I am sad,' with the great wailing of ego and possessiveness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा जनकु हे माता। हा मी गौर हीन पुरता । पुत्र वित्त कांता। माझें हें ना॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā janaku he mātā| hā mī gaura hīna puratā | putra vitta kāṃtā| mājheṃ heṃ nā||92||
verses.meaning: This is my father, this is my mother. I am a mere, insignificant son. This wealth and wife are not mine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसिया वेंघोनि स्वप्ना। धांवत भवस्वर्गाचिया राना। तया चैतन्या नाम अर्जुना । क्षर पुरुषु गा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyā veṃghoni svapnā| dhāṃvata bhavasvargāciyā rānā| tayā caitanyā nāma arjunā | kṣara puruṣu gā|| 93||
verses.meaning: Embracing such a dream, running through the forest of worldly existence and heavenly realms, that consciousness, Arjuna, is indeed called the perishable Purusha (Kshara Purusha).

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ऐक क्षेत्रज्ञु येणें । नामें जयातें बोलणें। जग जीवु कां म्हणे। जिये दशेतें॥९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ aika kṣetrajñu yeṇeṃ | nāmeṃ jayāteṃ bolaṇeṃ| jaga jīvu kāṃ mhaṇe| jiye daśeteṃ||94||
verses.meaning: Now listen to that state which is called Kshetrajna, and which is also referred to as the world or the individual soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो आपुलेनि विसरें। सर्वभूतत्वें अनुकरे। तो आत्मा बोलिजे क्षरें। पुरुष नामें ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo āpuleni visareṃ| sarvabhūtatveṃ anukare| to ātmā bolije kṣareṃ| puruṣa nāmeṃ || 95||
verses.meaning: That Atman, who, through His own forgetfulness, assumes the form of all beings, is called the perishable Purusha.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे तो वस्तुस्थितीपुरता। म्हणौनि आली पुरुषता। वरी देहपुरीं निदैजतां। पुरुषनामें ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: je to vastusthitīpuratā| mhaṇauni ālī puruṣatā| varī dehapurīṃ nidaijatāṃ| puruṣanāmeṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: Therefore, when the Self, which is the ultimate reality, enters the body and seems to sleep, it is called 'Purusha' (the individual soul or conscious entity).

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि क्षरपणाचा नाथिला। आळु यया ऐसेनि आला । जे उपाधींचि आतला । म्हणौनियां॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kṣarapaṇācā nāthilā| āḻu yayā aiseni ālā | je upādhīṃci ātalā | mhaṇauniyāṃ|| 97||
verses.meaning: And the blame of perishability came upon it in such a way, that it was caught within the adjuncts, and thus it was called perishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी खळाळीचिया उदका-। सरसीं आंदोळे चंद्रिका । तैसा विकारां औपाधिका। ऐसाचि गमे॥९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī khaḻāḻīciyā udakā-| sarasīṃ āṃdoḻe caṃdrikā | taisā vikārāṃ aupādhikā| aisāci game||98||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon's reflection trembles on the rippling water, so too does the Self appear to be affected by the illusory modifications of the mind and body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां खळाळु मोटका शोषे। आणि चंद्रिका तैं सरिसींच भ्रंशे। तैसा उपाधिनाशीं न दिसे। उपाधिकु ॥९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ khaḻāḻu moṭakā śoṣe| āṇi caṃdrikā taiṃ sarisīṃca bhraṃśe| taisā upādhināśīṃ na dise| upādhiku ||99||
verses.meaning: Just as a small, gurgling stream dries up, and the moonlight simultaneously vanishes, so too, with the destruction of the limiting adjunct (upadhi), the one associated with the upadhi (upadhiku) is no longer seen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें उपाधीचेनि पाडें। क्षणिकत्व यातें जोडे । तेणें खोंकरपणें घडे । क्षर हें नाम ॥ ५००॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ upādhīceni pāḍeṃ| kṣaṇikatva yāteṃ joḍe | teṇeṃ khoṃkarapaṇeṃ ghaḍe | kṣara heṃ nāma || 500||
verses.meaning: Thus, due to its transient nature, it acquires the quality of being momentary. Because of this fleetingness, it is called 'Kshara' (perishable).

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं जीवचेतन्य आधवें। हें क्षर पुरुष जाणावें । आतां रूप करूं बरवें। अक्षरासी ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ jīvacetanya ādhaveṃ| heṃ kṣara puruṣa jāṇāveṃ | ātāṃ rūpa karūṃ baraveṃ| akṣarāsī || 9||
verses.meaning: Thus, all embodied consciousness should be known as the perishable Purusha. Now, let us beautifully describe the imperishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अक्षरु जो दुसरा। पुरुष पैं धनुर्धरा। तो मध्यस्थु गा गिरिवरां। मेरु जैसा॥२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī akṣaru jo dusarā| puruṣa paiṃ dhanurdharā| to madhyasthu gā girivarāṃ| meru jaisā||2||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, the other imperishable Purusha, the Supreme Being, stands as a mediator, just as Mount Meru stands amidst other mountains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे तो पृथ्वी पाताळ स्वर्गी । इहीं न भेदे तिहीं भागीं । तैसा दोहीं ज्ञानाज्ञानांगीं। पडेना जो॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: je to pṛthvī pātāḻa svargī | ihīṃ na bhede tihīṃ bhāgīṃ | taisā dohīṃ jñānājñānāṃgīṃ| paḍenā jo|| 3||
verses.meaning: Just as the earth, netherworld, and heaven cannot divide it into three parts, so too, it is not affected by the duality of knowledge and ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना यथार्थज्ञाने एक होणें। ना अन्यथात्वें दुजें घेणें। ऐसें निखिळ जें नेणणें। तेंचि तें रूप॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā yathārthajñāne eka hoṇeṃ| nā anyathātveṃ dujeṃ gheṇeṃ| aiseṃ nikhiḻa jeṃ neṇaṇeṃ| teṃci teṃ rūpa|| 4||
verses.meaning: Neither becoming one through true knowledge, nor accepting duality through otherness; such complete unknowing is indeed its true form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पांसुता निःशेष जाये। ना घटभांडादि होये । तया मृत्पिंडा ऐसें आहे। मध्यस्थ जें॥५॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṃsutā niḥśeṣa jāye| nā ghaṭabhāṃḍādi hoye | tayā mṛtpiṃḍā aiseṃ āhe| madhyastha jeṃ||5||
verses.meaning: Just as the dust is completely removed, and no pot or vessel is yet formed, so too is the state of that lump of clay in between.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आटोनि गेलिया सागरु । मग तरंगु ना नीरु । तया ऐशी अनाकारु । जे दशा गा॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ āṭoni geliyā sāgaru | maga taraṃgu nā nīru | tayā aiśī anākāru | je daśā gā||6||
verses.meaning: When the ocean itself dries up, then there are no waves, nor water. Such is the formless state, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था जागणें तरी बुडे । परी स्वप्नाचें कांहीं न मांडे। तैसिये निद्रे सांगडे । न्याहाळणे जें ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā jāgaṇeṃ tarī buḍe | parī svapnāceṃ kāṃhīṃ na māṃḍe| taisiye nidre sāṃgaḍe | nyāhāḻaṇe jeṃ || 7||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, it is like a sleep where one is awake, yet the dream does not manifest. Such is the state of contemplation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विश्‍व आघवेंचि मावळे । आणि आत्मबोधु तरी नुजळे। तिये अज्ञानदशे केवळे। अक्षरु नाम॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: viś‍va āghaveṃci māvaḻe | āṇi ātmabodhu tarī nujaḻe| tiye ajñānadaśe kevaḻe| akṣaru nāma|| 8||
verses.meaning: When the entire universe dissolves, and yet the light of self-realization does not dawn, that state of utter ignorance is truly indescribable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सर्वा कळीं सांडिलें जैसें। चंद्रपण उरे अंबसे । रूप जाणावें तेसें। अक्षराचें ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: sarvā kaḻīṃ sāṃḍileṃ jaiseṃ| caṃdrapaṇa ure aṃbase | rūpa jāṇāveṃ teseṃ| akṣarāceṃ || 9||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon's essence remains even when all its phases are shed on the new moon night, so too should one understand the true nature of the imperishable Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सर्वोपाधिविनाशें । हे जीवदशा जेथ पैसे । फळपाकांत जेसें। झाड बीजीं ॥ ५१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ sarvopādhivināśeṃ | he jīvadaśā jetha paise | phaḻapākāṃta jeseṃ| jhāḍa bījīṃ || 510||
verses.meaning: Just as a tree, in its mature fruit, returns to its seed, so too, when all limiting conditions are destroyed, this state of individual soul merges back into its origin.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें उपाधी उपहित। थोकोनि ठाके जेथ। तयातें अव्यक्‍्त। बोलती गा॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ upādhī upahita| thokoni ṭhāke jetha| tayāteṃ avyak‍ta| bolatī gā|| 11||
verses.meaning: Just as the conditioned consciousness, limited by its adjuncts, comes to rest and dissolves, that state is called the Unmanifest, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: घन अज्ञान सुषुप्ती। तो बीजभावो म्हणती । येर स्वप्न हन जागृती। फळभावो तयाचा ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ghana ajñāna suṣuptī| to bījabhāvo mhaṇatī | yera svapna hana jāgṛtī| phaḻabhāvo tayācā || 12||
verses.meaning: The dense ignorance of deep sleep is called the seed state. The other states, dream and waking, are its fruit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयासी कां बीजभावो। वेदांती केला ऐसा आवो। तो तया पुरुषा ठावो। अक्षराचा॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāsī kāṃ bījabhāvo| vedāṃtī kelā aisā āvo| to tayā puruṣā ṭhāvo| akṣarācā|| 13||
verses.meaning: The one who has such a seed-like understanding, as described in Vedanta, that person is the abode of the imperishable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथूनि अन्यथाज्ञान। फांकोनि जागृति स्वप्न । नानाबुद्धीचें रान। रिगालें असे॥ ९१४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jethūni anyathājñāna| phāṃkoni jāgṛti svapna | nānābuddhīceṃ rāna| rigāleṃ ase|| 914||
verses.meaning: From where false knowledge spreads, and waking and dreaming states, and the forest of various intellects, have entered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जीवत्व जेथुनी किरीटी । विश्व उठतचि उठी । ते उभय भेदांची मिठी । अक्षरु पुरुषु॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jīvatva jethunī kirīṭī | viśva uṭhataci uṭhī | te ubhaya bhedāṃcī miṭhī | akṣaru puruṣu|| 15||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, from where the individual soul arises, and from where the universe simultaneously emerges, the Immutable Purusha is the confluence of these two distinctions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरु क्षर पुरुषु कां जनीं। जिहीं खेळे जागृतीं स्वप्नीं। तिया अवस्था जो दोन्ही । बियाला गा॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeru kṣara puruṣu kāṃ janīṃ| jihīṃ kheḻe jāgṛtīṃ svapnīṃ| tiyā avasthā jo donhī | biyālā gā|| 16||
verses.meaning: The other, the perishable Purusha, is indeed the one who plays in the states of waking and dreaming. He is the seed of both these states.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं अज्ञानघनसुषुप्ती। ऐसैसी जे कां ख्याती। या उणी एकी प्राप्ती । ब्रह्माची जे॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ ajñānaghanasuṣuptī| aisaisī je kāṃ khyātī| yā uṇī ekī prāptī | brahmācī je|| 97||
verses.meaning: The state of deep sleep, characterized by the density of ignorance, is a lesser attainment compared to the realization of Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: साचचि पुढती बीरा। जरी न येतां स्वप्न जागरा। तरी ब्रह्मभावो साचोकारा। म्हणों येता॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: sācaci puḍhatī bīrā| jarī na yetāṃ svapna jāgarā| tarī brahmabhāvo sācokārā| mhaṇoṃ yetā|| 18||
verses.meaning: Indeed, if the state of Brahman does not come even in dreams or waking, then it can truly be called the state of Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी प्रकृतिपुरुषें दोनी । अशभ्रें जाली जियें गगनीं क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञु स्वप्नीं । देखिला जियें॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī prakṛtipuruṣeṃ donī | aśabhreṃ jālī jiyeṃ gaganīṃ kṣetrakṣetrajñu svapnīṃ | dekhilā jiyeṃ|| 19||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky, due to the clouds of Prakriti and Purusha, appears to have two forms, similarly, the Knower of the Field and the Field are seen as if in a dream.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो अधोशाखा। या संसाररूपा रुखा। मूळ तें रूप पुरुषा। अक्षराचें ॥५२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso adhośākhā| yā saṃsārarūpā rukhā| mūḻa teṃ rūpa puruṣā| akṣarāceṃ ||520||
verses.meaning: Let this be the lower branches. Of this tree in the form of the world, the root is the form of the Imperishable Purusha.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा पुरुष कां म्हणिजे । जे पूर्णपणेंचि निजें। पैं मायापुरीं पहुडिजे। तेणेंहि बोलें॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā puruṣa kāṃ mhaṇije | je pūrṇapaṇeṃci nijeṃ| paiṃ māyāpurīṃ pahuḍije| teṇeṃhi boleṃ|| 29||
verses.meaning: Why is this called Purusha? Because He, in His fullness, sleeps in the city of Maya, and this is also spoken of.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि विकारांची जे वारी। ते विपरीत ज्ञानाची परी । नेणिजे जिये माझारीं। ते सुषुप्ती गा हा॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi vikārāṃcī je vārī| te viparīta jñānācī parī | neṇije jiye mājhārīṃ| te suṣuptī gā hā|| 22||
verses.meaning: And that state which is free from all modifications, where there is no knowledge of the opposite, that, indeed, is deep sleep (sushupti).

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि यया आपैसें। क्षरणें या नसे। आणिकेंही हा न नाशे । ज्ञानाउणें ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni yayā āpaiseṃ| kṣaraṇeṃ yā nase| āṇikeṃhī hā na nāśe | jñānāuṇeṃ || 23||
verses.meaning: Therefore, it does not decay on its own, nor is it destroyed by anything else, even by the absence of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यालागीं हा अक्षरु । ऐसा वेदांती डगरु । केला देशी थोरु । सिद्धांताच्या ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yālāgīṃ hā akṣaru | aisā vedāṃtī ḍagaru | kelā deśī thoru | siddhāṃtācyā || 24||
verses.meaning: Therefore, this Imperishable (Brahman) is proclaimed as the great truth by the Vedantins, like a drumbeat of their doctrine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जीवकार्यकारण। जया मायासंगुचि लक्षण। अक्षर पुरुषु जाण। चैतन्य तें॥२५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jīvakāryakāraṇa| jayā māyāsaṃguci lakṣaṇa| akṣara puruṣu jāṇa| caitanya teṃ||25||
verses.meaning: Such is the living principle, whose characteristic is association with Maya. Know that the Imperishable Purusha is that very Consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अन्यथाज्ञानीं। या दोनी अवस्था जया जनीं । तया हरपती घनीं । अज्ञानतत्त्वी ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ anyathājñānīṃ| yā donī avasthā jayā janīṃ | tayā harapatī ghanīṃ | ajñānatattvī || 26||
verses.meaning: Now, for those who are otherwise ignorant, these two states of being, for those people, disappear completely into the dense element of ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें अज्ञान ज्ञानी बुडालिया । ज्ञानें कीर्तिमुखत्व केलिया । जैसा वन्हि काष्ठ जाळूनियां। स्वयें जळे॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ ajñāna jñānī buḍāliyā | jñāneṃ kīrtimukhatva keliyā | jaisā vanhi kāṣṭha jāḻūniyāṃ| svayeṃ jaḻe|| 27||
verses.meaning: When ignorance is dissolved by knowledge, knowledge itself becomes like the 'Kirtimukha' (face of glory), just as fire, after burning wood, consumes itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अज्ञान ज्ञानें नेलें आपण वस्तु देऊनि गेलें। ऐसें जाणणेंनिवीण उरलें। जाणतें जें ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ajñāna jñāneṃ neleṃ āpaṇa vastu deūni geleṃ| aiseṃ jāṇaṇeṃnivīṇa uraleṃ| jāṇateṃ jeṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Just as ignorance is dispelled by knowledge, and then knowledge itself departs after revealing the true nature of reality, what remains is that which knows, beyond all knowing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें तो गा उत्तम पुरुषु। जो तृतीय कां निष्कर्ष) दोहींहून आणिकु । मागिला जो॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ to gā uttama puruṣu| jo tṛtīya kāṃ niṣkarṣa) dohīṃhūna āṇiku | māgilā jo|| 29||
verses.meaning: He is indeed the Supreme Being, the third and ultimate conclusion, distinct from both the perishable and imperishable, the one who is beyond them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुषुप्ती आणि स्वप्ना-। पासूनि बहुवें अर्जुना । जागणें जैसें आना। बोधाचेंचि॥ ५३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: suṣuptī āṇi svapnā-| pāsūni bahuveṃ arjunā | jāgaṇeṃ jaiseṃ ānā| bodhāceṃci|| 530||
verses.meaning: Just as waking is distinct from deep sleep and dream, Arjuna, so too is the awakening of true knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां रश्मी हन मृगजळा-। पासूनि अर्कमंडळा। अफाटु तेवीं वेगळा । उत्तमु गा॥३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ raśmī hana mṛgajaḻā-| pāsūni arkamaṃḍaḻā| aphāṭu tevīṃ vegaḻā | uttamu gā||31||
verses.meaning: Just as the mirage is distinct from the sun's rays, and the sun's orb is distinct from both, so too is the Supreme Being utterly separate and superior.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें ना काष्ठींचा काष्ठाहुनी । ३७० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी अनारिसा जैसा वन्ही । तैसा क्षराक्षरापासुनी। आनचि तो॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ nā kāṣṭhīṃcā kāṣṭhāhunī | 370 śrījñāneśvarī anārisā jaisā vanhī | taisā kṣarākṣarāpāsunī| ānaci to|| 32||
verses.meaning: Just as fire is distinct from the wood it consumes, so too is the Imperishable (Akshara) distinct from the perishable (Kshara).

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं ग्रासूनि आपली मर्यादा। एक करीत नदीनदां। उठी कल्पांती उदावादा । एकार्णवाचा॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ grāsūni āpalī maryādā| eka karīta nadīnadāṃ| uṭhī kalpāṃtī udāvādā | ekārṇavācā|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as at the end of a kalpa, all rivers and streams, having transcended their individual boundaries, merge into a single, vast ocean, so too does the entire creation dissolve into the primordial waters of the great deluge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें स्वप्न ना सुषुप्ती। ना जागराची गोठी आथी । जैसी गिळिली दिवोराती । प्रळयतेजें ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ svapna nā suṣuptī| nā jāgarācī goṭhī āthī | jaisī giḻilī divorātī | praḻayatejeṃ || 34||
verses.meaning: Similarly, there is no dream, no deep sleep, nor any state of wakefulness, just as day and night are swallowed by the light of the cosmic dissolution.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग एकपण ना दुजें।॥ असें नाहीं हें नेणिजे। अनुभव निर्बुजे। बुडाला जेथें ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ekapaṇa nā dujeṃ||| aseṃ nāhīṃ heṃ neṇije| anubhava nirbuje| buḍālā jetheṃ || 35||
verses.meaning: Then there is no 'one' or 'two'; this is not unknown. Experience itself is drowned there, in that fearless state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें आथि जें कांहीं। तें तो उत्तम पुरुषु पाहीं । जें परमात्मा इहीं। बोलिजे नामीं ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ āthi jeṃ kāṃhīṃ| teṃ to uttama puruṣu pāhīṃ | jeṃ paramātmā ihīṃ| bolije nāmīṃ || 36||
verses.meaning: Whatever is of such nature, that indeed is the Supreme Being, who is spoken of by these names as the Ultimate Reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंही एथ न मिसळतां। बोलणें जीवत्बें पंडुसुता । जैसी बुडणेयाची वार्ता । थडियेचा कौजे॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃhī etha na misaḻatāṃ| bolaṇeṃ jīvatbeṃ paṃḍusutā | jaisī buḍaṇeyācī vārtā | thaḍiyecā kauje|| 37||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, the talk of the living entity, without merging into That, is like the news of drowning being told by someone standing on the shore.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें विवेकाचिये कांठीं । उभें ठाकळेया किरीटी। 'पारावाराचिया गोठी । करणें वेदां॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ vivekāciye kāṃṭhīṃ | ubheṃ ṭhākaḻeyā kirīṭī| 'pārāvārāciyā goṭhī | karaṇeṃ vedāṃ|| 38||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, standing on the bank of discrimination, even the Vedas find themselves discussing the 'this shore and that shore' of reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि पुरुषु क्षराक्षरु । दोन्ही देखोनि अवरु । यातें म्हणती परु । आत्मरूप॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni puruṣu kṣarākṣaru | donhī dekhoni avaru | yāteṃ mhaṇatī paru | ātmarūpa|| 39||
verses.meaning: Therefore, seeing both the perishable and the imperishable as inferior, they call this the Supreme Self, the very form of the Atman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना ऐसिया परी। परमात्मा शब्दवरी। सूचिजे गा अवधारीं। पुरुषोत्तमु॥ ५४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā aisiyā parī| paramātmā śabdavarī| sūcije gā avadhārīṃ| puruṣottamu|| 540||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, in this manner, the Supreme Being, Purushottama, is indicated by the word 'Paramatma'. Listen attentively.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं न बोलणेंचि बोलणें । जेथिंचें सर्व नेणिवा जाणणें। कांहींच न होनि होणें । जे वस्तु गा॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ na bolaṇeṃci bolaṇeṃ | jethiṃceṃ sarva neṇivā jāṇaṇeṃ| kāṃhīṃca na honi hoṇeṃ | je vastu gā|| 41||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, not speaking is indeed speaking, where all unknowing is knowing, and becoming by not becoming anything at all—that is the true nature of reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सो$हं तेंही अस्तवलें। जेथ सांगतेंचि सांगणें जालें। द्रष्टृत्वेंसी गेळें। दृश्य जेथ ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: so$haṃ teṃhī astavaleṃ| jetha sāṃgateṃci sāṃgaṇeṃ jāleṃ| draṣṭṛtveṃsī geḻeṃ| dṛśya jetha || 42||
verses.meaning: The very notion of "I am He" (So'ham) has ceased to exist, where the act of speaking itself becomes the spoken. The seer, along with the seen, has vanished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां बिंबा आणि प्रतिबिंबा-। माजीं कैंची हें म्हणों नये प्रभा। जऱ्ही कैसेनि हे लाभा। जायेचि ना॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ biṃbā āṇi pratibiṃbā-| mājīṃ kaiṃcī heṃ mhaṇoṃ naye prabhā| jaṟhī kaiseni he lābhā| jāyeci nā|| 43||
verses.meaning: Now, between the original and its reflection, one should not question the existence of the light. For even if it appears to be lost in some way, it is never truly gone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां घ्राणा फुला दोहीं। द्रुती असे जे माझारिलां ठायीं। ते न दिसे तरी नाहीं । ऐसें बोलो नये॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ ghrāṇā phulā dohīṃ| drutī ase je mājhārilāṃ ṭhāyīṃ| te na dise tarī nāhīṃ | aiseṃ bolo naye|| 44||
verses.meaning: Just as the fragrance of a flower, though not visible, is not to be considered non-existent, so too is the divine presence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें द्रष्टा दृश्य हें जाये। मग कोण म्हणे काय आहे। हेंचि अनुभबें तेंचि पाहे। रूप तया ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ draṣṭā dṛśya heṃ jāye| maga koṇa mhaṇe kāya āhe| heṃci anubhabeṃ teṃci pāhe| rūpa tayā || 45 ||
verses.meaning: In the same way, when the seer and the seen disappear, who then can say what remains? That which is experienced is itself the form of that reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो प्रकाश्येंबीण प्रकाश । ईशितव्येवीण ईशु। आपणेंनीचि अवकाशु। बसवीत असे जो॥४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo prakāśyeṃbīṇa prakāśa | īśitavyevīṇa īśu| āpaṇeṃnīci avakāśu| basavīta ase jo||46||
verses.meaning: He who is light without being illuminated, the Lord without being ruled, and who himself creates space for all to reside.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो नादें ऐकिजता नादु । स्वादें चाखिजता स्वादु। जो भोगिजतसे आनंदु । आनंदेंचि॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo nādeṃ aikijatā nādu | svādeṃ cākhijatā svādu| jo bhogijatase ānaṃdu | ānaṃdeṃci|| 47||
verses.meaning: That which is the sound when sound is heard, the taste when taste is savored, that joy which is experienced, is joy itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो पूर्णतेचा परिणामु । पुरुषु गा पुरुषोत्तमु। विश्रांतीचाही विश्रामु। विराला जेथें ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo pūrṇatecā pariṇāmu | puruṣu gā puruṣottamu| viśrāṃtīcāhī viśrāmu| virālā jetheṃ || 48||
verses.meaning: He who is the culmination of perfection, the Supreme Being, the ultimate rest even for rest itself, merged there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुखासि सुख जोडिलें। जें तेज तेजासि सांपडलें। शून्यही बुडालें। महाशून्यीं जिये ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: sukhāsi sukha joḍileṃ| jeṃ teja tejāsi sāṃpaḍaleṃ| śūnyahī buḍāleṃ| mahāśūnyīṃ jiye || 49||
verses.meaning: Happiness merged with happiness, light found its light, and even the void dissolved into the great void.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो विकासाहीवरी उरता । ग्रासातेंही ग्रासूनि पुरता। जो बहुतें पारडे बहुतां-। पासूनि बहु॥ ५५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo vikāsāhīvarī uratā | grāsāteṃhī grāsūni puratā| jo bahuteṃ pāraḍe bahutāṃ-| pāsūni bahu|| 550||
verses.meaning: That which remains beyond all development, completely consuming even that which consumes; that which is much more than many, from many.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं नेणतयाप्रती । रुपेपणाची प्रतीती । रूपें न होऊनि शुक्‍्ती । दाबी जेवीं ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ neṇatayāpratī | rupepaṇācī pratītī | rūpeṃ na hoūni śuk‍tī | dābī jevīṃ || 51||
verses.meaning: Just as to the ignorant, the illusion of silver appears in a shell, even though it is not silver.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां नाना अलंकारदशे। सोनें न लपत लपालें असे। विश्व न होनियां तैसें । विश्व जो धरी ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ nānā alaṃkāradaśe| soneṃ na lapata lapāleṃ ase| viśva na honiyāṃ taiseṃ | viśva jo dharī || 52||
verses.meaning: Just as gold, even when fashioned into various ornaments, does not cease to be gold, so too the universe, though appearing as diverse forms, does not become separate from the One who sustains it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो जलतरंगा । नाहीं सिनानेपण जेबीं गा । तेवीं दिसता प्रकाशु जगा । आपणचि जो॥ ५३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso jalataraṃgā | nāhīṃ sinānepaṇa jebīṃ gā | tevīṃ disatā prakāśu jagā | āpaṇaci jo|| 53 ||
verses.meaning: Just as the waves are not separate from the water, so too is the light that illuminates the world not separate from the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपलिया संकोचविकाशा । आपणचि रूप वौीरेशा। हा जळीं चंद्र हन जैसा। समग्र गा॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaliyā saṃkocavikāśā | āpaṇaci rūpa vauīreśā| hā jaḻīṃ caṃdra hana jaisā| samagra gā|| 54||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon, though reflected in water, appears whole, so too does the Supreme Being manifest in both contraction and expansion through its own form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा बिशवपणें कांहीं होये । विश्वलोपीं कहीं न जाये । जैसा रात्रीं दिवसें नोहे । द्विधा रवि॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā biśavapaṇeṃ kāṃhīṃ hoye | viśvalopīṃ kahīṃ na jāye | jaisā rātrīṃ divaseṃ nohe | dvidhā ravi|| 55||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the universe does not cease to exist due to its manifestation, just as the sun is not divided into two by day and night.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कांहींचि कोणीकडे। कायिसेनिहि वेंचीं न पडे । जयाचें सांगडें। जयासीचि॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā kāṃhīṃci koṇīkaḍe| kāyisenihi veṃcīṃ na paḍe | jayāceṃ sāṃgaḍeṃ| jayāsīci|| 56||
verses.meaning: Just as nothing can be compared to it, and it cannot be measured by anything, so too, its greatness is only comparable to itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो आपणपेंचि आपणया। प्रकाशीतसे धनंजया। काय बहु बोलों जया । नाहीं दुजें ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo āpaṇapeṃci āpaṇayā| prakāśītase dhanaṃjayā| kāya bahu boloṃ jayā | nāhīṃ dujeṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, that which illuminates itself by itself, what more can I say about that which has no second?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो गा मी निरुपाधिकु । क्षराक्षरोत्तमु एकु । म्हणौनि म्हणे वेद लोकु। पुरुषोत्तमु॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: to gā mī nirupādhiku | kṣarākṣarottamu eku | mhaṇauni mhaṇe veda loku| puruṣottamu|| 58||
verses.meaning: He is I, the unconditioned, the supreme beyond the perishable and imperishable. Therefore, the Vedas and people call Him Purushottama (the Supreme Being).

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें असो ऐसिया। मज पुरुषोत्तमातें धनंजया । जाणे जो पाहलेया । ज्ञानमित्रें ॥५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ aso aisiyā| maja puruṣottamāteṃ dhanaṃjayā | jāṇe jo pāhaleyā | jñānamitreṃ ||59||
verses.meaning: But let this be, O Dhananjaya, he who knows Me, the Purushottama, through the eye of knowledge, truly sees.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चेइलिया आपुलें ज्ञान। जैसें नाहींचि होय स्वप्न । तैसें स्फुरतें त्रिभुवन। वावों जालें॥ ५६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ceiliyā āpuleṃ jñāna| jaiseṃ nāhīṃci hoya svapna | taiseṃ sphurateṃ tribhuvana| vāvoṃ jāleṃ|| 560||
verses.meaning: When one's own knowledge (of the world) ceases to exist, just like a dream vanishes, then the three worlds, which were perceived, also become void and unreal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां हातीं घेतलिया माळा। फिटे सर्पाभासाचा कांटाळा । तेसा माझेनि बोधें टबाळा | नागवे तो॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ hātīṃ ghetaliyā māḻā| phiṭe sarpābhāsācā kāṃṭāḻā | tesā mājheni bodheṃ ṭabāḻā | nāgave to|| 61||
verses.meaning: Just as by taking a garland in hand, the illusion of a snake vanishes, so too, by my teaching, one is not deceived by the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लेणें सोनेंचि जो जाणे। तो लेणेंपण तें बाबो म्हणे। तेवीं मी जाणोनि जेणें । वाळिला भेदु ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: leṇeṃ soneṃci jo jāṇe| to leṇeṃpaṇa teṃ bābo mhaṇe| tevīṃ mī jāṇoni jeṇeṃ | vāḻilā bhedu || 62||
verses.meaning: Just as one who knows gold understands that ornaments are merely gold, so too, one who knows Me abandons all sense of difference.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणे सर्वत्र सच्चिदानंदु। मीचि एकु स्वतःसिद्धु । जो आपणेनसीं भेदु। नेणोनियां जाणे ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇe sarvatra saccidānaṃdu| mīci eku svataḥsiddhu | jo āpaṇenasīṃ bhedu| neṇoniyāṃ jāṇe || 63||
verses.meaning: Then he says, "Everywhere there is सच्चिदानंदु (Sat-chit-ananda - Existence-Consciousness-Bliss). I alone am the self-evident one, who knows without knowing any difference from myself."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणेंचि सर्व जाणितलें। हेंही म्हणणें थेंकुलें। जे तया सर्व उरलें। द्वैत नाहीं ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃci sarva jāṇitaleṃ| heṃhī mhaṇaṇeṃ theṃkuleṃ| je tayā sarva uraleṃ| dvaita nāhīṃ || 64||
verses.meaning: By that alone, everything is known. Even this statement is inadequate, for to that (Brahman), no duality remains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि माझिया भजना । उचितु तोचि अर्जुना। गगन जैसें आलिंगना। गगनाचिया ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni mājhiyā bhajanā | ucitu toci arjunā| gagana jaiseṃ āliṃganā| gaganāciyā || 65||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, he alone is fit for My devotion, just as the sky embraces the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: क्षीरसागरा परगुणें। कौजे क्षीरसागरचिपणें। अमृतचि होऊनि मिळणें। अमृतीं जेवीं ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṣīrasāgarā paraguṇeṃ| kauje kṣīrasāgaracipaṇeṃ| amṛtaci hoūni miḻaṇeṃ| amṛtīṃ jevīṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: Just as milk, by its inherent qualities, becomes one with the ocean of milk, and nectar, by its very nature, merges with nectar, so too does the individual soul, through its intrinsic purity, unite with the Supreme Being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: साडेपंधरा मिसळावें। तें साडेपंधरेंचि होआवें। तेवीं मी जालिया संभवे। भक्ति माझी ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāḍepaṃdharā misaḻāveṃ| teṃ sāḍepaṃdhareṃci hoāveṃ| tevīṃ mī jāliyā saṃbhave| bhakti mājhī || 67||
verses.meaning: When fifteen and a half is mixed, it becomes fifteen and a half. Similarly, when I am realized, My devotion becomes possible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा सिंधूसि आनी होती । तरी गंगा कैसेनि मिळती । म्हणौनि मी न होतां भक्‍ती-। अन्वयो आहे॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā siṃdhūsi ānī hotī | tarī gaṃgā kaiseni miḻatī | mhaṇauni mī na hotāṃ bhak‍tī-| anvayo āhe|| 68 ||
verses.meaning: Indeed, if the Sindhu (river) were to arrive, how could it merge with the Ganga? Therefore, without my existence, devotion cannot truly manifest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसियालागीं सर्व प्रकारीं। जैसा कल्लोळु अनन्यु सागरीं। तैसा मातें ३७२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी अवधारीं। भजिन्नलळा जो॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyālāgīṃ sarva prakārīṃ| jaisā kalloḻu ananyu sāgarīṃ| taisā māteṃ 372 śrījñāneśvarī avadhārīṃ| bhajinnalaḻā jo|| 69||
verses.meaning: Therefore, in all respects, just as a wave is inseparable from the ocean, so too, O Dnyaneshwari, is the one who devoutly worships Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सूर्या आणि प्रभे। एकवंकी जेणें लोभें। तो पाडु मानूं लाभे। भजना तया ॥ ५७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: sūryā āṇi prabhe| ekavaṃkī jeṇeṃ lobheṃ| to pāḍu mānūṃ lābhe| bhajanā tayā || 570||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun and its radiance are inseparable, so too is the devotion to Him, which is the true gain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं कथिलयादारभ्य। हें जें सर्व शास्त्रेकलभ्य। उपनिषदां सौरभ्य । 'कमळदळां जेवीं ॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ kathilayādārabhya| heṃ jeṃ sarva śāstrekalabhya| upaniṣadāṃ saurabhya | 'kamaḻadaḻāṃ jevīṃ ||79||
verses.meaning: Thus, from the very beginning of this discourse, this entire scripture, which is attainable through all scriptures, is the fragrance of the Upanishads, just as the fragrance is inherent in lotus petals.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें शब्दब्रह्माचें मथितें। व्यासप्रज्ञेचेंनि हातें । मथूनि काढिलें आयितें। सार आम्हीं ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ śabdabrahmāceṃ mathiteṃ| vyāsaprajñeceṃni hāteṃ | mathūni kāḍhileṃ āyiteṃ| sāra āmhīṃ || 72||
verses.meaning: This essence of the Word-Brahman, churned by the hands of Vyasa's intellect, is what we have readily extracted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे ज्ञानामृताची जान्हवी । जे आनंदचंद्रींची सतरावी । विचारक्षीरार्णवींची नवी । लक्ष्मी जे हे ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: je jñānāmṛtācī jānhavī | je ānaṃdacaṃdrīṃcī satarāvī | vicārakṣīrārṇavīṃcī navī | lakṣmī je he || 73||
verses.meaning: She is the Ganges of the nectar of knowledge, the sixteenth digit of the moon of bliss, the new Lakshmi born from the ocean of milk of contemplation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आपुलेनि पर्दे वर्णे । अर्थाचेनि जीवेंप्राणे। मीवांचोनि हों नेणें । आन कांहीं ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni āpuleni parde varṇe | arthāceni jīveṃprāṇe| mīvāṃconi hoṃ neṇeṃ | āna kāṃhīṃ || 74||
verses.meaning: Therefore, by its own nature, by the very life and soul of its meaning, nothing else can exist without Me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: क्षराक्षरत्वें समोर जालें। तयांचें पुरुषत्व वाळिलें। मग सर्वस्व मज दिधलें। पुरुषोत्तमी ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṣarākṣaratveṃ samora jāleṃ| tayāṃceṃ puruṣatva vāḻileṃ| maga sarvasva maja didhaleṃ| puruṣottamī || 75||
verses.meaning: When the perishable and imperishable came before Me, their 'purushahood' (their distinct identity or essence) withered away. Then, they surrendered their all to Me, the Purushottama (the Supreme Being).

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जगीं गीता । मियां आत्मेनि पतित्रता। जे हे प्रस्तुत तुबां आतां। आकर्णिली ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jagīṃ gītā | miyāṃ ātmeni patitratā| je he prastuta tubāṃ ātāṃ| ākarṇilī || 76||
verses.meaning: Therefore, in this world, the Gita is like a chaste wife to Me, the Self, which you have now heard.

verses.shloka_devanagari: साचचि बोलाचें नव्हे हें शास्त्र । पैं संसारु जिणतें हें शस्त्र। आत्मा अबतरविते मंत्र। अक्षरें इयें ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: sācaci bolāceṃ navhe heṃ śāstra | paiṃ saṃsāru jiṇateṃ heṃ śastra| ātmā abataravite maṃtra| akṣareṃ iyeṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: These words are not merely scriptures; they are weapons to conquer the worldly existence, mantras that reveal the true Self. These are the very letters.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तुजपुढां सांगितलें। तें अर्जुना ऐसें जालें। जें गौप्यधन काढिलें। माझें आजि ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī tujapuḍhāṃ sāṃgitaleṃ| teṃ arjunā aiseṃ jāleṃ| jeṃ gaupyadhana kāḍhileṃ| mājheṃ āji || 78||
verses.meaning: But Arjuna, what I have told you today is like unearthing my hidden treasure.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मज चैतन्यशंभूचा माथां । जो निक्षेपु होता पार्था । तया गौतमु जालासि आस्था। निधी तूं गा॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maja caitanyaśaṃbhūcā māthāṃ | jo nikṣepu hotā pārthā | tayā gautamu jālāsi āsthā| nidhī tūṃ gā||79||
verses.meaning: O Partha, you have become the treasure chest, the very foundation, for that spiritual wealth which was the crown jewel on the head of Lord Shiva, the embodiment of pure consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चोखटिवा आपुलिया। पुढिला उगाणा घेयावया । तया दर्पणाचीचि परी धनंजया । केली आम्हां॥ ५८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: cokhaṭivā āpuliyā| puḍhilā ugāṇā gheyāvayā | tayā darpaṇācīci parī dhanaṃjayā | kelī āmhāṃ|| 580||
verses.meaning: Just as a mirror is needed to see one's own reflection, so too, Arjuna, have we been given this task to reveal the true nature of the self to others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का भरलें चंद्रतारांगणीं | नभ सिंधू आपणयामाजीं आणी । तैसा गीतेसीं मी अंतःकरणीं। सूदला तुवां॥८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā bharaleṃ caṃdratārāṃgaṇīṃ | nabha siṃdhū āpaṇayāmājīṃ āṇī | taisā gītesīṃ mī aṃtaḥkaraṇīṃ| sūdalā tuvāṃ||81||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky, filled with the moon and stars, draws the ocean into itself, so too have you drawn me, the Gita, into your heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे त्रिविधमळिकटा। तूं सांडिलासि सुभटा । म्हणौनि गीतेसी मज वसौटा। जालासि गा॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je trividhamaḻikaṭā| tūṃ sāṃḍilāsi subhaṭā | mhaṇauni gītesī maja vasauṭā| jālāsi gā|| 82||
verses.meaning: You, the brave one, have abandoned the three-fold impurities. Therefore, you have become a dwelling place for the Gita within me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें बोलों काय गीता । जे हे माझी उन्मेषलता । जाणे तो समस्ता । मोहा मुके ॥८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ boloṃ kāya gītā | je he mājhī unmeṣalatā | jāṇe to samastā | mohā muke ||83||
verses.meaning: What more can I say about this Gita? Whoever understands this vine of my spiritual awakening is freed from all delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सेविळी अमृतसरिता। रोगु दवडूनि पंडुसुता। अमरपण उचितां। देऊनि घाली ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: seviḻī amṛtasaritā| rogu davaḍūni paṃḍusutā| amarapaṇa ucitāṃ| deūni ghālī || 84||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, it is like a river of nectar that, by removing disease, bestows immortality upon the deserving.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी गीता हे जाणितळिया । काय विस्मयो मोह जावया । परी आत्मज्ञानें आपणपयां। मिळिजे येथ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī gītā he jāṇitaḻiyā | kāya vismayo moha jāvayā | parī ātmajñāneṃ āpaṇapayāṃ| miḻije yetha|| 85||
verses.meaning: Similarly, for one who has understood the Gita, what wonder is there that delusion and attachment vanish? But through self-knowledge, one merges with the Self here itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया आत्मज्ञानाच्या ठायीं । कर्म आपुलेया जीविता पाहीं । होऊनियां उतराई । लया जाय ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā ātmajñānācyā ṭhāyīṃ | karma āpuleyā jīvitā pāhīṃ | hoūniyāṃ utarāī | layā jāya || 86||
verses.meaning: Where, in the abode of self-knowledge, karma, having fulfilled its purpose in one's life, dissolves into nothingness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हरपलें दावूनि जैसा। मागु सरे वीरविलासा। ज्ञानचि कळस वळघे तैसा । कर्मप्रासादाचा ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: harapaleṃ dāvūni jaisā| māgu sare vīravilāsā| jñānaci kaḻasa vaḻaghe taisā | karmaprāsādācā || 87||
verses.meaning: Just as a hero, having found what was lost, returns victorious, so too does knowledge ascend to become the pinnacle of the palace of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ज्ञानिया पुरुषा। कृत्य करू सरलें देखा। ऐसा अनाथांचा सखा। बोळिला तो॥८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jñāniyā puruṣā| kṛtya karū saraleṃ dekhā| aisā anāthāṃcā sakhā| boḻilā to||88||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for the enlightened one, all actions are completed. Such a friend of the helpless is he, who has been sent forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें श्रीकृष्णवचनामृत। पार्थी भरोनि असे वबोसंडत। मग व्यासकृपा प्राप्त। संजयासी॥८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ śrīkṛṣṇavacanāmṛta| pārthī bharoni ase vabosaṃḍata| maga vyāsakṛpā prāpta| saṃjayāsī||89||
verses.meaning: That nectar of Shri Krishna's words, overflowing with meaning, was then, by Vyasa's grace, bestowed upon Sanjaya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो धृतराष्ट्रराया । सूतसे पान करावया । म्हणौनि जीवितांतु तया । नोहेचि भारी ॥ ५९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: to dhṛtarāṣṭrarāyā | sūtase pāna karāvayā | mhaṇauni jīvitāṃtu tayā | noheci bhārī || 590||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for King Dhritarashtra, it was like drinking a potion of immortality, and thus, life was not a burden for him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं गीताश्रवणअवसरीं। आवडों लागतां अनधिकारी। परि सेखीं तेचि उजरी । पातला भली ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ gītāśravaṇaavasarīṃ| āvaḍoṃ lāgatāṃ anadhikārī| pari sekhīṃ teci ujarī | pātalā bhalī || 91||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, during the occasion of listening to the Gita, if an unqualified person begins to like it, then ultimately, that very liking illuminates and benefits them greatly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेव्हां द्राक्षीं दूध घातलें । तेव्हां वायां गेलें गमलें। परी फळपाकीं दुणावलें। देखिजे जेवीं ॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jevhāṃ drākṣīṃ dūdha ghātaleṃ | tevhāṃ vāyāṃ geleṃ gamaleṃ| parī phaḻapākīṃ duṇāvaleṃ| dekhije jevīṃ ||92||
verses.meaning: When milk is poured into a grape vine, it seems wasted. But in the ripened fruit, its essence is seen to have doubled, just as it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं श्रीहरीवक्त्रींची अक्षरें। संजयें सांगितली आदरें। तिहीं अंधु तोही अवसरें। सुखिया जाला॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ śrīharīvaktrīṃcī akṣareṃ| saṃjayeṃ sāṃgitalī ādareṃ| tihīṃ aṃdhu tohī avasareṃ| sukhiyā jālā|| 93||
verses.meaning: In the same way, the words emanating from the mouth of Shri Hari, reverently narrated by Sanjaya, brought joy even to the blind Dhritarashtra in that opportune moment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंचि मऱ्हाटेनि विन्यासें । मियां उन्मेषें ठसेंठोंबसें । जी जाणें नेणें तैसें । निरोपिलें॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃci maṟhāṭeni vinyāseṃ | miyāṃ unmeṣeṃ ṭhaseṃṭhoṃbaseṃ | jī jāṇeṃ neṇeṃ taiseṃ | niropileṃ|| 94||
verses.meaning: That same knowledge, in Marathi, I have expressed to the best of my limited understanding, with whatever words I could find, whether I knew them well or not.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सेवंतीये अरिसि कांही । आंग पाहतां बिशेषु नाहीं। परी सौरभ्य नेलें तिहीं । भ्रमरीं जाणिजे ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: sevaṃtīye arisi kāṃhī | āṃga pāhatāṃ biśeṣu nāhīṃ| parī saurabhya neleṃ tihīṃ | bhramarīṃ jāṇije || 95||
verses.meaning: The Sevanti flower, when observed, has no special distinction in its appearance. Yet, its fragrance is carried away by the bees, who alone truly know its essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें घडतें प्रमेय घेइजे। उणें तें मज देइजे। जें नेणणें हेंचि सहजें। रूप कौ बाळा॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ghaḍateṃ prameya gheije| uṇeṃ teṃ maja deije| jeṃ neṇaṇeṃ heṃci sahajeṃ| rūpa kau bāḻā|| 96||
verses.meaning: Whatever is destined to happen, let it be. Whatever is lacking, give it to me. For this very ignorance, O child, is naturally your true form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी नेणतें जऱ्ही होये। तऱही देखोनि बाप कीं माये । हर्ष केंही न समाये। चोज करिती ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī neṇateṃ jaṟhī hoye| taṟahī dekhoni bāpa kīṃ māye | harṣa keṃhī na samāye| coja karitī || 97||
verses.meaning: Even if the child is ignorant, upon seeing the father or mother, their joy knows no bounds, and they are filled with wonder.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें संत माहेर माझें । तुम्ही मिनलिया मी लाडेजे। तेंचि ग्रंथाचेनि व्याजें। जाणिजो जी॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ saṃta māhera mājheṃ | tumhī minaliyā mī lāḍeje| teṃci graṃthāceni vyājeṃ| jāṇijo jī|| 98||
verses.meaning: Just as saints are my maternal home, and when I meet you, I am filled with affection, so too, through the pretext of this scripture, please know this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां विशवात्मकु हा माझा । स्वामी श्रीनिवृत्तिरजा। तो अवधारु वाक्‍पूजा । ज्ञानदेवो म्हणे॥५९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ viśavātmaku hā mājhā | svāmī śrīnivṛttirajā| to avadhāru vāk‍pūjā | jñānadevo mhaṇe||599||
verses.meaning: Now, this Vishwatmaku, my Lord, Shri Nivruttiraja, may he accept this offering of words, says Dnyandev.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मावळवीत विश्‍वाभासु। नवल उदयला चंडांशु । अद्वयाब्जिनीविकाशु । वंदूं आतां॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: māvaḻavīta viś‍vābhāsu| navala udayalā caṃḍāṃśu | advayābjinīvikāśu | vaṃdūṃ ātāṃ|| 1||
verses.meaning: The illusion of the universe is dispelled, and a new, brilliant sun has risen. Now, let us worship the one who causes the blossoming of the lotus of non-duality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो अविद्याराती रुसोनियां । गिळी ज्ञानाज्ञानचांदणिया । जो सुदिनु करी ज्ञानियां। स्वबोधाचा॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo avidyārātī rusoniyāṃ | giḻī jñānājñānacāṃdaṇiyā | jo sudinu karī jñāniyāṃ| svabodhācā|| 2||
verses.meaning: He who, being displeased with the night of ignorance, swallows the moonlight of knowledge and non-knowledge, and who makes the day of self-realization for the wise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेणें विवळतिये सवळे। लाहोनि आत्मज्ञानाचे डोळे। सांडिती देहाहंतेची अविसाळें । जीवपक्षी ॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṇeṃ vivaḻatiye savaḻe| lāhoni ātmajñānāce ḍoḻe| sāṃḍitī dehāhaṃtecī avisāḻeṃ | jīvapakṣī ||3||
verses.meaning: By which, the birds of life, having attained the eyes of self-knowledge in their distressed state, shed the serpent-like attachment to the body-ego.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लिंगदेहकमळाचा । पोटीं वेंचुतया चिद्भ्रमराचा । बंदिमोक्षु जयाचा । उदैला होय॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: liṃgadehakamaḻācā | poṭīṃ veṃcutayā cidbhramarācā | baṃdimokṣu jayācā | udailā hoya|| 4||
verses.meaning: The one for whom the liberation of the consciousness-bee, which is trapped within the lotus of the subtle body, has dawned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शब्दाचिया आसकडीं। भेदनदीच्या दोहीं थडीं। आरडाते बिरहवेडीं । बुऱ्यिबोधु ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: śabdāciyā āsakaḍīṃ| bhedanadīcyā dohīṃ thaḍīṃ| āraḍāte birahaveḍīṃ | buṟyibodhu || 5||
verses.meaning: On the two banks of the river of separation, due to the attachment to words, the mad one in separation, the ignorant, cries out.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया चक्रवाकांचें मिथुन । सामरस्याचें समाधान । भोगवी जो चिद्‌गगन। भुवनदिवा॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā cakravākāṃceṃ mithuna | sāmarasyāceṃ samādhāna | bhogavī jo cid‌gagana| bhuvanadivā|| 6||
verses.meaning: He, the sun of the spiritual sky, grants the pair of chakravaka birds the contentment of unity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेणें पाहालिये पाहांटे। भेदाची चोरवेळ फिटे। रिघती आत्मानुभववाटे। पांथिक योगी ॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṇeṃ pāhāliye pāhāṃṭe| bhedācī coraveḻa phiṭe| righatī ātmānubhavavāṭe| pāṃthika yogī ||7||
verses.meaning: At the break of dawn, when the darkness of duality dissipates, the yogis, like travelers, enter the path of self-realization.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचेनि बिवेककिरणसंगें। उन्मेखसूर्यकांतु फुणगे। दीपळे जाळिती दांगें। संसाराची ॥ ८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāceni bivekakiraṇasaṃgeṃ| unmekhasūryakāṃtu phuṇage| dīpaḻe jāḻitī dāṃgeṃ| saṃsārācī || 8 ||
verses.meaning: By the rays of whose discriminative wisdom, the sun-gem of spiritual awakening ignites, burning away the dense forest of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचा रश्मिपुंजु निबरु । होतां स्वरूप उखरीं स्थिरु । ये महासिद्धीचा पूरु । मृगजळ तें ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayācā raśmipuṃju nibaru | hotāṃ svarūpa ukharīṃ sthiru | ye mahāsiddhīcā pūru | mṛgajaḻa teṃ || 9||
verses.meaning: When the dense cluster of rays (of the sun of knowledge) becomes steady in the core of one's true Self, the flood of great spiritual powers (siddhis) that arises is merely a mirage.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो प्रत्यग्बोधाचिया माथया । सो5हंतेचा मध्यान्ही आलिया । लपे आत्मभ्रांतिछाया । आपणपां तळीं ॥ ९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo pratyagbodhāciyā māthayā | so5haṃtecā madhyānhī āliyā | lape ātmabhrāṃtichāyā | āpaṇapāṃ taḻīṃ || 90||
verses.meaning: When the sun of 'I am That' rises to its zenith on the peak of self-realization, the shadow of self-delusion completely disappears beneath oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं विश्‍वस्वप्नासहितें। 'कोण अन्यथामती निद्रेतें। सांभाळी नुरेचि जेथें । मायाराती ॥ ९११॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ viś‍vasvapnāsahiteṃ| 'koṇa anyathāmatī nidreteṃ| sāṃbhāḻī nureci jetheṃ | māyārātī || 911||
verses.meaning: At that time, along with the dream of the universe, who else would protect the sleep of delusion, where the night of Maya itself does not remain?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि अद्ठयबोधपाटणीं । तेथ महानंदाची दाटणी । मग सुखानुभूतीचीं घेणीं देणीं। मंदाबो ळागती॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni adṭhayabodhapāṭaṇīṃ | tetha mahānaṃdācī dāṭaṇī | maga sukhānubhūtīcīṃ gheṇīṃ deṇīṃ| maṃdābo ḻāgatī|| 12||
verses.meaning: Therefore, at the market of non-dual realization, there is a dense gathering of great bliss. Then, the transactions of experiencing joy begin to unfold gently.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना ऐसैसें। मुक्‍तकैवल्य सुदिवसें। सदा लाहिजे कां प्रकाशें। जयाचेनि॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā aisaiseṃ| muk‍takaivalya sudivaseṃ| sadā lāhije kāṃ prakāśeṃ| jayāceni|| 13||
verses.meaning: Indeed, such a day of liberation and ultimate bliss is attained through the light of whom?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो निजधामव्योमींचा रावो । उदैलाचि उदैजतखेंवो। फेडी पूर्वादि दिशांसि ठावो। उदोअस्तूचा ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo nijadhāmavyomīṃcā rāvo | udailāci udaijatakheṃvo| pheḍī pūrvādi diśāṃsi ṭhāvo| udoastūcā || 94||
verses.meaning: He, the king of the sky of his own abode, as soon as he rises, removes the very concept of east and west, of rising and setting.

verses.shloka_devanagari: न दिसणें दिसणेंनसीं मावळवी। दोहीं झांकिलें तें सैंघ पालवी। काय बहु बोलो ते आघवी । उखाच् आनी॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: na disaṇeṃ disaṇeṃnasīṃ māvaḻavī| dohīṃ jhāṃkileṃ teṃ saiṃgha pālavī| kāya bahu bolo te āghavī | ukhāc ānī|| 15||
verses.meaning: That which is not seen, and that which is seen, both are dissolved. What more can I say? All of it is a riddle.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो अहोरात्रांचा पैलकडु। कोणें देखावा ज्ञानमार्तडु। जो प्रकाश्येंबीण सुरवाडु। प्रकाशाचा ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to ahorātrāṃcā pailakaḍu| koṇeṃ dekhāvā jñānamārtaḍu| jo prakāśyeṃbīṇa suravāḍu| prakāśācā || 16||
verses.meaning: Who can behold that sun of knowledge, beyond day and night, who is the very essence of light, without any external source of illumination?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया चित्सूर्या श्रीनिवृत्ती। आतां नमो म्हणों पुढतपुढती। जे बाधका येइजतसे स्तुती । बोलाचिया॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā citsūryā śrīnivṛttī| ātāṃ namo mhaṇoṃ puḍhatapuḍhatī| je bādhakā yeijatase stutī | bolāciyā|| 17||
verses.meaning: To that sun of consciousness, Shri Nivrutti, I now offer salutations again and again. For it is through praise that one approaches the very essence of speech.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देवाचें महिमान पाहोनियां। स्तुती तरी येईजे चांगावया । जरी स्तव्यबुद्धीसीं लया। जाईजे कां॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: devāceṃ mahimāna pāhoniyāṃ| stutī tarī yeīje cāṃgāvayā | jarī stavyabuddhīsīṃ layā| jāīje kāṃ|| 18||
verses.meaning: Upon beholding the glory of God, praise naturally arises. But what if the very intellect that praises is absorbed into that glory?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो सर्वनेणिवां जाणिजे । मौनाचिया मिठीया वानिजे। कांहींच न होनि आणिजे। आपणपयां जो॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo sarvaneṇivāṃ jāṇije | maunāciyā miṭhīyā vānije| kāṃhīṃca na honi āṇije| āpaṇapayāṃ jo|| 19||
verses.meaning: That which is known by all knowledge, praised by the embrace of silence, and brought into being by itself, without becoming anything else.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया तुझिया उद्देशासाठी । पश्यंती मध्यमा पोटीं । सूनि परेसींही पाठीं। वैखरी विरे॥ २०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā tujhiyā uddeśāsāṭhī | paśyaṃtī madhyamā poṭīṃ | sūni paresīṃhī pāṭhīṃ| vaikharī vire|| 20||
verses.meaning: For your purpose, in the womb of Madhyama, having left even Para behind, Vaikhari dissolves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया तूतें मी सेवकपणें। लेवबीं बोलकेया स्तोत्राचे लेणें। हें उपसाहावेंही म्हणतां उणें । अद्वयानंदा ॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā tūteṃ mī sevakapaṇeṃ| levabīṃ bolakeyā stotrāce leṇeṃ| heṃ upasāhāveṃhī mhaṇatāṃ uṇeṃ | advayānaṃdā || 21||
verses.meaning: O Bliss of Non-duality, I, as your servant, adorn you with the ornament of eloquent hymns. Even to say 'please bear with this' would be an understatement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी रंकें अमृताचा सागरु । देखिलिया पडे उचिताचा विसरु। मग करू धांवे पाहुणेरु । शाकांचा तया॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī raṃkeṃ amṛtācā sāgaru | dekhiliyā paḍe ucitācā visaru| maga karū dhāṃve pāhuṇeru | śākāṃcā tayā|| 22||
verses.meaning: Just as a poor person, upon seeing an ocean of nectar, forgets all propriety and rushes to offer a feast of vegetables to it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ शाकुही कौर बहुत म्हणावा । तयाचा हर्षवेगुचि तो घ्यावा । उजळोनि दिव्यतेजा हातिवा । ते भक्‍तीचि पाहावी ॥२३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha śākuhī kaura bahuta mhaṇāvā | tayācā harṣaveguci to ghyāvā | ujaḻoni divyatejā hātivā | te bhak‍tīci pāhāvī ||23||
verses.meaning: There, the devotion itself should be seen, which, like a lamp, illuminates the divine light, and through which the great joy and enthusiasm of the Kauravas should be understood.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बाळा उचित जाणणें होये। तरी बाळपणचि कें आहे। परी साचचि येरी माये। म्हणौनि तोषे॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: bāḻā ucita jāṇaṇeṃ hoye| tarī bāḻapaṇaci keṃ āhe| parī sācaci yerī māye| mhaṇauni toṣe|| 24||
verses.meaning: A child knows what is proper, but where is childhood then? Yet, the mother truly believes it, and so she is pleased.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा गांवरसें भरळें। पाणी पाठीं पाय देत आलें। तें गंगा काय म्हणितलें। परतें सर॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā gāṃvaraseṃ bharaḻeṃ| pāṇī pāṭhīṃ pāya deta āleṃ| teṃ gaṃgā kāya mhaṇitaleṃ| parateṃ sara|| 25||
verses.meaning: If a river, swollen by rain, comes rushing towards the Ganga, does the Ganga say, "Move away"?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी भूगूचा कैसा अपकारु । कीं तो मानूनि प्रियोपचारु । तोषेचिना शार्जुधरु । गुरुत्वासीं ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī bhūgūcā kaisā apakāru | kīṃ to mānūni priyopacāru | toṣecinā śārjudharu | gurutvāsīṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: How can the earth be considered to have harmed the one who digs into it? Rather, the Lord Vishnu, considering it a loving service, is pleased with the earth's steadfastness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौ आंधारें खतेळें अंबर। झालेया दिवसनाथासमोर । तेणें तयातें पऱ्हा सर । म्हणितलें काई॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kau āṃdhāreṃ khateḻeṃ aṃbara| jhāleyā divasanāthāsamora | teṇeṃ tayāteṃ paṟhā sara | mhaṇitaleṃ kāī|| 27||
verses.meaning: How can darkness remain before the sun? Can it say to the sun, "Move aside"?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं भेदबुद्धीचिये तुळे। घाळूनि सूर्यश्लेषाचें कांटाळें। तुकिलासि तें येकी वेळे। उपसाहिजो जी॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ bhedabuddhīciye tuḻe| ghāḻūni sūryaśleṣāceṃ kāṃṭāḻeṃ| tukilāsi teṃ yekī veḻe| upasāhijo jī|| 28||
verses.meaning: In the same way, by placing the burden of the sun's brilliance on the scale of discriminatory intellect, you have been weighed at once; please bear with it, O Lord.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिहीं ध्यानाचा डोळां पाहिलासी। वेदादि वाचां वानिलासी। जें उपसाहिलें तयासी । तें आम्हांही करीं ॥२९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jihīṃ dhyānācā ḍoḻāṃ pāhilāsī| vedādi vācāṃ vānilāsī| jeṃ upasāhileṃ tayāsī | teṃ āmhāṃhī karīṃ ||29||
verses.meaning: You, who are seen by the eye of meditation, and described by the Vedas and other scriptures, whatever You have bestowed upon them, please grant that to us as well.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मी आजि तुझ्या गुणीं। लांचावलळो अपराधु न गणीं। भलतें करीं परी अर्धधणीं। नुठी कदा ॥ ३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī mī āji tujhyā guṇīṃ| lāṃcāvalaḻo aparādhu na gaṇīṃ| bhalateṃ karīṃ parī ardhadhaṇīṃ| nuṭhī kadā || 30||
verses.meaning: But today, I am so enamored by your virtues that I do not count any offense. Do whatever you wish, but never leave me halfway.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मियां गीता येणें नांवें। तुझें पसायामृत सुहावें। वानूं लाधलो तें दुणेन थावें। दैवलो दैवें॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: miyāṃ gītā yeṇeṃ nāṃveṃ| tujheṃ pasāyāmṛta suhāveṃ| vānūṃ lādhalo teṃ duṇena thāveṃ| daivalo daiveṃ|| 31||
verses.meaning: Through this Gita, I have been blessed to describe the sweet nectar of your grace, and my fortune has doubled by this divine opportunity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: माझिया सत्यवादाचें तप। वाचा केलें बहुत कल्प। तया फळाचे हें महाद्वीप) पातला प्रभु॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mājhiyā satyavādāceṃ tapa| vācā keleṃ bahuta kalpa| tayā phaḻāce heṃ mahādvīpa) pātalā prabhu|| 32||
verses.meaning: The Lord has arrived, the fruit of the penance of my truthful speech, which I have performed for many eons.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुण्यें पोशिलीं असाधारणें। तियें तुझें गुण वानणें। देऊनि मज उत्तीर्ण, जालीं आजी॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: puṇyeṃ pośilīṃ asādhāraṇeṃ| tiyeṃ tujheṃ guṇa vānaṇeṃ| deūni maja uttīrṇa, jālīṃ ājī|| 33||
verses.meaning: The extraordinary merits I have accumulated, by praising Your virtues, have today made me debt-free.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी जीवित्वाच्या आडवीं। आतुडलो होतों मरणगांवीं।॥ ते अवदसाचि आधवी। फेडिली आजी॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī jīvitvācyā āḍavīṃ| ātuḍalo hotoṃ maraṇagāṃvīṃ||| te avadasāci ādhavī| pheḍilī ājī|| 34||
verses.meaning: The misfortune that had trapped me in the village of death, obstructing my life, has been dispelled today.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे गीता येणें नांवें नावाणिगी । जे अविद्या जिणोनि दाटुगी । ते कौर्ती तुझी आम्हांजोगी। वानावया जाली ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: je gītā yeṇeṃ nāṃveṃ nāvāṇigī | je avidyā jiṇoni dāṭugī | te kaurtī tujhī āmhāṃjogī| vānāvayā jālī || 35||
verses.meaning: The Gita, by this very name, is renowned; it is powerful, having conquered ignorance. Such is Your glory, suitable for us to praise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं निर्धना घरीं 'वानिवसें । महालक्ष्मी येऊनि बैसे । तयातें निर्धन ऐसें। म्हणों ये काई ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ nirdhanā gharīṃ 'vānivaseṃ | mahālakṣmī yeūni baise | tayāteṃ nirdhana aiseṃ| mhaṇoṃ ye kāī || 36||
verses.meaning: When Mahalakshmi herself comes and resides in the house of a poor person, can that person still be called poor?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां अंधकाराचिया ठाया । दैवें सुर्य आलिया। तो अंधारुचि जगा यया। प्रकाशु नोहे ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ aṃdhakārāciyā ṭhāyā | daiveṃ surya āliyā| to aṃdhāruci jagā yayā| prakāśu nohe || 37||
verses.meaning: If by chance the sun were to arrive in the realm of darkness, that darkness would not become light for this world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया देवाची पाहतां थोरी । विश्व परमाणुही दशा न ३७६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी धरी। तो भावाचिये सरोभरी। नव्हेचि काई॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā devācī pāhatāṃ thorī | viśva paramāṇuhī daśā na 376 śrījñāneśvarī dharī| to bhāvāciye sarobharī| navheci kāī|| 38||
verses.meaning: When one beholds the greatness of God, the universe itself does not hold even the status of an atom. How then could He not be contained within the fullness of devotion?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा मी गीता वाखाणीं। हे खपुष्पाची तुरेंबणी। परी समर्थे तुवां शिरयाणी। फेडिली ते॥३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā mī gītā vākhāṇīṃ| he khapuṣpācī tureṃbaṇī| parī samarthe tuvāṃ śirayāṇī| pheḍilī te||39||
verses.meaning: Just as I am explaining the Gita, it is like adorning myself with sky-flowers (impossible things). But you, O capable Krishna, have removed that impossibility.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तुझेनि प्रसार्दे। मी गीतापद्यें अगाधें। निरूपीन जी विशदें॥। ज्ञानदेवो म्हणे॥ ४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tujheni prasārde| mī gītāpadyeṃ agādheṃ| nirūpīna jī viśadeṃ||| jñānadevo mhaṇe|| 40||
verses.meaning: Therefore, by your grace, I, Dnyandev, will clearly expound upon the profound verses of the Gita.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अध्यायीं पंधरावां। श्रीकृष्णें तया पांडवा । शास्त्रसिद्धांतु आघवा । उगाणिला ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī adhyāyīṃ paṃdharāvāṃ| śrīkṛṣṇeṃ tayā pāṃḍavā | śāstrasiddhāṃtu āghavā | ugāṇilā || 49||
verses.meaning: Thus, in the fifteenth chapter, Shri Krishna revealed to Pandava the entire essence of the scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे वृक्षरूपक परिभाषा । केलें उपाधि रूप अशेषा। सद्वैद्यें जैसें दोषा। अंगलीना॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je vṛkṣarūpaka paribhāṣā | keleṃ upādhi rūpa aśeṣā| sadvaidyeṃ jaiseṃ doṣā| aṃgalīnā|| 42||
verses.meaning: Just as a skilled physician diagnoses and treats a disease that has taken root in the body, so too is the analogy of the tree, which represents the entire universe of limiting adjuncts (upadhis).

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कूटस्थु जो अक्षरु । दाविला पुरुषप्रकारु । तेणें उपहिताही आकारू । चैतन्या केला॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kūṭasthu jo akṣaru | dāvilā puruṣaprakāru | teṇeṃ upahitāhī ākārū | caitanyā kelā|| 43||
verses.meaning: And the immutable, unmanifested Purusha, who is the indwelling spirit, by His presence, gave form even to the manifested consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठीं उत्तमपुरुष। शब्दाचें करूनि मिष। दाविलें चोख । आत्मतत्त्व ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭhīṃ uttamapuruṣa| śabdāceṃ karūni miṣa| dāvileṃ cokha | ātmatattva || 44||
verses.meaning: Subsequently, the Supreme Being, using words as a pretext, revealed the pure essence of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आत्मविषयीं आंतुवट। साधन जें आंगदट । ज्ञान हेंही स्पष्ट। चावळला ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātmaviṣayīṃ āṃtuvaṭa| sādhana jeṃ āṃgadaṭa | jñāna heṃhī spaṣṭa| cāvaḻalā || 45 ||
verses.meaning: Even the knowledge that is a profound and difficult means to realize the Self is clearly just babbling.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि इये अध्यायीं। निरूप्य नुरेचि कांहीं। आतां गुरुशिष्यां दोहीं । स्नेहो लाहणा ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni iye adhyāyīṃ| nirūpya nureci kāṃhīṃ| ātāṃ guruśiṣyāṃ dohīṃ | sneho lāhaṇā || 46||
verses.meaning: Therefore, in this chapter, there remains nothing more to expound. Now, the love between the Guru and disciple is the only offering.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं इयेविषयीं कीर । जाणते बुझावळे अपार । परी मुमुक्ष इतर। साकांक्ष जाले॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ iyeviṣayīṃ kīra | jāṇate bujhāvaḻe apāra | parī mumukṣa itara| sākāṃkṣa jāle|| 47||
verses.meaning: Thus, regarding this matter, the wise have indeed understood it immensely. But other seekers of liberation have become desirous.

verses.shloka_devanagari: त्या मज पुरुषोत्तमा । ज्ञानें भेटे जो सुवर्मा । तो सर्वज्ञु तोचि सीमा । भक्‍तीचीही ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tyā maja puruṣottamā | jñāneṃ bheṭe jo suvarmā | to sarvajñu toci sīmā | bhak‍tīcīhī || 48||
verses.meaning: The one who meets Me, the Purushottama (Supreme Being), through knowledge, that wise one is the ultimate limit of devotion itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें हें त्रेलोक्यनायकें । बोलिलें अध्यायांत शलोकें । तेथें ज्ञानचि बहुतेकें । वानिलें तोषें ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ heṃ trelokyanāyakeṃ | bolileṃ adhyāyāṃta śalokeṃ | tetheṃ jñānaci bahutekeṃ | vānileṃ toṣeṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: Thus, the Lord of the three worlds spoke in this chapter through verses, wherein He mostly praised knowledge with great satisfaction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भरूनि प्रपंचाचा घोंटु। कीजे देखतांचि देखतया द्रष्टु। आनंदसाम्राज्यीं पाटु। बांधिजे जीवा ॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: bharūni prapaṃcācā ghoṃṭu| kīje dekhatāṃci dekhatayā draṣṭu| ānaṃdasāmrājyīṃ pāṭu| bāṃdhije jīvā || 50||
verses.meaning: Having drunk the draught of worldly existence, the seer, while seeing, becomes the seen, and the soul is crowned in the empire of bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येवढेया लाठेपणाचा उपावो । आनु नाहींचि म्हणे देवो। हा सम्यग्ज्ञानाचा रावो । उपायांमाजीं ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yevaḍheyā lāṭhepaṇācā upāvo | ānu nāhīṃci mhaṇe devo| hā samyagjñānācā rāvo | upāyāṃmājīṃ || 51||
verses.meaning: The Lord says that there is no other remedy for such arrogance. This is the king of all remedies, the perfect knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे आत्मजिज्ञासु जे होते । तिहीं तोषलेनि चित्ते । आदरें तया ज्ञानातें । बोंबाळिलें जीवें॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise ātmajijñāsu je hote | tihīṃ toṣaleni citte | ādareṃ tayā jñānāteṃ | boṃbāḻileṃ jīveṃ|| 52||
verses.meaning: Such seekers of the Self, with joyful hearts, reverently proclaimed that knowledge with all their being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां आवडी जेथ पडे । तयाची अवसरी पुढें पुढें। रिगों लागे हें घडे । प्रेम ऐसें ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ āvaḍī jetha paḍe | tayācī avasarī puḍheṃ puḍheṃ| rigoṃ lāge heṃ ghaḍe | prema aiseṃ || 53||
verses.meaning: Now, wherever love falls, its opportune moment comes forward, one after another; such is the nature of love.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जिज्ञासूंच्या पैकी । ज्ञानी प्रतीति होय ना जंब निकी। तंब योगक्षेमु ज्ञानविखीं। स्फुरेलचि कीं ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jijñāsūṃcyā paikī | jñānī pratīti hoya nā jaṃba nikī| taṃba yogakṣemu jñānavikhīṃ| sphurelaci kīṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: Therefore, among those who are seekers, until the knower attains perfect realization, the well-being and security in the realm of knowledge will surely continue to manifest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तेंचि सम्यग्ज्ञान । कैसेनि होय स्वाधीन । जालिया वृद्दियत्न। घडेल केवीं ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni teṃci samyagjñāna | kaiseni hoya svādhīna | jāliyā vṛddiyatna| ghaḍela kevīṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: Therefore, how can that true knowledge be attained? How can it be achieved through diligent effort?

verses.shloka_devanagari: 'कां उपजोंचि जें न लाहे। जें उपजलेंही अव्हांटा सूये । तें ज्ञानी विरुद्ध काय आहे। हें जाणावें कौं॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: 'kāṃ upajoṃci jeṃ na lāhe| jeṃ upajaleṃhī avhāṃṭā sūye | teṃ jñānī viruddha kāya āhe| heṃ jāṇāveṃ kauṃ|| 56||
verses.meaning: That which cannot even be born, and that which, even if born, takes a wrong path, how can such a thing be contrary to the wise? Know this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग जाणतया जें विरू। तयाची वाट वाहती करूं। ज्ञाना हित तेंचि विचारूं। सर्वभावे ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga jāṇatayā jeṃ virū| tayācī vāṭa vāhatī karūṃ| jñānā hita teṃci vicārūṃ| sarvabhāve || 57||
verses.meaning: Then, whatever is known to the wise, we shall make that path our own. We shall consider only that which is beneficial for knowledge, with our whole being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा जिज्ञासु तुम्हीं समस्तीं। भावो जो धरिला असे चित्तीं। तो पुरवावया लक्ष्मीपती। बोलिजेल॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jijñāsu tumhīṃ samastīṃ| bhāvo jo dharilā ase cittīṃ| to puravāvayā lakṣmīpatī| bolijela|| 58||
verses.meaning: To fulfill the earnest desire that you, the seekers, hold in your hearts, the Lord of Lakshmi (Vishnu) will now speak.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ज्ञानासि सुजन्म जोडे । आपली विश्रांतिही वरी वाढे । ते संपत्तीचे पवाडे। सांगिजेल दैवी॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jñānāsi sujanma joḍe | āpalī viśrāṃtihī varī vāḍhe | te saṃpattīce pavāḍe| sāṃgijela daivī|| 59||
verses.meaning: Knowledge finds its auspicious birth, and its own rest grows abundantly. The glory of such wealth is said to be divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि ज्ञानाचेनि कामाकारें। जे रागद्वेषांसि दे थारे) तिये आसुरियेहि घोरे। करील रूप॥ ६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jñānāceni kāmākāreṃ| je rāgadveṣāṃsi de thāre) tiye āsuriyehi ghore| karīla rūpa|| 60||
verses.meaning: And through the actions of knowledge, which give rise to attachment and aversion, it will assume a terrible demonic form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सहज इष्टानिष्टकरणी । दोघीचि इया कवतुकिणी। हे नबमाध्यायीं उभारणी । केली होती॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: sahaja iṣṭāniṣṭakaraṇī | doghīci iyā kavatukiṇī| he nabamādhyāyīṃ ubhāraṇī | kelī hotī||61||
verses.meaning: These two, good and evil, are merely playful acts. This was established in the ninth chapter.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ साउमा घेयावया उवबावो। तंव वबोडवळा आन प्रस्तावो। तरी तया प्रसंगें आतां देवो। निरूपीत असे॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha sāumā gheyāvayā uvabāvo| taṃva vaboḍavaḻā āna prastāvo| tarī tayā prasaṃgeṃ ātāṃ devo| nirūpīta ase||62||
verses.meaning: To understand this, there is a different occasion and a different context. Therefore, in that context, the Lord is now being described.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया निरूपणाचेनि नांबें। अध्याय पद सोळावें। लावणी पाहतां जाणावें । मागिलावरी॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā nirūpaṇāceni nāṃbeṃ| adhyāya pada soḻāveṃ| lāvaṇī pāhatāṃ jāṇāveṃ | māgilāvarī|| 63||
verses.meaning: Know that this sixteenth chapter, named after that discourse, is planted upon the previous one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें असो आतां प्रस्तुतीं। ज्ञानाच्या हिताहितीं । समर्था संपत्ती। इयाचि दोन्ही॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ aso ātāṃ prastutīṃ| jñānācyā hitāhitīṃ | samarthā saṃpattī| iyāci donhī|| 64||
verses.meaning: But let this be for now. In the matter of what is beneficial and what is harmful for knowledge, both these (the guru's grace and the disciple's effort) are capable and sufficient.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे मुमुक्षुमार्गीची बोळावी। जे मोहरात्रीची धर्मदिवी। ते आधीं तंव दैवी । संपत्ती ऐका ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: je mumukṣumārgīcī boḻāvī| je moharātrīcī dharmadivī| te ādhīṃ taṃva daivī | saṃpattī aikā || 65||
verses.meaning: Listen first to the divine wealth, which is the path for those seeking liberation, and the lamp that illuminates the night of delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ एक एकातें पोखी। ऐसे बहुत पदार्थ येकीं। संपादिजती ते लोकीं । संपत्ति म्हणिजे॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha eka ekāteṃ pokhī| aise bahuta padārtha yekīṃ| saṃpādijatī te lokīṃ | saṃpatti mhaṇije|| 66||
verses.meaning: Where one thing nourishes another, and many such things come together in unity, that is what people call 'wealth'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते दैवी सुखसंभवी। तेथ दैवगुणें येकोपजीवीं। जाली म्हणौनि दैवी । संपत्ति हे॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te daivī sukhasaṃbhavī| tetha daivaguṇeṃ yekopajīvīṃ| jālī mhaṇauni daivī | saṃpatti he|| 67||
verses.meaning: That divine happiness is born from good fortune; therefore, it is called divine wealth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां तयाचि दैवगुणां-। माजीं धुरेचा बैसणा। बैसे तया आकर्णा । अभय ऐसें॥६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ tayāci daivaguṇāṃ-| mājīṃ dhurecā baisaṇā| baise tayā ākarṇā | abhaya aiseṃ||68||
verses.meaning: Now, among those divine qualities, the foremost one, the seat of leadership, is established in the ear, which is fearlessness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी न घालूनि महापुरीं। न घेपे बुडणयाची शियारी । कां रोगु न गणिजे घरीं। पथ्याचिया ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī na ghālūni mahāpurīṃ| na ghepe buḍaṇayācī śiyārī | kāṃ rogu na gaṇije gharīṃ| pathyāciyā || 69||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not drown in a great flood by not entering it, or does not consider illness at home by observing a proper diet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कर्माकर्माचिया मोहरा । उठूं नेदूनि अहंकारा। संसाराचा दरारा। सांडणें येणें ॥ ७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā karmākarmāciyā moharā | uṭhūṃ nedūni ahaṃkārā| saṃsārācā darārā| sāṃḍaṇeṃ yeṇeṃ || 70||
verses.meaning: In the same way, one should not allow ego to arise from good or bad deeds, and thereby overcome the fear of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा ऐक्यभावाचेनि पैसें। दुजे मानूनि आत्मा ऐसें। भयवार्ता देशें। दवडणें जे॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā aikyabhāvāceni paiseṃ| duje mānūni ātmā aiseṃ| bhayavārtā deśeṃ| davaḍaṇeṃ je|| 71||
verses.meaning: Or, by the vastness of oneness, considering the other as the Self, thereby banishing all talk of fear from the land.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाणी बुडऊं ये मिठातें। तंव मीठचि पाणी आतें। तेवीं आपण जालेनि अद्वैतें। नाशे भय॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṇī buḍaūṃ ye miṭhāteṃ| taṃva mīṭhaci pāṇī āteṃ| tevīṃ āpaṇa jāleni advaiteṃ| nāśe bhaya|| 72||
verses.meaning: Just as salt dissolves into water, becoming one with it, so too does fear vanish when one realizes the non-dual nature of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा अभय येणें नांवें। बोलिजे तें हें जाणावें । सम्यगूज्ञानाचें आधवें। धांबणें हें ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā abhaya yeṇeṃ nāṃveṃ| bolije teṃ heṃ jāṇāveṃ | samyagūjñānāceṃ ādhaveṃ| dhāṃbaṇeṃ heṃ || 73||
verses.meaning: Know that this fearlessness, by which it is known, is the very foundation of perfect knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां सत्त्वशुद्धी जे म्हणिजे। ते ऐशा चिन्हीं जाणिजे । तरी जळे ना विझे। राखोंडी जैसी ॥ ७४॥
