verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ sattvaśuddhī je mhaṇije| te aiśā cinhīṃ jāṇije | tarī jaḻe nā vijhe| rākhoṃḍī jaisī || 74||
verses.meaning: Now, what is called purity of sattva (goodness) is known by these signs: it is like ash, which neither burns nor extinguishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां पाडिवा वाढी न मगे । अंबसे तुटी सांडूनि मार्गे । माजीं अतिसूक्ष्म अंगें । चंद्र जैसा राहे ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ pāḍivā vāḍhī na mage | aṃbase tuṭī sāṃḍūni mārge | mājīṃ atisūkṣma aṃgeṃ | caṃdra jaisā rāhe || 75 ||
verses.meaning: Or, just as the moon, after the new moon day (Padiva) has passed and the crescent has grown, and then the full moon has waned, still remains in its extremely subtle form, so too the Self remains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी वार्षिया नाहीं मांडिली । ग्रीष्में नाहीं सांडिली । माजीं निजरूपें निवडली । गंगा जैसी॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī vārṣiyā nāhīṃ māṃḍilī | grīṣmeṃ nāhīṃ sāṃḍilī | mājīṃ nijarūpeṃ nivaḍalī | gaṃgā jaisī|| 76||
verses.meaning: Just as the Ganges, without being created by the monsoon or abandoned by the summer, always flows in its own inherent form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी संकल्पविकल्पाची वोढी। सांडूनि रजतमाची कावडी। भोगितां निजधर्माची आवडी । बुद्धि उरे॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī saṃkalpavikalpācī voḍhī| sāṃḍūni rajatamācī kāvaḍī| bhogitāṃ nijadharmācī āvaḍī | buddhi ure|| 77||
verses.meaning: Similarly, by abandoning the burden of संकल्प (thoughts/resolutions) and विकल्प (doubts/indecision), which are like the carrying pole of Rajas (passion) and Tamas (ignorance), and by delighting in one's own true nature (Dharma), the intellect becomes clear.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियवर्गी दाखविलिया। विरुद्धा अथवा भलीया । ३७८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी विस्मयो कांहीं केलिया। नुठी चित्तीं॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyavargī dākhaviliyā| viruddhā athavā bhalīyā | 378 śrījñāneśvarī vismayo kāṃhīṃ keliyā| nuṭhī cittīṃ|| 78||
verses.meaning: When the senses perceive things, whether good or bad, no surprise arises in the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गांवा गेलिया बल्लभु। 'पतित्रतेचा विरहक्षोभु। भलतेसणी हानिलाभु। न मनी जेवीं ॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: gāṃvā geliyā ballabhu| 'patitratecā virahakṣobhu| bhalatesaṇī hānilābhu| na manī jevīṃ ||79||
verses.meaning: Just as a chaste wife, whose beloved has gone to another village, does not consider any gain or loss from anyone else's advances, so too the true seeker remains undisturbed by worldly distractions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं सत्स्वरूप रुचलेपणें। बुद्धी जें ऐसें अनन्य होणें। ते सत्त्वशुद्धी म्हणे । केशिहंता॥ ८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ satsvarūpa rucalepaṇeṃ| buddhī jeṃ aiseṃ ananya hoṇeṃ| te sattvaśuddhī mhaṇe | keśihaṃtā|| 80||
verses.meaning: Just as the intellect, by relishing the true nature of existence, becomes one with it, that is called purity of sattva, says the slayer of Keshi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां आत्मलाभाविखीं। ज्ञानयोगामाजीं एकीं। जे आपुलिया ठाकीं। हांबें भरे॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ ātmalābhāvikhīṃ| jñānayogāmājīṃ ekīṃ| je āpuliyā ṭhākīṃ| hāṃbeṃ bhare|| 81||
verses.meaning: Now, regarding the attainment of the Self, in the path of knowledge, some, in their own place, are filled with pride.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ सगळिये चित्तवृत्ती। त्यागु करणें या रीती । निष्कामें पूर्णाहुती । हुताशीं जैसी ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha sagaḻiye cittavṛttī| tyāgu karaṇeṃ yā rītī | niṣkāmeṃ pūrṇāhutī | hutāśīṃ jaisī || 82||
verses.meaning: Therefore, all mental modifications should be renounced in this manner, like a complete offering (purnahuti) made selflessly into the sacrificial fire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां सुकुळीनें आपुली । आत्मजा सत्कुळींचि दिधली । हें असो लक्ष्मी स्थिरावली । मुकुंदीं जैसी ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ sukuḻīneṃ āpulī | ātmajā satkuḻīṃci didhalī | heṃ aso lakṣmī sthirāvalī | mukuṃdīṃ jaisī || 83||
verses.meaning: Or like a delicate maiden given in marriage to a good family. Let that be; it is like Lakshmi becoming stable with Mukunda.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें निर्विकल्पपणें। जें योगज्ञानींच या वृत्तिक होणें। तो तिजा गुण म्हणे । श्रीकृष्णनाथु॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ nirvikalpapaṇeṃ| jeṃ yogajñānīṃca yā vṛttika hoṇeṃ| to tijā guṇa mhaṇe | śrīkṛṣṇanāthu|| 84||
verses.meaning: Lord Krishna says that the third quality is the state of being without thought or concept, which is attained by yogis through knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां देहवाचाचित्तें । यथासंपन्नें वित्तें। वैरी जालियाही आतातें॥ न वंचणें जें कां॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ dehavācācitteṃ | yathāsaṃpanneṃ vitteṃ| vairī jāliyāhī ātāteṃ|| na vaṃcaṇeṃ jeṃ kāṃ|| 85||
verses.meaning: Now, with body, speech, and mind, and with all one's wealth, even if an enemy were to come, one should not deceive them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पत्र पुष्प छाया। फळ मूळ धनंजया । वाटेचा न चुके आलिया । वृक्षु जैसा॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: patra puṣpa chāyā| phaḻa mūḻa dhanaṃjayā | vāṭecā na cuke āliyā | vṛkṣu jaisā|| 86||
verses.meaning: Just as a tree, when approached, never withholds its leaves, flowers, shade, fruits, or roots, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें मनौनि धनधान्यवरी । विद्यमाने आल्या अवसरीं । श्रांतांचिये मनोहारीं । उपयोगा जाणें ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ manauni dhanadhānyavarī | vidyamāne ālyā avasarīṃ | śrāṃtāṃciye manohārīṃ | upayogā jāṇeṃ || 87||
verses.meaning: Just as, when wealth and grain are present, they are used to please the weary, so too should one's possessions be utilized for the benefit of others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया नांब जाण दान। जें मोक्षनिधानार्चे अंजन । हें असो आइक चिन्ह। दमाचें तें ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā nāṃba jāṇa dāna| jeṃ mokṣanidhānārce aṃjana | heṃ aso āika cinha| damāceṃ teṃ || 88||
verses.meaning: Know that this self-restraint is the collyrium that reveals the treasure of liberation. Let this be; now listen to the characteristics of self-control.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी विषयेंद्रियां मिळणी। करूनि घापे वितुटणी । जैसें तोडिजे खडूगपाणी। पारकेया । ८९॥ तैसा विषयजातांचा वारा । वाजों नेदिजे इंद्रियद्वारां। इयें बांधोनि प्रत्याहारा। हातीं बोपी॥ ९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī viṣayeṃdriyāṃ miḻaṇī| karūni ghāpe vituṭaṇī | jaiseṃ toḍije khaḍūgapāṇī| pārakeyā | 89|| taisā viṣayajātāṃcā vārā | vājoṃ nedije iṃdriyadvārāṃ| iyeṃ bāṃdhoni pratyāhārā| hātīṃ bopī|| 90||
verses.meaning: Just as a sword is used to sever the bond between a person and their enemy, so too should the connection between the senses and their objects be severed. The wind of worldly desires should not be allowed to enter through the doors of the senses; instead, these senses should be bound by the practice of Pratyahara, thus offering them into the hands of the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आंतुला चित्ताचें अंगबरी । प्रवृत्ति पळे पर बाहेरी। आगी सुयिजे दाहींहि द्वारीं । बैराग्याची ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṃtulā cittāceṃ aṃgabarī | pravṛtti paḻe para bāherī| āgī suyije dāhīṃhi dvārīṃ | bairāgyācī || 91||
verses.meaning: When the inner consciousness is thus purified, all worldly tendencies flee outwards. It is as if the fire of detachment is kindled at all ten doors (senses and faculties).

verses.shloka_devanagari: इवासोश्वासाहुनी बहुवसें । व्रतें आचरे खरपुसें । बोसंतिता रात्रिदिवसें। नाराणुक जया॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ivāsośvāsāhunī bahuvaseṃ | vrateṃ ācare kharapuseṃ | bosaṃtitā rātridivaseṃ| nārāṇuka jayā|| 92||
verses.meaning: More than breathing, he performs severe vows, day and night, without ceasing, for the sake of Narayana.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं दमु ऐसा म्हणिपे। तो हा जाण स्वरूपें। यागार्थुहि संक्षेपें। सांगों ऐक ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ damu aisā mhaṇipe| to hā jāṇa svarūpeṃ| yāgārthuhi saṃkṣepeṃ| sāṃgoṃ aika || 93||
verses.meaning: That which is called 'damu' (self-restraint), know it to be this in essence. I will briefly explain its purpose as well; listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी ब्राह्मण करूनि धुरे। स्त्रियादिक पैल मेरे। माझारीं अधिकारें। आपुलाळेनि॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī brāhmaṇa karūni dhure| striyādika paila mere| mājhārīṃ adhikāreṃ| āpulāḻeni|| 94||
verses.meaning: Thus, Brahmins and women, and others, each according to their own capacity, are on the other side (of the river of worldly existence).

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया जे सर्वोत्तम । भजनीय देवताधर्म । तें तेणें यथागम। विधी यजिजे॥ ९५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā je sarvottama | bhajanīya devatādharma | teṃ teṇeṃ yathāgama| vidhī yajije|| 95 ||
verses.meaning: Whatever is considered the highest and most worshipful deity or dharma by an individual, that should be worshipped by them according to the prescribed rituals and scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा द्विज षट्कमे करी । शूद्र तयातें नमस्कारी । कीं दोहींसही सरोभरी । निपजे यागु॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā dvija ṣaṭkame karī | śūdra tayāteṃ namaskārī | kīṃ dohīṃsahī sarobharī | nipaje yāgu|| 96||
verses.meaning: Just as a Brahmin performs the six prescribed duties and a Shudra bows to him, so too does the fruit of their actions become equal for both.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अधिकारपर्यालोचें। हें यज्ञ करणें सर्वांचें। परी विष फळाशेचें।॥। न घापे माजीं ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ adhikāraparyāloceṃ| heṃ yajña karaṇeṃ sarvāṃceṃ| parī viṣa phaḻāśeceṃ|||| na ghāpe mājīṃ || 97||
verses.meaning: Similarly, considering the eligibility of all, this sacrifice is for everyone. But the poison of desiring the fruit of action should not be included in it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मी कर्ता ऐसा भावो। नेदिजे देहाचेनि द्वारें जावो । ना वेदाज्ञेसि तरी ठावो । होइजे स्वयें ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mī kartā aisā bhāvo| nedije dehāceni dvāreṃ jāvo | nā vedājñesi tarī ṭhāvo | hoije svayeṃ || 98||
verses.meaning: And the thought, "I am the doer," should not be allowed to enter through the body. Otherwise, one should become the very embodiment of the Vedic injunctions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना एवं यज्ञु। सर्वत्र जाण साजु। कैवल्यमार्गांचा अभिजु। सांगाती हा॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā evaṃ yajñu| sarvatra jāṇa sāju| kaivalyamārgāṃcā abhiju| sāṃgātī hā|| 99||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, know this sacrifice to be ever-present everywhere, the constant companion on the path to liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां चेंडुवें भूमी हाणिजे। नव्हे तो हाता आणिजे। कीं शेतीं बीं विखुरिजे । परी पिकीं लक्ष॥ ९००॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ ceṃḍuveṃ bhūmī hāṇije| navhe to hātā āṇije| kīṃ śetīṃ bīṃ vikhurije | parī pikīṃ lakṣa|| 900||
verses.meaning: Now, a ball is struck to the ground, but it is brought back to the hand. Or, seeds are scattered in the field, but the focus is on the harvest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी ठेविलें देखावया। आदर कोजे दिविया। कां शाखा फळें यावया । सिंपिजे मूळ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī ṭhevileṃ dekhāvayā| ādara koje diviyā| kāṃ śākhā phaḻeṃ yāvayā | siṃpije mūḻa|| 1||
verses.meaning: Or, to see something, one lights a lamp with reverence. Or, to make the branches bear fruit, the roots are watered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें बहु असो आरिसा। आपणपें देखावया जैसा। पुढतपुढती बहुवसा। उटिजे प्रीती ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ bahu aso ārisā| āpaṇapeṃ dekhāvayā jaisā| puḍhatapuḍhatī bahuvasā| uṭije prītī || 2||
verses.meaning: Let this be enough. Just as one repeatedly cleans a mirror with love to see oneself clearly, so too should one cleanse the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा वेदप्रतिपाद्यु जो ईश्वरूु। तो होआवयालागीं गोचरु । श्रुतीचा निरंतरु । अभ्यासु करणें॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā vedapratipādyu jo īśvarūu| to hoāvayālāgīṃ gocaru | śrutīcā niraṃtaru | abhyāsu karaṇeṃ||3||
verses.meaning: Similarly, to perceive God, who is revealed by the Vedas, one must continuously study the scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें द्विजांसीच ब्रह्मसूत्र। येरां स्तोत्र कां नाममंत्र । आवर्तवणें पवित्र। पावाबया तत्त्व ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ dvijāṃsīca brahmasūtra| yerāṃ stotra kāṃ nāmamaṃtra | āvartavaṇeṃ pavitra| pāvābayā tattva || 4||
verses.meaning: That Brahma Sutra is for the twice-born (Brahmins); for others, chanting hymns or divine names is sacred for attaining the truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था गा स्वाध्यावो। बोलिजे तो हा म्हणे देवो। आतां तप शब्दाभिप्रावो। आईक सांगों॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā gā svādhyāvo| bolije to hā mhaṇe devo| ātāṃ tapa śabdābhiprāvo| āīka sāṃgoṃ|| 5||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, this is what is called Swadhyaya (self-study). Now, listen as I explain the meaning of the word 'Tapa' (austerity).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी दानें सर्वस्व देणें । वेंचणें तें व्यर्थ करणें । जैसें फळोनि स्वयें सुकणें। इंद्रावणी जेबीं॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī dāneṃ sarvasva deṇeṃ | veṃcaṇeṃ teṃ vyartha karaṇeṃ | jaiseṃ phaḻoni svayeṃ sukaṇeṃ| iṃdrāvaṇī jebīṃ||6||
verses.meaning: Giving away everything in charity, or spending it wastefully, is like the Indrayani creeper that bears fruit and then withers away on its own.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना धूपाचा अग्निप्रवेशु, कनकीं तुकाचा नाशु । पितृपक्षु 'पोषिता र्‍हासु। चंद्राचा जैसा ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā dhūpācā agnipraveśu, kanakīṃ tukācā nāśu | pitṛpakṣu 'poṣitā r‍hāsu| caṃdrācā jaisā || 7||
verses.meaning: Just as various incenses are consumed by fire, or gold is refined by melting, or the moon wanes during the dark fortnight, so too does the physical body diminish and decay.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा स्वरूपाचिया प्रसरा-। लागीं प्राणेंद्रियशरीरां। आटणी करणें जे वीरा । तेंचि तप॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā svarūpāciyā prasarā-| lāgīṃ prāṇeṃdriyaśarīrāṃ| āṭaṇī karaṇeṃ je vīrā | teṃci tapa|| 8||
verses.meaning: Just as, O brave one, the austerity that involves the complete absorption of the vital breath, senses, and body for the manifestation of the true Self, that alone is true penance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा अनारिसें। तपाचे रूप जरी असे। तरी जाण जेवीं दुधीं हंसें। सूदली चांचू ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā anāriseṃ| tapāce rūpa jarī ase| tarī jāṇa jevīṃ dudhīṃ haṃseṃ| sūdalī cāṃcū || 9||
verses.meaning: Or, if it is an unblemished form of penance, then know that it is like a swan purifying its beak in milk.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें देहजीबाचिये मिळणीं। जो उदयजत सूये पाणी। तो विवेक अंतःकरणी । जागवीजे॥ ११०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ dehajībāciye miḻaṇīṃ| jo udayajata sūye pāṇī| to viveka aṃtaḥkaraṇī | jāgavīje|| 110||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun rises from the union of the body and the soul, so too should discrimination be awakened within the heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहतां आत्मयाकडे। बुद्धीचा पैसु सांकडें। सनिद्र स्वप्न बुडे। जागणीं जैसें ॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāhatāṃ ātmayākaḍe| buddhīcā paisu sāṃkaḍeṃ| sanidra svapna buḍe| jāgaṇīṃ jaiseṃ || 11||
verses.meaning: When one looks at the Self, the intellect's grasp becomes narrow, just as a dream, whether with or without sleep, vanishes upon waking.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा आत्मपर्यालोचु। प्रवर्त जो साचु । तपाचा हा निर्वेचु। धनुर्धगा॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā ātmaparyālocu| pravarta jo sācu | tapācā hā nirvecu| dhanurdhagā|| 12||
verses.meaning: Just as the true and unwavering contemplation of the Self is indeed the highest penance, O Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां बाळाच्या हितीं स्तन्य । जैसें नानाभूतीं चैतन्य । तैसें प्राणिमात्रीं सौजन्य। आर्जव तें॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ bāḻācyā hitīṃ stanya | jaiseṃ nānābhūtīṃ caitanya | taiseṃ prāṇimātrīṃ saujanya| ārjava teṃ|| 13||
verses.meaning: Just as a mother's milk is for the child's well-being, and consciousness is present in all beings, so too is gentleness and straightforwardness inherent in all living creatures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जगाचिया सुखोद्देशें । शरीरवाचामानसें । राहाटणें तें अहिंसे। रूप जाण॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jagāciyā sukhoddeśeṃ | śarīravācāmānaseṃ | rāhāṭaṇeṃ teṃ ahiṃse| rūpa jāṇa|| 14||
verses.meaning: And to act with body, speech, and mind for the well-being of the world, know that to be the form of non-violence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां तीख होऊनि मवाळ । जैसें जातीचें मुकुळ। कां तेज परी शीतळ शशांकाचें ॥ ९१५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ tīkha hoūni mavāḻa | jaiseṃ jātīceṃ mukuḻa| kāṃ teja parī śītaḻa śaśāṃkāceṃ || 915||
verses.meaning: Now, like the bud of a jasmine flower, which is sharp yet soft, or like the moon's radiance, which is bright yet cool.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शके दावितांचि रोगु फेडूं। आणि जिभे तरी नव्हे कडु। तें बोखदु नाहीं मा घडु। उपमा कैंची ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: śake dāvitāṃci rogu pheḍūṃ| āṇi jibhe tarī navhe kaḍu| teṃ bokhadu nāhīṃ mā ghaḍu| upamā kaiṃcī || 16||
verses.meaning: A medicine that cures the disease as soon as it is shown, and yet does not taste bitter to the tongue—such a medicine is truly rare. What can it be compared to?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी मऊपणें बुबुळें। झगडतांही परी नाडळे। एऱ्हवीं फोडी कोंराळें। पाणी जैसें ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī maūpaṇeṃ bubuḻeṃ| jhagaḍatāṃhī parī nāḍaḻe| eṟhavīṃ phoḍī koṃrāḻeṃ| pāṇī jaiseṃ || 17||
verses.meaning: Even though the soft eyeballs rub against each other, they are not harmed, just as water, though soft, can erode hard rock.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें तोडावया संदेह। तीख जैसें कां लोह श्राव्यत्बें तरी माधुर्य । पायीं घालीं ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ toḍāvayā saṃdeha| tīkha jaiseṃ kāṃ loha śrāvyatbeṃ tarī mādhurya | pāyīṃ ghālīṃ || 98||
verses.meaning: Just as a sharp iron tool cuts through doubt, so too does the sweetness of this discourse lay itself at your feet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐकों ठातां कौतुकें । कानातेंचि निघती मुखें । जें साचारिवेचेनि बिकें। ब्रह्मही भेदी॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aikoṃ ṭhātāṃ kautukeṃ | kānāteṃci nighatī mukheṃ | jeṃ sācāriveceni bikeṃ| brahmahī bhedī|| 19||
verses.meaning: When one listens with curiosity, the ears themselves become mouths, for with the power of truth, even Brahman can be pierced.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना प्रियपणें। कोणातेंही झकऊं नेणें । यथार्थ तरी खुपणें । नाहीं कवणा॥ १२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā priyapaṇeṃ| koṇāteṃhī jhakaūṃ neṇeṃ | yathārtha tarī khupaṇeṃ | nāhīṃ kavaṇā|| 120||
verses.meaning: Indeed, it does not know how to deceive anyone with affection; in truth, no one can truly grasp it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं गोरी कीर काना गोड । ३८० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी परी साचाचा पाखाळीं कौड। आगीचे करणें उघड। परी जळों तें साच॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ gorī kīra kānā goḍa | 380 śrījñāneśvarī parī sācācā pākhāḻīṃ kauḍa| āgīce karaṇeṃ ughaḍa| parī jaḻoṃ teṃ sāca|| 21||
verses.meaning: Indeed, the words may sound pleasant to the ear, but the true test is in their essence, like fire, whose nature is to burn, and its truth is in that burning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कानीं लागतां महुर। अर्थे विभांडी जिव्हार। तें वाचा नव्हे सुंदर। लांबचि पां॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kānīṃ lāgatāṃ mahura| arthe vibhāṃḍī jivhāra| teṃ vācā navhe suṃdara| lāṃbaci pāṃ|| 22||
verses.meaning: When words, upon reaching the ears, pierce the heart with their meaning, such speech is not beautiful, but rather long and drawn out.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी अहितीं कोपोनि सोप। लालनीं मऊ जेसें पुष्प। तिये मातेचें स्वरूप। जैसें कां होय॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī ahitīṃ koponi sopa| lālanīṃ maū jeseṃ puṣpa| tiye māteceṃ svarūpa| jaiseṃ kāṃ hoya|| 23||
verses.meaning: Just as a mother's anger towards her children is soft like a flower, so too is her true nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें श्रवणसुखचतुर। 'परिणमोनि साचार। बोलणें जें अविकार|। तें सत्य येथें॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ śravaṇasukhacatura| 'pariṇamoni sācāra| bolaṇeṃ jeṃ avikāra|| teṃ satya yetheṃ|| 24||
verses.meaning: Just as the joy of hearing, when it truly matures, transforms into speech that is pure and unchanging, that indeed is the truth here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां घालितांहि पाणी। पाषाणीं न निघे आणी। कां मथिलिया लोणी। कांजी नेदी॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ ghālitāṃhi pāṇī| pāṣāṇīṃ na nighe āṇī| kāṃ mathiliyā loṇī| kāṃjī nedī|| 25||
verses.meaning: Now, even if you pour water, it won't sprout from a stone. Nor will buttermilk yield butter if churned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: त्वचा पायें शिरीं। हाळलेयाही फडे न करी । बसंतींहीं अंबरी । न होती फुलें॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tvacā pāyeṃ śirīṃ| hāḻaleyāhī phaḍe na karī | basaṃtīṃhīṃ aṃbarī | na hotī phuleṃ|| 26||
verses.meaning: Even if the skin of the feet were placed on the head, it would not become a crown. Similarly, flowers do not bloom in the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना रंभेचेनिही रूपें। शुकीं नुठिजेचि कंदरपे। कां भस्मीं वन्हि न उददीपे। घृतेंही जेवीं ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā raṃbhecenihī rūpeṃ| śukīṃ nuṭhijeci kaṃdarape| kāṃ bhasmīṃ vanhi na udadīpe| ghṛteṃhī jevīṃ || 27||
verses.meaning: Just as a parrot is not aroused by the various forms of Rambha (a celestial nymph), or as fire does not ignite in ash even with ghee, so too is the nature of the enlightened.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेबींचि कुमारु क्रोधें भरे। तैसिया मंत्राचीं बीजाक्षरें। तियें निमित्तेंही अपारें। मीनलिया॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tebīṃci kumāru krodheṃ bhare| taisiyā maṃtrācīṃ bījākṣareṃ| tiyeṃ nimitteṃhī apāreṃ| mīnaliyā|| 28||
verses.meaning: Just as a child born from a seed is filled with anger, so too are the seed-letters of a mantra. Even when these are joined together, they become immeasurable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि धातयाही पायां पडतां।॥ नुठी गतायु पंडुसुता। तैसी नुपजे उपजवितां। क्रोधोर्मी गा॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari dhātayāhī pāyāṃ paḍatāṃ||| nuṭhī gatāyu paṃḍusutā| taisī nupaje upajavitāṃ| krodhormī gā|| 29||
verses.meaning: Even if one falls at the feet of the destroyer, O son of Pandu, the life that has passed does not return. Similarly, when anger arises, it does not arise from a desire to create, but rather from a destructive impulse.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अक्रोधत्व ऐसें। नांव तें ये दशे । जाण ऐसें श्रीनिवासें । म्हणितलें तया ॥ १३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: akrodhatva aiseṃ| nāṃva teṃ ye daśe | jāṇa aiseṃ śrīnivāseṃ | mhaṇitaleṃ tayā || 130||
verses.meaning: Lord Shrinivasa said that this state of being free from anger is known as 'akrodhatva'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां मृत्तिकात्यागें घटु। तंतुत्यागें पटु। त्यजिजे जेवीं वटु। बीजत्यागें॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ mṛttikātyāgeṃ ghaṭu| taṃtutyāgeṃ paṭu| tyajije jevīṃ vaṭu| bījatyāgeṃ|| 39||
verses.meaning: Just as a pot is abandoned by discarding the clay, a cloth by discarding the threads, and a banyan tree by discarding its seed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां त्यजूनि भिंतीमात्र। त्यजिजे आघवेंचि चित्र। कां निद्रात्यागें विचित्र। स्वप्नजाळ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ tyajūni bhiṃtīmātra| tyajije āghaveṃci citra| kāṃ nidrātyāgeṃ vicitra| svapnajāḻa|| 32||
verses.meaning: Just as by abandoning the wall, all the paintings on it are abandoned, or by abandoning sleep, the strange web of dreams is abandoned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना जळत्यागें तरंग । वर्षात्यागें मेघ। त्यजिजती जैसे भोग। धनत्यागें॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā jaḻatyāgeṃ taraṃga | varṣātyāgeṃ megha| tyajijatī jaise bhoga| dhanatyāgeṃ|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as water gives up its waves, clouds give up their rain, and a wealthy person gives up their possessions, so too should one renounce worldly pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं बुद्धिमंतीं देहीं । अहंता सांडूनि पाहीं । सांडिजे अशेषही । संसारजात॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ buddhimaṃtīṃ dehīṃ | ahaṃtā sāṃḍūni pāhīṃ | sāṃḍije aśeṣahī | saṃsārajāta|| 34||
verses.meaning: Similarly, in the bodies of the wise, by abandoning ego, the entire cycle of worldly existence is relinquished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया नांव त्यागु। म्हणे तो यज्ञांगु। हें मानूनि सुभगु । पार्थु पुसे॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā nāṃva tyāgu| mhaṇe to yajñāṃgu| heṃ mānūni subhagu | pārthu puse|| 35||
verses.meaning: Considering this renunciation as a blessed part of the sacrifice, Arjuna then asks.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां शांतीचें लिंग। तें व्यक्‍त मज सांग। देवो म्हणती चांग। अवधान देई ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ śāṃtīceṃ liṃga| teṃ vyak‍ta maja sāṃga| devo mhaṇatī cāṃga| avadhāna deī || 36||
verses.meaning: Now, tell me, what is the manifest form of peace? The gods say, "Good, pay attention."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी गिळोनि ज्ञेयातें। ज्ञाता ज्ञानही माघोतें। हारपे निरुतें। ते शांति पैं गा।॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī giḻoni jñeyāteṃ| jñātā jñānahī māghoteṃ| hārape niruteṃ| te śāṃti paiṃ gā||| 37||
verses.meaning: Thus, having absorbed the knowable, the knower and the knowledge also recede. This indeed is true peace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा प्रळयांबूचा उभडु। बुडवुनि विश्वाचा पवाडु। होय आपणपें निबिडु । आपणचि ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā praḻayāṃbūcā ubhaḍu| buḍavuni viśvācā pavāḍu| hoya āpaṇapeṃ nibiḍu | āpaṇaci || 38||
verses.meaning: Just as the deluge of the cosmic dissolution, having submerged the vast expanse of the universe, becomes intensely dense within itself, so too does the Self remain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग उगम ओघ सिंधु । हा नुरेचि व्यवहारभेदु। परी जलैक्याचा बोधु। तोही कवणा ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ugama ogha siṃdhu | hā nureci vyavahārabhedu| parī jalaikyācā bodhu| tohī kavaṇā || 39||
verses.meaning: Then the source, the stream, the ocean—this distinction of behavior does not remain. But the understanding of the oneness of water, to whom does that even occur?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी ज्ञेया देतां मिठी । ज्ञातृत्वही पडे पोटीं । मग उरे तेंचि किरीटी। शांतीचें रूप॥ १४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī jñeyā detāṃ miṭhī | jñātṛtvahī paḍe poṭīṃ | maga ure teṃci kirīṭī| śāṃtīceṃ rūpa|| 140||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the knowable is embraced, even the state of being a knower dissolves within. Then, O Kiriti, what remains is the very form of peace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां कदर्थवीत व्याधी । बळीकरणाचिया आधीं। आपपरु न शोधी । सह्वैद्यु जैसा ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ kadarthavīta vyādhī | baḻīkaraṇāciyā ādhīṃ| āpaparu na śodhī | sahvaidyu jaisā || 49 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a good physician, before strengthening the body, first eliminates the disease without distinguishing between 'mine' or 'yours'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां चिखलीं रुतली गाये। धडभाकड न पाहे । जो तियेचिया ग्लानी होये । 'कालाभुला॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ cikhalīṃ rutalī gāye| dhaḍabhākaḍa na pāhe | jo tiyeciyā glānī hoye | 'kālābhulā|| 42||
verses.meaning: Just as a cow stuck in mud does not look at the good or bad of the path, but only becomes confused and distressed by its predicament.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना बुडतयातें सकरुणु। न पुसे अंत्यजु कां ब्राह्मणु । काढूनि राखे प्राणु। हेंचि जाणे॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā buḍatayāteṃ sakaruṇu| na puse aṃtyaju kāṃ brāhmaṇu | kāḍhūni rākhe prāṇu| heṃci jāṇe|| 43||
verses.meaning: With compassion, it saves many who are drowning, not distinguishing between an untouchable or a Brahmin. It knows only to rescue and preserve life.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं माय वनीं पापिये। उघडी केली विपायें। ते नेसल्यावीण न पाहे । शिष्टु जैसा ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ māya vanīṃ pāpiye| ughaḍī kelī vipāyeṃ| te nesalyāvīṇa na pāhe | śiṣṭu jaisā || 44||
verses.meaning: Just as a virtuous person would not look at a mother who has been accidentally exposed in the forest, so too, one should not look at such a sight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें अज्ञानप्रमादादिकीं। कां प्राक्तनहीन सदोखी । निंदत्वाच्या सर्वविखीं । खिळिले जे॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ ajñānapramādādikīṃ| kāṃ prāktanahīna sadokhī | niṃdatvācyā sarvavikhīṃ | khiḻile je|| 45||
verses.meaning: Similarly, those who are bound by ignorance, error, or misfortune, and are thus entangled in all forms of blameworthiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयां आंगीक आपुलें) देऊनियां भलें। विसरविजती सलें। सलतीं तियें ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāṃ āṃgīka āpuleṃ) deūniyāṃ bhaleṃ| visaravijatī saleṃ| salatīṃ tiyeṃ || 46||
verses.meaning: By bestowing upon them their own divine essence, they are made to forget the sorrows that afflict them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा पुढिलाचा दोखु। करूनि आपुलिये दिठी चोखु । मग घापे अवलोकु । तयावरी ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā puḍhilācā dokhu| karūni āpuliye diṭhī cokhu | maga ghāpe avaloku | tayāvarī || 47||
verses.meaning: First, one must cleanse their own vision of any faults, and only then should they cast their gaze upon others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा पुजूनि देवो पाहिजे। पेरूनि शेता जाइजे । तोषौनि प्रसादु घेइजे। अतिथीचा ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā pujūni devo pāhije| perūni śetā jāije | toṣauni prasādu gheije| atithīcā || 48||
verses.meaning: Just as one worships God and then goes to the field to sow, or receives the prasada after satisfying a guest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आपुलेनि गुणें। पुढिलाचें उणें। फेडूनियां पाहणें। तयाकडे ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ āpuleni guṇeṃ| puḍhilāceṃ uṇeṃ| pheḍūniyāṃ pāhaṇeṃ| tayākaḍe || 49||
verses.meaning: Similarly, by one's own virtues, one should look upon others' shortcomings with the intention of rectifying them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि न विंधिजें वर्मी । नातुडविजे अकर्मी । न बोलविजे नामीं । सदोषीं तिहीं ॥ ९१५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni na viṃdhijeṃ varmī | nātuḍavije akarmī | na bolavije nāmīṃ | sadoṣīṃ tihīṃ || 9150||
verses.meaning: Without it, one cannot be pierced in the vital spot, nor caught in unrighteous deeds, nor made to utter the name in a flawed manner, in these three ways.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरी कोणे एके उपायें। पडिलें तें उभें होये। तेंच कीजे परी घाये। नेदावे वर्मी॥५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: varī koṇe eke upāyeṃ| paḍileṃ teṃ ubheṃ hoye| teṃca kīje parī ghāye| nedāve varmī||51||
verses.meaning: By some means or another, that which has fallen can rise again. That indeed should be done, but do not strike at the vital spot.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं उत्तमाचियासाठीं। नीच मानिजे किरीटी। हे वांचोनि दिठी। दोषु न घेपे॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ uttamāciyāsāṭhīṃ| nīca mānije kirīṭī| he vāṃconi diṭhī| doṣu na ghepe|| 52||
verses.meaning: For the sake of the excellent, the inferior is considered, O Kiriti; other than this, the eye does not perceive fault.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा अपैशून्याचें लक्षण । अर्जुना हें फुडें जाण । मोक्षमार्गीचें सुखासन। मुख्य हें गा॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā apaiśūnyāceṃ lakṣaṇa | arjunā heṃ phuḍeṃ jāṇa | mokṣamārgīceṃ sukhāsana| mukhya heṃ gā|| 53||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, know this as the foremost sign of auspiciousness, the primary comfortable seat on the path to liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां दया ते ऐसी। पूर्णचंद्रिका जैसी । निववितां न कडसी। सानें थोर॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ dayā te aisī| pūrṇacaṃdrikā jaisī | nivavitāṃ na kaḍasī| sāneṃ thora|| 54||
verses.meaning: Now, compassion is like the full moon's light, which, when it cools, does not distinguish between small and great.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें दुःखिताचें शिणणें। हिरतां सकणवपणें । उत्तमाधम नेणे। विवंचूं गा ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ duḥkhitāceṃ śiṇaṇeṃ| hiratāṃ sakaṇavapaṇeṃ | uttamādhama neṇe| vivaṃcūṃ gā || 55||
verses.meaning: Just as compassion, when alleviating the suffering of the distressed, does not discriminate between the high and the low, nor does it pause to consider.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं जगीं जीवनासारिखें। वस्तु अंगवरी उपखें। परी जातें जीवित राखे। तृणाचेंहि॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ jagīṃ jīvanāsārikheṃ| vastu aṃgavarī upakheṃ| parī jāteṃ jīvita rākhe| tṛṇāceṃhi|| 56||
verses.meaning: In this world, nothing is as vital as life itself. It sustains even a blade of grass.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें पुढिलाचेनि तापें। कळवळळलिये कृपें। सर्वस्वेंसी दिधलेंहि आपणपे । थोडेंचि गमे॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ puḍhilāceni tāpeṃ| kaḻavaḻaḻaliye kṛpeṃ| sarvasveṃsī didhaleṃhi āpaṇape | thoḍeṃci game|| 57||
verses.meaning: Similarly, out of compassion, when one is moved by the suffering of others, even if one gives away everything, it still feels insufficient.

verses.shloka_devanagari: निम्न भरलियाविणें । पाणी ढळोंचि नेणें । तेवीं श्रांता तोषौनि जाणें । सामोरें पां॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nimna bharaliyāviṇeṃ | pāṇī ḍhaḻoṃci neṇeṃ | tevīṃ śrāṃtā toṣauni jāṇeṃ | sāmoreṃ pāṃ|| 58||
verses.meaning: Just as water does not overflow until the lower vessel is filled, so too, one should approach the weary after satisfying them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं पायीं कांटा नेहटे। तंब व्यथा जीवीं उमटे। तैसा पोळे संकटें। पुढिलांचेनि॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ pāyīṃ kāṃṭā nehaṭe| taṃba vyathā jīvīṃ umaṭe| taisā poḻe saṃkaṭeṃ| puḍhilāṃceni|| 59||
verses.meaning: Just as a thorn piercing one's foot causes pain in the heart, so too does one feel the distress of others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां पावो शीतळता लाहे। कौं ते डोळ्याचिलागीं होये। तैसें परसुखें जाये। सुखावतु॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ pāvo śītaḻatā lāhe| kauṃ te ḍoḻyācilāgīṃ hoye| taiseṃ parasukheṃ jāye| sukhāvatu|| 160||
verses.meaning: Just as one experiences coolness, or as the eyes perceive, so too does one find joy in the happiness of others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना तृषितालागीं। पाणी आरायिलें असे जगीं। तैसें दुःखितांचे सेलभागीं। जिणें जयाचें॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā tṛṣitālāgīṃ| pāṇī ārāyileṃ ase jagīṃ| taiseṃ duḥkhitāṃce selabhāgīṃ| jiṇeṃ jayāceṃ|| 61||
verses.meaning: Indeed, just as water is sought after in the world by the thirsty, so too is the life of one who lives for the sake of the distressed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो पुरुष वीरराया । मूर्तिमंत जाण दया। मी उदयजतांचि तया । क्रणिया लाभें॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: to puruṣa vīrarāyā | mūrtimaṃta jāṇa dayā| mī udayajatāṃci tayā | kraṇiyā lābheṃ||62||
verses.meaning: That Purusha, the valiant king, is the very embodiment of compassion. As soon as I arise, I attain that kingdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां सूर्यासि जीवें। अनुसरलिया राजीवें। परी तें तो न शिवे। सौरभ्य जैसें ॥६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ sūryāsi jīveṃ| anusaraliyā rājīveṃ| parī teṃ to na śive| saurabhya jaiseṃ ||63||
verses.meaning: Just as a lotus, though it lives by the sun, does not touch its fragrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वसंताचिया वाहाणीं । आलिया वनश्रीच्या अक्षोहिणी । ते न करीतुचि घेणी । निगाला तो॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vasaṃtāciyā vāhāṇīṃ | āliyā vanaśrīcyā akṣohiṇī | te na karītuci gheṇī | nigālā to|| 64||
verses.meaning: Or, as the spring arrives, the forest's armies of beauty spontaneously emerge, without any effort or taking from anyone, it simply manifests.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो महासिद्धीसी। लक्ष्मीही आलिया पाशीं। परी महाविष्णु जैसी। न गणीच ते॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso mahāsiddhīsī| lakṣmīhī āliyā pāśīṃ| parī mahāviṣṇu jaisī| na gaṇīca te|| 65||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Even if great spiritual powers come near, or even if Lakshmi herself arrives, the Great Vishnu does not consider them at all.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसे ऐहिकींचे कां स्वर्गीचे। भोग पाइक जालिया इच्छेचे। परी भोगावें हें न रुचे। मनामाजीं ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taise aihikīṃce kāṃ svargīce| bhoga pāika jāliyā icchece| parī bhogāveṃ heṃ na ruce| manāmājīṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: Similarly, whether it is the pleasures of this world or of heaven, even if one becomes a servant of desires, the thought of experiencing them does not appeal to the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ३८२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी बहुवें काय कौतुकीं । जीव नोहे विषयाभिलाखी । अलोलुप्त्वदशा ठाउकी । जाण ते हे॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: 382 śrījñāneśvarī bahuveṃ kāya kautukīṃ | jīva nohe viṣayābhilākhī | aloluptvadaśā ṭhāukī | jāṇa te he|| 67||
verses.meaning: What more can be said about the wonders of Shri Dnyaneshwari? The soul is not desirous of worldly pleasures. This state of non-attachment is known to be true wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां माशियां जैसें मोहळ। जळचरां जेवीं जळ । कां पक्षीयां अंतराळ । मोकळें हें ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ māśiyāṃ jaiseṃ mohaḻa| jaḻacarāṃ jevīṃ jaḻa | kāṃ pakṣīyāṃ aṃtarāḻa | mokaḻeṃ heṃ || 68 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a beehive is for bees, water for aquatic creatures, or the sky for birds, so is this (the universe) for them, free and unhindered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी बाळकोद्देशें । मातेचें स्नेह जैसें । कां वसंतींच्या स्पर्शे। मऊ मल्यानिळु ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī bāḻakoddeśeṃ | māteceṃ sneha jaiseṃ | kāṃ vasaṃtīṃcyā sparśe| maū malyāniḻu || 69||
verses.meaning: Or, just as a mother's affection is for her child, or like the gentle breeze from the Malaya mountains in spring.

verses.shloka_devanagari: डोळयां प्रियाची भेटी । कां पिलियां कुर्मीची दिठी। तैसी भूतमात्रीं राहटी । मवाळ ते॥ १७० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ḍoḻayāṃ priyācī bheṭī | kāṃ piliyāṃ kurmīcī diṭhī| taisī bhūtamātrīṃ rāhaṭī | mavāḻa te|| 170 ||
verses.meaning: Just as the eyes long to meet their beloved, or as a tortoise gazes upon its young, so too does the gentle soul dwell within all beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्पर्श अतिमृदु। मुखीं घेतां सुस्वादु। घ्राणासि सुगंधु। उजाळु आंगें॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: sparśa atimṛdu| mukhīṃ ghetāṃ susvādu| ghrāṇāsi sugaṃdhu| ujāḻu āṃgeṃ||79||
verses.meaning: It is exceedingly soft to the touch, sweet to the taste when taken into the mouth, fragrant to the nose, and illuminating to the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो आवडे तेवढा घेतां। विरुद्ध जरी न होता। तरी उपमे येता। कापूर कौं॥७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: to āvaḍe tevaḍhā ghetāṃ| viruddha jarī na hotā| tarī upame yetā| kāpūra kauṃ||72||
verses.meaning: If it could be taken as much as one liked, and if it were not contradictory, then camphor could be used as a simile.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी महाभूतें पोटीं वाहे । तेवींचि परमाणूमाजीं सामाये। या बिश्वानुसार होये । गगन जैसें ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī mahābhūteṃ poṭīṃ vāhe | tevīṃci paramāṇūmājīṃ sāmāye| yā biśvānusāra hoye | gagana jaiseṃ || 73||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky (ether) encompasses the great elements within itself, and similarly pervades even the smallest atom, so too does it accommodate itself to the entire universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: काय सांगों ऐसें जिणें । जें जगाचेनि जीवें प्राणें। तयां नांव म्हणें । मार्दव मी ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāya sāṃgoṃ aiseṃ jiṇeṃ | jeṃ jagāceni jīveṃ prāṇeṃ| tayāṃ nāṃva mhaṇeṃ | mārdava mī || 74||
verses.meaning: What can I say about such a life, which is the very life and breath of the world? That, I say, is My gentleness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां पराजयें राजा । जैसा कदर्थिजे लाजा। कां मानिया निस्तेजा । निकृष्टास्तव ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ parājayeṃ rājā | jaisā kadarthije lājā| kāṃ māniyā nistejā | nikṛṣṭāstava || 75||
verses.meaning: Just as a king, defeated in battle, is humiliated and shamed, or a respected person loses their luster due to a lowly act.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना चांडाळ मंदिराशीं। अवचटें आलिया संन्यासी। मग लाज होय जैसी। उत्तमा तया ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā cāṃḍāḻa maṃdirāśīṃ| avacaṭeṃ āliyā saṃnyāsī| maga lāja hoya jaisī| uttamā tayā || 76||
verses.meaning: Just as a noble person feels ashamed if by chance a Chandala (outcaste) enters a temple, so too does the mind feel shame when it encounters worldly desires.

verses.shloka_devanagari: क्षत्रिया रणीं पळोनि जाणें । तें कोण साहे लाजिरवाणे । कां वैधव्यें पाचारणे । महासतियेतें ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṣatriyā raṇīṃ paḻoni jāṇeṃ | teṃ koṇa sāhe lājiravāṇe | kāṃ vaidhavyeṃ pācāraṇe | mahāsatiyeteṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: For a Kshatriya, fleeing from the battlefield is a shameful act. Who would tolerate such disgrace? It is like calling upon widowhood for a chaste and devoted wife.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रूपसा उदयलें कुष्ट। संभावितां कुटीचें बोट । तया लाजा प्राणसंकट । होय जेसें ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: rūpasā udayaleṃ kuṣṭa| saṃbhāvitāṃ kuṭīceṃ boṭa | tayā lājā prāṇasaṃkaṭa | hoya jeseṃ || 78 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a person with leprosy, seeing a beautiful form, feels ashamed of their own diseased finger and wishes for death, so too does the soul feel anguish when it perceives the divine beauty.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें औटहातपणें । जें शव होऊनि जिणें। उपजों उपजों मरणें। नावानाबा॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ auṭahātapaṇeṃ | jeṃ śava hoūni jiṇeṃ| upajoṃ upajoṃ maraṇeṃ| nāvānābā|| 79||
verses.meaning: Similarly, to live as a corpse, though having a body of three and a half cubits, to be born again and again only to die, is to be utterly ruined.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियें गर्भमेदमुसें । रक्‍तमूत्ररसें। बोंतीव होऊनि असे। तें लाजिरवाणें ॥ १८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyeṃ garbhamedamuseṃ | rak‍tamūtraraseṃ| boṃtīva hoūni ase| teṃ lājiravāṇeṃ || 180||
verses.meaning: In that womb, amidst fat and marrow, blood and urine, it is formed and exists—a truly shameful state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें बहु असो देहपणें । नामरूपासि येणें । नाहीं गा लाजिरवाणें । तयाहूनी ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ bahu aso dehapaṇeṃ | nāmarūpāsi yeṇeṃ | nāhīṃ gā lājiravāṇeṃ | tayāhūnī || 89||
verses.meaning: Let this be. To take on a body and come into name and form is not shameful for the soul; rather, it is less shameful than that.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसैसिया अवकळा । घेपे शरीराचा कंटाळा । ते लाज पैं निर्मळा। निसुगा गोड॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisaisiyā avakaḻā | ghepe śarīrācā kaṃṭāḻā | te lāja paiṃ nirmaḻā| nisugā goḍa|| 82||
verses.meaning: When such a state of aversion arises, leading to a weariness of the body, then even the pure and unattached find sweetness in this shame.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां सूत्रतंतु तुटलिया। चेष्टाचि ठाके सायखडिया। तैसी प्राणजयें कर्मेद्रियां। खुंटे गती॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ sūtrataṃtu tuṭaliyā| ceṣṭāci ṭhāke sāyakhaḍiyā| taisī prāṇajayeṃ karmedriyāṃ| khuṃṭe gatī|| 83||
verses.meaning: Just as a puppet stops moving when its string breaks, so too do the organs of action cease their activity when the vital breath is controlled.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं मावळलिया दिनकरु। सरे किरणांचा प्रसरु । तैसा मनोजयें प्रकारु । ज्ञानेंद्रियांचा ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ māvaḻaliyā dinakaru| sare kiraṇāṃcā prasaru | taisā manojayeṃ prakāru | jñāneṃdriyāṃcā || 84 ||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's rays withdraw when the sun sets, so too do the senses' activities cease when the mind is subdued.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं मनपवननियमें। होती दाही इंद्रियें अक्षमें। तें अचापल्य वर्मे । येणें होय ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ manapavananiyameṃ| hotī dāhī iṃdriyeṃ akṣameṃ| teṃ acāpalya varme | yeṇeṃ hoya || 85||
verses.meaning: Thus, by the discipline of mind and breath, the ten senses become incapable of agitation. This steadiness is achieved through this very means.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ईश्‍वरप्राप्तीलागीं। प्रवर्ततां ज्ञानमार्गी । धिंवसेयाचि आंगीं । उणीव नोहे ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ īś‍varaprāptīlāgīṃ| pravartatāṃ jñānamārgī | dhiṃvaseyāci āṃgīṃ | uṇīva nohe || 86||
verses.meaning: Now, for the attainment of God, when one embarks on the path of knowledge, there is no lack of courage in their being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बोखटें मरणाऐसें । तेंही आलें अग्निप्रवेशें । परी प्राणेश्‍वरोद्देशें । न गणीचि सती ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: bokhaṭeṃ maraṇāaiseṃ | teṃhī āleṃ agnipraveśeṃ | parī prāṇeś‍varoddeśeṃ | na gaṇīci satī || 87||
verses.meaning: Even though death is a terrifying ordeal, like entering fire, a devoted wife (sati) does not consider it, for the sake of her beloved husband.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आत्मनाथाचिया आधी । लाऊनि विषयविषाची बाधी | धांबों आवडे पाणधी। शून्याचिये ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ ātmanāthāciyā ādhī | lāūni viṣayaviṣācī bādhī | dhāṃboṃ āvaḍe pāṇadhī| śūnyāciye || 88||
verses.meaning: Just as one, by first applying the poison of worldly desires to the Lord of the Self, then wishes to draw water from a dry well.

verses.shloka_devanagari: न ठाके निषेधु आड । न पडे विधीची भीड। नुपजेचि जीवीं कोड। महासिद्धीचें॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: na ṭhāke niṣedhu āḍa | na paḍe vidhīcī bhīḍa| nupajeci jīvīṃ koḍa| mahāsiddhīceṃ|| 89||
verses.meaning: There is no prohibition that can stop it, no fear of injunctions, nor does the mind crave for great spiritual powers.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें ईश्वराकडे निज। धांवे आपसया सहज। तया नांब तेज। अध्यात्मिक तें॥१९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ īśvarākaḍe nija| dhāṃve āpasayā sahaja| tayā nāṃba teja| adhyātmika teṃ||190||
verses.meaning: Thus, the spiritual radiance of one whose mind spontaneously and effortlessly flows towards God is truly magnificent.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां सर्वही साहातिया गरिमा । गर्वा न ये तेचि क्षमा । जेसें देह वाहोनि रोमा । वाहणें नेणें ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ sarvahī sāhātiyā garimā | garvā na ye teci kṣamā | jeseṃ deha vāhoni romā | vāhaṇeṃ neṇeṃ || 91||
verses.meaning: Now, to endure all things with greatness, yet without pride, that is forgiveness. Just as the body carries the hair, but the hair does not know it is being carried.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मातल्िया इंद्रियांचे वेग । कां प्राचीनें' खवळले रोग अथवा योगवियोग। प्रियाप्रियांचे॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mātaliyā iṃdriyāṃce vega | kāṃ prācīneṃ' khavaḻale roga athavā yogaviyoga| priyāpriyāṃce|| 92||
verses.meaning: Or the uncontrolled senses, or diseases inflamed by past karma, or the union and separation of loved ones and unloved ones.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया आघवियांचाचि थोरु । एके वेळे आलिया पूरु। तरी अगस्त्य कां होऊनि धीरु ॥ उभा ठाके ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā āghaviyāṃcāci thoru | eke veḻe āliyā pūru| tarī agastya kāṃ hoūni dhīru || ubhā ṭhāke || 93||
verses.meaning: If all these (sins) were to surge forth at once like a flood, then, becoming as resolute as Agastya, one would stand firm.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आकाशीं धूमाची रेखा | उठिली बहुबा आगळिका। ते गिळी येकीं झुळुका। वारा जेवीं॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ākāśīṃ dhūmācī rekhā | uṭhilī bahubā āgaḻikā| te giḻī yekīṃ jhuḻukā| vārā jevīṃ|| 94||
verses.meaning: A line of smoke rises in the sky, a great and powerful phenomenon. But a single gust of wind swallows it, just as the wind does.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अधिभूताधिदैवां। अध्यात्मादि उपद्रवां। पातळेया पांडवा। गिळूनि घाली ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ adhibhūtādhidaivāṃ| adhyātmādi upadravāṃ| pātaḻeyā pāṃḍavā| giḻūni ghālī || 95||
verses.meaning: Similarly, O Pandava, when troubles like those related to the physical world, the divine, and the spiritual self arise, He swallows them all.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें चित्तक्षोभाच्या अवसरीं । उचलूनि धेर्या जें चांगावें करी। धृती म्हणिपे अवधारी । तियेतें गा ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ cittakṣobhācyā avasarīṃ | ucalūni dheryā jeṃ cāṃgāveṃ karī| dhṛtī mhaṇipe avadhārī | tiyeteṃ gā || 96||
verses.meaning: In such moments of mental agitation, that which, by lifting courage, acts appropriately, know that to be called fortitude.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां निर्वाळूनि कनकें । भरिला गांगेंपीयूखें । तया कलशाचियासारिखें। शौच असे॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ nirvāḻūni kanakeṃ | bharilā gāṃgeṃpīyūkheṃ | tayā kalaśāciyāsārikheṃ| śauca ase|| 97||
verses.meaning: Now, as if a golden pot, purified and filled with the sacred nectar of the Ganges, such is the purity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे आंगीं निष्काम आचारु । जीवीं विवेकु साचारु । तो सबाह्य घडला आकारु । शुचित्वाचाचि॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: je āṃgīṃ niṣkāma ācāru | jīvīṃ viveku sācāru | to sabāhya ghaḍalā ākāru | śucitvācāci|| 98||
verses.meaning: One whose actions are selfless, and whose heart is truly discerning, that person is outwardly and inwardly the very embodiment of purity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां फेडित पाप ताप। पोखीत तीरींचे पादप। समुद्रा जाय आप। गंगेचें जैसें॥९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ pheḍita pāpa tāpa| pokhīta tīrīṃce pādapa| samudrā jāya āpa| gaṃgeceṃ jaiseṃ||99||
verses.meaning: Just as the Ganges river, by washing away sins and sorrows, and eroding the trees on its banks, ultimately merges into the ocean.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां जगाचें आंध्य फेडितु। श्रियेचीं राउळें उघडितु । निघे जैसा भास्वतु। प्रदक्षिणे ॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ jagāceṃ āṃdhya pheḍitu| śriyecīṃ rāuḻeṃ ughaḍitu | nighe jaisā bhāsvatu| pradakṣiṇe || 200||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun rises to dispel the world's darkness, opening the doors of prosperity, so does it embark on its circumambulation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं बांधिली सोडिता। बुडाली काढिता। सांकडी फेडिता। आर्तांचिया॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ bāṃdhilī soḍitā| buḍālī kāḍhitā| sāṃkaḍī pheḍitā| ārtāṃciyā|| 1||
verses.meaning: Just as one who is bound is freed, one who is drowned is pulled out, and the distress of the afflicted is removed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना दिवसराती। पुढिलांचें सुख उन्नति) आणित आणित स्वार्थी । प्रवेशिजे॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā divasarātī| puḍhilāṃceṃ sukha unnati) āṇita āṇita svārthī | praveśije|| 2||
verses.meaning: Indeed, day and night, one should strive for the happiness and progress of others, and through this selfless service, attain their own spiritual advancement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि आपुल्िये काजालागीं । प्राणिजाताच्या अहितभागीं। संकल्पाचीही आडवंगी । न करणें जें॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni āpuliye kājālāgīṃ | prāṇijātācyā ahitabhāgīṃ| saṃkalpācīhī āḍavaṃgī | na karaṇeṃ jeṃ||3||
verses.meaning: Furthermore, for one's own benefit, one should not even conceive of any thought that would cause harm to any living being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं अद्रोहत्व ऐशिया गोष्टी। ऐकसि जिया किरीटी । तें सांगितलें हें दिठी। पाहों ये तैसें ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ adrohatva aiśiyā goṣṭī| aikasi jiyā kirīṭī | teṃ sāṃgitaleṃ heṃ diṭhī| pāhoṃ ye taiseṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, listen to these things about non-enmity. What has been told can be seen with the eyes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि गंगा शंभूचा माथां। पाबोनि संकोचे जेवीं पार्था । तेवीं मान्यपणें सर्वथा। लाजणें जें॥५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi gaṃgā śaṃbhūcā māthāṃ| pāboni saṃkoce jevīṃ pārthā | tevīṃ mānyapaṇeṃ sarvathā| lājaṇeṃ jeṃ||5||
verses.meaning: And just as the Ganga, having drunk from Shiva's head, becomes shy, so too does one become shy due to excessive honor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें हें पुढत पुढती । अमानित्व जाण सुमती । मागां सांगितलेंसे किती । तेंचि तें बोलो ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ heṃ puḍhata puḍhatī | amānitva jāṇa sumatī | māgāṃ sāṃgitaleṃse kitī | teṃci teṃ bolo || 6||
verses.meaning: This very same 'absence of pride' (amanitva) is what I have repeatedly explained to you, O good-minded one. What has been said before, I speak of that very same thing again.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं इहीं सव्बिसें। ब्रह्मसंपदा हे बसत असे। मोक्षचक्रवर्तींचें जैसें । अग्रहार होय ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ ihīṃ savbiseṃ| brahmasaṃpadā he basata ase| mokṣacakravartīṃceṃ jaiseṃ | agrahāra hoya || 7||
verses.meaning: Thus, in these twenty-six qualities, the wealth of Brahman is established, just as it is the royal grant of the emperor of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना हे संपत्ति दैवी । या गुणतीर्थांची नीच नवी । निर्विण्णसगरांची दैवी । गंगाचि आली ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā he saṃpatti daivī | yā guṇatīrthāṃcī nīca navī | nirviṇṇasagarāṃcī daivī | gaṃgāci ālī || 8||
verses.meaning: These diverse divine qualities are like ever-new, sacred pilgrimage sites of virtues. They are like the Ganges itself, flowing to purify the weary and worldly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं गुणकुसुमांची माळा । हे घेऊनि मुक्तिबाळा। वैराग्यनिरपेक्षाचा गळा। गिंवसीत असे॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ guṇakusumāṃcī māḻā | he gheūni muktibāḻā| vairāgyanirapekṣācā gaḻā| giṃvasīta ase||9||
verses.meaning: Or, the garland of virtues, this child of liberation takes and embraces the neck of detachment and desirelessness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कों सव्वबिसें गुणज्योती। ३८४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी इहीं उजळूनि आरती । गीता आत्मया निजपती। नीरांजना आली ॥ २१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: koṃ savvabiseṃ guṇajyotī| 384 śrījñāneśvarī ihīṃ ujaḻūni āratī | gītā ātmayā nijapatī| nīrāṃjanā ālī || 210||
verses.meaning: With these twenty-six qualities, the light of the Gita, illuminating the inner self, has come to perform the arati (waving of lamps) for its true Lord.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उगळितें निर्मळें। गुण इयेचि मुक्‍ताफळें। दैवी शुक्तिकळें। गीतार्णबींची॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: ugaḻiteṃ nirmaḻeṃ| guṇa iyeci muk‍tāphaḻeṃ| daivī śuktikaḻeṃ| gītārṇabīṃcī|| 11||
verses.meaning: These pure qualities are like pearls, divine and radiant, born from the ocean of the Gita.

verses.shloka_devanagari: काय बहु वानूं ऐसी। अभिव्यक्ती ये अपैसी। केलें दैवी गुणराशी । संपत्तिरूप ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāya bahu vānūṃ aisī| abhivyaktī ye apaisī| keleṃ daivī guṇarāśī | saṃpattirūpa || 12||
verses.meaning: How much more can I describe? This spontaneous manifestation, by divine qualities, has taken the form of wealth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां दुःखाची आंतुवट वेली । दोषकाट्यांची जरी भरली । तरी निजाभिधानीं घाली । आसुरी ते॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ duḥkhācī āṃtuvaṭa velī | doṣakāṭyāṃcī jarī bharalī | tarī nijābhidhānīṃ ghālī | āsurī te|| 13||
verses.meaning: Now, even if the inner vine of sorrow is filled with thorns of faults, still, in its true name, it is called demonic.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं त्याज्य त्यजावयालागीं। जाणावी जरी अनुपयोगी। तरी ऐका ते चांगी। श्रोत्रशक्‍ती ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ tyājya tyajāvayālāgīṃ| jāṇāvī jarī anupayogī| tarī aikā te cāṃgī| śrotraśak‍tī || 14||
verses.meaning: Even if you consider the faculty of hearing to be useless for renouncing what should be renounced, still, listen to its excellent power.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी नरकव्यथा थोरी । आणावया दोषींघोरीं । मेळू केला ते आसुरी। संपत्ति हे॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī narakavyathā thorī | āṇāvayā doṣīṃghorīṃ | meḻū kelā te āsurī| saṃpatti he|| 15||
verses.meaning: Thus, to bring about the great suffering of hell upon grave sinners, this demonic wealth is gathered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना विषवर्गु एकवटु। तया नांव जैसा बासटु। आसुरी संपत्ति हा खोटु। दोषांचा तैसा॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā viṣavargu ekavaṭu| tayā nāṃva jaisā bāsaṭu| āsurī saṃpatti hā khoṭu| doṣāṃcā taisā|| 16||
verses.meaning: Just as various poisons gather together to form a deadly venom, so too is the demonic nature (asuri sampatti) a collection of all faults and vices.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तयाचि असुरां। दोषांमाजीं जया वीरा । वाडपणाचा डांगोरा । तो दंभु ऐसा॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tayāci asurāṃ| doṣāṃmājīṃ jayā vīrā | vāḍapaṇācā ḍāṃgorā | to daṃbhu aisā|| 17||
verses.meaning: Among those demonic qualities, the one that proclaims its greatness with a loud drumbeat, that is hypocrisy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी आपुली जननी । नग्न दाविलिया जनीं। तें तीर्थचि परी पतनीं। कारण होय॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī āpulī jananī | nagna dāviliyā janīṃ| teṃ tīrthaci parī patanīṃ| kāraṇa hoya|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as one's own mother, if exposed naked in public, though revered, becomes a cause for one's downfall.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां विद्या गुरूपदिष्टा। बोभाइलिया चोहटां। इष्टदा परी अनिष्टा । हेतु होती॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vidyā gurūpadiṣṭā| bobhāiliyā cohaṭāṃ| iṣṭadā parī aniṣṭā | hetu hotī|| 19||
verses.meaning: Just as knowledge imparted by a Guru, if proclaimed in the marketplace, though beneficial, can lead to undesirable outcomes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आंगें बुडतां महापूरीं । जे वेगें काढी पैलतीरीं। ते नावचि बांधिलिया शिरीं। बुडवी जैसी॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ āṃgeṃ buḍatāṃ mahāpūrīṃ | je vegeṃ kāḍhī pailatīrīṃ| te nāvaci bāṃdhiliyā śirīṃ| buḍavī jaisī|| 220||
verses.meaning: Just as a boat, which swiftly carries one to the other shore when drowning in a great flood, will itself drown one if tied to the head.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कारण जें जीविता। तें बानिळें जरी सेवितां। तरी अन्नचि पंडुसुता । होय विष॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāraṇa jeṃ jīvitā| teṃ bāniḻeṃ jarī sevitāṃ| tarī annaci paṃḍusutā | hoya viṣa|| 21||
verses.meaning: Because if life itself, when consumed, becomes harmful, then food itself, O son of Pandu, turns into poison.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा दृष्टादृष्टाचा सखा । धर्म जाला तो फोकारिजे देखा । तरी तारिता तोचि दोखा-। लागीं होय॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭācā sakhā | dharma jālā to phokārije dekhā | tarī tāritā toci dokhā-| lāgīṃ hoya|| 22||
verses.meaning: Just as a friend, whether seen or unseen, becomes a source of suffering if dharma is proclaimed in such a way, then that very dharma becomes the cause of distress.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि वाचेचा चौबारा। घातलिया धर्माचा पसारा । धर्मुचि तो अधर्मु होय वीरा । तो दंभु जाणे॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni vācecā caubārā| ghātaliyā dharmācā pasārā | dharmuci to adharmu hoya vīrā | to daṃbhu jāṇe|| 23||
verses.meaning: Therefore, if one spreads the display of righteousness through words, that very righteousness becomes unrighteousness, O brave one; know that to be hypocrisy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां मूर्खाचिये जिभे। अक्षरांचा आंबुखा सुभे। आणि तो ब्रह्मसभे। न रिझे जैसा॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ mūrkhāciye jibhe| akṣarāṃcā āṃbukhā subhe| āṇi to brahmasabhe| na rijhe jaisā|| 24||
verses.meaning: Now, the tongue of a fool may utter many words, but they are not appreciated in an assembly of the wise, just as a donkey's braying is not music.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां मादुरी लोकांचा घोडा। गजपतिही मानी थोडा । कां कांटियेवरिल्या सरडा । स्वर्गुही नीच ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ mādurī lokāṃcā ghoḍā| gajapatihī mānī thoḍā | kāṃ kāṃṭiyevarilyā saraḍā | svarguhī nīca || 25||
verses.meaning: Just as a horse belonging to a mad person is considered insignificant even by an elephant, or a chameleon on a thorny bush considers even heaven to be lowly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तृणाचेनि इंधनें। आगी धांवे गगनें। थिल्लरबळें मीनें। न गणिजे सिंधु ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tṛṇāceni iṃdhaneṃ| āgī dhāṃve gaganeṃ| thillarabaḻeṃ mīneṃ| na gaṇije siṃdhu || 26||
verses.meaning: Just as a fire fueled by dry grass blazes towards the sky, or a small fish in a puddle does not comprehend the vastness of the ocean, so too is the limited understanding of the worldly mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा माजे स्त्रिया धनें। विद्या स्तुती बहुतें मानें। एके दिवसींचेनि परान्नें। अल्पकु जैसा ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā māje striyā dhaneṃ| vidyā stutī bahuteṃ māneṃ| eke divasīṃceni parānneṃ| alpaku jaisā || 27||
verses.meaning: Just as a poor person, who has never known wealth, might consider a single day's feast at someone else's home as his own women, riches, knowledge, and great praise, so too does the ignorant soul mistake fleeting worldly pleasures for true fulfillment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अभ्रच्छायेचिया जोडी । निदैवु घर मोडी । मृगांबु देखोनि फोडी । पाणियाडें मूर्ख॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: abhracchāyeciyā joḍī | nidaivu ghara moḍī | mṛgāṃbu dekhoni phoḍī | pāṇiyāḍeṃ mūrkha|| 28||
verses.meaning: Just as an unfortunate person demolishes their house for the shade of a cloud, or a fool breaks a water pot upon seeing a mirage, so too do people pursue illusory pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना ऐसैसें । उतणें जें संपत्तिमिसें। तो दर्पु गा अनारिसें। न बोलें घेई ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā aisaiseṃ | utaṇeṃ jeṃ saṃpattimiseṃ| to darpu gā anāriseṃ| na boleṃ gheī || 29||
verses.meaning: Indeed, such an abundance of wealth, disguised as prosperity, should not be spoken of with arrogance. Do not take pride in it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जगा वेदीं विश्‍वासु। आणि विश्‍वासीं पूज्य ईशु । जगीं एक तेजसु । सूर्यच हा ॥ २३० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jagā vedīṃ viś‍vāsu| āṇi viś‍vāsīṃ pūjya īśu | jagīṃ eka tejasu | sūryaca hā || 230 ||
verses.meaning: And in the world, faith is the altar; and in the faithful, God is worshipped. In the world, there is only one radiance, and that is the sun.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जगस्पृहे आस्पद । एक सार्वभौमपद । न मरणें निर्विवाद। जगा पढियें ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jagaspṛhe āspada | eka sārvabhaumapada | na maraṇeṃ nirvivāda| jagā paḍhiyeṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: The only object of worldly desire, the one sovereign position, is immortality, which is undoubtedly dear to the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जग उत्साहें। यातें वानू जाये। कीं तें आइकोनि मत्सरु वाहे। फुगों लागे॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jaga utsāheṃ| yāteṃ vānū jāye| kīṃ teṃ āikoni matsaru vāhe| phugoṃ lāge|| 32||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the world enthusiastically praises this, but upon hearing it, envy swells and begins to inflate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे ईश्‍वरातें खायें॥ तया वेदा विष सूर्ये । गौरवामाजीं त्राये। भंगीत असे ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe īś‍varāteṃ khāyeṃ|| tayā vedā viṣa sūrye | gauravāmājīṃ trāye| bhaṃgīta ase || 33||
verses.meaning: He says, "I will consume God." To such a one, the Vedas are like poison, and even the sun's glory is diminished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पतंगा नावडे ज्योती। खद्योता भानूची खंती। कां टिटिभेनें आपांपती। वैरी केला॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: pataṃgā nāvaḍe jyotī| khadyotā bhānūcī khaṃtī| kāṃ ṭiṭibheneṃ āpāṃpatī| vairī kelā|| 34||
verses.meaning: The moth dislikes the flame, the firefly resents the sun, or why would the lapwing consider the sky its enemy?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसा अभिमानाचेनि मोहें। ईश्‍वराचें नामही न साहे। वेदातें म्हणे मज हे। सवती जाली ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tesā abhimānāceni moheṃ| īś‍varāceṃ nāmahī na sāhe| vedāteṃ mhaṇe maja he| savatī jālī || 35||
verses.meaning: Such is the delusion of ego that it cannot tolerate even the name of God. It says, "The Vedas have become my rivals."

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा मान्यतेचा पुष्टगंडु। तो अभिमानी परमलंडु। रौरवाचा रूढु। मार्गुचि पैं॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā mānyatecā puṣṭagaṃḍu| to abhimānī paramalaṃḍu| rauravācā rūḍhu| mārguci paiṃ|| 36||
verses.meaning: Such a person, puffed up with pride, is extremely arrogant, and indeed, is firmly set on the path to hell.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पुढिलांचे सुख। देखणियाचें होय मिख । चढे क्रोधाग्नीचें विख । मनोवृत्ती ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi puḍhilāṃce sukha| dekhaṇiyāceṃ hoya mikha | caḍhe krodhāgnīceṃ vikha | manovṛttī || 37||
verses.meaning: And seeing the happiness of others, the poison of the fire of anger rises in the mind's tendencies.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शीतळाचिये भेटी। तातला तेली आगी उठी। चंद्र देखोनि जळे पोटीं। कोल्हा जैसा॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: śītaḻāciye bheṭī| tātalā telī āgī uṭhī| caṃdra dekhoni jaḻe poṭīṃ| kolhā jaisā|| 38||
verses.meaning: Just as a fox, upon seeing the moon, feels a burning sensation in its stomach, so too does a fire, upon meeting the cold, blaze up with increased intensity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विश्‍श्वाचें आयुष्य जेणें उजळे। तो सूर्यु उदैला देखोनि सवळे। पापिया फुटती डोळे । डुडुळाचे॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: viś‍śvāceṃ āyuṣya jeṇeṃ ujaḻe| to sūryu udailā dekhoni savaḻe| pāpiyā phuṭatī ḍoḻe | ḍuḍuḻāce|| 39||
verses.meaning: The sun that illuminates the life of the universe has risen. Seeing this, the eyes of the sinful, like those of an owl, burst open.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जगाची सुखपहांट । चोरां मरणाहूनि निकृष्ट। दुधाचे काळकूट। होय व्याळीं ॥ २४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jagācī sukhapahāṃṭa | corāṃ maraṇāhūni nikṛṣṭa| dudhāce kāḻakūṭa| hoya vyāḻīṃ || 240||
verses.meaning: The dawn of worldly pleasures is worse than death for thieves. Milk turns into deadly poison for snakes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगाधें समुद्रजळें। प्राशितां अधिकें जळे। वडवाग्नी न मिळे। शांति कहीं ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agādheṃ samudrajaḻeṃ| prāśitāṃ adhikeṃ jaḻe| vaḍavāgnī na miḻe| śāṃti kahīṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: The submarine fire, Vadavanala, cannot find peace even by drinking the immense ocean waters, but rather burns more intensely.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा विद्याविनोदविभवें । देखे पुढिलांचीं दैवें। तंब तंव रोषु दुणावे। क्रोधु तो जाण॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā vidyāvinodavibhaveṃ | dekhe puḍhilāṃcīṃ daiveṃ| taṃba taṃva roṣu duṇāve| krodhu to jāṇa|| 42||
verses.meaning: When one sees the prosperity of others, their good fortune, their enjoyment of knowledge and entertainment, their anger and rage double. This is what is known as wrath.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मन सर्पाची कुटी । डोळे नाराचांची सुटी । बोलणें ते वृष्टी । इंगळांची ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mana sarpācī kuṭī | ḍoḻe nārācāṃcī suṭī | bolaṇeṃ te vṛṣṭī | iṃgaḻāṃcī || 43||
verses.meaning: And the mind is like a serpent's coil, the eyes are like arrows released, and the speech is a shower of embers.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येर जें क्रियाजात। तें तिखयाचें कर्वत। ऐसें सबाह्य खसासित। जयाचें गा॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yera jeṃ kriyājāta| teṃ tikhayāceṃ karvata| aiseṃ sabāhya khasāsita| jayāceṃ gā|| 44||
verses.meaning: All other actions are like a saw made of straw, cutting through everything, both inside and out, for such a one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो मनुष्यांत अधमु जाण। पारुष्याचें अवतरण । आतां आइक खूण। अज्ञानाची ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: to manuṣyāṃta adhamu jāṇa| pāruṣyāceṃ avataraṇa | ātāṃ āika khūṇa| ajñānācī || 45||
verses.meaning: Such a person is the lowest among humans, an embodiment of harshness. Now listen to the signs of ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी शोतोष्णस्पर्शा । निवाडु नेणे पाषाणु जैसा । कां रात्री आणि दिवसा। जात्यंधु तो॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī śotoṣṇasparśā | nivāḍu neṇe pāṣāṇu jaisā | kāṃ rātrī āṇi divasā| jātyaṃdhu to|| 46||
verses.meaning: Just as a stone does not distinguish between the touch of heat and cold, or as a person born blind does not distinguish between night and day.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आगी उठिला आरोगणें। जैसा खाद्याखाद्य न म्हणे। कां परिसा पाडु नेणे । सोनया लोहा॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āgī uṭhilā ārogaṇeṃ| jaisā khādyākhādya na mhaṇe| kāṃ parisā pāḍu neṇe | sonayā lohā|| 47||
verses.meaning: Just as fire, once ignited, consumes all, regardless of whether it is edible or inedible, or just as the philosopher's stone does not distinguish between gold and iron.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी ते नानारसीं। रिघोनि दर्बी जैसी । परी रसस्वादासी । चाखों नेणें ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī te nānārasīṃ| righoni darbī jaisī | parī rasasvādāsī | cākhoṃ neṇeṃ || 48||
verses.meaning: Or, just as a ladle, though immersed in various dishes, does not know the taste of any of them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वारा जैसा पारखी । नव्हेचि गा मार्गामार्गाविखीं। तैसें कृत्याकृत्यविवेकीं। अंधपण जें ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vārā jaisā pārakhī | navheci gā mārgāmārgāvikhīṃ| taiseṃ kṛtyākṛtyavivekīṃ| aṃdhapaṇa jeṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: Just as the wind is impartial, not distinguishing between paths, so too is the blindness in discerning right from wrong actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें चोख हें मैळ। ऐसें नेणोनियां बाळ। देखे तें केवळ। मुखींचि घाली ॥ २५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ cokha heṃ maiḻa| aiseṃ neṇoniyāṃ bāḻa| dekhe teṃ kevaḻa| mukhīṃci ghālī || 250||
verses.meaning: A child, not knowing what is clean or unclean, simply puts whatever it sees into its mouth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें 'पापपुण्याचें खिचटें। करोनि खातां बुद्धिचेष्टे। कडु मधुर न वाटे। ऐसी जे दशा॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ 'pāpapuṇyāceṃ khicaṭeṃ| karoni khātāṃ buddhiceṣṭe| kaḍu madhura na vāṭe| aisī je daśā|| 51||
verses.meaning: Just as, when one eats a mixture of good and bad deeds with the intellect, one does not perceive it as bitter or sweet; such is that state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये नाम अज्ञान या बोला नाहीं आन। एवं साही दोषांचें चिन्ह। सांगितलें॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye nāma ajñāna yā bolā nāhīṃ āna| evaṃ sāhī doṣāṃceṃ cinha| sāṃgitaleṃ|| 52||
verses.meaning: This state is called ignorance; there is no other explanation for it. Thus, the characteristics of the six faults have been described.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इहींच साही दोषांगीं। हे आसुरी संपत्ति दाटुगी। ३८६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी जैसें थोर विषय सुभगे अंगीं । अंग सानें ॥५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ihīṃca sāhī doṣāṃgīṃ| he āsurī saṃpatti dāṭugī| 386 śrījñāneśvarī jaiseṃ thora viṣaya subhage aṃgīṃ | aṃga sāneṃ ||53||
verses.meaning: These six defects are the powerful demonic wealth. Just as a great subject is contained within a small part of a beautiful body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां तिघां वन्हींच्या पांतीं । पाहतां थोडे ठाय गमती । परी विश्‍शवही प्राणाहुती। करूं न पुरे॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ tighāṃ vanhīṃcyā pāṃtīṃ | pāhatāṃ thoḍe ṭhāya gamatī | parī viś‍śavahī prāṇāhutī| karūṃ na pure|| 54||
verses.meaning: Or, if one looks at the three sacred fires, they appear small in their place. Yet, even the entire universe is not enough to offer as a sacrifice into them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: धातयाही गेलिया शरण । त्रिदोषीं न चुके मरण । तया तिहींची दुणी जाण। साही दोष हे॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: dhātayāhī geliyā śaraṇa | tridoṣīṃ na cuke maraṇa | tayā tihīṃcī duṇī jāṇa| sāhī doṣa he|| 55||
verses.meaning: Even if one surrenders to the Creator, death due to the three humors (vata, pitta, kapha) is not avoided. Know that these three, when doubled, become the six faults.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इहीं साही दोषीं संपूर्णी। जाली इयेचि उभारणी । म्हणौनि आसुरी उणी । संपदा नव्हे ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ihīṃ sāhī doṣīṃ saṃpūrṇī| jālī iyeci ubhāraṇī | mhaṇauni āsurī uṇī | saṃpadā navhe || 56||
verses.meaning: These six faults completely give rise to this demonic wealth. Therefore, it is not a lesser demonic quality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी क्रूरग्रहांची जैसी । मांदी मिळे एकेचि राशी । कां येती निंदकापासीं । अशेष पापें ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī krūragrahāṃcī jaisī | māṃdī miḻe ekeci rāśī | kāṃ yetī niṃdakāpāsīṃ | aśeṣa pāpeṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: Just as a multitude of malefic planets gather in a single zodiac sign, or as all sins accumulate around a slanderer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मरणाराचें आंग। पडिघाती अवघेचि रोग। कां कुमुहूर्ती दुर्योग। एकवटती॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maraṇārāceṃ āṃga| paḍighātī avagheci roga| kāṃ kumuhūrtī duryoga| ekavaṭatī|| 58||
verses.meaning: Just as all diseases afflict a dying person's body, or all misfortunes gather at an inauspicious moment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बिश्वासला आतुडवीजे चोरा । शिणला सुडजे महापुरा । तैसें दोषी इहीं नरा । अनिष्ट कीजे॥५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: biśvāsalā ātuḍavīje corā | śiṇalā suḍaje mahāpurā | taiseṃ doṣī ihīṃ narā | aniṣṭa kīje||59||
verses.meaning: Just as a thief is caught by trust, and one who is tired is swept away by a great flood, so too, evil befalls these sinful people.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां आयुष्य जातिये वेळे । शेळिये सातवेउळी मिळे । तेसे साही दोष सगळे। जोडती तया ॥ २६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ āyuṣya jātiye veḻe | śeḻiye sātaveuḻī miḻe | tese sāhī doṣa sagaḻe| joḍatī tayā || 260||
verses.meaning: Or, just as a sheep meets its end at the time of its life's departure, similarly, all six faults accumulate for such a person.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मोक्षमार्गाकडे। जैं यांचा आंबुखा पडे । तैं न निघे म्हणौनि बुडे । संसारीं तो ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mokṣamārgākaḍe| jaiṃ yāṃcā āṃbukhā paḍe | taiṃ na nighe mhaṇauni buḍe | saṃsārīṃ to || 61||
verses.meaning: When their desire falls upon the path to liberation, they do not emerge, and thus they drown in the worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अधमां योनींच्या 'पाउटीं । उतरत जो किरीटी। स्थावरांही तळवटीं । बैसणें घे॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: adhamāṃ yonīṃcyā 'pāuṭīṃ | utarata jo kirīṭī| sthāvarāṃhī taḻavaṭīṃ | baisaṇeṃ ghe|| 62||
verses.meaning: Oh Kiriti (Arjuna), he who descends into the lowest of wombs, even taking a seat at the very bottom amongst the immovables.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो तयाच्या ठायीं । मिळोनि साही दोषीं इहीं । आसुरी संपत्ति पाहीं । वाढविजे॥ ६३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso tayācyā ṭhāyīṃ | miḻoni sāhī doṣīṃ ihīṃ | āsurī saṃpatti pāhīṃ | vāḍhavije|| 63 ||
verses.meaning: Let this be. In that person, these six faults combine and indeed foster demonic wealth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसिया या दोनी । संपदा प्रसिद्धा जनीं । सांगितलिया चिन्हीं । वेगळाल्या ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyā yā donī | saṃpadā prasiddhā janīṃ | sāṃgitaliyā cinhīṃ | vegaḻālyā || 64||
verses.meaning: Thus, these two types of wealth, known to the people, have been described with their distinct characteristics.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इया दोन्हींमाजी पहिली । दैवी जे म्हणितली । ते मोक्षसूर्ये पाहळी । उखाचि जाण॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: iyā donhīṃmājī pahilī | daivī je mhaṇitalī | te mokṣasūrye pāhaḻī | ukhāci jāṇa|| 65 ||
verses.meaning: Of these two, the first, which is called divine, know that it is the dawn of the sun of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरी जे दुसरी । संपत्ति कां आसुरी । ते मोहलोहाची खरी । सांखळी जीवां॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerī je dusarī | saṃpatti kāṃ āsurī | te mohalohācī kharī | sāṃkhaḻī jīvāṃ|| 66||
verses.meaning: The other, either divine or demonic wealth, is truly a chain of iron that binds the souls.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परि हें आइकोनि झणें। भय घेसी हो मनें । काय रात्रीचा दिनें। धाकु धरिजे॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pari heṃ āikoni jhaṇeṃ| bhaya ghesī ho maneṃ | kāya rātrīcā dineṃ| dhāku dharije|| 67||
verses.meaning: But hearing this, O mind, do not be afraid. What fear can the day hold for the night?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे आसुरी संपत्ति तया । बंधालागीं धनंजया । जो साही दोषां ययां। आश्रयो होये ॥६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: he āsurī saṃpatti tayā | baṃdhālāgīṃ dhanaṃjayā | jo sāhī doṣāṃ yayāṃ| āśrayo hoye ||68||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, this demonic wealth is for bondage. It becomes the abode of these six faults.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तूं तंब पांडवा । सांगितलेया दैवा। गुणनिधी बरवा । जन्मलासी॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tūṃ taṃba pāṃḍavā | sāṃgitaleyā daivā| guṇanidhī baravā | janmalāsī|| 69||
verses.meaning: You, O Pandava, are indeed fortunate, for you are born as a treasure trove of virtues, as I have told you.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि पार्था तूं या। दैवी संपत्ती स्वामिया । होऊनि यावें उवाया । कैवल्याचिया ॥ २७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni pārthā tūṃ yā| daivī saṃpattī svāmiyā | hoūni yāveṃ uvāyā | kaivalyāciyā || 270||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, you should become the master of this divine wealth and come forth for the ultimate liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि दैवां आसुरां । संपत्तिवंतां नरां। अनादिसिद्ध उजगरा । राहाटीचा आहे ॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi daivāṃ āsurāṃ | saṃpattivaṃtāṃ narāṃ| anādisiddha ujagarā | rāhāṭīcā āhe || 71||
verses.meaning: And for those with divine and demonic natures, for those who are wealthy, this way of life has been eternally established and is well-known.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें रात्रीच्या अवसरीं । व्यापारिजे निशाचरीं । दिवसा सुव्यवहारीं । मनुष्यादिकीं॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ rātrīcyā avasarīṃ | vyāpārije niśācarīṃ | divasā suvyavahārīṃ | manuṣyādikīṃ|| 72||
verses.meaning: Just as at night, nocturnal beings conduct their activities, so too during the day, humans and others engage in their proper affairs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसिया आपुलालिया राहाटीं। वर्तती दोन्ही सृष्टी । दैवी आणि किरीटी। आसुरी येथ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisiyā āpulāliyā rāhāṭīṃ| vartatī donhī sṛṣṭī | daivī āṇi kirīṭī| āsurī yetha|| 73||
verses.meaning: In this way, both the divine and the demonic creations, O Kiriti, function according to their own inherent natures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि विस्तारूनि दैवी। ज्ञानकथनादि प्रस्तावीं। मागील ग्रंथीं बरवी । सांगितली ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci vistārūni daivī| jñānakathanādi prastāvīṃ| māgīla graṃthīṃ baravī | sāṃgitalī || 74||
verses.meaning: Thus, the divine nature, with its discourse on knowledge and other topics, has been beautifully expounded in the previous texts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां आसुरी जे सृष्टी । तेथिंची उपलऊं गोठी । अबधानाची दिठी । दे पां निकी ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ āsurī je sṛṣṭī | tethiṃcī upalaūṃ goṭhī | abadhānācī diṭhī | de pāṃ nikī || 75 ||
verses.meaning: Now, about the demonic creation, I will explain its nature. Pay close attention with a discerning eye.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी वाद्येंबीण नादु। नेदी कवणाही सादु । कां अपुष्पीं मकरंदु। न लभे जैसा॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī vādyeṃbīṇa nādu| nedī kavaṇāhī sādu | kāṃ apuṣpīṃ makaraṃdu| na labhe jaisā|| 76||
verses.meaning: Just as a sound cannot be produced without an instrument, and nectar cannot be found in a flower without blossoms, so too is the nature of the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी प्रकृति हे आसुर। एकली नोहे गोचर। जंव एकाधें शरीर। माल्हाती ना ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī prakṛti he āsura| ekalī nohe gocara| jaṃva ekādheṃ śarīra| mālhātī nā || 77||
verses.meaning: Similarly, this demonic nature is not perceptible on its own, until it takes hold of some body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आविष्करला लांकुडें। पावकु जैसा जोडे । तैसी प्राणिदेहीं सांपडे । आटोपली हे॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga āviṣkaralā lāṃkuḍeṃ| pāvaku jaisā joḍe | taisī prāṇidehīṃ sāṃpaḍe | āṭopalī he|| 78||
verses.meaning: Just as fire manifests from wood, so too does the soul, though subtle, become evident within the bodies of living beings.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते वेळीं जे वाढी ऊंसा। तेचि आंतुला रसा। देहाकारु होय तैसा । प्राणियांचा ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: te veḻīṃ je vāḍhī ūṃsā| teci āṃtulā rasā| dehākāru hoya taisā | prāṇiyāṃcā || 79||
verses.meaning: At that time, just as the sugarcane grows and becomes the juice within, so too does the body of living beings become the life-force within.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां तयाचि प्राणियां। रूप करूं धनंजया। घडले जे आसुरीया । दोषवृंदीं ॥ २८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ tayāci prāṇiyāṃ| rūpa karūṃ dhanaṃjayā| ghaḍale je āsurīyā | doṣavṛṃdīṃ || 280||
verses.meaning: Now, Arjuna, I will describe those beings who are born with demonic qualities and are steeped in a multitude of sins.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी पुण्यालागीं प्रवृत्ती। कां पापाविषयीं निवृत्ती) या जाणणेयाची राती । तयाचें मन॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī puṇyālāgīṃ pravṛttī| kāṃ pāpāviṣayīṃ nivṛttī) yā jāṇaṇeyācī rātī | tayāceṃ mana|| 81||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the mind of one who understands this is inclined towards virtuous actions and averse to sinful deeds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: निगणेया आणि प्रवेशा । चित्त नेदीतु आवेशा । कोशकिटु जैसा। जाचिन्नला पैं॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: nigaṇeyā āṇi praveśā | citta nedītu āveśā | kośakiṭu jaisā| jācinnalā paiṃ|| 82||
verses.meaning: Just as a silkworm, trapped within its own cocoon, cannot move out or enter, so too the mind, caught in its own attachments, cannot find true freedom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां दिधलें मागुती येईल। कीं न ये हें पुढीलळ। न पाहतां दे भांडवल मूर्ख चोरां॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ didhaleṃ māgutī yeīla| kīṃ na ye heṃ puḍhīlaḻa| na pāhatāṃ de bhāṃḍavala mūrkha corāṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: Or, will what was given return? Or will it not? Without considering this future, a fool gives capital to thieves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसिया प्रवृत्ति निवृत्ति दोनी । नेणिजती आसुरीं जनीं। आणि शोौच तें स्वप्नीं। देखती ना ते॥८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisiyā pravṛtti nivṛtti donī | neṇijatī āsurīṃ janīṃ| āṇi śoauca teṃ svapnīṃ| dekhatī nā te||84||
verses.meaning: Similarly, those of demonic nature know neither pravritti (action with attachment) nor nivritti (renunciation). And purity, they do not even dream of it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: काळिमा सांडील कोळसा । वरी चोखी होईल वायसा । राक्षसही मांसा। विटों शके॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāḻimā sāṃḍīla koḻasā | varī cokhī hoīla vāyasā | rākṣasahī māṃsā| viṭoṃ śake|| 85||
verses.meaning: The coal will shed its blackness, and the crow will become pure. Even a demon will be disgusted by flesh.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी आसुरां प्राणियां। शौच नाहीं धनंजया । पवित्रत्व जेवीं भांडिया। मद्याचिया॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī āsurāṃ prāṇiyāṃ| śauca nāhīṃ dhanaṃjayā | pavitratva jevīṃ bhāṃḍiyā| madyāciyā|| 86||
verses.meaning: But for demoniac beings, there is no purity, O Dhananjaya, just as there is no sanctity in a vessel that has held liquor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वाढविती विधीची आस। कां पाहाती वडिलांची वास । आचाराची भाष । नेणतीचि ते॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāḍhavitī vidhīcī āsa| kāṃ pāhātī vaḍilāṃcī vāsa | ācārācī bhāṣa | neṇatīci te|| 87||
verses.meaning: They do not know the language of conduct, nor do they increase their desire for rituals, nor do they look to their elders for guidance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें चरणें शेळियेचें। कां धांबणें वारियाचें।॥ जाळणें आगीचें । भलतेउतें ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ caraṇeṃ śeḻiyeceṃ| kāṃ dhāṃbaṇeṃ vāriyāceṃ||| jāḻaṇeṃ āgīceṃ | bhalateuteṃ || 88 ||
verses.meaning: Just as grazing is natural to a sheep, or the swift movement to the wind, or burning to fire, so is its inherent nature, wherever it may be.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें पुढां सूनि स्वैर आचरती ते गा आसुर। सत्येंसि कीर बैर। सदाचि तयां ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ puḍhāṃ sūni svaira ācaratī te gā āsura| satyeṃsi kīra baira| sadāci tayāṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Similarly, those who act wantonly and without restraint are indeed demonic. They are always hostile towards truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी नांगिया आपुलिया । विंचू करी गुदगुलिया। तरी साचा बोली बोलिया। बोलती ते॥ २९०॥
