verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ४२२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी मागील जे अध्याय । ते चढते भूमीचे आये । तयांचें पुरें दाविताहे । आपुल्या आंगीं ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni 422 śrījñāneśvarī māgīla je adhyāya | te caḍhate bhūmīce āye | tayāṃceṃ pureṃ dāvitāhe | āpulyā āṃgīṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the preceding chapters of Shri Dnyaneshwari are like ascending steps of a spiritual journey. This chapter now reveals the fullness of their culmination within itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जाल्या कामा नाहीं चोरी। ते कळसें होय उजरी। तेवीं अष्टादशु विवरी । साद्यंत गीता ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jālyā kāmā nāhīṃ corī| te kaḻaseṃ hoya ujarī| tevīṃ aṣṭādaśu vivarī | sādyaṃta gītā || 43||
verses.meaning: Just as a thief's actions are not hidden, but rather exposed by the very act of stealing, so too the eighteen chapters of the Gita reveal themselves from beginning to end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा व्यासें विंदाणिये । गीताप्रासादु सोडवणिये । आणूनि राखिले प्राणिये । नानापरी ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā vyāseṃ viṃdāṇiye | gītāprāsādu soḍavaṇiye | āṇūni rākhile prāṇiye | nānāparī || 44||
verses.meaning: Thus, Vyasa, with great skill, brought forth the palace of the Gita, and thereby saved countless beings in various ways.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक प्रदक्षिणा जपाचिया । बाहेरोनि करिती यया। एक ते श्रवणमिषें छाया । सेविती ययाची ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka pradakṣiṇā japāciyā | bāheroni karitī yayā| eka te śravaṇamiṣeṃ chāyā | sevitī yayācī || 45||
verses.meaning: Some perform a circumambulation of this (knowledge) through chanting, while others, under the pretext of listening, serve its shadow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक ते अवधानाचा पुरा। विडापाऊड भीतरां। घेऊनि रिघती गाभारां। अर्थज्ञानाच्या॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka te avadhānācā purā| viḍāpāūḍa bhītarāṃ| gheūni righatī gābhārāṃ| arthajñānācyā|| 46||
verses.meaning: They, with the offering of their entire attention, enter the inner sanctum of true knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते निजबोधें उराउरी। भेटती आत्मया श्रीहरी । परी मोक्षप्रासादीं सरी । सर्वांही आथी ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te nijabodheṃ urāurī| bheṭatī ātmayā śrīharī | parī mokṣaprāsādīṃ sarī | sarvāṃhī āthī || 47||
verses.meaning: Through self-realization, they intimately meet the Lord, the Self. Yet, in the palace of liberation, all are equal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: समर्थाचिये पंक्तिभोजनें । तळिल्या वरिल्या एकचि पक्‍्वान्नें। तेवीं श्रवणें अर्थे पठणें। मोक्षुचि लाभे॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: samarthāciye paṃktibhojaneṃ | taḻilyā varilyā ekaci pak‍vānneṃ| tevīṃ śravaṇeṃ arthe paṭhaṇeṃ| mokṣuci lābhe|| 48||
verses.meaning: Just as in a feast hosted by a great master, all dishes, whether fried or boiled, are of the same excellent quality, similarly, through listening, understanding, and reciting, one attains liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा गीता वैष्णवप्रासादु। अठरावा अध्याय कळसु विशदु । म्यां म्हणितला हा भेदु। जाणोनियां ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā gītā vaiṣṇavaprāsādu| aṭharāvā adhyāya kaḻasu viśadu | myāṃ mhaṇitalā hā bhedu| jāṇoniyāṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: Thus, this Gita, a sacred offering to Vishnu, has its clear pinnacle in the eighteenth chapter. I have explained this secret, knowing it fully.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां सप्तदशापाठीं । अध्याय कैसेनि उठी । तो संबंधु सांगों दिठी। दिसे तैसा॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ saptadaśāpāṭhīṃ | adhyāya kaiseni uṭhī | to saṃbaṃdhu sāṃgoṃ diṭhī| dise taisā|| 50||
verses.meaning: Now, how does the next chapter, the eighteenth, arise after the seventeenth? I will explain that connection as it appears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां गंगायमुना उदक । वोघबगें वेगळिक । दावी होऊनि एक । पाणीपणें ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ gaṃgāyamunā udaka | voghabageṃ vegaḻika | dāvī hoūni eka | pāṇīpaṇeṃ || 51||
verses.meaning: Just as the waters of the Ganga and Yamuna, though appearing distinct in their currents, are in essence one and the same water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: न मोडतां दोन्ही आकार । घडिळें एक शरीर हें अर्धनारीनटेश्वर-। रूपीं दिसे॥५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: na moḍatāṃ donhī ākāra | ghaḍiḻeṃ eka śarīra heṃ ardhanārīnaṭeśvara-| rūpīṃ dise||52||
verses.meaning: Without breaking the two forms, they were molded into a single body, which is seen in the form of Ardhanarinateshwara.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना वाढिली दिवसें।॥ कळा बिंबीं पैसे। परी सिनानें लेवे जैसें । चंद्रीं नाहीं ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā vāḍhilī divaseṃ||| kaḻā biṃbīṃ paise| parī sināneṃ leve jaiseṃ | caṃdrīṃ nāhīṃ || 53||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon's phases wax and wane over many days, yet the moon itself remains undiminished, so too the Self is untouched by the changing states of the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं सिनानीं चारीं पदें। लोक तो एलोकावच्छेदें। अध्याबो अध्यायभेदें। गमे कौर॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ sinānīṃ cārīṃ padeṃ| loka to elokāvacchedeṃ| adhyābo adhyāyabhedeṃ| game kaura|| 54||
verses.meaning: Just as the four Vedas, though one, appear as distinct chapters to the common people, so too does the one Kaurava lineage appear divided by different branches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी प्रमेयाची उजरी। आनान रूप न धरी। नाना रत्नमणीं दोरी। एकचि जेसी ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī prameyācī ujarī| ānāna rūpa na dharī| nānā ratnamaṇīṃ dorī| ekaci jesī || 55||
verses.meaning: Just as a single thread holds together various precious gems, so too does the ultimate truth illuminate all forms without itself taking any specific form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मोतियें मिळोनि बहुवें। एकावळीचा पाडु आहे। परी शोभे रूप होये। एकचि तेथ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: motiyeṃ miḻoni bahuveṃ| ekāvaḻīcā pāḍu āhe| parī śobhe rūpa hoye| ekaci tetha|| 56||
verses.meaning: Many pearls together form a necklace, but the beauty and form are one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: फुलांफुलसरां लेख चढे । द्वुतीं दुजी अंगुळी न पडे। एलोक अध्याय तेणें पाडें। जाणावे हे ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: phulāṃphulasarāṃ lekha caḍhe | dvutīṃ dujī aṃguḻī na paḍe| eloka adhyāya teṇeṃ pāḍeṃ| jāṇāve he || 57||
verses.meaning: Just as a flower is not separate from its fragrance, and a finger cannot be separated from its second finger, so too should this chapter be understood as inseparable from the whole.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सात शतें श्लोक । अध्यायां अठरांचे लेख । परी देवो बोलिले एक। जें दुजें नाहीं ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāta śateṃ śloka | adhyāyāṃ aṭharāṃce lekha | parī devo bolile eka| jeṃ dujeṃ nāhīṃ || 58||
verses.meaning: Seven hundred verses, eighteen chapters' accounts, but the Lord spoke one truth, which has no second.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि म्यांही न सांडूनि ते सोये। ग्रंथ व्यक्ती केली आहे । प्रस्तुत तेणें निर्वाहें। निरूपण आइका ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi myāṃhī na sāṃḍūni te soye| graṃtha vyaktī kelī āhe | prastuta teṇeṃ nirvāheṃ| nirūpaṇa āikā || 59||
verses.meaning: And I, too, without abandoning that path, have brought this scripture into being. Now, through that very means, listen to this exposition.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सतरावा अध्यावो। पावतां पुरता ठावो । जे संपतां श्लोकीं देवो। बोलिले ऐसें ॥ ६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī satarāvā adhyāvo| pāvatāṃ puratā ṭhāvo | je saṃpatāṃ ślokīṃ devo| bolile aiseṃ || 60||
verses.meaning: Thus, upon reaching the end of the seventeenth chapter, the Lord spoke these words in the concluding verse.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना ब्रह्मनामाच्या विखीं । बुद्धि सांडूनि आस्तिकीं । कर्मे कीजती तितुकीं । असंतें होतीं ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā brahmanāmācyā vikhīṃ | buddhi sāṃḍūni āstikīṃ | karme kījatī titukīṃ | asaṃteṃ hotīṃ || 61||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, when the intellect abandons faith in the name of Brahman, all actions performed become unreal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा ऐकोनि देवाचा बोलु । अर्जुना आला डोलु। म्हणे कर्मनिष्ठां मळु । ठेविला देखों॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā aikoni devācā bolu | arjunā ālā ḍolu| mhaṇe karmaniṣṭhāṃ maḻu | ṭhevilā dekhoṃ||62||
verses.meaning: Hearing these words of the Lord, Arjuna was moved, thinking, "He has indeed shown the impurity in those devoted to action."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो अज्ञानांधु तंव बापुडा। ईश्वरुचि न देखे एवढा । तेथ नामचि एक पुढां। कां सुझे तया ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: to ajñānāṃdhu taṃva bāpuḍā| īśvaruci na dekhe evaḍhā | tetha nāmaci eka puḍhāṃ| kāṃ sujhe tayā || 63 ||
verses.meaning: As long as one is blinded by ignorance, they cannot even perceive God, who is so great. How then can they understand the significance of His name?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि रजतमें दोन्ही । गेलियावीण श्रद्धा सानी। ते कां लागे अभिधानीं | ब्रह्माचिये ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi rajatameṃ donhī | geliyāvīṇa śraddhā sānī| te kāṃ lāge abhidhānīṃ | brahmāciye || 64||
verses.meaning: And without the removal of both rajas and tamas, how can even a little faith be established in the concept of Brahman?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग कोता खेंब देणें।॥ वार्तेवरील धांवणें। सांडी पडे खेळणें। नागिणीचें तें॥६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga kotā kheṃba deṇeṃ||| vārtevarīla dhāṃvaṇeṃ| sāṃḍī paḍe kheḻaṇeṃ| nāgiṇīceṃ teṃ||65||
verses.meaning: Then, what is the use of giving a support, or running after the news, or playing with a discarded toy, when it is a serpent's play?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं कर्मे दुवाडें। तयां जन्मांतराची कडे । दुर्मेळावे येवढे । कर्मामाजीं ॥६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ karme duvāḍeṃ| tayāṃ janmāṃtarācī kaḍe | durmeḻāve yevaḍhe | karmāmājīṃ ||66||
verses.meaning: Just as actions are difficult, so too is the cycle of rebirth. It is rare to achieve such a state through actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना विपायें हें उजू होये। तरी ज्ञानाची योग्यता लाहे । एऱ्हबीं येणेंचि जाये । निरयालया ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā vipāyeṃ heṃ ujū hoye| tarī jñānācī yogyatā lāhe | eṟhabīṃ yeṇeṃci jāye | nirayālayā || 67||
verses.meaning: If this (mind) does not become straightforward, then it attains the worthiness of knowledge. Otherwise, through this very (mind), one goes to hell.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कर्मी हा ठायवरी । आहाती बहुवा अवसरी । आतां कर्मठां कैं वारी । मोक्षाची हे॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: karmī hā ṭhāyavarī | āhātī bahuvā avasarī | ātāṃ karmaṭhāṃ kaiṃ vārī | mokṣācī he|| 68||
verses.meaning: To this extent, actions (karma) are indeed many and varied. Now, how can those who are engrossed in rituals and actions ever attain liberation?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी फिटो कर्माचा पांगु, कौजो अवघाचि त्यागु।) आदरिजो अव्यंगु। संन्यासु हा॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī phiṭo karmācā pāṃgu, kaujo avaghāci tyāgu|) ādarijo avyaṃgu| saṃnyāsu hā||69||
verses.meaning: Therefore, let the debt of karma be repaid, let all attachment be renounced. Let this flawless renunciation be embraced.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कर्मबाधेची कहीं। जेथ भयाची गोठी नाहीं। तें आत्मज्ञान जिहीं। स्वाधीन होय ॥ ७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: karmabādhecī kahīṃ| jetha bhayācī goṭhī nāhīṃ| teṃ ātmajñāna jihīṃ| svādhīna hoya || 70||
verses.meaning: Where there is no fear of the bondage of karma, there self-knowledge becomes one's own.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ज्ञानाचे आवाहनमंत्र। जें ज्ञान पिकतें सुक्षेत्र। ज्ञान आकर्षितें सूत्र-। तंतु जे का॥७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jñānāce āvāhanamaṃtra| jeṃ jñāna pikateṃ sukṣetra| jñāna ākarṣiteṃ sūtra-| taṃtu je kā||71||
verses.meaning: Knowledge is like an invocation mantra, a fertile field where wisdom ripens, and a thread that draws all understanding together.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते दोनी संन्यास त्याग। अनुष्ठूनि सुटे जग। तरी हेंचि आतां चांग । व्यक्‍त पुसों ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: te donī saṃnyāsa tyāga| anuṣṭhūni suṭe jaga| tarī heṃci ātāṃ cāṃga | vyak‍ta pusoṃ || 72||
verses.meaning: If the world is liberated by practicing both renunciation and abandonment, then this is indeed a good thing to ask about now.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें म्हणौनि पार्थे । त्यागसंन्यासव्यवस्थे । रूप होआवया जेथें । प्रश्‍नु केला ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ mhaṇauni pārthe | tyāgasaṃnyāsavyavasthe | rūpa hoāvayā jetheṃ | praś‍nu kelā || 73||
verses.meaning: Having said this, Arjuna then posed a question to give form to the system of renunciation and abandonment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ प्रत्युत्तरे बोली । श्रीकृष्णें जे चावळिली । तया व्यक्‍ती जाळी अष्टादशा ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha pratyuttare bolī | śrīkṛṣṇeṃ je cāvaḻilī | tayā vyak‍tī jāḻī aṣṭādaśā || 74||
verses.meaning: There, the replies spoken by Shri Krishna, which illuminated the eighteen chapters, burned away the individual self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं जन्यजनकभावें । अध्यावो अध्यायातें प्रसवे। आतां ऐका बरवें। पुसिलें जें॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ janyajanakabhāveṃ | adhyāvo adhyāyāteṃ prasave| ātāṃ aikā baraveṃ| pusileṃ jeṃ|| 75||
verses.meaning: Thus, through the relationship of parent and offspring, one chapter gives birth to another. Now, listen carefully to what has been asked.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी पंडुकुमरें तेणें । देवाचें सरतें बोलणें । जाणोनि अंतःकरणें। काणी घेतली ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī paṃḍukumareṃ teṇeṃ | devāceṃ sarateṃ bolaṇeṃ | jāṇoni aṃtaḥkaraṇeṃ| kāṇī ghetalī || 76||
verses.meaning: Then, Arjuna, understanding that the Lord's discourse was coming to an end, took it to heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं तत्त्वविषयीं भला । तो निश्‍चितु असे कौर जाहला । परी देवो राहे उगला । तें साहावेना ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ tattvaviṣayīṃ bhalā | to niś‍citu ase kaura jāhalā | parī devo rāhe ugalā | teṃ sāhāvenā || 77||
verses.meaning: Indeed, he (Arjuna) was certain about the truth of the Self, but he could not bear the Lord remaining silent.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वत्स धालयाही वरी। धेनू न बचावी दुरी । अनन्य प्रीतीची परी। ऐसी आहे॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: vatsa dhālayāhī varī| dhenū na bacāvī durī | ananya prītīcī parī| aisī āhe|| 78||
verses.meaning: Even after the calf has drunk its fill, the cow does not move away from it. Such is the nature of unwavering love.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें काजेंबीणही बोलावें । तें देखिलें तरी पाहावें। भोगितां चाड दुणावे । पढियंतयाठायीं ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ kājeṃbīṇahī bolāveṃ | teṃ dekhileṃ tarī pāhāveṃ| bhogitāṃ cāḍa duṇāve | paḍhiyaṃtayāṭhāyīṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: Therefore, one should speak without any purpose, look without seeing, and desire more while experiencing, especially when it comes to the beloved.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी प्रेमाची हे जाती । आणि पार्थ तंब तेचि मूर्ती । म्हणौनि करूं लाहे खंती । उगेपणाची ॥ ८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī premācī he jātī | āṇi pārtha taṃba teci mūrtī | mhaṇauni karūṃ lāhe khaṃtī | ugepaṇācī || 80||
verses.meaning: Such is the nature of love, O Arjuna, and you are indeed that very embodiment. Therefore, you are able to lament the state of inaction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि संवादाचेनि मिषें। जे अव्यवहारी वस्तु असे । तेचि भोगिजे कौं जैसें । आरिसां रूप॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi saṃvādāceni miṣeṃ| je avyavahārī vastu ase | teci bhogije kauṃ jaiseṃ | ārisāṃ rūpa|| 81||
verses.meaning: And through the medium of dialogue, that which is beyond worldly dealings is experienced, just as a reflection is seen in a mirror.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग संवादु तोही पारुखे। तरी भोगितां भोगणें थोके । हें कां साहावेल सुखें । लांचावळेया ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga saṃvādu tohī pārukhe| tarī bhogitāṃ bhogaṇeṃ thoke | heṃ kāṃ sāhāvela sukheṃ | lāṃcāvaḻeyā || 82||
verses.meaning: Then even the conversation ceases, and the enjoyment of experiences stops. How can this be easily endured by one who is greedy?

verses.shloka_devanagari: यालागीं त्याग संन्यास। पुसावयाचें घेऊनि मिस। मग उपलबिलें दुस। गीतेचें तें॥८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: yālāgīṃ tyāga saṃnyāsa| pusāvayāceṃ gheūni misa| maga upalabileṃ dusa| gīteceṃ teṃ||83||
verses.meaning: Therefore, taking the pretext of asking about renunciation (tyaga) and asceticism (sannyasa), the second chapter of the Gita was then revealed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अठरावा अध्यावो नोहे। हे एकाध्यायी गीताचि आहे। जें बांसरुचि गाय दुहे। तें वेळु कायसा ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aṭharāvā adhyāvo nohe| he ekādhyāyī gītāci āhe| jeṃ bāṃsaruci gāya duhe| teṃ veḻu kāyasā || 84||
verses.meaning: This is not merely the eighteenth chapter; it is the entire Gita in one chapter. When a calf drinks milk from its mother, what need is there for a measure?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी संपतां अवसरीं । गीता आदरविली माघारीं। स्वामी भृत्याचा न करी । संबादु काई ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī saṃpatāṃ avasarīṃ | gītā ādaravilī māghārīṃ| svāmī bhṛtyācā na karī | saṃbādu kāī || 85 ||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the opportune moment arrived, the Gita was brought forth again. Why would the Master not converse with His servant?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें असो ऐसें । अर्जुने पुसिजत असे । म्हणे विनंती विश्‍वेशें। अबधारिजो॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ aso aiseṃ | arjune pusijata ase | mhaṇe vinaṃtī viś‍veśeṃ| abadhārijo|| 86||
verses.meaning: But let this be so. Arjuna is asking, saying, "O Lord of the Universe, please accept my request."

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां जी संन्यासु आणि त्यागु। इयां दोहीं एक अर्थी लागु। जैसा संघातु आणि संघु। संघातेंचि बोलिजे॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ jī saṃnyāsu āṇi tyāgu| iyāṃ dohīṃ eka arthī lāgu| jaisā saṃghātu āṇi saṃghu| saṃghāteṃci bolije|| 87||
verses.meaning: Indeed, Sannyasa and Tyaga, these two terms carry the same meaning. Just as 'sanghatu' and 'sanghu' both refer to the same 'sanghata' (union/collection).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंचि त्यागें आणि संन्यासें। त्यागुचि बोलिजतु असे। आमचेनि तंब मानसें। जाणिजे हेंचि॥८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃci tyāgeṃ āṇi saṃnyāseṃ| tyāguci bolijatu ase| āmaceni taṃba mānaseṃ| jāṇije heṃci||88||
verses.meaning: Similarly, through renunciation and asceticism, only renunciation is spoken of. By our mind, this alone is to be understood.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना कांहीं आथी अर्थभेदु। तो देवो करोतु विशदु । तेथ म्हणती श्रीमुकुंदु। भिन्नचि पैं॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā kāṃhīṃ āthī arthabhedu| to devo karotu viśadu | tetha mhaṇatī śrīmukuṃdu| bhinnaci paiṃ|| 89||
verses.meaning: There is no difference in meaning. May that God make it clear. There, Shri Mukunda says, "Indeed, I am different."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अर्जुना तुझ्या मनीं। त्याग संन्यास दोनी। एकार्थ गमले हें मानीं। मीही साच ॥ ९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī arjunā tujhyā manīṃ| tyāga saṃnyāsa donī| ekārtha gamale heṃ mānīṃ| mīhī sāca || 90||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, if you consider renunciation and relinquishment to be one and the same in your mind, then know that I also affirm this truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इहीं दोहीं कौर शब्दीं। त्यागुचि बोलिजे त्रिशुद्धी। परी कारण एथ भेदीं।॥ येतुलेंचि॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ihīṃ dohīṃ kaura śabdīṃ| tyāguci bolije triśuddhī| parī kāraṇa etha bhedīṃ||| yetuleṃci||91||
verses.meaning: By these two words, renunciation is indeed spoken of as the absolute truth. But the reason for the distinction here is only this much.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें निपटूनि कर्म सांडिजे। तें सांडणें संन्यासु म्हणिजे । आणि फलमात्र कां त्यजिजे। तो त्यागु गा॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ nipaṭūni karma sāṃḍije| teṃ sāṃḍaṇeṃ saṃnyāsu mhaṇije | āṇi phalamātra kāṃ tyajije| to tyāgu gā|| 92||
verses.meaning: When actions are completely renounced, that renunciation is called Sannyasa. And when only the fruits of action are abandoned, that is known as Tyaga.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कोणा कर्माचे फळ। सांडिजे कोण कर्म केवळ हेंही सांगों विवळ। चित्त दे पां॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī koṇā karmāce phaḻa| sāṃḍije koṇa karma kevaḻa heṃhī sāṃgoṃ vivaḻa| citta de pāṃ|| 93||
verses.meaning: Therefore, what is the fruit of which action? What action is purely that? I will explain this clearly; please pay attention.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आपैसीं दांगें डोंगर । झाडें डाळती अपार । तैसे लांबे राजागर। नुठिती ते॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī āpaisīṃ dāṃgeṃ ḍoṃgara | jhāḍeṃ ḍāḻatī apāra | taise lāṃbe rājāgara| nuṭhitī te|| 94||
verses.meaning: Just as mountains and countless trees and branches grow spontaneously, so too do these long-standing royal residences arise without effort.

verses.shloka_devanagari: न पेरितां सैंघ तृणें। उठती तैसें साळीचें होणें । नाहीं गा राबाउणें । जियापरी ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: na peritāṃ saiṃgha tṛṇeṃ| uṭhatī taiseṃ sāḻīceṃ hoṇeṃ | nāhīṃ gā rābāuṇeṃ | jiyāparī || 95||
verses.meaning: Just as grass grows without being sown, but rice cannot grow without cultivation, so too is the nature of things.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का अंग जाहलें सहजें। परी लेणें उद्यमें कीजे। नदी आपैसी आपादिजे। विहिरी जेवीं ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā aṃga jāhaleṃ sahajeṃ| parī leṇeṃ udyameṃ kīje| nadī āpaisī āpādije| vihirī jevīṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: Just as the body is naturally formed, ornaments are made through effort. A river forms on its own, but a well is dug with effort.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें नित्य नैमित्तिक। कर्म होय स्वाभाविक । परी न कामितां कामिक। न निफजे जें॥९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ nitya naimittika| karma hoya svābhāvika | parī na kāmitāṃ kāmika| na niphaje jeṃ||97||
verses.meaning: Similarly, daily and occasional rituals happen naturally, but without desire, no desire-driven action is accomplished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का कामनेचेनि दळवाडें। जें उभारावया घडे। अशवमेधादिक फुडे। याग जेथ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā kāmaneceni daḻavāḍeṃ| jeṃ ubhārāvayā ghaḍe| aśavamedhādika phuḍe| yāga jetha|| 98||
verses.meaning: Or, by the power of desire, are those great sacrifices like Ashwamedha performed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वापी कूप आराम अग्रहारें हन महाग्राम। आणीकही नानासंभ्रम । व्रतांचे ते॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāpī kūpa ārāma agrahāreṃ hana mahāgrāma| āṇīkahī nānāsaṃbhrama | vratāṃce te|| 99||
verses.meaning: By building wells, step-wells, gardens, and agraharas (villages granted to Brahmins), and by performing various other elaborate vows, great merit is accumulated.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें इष्टापूत सकळ। जया कामना एक मूळ। जें केलें भोगवी फळ बांधोनियां ॥ १००॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ iṣṭāpūta sakaḻa| jayā kāmanā eka mūḻa| jeṃ keleṃ bhogavī phaḻa bāṃdhoniyāṃ || 100||
verses.meaning: Thus, all good deeds and sacrifices, which have desire as their sole root, bind one to experience their fruits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देहाचिया गांबा आलिया । जन्ममृत्यूचिया सोहळिया। ना म्हणों नये धनंजया। जियापरी॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: dehāciyā gāṃbā āliyā | janmamṛtyūciyā sohaḻiyā| nā mhaṇoṃ naye dhanaṃjayā| jiyāparī|| 1||
verses.meaning: When one takes on a body, O Dhananjaya, one cannot refuse the celebrations of birth and death, just as it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का ललाटांचें लिहिलें) न मोडे गा कांहीं केलें। काळेगोरेपण धुतलें। फिटों नेणें॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā lalāṭāṃceṃ lihileṃ) na moḍe gā kāṃhīṃ keleṃ| kāḻegorepaṇa dhutaleṃ| phiṭoṃ neṇeṃ|| 2||
verses.meaning: What is written on the forehead by destiny cannot be undone by any effort. Just as fairness or darkness of skin cannot be washed away, so too fate is unchangeable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: केलें काम्य कर्म तैसें। फळ भोगावया धरणें बैेसे। न फेडितां त्रण जैसें। बोसंडीना॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: keleṃ kāmya karma taiseṃ| phaḻa bhogāvayā dharaṇeṃ baiese| na pheḍitāṃ traṇa jaiseṃ| bosaṃḍīnā|| 3||
verses.meaning: Just as one must experience the fruit of actions performed with desire, and just as a debt must be repaid, so too one cannot escape the consequences of such deeds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का कामनाही न करितां। अवसांत घडे पंडुसुता । तरी वायकांडें न झुंझतां। लागे जैसें ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā kāmanāhī na karitāṃ| avasāṃta ghaḍe paṃḍusutā | tarī vāyakāṃḍeṃ na jhuṃjhatāṃ| lāge jaiseṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, if one achieves something without any desire, it is like hitting a target without even aiming an arrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गूळ नेणतां तोंडीं । घातला देचि गोडी । आगी मानूनि राखोंडी । चेपिला पोळी ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: gūḻa neṇatāṃ toṃḍīṃ | ghātalā deci goḍī | āgī mānūni rākhoṃḍī | cepilā poḻī || 5||
verses.meaning: Just as jaggery, even if one doesn't know what it is, gives sweetness when put in the mouth, and fire, even if mistaken for ash, burns when poked, so too does the divine principle act according to its nature, regardless of human perception or understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: काम्यकर्मी हें एक। सामर्थ्य आथी स्वाभाविक । म्हणौनि नको कौतुक । मुमुक्षु एथ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāmyakarmī heṃ eka| sāmarthya āthī svābhāvika | mhaṇauni nako kautuka | mumukṣu etha|| 6||
verses.meaning: Performing actions with a desire for their fruits is inherently powerful. Therefore, those seeking liberation should not be curious about such actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना पार्था ऐसें। जें काम्य कर्म गा असे। तें त्यजिजे विष जैसें। बोकूनियां॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā pārthā aiseṃ| jeṃ kāmya karma gā ase| teṃ tyajije viṣa jaiseṃ| bokūniyāṃ|| 7||
verses.meaning: Indeed, O Partha, any action performed with a desire for its fruits should be abandoned, just as one would abandon poison after recognizing it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तया त्यागातें जगीं। संन्यासु ऐसया भंगीं। बोलिजे अंतरंगीं। सर्वद्रष्टा॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga tayā tyāgāteṃ jagīṃ| saṃnyāsu aisayā bhaṃgīṃ| bolije aṃtaraṃgīṃ| sarvadraṣṭā|| 8||
verses.meaning: Then, in this world, such renunciation is internally called Sannyasa by the all-seer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें काम्यकर्म सांडणें। तें कामनेतेंचि उपडणें। द्रव्यत्यागें दवडणें । भय जैसें ॥ ९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ kāmyakarma sāṃḍaṇeṃ| teṃ kāmaneteṃci upaḍaṇeṃ| dravyatyāgeṃ davaḍaṇeṃ | bhaya jaiseṃ || 9 ||
verses.meaning: Abandoning desire-driven actions is like uprooting desire itself, or like dispelling fear by giving up wealth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि सोमसूर्यग्रहणें। येऊनि करविती पार्वणें। कां मातापितरमरणें । अंकित जे दिवस ॥ ११० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi somasūryagrahaṇeṃ| yeūni karavitī pārvaṇeṃ| kāṃ mātāpitaramaraṇeṃ | aṃkita je divasa || 110 ||
verses.meaning: Just as solar and lunar eclipses bring about special observances, or the days marked by the passing of one's parents.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा अतिथी हन पावे । ऐसैसें पडे जें करावें। तें तें कर्म जाणावें। नैमित्तिक गा॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā atithī hana pāve | aisaiseṃ paḍe jeṃ karāveṃ| teṃ teṃ karma jāṇāveṃ| naimittika gā|| 11||
verses.meaning: Or, if a guest arrives, whatever needs to be done for them, know that to be a Naimittika Karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वार्षिया क्षोभे गगन । वसंतें दुणावे वन । देहा श्वंगारी यौवन-। दशा जैसी॥१२॥
verses.shloka_iast: vārṣiyā kṣobhe gagana | vasaṃteṃ duṇāve vana | dehā śvaṃgārī yauvana-| daśā jaisī||12||
verses.meaning: Just as the monsoon rains stir the sky, and spring doubles the beauty of the forest, so too does the state of youth adorn the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का सोमकांतु सोमें पघळे। सूर्ये फांकती कमळें। 'एथ असे तेंचि पाल्हाळे। आन नये॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā somakāṃtu someṃ paghaḻe| sūrye phāṃkatī kamaḻeṃ| 'etha ase teṃci pālhāḻe| āna naye|| 13||
verses.meaning: Just as the moonstone melts by the moon, and lotuses bloom by the sun, so too, what is already present within expands and flourishes; nothing new is created.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें नित्य जें का कर्म। तेंचि निमित्ताचे लाहे नियम। एथ उंचावे तेणें नाम। नैमित्तिक होय ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ nitya jeṃ kā karma| teṃci nimittāce lāhe niyama| etha uṃcāve teṇeṃ nāma| naimittika hoya || 14||
verses.meaning: Thus, the daily prescribed actions, when performed with a specific purpose, acquire the name 'naimittik' or occasional actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि सायंप्रातर्मध्यान्हीं। जें कां करणीय प्रतिदिनीं।॥ परी दृष्टि जैसी 'लोचनीं। अधिक नोहे॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi sāyaṃprātarmadhyānhīṃ| jeṃ kāṃ karaṇīya pratidinīṃ||| parī dṛṣṭi jaisī 'locanīṃ| adhika nohe|| 15||
verses.meaning: And that which is to be done daily, morning, evening, and noon, is like the eye's sight; it is not something extra or additional.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां नापादितां गती। चरणीं जैसी आथी । नातरी ते दीप्ती । दीपब्रिंबीं॥। १६॥ वासु नेदितां जैसें । चंदनीं सौरभ्य असे । अधिकाराचे तेसें। रूपचि जें॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ nāpāditāṃ gatī| caraṇīṃ jaisī āthī | nātarī te dīptī | dīpabriṃbīṃ||| 16|| vāsu neditāṃ jaiseṃ | caṃdanīṃ saurabhya ase | adhikārāce teseṃ| rūpaci jeṃ|| 17||
verses.meaning: Just as the movement of the feet is inherent in them, or as the radiance is inherent in the flame of a lamp. Or just as fragrance is inherent in sandalwood without being imparted to it, so too is the form of authority inherent in itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नित्य कर्म ऐसें जनीं। पार्था बोलिजे तें मानीं । एवं नित्य नैमित्तिक दोन्हीं । दाविलीं तुज ॥ १८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nitya karma aiseṃ janīṃ| pārthā bolije teṃ mānīṃ | evaṃ nitya naimittika donhīṃ | dāvilīṃ tuja || 18 ||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, what is known as 'Nitya Karma' (daily duties) in this world, consider that to be both 'Nitya' (regular) and 'Naimittika' (occasional) duties, as I have explained to you.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हेंचि नित्यनैमित्तिक । अनुष्ठेय आवश्यक । म्हणौनि म्हणों पाहती एक। वांझ ययातें ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃci nityanaimittika | anuṣṭheya āvaśyaka | mhaṇauni mhaṇoṃ pāhatī eka| vāṃjha yayāteṃ || 99||
verses.meaning: Some consider this to be merely a daily and occasional ritual, an essential practice, and thus they see it as barren.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी भोजनीं जैसें होये। तृप्ति लाभे भूक जाये। तैसें नित्य नैमित्तिकीं आहे। सर्वांगी फळ॥ १२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī bhojanīṃ jaiseṃ hoye| tṛpti lābhe bhūka jāye| taiseṃ nitya naimittikīṃ āhe| sarvāṃgī phaḻa|| 120||
verses.meaning: Just as eating food brings satisfaction and alleviates hunger, so too, performing daily and occasional rituals yields comprehensive benefits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौड आगिठां पडे। तरी मळु तुटे वानी चढे। या कर्मा तया सांगडें। फळ जाणावें ॥ २१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauḍa āgiṭhāṃ paḍe| tarī maḻu tuṭe vānī caḍhe| yā karmā tayā sāṃgaḍeṃ| phaḻa jāṇāveṃ || 219||
verses.meaning: Just as gold, when put into fire, loses its impurities and its luster increases, so too should one understand the fruit of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे प्रत्यवाय तंव गळे । स्वाधिकार बहुवें उजळे। तेथ हातोफळिया मिळे। सद्‌गतीसी॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je pratyavāya taṃva gaḻe | svādhikāra bahuveṃ ujaḻe| tetha hātophaḻiyā miḻe| sad‌gatīsī|| 22||
verses.meaning: When all obstacles are removed, and one's inherent spiritual authority shines brightly, then the path to the highest spiritual state becomes as easily attainable as a fruit in hand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येवढेवरी ढिसाळ। नित्यनैमित्तिकीं आहे फळ। परी तें त्यजिजे मूळ। नक्षत्रीं जैसें॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: yevaḍhevarī ḍhisāḻa| nityanaimittikīṃ āhe phaḻa| parī teṃ tyajije mūḻa| nakṣatrīṃ jaiseṃ|| 23||
verses.meaning: Even though there is a reward for performing daily and occasional rituals, it is ultimately abandoned, just as a star is abandoned at the rising of the moon.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लता पिके आघवी। तंब च्यूत बांधे पालबीं। मग हात न लावित माधवीं। सोडूनि घाली॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: latā pike āghavī| taṃba cyūta bāṃdhe pālabīṃ| maga hāta na lāvita mādhavīṃ| soḍūni ghālī|| 24||
verses.meaning: The creeper, having grown fully, entwines itself around the mango tree's new shoots. Then, in the spring season, it lets go without being touched.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी नोलांडितां कर्मरेखा। ४२६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी चित्त दीजे नित्यनैमित्तिका । पाठीं फळा कीजे अशेखा । वातांचे वानी ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī nolāṃḍitāṃ karmarekhā| 426 śrījñāneśvarī citta dīje nityanaimittikā | pāṭhīṃ phaḻā kīje aśekhā | vātāṃce vānī || 25||
verses.meaning: Similarly, without transgressing the line of action (karma), O Dnyaneshwari, one should always perform the daily and occasional duties. Afterwards, one should offer all the fruits of these actions to the Lord, like offering the wind to the wind itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया कर्मफळत्यागातें॥ त्यागु म्हणती पैं जाणते। एवं त्याग संन्यास तूतें। परिसविळे॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā karmaphaḻatyāgāteṃ|| tyāgu mhaṇatī paiṃ jāṇate| evaṃ tyāga saṃnyāsa tūteṃ| parisaviḻe|| 26||
verses.meaning: The wise call this renunciation of the fruits of action as true renunciation. Thus, I have explained to you the meaning of renunciation and sannyasa.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा संन्यासु जैं संभवे। तैं काम्य बाधूं न पावे। निषिद्ध तंब स्वभावें। निषेधें गेळें॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā saṃnyāsu jaiṃ saṃbhave| taiṃ kāmya bādhūṃ na pāve| niṣiddha taṃba svabhāveṃ| niṣedheṃ geḻeṃ|| 27||
verses.meaning: When such renunciation is attained, then desire cannot hinder; and naturally, what is forbidden is eliminated by its very prohibition.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि नित्यादिक जें असे। तें येणें 'फळत्यागें नासे। शिर लोटलिया जैसें । येर आंग ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi nityādika jeṃ ase| teṃ yeṇeṃ 'phaḻatyāgeṃ nāse| śira loṭaliyā jaiseṃ | yera āṃga || 28||
verses.meaning: And all the daily rituals and other actions, by this renunciation of the fruits of action, are destroyed, just as when the head is severed, the rest of the body perishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सस्य फळपाकांत। तैसें निमालिया कर्मजात। आत्मज्ञान गिंवसित। अपैसें ये॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sasya phaḻapākāṃta| taiseṃ nimāliyā karmajāta| ātmajñāna giṃvasita| apaiseṃ ye|| 29||
verses.meaning: Just as the crop naturally yields fruit, so too, when all actions cease, self-knowledge spontaneously arises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसिया निगुती दोनी । त्याग संन्यास अनुष्ठानीं। पडले गा आत्मज्ञानीं। बांधती पाटु॥ १३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyā nigutī donī | tyāga saṃnyāsa anuṣṭhānīṃ| paḍale gā ātmajñānīṃ| bāṃdhatī pāṭu|| 130||
verses.meaning: In this way, the renunciates, through the practice of renunciation and detachment, attain the state of self-realization and establish themselves firmly in it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी हे निगुती चुके । मग त्यागु कौजे हाततुकें । तें कांहीं न त्यजे अधिकें। गोंबींचि पडे॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī he nigutī cuke | maga tyāgu kauje hātatukeṃ | teṃ kāṃhīṃ na tyaje adhikeṃ| goṃbīṃci paḍe|| 31||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, if this precision is missed, then the renunciation becomes a mere guess. Nothing more is renounced; one falls into a greater entanglement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें औषध व्याधी अनोळख । तें घेतलिया परतें विख। कां अन्न न मानितां भूक । मारी ना काय ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ auṣadha vyādhī anoḻakha | teṃ ghetaliyā parateṃ vikha| kāṃ anna na mānitāṃ bhūka | mārī nā kāya || 32||
verses.meaning: When medicine is taken without knowing the disease, it becomes poison. Similarly, if food is consumed without hunger, will it not kill?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि त्याज्य जें नोहे। तेथ त्यागातें न सुवावें। त्याज्यालागीं नोहावें । 'लोभापर॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tyājya jeṃ nohe| tetha tyāgāteṃ na suvāveṃ| tyājyālāgīṃ nohāveṃ | 'lobhāpara|| 33||
verses.meaning: Therefore, that which is not to be renounced, should not be renounced. For that which is to be renounced, one should not be attached to it out of greed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चुकलिया त्यागाचे वेझें। केला सर्वत्यागुही होय वोझें । न देखती सर्वत्र दुजें। बीतराग ते॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: cukaliyā tyāgāce vejheṃ| kelā sarvatyāguhī hoya vojheṃ | na dekhatī sarvatra dujeṃ| bītarāga te|| 34||
verses.meaning: When the path of renunciation is missed, even complete renunciation becomes a burden. Those who are truly detached do not perceive duality anywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एकां फळाभिलाष न ठके । ते कर्मातें म्हणती बंधकें । जैसें आपण नग्न भांडकें । जगातें म्हणे ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ekāṃ phaḻābhilāṣa na ṭhake | te karmāteṃ mhaṇatī baṃdhakeṃ | jaiseṃ āpaṇa nagna bhāṃḍakeṃ | jagāteṃ mhaṇe || 35||
verses.meaning: Some, whose desire for the fruits of action does not cease, call those actions binding. It is like a naked, quarrelsome person calling the world naked.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का जिव्हालंपट रोगिया । अन्नें दूषी धनंजया । आंगा न रुसे कोढिया। मासियां कोपे॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā jivhālaṃpaṭa rogiyā | anneṃ dūṣī dhanaṃjayā | āṃgā na ruse koḍhiyā| māsiyāṃ kope|| 36||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, why does a gluttonous patient find fault with food? Or why does a leper not like his own flesh, but gets angry at flies?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें फळकाम दुर्बळ। म्हणती कर्मचि किडाळ। मग निर्णयो देती केवळ । त्यजावें ऐसा॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ phaḻakāma durbaḻa| mhaṇatī karmaci kiḍāḻa| maga nirṇayo detī kevaḻa | tyajāveṃ aisā|| 37||
verses.meaning: Similarly, those who are weak due to the desire for fruits of action consider action itself to be impure. Then they simply decide that it should be abandoned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एक म्हणती यागादिक । करावेंचि आवश्यक । जे यावांचूनि शोधक । आन नसे॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: eka mhaṇatī yāgādika | karāveṃci āvaśyaka | je yāvāṃcūni śodhaka | āna nase|| 38||
verses.meaning: Some say that performing sacrifices and rituals is absolutely essential, for without them, there is no other path to purification.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मनशुद्धीच्या मार्गी । जैं विजयी व्हावें वेगीं । तैं कर्म सबळालागीं ( संबंधालागीं )। आळसु न कोजे॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: manaśuddhīcyā mārgī | jaiṃ vijayī vhāveṃ vegīṃ | taiṃ karma sabaḻālāgīṃ ( saṃbaṃdhālāgīṃ )| āḻasu na koje|| 39||
verses.meaning: When one wishes to swiftly achieve victory on the path of mental purity, then one should not be lazy in performing strong actions (or in engaging with strong connections).

verses.shloka_devanagari: भांगार आथी शोधावें। तरी आगी जेबीं नुबगावें। कां दर्पणालागीं सांचावें। अधिक रज॥ १४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhāṃgāra āthī śodhāveṃ| tarī āgī jebīṃ nubagāveṃ| kāṃ darpaṇālāgīṃ sāṃcāveṃ| adhika raja|| 140||
verses.meaning: Just as one should not be averse to fire when searching for gold, or accumulate more dust on a mirror, so too should one not be averse to the means of spiritual realization.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना वस्त्रे चोख होआवीं। ऐसें आथी जरी जीवीं। तरी संवदणी न मनावी। मलिन जैसी ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā vastre cokha hoāvīṃ| aiseṃ āthī jarī jīvīṃ| tarī saṃvadaṇī na manāvī| malina jaisī || 49||
verses.meaning: If one desires various clothes to be clean, then one should not consider the washerwoman as impure.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं कर्मे क्लेशकारें। म्हणौनि न न्यावीं अव्हेरें। कां अन्नलाभें अरुवारें। रांधितिये उणें ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ karme kleśakāreṃ| mhaṇauni na nyāvīṃ avhereṃ| kāṃ annalābheṃ aruvāreṃ| rāṃdhitiye uṇeṃ || 42||
verses.meaning: Similarly, actions that cause distress should not be neglected. Or, just as one does not cook food carelessly when there is a scarcity of provisions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इहीं इहीं गा शब्दीं। एक कर्मी बांधिती बुद्धी। ऐसा त्यागु विसंवादीं।॥ पडोनि ठेला ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ihīṃ ihīṃ gā śabdīṃ| eka karmī bāṃdhitī buddhī| aisā tyāgu visaṃvādīṃ||| paḍoni ṭhelā || 43||
verses.meaning: Indeed, by these very words, some bind their intellect to action. Thus, renunciation falls into discord.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी विसंवादु तो फिटे। त्यागाचा निश्चयो भेटे । तैसें बोलो गोमटें । अवधान देई ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī visaṃvādu to phiṭe| tyāgācā niścayo bheṭe | taiseṃ bolo gomaṭeṃ | avadhāna deī || 44||
verses.meaning: Then the discord will cease, and the resolve for renunciation will be attained. Therefore, listen attentively to these beautiful words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी त्यागु एथें पांडवा । त्रिविधु पैं जाणावा । तया त्रिविधाही बरवा । विभाग करू ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tyāgu etheṃ pāṃḍavā | trividhu paiṃ jāṇāvā | tayā trividhāhī baravā | vibhāga karū || 45||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Pandava, know that renunciation is of three kinds. I shall now clearly explain these three divisions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: त्यागाचे तीन्ही प्रकार। कीजती जरी गोचर। तरी तूं इत्यर्थाचें सार । इतुलें जाण॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tyāgāce tīnhī prakāra| kījatī jarī gocara| tarī tūṃ ityarthāceṃ sāra | ituleṃ jāṇa|| 46||
verses.meaning: Even if the three types of renunciation are performed visibly, know this much to be the essence of the ultimate truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मज सर्वज्ञाचिये बुद्धी । जें अलोट माने त्रिशुद्धी। निश्चयतत्त्व तें आधीं। अवधारीं पां॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maja sarvajñāciye buddhī | jeṃ aloṭa māne triśuddhī| niścayatattva teṃ ādhīṃ| avadhārīṃ pāṃ|| 47||
verses.meaning: Listen first to that principle which, in my all-knowing intellect, is considered undeniable and absolutely true in all three ways (thought, word, and deed).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आपुल्िये सोडवणे । जो मुमुक्षु जागो म्हणे । तया सर्वस्वें करणें । हेंचि एक॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī āpuliye soḍavaṇe | jo mumukṣu jāgo mhaṇe | tayā sarvasveṃ karaṇeṃ | heṃci eka|| 48||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for the seeker who desires to awaken to their own liberation, this alone is the ultimate endeavor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जियें यज्ञदानतपादिकें । इयें कर्मे आवश्यकें । तियें न सांडावीं पांधिकें । पाउलें जैसीं ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiyeṃ yajñadānatapādikeṃ | iyeṃ karme āvaśyakeṃ | tiyeṃ na sāṃḍāvīṃ pāṃdhikeṃ | pāuleṃ jaisīṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: Therefore, acts like sacrifices, charity, and penance, which are essential, should not be abandoned, just as one does not abandon the steps on a path.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हारपळें न देखिजे। तंव तयाचा मागु न सांडिजे। कां तृप्त न होतां न लोटिजे। भाणें जेवीं ॥ १५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: hārapaḻeṃ na dekhije| taṃva tayācā māgu na sāṃḍije| kāṃ tṛpta na hotāṃ na loṭije| bhāṇeṃ jevīṃ || 150||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not give up searching until something lost is found, or as one does not remove a plate of food until satisfied, so too should one not abandon the spiritual quest until the ultimate truth is realized.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाव थडी न पवतां। न खांडिजे केळी न फळतां। का ठेविलें न दिसतां। दीपु जैसा ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: nāva thaḍī na pavatāṃ| na khāṃḍije keḻī na phaḻatāṃ| kā ṭhevileṃ na disatāṃ| dīpu jaisā || 51||
verses.meaning: Just as a boat does not reach the shore, a banana tree is not cut before it bears fruit, or a lamp is not kept hidden from sight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी आत्मज्ञानविखीं। जंब निश्‍चिती नाहीं निकी । तंब नोहावें यागादिकीं। उदासीन ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī ātmajñānavikhīṃ| jaṃba niś‍citī nāhīṃ nikī | taṃba nohāveṃ yāgādikīṃ| udāsīna || 52||
verses.meaning: Similarly, as long as there is no firm conviction in self-knowledge, one should not be indifferent to sacrifices and other spiritual practices.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी स्वाधिकारानुरूपें। तियें यज्ञदानें तपें। अनुष्ठावींचि साक्षेपें। अधिकेंवर॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī svādhikārānurūpeṃ| tiyeṃ yajñadāneṃ tapeṃ| anuṣṭhāvīṃci sākṣepeṃ| adhikeṃvara|| 53||
verses.meaning: Therefore, according to one's own authority and capacity, one should diligently perform these sacrifices, charities, and austerities with even greater zeal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें चालणें वेगावत जाये। तो वेगु बैसावयाचि होये। तैसा कर्मातिशयो आहे । नेष्कर्म्यालागीं ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ cālaṇeṃ vegāvata jāye| to vegu baisāvayāci hoye| taisā karmātiśayo āhe | neṣkarmyālāgīṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: Just as the speed of walking eventually leads to sitting, so too does the excess of action (karma) ultimately lead to inaction (naishkarmya).

verses.shloka_devanagari: अधिकें जंब जंब औषधी । सेवनेंचि मांडी बांधी । तंब तंव मुकिजे व्याधी । तयाचिये ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: adhikeṃ jaṃba jaṃba auṣadhī | sevaneṃci māṃḍī bāṃdhī | taṃba taṃva mukije vyādhī | tayāciye || 55||
verses.meaning: The more one consumes various medicines, the more one is freed from diseases.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं कर्मे हातोपातीं। जैं कीजती यथानिगुती। तें रजतमें झडती । झाडा देऊनी ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ karme hātopātīṃ| jaiṃ kījatī yathānigutī| teṃ rajatameṃ jhaḍatī | jhāḍā deūnī || 56||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when actions are performed with such precision and devotion, the qualities of Rajas and Tamas are shed, leaving no trace behind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का पाठोवाटीं पुटें। भांगारा खारु देणें घटे। तैं कोड झडकरी तुटे । निर्व्याजु होय ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā pāṭhovāṭīṃ puṭeṃ| bhāṃgārā khāru deṇeṃ ghaṭe| taiṃ koḍa jhaḍakarī tuṭe | nirvyāju hoya || 57||
verses.meaning: Just as gold is purified by repeated heating and beating, so too, the impurities of the mind are quickly removed, and it becomes pure and free from blemish.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें निष्ठा केलें कर्म। तें झाडी करूनि रजतम। सत्त्वशुद्धीचें धाम। डोळां दावी॥ ५८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ niṣṭhā keleṃ karma| teṃ jhāḍī karūni rajatama| sattvaśuddhīceṃ dhāma| ḍoḻāṃ dāvī|| 58 ||
verses.meaning: Just as actions performed with unwavering devotion, by clearing away the qualities of Rajas and Tamas, reveal the abode of pure Sattva to the inner eye.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनियां धनंजया । सत्त्वशुद्धी गिंवसितया। तीर्थांचिया सावाया। आलीं कर्मे ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauniyāṃ dhanaṃjayā | sattvaśuddhī giṃvasitayā| tīrthāṃciyā sāvāyā| ālīṃ karme || 59||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, actions (karma) have come to the aid of pilgrimages (tirthas) in their quest for purity of being (sattva-shuddhi).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तीर्थे बाह्ममळु क्षाळे। कर्मे अभ्यंतर उजळे। एवं तीर्थे जाण निर्मळें। सत्कर्मेचि ॥ १६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tīrthe bāhmamaḻu kṣāḻe| karme abhyaṃtara ujaḻe| evaṃ tīrthe jāṇa nirmaḻeṃ| satkarmeci || 160||
verses.meaning: Pilgrimages cleanse external impurities, while good deeds purify the inner self. Thus, know that pilgrimages are truly pure when accompanied by virtuous actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तृषार्ता मरुदेशीं। झळे अमृते बोळलीं जेसीं। कीं अंधालागीं डोळ्यांसीं । सूर्य आला ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tṛṣārtā marudeśīṃ| jhaḻe amṛte boḻalīṃ jesīṃ| kīṃ aṃdhālāgīṃ ḍoḻyāṃsīṃ | sūrya ālā || 61||
verses.meaning: As if nectar were poured upon a thirsty person in a desert, or as if the sun rose for the blind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बुडतया नदीच धाविन्निली । 'पडतया पृथ्वीच कळवळिली । निमतया मृत्यूने दिधली । आयुष्यवृष्धी ॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: buḍatayā nadīca dhāvinnilī | 'paḍatayā pṛthvīca kaḻavaḻilī | nimatayā mṛtyūne didhalī | āyuṣyavṛṣdhī ||62||
verses.meaning: The drowning river was made to flow, the falling earth was steadied, and from the dying death, life's growth was bestowed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ४२८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी तैसें कर्मे कर्मबद्धता। मुमुक्षु सोडविले पंडुसुता । जैसा रसरीति मरतां। राखिला विषें॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: 428 śrījñāneśvarī taiseṃ karme karmabaddhatā| mumukṣu soḍavile paṃḍusutā | jaisā rasarīti maratāṃ| rākhilā viṣeṃ|| 63||
verses.meaning: Just as a dying person is saved by a physician's skill, so too, O son of Pandu, are seekers of liberation freed from the bondage of karma by karma itself, when performed without attachment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी एके हातवटिया। कर्मे कौजती धनंजया । बंधकेंचि सोडवावया । मुख्यें होती ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī eke hātavaṭiyā| karme kaujatī dhanaṃjayā | baṃdhakeṃci soḍavāvayā | mukhyeṃ hotī || 64||
verses.meaning: Just as with a particular skill, actions, O Dhananjaya, become the primary means to liberate one from bondage.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां तेचि हातवटी । तुज सांगों गोमटी । जया कर्मातें किरीटी। कर्मचि रुसे॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ teci hātavaṭī | tuja sāṃgoṃ gomaṭī | jayā karmāteṃ kirīṭī| karmaci ruse|| 65||
verses.meaning: Now, Arjuna, I will tell you that excellent technique by which karma itself becomes displeased with karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी महायागप्रमुखें। कर्मे निफजतांही अचुकें । कर्तेपणाचें न ठाके । फुंजणें आंगीं ॥६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī mahāyāgapramukheṃ| karme niphajatāṃhī acukeṃ | kartepaṇāceṃ na ṭhāke | phuṃjaṇeṃ āṃgīṃ ||66||
verses.meaning: Even when great sacrifices and actions are performed flawlessly, the pride of doership does not cling to the self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो मोलें तीर्था जाये। तया मी यात्रा करितु आहें । ऐसिये शलाघ्यतेचा नोहे। तोषु जेवीं ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo moleṃ tīrthā jāye| tayā mī yātrā karitu āheṃ | aisiye śalāghyatecā nohe| toṣu jevīṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: Just as a person who goes on a pilgrimage for a price does not experience the joy of such a praiseworthy act.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का मुद्रा समर्थाचिया। जो एकवट झोंबे राया। तो मी जिणता ऐसिया। न येचि गर्वा॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā mudrā samarthāciyā| jo ekavaṭa jhoṃbe rāyā| to mī jiṇatā aisiyā| na yeci garvā|| 68||
verses.meaning: Just as a seal is affixed by a powerful ruler, and whoever dares to challenge such a king is defeated, I, the victor, do not succumb to pride.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो कांसे 'लागोनि तरे। तया पोहती उर्मी नुरे। पुरोहितु नाविष्करे। दातेपणें ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo kāṃse 'lāgoni tare| tayā pohatī urmī nure| purohitu nāviṣkare| dātepaṇeṃ || 69||
verses.meaning: One who clings to a raft to cross, does not need to swim through the waves. Similarly, a priest does not need to display his generosity.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें कर्तृत्व अहंकारें। नेघोनि यथा अवसरें। कृत्यजातांचें मोहरें। सारीजती ॥ १७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ kartṛtva ahaṃkāreṃ| neghoni yathā avasareṃ| kṛtyajātāṃceṃ mohareṃ| sārījatī || 170||
verses.meaning: Just as actions, when performed without ego and at the appropriate time, lead to the completion of all tasks.

verses.shloka_devanagari: केल्या कर्मा पांडवा। जो आथी फळाचा यावा । तया मोहरा हों नेदावा । मनोरथु ॥७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kelyā karmā pāṃḍavā| jo āthī phaḻācā yāvā | tayā moharā hoṃ nedāvā | manorathu ||71||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, do not let the desire for the fruits of your actions become the primary motivation for your endeavors.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधींचि फळीं आस तुटिया। कर्मे आरंभावीं धनंजया । परावें बाळ धाया। पाहिजे जैसें ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhīṃci phaḻīṃ āsa tuṭiyā| karme āraṃbhāvīṃ dhanaṃjayā | parāveṃ bāḻa dhāyā| pāhije jaiseṃ || 72||
verses.meaning: Just as a foster child needs to be nurtured, so too, O Dhananjaya, should actions be initiated, even if the initial desire for them is broken.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पिंपरुवांचिया आशा । न शिंपिजे पिंपळु जैसा । तैसिया फळनिराशा । कौजती कर्मे ॥७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: piṃparuvāṃciyā āśā | na śiṃpije piṃpaḻu jaisā | taisiyā phaḻanirāśā | kaujatī karme ||73||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not water a peepal tree in the hope of pipal berries, so too, actions performed without expectation of fruit do not bind one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांडूनि दुधाची टकळी । गोंबारी गांबधेनु वेंटाळी । किंबहुना कर्मफळीं । तैसें कौजे॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃḍūni dudhācī ṭakaḻī | goṃbārī gāṃbadhenu veṃṭāḻī | kiṃbahunā karmaphaḻīṃ | taiseṃ kauje|| 74||
verses.meaning: Just as a cow, abandoning the milk-giving udder, chases after the afterbirth, so too do people, forsaking the true spiritual path, pursue the fruits of their actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी हे हातवटी। घेऊनि जे क्रिया उठी। आपुलिया आपण गांठी । लाहेचि तो॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī he hātavaṭī| gheūni je kriyā uṭhī| āpuliyā āpaṇa gāṃṭhī | lāheci to|| 75||
verses.meaning: Thus, the action that arises with such skillfulness, through its own accord, attains its goal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि फळीं लागु । सांडोनी देहसंगु। कर्मे करावीं हा चांगु । निरोपु माझा ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni phaḻīṃ lāgu | sāṃḍonī dehasaṃgu| karme karāvīṃ hā cāṃgu | niropu mājhā || 76||
verses.meaning: Therefore, abandoning attachment to the fruits of action and the identification with the body, perform your duties. This is my excellent instruction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो जीव बंधें शिणला । सुटके जाचे आपला । तेणें पुढतपुढतीं या बोला । आन न कोजे॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo jīva baṃdheṃ śiṇalā | suṭake jāce āpalā | teṇeṃ puḍhatapuḍhatīṃ yā bolā | āna na koje|| 77||
verses.meaning: The soul that is weary of bondage, and whose own liberation is desired, should repeatedly listen to these words, and not seek anything else.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी आंधाराचेनि रोखें। जैसीं डोळां रोंबिजती नखें। तैसा कर्मद्वेषें अशेखें। कर्मेचि सांडी ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī āṃdhārāceni rokheṃ| jaisīṃ ḍoḻāṃ roṃbijatī nakheṃ| taisā karmadveṣeṃ aśekheṃ| karmeci sāṃḍī || 78||
verses.meaning: Just as darkness causes one to rub their eyes, so too does aversion to action lead to the abandonment of all actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचें जें कर्म सांडणें। तें तामस पैं मी म्हणें । शिसाराचे रागें लोटणें। शिरचि जैसें ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāceṃ jeṃ karma sāṃḍaṇeṃ| teṃ tāmasa paiṃ mī mhaṇeṃ | śisārāce rāgeṃ loṭaṇeṃ| śiraci jaiseṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: To abandon one's duty, that I call Tamasic (ignorant, dull). It is like cutting off one's own head in a fit of anger.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हां गा मार्गु दुबाडु होये । तरी निस्तरितीळ पाये। कीं तेचि खांडणें आहे। मार्गापराधें ॥ ९८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃ gā mārgu dubāḍu hoye | tarī nistaritīḻa pāye| kīṃ teci khāṃḍaṇeṃ āhe| mārgāparādheṃ || 980||
verses.meaning: If the path becomes difficult, the feet will still cross it. Or, is it that the path itself is cut off due to offenses against it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: भुकेलियापुढें अन्न। हो कां भलतेसें उन्ह। तरी बुद्धी न घेतां लंघन । भाणें पापरां हल्या॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhukeliyāpuḍheṃ anna| ho kāṃ bhalateseṃ unha| tarī buddhī na ghetāṃ laṃghana | bhāṇeṃ pāparāṃ halyā|| 81||
verses.meaning: When a hungry person is presented with food, no matter how hot it is, they do not think of fasting but rather devour the meal with great eagerness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कर्माचा बाधु कर्मे । निस्तरिजे करितेनि वर्मे । हें तामसु नेणें भ्रमें। माजविला ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā karmācā bādhu karme | nistarije kariteni varme | heṃ tāmasu neṇeṃ bhrameṃ| mājavilā || 82||
verses.meaning: Just as the entanglement of karma is overcome by performing actions skillfully, the ignorant, deluded by their own confusion, do not understand this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं स्वभावें आलें विभागा । तें कर्मचि बोसंडी पैं गा। परी झणें आतळा त्यागा। तामसा तया॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ svabhāveṃ āleṃ vibhāgā | teṃ karmaci bosaṃḍī paiṃ gā| parī jhaṇeṃ ātaḻā tyāgā| tāmasā tayā|| 83||
verses.meaning: Or, if division comes naturally, that is indeed action that binds. But do not fall into that tamasic renunciation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा स्वाधिकारु बुझे। आपलें विहितही सुजे। परी करितया उमजे। निबरपणा॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā svādhikāru bujhe| āpaleṃ vihitahī suje| parī karitayā umaje| nibarapaṇā|| 84||
verses.meaning: Or, one understands their own authority, and their prescribed duties become clear, yet the doer perceives only stubbornness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे कर्माची ऐली कड । नावेक दिसे दुवाड। जे वाहतिये वेळे जड । शिदोरी जैसी॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: je karmācī ailī kaḍa | nāveka dise duvāḍa| je vāhatiye veḻe jaḍa | śidorī jaisī|| 85||
verses.meaning: That which is on the other side of action, appears difficult for a moment, like a heavy provision during the journey.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा निंब जिभे कडवटु । हिरडा पहिलें तुरटु। तैसा कर्मा ऐल शेवटु। खणुवाळा होय ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā niṃba jibhe kaḍavaṭu | hiraḍā pahileṃ turaṭu| taisā karmā aila śevaṭu| khaṇuvāḻā hoya || 86||
verses.meaning: Just as the neem is bitter to the tongue, and the haritaki is astringent at first, so too is the initial and final stage of action (karma) difficult.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां धेनु दुवाड शिंग। शेवंतीये अडवब आंग। भोजनसुख महाग। पाकु करितां॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ dhenu duvāḍa śiṃga| śevaṃtīye aḍavaba āṃga| bhojanasukha mahāga| pāku karitāṃ|| 87||
verses.meaning: Just as a cow with unruly horns, or a thorny plant like the Shevanti, makes the joy of eating difficult for the cook.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें पुढतपुढती कर्म। आरंभींच अति विषम। म्हणौनि तो तें श्रम। करितां मानी॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ puḍhatapuḍhatī karma| āraṃbhīṃca ati viṣama| mhaṇauni to teṃ śrama| karitāṃ mānī|| 88||
verses.meaning: Similarly, actions that are repeatedly undertaken are extremely difficult in the beginning. Therefore, one considers them to be toilsome.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं बिहितत्वें मांडी। परी घालितां असुरवाडीं । तेथ 'पोळला ऐसा सांडी । आदरिलेंही ॥८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ bihitatveṃ māṃḍī| parī ghālitāṃ asuravāḍīṃ | tetha 'poḻalā aisā sāṃḍī | ādarileṃhī ||89||
verses.meaning: Ordinarily, he establishes the principle of fear, but when he enters the abode of demons, he abandons even that which he has begun, as if burned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे वस्तु देहासारिखी। आली बहुतीं भाग्यविशेखीं। मा जाचूं कां कर्मादिकों। पापिया जैसा॥ १९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe vastu dehāsārikhī| ālī bahutīṃ bhāgyaviśekhīṃ| mā jācūṃ kāṃ karmādikoṃ| pāpiyā jaisā|| 190||
verses.meaning: The self is like the body, attained through great fortune. Why then should it be tormented by karma and the like, like a sinner?

verses.shloka_devanagari: केलें कर्मी जें द्यावें। तें झणें मज होआवें। आजि भोगूं ना कां बरवे । हातींचे भोग॥ ९१। ऐसा शरीराचिया क्लेशा-। भेणें कर्मे बीरेशा। सांडी तो परियेसा । राजसु त्यागु॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: keleṃ karmī jeṃ dyāveṃ| teṃ jhaṇeṃ maja hoāveṃ| āji bhogūṃ nā kāṃ barave | hātīṃce bhoga|| 91| aisā śarīrāciyā kleśā-| bheṇeṃ karme bīreśā| sāṃḍī to pariyesā | rājasu tyāgu|| 92||
verses.meaning: Whatever deeds are done, let them befall me. Why not enjoy the fruits of my actions today? One who abandons actions out of fear of bodily suffering, O Virusha, know that to be a Rajasic renunciation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं तेथही कर्म सांडे। परी तया त्यागफळ न जोडे । जैसें उतलें आगीं पडे। तें नलगेचि होमा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ tethahī karma sāṃḍe| parī tayā tyāgaphaḻa na joḍe | jaiseṃ utaleṃ āgīṃ paḍe| teṃ nalageci homā|| 93||
verses.meaning: Even there, actions cease, but the fruit of renunciation is not attained. Just as something overflowing falls into the fire, it is not considered an offering.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां बुडोनि प्राण गेळे। ते अर्धोदकीं निमाले। हें म्हणों नये जाहलें । दुर्मगरणचि ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ buḍoni prāṇa geḻe| te ardhodakīṃ nimāle| heṃ mhaṇoṃ naye jāhaleṃ | durmagaraṇaci || 94||
verses.meaning: Or, if one were to say that their life was drowned and perished halfway, this would not be right; it would be a bad death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें देहाचेनि लोभें॥ जेणें कर्मा पाणी सुभे। तेणें साच न लभे। त्यागाचें 'फळ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ dehāceni lobheṃ|| jeṇeṃ karmā pāṇī subhe| teṇeṃ sāca na labhe| tyāgāceṃ 'phaḻa|| 95||
verses.meaning: Similarly, by attachment to the body, if one performs actions with a desire for their fruits, then the true fruit of renunciation is not attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना आपुलें। जैं ज्ञान होय उदया आलें। तैं नक्षत्रातें पाहलें। गिळी जैसें ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā āpuleṃ| jaiṃ jñāna hoya udayā āleṃ| taiṃ nakṣatrāteṃ pāhaleṃ| giḻī jaiseṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: Indeed, when one's own true knowledge dawns, it swallows up the stars, just as the morning light does.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैशा सकारण क्रिया । हारपती धनंजया । तो कर्मत्यागु ये जया। मोक्षफळासी॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiśā sakāraṇa kriyā | hārapatī dhanaṃjayā | to karmatyāgu ye jayā| mokṣaphaḻāsī|| 97||
verses.meaning: Just as actions with motives, O Dhananjaya, cease to exist, so too does the renunciation of actions lead to the fruit of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें मोक्षफळ अज्ञाना । त्यागिया नाहीं अर्जुना। म्हणौनि तो त्यागु न माना। राजसु जो॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ mokṣaphaḻa ajñānā | tyāgiyā nāhīṃ arjunā| mhaṇauni to tyāgu na mānā| rājasu jo|| 98||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, the fruit of liberation is not attained by one who abandons action out of ignorance. Therefore, that abandonment, which is born of the quality of 'rajas,' is not considered true renunciation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कोणे पां एथ त्यागें । तें मोक्षफळ घर रिघे। हेंही आइक प्रसंगें। बोलिजेळ ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī koṇe pāṃ etha tyāgeṃ | teṃ mokṣaphaḻa ghara righe| heṃhī āika prasaṃgeṃ| bolijeḻa || 99||
verses.meaning: Therefore, how does the fruit of liberation enter one's home through renunciation? Listen to this as well, as it is being told in due course.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी स्वाधिकाराचेनि नांबें। जें वांटिया आलें स्वभावें। तें आचरे ४३० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी बिधिगोौरबवें । श्वृंगारोनि॥ २००॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī svādhikārāceni nāṃbeṃ| jeṃ vāṃṭiyā āleṃ svabhāveṃ| teṃ ācare 430 śrījñāneśvarī bidhigoaurabaveṃ | śvṛṃgāroni|| 200||
verses.meaning: Therefore, whatever has naturally fallen to one's lot by virtue of one's inherent right, that should be performed with due reverence, adorned with the glory of prescribed actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें मी करितु असें । ऐसा आठवु त्यजी मानसें। तैसेचि पाणी दे आशे। फळाचिये॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ mī karitu aseṃ | aisā āṭhavu tyajī mānaseṃ| taiseci pāṇī de āśe| phaḻāciye|| 19||
verses.meaning: But discard from your mind the thought, "I am the doer." Similarly, abandon the desire for the fruits of your actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं अवज्ञा आणि कामना । मातेच्या ठायीं अर्जुना । केलिया दोनी पतना। कारण होती॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ avajñā āṇi kāmanā | mātecyā ṭhāyīṃ arjunā | keliyā donī patanā| kāraṇa hotī|| 2||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, disrespect and desire directed towards one's mother, both lead to downfall.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी दोनीं यें त्यजावीं। मग माताचि ते भजावी । वांचूनि मुखालागीं वाळावी । गायचि सगळी ॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī donīṃ yeṃ tyajāvīṃ| maga mātāci te bhajāvī | vāṃcūni mukhālāgīṃ vāḻāvī | gāyaci sagaḻī || 3||
verses.meaning: Therefore, both should be abandoned. Then, one should worship only the mother (cow). Otherwise, for the sake of the mouth, the entire cow would be wasted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आवडतिये फळीं। असारें साली आंठोळी । त्यासाठीं अवगळी । फळातें कोण्ही॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āvaḍatiye phaḻīṃ| asāreṃ sālī āṃṭhoḻī | tyāsāṭhīṃ avagaḻī | phaḻāteṃ koṇhī|| 4||
verses.meaning: When a fruit is liked, who would discard the entire fruit just because of its unpalatable skin and seed?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कर्तृत्वाचा मदु। आणि कर्मफळाचा आस्वादु । या दोहींचें नांव बंधु। कर्माचा कौं॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā kartṛtvācā madu| āṇi karmaphaḻācā āsvādu | yā dohīṃceṃ nāṃva baṃdhu| karmācā kauṃ|| 5||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the pride of doership and the enjoyment of the fruits of action—these two are indeed the bondage of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी या दोहींच्या विखीं। जैसा बापु नातळे लेकी । तैसा हों न शके दुःखी। विहिता क्रिया॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī yā dohīṃcyā vikhīṃ| jaisā bāpu nātaḻe lekī | taisā hoṃ na śake duḥkhī| vihitā kriyā||6||
verses.meaning: Just as a father does not touch his daughter in these two respects (desire and anger), so too, the prescribed actions (duties) do not cause sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा तो त्यागतरुवरु। जो गा मोक्षफळें ये थोरु । सात्त्विक ऐसा डगरु । यासींच जगीं॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā to tyāgataruvaru| jo gā mokṣaphaḻeṃ ye thoru | sāttvika aisā ḍagaru | yāsīṃca jagīṃ|| 7||
verses.meaning: This is that tree of renunciation, which bears the great fruit of liberation. Such a sattvic (pure) and firm foundation is indeed this in the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां जाळूनि बीज जैसें। झाडा कीजे निर्वशें। फळ त्यागूनि कर्म तैसें। त्यजिलें जेणें ॥ ८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ jāḻūni bīja jaiseṃ| jhāḍā kīje nirvaśeṃ| phaḻa tyāgūni karma taiseṃ| tyajileṃ jeṇeṃ || 8 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a seed, once burnt, renders the tree barren, so too are actions renounced by one who has given up their fruits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लोह ळागतखेंबो परिसीं । धातूची गंधिकाळिमा जैसी । जाती रजतमें तैसीं। तुटली दोन्ही ॥ ९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: loha ḻāgatakheṃbo parisīṃ | dhātūcī gaṃdhikāḻimā jaisī | jātī rajatameṃ taisīṃ| tuṭalī donhī || 9 ||
verses.meaning: Just as iron, when it touches the philosopher's stone, loses its metallic impurities, so too do the qualities of Rajas and Tamas disappear, both being severed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सत्त्वें चोखाळे । उघडती आत्मबोधाचे डोळे । तेथ मृगांबु सांजवेळे। होय जैसें॥ २१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sattveṃ cokhāḻe | ughaḍatī ātmabodhāce ḍoḻe | tetha mṛgāṃbu sāṃjaveḻe| hoya jaiseṃ|| 210||
verses.meaning: Then, purified by Sattva, the eyes of self-realization open, and the illusion of the mirage at dusk vanishes, just as it would.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा बुद्धयादिकांपुढां। असतु विश्वाभासु हा येवढा। तो न देखे कवणीकडां। आकाश जेसें॥११॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā buddhayādikāṃpuḍhāṃ| asatu viśvābhāsu hā yevaḍhā| to na dekhe kavaṇīkaḍāṃ| ākāśa jeseṃ||11||
verses.meaning: Just as the vast universe appears before the intellect and other faculties, yet it does not perceive the all-pervading space, so too is the nature of reality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि प्राचीनाचेनि बळें । अलंकृतें कुशलाकुशलें। तियें व्योमाआंगी आभाळें। जिरालीं जैसीं ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni prācīnāceni baḻeṃ | alaṃkṛteṃ kuśalākuśaleṃ| tiyeṃ vyomāāṃgī ābhāḻeṃ| jirālīṃ jaisīṃ || 12||
verses.meaning: Therefore, by the power of the ancient, the adorned skillful and unskillful, they dissolved into the body of the sky, just like clouds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं तयाचिये दिठी। कर्मे चोखाळलीं किरीटी। म्हणौनि सुखदुःखीं उठी। पडेना तो॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ tayāciye diṭhī| karme cokhāḻalīṃ kirīṭī| mhaṇauni sukhaduḥkhīṃ uṭhī| paḍenā to|| 13||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, for such a person, actions are purified by their very sight. Therefore, they are not affected by joy or sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें शुभकर्म जाणावें । मग तें हर्षे करावें। का अशुभालागीं होआवें। हवेषिया ना॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ śubhakarma jāṇāveṃ | maga teṃ harṣe karāveṃ| kā aśubhālāgīṃ hoāveṃ| haveṣiyā nā|| 14||
verses.meaning: Therefore, know what is a good deed, then perform it with joy. Or, should one desire to commit an evil act, do not even harbor the slightest inclination towards it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी इयाविषयींचा कांहीं । तया एकुही संदेहो नाहीं । जैसा स्वप्नाच्या ठायीं । जागिन्नलिया॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī iyāviṣayīṃcā kāṃhīṃ | tayā ekuhī saṃdeho nāhīṃ | jaisā svapnācyā ṭhāyīṃ | jāginnaliyā|| 15||
verses.meaning: Therefore, regarding this, there is not even a single doubt for him, just as when one awakens from a dream.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि कर्म आणि कर्ता । या द्वैतभावाची वार्ता । नेणें तो पंडुसुता । सात्त्विक त्यागु ( त्यागी )॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni karma āṇi kartā | yā dvaitabhāvācī vārtā | neṇeṃ to paṃḍusutā | sāttvika tyāgu ( tyāgī )|| 16||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O son of Pandu, one who knows nothing of the duality of action and doer, that renunciation is considered sattvic.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि कर्मे पार्था । त्यजिलीं त्यजिती सर्वथा । अधिकें बांधिती अन्यथा । सांडिलीं तरी ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni karme pārthā | tyajilīṃ tyajitī sarvathā | adhikeṃ bāṃdhitī anyathā | sāṃḍilīṃ tarī || 17||
verses.meaning: O Partha, those who abandon such actions, or intend to abandon them completely, are bound even more tightly if they are forsaken incorrectly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हां गा सव्यसाची । मूर्ति लाहोनि देहाची । खंती करिती कर्माची । ते गांवढे गा॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi hāṃ gā savyasācī | mūrti lāhoni dehācī | khaṃtī karitī karmācī | te gāṃvaḍhe gā|| 18||
verses.meaning: Oh Arjuna, those who, having attained a human body, lament about performing actions, are indeed ignorant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मृत्तिकेचा वीटु। घेऊनि काय करील घटु। केउता ताथु पटु। सांडील तो॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mṛttikecā vīṭu| gheūni kāya karīla ghaṭu| keutā tāthu paṭu| sāṃḍīla to|| 19||
verses.meaning: What can a pot, made of clay, do to the clay itself? How can it abandon its very essence?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि वन्हित्व आंगी । आणि उबे उबगणें आगी । कीं तो दीपु प्रभेलागीं । द्वेषु करील काई ॥ २२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci vanhitva āṃgī | āṇi ube ubagaṇeṃ āgī | kīṃ to dīpu prabhelāgīṃ | dveṣu karīla kāī || 220||
verses.meaning: Just as fire inherently possesses the quality of burning, and heat is not averse to fire, would a lamp ever despise its own light?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हिंगु त्रासिला घाणी । तरी कैचें सुगंधत्व आणी । द्रवपण सांडूनि पाणी। कें राहे तें॥२१॥
verses.shloka_iast: hiṃgu trāsilā ghāṇī | tarī kaiceṃ sugaṃdhatva āṇī | dravapaṇa sāṃḍūni pāṇī| keṃ rāhe teṃ||21||
verses.meaning: If asafoetida is troubled by its smell, how can it acquire fragrance? Or if water abandons its fluidity, how can it remain water?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा शरीराचेनि आभासें। नांदतु जंब असे। तंब कर्मत्यागाचें पिसें। काइसें तरी॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā śarīrāceni ābhāseṃ| nāṃdatu jaṃba ase| taṃba karmatyāgāceṃ piseṃ| kāiseṃ tarī|| 22||
verses.meaning: Just as the soul, residing within the illusion of the body, continues to exist, so too does the madness of renouncing actions persist, in some form or another.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपण लाविजे टिळा । म्हणौनि पुसों ये वेळोवेळा । मा घाली फेडी निडळा। कां करूं्ये गा॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaṇa lāvije ṭiḻā | mhaṇauni pusoṃ ye veḻoveḻā | mā ghālī pheḍī niḍaḻā| kāṃ karūṃye gā|| 23||
verses.meaning: You apply the tilak yourself, so why do you repeatedly ask about the auspicious time? Why do you then rub it off your forehead?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें विहित स्वयें आदरिलें। म्हणौनि त्यजूं ये त्यजिलें। परी कर्मच देह आतलें। तें कां सांडील गा॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ vihita svayeṃ ādarileṃ| mhaṇauni tyajūṃ ye tyajileṃ| parī karmaca deha ātaleṃ| teṃ kāṃ sāṃḍīla gā|| 24||
verses.meaning: Thus, what is prescribed is undertaken by oneself; therefore, what can be abandoned is abandoned. But how can the actions inherent in the body be forsaken?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें इवासोच्छासवरी । होत निजेलियाहीवरी। कांहीं न करणेंयाचि परी। होती जयाची ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ ivāsocchāsavarī | hota nijeliyāhīvarī| kāṃhīṃ na karaṇeṃyāci parī| hotī jayācī || 25||
verses.meaning: Even during deep sleep, when no action is performed, the breath continues its natural rhythm. This is the nature of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या शरीराचेनि मिसकें। कर्मचि लागलें असिकें। जितां मेलया न ठाके । इया रीती॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā śarīrāceni misakeṃ| karmaci lāgaleṃ asikeṃ| jitāṃ melayā na ṭhāke | iyā rītī|| 26||
verses.meaning: Through the pretext of this body, karma has become so deeply ingrained that it does not leave, whether one is alive or dead, in this manner.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया कर्मातें सांडिती परी। एकीचि ते अवधारीं। जे करितां न जाइजे हारी। फळाशेचिये ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā karmāteṃ sāṃḍitī parī| ekīci te avadhārīṃ| je karitāṃ na jāije hārī| phaḻāśeciye || 27||
verses.meaning: But there is one kind of action, listen, by which one does not fall into the trap of desiring the fruits of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कर्मफळ ईश्‍वरीं अर्पे। तत्प्रसादें बोधु उहीपे। तेथ रजुज्ञानें लोपे। व्याळशंका॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: karmaphaḻa īś‍varīṃ arpe| tatprasādeṃ bodhu uhīpe| tetha rajujñāneṃ lope| vyāḻaśaṃkā|| 28||
verses.meaning: When the fruits of action are offered to God, through His grace, spiritual knowledge dawns. Then, with the light of true knowledge, the illusion of the serpent vanishes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें आत्मबोधें तैसें । अविद्येसीं कर्म नाशे । पार्था त्यजिजे जैं ऐसें। तें त्यजिलें होय॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ ātmabodheṃ taiseṃ | avidyesīṃ karma nāśe | pārthā tyajije jaiṃ aiseṃ| teṃ tyajileṃ hoya|| 29||
verses.meaning: Through that self-realization, just as ignorance is destroyed, so too are actions (karma) relinquished, O Partha. When one truly abandons them, they are indeed abandoned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि इयापरी जगीं। कर्मे करितां मानूं त्यागी । येर मूर्च्छने नांब रोगीं। विसांबा जैसा ॥ २३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni iyāparī jagīṃ| karme karitāṃ mānūṃ tyāgī | yera mūrcchane nāṃba rogīṃ| visāṃbā jaisā || 230||
verses.meaning: Therefore, in this way, performing actions in the world, consider yourself as renounced. Otherwise, it is like a sick person resting due to unconsciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कर्मी शिणे एकीं। तो विसांबों पाहे आणिकीं । दांडेयाचे घाय बुकी। धाडणें जैसें॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā karmī śiṇe ekīṃ| to visāṃboṃ pāhe āṇikīṃ | dāṃḍeyāce ghāya bukī| dhāḍaṇeṃ jaiseṃ|| 39||
verses.meaning: Just as a person exhausted by one task seeks rest in another, or as blows from a stick are countered by punches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें असो पुढती । तोचि त्यागी त्रिजगतीं । जेणें फळत्यागें निष्कृती। नेलें कर्म॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ aso puḍhatī | toci tyāgī trijagatīṃ | jeṇeṃ phaḻatyāgeṃ niṣkṛtī| neleṃ karma|| 32||
verses.meaning: But let that be. He alone is truly renounced in all three worlds, by whom action is brought to its ultimate conclusion through the renunciation of its fruits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं तरी धनंजया । त्रिविधा कर्मफळा गा यया। समर्थ ते कीं भोगावया। जे न सांडितीचि आशा॥ ३३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ tarī dhanaṃjayā | trividhā karmaphaḻā gā yayā| samartha te kīṃ bhogāvayā| je na sāṃḍitīci āśā|| 33 ||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, O Dhananjaya, only those who do not abandon hope are capable of experiencing the three types of fruits of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपणचि विऊनि दुहिता। कीं न मम म्हणे पिता। तो सुटे कौं प्रतिग्रहिता। जांबई शिरके ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaṇaci viūni duhitā| kīṃ na mama mhaṇe pitā| to suṭe kauṃ pratigrahitā| jāṃbaī śirake || 34||
verses.meaning: When a father gives birth to a daughter, he does not say, 'She is not mine.' How then can the son-in-law, who receives her, be considered separate?

verses.shloka_devanagari: विषाचे आगरही वाहती । ते विकितां सुखें लाभें जिती । येर निमालें जे घेती । वेंचोनि मोलें॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: viṣāce āgarahī vāhatī | te vikitāṃ sukheṃ lābheṃ jitī | yera nimāleṃ je ghetī | veṃconi moleṃ|| 35||
verses.meaning: Even if one sells a storehouse of poison, they live happily by the profits. But those who consume it, perish, having paid the price.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें कर्ता कर्म करू। अकर्ता फळाशा न धरू । एथ न शके आवरूं। दोहींतें कर्म ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ kartā karma karū| akartā phaḻāśā na dharū | etha na śake āvarūṃ| dohīṃteṃ karma || 36||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the doer performs actions, and the non-doer does not cling to the desire for fruits. Here, action cannot restrain both.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वाटे पिकलिया रुखाचें। फळ अपेक्षी तयाचें। तेवीं साधारण कर्माचें। फळ घे तया॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṭe pikaliyā rukhāceṃ| phaḻa apekṣī tayāceṃ| tevīṃ sādhāraṇa karmāceṃ| phaḻa ghe tayā|| 37||
verses.meaning: Just as one expects fruit from a ripe tree, so too does one receive the fruit of ordinary actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी करूनि फळ ४३२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी नेघे।॥ तो जगाच्या कामीं न रिघे। जे त्रिविध जग अवघें । कर्मफळ हें ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī karūni phaḻa 432 śrījñāneśvarī neghe||| to jagācyā kāmīṃ na righe| je trividha jaga avagheṃ | karmaphaḻa heṃ || 38||
verses.meaning: But the one who does not accept the fruit of action, does not engage in the affairs of the world, for this entire threefold world is nothing but the fruit of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देव मनुष्य स्थावर। यया नांब जगडंबर। आणि हे तंब तिन्ही प्रकार । कर्मफळांचे॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: deva manuṣya sthāvara| yayā nāṃba jagaḍaṃbara| āṇi he taṃba tinhī prakāra | karmaphaḻāṃce|| 39||
verses.meaning: God, humans, and the inanimate world; these are but names for the cosmic illusion. And these three types are the results of actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंचि एक गा अनिष्ट । एक तें केवळ इष्ट । आणि एक इृष्टानिष्ट। त्रिविध ऐसें ॥ २४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃci eka gā aniṣṭa | eka teṃ kevaḻa iṣṭa | āṇi eka iṛṣṭāniṣṭa| trividha aiseṃ || 240||
verses.meaning: One is indeed inauspicious, one is purely auspicious, and one is both auspicious and inauspicious; thus, there are these three kinds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी विषयमंतीं बुद्धी। आंगीं सूनि अविधी । प्रवर्तती जे निषिद्धीं। कुव्यापारीं ॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī viṣayamaṃtīṃ buddhī| āṃgīṃ sūni avidhī | pravartatī je niṣiddhīṃ| kuvyāpārīṃ || 41||
verses.meaning: But those whose intellect is steeped in worldly pleasures, and who, by their very nature, engage in forbidden and evil deeds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ कृमि कौट लोष्ट। हे देह लाहती निकृष्ट। तया नाम तें अनिष्ट । कर्मफळ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha kṛmi kauṭa loṣṭa| he deha lāhatī nikṛṣṭa| tayā nāma teṃ aniṣṭa | karmaphaḻa|| 42||
verses.meaning: There, worms, insects, and clods of earth—these obtain a degraded body. That is called the inauspicious fruit of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां स्वधर्मा मानु देतां। स्वाधिकारु पुढां सूतां। सुकृत कौजे पुसतां। आम्नायातें ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ svadharmā mānu detāṃ| svādhikāru puḍhāṃ sūtāṃ| sukṛta kauje pusatāṃ| āmnāyāteṃ || 43||
verses.meaning: Or, by giving respect to one's own dharma, and by placing one's own authority forward, good deeds inquire of the Vedas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें इंद्रादिक देवांचीं । देहे लाहिजती सव्यसाची । तया कर्मफळा डइृष्टाची । प्रसिद्धि गा॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ iṃdrādika devāṃcīṃ | dehe lāhijatī savyasācī | tayā karmaphaḻā ḍaiṛṣṭācī | prasiddhi gā|| 44||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, even the bodies of gods like Indra are attained through the visible fruits of their actions; this is well-known.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि गोड आंबट मिळे । तेथ रसांतर फरसाळें । उठी दोहीं वेगळें । दोहीं जिणतें ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi goḍa āṃbaṭa miḻe | tetha rasāṃtara pharasāḻeṃ | uṭhī dohīṃ vegaḻeṃ | dohīṃ jiṇateṃ || 45 ||
verses.meaning: And where sweet and sour meet, a different taste emerges, distinct from both, yet overcoming both.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रेचकुचि योगवशें। होय स्तंभावयादोषें । तेवीं सत्यासत्य समरसें। सत्यासत्यच् जिणिजे॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: recakuci yogavaśeṃ| hoya staṃbhāvayādoṣeṃ | tevīṃ satyāsatya samaraseṃ| satyāsatyac jiṇije|| 46||
verses.meaning: Just as a yogi's breath control (rechaka) can temporarily suspend the body's natural functions, so too is truth (satya) and untruth (asatya) overcome by their very essence, becoming one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि समभागें शुभाशुभें। मिळोनि अनुष्ठानाचें उभें । तेणें मनुष्यत्व लाभे। तें मिश्र 'फळ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni samabhāgeṃ śubhāśubheṃ| miḻoni anuṣṭhānāceṃ ubheṃ | teṇeṃ manuṣyatva lābhe| teṃ miśra 'phaḻa|| 47||
verses.meaning: Therefore, when good and bad deeds are performed in equal measure, the resulting human birth is a mixed fruit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें त्रिविध यया भागीं। कर्मफळ मांडलेंसे जगीं। हें न सांडी तयां भोगीं। जें सूदळे आशा ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ trividha yayā bhāgīṃ| karmaphaḻa māṃḍaleṃse jagīṃ| heṃ na sāṃḍī tayāṃ bhogīṃ| jeṃ sūdaḻe āśā || 48||
verses.meaning: Thus, in this world, the three-fold fruit of action is established. Those who do not abandon it, but rather cling to it with hope, experience its consequences.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथें जिव्हेचा हातु फांटे। तंव जेवितां वाटे गोमटें। परि परिणामीं शेवटें । अवश्य मरण ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetheṃ jivhecā hātu phāṃṭe| taṃva jevitāṃ vāṭe gomaṭeṃ| pari pariṇāmīṃ śevaṭeṃ | avaśya maraṇa || 49||
verses.meaning: Where the tongue's hand branches out, it feels good while eating, but in the end, death is certain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संवचोरमैत्री चांग । जंब न पविजे तें दांग। सामान्या भली आंग। न शिवे तंव॥ २५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃvacoramaitrī cāṃga | jaṃba na pavije teṃ dāṃga| sāmānyā bhalī āṃga| na śive taṃva|| 250||
verses.meaning: Friendship with a wicked person is good only as long as one does not encounter their true nature. It is best not to associate with such a person at all.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं कर्मे करितां शरीरीं । लाहती महत्त्वाची फरारी । पाठीं निधनीं एकसरी। पावती फळें ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ karme karitāṃ śarīrīṃ | lāhatī mahattvācī pharārī | pāṭhīṃ nidhanīṃ ekasarī| pāvatī phaḻeṃ || 51||
verses.meaning: Similarly, those who perform actions in the body attain great importance, and later, at the time of their death, they receive the fruits of their deeds all at once.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा समर्थ आणि क्रणिया। मागों आला बाइणिया। न लोटे तैसा प्राणिया। पडे तो भोगु ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā samartha āṇi kraṇiyā| māgoṃ ālā bāiṇiyā| na loṭe taisā prāṇiyā| paḍe to bhogu || 52||
verses.meaning: Just as a powerful and capable person, when asked for something, cannot refuse, so too a living being cannot escape the consequences of their actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग कणिसौनि कणु झडे । तो विरूढळा कणिसा चढे। पुढती भूमी पडे। पुढती उठी॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga kaṇisauni kaṇu jhaḍe | to virūḍhaḻā kaṇisā caḍhe| puḍhatī bhūmī paḍe| puḍhatī uṭhī|| 53||
