verses.meaning: Then, a grain falls from the ear of corn. It sprouts and grows back onto the ear. Again it falls to the ground. Again it rises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें भोगीं जें फळ होय। तें फळांतरें बीत जाय । चालतां पावो पाय। जिणिजे जैसा॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ bhogīṃ jeṃ phaḻa hoya| teṃ phaḻāṃtareṃ bīta jāya | cālatāṃ pāvo pāya| jiṇije jaisā|| 54||
verses.meaning: Just as the fruit of enjoyment is consumed by other fruits, so too is the foot overcome by walking.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उताराचिये सांगडी । ठाके ते ऐलीच थडी। तेवीं न मुकिंजती बोढी। भोग्याचिये ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: utārāciye sāṃgaḍī | ṭhāke te ailīca thaḍī| tevīṃ na mukiṃjatī boḍhī| bhogyāciye || 55||
verses.meaning: Just as a raft, having crossed the river, is not abandoned on the other shore, so too, the pleasures of the senses are not forsaken.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं साध्यसाधनप्रकारें। फळभोगु तो पसरे। एवं गोंबिले संसारें। अत्यागी ते॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ sādhyasādhanaprakāreṃ| phaḻabhogu to pasare| evaṃ goṃbile saṃsāreṃ| atyāgī te|| 56||
verses.meaning: Thus, those who are attached to the world remain entangled in the cycle of worldly existence, experiencing the fruits of their actions, whether they are means or ends.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱहवी जाईचियां फुलां फांकणें। त्याचि नाम जैसें सुकणें। तैसें कर्ममिषें न करणें। केलें जिहीं ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟahavī jāīciyāṃ phulāṃ phāṃkaṇeṃ| tyāci nāma jaiseṃ sukaṇeṃ| taiseṃ karmamiṣeṃ na karaṇeṃ| keleṃ jihīṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: Just as the jasmine flower, once it blossoms, is destined to wither, so too are those actions that are performed under the guise of non-action, or those who claim to have performed actions while truly doing nothing.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बीजचि वबरोसि वेंचे। तेथ वाढती कुळवाडी खांचे। तेवीं फळत्यागें कर्माचें। सारिलें 'काम॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: bījaci vabarosi veṃce| tetha vāḍhatī kuḻavāḍī khāṃce| tevīṃ phaḻatyāgeṃ karmāceṃ| sārileṃ 'kāma|| 58||
verses.meaning: Just as a seed, when sown, grows into a field of crops, so too, by renouncing the fruit of actions, one conquers desire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते सत्त्वशुद्धी साहाकारें। गुरुकृपामृततुषारें। सासिन्नलेनि बोधें बोसरे। द्वैतदैन्य ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: te sattvaśuddhī sāhākāreṃ| gurukṛpāmṛtatuṣāreṃ| sāsinnaleni bodheṃ bosare| dvaitadainya || 59||
verses.meaning: With the aid of purity of sattva (goodness), and the dew-like drops of the Guru's grace, the misery of duality is dispelled by the blossoming of spiritual knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां जगदाभासमिषें । स्फुरे तें त्रिविध फळ नाशे। येथ भोक्ता भोग्य आपैसें। निमालें हें ॥ २६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ jagadābhāsamiṣeṃ | sphure teṃ trividha phaḻa nāśe| yetha bhoktā bhogya āpaiseṃ| nimāleṃ heṃ || 260||
verses.meaning: Then, the three-fold fruit, which appears as the illusion of the world, perishes. Here, the enjoyer and the enjoyed naturally cease to exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: घडे ज्ञानप्रधानु हा ऐसा । संन्यासु जयां वीरेशा । तेचि फळभोगसोसा । मुकले गा ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ghaḍe jñānapradhānu hā aisā | saṃnyāsu jayāṃ vīreśā | teci phaḻabhogasosā | mukale gā || 61||
verses.meaning: Such a renunciate, whose renunciation is knowledge-based, is freed from the experience of the fruits of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि येणें कौर संन्यासें। जें आत्मरूपीं दिठी पैसे। तें कर्म एक ऐसें। देखणें आहे॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi yeṇeṃ kaura saṃnyāseṃ| jeṃ ātmarūpīṃ diṭhī paise| teṃ karma eka aiseṃ| dekhaṇeṃ āhe|| 62||
verses.meaning: And through this renunciation, that which is seen as the true self, that alone is to be understood as the one action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पडोनि गेलिया भिंती । चित्रांची केवळ होय माती । कां 'पाहाळेया राती । आंधारें उरे॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: paḍoni geliyā bhiṃtī | citrāṃcī kevaḻa hoya mātī | kāṃ 'pāhāḻeyā rātī | āṃdhāreṃ ure|| 63||
verses.meaning: When the wall collapses, the paintings on it simply turn to dust. Similarly, when the night ends, only darkness remains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैं रूपचि नाहीं उभें। तैं साउली काह्याची शोभे। दर्पणेवीण बिंबे। वदन कें पां॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiṃ rūpaci nāhīṃ ubheṃ| taiṃ sāulī kāhyācī śobhe| darpaṇevīṇa biṃbe| vadana keṃ pāṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: When there is no form, how can there be a shadow? How can a face be reflected without a mirror?

verses.shloka_devanagari: फिटलिया निद्रेचा ठाबो। कैंचा स्वप्नासि प्रस्तावो। मग साच का वावो। कोण म्हणे ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: phiṭaliyā nidrecā ṭhābo| kaiṃcā svapnāsi prastāvo| maga sāca kā vāvo| koṇa mhaṇe || 65||
verses.meaning: When the sleep is gone, how can there be any talk of dreams? Then who would say whether they were real or false?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें गा संन्यासें येणें। मूळ अविद्येसीचि नाहीं जिणें। मा तियेचें कार्य कोणें। घेपे दीजे॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ gā saṃnyāseṃ yeṇeṃ| mūḻa avidyesīci nāhīṃ jiṇeṃ| mā tiyeceṃ kārya koṇeṃ| ghepe dīje|| 66||
verses.meaning: Similarly, by this renunciation, the root ignorance itself is destroyed. Then, who would accept or give its effects?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि संन्यासींये पाहीं । कर्माची गोठी कीजेल 'काई। परी अविद्या आपुलां देहीं। आहे जैं कां॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni saṃnyāsīṃye pāhīṃ | karmācī goṭhī kījela 'kāī| parī avidyā āpulāṃ dehīṃ| āhe jaiṃ kāṃ|| 67||
verses.meaning: Therefore, what is the point of discussing actions for a renunciate? For as long as ignorance resides in one's body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैं कर्तेपणाचेनि थांबें। आत्मा शुभाशुभीं धांवे । दृष्टि भेदाचिये राणिवे । रचलीसे जें ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiṃ kartepaṇāceni thāṃbeṃ| ātmā śubhāśubhīṃ dhāṃve | dṛṣṭi bhedāciye rāṇive | racalīse jeṃ || 68||
verses.meaning: When the soul, driven by the notion of doership, rushes into good and bad actions, it is because the vision of duality has been established within it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैं तरी गा सुवर्मा । बिजावळी आत्मया कर्मा । अपाडें जैसी पश्‍चिमा । पूर्वेसि कां॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiṃ tarī gā suvarmā | bijāvaḻī ātmayā karmā | apāḍeṃ jaisī paś‍cimā | pūrvesi kāṃ||69||
verses.meaning: O good listener, just as the west cannot be compared to the east, so too the actions of the self cannot be compared to the seed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी आकाशा का आभाळा। सूर्या आणि मृगजळा। बिजावळी भूतळा। वायूसि जैसी ॥ २७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī ākāśā kā ābhāḻā| sūryā āṇi mṛgajaḻā| bijāvaḻī bhūtaḻā| vāyūsi jaisī || 270||
verses.meaning: Or just as the sky is to the clouds, the sun to the mirage, the lightning to the earth, and the wind to itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पांघरौनि नईचें उदक। असे नईचिमाजीं खडक । परी जाणसी का वेगळिक। कोडीची ते॥७१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṃgharauni naīceṃ udaka| ase naīcimājīṃ khaḍaka | parī jāṇasī kā vegaḻika| koḍīcī te||719||
verses.meaning: The water of the river covers the rock, and the rock is within the river, yet can you perceive any separation between them?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हो कां उदकाजवळी। परी सीनानीचि ते बाबुळी। काय संगास्तब काजळी । दीपु म्हणों ये ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ho kāṃ udakājavaḻī| parī sīnānīci te bābuḻī| kāya saṃgāstaba kājaḻī | dīpu mhaṇoṃ ye || 72||
verses.meaning: Just as a babul tree, though near water, remains thorny, or how soot, though near a lamp, cannot be called light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी चंद्रीं जाला कलंकु । तरी चंद्रेंसी नव्हे एकु । आहे दृष्टी डोळ्यां विवेकु । अपाडु जेतुला ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī caṃdrīṃ jālā kalaṃku | tarī caṃdreṃsī navhe eku | āhe dṛṣṭī ḍoḻyāṃ viveku | apāḍu jetulā || 73||
verses.meaning: Even if there is a blemish on the moon, it does not become one with the moon. There is a distinction in the eye of discernment, as much as is necessary.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना वाटा वाटे जातया । बोघा वबोघीं वाहतया । आरसा आरसां पाहातया । अपाडु जेतुला ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā vāṭā vāṭe jātayā | boghā vaboghīṃ vāhatayā | ārasā ārasāṃ pāhātayā | apāḍu jetulā || 74||
verses.meaning: Just as there is no difference between various paths for a traveler, or between a boat and its oarsman, or between a mirror and its reflection, so too is the oneness of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था गा तेतुलेनि मानें। आत्मेंनिसीं कर्म सिनें। परी घेवविजे अज्ञानें। तें कीर ऐसें ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā gā tetuleni māneṃ| ātmeṃnisīṃ karma sineṃ| parī ghevavije ajñāneṃ| teṃ kīra aiseṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, by that measure, the Self is not tainted by actions; but it is ignorance that makes one perceive it as such.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विकाशें रवीतें उपजवी । द्रुती अलीकरवीं भोगवी। ते सरोवरीं कां बरवी । अब्जिनी जैसी ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: vikāśeṃ ravīteṃ upajavī | drutī alīkaravīṃ bhogavī| te sarovarīṃ kāṃ baravī | abjinī jaisī || 76||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun, by its very expansion, brings forth the lotus, and then, through its swift rays, allows the bees to enjoy its nectar, so too does the lotus pond appear beautiful.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुढतपुढती आत्मक्रिया । अन्यकारणकाचि तैशिया। करूं पांचांही तयां। कारणां रूप॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: puḍhatapuḍhatī ātmakriyā | anyakāraṇakāci taiśiyā| karūṃ pāṃcāṃhī tayāṃ| kāraṇāṃ rūpa|| 77||
verses.meaning: Again and again, the Self's action, like that of an independent cause, gives form to all five of those causes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पांचही कारणें तिये । तूंही जाणसील विपायें। जे शास्त्रें _उभऊनी बाहे। बोलती तयांतें ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pāṃcahī kāraṇeṃ tiye | tūṃhī jāṇasīla vipāyeṃ| je śāstreṃ _ubhaūnī bāhe| bolatī tayāṃteṃ || 78||
verses.meaning: And you will also know those five causes, which the scriptures, raising their arms, proclaim.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वेदरायाचिया राजधानीं। सांख्यवेदांताच्या भुवनीं । निरूपणाच्या निशाणध्वनीं। गर्जती तियें ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vedarāyāciyā rājadhānīṃ| sāṃkhyavedāṃtācyā bhuvanīṃ | nirūpaṇācyā niśāṇadhvanīṃ| garjatī tiyeṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: In the capital city of the Vedas, within the palaces of Samkhya and Vedanta, they resound with the triumphant declarations of spiritual discourse.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे सर्वकर्मसिद्धीलागीं। ४३४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी इयेंचि मुद्दलें हो जगीं। येथ न सुवावा अभंगीं। आत्मराजु॥२८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: je sarvakarmasiddhīlāgīṃ| 434 śrījñāneśvarī iyeṃci muddaleṃ ho jagīṃ| yetha na suvāvā abhaṃgīṃ| ātmarāju||280||
verses.meaning: These very principles of the Shri Dnyaneshwari are the fundamental capital for the accomplishment of all actions in this world. Here, the indestructible Self-King should not be neglected.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या बोलाची डांगुरटी । तियें प्रसिद्धीचिं आली किरीटी। म्हणौनि तुझ्या हन कर्णपुटीं। बसों हें काज॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā bolācī ḍāṃguraṭī | tiyeṃ prasiddhīciṃ ālī kirīṭī| mhaṇauni tujhyā hana karṇapuṭīṃ| basoṃ heṃ kāja|| 81||
verses.meaning: The fame of these words has reached its peak, therefore, let them resonate in your ears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मुखांतरीं आइकिजे। तैसें कायसें हें ओझें। मी चिद्रलत तुझें । असतां हातीं ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mukhāṃtarīṃ āikije| taiseṃ kāyaseṃ heṃ ojheṃ| mī cidralata tujheṃ | asatāṃ hātīṃ || 82||
verses.meaning: And what is this burden, when I, your very own sentient creeper, am in your hands, to be heard through your mouth?

verses.shloka_devanagari: दर्पणु पुढां मांडलेया । कां 'लोकांचिया डोळयां। मानु द्यावा पहावया। आपुलें निकें॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: darpaṇu puḍhāṃ māṃḍaleyā | kāṃ 'lokāṃciyā ḍoḻayāṃ| mānu dyāvā pahāvayā| āpuleṃ nikeṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: Just as a mirror is placed before one, so too should one give respect to the eyes of others, to see one's own true nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भक्त जैसेनि जेथ पाहे। तेथ तें तेंचि होत जाये । तो मी तुझें जाहलो आहें।॥ खेळणें आजी ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhakta jaiseni jetha pāhe| tetha teṃ teṃci hota jāye | to mī tujheṃ jāhalo āheṃ||| kheḻaṇeṃ ājī || 84||
verses.meaning: Wherever the devotee looks, there I become that very thing. Today, I have become your plaything.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें हें प्रीतीचेनि वेगें। देवो बोलतां से नेघे। तंव आनंदामाजीं आंगें। विरतसे येरु ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ heṃ prītīceni vegeṃ| devo bolatāṃ se neghe| taṃva ānaṃdāmājīṃ āṃgeṃ| viratase yeru || 85||
verses.meaning: Such is the speed of this love, that as God speaks, the other (devotee) dissolves into bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चांदिणियाचा पडिभरु । होतां सोमकांताचा डोंगरु । विघरोनि सरोवरु । हों पाहे जैसा॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: cāṃdiṇiyācā paḍibharu | hotāṃ somakāṃtācā ḍoṃgaru | vigharoni sarovaru | hoṃ pāhe jaisā|| 86||
verses.meaning: Just as a mountain of moonstone, upon receiving the moonlight, melts and transforms into a lake.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सुख आणि अनुभूती । या भावांची मोडूनि भिंती। आतलें अर्जुनाकृती। सुखचि जेथ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sukha āṇi anubhūtī | yā bhāvāṃcī moḍūni bhiṃtī| ātaleṃ arjunākṛtī| sukhaci jetha|| 87||
verses.meaning: Just as happiness and experience, breaking down the walls of these feelings, Arjuna, there is only happiness within.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ समर्थ म्हणौनि देवा। अवकाशु जाहळा आठवा । मग बुडतयाचा धांवा। जीवें केळा॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha samartha mhaṇauni devā| avakāśu jāhaḻā āṭhavā | maga buḍatayācā dhāṃvā| jīveṃ keḻā|| 88||
verses.meaning: Then, because of the Lord's omnipotence, there was a moment of remembrance. And so, He came to the rescue of the drowning soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना येसणें धेंडें। प्रज्ञा पसरेंसीं बुडे। आलें भरतें एवढें।॥ तें काढूनि पुढती ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā yesaṇeṃ dheṃḍeṃ| prajñā pasareṃsīṃ buḍe| āleṃ bharateṃ evaḍheṃ||| teṃ kāḍhūni puḍhatī || 89||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, just as a large log, submerged by a great flood, is then carried forward by the current, so too is the intellect carried forward by the surge of spiritual experience.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देवो म्हणे हां गा पार्था । तूं आपणपें देख सर्वथा । तंव शवासूनि येरें माथा। तुकियेला॥ २९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: devo mhaṇe hāṃ gā pārthā | tūṃ āpaṇapeṃ dekha sarvathā | taṃva śavāsūni yereṃ māthā| tukiyelā|| 290||
verses.meaning: The Lord said, "Listen, Arjuna, you must always see yourself in everything." Then, bowing his head, Arjuna assented.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे जाणसी दातारा । मी तुजशीं व्यक्‍्तिशेजारा । उबगला आजी एकाहारा । येवों पाहें॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe jāṇasī dātārā | mī tujaśīṃ vyak‍tiśejārā | ubagalā ājī ekāhārā | yevoṃ pāheṃ|| 91||
verses.meaning: He says, "O Giver, I am weary of being alone with you, and now I wish to come and be with you."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाही हा ऐसा । लोभें देतसां जरी लालसा । तरी कां जी घालीतसां। आड आड जीवा॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāhī hā aisā | lobheṃ detasāṃ jarī lālasā | tarī kāṃ jī ghālītasāṃ| āḍa āḍa jīvā|| 92||
verses.meaning: Even if you give with such greed and longing, why do you then obstruct the soul, O Lord?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ श्रीकृष्ण म्हणती निकें । अद्यापि नाहीं मा ठाऊकें । वेड्या चंद्रा आणि चंद्रिकें ॥ न मिळणें आहे ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha śrīkṛṣṇa mhaṇatī nikeṃ | adyāpi nāhīṃ mā ṭhāūkeṃ | veḍyā caṃdrā āṇi caṃdrikeṃ || na miḻaṇeṃ āhe || 93||
verses.meaning: Then Shri Krishna said, "Indeed, you still do not know that the moon and its moonlight are inseparable."

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हाही बोळोनि भावो। तुज दाऊं आम्ही भिवों। जे रुसतां बांधे थांबो । तें प्रेम गा हें॥९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi hāhī boḻoni bhāvo| tuja dāūṃ āmhī bhivoṃ| je rusatāṃ bāṃdhe thāṃbo | teṃ prema gā heṃ||94||
verses.meaning: And this sentiment, we are afraid to show it to you, lest you get upset. This is indeed that love which, when displeased, binds and stops.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ एकमेकांचिये खुणे। विसंवादु तंवचि जिणें। म्हणौनि असो हें बोलणें । इयेविषयींचें ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha ekamekāṃciye khuṇe| visaṃvādu taṃvaci jiṇeṃ| mhaṇauni aso heṃ bolaṇeṃ | iyeviṣayīṃceṃ || 95||
verses.meaning: As long as there is disagreement among themselves, life continues. Therefore, let us set aside this discussion on this topic.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग कैशी कैशी ते आतां। बोलत होतों पंडुसुता । सर्व कर्मा भिन्नता । आत्मेनिसीं ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga kaiśī kaiśī te ātāṃ| bolata hotoṃ paṃḍusutā | sarva karmā bhinnatā | ātmenisīṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: Now, O son of Pandu, I was explaining how all actions are distinct from the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंव अर्जुन म्हणे देवें । माझिये मनींचेंचि स्वभावें । प्रस्ताविलें बरवें । प्रमेय तें जी ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃva arjuna mhaṇe deveṃ | mājhiye manīṃceṃci svabhāveṃ | prastāvileṃ baraveṃ | prameya teṃ jī || 97||
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna said, "O Lord, what you have naturally and beautifully proposed is indeed the very truth that was in my mind."

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें सकळ कर्मांचे बीज) कारणपंचक तुज। सांगेन ऐसी पैज। घेतली कां॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ sakaḻa karmāṃce bīja) kāraṇapaṃcaka tuja| sāṃgena aisī paija| ghetalī kāṃ|| 98||
verses.meaning: I will tell you about the five causes, which are the seed of all actions. Have I not taken such a vow?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आत्मया एथ कांहीं। सर्वथा लागु नाहीं। हे पुढारलासि ते देई । लाहाणें माझें ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ātmayā etha kāṃhīṃ| sarvathā lāgu nāhīṃ| he puḍhāralāsi te deī | lāhāṇeṃ mājheṃ || 99||
verses.meaning: And to the Self, there is absolutely no attachment. This is what you have revealed; grant me this understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया बोला विशवेशें। म्हणितलें तोषें बहुवसें । इयेविषयीं धरणें बैसे। ऐसें कें जोडे ॥ ३०० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā bolā viśaveśeṃ| mhaṇitaleṃ toṣeṃ bahuvaseṃ | iyeviṣayīṃ dharaṇeṃ baise| aiseṃ keṃ joḍe || 300 ||
verses.meaning: Upon hearing these words, Lord Vishvesha was greatly pleased and said, "How can one attain such a state of unwavering devotion and steadfastness in this matter?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अर्जुना निरूपिजेल। तें कौर भाषेआंतुल। परी मेचु ये होइजेळ। क्रणिया तुज॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī arjunā nirūpijela| teṃ kaura bhāṣeāṃtula| parī mecu ye hoijeḻa| kraṇiyā tuja|| 9||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, what I am about to explain, though it is in the language of the Kauravas, will be understood by you, the listener, as if it were your own.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब अर्जुन म्हणे देवो। काई विसरले मागील भावो । इये गोठीं कीं राखत आहों । मीतूंपण जी॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba arjuna mhaṇe devo| kāī visarale māgīla bhāvo | iye goṭhīṃ kīṃ rākhata āhoṃ | mītūṃpaṇa jī|| 2||
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna said, "O Lord, have you forgotten our past relationship? In these matters, I am still preserving the distinction of 'I' and 'you'."

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ श्रीकृष्ण म्हणती हो कां। आतां अवबधानाचा पसरु निका । 'करूनियां आइका । पुढारलो तें॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha śrīkṛṣṇa mhaṇatī ho kāṃ| ātāṃ avabadhānācā pasaru nikā | 'karūniyāṃ āikā | puḍhāralo teṃ|| 3||
verses.meaning: Here, Shri Krishna says, "Now, listen carefully to the explanation I am about to give."

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सत्यचि गा धनुर्धरा। सर्व कर्मांचा उभारा। होतसे बाहिरबाहिरा। करणीं पांचें ॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī satyaci gā dhanurdharā| sarva karmāṃcā ubhārā| hotase bāhirabāhirā| karaṇīṃ pāṃceṃ || 4||
verses.meaning: O Arjuna, the truth is that all actions, whether external or internal, are performed by the five senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पांच 'कारणदळवाडें । जिहीं कर्माकारु मांडे। ते हेतुस्तव घडे । पांच आथी ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pāṃca 'kāraṇadaḻavāḍeṃ | jihīṃ karmākāru māṃḍe| te hetustava ghaḍe | pāṃca āthī || 5||
verses.meaning: And the five 'causal factors' by which the form of action is established, these five causes are therefore present.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ शुभाशुभीं अंशीं । निफजती कर्मे ऐसीं। राती दिवो आकाशीं । जियापरी॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha śubhāśubhīṃ aṃśīṃ | niphajatī karme aisīṃ| rātī divo ākāśīṃ | jiyāparī|| 7||
verses.meaning: Just as day and night alternate in the sky, so too do good and bad deeds arise from the partiality of the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोय तेज धूमु। ययां वायूसीं संगमु। जालिया होय अभ्रागमु। व्योम तें नेणें ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: toya teja dhūmu| yayāṃ vāyūsīṃ saṃgamu| jāliyā hoya abhrāgamu| vyoma teṃ neṇeṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: When water, fire, and smoke unite with the wind, clouds form, but the sky remains untouched and unaware.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना काष्ठीं नाव मिळे। ते नावाडेनि चळे । चालविजे अनिळें। उदक तें साक्षी॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā kāṣṭhīṃ nāva miḻe| te nāvāḍeni caḻe | cālavije aniḻeṃ| udaka teṃ sākṣī||9||
verses.meaning: Just as a boat, made of various woods, is propelled by a boatman and moved by the wind, with the water as its witness, so too is the soul's journey.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का कवणें एके पिंडें। वेंचितां अवतरे भांडें । मग भवंडीजे दंडें। ग्रमे चक्र ॥ ३१० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā kavaṇeṃ eke piṃḍeṃ| veṃcitāṃ avatare bhāṃḍeṃ | maga bhavaṃḍīje daṃḍeṃ| grame cakra || 310 ||
verses.meaning: Or, when a potter's wheel is turned by a stick, it revolves in a circular motion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कर्तृत्व कुलालाचें। तेथ काय तें पृथ्वीयेचें। आधारावांचूनि वेंचे । विचारीं पां॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kartṛtva kulālāceṃ| tetha kāya teṃ pṛthvīyeceṃ| ādhārāvāṃcūni veṃce | vicārīṃ pāṃ|| 11||
verses.meaning: And the potter's skill, what is it without the earth? Consider, it perishes without its support.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हेंही असो लोकांचिया। राहाटी होतां आघविया। कोण काम सवितया । आंगा आलें॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃhī aso lokāṃciyā| rāhāṭī hotāṃ āghaviyā| koṇa kāma savitayā | āṃgā āleṃ|| 12||
verses.meaning: Let this also be. When all the worldly affairs are happening, what work does the sun have to do?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें पांचहेतुमिळणीं। पांचेंचि इहीं कारणीं। कौजे कर्मलतांची लावणी । आत्मा सिना॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ pāṃcahetumiḻaṇīṃ| pāṃceṃci ihīṃ kāraṇīṃ| kauje karmalatāṃcī lāvaṇī | ātmā sinā|| 13||
verses.meaning: Just as the five elements combine, and through these very five causes, the planting of the creeper of karma takes place, but the Soul remains untouched.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां तेंचि वेगळाली । पांचही विवंचूं गा भलीं । तुकोनि घेतलीं । मोतियें जैसीं ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ teṃci vegaḻālī | pāṃcahī vivaṃcūṃ gā bhalīṃ | tukoni ghetalīṃ | motiyeṃ jaisīṃ || 14||
verses.meaning: Now, let us consider these five separately, like pearls carefully selected and strung together.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं यथालक्षणें। आइक पां कर्म-कारणें । तरी देह हें मी म्हणें । पहिलें एथ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ yathālakṣaṇeṃ| āika pāṃ karma-kāraṇeṃ | tarī deha heṃ mī mhaṇeṃ | pahileṃ etha|| 15||
verses.meaning: Similarly, listen to the characteristics of the cause of action. First, I say that this body is the primary cause here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ययातें अधिष्ठान ऐसें। म्हणिजे तें याचि उद्देशों । जे स्वभोग्येंसीं वसे । भोक्ता येथ॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayāteṃ adhiṣṭhāna aiseṃ| mhaṇije teṃ yāci uddeśoṃ | je svabhogyeṃsīṃ vase | bhoktā yetha|| 16||
verses.meaning: This is called the abode, for this very purpose: that the enjoyer resides here with what is to be enjoyed by himself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियांच्या दाहें हातीं । जाचोनियां दिवोराती । सुखदुःखे प्रकृती। जोडीजती जियें॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyāṃcyā dāheṃ hātīṃ | jāconiyāṃ divorātī | sukhaduḥkhe prakṛtī| joḍījatī jiyeṃ|| 17||
verses.meaning: The senses burn day and night, tormenting the individual. Through this, the nature of happiness and sorrow is acquired.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियें भोगावया पुरुखा। आन ठावोचि नाहीं देखा । म्हणौनि अधिष्ठानभाखा। बोलिजे देह॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyeṃ bhogāvayā purukhā| āna ṭhāvoci nāhīṃ dekhā | mhaṇauni adhiṣṭhānabhākhā| bolije deha|| 18||
verses.meaning: For the Purusha to experience, there is no other place; therefore, the body is called the abode.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें चोविसांही तत्त्वांचें। कुटुंब घर वस्तीचे । तुटे बंधमोक्षाचें । गुंथाडे एथ ॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ covisāṃhī tattvāṃceṃ| kuṭuṃba ghara vastīce | tuṭe baṃdhamokṣāceṃ | guṃthāḍe etha || 19||
verses.meaning: Here, the family home of the twenty-four principles, the entanglement of bondage and liberation, is severed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना अवस्थात्रया। हें अधिष्ठान धनंजया । म्हणौनि देहा यया । हेंचि नाम॥ ३२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā avasthātrayā| heṃ adhiṣṭhāna dhanaṃjayā | mhaṇauni dehā yayā | heṃci nāma|| 320||
verses.meaning: Indeed, O Dhananjaya, these three states (waking, dreaming, deep sleep) are the very foundation of this body, and hence, this is its true name.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कर्ता हे दुजें। कर्माचें कारण जाणिजे । प्रतिबिंब म्हणिजे। चैतन्याचें जें॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kartā he dujeṃ| karmāceṃ kāraṇa jāṇije | pratibiṃba mhaṇije| caitanyāceṃ jeṃ|| 21||
verses.meaning: And the doer, know that it is the cause of action, which is called the reflection of consciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आकाशचि वर्षे नीर। तें तळवटीं बांधे नाडर। मग ब्िंबोनि तदाकार। होय जेवीं॥२२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ākāśaci varṣe nīra| teṃ taḻavaṭīṃ bāṃdhe nāḍara| maga biṃboni tadākāra| hoya jevīṃ||22||
verses.meaning: Just as the water that falls from the sky is contained in a reservoir, and then reflects the sky, becoming one with its form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां निद्राभरें बहुवें। ४३६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी राया आपणपें ठाउवें नव्हे। मग स्वप्नींचिये सामावे। रंकपणीं ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ nidrābhareṃ bahuveṃ| 436 śrījñāneśvarī rāyā āpaṇapeṃ ṭhāuveṃ navhe| maga svapnīṃciye sāmāve| raṃkapaṇīṃ || 23||
verses.meaning: Just as one, overcome by deep sleep, does not know oneself, and then in a dream, becomes absorbed in the state of a pauper.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आपुलेनि विसरें। चैतन्यचि देहाकारें। आभासोनि आविष्करे। देहपणें जें॥२४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ āpuleni visareṃ| caitanyaci dehākāreṃ| ābhāsoni āviṣkare| dehapaṇeṃ jeṃ||24||
verses.meaning: Just as Consciousness, through its own forgetfulness, appears in the form of the body and manifests as the state of being a body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया विसराच्या देशीं। प्रसिद्धि गा जीवु ऐसी । जेणें भाष केली देहेंसी । आघवाविषयीं ॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā visarācyā deśīṃ| prasiddhi gā jīvu aisī | jeṇeṃ bhāṣa kelī deheṃsī | āghavāviṣayīṃ || 25||
verses.meaning: In the land of forgetfulness, the soul (Jiva) is renowned for identifying itself with the body, thereby engaging in all worldly affairs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्रकृति करी कर्मे । तीं म्यां केली म्हणे भ्रमें। येथ कर्ता येणें नामें। बोलिजे जीवु ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: prakṛti karī karme | tīṃ myāṃ kelī mhaṇe bhrameṃ| yetha kartā yeṇeṃ nāmeṃ| bolije jīvu || 26||
verses.meaning: Actions are performed by Prakriti (Nature), but due to delusion, the embodied soul (Jiva) believes, "I did them." Thus, the Jiva is called the doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग पातेयांच्या केशीं । एकीच उठी दिठी जैसी । मोकळी चवरी ऐसी । चिरीव गमे॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga pāteyāṃcyā keśīṃ | ekīca uṭhī diṭhī jaisī | mokaḻī cavarī aisī | cirīva game|| 27||
verses.meaning: Just as a single glance rises from the hair of the patil (village headman), so too does the loose chauri (fly-whisk) seem to be split.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां घराआंतुल एकु । दीपाचा तो अबलोकु । गवाक्षभेदें अनेकु। आवडे जेवीं ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ gharāāṃtula eku | dīpācā to abaloku | gavākṣabhedeṃ aneku| āvaḍe jevīṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Just as a single lamp inside a house appears as many through various windows, so too does the divine light manifest in diverse forms.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां एकुच्ि पुरुषु जैसा। अनुसरत नवां रसां। नवविधु ऐसा। आवडों लागे॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ ekuci puruṣu jaisā| anusarata navāṃ rasāṃ| navavidhu aisā| āvaḍoṃ lāge|| 29||
verses.meaning: Just as a single man, when he embodies the nine sentiments, becomes pleasing in nine different ways.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं बुद्धीचे एक जाणणें। श्रोत्रादिभेदें येणें। बाहेरी इंद्रियपणें । फांके जें कां॥ ३३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ buddhīce eka jāṇaṇeṃ| śrotrādibhedeṃ yeṇeṃ| bāherī iṃdriyapaṇeṃ | phāṃke jeṃ kāṃ|| 330||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the intellect's singular knowing manifests through the distinctions of hearing and other senses, spreading outwards as the functions of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें पृथग्बिध करण। कर्माचें इया कारण । तिसरें गा जाण। नृपनंदना ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ pṛthagbidha karaṇa| karmāceṃ iyā kāraṇa | tisareṃ gā jāṇa| nṛpanaṃdanā || 39||
verses.meaning: Know, O Prince, that these distinct instruments are the third cause of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पूर्वपश्चिमवाहणीं। निघालिया 'वोघाचिया मिळणी। होय नदी नद पाणी । एकचि जेवीं॥३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pūrvapaścimavāhaṇīṃ| nighāliyā 'voghāciyā miḻaṇī| hoya nadī nada pāṇī | ekaci jevīṃ||32||
verses.meaning: Just as the waters of rivers and streams become one when they meet, flowing from east and west.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी क्रियाशक्ति पवनीं। असे जे अनपायिनी। ते पडिली नानास्थानीं। नाना होय॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī kriyāśakti pavanīṃ| ase je anapāyinī| te paḍilī nānāsthānīṃ| nānā hoya|| 33||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the power of action, which is imperishable and resides in the vital breath, manifests in various forms when it enters different places.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैं वाचे करी येणें। तैं तेंचि होय बोलणें । हाता आली तरी घेणें। देणें होय ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiṃ vāce karī yeṇeṃ| taiṃ teṃci hoya bolaṇeṃ | hātā ālī tarī gheṇeṃ| deṇeṃ hoya || 34||
verses.meaning: When it comes to speech, then that itself becomes the speaking. If it comes to hand, then it becomes taking and giving.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा चरणाच्या ठायीं। तरी गति तेचि पाहीं । अधोद्वारीं दोहीं। क्षरणें तेचि ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā caraṇācyā ṭhāyīṃ| tarī gati teci pāhīṃ | adhodvārīṃ dohīṃ| kṣaraṇeṃ teci || 35||
verses.meaning: Indeed, the feet are for movement, and similarly, the two lower doors (of the body) are for excretion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कंदौनि हृदयवरी। प्रणवाची उजरी। करितां तेचि शरीरीं । प्राणु म्हणिजे ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kaṃdauni hṛdayavarī| praṇavācī ujarī| karitāṃ teci śarīrīṃ | prāṇu mhaṇije || 36 ||
verses.meaning: When the light of Pranava (Om) is kindled in the heart, that very body is then called Prana (the vital life force).

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग उर्ध्वींचिया रिगानिगा। पुढती तेचि शक्ति पैं गा। उदानु ऐसिया लिंगा । पात्र जाहली ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga urdhvīṃciyā rigānigā| puḍhatī teci śakti paiṃ gā| udānu aisiyā liṃgā | pātra jāhalī || 37||
verses.meaning: Then, through the upward movement, that very same power, O listener, became worthy of the designation 'Udana'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अधोरंश्राचेनि वाहे। अपानु हें नाम लाहे। व्यापकपणें होये। व्यानु तेचि॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: adhoraṃśrāceni vāhe| apānu heṃ nāma lāhe| vyāpakapaṇeṃ hoye| vyānu teci|| 38||
verses.meaning: The downward-moving breath is called Apana. That which pervades the entire body is known as Vyana.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आरोगिलेनि रसें। शरीर भरी सरिसें। आणि न सांडितां असे । सर्वसंधीं ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ārogileni raseṃ| śarīra bharī sariseṃ| āṇi na sāṃḍitāṃ ase | sarvasaṃdhīṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: The body is filled equally with the absorbed essence, and it remains present in all its joints without being discarded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसिया इया राहटीं। मग तेचि क्रिया पाठीं । समान ऐसी किरीटी। बोलिजे गा॥ ३४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyā iyā rāhaṭīṃ| maga teci kriyā pāṭhīṃ | samāna aisī kirīṭī| bolije gā|| 340||
verses.meaning: In this manner, O Kiriti, the actions that follow are considered equal.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जांभई शिंक ढेंकर। ऐसैसा होतसे व्यापार। नाग कूर्म कृकर। इत्यादि होय॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jāṃbhaī śiṃka ḍheṃkara| aisaisā hotase vyāpāra| nāga kūrma kṛkara| ityādi hoya|| 41||
verses.meaning: And yawning, sneezing, belching—such actions occur. Nag, Kurma, Krikara—these and others happen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं वायूची हे चेष्टा। एकीचि परी सुभटा । वर्तनास्तव पालटा। येतसे जे॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ vāyūcī he ceṣṭā| ekīci parī subhaṭā | vartanāstava pālaṭā| yetase je|| 42||
verses.meaning: Thus, the sport of the wind, though it is one and the same, appears to change due to its various actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते भेदली वृत्तिपंथें। वायुशक्ति गा एथें।॥ कर्मकारण चौथें। ऐसें जाण ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: te bhedalī vṛttipaṃtheṃ| vāyuśakti gā etheṃ||| karmakāraṇa cautheṃ| aiseṃ jāṇa || 43 ||
verses.meaning: That vital energy, O Ganesha, is divided by the paths of the mind's modifications. Know this to be the fourth cause of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि क्रःतु बरवा शारदु । शारदीं पुढती चांदु । चंद्रीं जैसा संबंधु । पूर्णामेिचा ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kraḥtu baravā śāradu | śāradīṃ puḍhatī cāṃdu | caṃdrīṃ jaisā saṃbaṃdhu | pūrṇāmeicā || 44||
verses.meaning: And just as the autumn season is beautiful, and in autumn, the moon is even more so, the moon is like the full moon's connection.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वसंतीं बरवा आरामु। आरामींही प्रियसंगमु। संगमीं आगमु। उपचारांचा ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vasaṃtīṃ baravā ārāmu| ārāmīṃhī priyasaṃgamu| saṃgamīṃ āgamu| upacārāṃcā || 45||
verses.meaning: Or, how beautiful is a garden in spring! And in that garden, the company of a beloved! And in that company, the arrival of loving gestures!

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना कमळीं पांडवा। बिकासु जैसा बरवा। विकासींही यावा। परागाचा तो॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā kamaḻīṃ pāṃḍavā| bikāsu jaisā baravā| vikāsīṃhī yāvā| parāgācā to|| 46||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, just as a lotus naturally blossoms beautifully, so too does the pollen within it develop.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वाचे बरवें कवित्व। कवित्वीं बरवें रसिकत्व। रसिकत्वीं परतत्त्व-। स्पर्श जैसा॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāce baraveṃ kavitva| kavitvīṃ baraveṃ rasikatva| rasikatvīṃ paratattva-| sparśa jaisā|| 47||
verses.meaning: Speech is good, but poetry is better in speech. In poetry, appreciation is better. And in appreciation, the touch of the Supreme Reality is best.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी सर्ववृत्तिवेभवीं। बुद्धिचि एकली बरवी। बुद्धीही बरव नवी । इंद्रियप्रौढी ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī sarvavṛttivebhavīṃ| buddhici ekalī baravī| buddhīhī barava navī | iṃdriyaprauḍhī || 48 ||
verses.meaning: Similarly, amidst all the splendor of the senses, it is the intellect alone that is excellent. And even the excellence of the intellect is new and fresh due to the prowess of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इंद्रियप्रौढीमंडळा। श्रृंगार एकचि निर्मळा । जें अधिष्ठात्रियां कां मेळा। देवतांचा जो॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: iṃdriyaprauḍhīmaṃḍaḻā| śrṛṃgāra ekaci nirmaḻā | jeṃ adhiṣṭhātriyāṃ kāṃ meḻā| devatāṃcā jo|| 49||
verses.meaning: It is the pure and singular adornment of the assembly of the senses, the very gathering of the presiding deities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि चश्षुरादिकीं दाहें। इंद्रियां पाठीं स्वानुग्रहें । सूर्यादिकां कां आहे। सुरांचे वृंद ॥ ३५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni caśṣurādikīṃ dāheṃ| iṃdriyāṃ pāṭhīṃ svānugraheṃ | sūryādikāṃ kāṃ āhe| surāṃce vṛṃda || 350||
verses.meaning: Therefore, why do the hosts of gods, with the sun and others, exist behind the senses, with their own grace, burning in the eyes and other organs?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें देववृंद बरवें । कर्मकारण पांचवें। अर्जुना एथ जाणावें । देवो म्हणे॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ devavṛṃda baraveṃ | karmakāraṇa pāṃcaveṃ| arjunā etha jāṇāveṃ | devo mhaṇe|| 51||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, know that the assembly of deities is the fifth cause of action, so says the Lord.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं माने तुझिये आयणी। तैसी कर्मजातांची हे खाणी । पंचविध आकर्णी । निरूपिळी ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ māne tujhiye āyaṇī| taisī karmajātāṃcī he khāṇī | paṃcavidha ākarṇī | nirūpiḻī || 52||
verses.meaning: Thus, in your presence, is the very source of all actions, which are described as fivefold in the scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां हेचि खाणी वाढे । मग कर्माची सृष्टि घडे । जिहीं ते हेतुही उघडे। दाऊं पांचै॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ heci khāṇī vāḍhe | maga karmācī sṛṣṭi ghaḍe | jihīṃ te hetuhī ughaḍe| dāūṃ pāṃcai|| 53||
verses.meaning: Now, from this very source, the creation of actions expands. I will reveal the intentions behind them as well.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अवसांत आली माधवी । ते हेतु होय नवपल्लवीं । पल्लव पुष्पपुंज दावी । पुष्प फळातें ॥५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī avasāṃta ālī mādhavī | te hetu hoya navapallavīṃ | pallava puṣpapuṃja dāvī | puṣpa phaḻāteṃ ||54||
verses.meaning: Just as the spring season arrives, it causes new sprouts to appear. These sprouts then bear flowers, and the flowers, in turn, yield fruit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वार्षिये आणिजे मेघु । मेघें वृष्टिप्रसंगु । वृष्टीस्तव भोगु। सस्यसुखाचा ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vārṣiye āṇije meghu | megheṃ vṛṣṭiprasaṃgu | vṛṣṭīstava bhogu| sasyasukhācā || 55||
verses.meaning: Why is the cloud called upon? Because of the cloud, there is rain. Because of the rain, there is the enjoyment of abundant crops.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी प्राची अरुणातें विये। अरुणें सूर्योदयो होये । सूर्ये सगळा पाहे। दिवो जैसा ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī prācī aruṇāteṃ viye| aruṇeṃ sūryodayo hoye | sūrye sagaḻā pāhe| divo jaisā || 56||
verses.meaning: Just as the East gives birth to the dawn, and the dawn brings forth the sunrise, and the sun illuminates the entire day.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें मन हेतु पांडवा । होय कर्मसंकल्पभावा। तो संकल्पु लावी दिवा। वाचेचा गा॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ mana hetu pāṃḍavā | hoya karmasaṃkalpabhāvā| to saṃkalpu lāvī divā| vācecā gā|| 57||
verses.meaning: Just as the mind, O Pandava, becomes the intention and the source of action, that very intention lights the lamp of speech.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग वाचेचा तो दिवटा। दावी कृत्यजातांचिया वाटा । तेव्हां कर्ता रिगे कामठां। कर्तृत्वाच्या ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga vācecā to divaṭā| dāvī kṛtyajātāṃciyā vāṭā | tevhāṃ kartā rige kāmaṭhāṃ| kartṛtvācyā || 58||
verses.meaning: Then, the lamp of speech illuminates the paths of all actions. It is then that the doer enters the workshop of doership.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ शरीरादिक दळवाडें। शरीरादिकां हेतुचि घडे । 'लोहकाम लोखंडें। निर्वाळिजे जैसें ॥५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha śarīrādika daḻavāḍeṃ| śarīrādikāṃ hetuci ghaḍe | 'lohakāma lokhaṃḍeṃ| nirvāḻije jaiseṃ ||59||
verses.meaning: Just as iron is purified by iron, so too the body and its associated elements are purified by the very cause of the body and its elements.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां तांथुबाचा ताणा । तांधथु घालितां वैरणा । तो तंतुचि विचक्षणा । होय पटु ॥ ३६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ tāṃthubācā tāṇā | tāṃdhathu ghālitāṃ vairaṇā | to taṃtuci vicakṣaṇā | hoya paṭu || 360||
verses.meaning: Just as a thread, when woven into the warp and weft, becomes a cloth, so too does the subtle thread of spiritual understanding, when properly interwoven with experience, become the fabric of wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें मनवाचादेहाचें । कर्म मनादि हेतुचि रचे। रत्नीं घडे रलाचें। दळवाडें जेवीं॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ manavācādehāceṃ | karma manādi hetuci race| ratnīṃ ghaḍe ralāceṃ| daḻavāḍeṃ jevīṃ||61||
verses.meaning: Just as the actions of the mind and body are formed by the intentions of the mind, so too are jewels crafted into ornaments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एथ शरीरादिकें कारणें। तेंचि हेतु केवीं हें कोणें। अपेक्षिजे तरी तेणें । अवधारिजो ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: etha śarīrādikeṃ kāraṇeṃ| teṃci hetu kevīṃ heṃ koṇeṃ| apekṣije tarī teṇeṃ | avadhārijo || 62||
verses.meaning: If someone asks how the body and such are the cause, then they should listen to this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आइका सूर्याचिया प्रकाशा । हेतु कारण सूर्युचि जैसा । कां ऊंसाचें कांडें ऊंसा। वाढी हेतु॥६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āikā sūryāciyā prakāśā | hetu kāraṇa sūryuci jaisā | kāṃ ūṃsāceṃ kāṃḍeṃ ūṃsā| vāḍhī hetu||63||
verses.meaning: Listen, just as the sun itself is the cause and reason for the sun's light, or as the sugarcane stalk is the cause of the sugarcane's growth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना वाग्देवता वानावी। तें वाचाचि लागे कामवावी। कां वेदां वेदेंचि बोलावी । प्रतिष्ठा जेवीं ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā vāgdevatā vānāvī| teṃ vācāci lāge kāmavāvī| kāṃ vedāṃ vedeṃci bolāvī | pratiṣṭhā jevīṃ || 64||
verses.meaning: Why should one praise various goddesses of speech? It is like making speech itself work for its own praise, or like the Vedas themselves speaking to establish their own authority.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें कर्मा शरीरादिकें । कारण हें कौर ठाउकें । परी हेंचि हेतु न चुके । हेंही एथ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ karmā śarīrādikeṃ | kāraṇa heṃ kaura ṭhāukeṃ | parī heṃci hetu na cuke | heṃhī etha|| 65 ||
verses.meaning: Just as the body and actions are known to be the cause, so too, this very cause does not fail to produce its effect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि देहादिकीं कारणीं। देहादि हेतु मिळणीं। होय जया उभारणी । कर्मजातां ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi dehādikīṃ kāraṇīṃ| dehādi hetu miḻaṇīṃ| hoya jayā ubhāraṇī | karmajātāṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: And in the causes related to the body and so on, when the reasons for the body and other things come together, that is how the entire edifice of actions is raised.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें शास्त्रार्थ मानिळेया । मार्गा अनुसरे धनंजया । ४३८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी तरी न्याय तो न्याया । हेतु होय ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ śāstrārtha māniḻeyā | mārgā anusare dhanaṃjayā | 438 śrījñāneśvarī tarī nyāya to nyāyā | hetu hoya || 67||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, that which is accepted as the true meaning of the scriptures, that path is followed. In Shri Dnyaneshwari, justice becomes the cause of justice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा पर्जन्योदकाचा लोटु । विपायें धरी साळीचा पाटु। तो जिरे परी अचाटु। उपयोगु आथी ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā parjanyodakācā loṭu | vipāyeṃ dharī sāḻīcā pāṭu| to jire parī acāṭu| upayogu āthī || 68||
verses.meaning: Just as a flood of rainwater, by chance, irrigates a rice field, the water may recede, but its benefit remains immense.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां रोषें निघालें अवचटें । पडिलें द्वारकेचिया वाटे । तें शिणे परी सुनाटें। न बचिती पदें॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ roṣeṃ nighāleṃ avacaṭeṃ | paḍileṃ dvārakeciyā vāṭe | teṃ śiṇe parī sunāṭeṃ| na bacitī padeṃ|| 69||
verses.meaning: Or perhaps, having set out in sudden anger, and fallen upon the path to Dwarka, though weary, his steps did not falter in the desolate way.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें हेतुकारण मेळें। उठी कर्म जें आंधळें। तें शास्त्राचें लाहे डोळे । तैं न्याय म्हणिपे ॥ ३७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ hetukāraṇa meḻeṃ| uṭhī karma jeṃ āṃdhaḻeṃ| teṃ śāstrāceṃ lāhe ḍoḻe | taiṃ nyāya mhaṇipe || 370||
verses.meaning: Just as a blind action arises from a confluence of causes, when it gains the 'eyes' of scripture, then it is called 'justice' or 'righteousness'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना दूध वाढितां ठावो पावे। तंब उतोनि जाय स्वभावें । तोही वेंचु परी नव्हे । वेंचिलें तें ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā dūdha vāḍhitāṃ ṭhāvo pāve| taṃba utoni jāya svabhāveṃ | tohī veṃcu parī navhe | veṃcileṃ teṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: Just as milk, when it boils over, naturally overflows and is wasted, yet it is not truly spent or consumed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें शास्त्रसाहयेंबीण । केलें नोहे जरी अकारण। तरी लागो कां नागवण । दानलेखीं ॥७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ śāstrasāhayeṃbīṇa | keleṃ nohe jarī akāraṇa| tarī lāgo kāṃ nāgavaṇa | dānalekhīṃ ||72||
verses.meaning: Just as an action performed without the aid of scriptures is not considered futile, why then should there be any impediment in the account of charity?

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा बावन्ना वर्णापरता। कोण मंत्रु आहे पंडुसुता। कां बावन्नही नुच्चारितां। जीवु आथी ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā bāvannā varṇāparatā| koṇa maṃtru āhe paṃḍusutā| kāṃ bāvannahī nuccāritāṃ| jīvu āthī || 73||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, what mantra is there beyond the fifty-two letters? Or is there any life without uttering these fifty-two?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मंत्राची कडसणी। जंब नेणिजे कोदंडपाणी। तंव उच्चारफळ वाणी । न पवे जेवीं ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī maṃtrācī kaḍasaṇī| jaṃba neṇije kodaṃḍapāṇī| taṃva uccāraphaḻa vāṇī | na pave jevīṃ || 74||
verses.meaning: Just as the utterance of a mantra does not yield its fruit if one does not know the wielder of the bow (Lord Rama), so too does speech not attain its full effect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं कारणहेतुयोगें। जें बरिसाट कर्म निगे। तें शास्त्राचिये न लगे। कांसे जंव॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ kāraṇahetuyogeṃ| jeṃ barisāṭa karma nige| teṃ śāstrāciye na lage| kāṃse jaṃva|| 75||
verses.meaning: Similarly, actions that arise from causes and motives, however good they may seem, are not truly bound by the scriptures until they are performed without attachment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कर्म होतचि असे तेव्हांही । परी तें होणें नव्हे पाहीं । तो अन्यायो गा अन्यायीं । हेतु होय ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: karma hotaci ase tevhāṃhī | parī teṃ hoṇeṃ navhe pāhīṃ | to anyāyo gā anyāyīṃ | hetu hoya || 76||
verses.meaning: Even then, action certainly happens, but understand that it is not truly happening. That injustice, indeed, becomes the motive for the unjust.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं पंचकारणां कर्मा। पांचही हेतु हे सुमहिमा। आतां एथें पाहें पां आत्मा । सांपडला असे॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ paṃcakāraṇāṃ karmā| pāṃcahī hetu he sumahimā| ātāṃ etheṃ pāheṃ pāṃ ātmā | sāṃpaḍalā ase|| 77||
verses.meaning: Thus, the five causes of action, these five are of great glory. Now, behold, the Self is found within them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भानु न होनि रूपें जैसीं। चश्षुरूपातें प्रकाशी । आत्मा न होनि कर्मे तैसीं। प्रकटित असे गा॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhānu na honi rūpeṃ jaisīṃ| caśṣurūpāteṃ prakāśī | ātmā na honi karme taisīṃ| prakaṭita ase gā|| 78||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun, without becoming the forms it illuminates, reveals them to the eyes, so too the Atman, without becoming the actions, manifests them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं प्रतिबिंब आरिसा। दोन्ही न होनि वौरेशा। दोहींतें प्रकाशी जैसा। न्याहाळिता तो॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ pratibiṃba ārisā| donhī na honi vaureśā| dohīṃteṃ prakāśī jaisā| nyāhāḻitā to||79||
verses.meaning: Just as the reflection and the mirror are not two separate entities, but rather the observer illuminates both, so too is the relationship between the individual soul and the Supreme Being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां अहोरात्र सविता। न होनि करी पंडुसुता । तैसा आत्मा कर्मकर्ता। न होनि दावी॥ ३८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ ahorātra savitā| na honi karī paṃḍusutā | taisā ātmā karmakartā| na honi dāvī|| 380||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun, day and night, acts without truly being the doer, O son of Pandu, so too the Self, without being the doer, manifests action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी देहाहंमानभुलळी । जयाची बुग्ि देहींच आतली । जया आत्मविषयीं जाली । मध्यरात्री गा॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī dehāhaṃmānabhulaḻī | jayācī bugi dehīṃca ātalī | jayā ātmaviṣayīṃ jālī | madhyarātrī gā|| 89||
verses.meaning: But for those whose intellect is deluded by the identification with the body, whose understanding is confined to the physical form, for them, regarding the true Self, it is as if it were the dead of night.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेणें चैतन्या ईश्वरा ब्रह्मा । देहचि केलें परमसीमा। तया आत्मा कर्ता हे प्रमा । अलोट उपजे॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṇeṃ caitanyā īśvarā brahmā | dehaci keleṃ paramasīmā| tayā ātmā kartā he pramā | aloṭa upaje|| 82||
verses.meaning: When the Supreme Being, the very consciousness, makes the body its ultimate abode, then the conviction that the Self is the doer arises irresistibly.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आत्माचि कर्मकर्ता। हाही निश्चयो नाहीं तत्त्वतां। देहोचि मी कर्मकर्ता। मानितो साचे॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātmāci karmakartā| hāhī niścayo nāhīṃ tattvatāṃ| dehoci mī karmakartā| mānito sāce|| 83||
verses.meaning: The Self is not truly the doer of actions; this is not the ultimate truth. It is the body that truly believes, "I am the doer of actions."

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे आत्मा मी कर्मातीतु। सर्वकर्मसाक्षिभूतु। हे आपली कहीं मातु। नायकेचि कानीं ॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: je ātmā mī karmātītu| sarvakarmasākṣibhūtu| he āpalī kahīṃ mātu| nāyakeci kānīṃ || 84||
verses.meaning: The Self, which is beyond all actions, the witness of all actions, does not hear this truth anywhere, in any ear.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि उमपा आत्मयातें। देहचिवरी मविजे एथें। विचित्र काई रात्रि दिवसातें। डुडुळ न करी॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni umapā ātmayāteṃ| dehacivarī mavije etheṃ| vicitra kāī rātri divasāteṃ| ḍuḍuḻa na karī|| 85||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the immeasurable Self is measured by the body here. Is it not strange that an owl does not perceive day?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं जेणें आकाशींचा कहीं । सत्य सूर्य देखिला नाहीं । तो थिल्लरींचें बिंब काई। मानूं न लाहे॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ jeṇeṃ ākāśīṃcā kahīṃ | satya sūrya dekhilā nāhīṃ | to thillarīṃceṃ biṃba kāī| mānūṃ na lāhe|| 86||
verses.meaning: One who has never seen the true sun in the sky, how can he accept the reflection in a small puddle as real?

verses.shloka_devanagari: थिल्लराचेनि जालेपणें । सूर्यासि आणी होणें। त्याच्या नाशीं नाशणें। कंपें कंपू॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: thillarāceni jālepaṇeṃ | sūryāsi āṇī hoṇeṃ| tyācyā nāśīṃ nāśaṇeṃ| kaṃpeṃ kaṃpū|| 87||
verses.meaning: The existence of a tiny dewdrop does not bring about the sun's existence, nor does its destruction cause the sun's destruction, just as a tremor does not cause a mountain to tremble.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा निद्रिस्ता चेबो नये। तंव स्वप्न साच हों लाहे। रज्जु नेणतां सापा ब्िहे। विस्मो कवण॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā nidristā cebo naye| taṃva svapna sāca hoṃ lāhe| rajju neṇatāṃ sāpā bihe| vismo kavaṇa|| 88||
verses.meaning: One should not awaken a sleeping person, for then their dream seems real. If one mistakes a rope for a snake, what wonder is there in being afraid?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जंब कवळ आधि डोळां। तंव चंद्र देखावा कीं पिंबळा । काय मृगींहीं मृगजळा। भाळावें नाहीं ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaṃba kavaḻa ādhi ḍoḻāṃ| taṃva caṃdra dekhāvā kīṃ piṃbaḻā | kāya mṛgīṃhīṃ mṛgajaḻā| bhāḻāveṃ nāhīṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: When the eyes are afflicted by jaundice, the moon appears yellow. Why should the deer be blamed for mistaking a mirage for water?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा शास्त्रगुरूचेनि नांबें। जो वाराही टेंकों नेदी सिवें। केवळ मोढ्याचेनिचि जीवें। जियाला जो॥ ३९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā śāstragurūceni nāṃbeṃ| jo vārāhī ṭeṃkoṃ nedī siveṃ| kevaḻa moḍhyācenici jīveṃ| jiyālā jo|| 390||
verses.meaning: Just as one who, in the name of a spiritual teacher, does not allow even a breeze to touch them, living solely by their own foolishness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें देहात्मदृष्टीमुळें। आत्मया घापे देहाचें जाळें। जैसा अभ्राचा वेगु कोल्हे । चंद्री मानी ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ dehātmadṛṣṭīmuḻeṃ| ātmayā ghāpe dehāceṃ jāḻeṃ| jaisā abhrācā vegu kolhe | caṃdrī mānī || 91 ||
verses.meaning: Due to the identification of the self with the body, the self is ensnared by the body, just as one mistakenly attributes the movement of clouds to the moon.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तया मानणयासाठीं । देहबंदिशाळे किरीटी। कर्माच्या वज्रगांठी।) कळासे तो॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga tayā mānaṇayāsāṭhīṃ | dehabaṃdiśāḻe kirīṭī| karmācyā vajragāṃṭhī|) kaḻāse to|| 92||
verses.meaning: Then, to honor that, O Kiriti, he is bound in the prison of the body by the unbreakable knots of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाहें पां बद्ध भावना दृढा। नळियेवरी तो बापुडा। काय मोकळेयाहि पायाचा चवबडा। न ठकेचि पुंसा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāheṃ pāṃ baddha bhāvanā dṛḍhā| naḻiyevarī to bāpuḍā| kāya mokaḻeyāhi pāyācā cavabaḍā| na ṭhakeci puṃsā|| 93||
verses.meaning: Behold, how strong is the feeling of bondage! Even a poor man, though his feet are free, cannot escape the pursuit of his own shadow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि निर्मळे आत्मस्वरूपीं । जो प्रकृतीचें केलें आरोपी । तो कल्पकोडीच्या मापी । मवीचि कर्मे ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni nirmaḻe ātmasvarūpīṃ | jo prakṛtīceṃ keleṃ āropī | to kalpakoḍīcyā māpī | mavīci karme || 94||
verses.meaning: Therefore, one who attributes the actions of Prakriti (nature/matter) to the pure Self (Atman) will continue to accumulate karma through countless eons.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां कर्मामाजीं असे। परी तयातें कर्म न स्पर्शे। बडवानळातें जैसें । समुद्रोदक॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ karmāmājīṃ ase| parī tayāteṃ karma na sparśe| baḍavānaḻāteṃ jaiseṃ | samudrodaka|| 95||
verses.meaning: Now, though one may be engaged in action, action does not touch them, just as the ocean's water does not extinguish the submarine fire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंनि वेगळेपणें। जयाचें कर्मी असणें तो कीर ओळखावा कवणें। तरी सांगों ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃni vegaḻepaṇeṃ| jayāceṃ karmī asaṇeṃ to kīra oḻakhāvā kavaṇeṃ| tarī sāṃgoṃ || 96||
verses.meaning: How then can one recognize that being whose presence is in all actions, yet who remains distinct? I shall explain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे मुक्‍्तातें निर्धारितां। लाभे आपलीच मुक्‍तता। जैसी दीपें दिसे पाहतां। आपली वस्तु॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: je muk‍tāteṃ nirdhāritāṃ| lābhe āpalīca muk‍tatā| jaisī dīpeṃ dise pāhatāṃ| āpalī vastu|| 97||
verses.meaning: When one contemplates the liberated, one attains one's own liberation, just as by the light of a lamp, one sees one's own possessions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी दर्पणु जंब उटिजे। तंब आपणपयां आपण भेटिजे। कां तोय पावतां तोय होईजे । लवणें जेवीं ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī darpaṇu jaṃba uṭije| taṃba āpaṇapayāṃ āpaṇa bheṭije| kāṃ toya pāvatāṃ toya hoīje | lavaṇeṃ jevīṃ || 98 ||
verses.meaning: When a mirror is cleaned, one sees oneself in it. Or, just as salt dissolves into water and becomes one with it, so too does the individual soul merge with the Universal Soul upon attaining it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो परतोनि मागुतें। प्रतिबिंब पाहे बिंबातें । तंव पाहणें जाउनी आयितें। बिंबचि होय॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso paratoni māguteṃ| pratibiṃba pāhe biṃbāteṃ | taṃva pāhaṇeṃ jāunī āyiteṃ| biṃbaci hoya|| 99||
verses.meaning: Let this be. When the reflection turns back and looks at the original, that very act of seeing becomes the original itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें हारपळें आपणपें पावे। तैं संतांतें पाहतां गिंबसावें । म्हणौनि वानावे ऐकावे । तेचि सदा॥ ४००॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ hārapaḻeṃ āpaṇapeṃ pāve| taiṃ saṃtāṃteṃ pāhatāṃ giṃbasāveṃ | mhaṇauni vānāve aikāve | teci sadā|| 400||
verses.meaning: Just as one finds their lost self, so too should one seek out the saints. Therefore, one should always praise and listen to them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी कर्मी असोनि कर्मे। जो नावरे समेंविषमें। चर्मचश्षूंचेनि चामें। दृष्टि जैसी ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī karmī asoni karme| jo nāvare sameṃviṣameṃ| carmacaśṣūṃceni cāmeṃ| dṛṣṭi jaisī || 1||
verses.meaning: Just as the eyes, though engaged in seeing, are not bound by the good or bad things they perceive, so too is the one who, while performing actions, remains untouched by their dualistic outcomes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा सोडवला जो आहे। तयाचें रूप आतां पाहें। उपपत्तीची बाहे। उभऊनि सांगों ॥२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā soḍavalā jo āhe| tayāceṃ rūpa ātāṃ pāheṃ| upapattīcī bāhe| ubhaūni sāṃgoṃ ||2||
verses.meaning: Now, behold the form of one who is thus liberated. I will explain it by erecting a structure of reasoning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अविद्येचिया निदा । विश्‍वस्वप्नाचा हा धांदा । भोगीत होता प्रबुद्धा । अनादि जो॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī avidyeciyā nidā | viś‍vasvapnācā hā dhāṃdā | bhogīta hotā prabuddhā | anādi jo||3||
verses.meaning: Thus, in the sleep of ignorance, the primordial one, though enlightened, was experiencing the dream-like activity of the universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो महावाक्‍्याचेनि नांवें। गुरुकृपेचेनि थांबें। माथां हातु ठेविला नव्हे। थापटिला जैसा॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: to mahāvāk‍yāceni nāṃveṃ| gurukṛpeceni thāṃbeṃ| māthāṃ hātu ṭhevilā navhe| thāpaṭilā jaisā|| 4||
verses.meaning: That Supreme Word, by the grace of the Guru, is not merely placed upon the head, but rather, it is as if patted into place, firmly established.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा विश्‍वस्वप्नेंसीं माया। नीद सांडूनि धनंजया । सहसा चेइला अट्ठया-। नंदपणें जो॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā viś‍vasvapneṃsīṃ māyā| nīda sāṃḍūni dhanaṃjayā | sahasā ceilā aṭṭhayā-| naṃdapaṇeṃ jo|| 5||
verses.meaning: Just as the universe is a dream, so too is Maya. O Dhananjaya, when one suddenly awakens from the sleep of Maya, they realize their true nature as pure bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां मृगजळाचे पूर । ४४० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी दिसते एक निरंतर । हारपती कां चंद्रकर। फांकतां जैसे॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ mṛgajaḻāce pūra | 440 śrījñāneśvarī disate eka niraṃtara | hārapatī kāṃ caṃdrakara| phāṃkatāṃ jaise|| 6||
verses.meaning: Just as the continuous flow of a mirage appears, but then vanishes like moonlight when the sun rises.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां बाळत्व निघोनि जाय। तैं बागुला नाहीं त्राय। पैं जळालिया इंधन न होय । रंधन जेवीं ॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ bāḻatva nighoni jāya| taiṃ bāgulā nāhīṃ trāya| paiṃ jaḻāliyā iṃdhana na hoya | raṃdhana jevīṃ ||7||
verses.meaning: Just as childhood passes away, and the fear of the bogeyman no longer holds sway, so too, burnt wood cannot be used again for cooking.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना चेवबो आलिया पाठीं। तैं स्वप्न न दिसे दिठी। तैसी अहंममता किरीटी। नुरेचि तया॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā cevabo āliyā pāṭhīṃ| taiṃ svapna na dise diṭhī| taisī ahaṃmamatā kirīṭī| nureci tayā|| 8||
verses.meaning: Just as various objects seen in a dream vanish upon waking, so too, O Kiriti (Arjuna), does the ego and possessiveness of such a one cease to exist.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग सूर्य आंधारालागीं। रिघो कां भलते सुरंगीं। परी तो तयाच्या भागीं। नाहींचि जैसा॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga sūrya āṃdhārālāgīṃ| righo kāṃ bhalate suraṃgīṃ| parī to tayācyā bhāgīṃ| nāhīṃci jaisā|| 9||
verses.meaning: Then, even if the sun were to enter any dark cave, darkness would not be found in its presence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा आत्मत्वें वेष्टिला होये। तो जया तया दृश्यातें पाहे । तें दृश्य द्रष्टेपणेंसीं होत जाये । तयाचेंचि रूप॥ ४१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā ātmatveṃ veṣṭilā hoye| to jayā tayā dṛśyāteṃ pāhe | teṃ dṛśya draṣṭepaṇeṃsīṃ hota jāye | tayāceṃci rūpa|| 410||
verses.meaning: Just as one enveloped in the Self, whatever he perceives, that perception itself becomes one with the perceiver, taking on his very form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा वन्हि जया लागे। तें बन्हिचि जालिया आंगें। दाह्यदाहकविभागें। सांडिजे तें ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā vanhi jayā lāge| teṃ banhici jāliyā āṃgeṃ| dāhyadāhakavibhāgeṃ| sāṃḍije teṃ || 91||
verses.meaning: Just as fire, when it consumes something, makes that thing itself into fire, thereby abandoning the distinction between what burns and what is burned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कर्माकारा दुजेया । तो कर्तेपणाचा आत्मया। आळु आला तो गेलिया। कांहीं बाहीं जें उरे॥१२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā karmākārā dujeyā | to kartepaṇācā ātmayā| āḻu ālā to geliyā| kāṃhīṃ bāhīṃ jeṃ ure||12||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the blemish of doership, which is the second form of action, is removed, whatever remains is the true essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये आत्मस्थितीचा जो रावो। मग तो देहीं इये जाणेल ठावो । काय प्रल्यांबूचा उन्नाहो। बोघु मानी॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye ātmasthitīcā jo rāvo| maga to dehīṃ iye jāṇela ṭhāvo | kāya pralyāṃbūcā unnāho| boghu mānī|| 13||
verses.meaning: Then, the one who is the king of that state of self-realization, will he consider this body as his abode? What is the use of the rising flood of the deluge, if one considers it as a small pool?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी ते पूर्ण अहंता । काई देहपणें पंडुसुता । आवरे काई सविता । बिंबें धरिला ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī te pūrṇa ahaṃtā | kāī dehapaṇeṃ paṃḍusutā | āvare kāī savitā | biṃbeṃ dharilā || 14||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's image cannot be contained by its reflection, so too, O son of Pandu, can the complete ego not be confined by the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं मथूनि लोणी घेपे। तें मागुती 'ताकीं घापे। तरी तें अलिप्तपणें सिंपे । तेणेंसीं काई ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ mathūni loṇī ghepe| teṃ māgutī 'tākīṃ ghāpe| tarī teṃ aliptapaṇeṃ siṃpe | teṇeṃsīṃ kāī || 95||
verses.meaning: Just as butter, once churned from buttermilk, does not mix back with it even if placed back in it, so too is the detached soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना काष्ठौनी बीरेशा । वेगळा केलिया हुताशा । राहे काष्ठाचिया मांदुसा । कोंडलेपणें॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā kāṣṭhaunī bīreśā | vegaḻā keliyā hutāśā | rāhe kāṣṭhāciyā māṃdusā | koṃḍalepaṇeṃ|| 96||
verses.meaning: When fire is separated from various woods, it remains confined within the wood, as if imprisoned.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां रात्रीचिया उदराआंतु। निघाला जो हा भास्वतु। तो रात्री ऐसी मातु । ऐके कायी॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ rātrīciyā udarāāṃtu| nighālā jo hā bhāsvatu| to rātrī aisī mātu | aike kāyī|| 17||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun, born from the womb of night, does not heed the talk of night, so too the enlightened soul transcends worldly illusions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें वेद्य वेदकपणेंसी । पडिलें कां जयाचे ग्रासीं। तया देह मी ऐसी। अहंता कैंची॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ vedya vedakapaṇeṃsī | paḍileṃ kāṃ jayāce grāsīṃ| tayā deha mī aisī| ahaṃtā kaiṃcī|| 18||
verses.meaning: How can the ego of "I am this body" arise in one who has transcended the knower and the known, and for whom even the act of knowing has dissolved into their true nature?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आकाशें जेथें जेथुनी। जाईजे तेथ असे भरोनी। म्हणौनि ठेळें कोंदोनि। आपेंआप॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ākāśeṃ jetheṃ jethunī| jāīje tetha ase bharonī| mhaṇauni ṭheḻeṃ koṃdoni| āpeṃāpa|| 19||
verses.meaning: And wherever one goes, the sky is filled there, and thus it remains, ever-present and self-contained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें जें तेणें करावें । तो तेंचि आहे स्वभावें। मा कोणें कर्मी वेष्टावें। कर्तपणें ॥ ४२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jeṃ teṇeṃ karāveṃ | to teṃci āhe svabhāveṃ| mā koṇeṃ karmī veṣṭāveṃ| kartapaṇeṃ || 420||
verses.meaning: Whatever He has to do, He is that by nature. Then, in which action should He engage with a sense of doership?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नुरेचि गगनावीण ठावो । नोहेचि समुद्रा प्रवाहो। नुठीचि श्रुबा जावों। तैसें जाहालें ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nureci gaganāvīṇa ṭhāvo | noheci samudrā pravāho| nuṭhīci śrubā jāvoṃ| taiseṃ jāhāleṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: Just as there is no space without the sky, no flow without the ocean, and no rising without the sun, so it has become.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि अहंकृतिभावो। जयाचा बोधीं जाहला वावो । तऱही देहा जंब निर्वाहो। तंव आथी कर्मे ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni ahaṃkṛtibhāvo| jayācā bodhīṃ jāhalā vāvo | taṟahī dehā jaṃba nirvāho| taṃva āthī karme || 22||
verses.meaning: Thus, for one whose ego-sense has been rendered void by true knowledge, actions will continue as long as the body endures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वारा जरी वाजोनि वोसरे। तरी तो डोल रुखीं उरे। कां सेंदें द्रुति राहे कापुरें। वेंचलेनी ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: vārā jarī vājoni vosare| tarī to ḍola rukhīṃ ure| kāṃ seṃdeṃ druti rāhe kāpureṃ| veṃcalenī || 23||
verses.meaning: Even if the wind blows and then subsides, its sway remains in the trees. Or, just as the fragrance of camphor lingers even after it has vanished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां सरलेया गीताचा समारंभु। न वचे राहवलेपणाचा क्षोभु। भूमी लोळोनी गेलिया अंबु । बोल थारे॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ saraleyā gītācā samāraṃbhu| na vace rāhavalepaṇācā kṣobhu| bhūmī loḻonī geliyā aṃbu | bola thāre|| 24||
verses.meaning: When the discourse of the Gita concludes, the agitation of not being able to contain oneself does not subside. Just as water, having flowed over the earth, eventually settles, so too do words find their rest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा मावळलेनि अर्के । संध्येचिये भूमिके । ज्योतिदीप्ती कौतुकें।॥ दिसे जैसी॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā māvaḻaleni arke | saṃdhyeciye bhūmike | jyotidīptī kautukeṃ||| dise jaisī|| 25||
verses.meaning: Just as, when the sun has set, the light of the stars appears wondrously in the twilight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं लक्ष भेदिलियाहीवरी। बाण धांवेचि तंबवरी। जंब भरली आथी उरी। बळाची ते॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ lakṣa bhediliyāhīvarī| bāṇa dhāṃveci taṃbavarī| jaṃba bharalī āthī urī| baḻācī te|| 26||
verses.meaning: Even after piercing the target, the arrow continues to fly as long as it is filled with the power of the bowstring.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना चक्रीं भांडे जालें। तें कुलालें परतें नेलें। परी भ्रमेंचि तें मागिळे। भोवंडिलेपणें ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā cakrīṃ bhāṃḍe jāleṃ| teṃ kulāleṃ parateṃ neleṃ| parī bhrameṃci teṃ māgiḻe| bhovaṃḍilepaṇeṃ || 27||
verses.meaning: Many pots were made on the wheel, which the potter took away. But due to illusion, they were still considered to be spinning, as if they were still on the wheel.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा देहाभिमानु गेलिया । देह जेणें स्वभावें धनंजया । जालें तें अपैसया । चेष्टवीच तें ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā dehābhimānu geliyā | deha jeṇeṃ svabhāveṃ dhanaṃjayā | jāleṃ teṃ apaisayā | ceṣṭavīca teṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Just as, when the identification with the body is gone, O Dhananjaya, the body, by its very nature, spontaneously performs its actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संकल्पेंबीण स्वप्न । न लावितां दांगीचें बन। न रचितां गंधर्वभुवन । उठी जैसें ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃkalpeṃbīṇa svapna | na lāvitāṃ dāṃgīceṃ bana| na racitāṃ gaṃdharvabhuvana | uṭhī jaiseṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: Just as a dream arises without any conscious intention, or a forest appears without being planted, or a city of Gandharvas (a mirage) forms without being built.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आत्मयाचेनि उद्यमेंबीण । तैसें देहादिपंचकारण । होय आपणयां आपण। क्रियाजात ॥ ४३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātmayāceni udyameṃbīṇa | taiseṃ dehādipaṃcakāraṇa | hoya āpaṇayāṃ āpaṇa| kriyājāta || 430||
verses.meaning: Just as without the effort of the Atman, the five elements of the body become themselves, so too all actions happen spontaneously.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं प्राचीनसंस्कारवशें । पांचही कारणें सहेतुकें । कामवीजती गा अनेकें। कर्माकारें॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ prācīnasaṃskāravaśeṃ | pāṃcahī kāraṇeṃ sahetukeṃ | kāmavījatī gā anekeṃ| karmākāreṃ|| 39||
verses.meaning: Indeed, due to the influence of past impressions, the five causes, with their inherent motives, give rise to numerous actions in the form of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया कर्मामाजीं मग। संहरो आधवें जग। अथवा नवें चांग) अनुकरो॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā karmāmājīṃ maga| saṃharo ādhaveṃ jaga| athavā naveṃ cāṃga) anukaro|| 32||
verses.meaning: Then, in that very action, the entire world may be destroyed, or a new and good one may be created.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी कुमुद कैसेनि सुके । कैसें तें कमळ फांके । हीं दोन्हीं रवी न देखे। जयापरी॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī kumuda kaiseni suke | kaiseṃ teṃ kamaḻa phāṃke | hīṃ donhīṃ ravī na dekhe| jayāparī|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun does not perceive how the lotus withers or how it blossoms, so too is the nature of the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां बीजु वर्षोनि आभाळ। ठिकरिया आतो भूतळ । अथवा करूं शाडूबळ। प्रसन्नावृष्टी ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ bīju varṣoni ābhāḻa| ṭhikariyā āto bhūtaḻa | athavā karūṃ śāḍūbaḻa| prasannāvṛṣṭī || 34||
verses.meaning: Or, if the clouds were to rain down in fragments upon the earth, or if I were to make the rain of blessings fall upon the earth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तया दोहींतें जैसें । नेणिजेचि कां आकाशें । तेसा देहींच जो असे। विदेहदृष्टी॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tayā dohīṃteṃ jaiseṃ | neṇijeci kāṃ ākāśeṃ | tesā dehīṃca jo ase| videhadṛṣṭī|| 35||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky is unaware of the two (body and soul), so too is the one who, though dwelling in the body, possesses the vision of being bodiless.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो देहादिकीं चेष्टीं । घडतां मोडतां हे सृष्टी। न देखे स्वप्न दृष्टी। चेइला जैसा॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to dehādikīṃ ceṣṭīṃ | ghaḍatāṃ moḍatāṃ he sṛṣṭī| na dekhe svapna dṛṣṭī| ceilā jaisā|| 36||
verses.meaning: Just as a person who has awakened from a dream does not see the dream world, so too, the enlightened one does not perceive this creation, whether it is being formed or dissolved, in their body or in their actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं चामाचे डोळेवरी । जे देखती देहचिवरी। ते कौर तो व्यापारी । ऐसेंचि मानिती ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ cāmāce ḍoḻevarī | je dekhatī dehacivarī| te kaura to vyāpārī | aiseṃci mānitī || 37||
verses.meaning: Those who perceive only the physical body with their material eyes believe that Kaurava is merely a merchant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां तणाचा बाहुला । जो आगरामेरें ठेविला । तो साचचि राखता कोल्हा । मानिजे ना॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ taṇācā bāhulā | jo āgarāmereṃ ṭhevilā | to sācaci rākhatā kolhā | mānije nā|| 38||
verses.meaning: Just as a scarecrow, placed in a field, is not truly considered a protector by a fox.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पिसें नेसलें कां नागवें। हें लोकीं येऊनि जाणावें । ठाणोरियांचें मवावें। आणिकीं घाय॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: piseṃ nesaleṃ kāṃ nāgaveṃ| heṃ lokīṃ yeūni jāṇāveṃ | ṭhāṇoriyāṃceṃ mavāveṃ| āṇikīṃ ghāya|| 39||
verses.meaning: Whether one wears feathers or is naked, this should be understood by coming into the world. The blows of others should be endured.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां महासतीचे भोग। देखे कौर सकळ जग। परी ते आगी ना आंग। ना लोकु देखे॥ ४४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ mahāsatīce bhoga| dekhe kaura sakaḻa jaga| parī te āgī nā āṃga| nā loku dekhe|| 440||
verses.meaning: Just as the whole world sees the suffering of a great chaste woman, yet fire does not touch her body, nor does anyone see her being consumed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा स्वस्वरूपें उठिला। जो दृश्येंसीं द्रष्टा आटला। तो नेणे काय राहटला। इंद्रियग्रामु॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā svasvarūpeṃ uṭhilā| jo dṛśyeṃsīṃ draṣṭā āṭalā| to neṇe kāya rāhaṭalā| iṃdriyagrāmu|| 41||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when one awakens to their true self, and the seer merges with the seen, then what remains of the senses is unknown.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा थोरीं कल्लोळीं कल्लोळ साने। लोपतां तिरींचेनि जनें। एकीं एक गिळिलें हें मनें। मानिजे जऱ्ही ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā thorīṃ kalloḻīṃ kalloḻa sāne| lopatāṃ tirīṃceni janeṃ| ekīṃ eka giḻileṃ heṃ maneṃ| mānije jaṟhī || 42||
verses.meaning: When great waves engulf smaller ones, and people on the shore perceive that one has swallowed the other, even if it is believed in the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तऱही उदकाप्रति पाहीं॥ कोण ग्रसितसे काई । तैसें पूर्णा दुजें नाहीं। जें तो मारी ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṟahī udakāprati pāhīṃ|| koṇa grasitase kāī | taiseṃ pūrṇā dujeṃ nāhīṃ| jeṃ to mārī || 43||
verses.meaning: Look, who can consume water? Similarly, there is no other complete entity that can destroy the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुवर्णाचिया चंडिका। सुवर्णशूळेंचि देखा। सुवर्णाचिया महिखा। नाशु केला॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: suvarṇāciyā caṃḍikā| suvarṇaśūḻeṃci dekhā| suvarṇāciyā mahikhā| nāśu kelā|| 44||
verses.meaning: Just as a golden idol is destroyed by a golden spear, and a golden demon is vanquished by a golden buffalo, so too is the illusion of the world overcome by the very consciousness that creates it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो देवळवसिया कडा । व्यवहारु गमला फुडा। वांचूनि शूळ महिष चामुंडा । सुवर्णचि तें ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: to devaḻavasiyā kaḍā | vyavahāru gamalā phuḍā| vāṃcūni śūḻa mahiṣa cāmuṃḍā | suvarṇaci teṃ || 45||
verses.meaning: To the one who sees with true understanding, the world is clearly perceived as real. Otherwise, the trident, the buffalo, and the goddess Chamunda are all but gold.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं चित्रींचें जळ हुतांशु । तो दृष्टीचाचि आभासु। पटीं आगी बोलांशु । दोन्ही नाहीं ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ citrīṃceṃ jaḻa hutāṃśu | to dṛṣṭīcāci ābhāsu| paṭīṃ āgī bolāṃśu | donhī nāhīṃ || 46||
verses.meaning: Just as the water in a painting or the fire in a picture are mere illusions of sight, and there is no actual water or fire on the canvas, so too are many worldly perceptions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मुकताचें देह तैसें । हालत संस्कारवशें। तें देखोनि लोक पिसे। कर्ता म्हणती॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: mukatāceṃ deha taiseṃ | hālata saṃskāravaśeṃ| teṃ dekhoni loka pise| kartā mhaṇatī|| 47||
verses.meaning: The body of a liberated soul, though appearing to act, moves only by the force of past impressions. Seeing this, people, deluded, call them the doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि तयां 'करणेया आंतु। घडो तिहीं लोकां घातु। परी तेणें केला हे मातु । बोलों नये ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi tayāṃ 'karaṇeyā āṃtu| ghaḍo tihīṃ lokāṃ ghātu| parī teṇeṃ kelā he mātu | boloṃ naye || 48||
verses.meaning: And even if by their actions, the three worlds were to be destroyed, it should not be said that they caused it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा अंधारुचि देखावा तेजें। मग तो फेडी हें बोलिजे । तैसें ज्ञानिया नाहीं दुजें। जें तो मारी ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā aṃdhāruci dekhāvā tejeṃ| maga to pheḍī heṃ bolije | taiseṃ jñāniyā nāhīṃ dujeṃ| jeṃ to mārī || 49||
verses.meaning: Can darkness itself behold light? And then, can it dispel that light? Similarly, there is no 'other' for the enlightened one that he would need to conquer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तयाची बुद्धी । ४४२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी नेणे पापपुण्याची गंधी। गंगा मीनलिया नदी। बिटाळु जैसा॥ ४५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tayācī buddhī | 442 śrījñāneśvarī neṇe pāpapuṇyācī gaṃdhī| gaṃgā mīnaliyā nadī| biṭāḻu jaisā|| 450||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the intellect of such a person does not perceive the scent of sin or merit, just as a river merging with the Ganges does not become impure.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आगीसी आगी झगटळलिया। काय पोळे धनंजया । कीं शस्त्र रुपे आपणया । आपणचि ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āgīsī āgī jhagaṭaḻaliyā| kāya poḻe dhanaṃjayā | kīṃ śastra rupe āpaṇayā | āpaṇaci || 51||
verses.meaning: When fire clashes with fire, O Dhananjaya, what can it burn? Or can a weapon wound itself?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें आपणपयापरतें। जो नेणे क्रियाजातातें। तेथ काय लिंपबी बुद्धीतें। तयाचिये ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ āpaṇapayāparateṃ| jo neṇe kriyājātāteṃ| tetha kāya liṃpabī buddhīteṃ| tayāciye || 52||
verses.meaning: Similarly, for one who knows no action beyond their own self, what can bind their intellect?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि कार्य कर्ता क्रिया । हें स्वरूपचि जाहलें जया। नाहीं शरीरादिकीं तया। कर्मी बंधु ॥५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni kārya kartā kriyā | heṃ svarūpaci jāhaleṃ jayā| nāhīṃ śarīrādikīṃ tayā| karmī baṃdhu ||53||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for one who has realized that action and the doer are his very nature, there is no bondage through actions, even if performed through the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे कर्ता जीव विंदाणीं। काढूनि पांचही खाणी । घडित आहे करणीं। आउतीं दाहें ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: je kartā jīva viṃdāṇīṃ| kāḍhūni pāṃcahī khāṇī | ghaḍita āhe karaṇīṃ| āutīṃ dāheṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: The creator, the soul, with discerning wisdom, extracts from the five elements and shapes with ten instruments.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ न्यावो आणि अन्यावो। हा द्विविधु साधूनि आवो। उभवितां न लवी खेंबो। कर्मभुवनें ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha nyāvo āṇi anyāvo| hā dvividhu sādhūni āvo| ubhavitāṃ na lavī kheṃbo| karmabhuvaneṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: There, justice and injustice—these two, having been brought forth, do not cause any hindrance to the realm of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या थोराडा कीर कामा । विरजा नोहे आत्मा । परी म्हणसी हन उपक्रमा । हातु लावी॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā thorāḍā kīra kāmā | virajā nohe ātmā | parī mhaṇasī hana upakramā | hātu lāvī|| 56||
verses.meaning: This great task is not for the soul to be defiled. But you say, 'Let's begin this endeavor.'

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो साक्षी चिदरूपु। कर्मप्रवृत्तीचा संकल्पु। उठी तो कां निरोपु। आपणचि दे॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: to sākṣī cidarūpu| karmapravṛttīcā saṃkalpu| uṭhī to kāṃ niropu| āpaṇaci de|| 57||
verses.meaning: That Witness, the form of pure consciousness, does He Himself give the command when the resolve for action arises?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कर्मप्रवृत्तीहीलागीं। तया आयासु नाहीं आंगीं। जे प्रवृत्तीचेही उळिंगीं। लोकुचि आथी ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī karmapravṛttīhīlāgīṃ| tayā āyāsu nāhīṃ āṃgīṃ| je pravṛttīcehī uḻiṃgīṃ| lokuci āthī || 58||
verses.meaning: Therefore, even in the midst of worldly activities, there is no effort for him, as the world itself is but a reflection of his being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि आत्मयाचें केवळ) जो रूपचि जाहला निखिळ। तया नाहीं बंदिशाळ। कर्माची हे॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni ātmayāceṃ kevaḻa) jo rūpaci jāhalā nikhiḻa| tayā nāhīṃ baṃdiśāḻa| karmācī he|| 59||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for one who has become entirely the very form of the Self, there is no prison of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी अज्ञानाच्या पटीं। अन्यथा ज्ञानाचें चित्र उठी। तेथ चितारणी हे त्रिपुटी । प्रसिद्ध जे कां॥ ४६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī ajñānācyā paṭīṃ| anyathā jñānāceṃ citra uṭhī| tetha citāraṇī he tripuṭī | prasiddha je kāṃ|| 460||
verses.meaning: But on the canvas of ignorance, the picture of knowledge arises differently. There, the act of painting is the well-known triad (knower, known, knowing).

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें ज्ञान ज्ञाता ज्ञेय । हें जगाचें बीजत्रय। तें कर्माची निःसंदेह। प्रवृत्ति जाण॥६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ jñāna jñātā jñeya | heṃ jagāceṃ bījatraya| teṃ karmācī niḥsaṃdeha| pravṛtti jāṇa||61||
verses.meaning: That knowledge, the knower, and the known—these three are the seeds of the world. Know that they are undoubtedly the cause of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ययाचि गा त्रया। व्यक्‍ती वेगळालिया। आहकें धनंजया । करूं रूप॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yayāci gā trayā| vyak‍tī vegaḻāliyā| āhakeṃ dhanaṃjayā | karūṃ rūpa|| 62||
verses.meaning: Now, O Dhananjaya, I will describe the distinct forms of these three.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी जीवसूर्यबिंबाचे । रश्मी श्रोत्रादिकें पांचें । धांबोनि विषयपद्याचे । फोडिती मढ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī jīvasūryabiṃbāce | raśmī śrotrādikeṃ pāṃceṃ | dhāṃboni viṣayapadyāce | phoḍitī maḍha|| 63||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's rays illuminate the world, so too do the five senses, like rays from the sun of the soul, rush forth to pierce and reveal the objects of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं जीवनृपाचे वारु उपलाणें। घेऊनि इंद्रियांची केकाणें । विषयदेशींचें नागवणें। आणीत जे॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ jīvanṛpāce vāru upalāṇeṃ| gheūni iṃdriyāṃcī kekāṇeṃ | viṣayadeśīṃceṃ nāgavaṇeṃ| āṇīta je|| 64||
verses.meaning: Or, like a horseman of life, taking the reins of the senses, they bring back the plunder from the land of worldly pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो इहीं इंद्रियीं राहाटे। जें सुखदुःखेंसीं जीवा भेटे। तें सुषुप्तिकालीं बोहटे। जेथ ज्ञान ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso ihīṃ iṃdriyīṃ rāhāṭe| jeṃ sukhaduḥkheṃsīṃ jīvā bheṭe| teṃ suṣuptikālīṃ bohaṭe| jetha jñāna || 65||
verses.meaning: Let this be. The experience of pleasure and pain that the soul encounters through these senses, that very experience is dissolved in the state of deep sleep, where there is no knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया जीवा नांव ज्ञाता। आणि जें हें सांगितलें आतां। तेंचि एथ पंडुसुता। ज्ञान जाण॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā jīvā nāṃva jñātā| āṇi jeṃ heṃ sāṃgitaleṃ ātāṃ| teṃci etha paṃḍusutā| jñāna jāṇa|| 66||
verses.meaning: That very soul is called the Knower. And what has been explained now, O son of Pandu, know that to be Knowledge itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें अविद्येचिये पोटीं । उपजतखेंबो किरीटी। आपणयातें वांटी। तिहीं ठायीं ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ avidyeciye poṭīṃ | upajatakheṃbo kirīṭī| āpaṇayāteṃ vāṃṭī| tihīṃ ṭhāyīṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti (Arjuna)! That which is born from the womb of ignorance immediately divides itself into three parts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपुलिये धांवे पुढां। घालूनि ज्ञेयाचा गुंडा। उभारी मागिलीकडां । ज्ञातृत्वातें ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpuliye dhāṃve puḍhāṃ| ghālūni jñeyācā guṃḍā| ubhārī māgilīkaḍāṃ | jñātṛtvāteṃ || 68 ||
