verses.meaning: The seeker, having placed the object of knowledge (the knowable) before himself, then raises his own knowing faculty (the knower) to grasp it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग ज्ञातया ज्ञेया दोघां। तो नांदणुकेचा बगा। माजीं जालेनि पैं गा। बाहे जेणें ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga jñātayā jñeyā doghāṃ| to nāṃdaṇukecā bagā| mājīṃ jāleni paiṃ gā| bāhe jeṇeṃ || 69||
verses.meaning: Then, the Knower and the Known, both, become the very dwelling place, and from within this dwelling, the Knower emerges.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ठाकूनि ज्ञेयाची शिंव। पुरे जयाची धांव । सकळ पदार्था नांव । सूतसे जें॥ ४७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ṭhākūni jñeyācī śiṃva| pure jayācī dhāṃva | sakaḻa padārthā nāṃva | sūtase jeṃ|| 470||
verses.meaning: That which, having reached the boundary of the knowable, exhausts its own reach; that which gives names to all objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें गा सामान्यज्ञान। या बोला नाहीं आन । ज्ञेयाचेंही चिन्ह। आइक आतां॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ gā sāmānyajñāna| yā bolā nāhīṃ āna | jñeyāceṃhī cinha| āika ātāṃ|| 71||
verses.meaning: That indeed is common knowledge; there is no other way to describe it. Now listen to the characteristics of the knowable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी शब्द स्पर्शु। रूप गंध रसु। हा पंचविध आभासु । ज्ञेयाचा जो॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī śabda sparśu| rūpa gaṃdha rasu| hā paṃcavidha ābhāsu | jñeyācā jo|| 72||
verses.meaning: Thus, sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—these five kinds of appearances are of the knowable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें एकेंचि चूतफळें । इंद्रियां वेगवेगळें । रसें वर्णे परिमळें। भेटिजे स्पर्शे ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ ekeṃci cūtaphaḻeṃ | iṃdriyāṃ vegavegaḻeṃ | raseṃ varṇe parimaḻeṃ| bheṭije sparśe || 73||
verses.meaning: Just as a single mango fruit, though one, is experienced differently by each sense: its taste by the tongue, its color by the eyes, its fragrance by the nose, and its touch by the skin.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें ज्ञेय तरी एकसरें। परी ज्ञान इंद्रियद्वारें। घे म्हणौनि प्रकारें। पांचें जाळें॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ jñeya tarī ekasareṃ| parī jñāna iṃdriyadvāreṃ| ghe mhaṇauni prakāreṃ| pāṃceṃ jāḻeṃ|| 74||
verses.meaning: The knowable is indeed one and uniform, but knowledge is acquired through the senses. Therefore, it is perceived in five different ways, like a net with five meshes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि समुद्री बोघाचें जाणें। सरे लाणीपासीं धांवणें । कां फळीं सरे वाढणें । सस्याचें जेवीं ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi samudrī boghāceṃ jāṇeṃ| sare lāṇīpāsīṃ dhāṃvaṇeṃ | kāṃ phaḻīṃ sare vāḍhaṇeṃ | sasyāceṃ jevīṃ || 75 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a ship's journey ends at the shore, or a runner's race concludes at the finish line, or a plant's growth culminates in its fruit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें इंद्रियांच्या बाहवटीं। धांवतया ज्ञाना जेथ ठी। होय तें गा किरीटी। विषय ज्ञेय ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ iṃdriyāṃcyā bāhavaṭīṃ| dhāṃvatayā jñānā jetha ṭhī| hoya teṃ gā kirīṭī| viṣaya jñeya || 76||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, just as the senses run outwards, that upon which knowledge rests, that is the object of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं ज्ञातया ज्ञाना ज्ञेया। तिहीं रूप केलें धनंजया । हे त्रिविध सर्व क्रिया-। प्रवृत्ति जाण ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ jñātayā jñānā jñeyā| tihīṃ rūpa keleṃ dhanaṃjayā | he trividha sarva kriyā-| pravṛtti jāṇa || 77||
verses.meaning: Thus, the knower, the knowledge, and the known – these three, O Dhananjaya, constitute all activity and its inclination.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे शब्दादि विषय। हें पंचविध जें ज्ञेय। तेंचि प्रिय कां अप्रिय । एकेपरीचें ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: je śabdādi viṣaya| heṃ paṃcavidha jeṃ jñeya| teṃci priya kāṃ apriya | ekeparīceṃ || 78 ||
verses.meaning: The objects of the senses, such as sound, which are the fivefold knowable, are either pleasant or unpleasant, but they are all of one kind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ज्ञान मोटकें ज्ञातया । दावी ना जंब धनंजया । तंव स्वीकारा कीं त्यजावया । प्रवर्तेचि तो॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jñāna moṭakeṃ jñātayā | dāvī nā jaṃba dhanaṃjayā | taṃva svīkārā kīṃ tyajāvayā | pravarteci to|| 79||
verses.meaning: Knowledge, though it may be small, reveals itself to the knower, O Dhananjaya. Then, whether to accept it or reject it, that choice arises for him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मीनातें देखोनि बकु । जैसा निधानातें रंकु । कां स्त्री देखोनि कामुकु । प्रवृत्ति धरी ॥ ४८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī mīnāteṃ dekhoni baku | jaisā nidhānāteṃ raṃku | kāṃ strī dekhoni kāmuku | pravṛtti dharī || 480||
verses.meaning: Just as a heron, seeing fish, or a pauper, seeing treasure, or a lustful man, seeing a woman, becomes inclined towards them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें खालारां धांवे पाणी । भ्रमर पुष्पाचिये घाणीं । नाना सुटला सांजवणीं। वत्सुचि पां॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ khālārāṃ dhāṃve pāṇī | bhramara puṣpāciye ghāṇīṃ | nānā suṭalā sāṃjavaṇīṃ| vatsuci pāṃ|| 89||
verses.meaning: Just as water flows downwards, the bumblebee rushes to the fragrance of a flower, or a calf, freed in the evening, runs to its mother.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा स्वर्गाची उर्वशी । ऐकोनि जेवीं माणुसीं । वराता लावबीजती आकाशीं । यागांचिया ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā svargācī urvaśī | aikoni jevīṃ māṇusīṃ | varātā lāvabījatī ākāśīṃ | yāgāṃciyā || 82||
verses.meaning: Just as humans, upon hearing of Urvashi of heaven, would eagerly desire to attain her through sacrifices performed in the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं पारिवा जैसा किरीटी। चढला नभाचिये पोटीं। पारवी देखोनि लोटी। आंगचि सगळें ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ pārivā jaisā kirīṭī| caḍhalā nabhāciye poṭīṃ| pāravī dekhoni loṭī| āṃgaci sagaḻeṃ || 83||
verses.meaning: Just as a hawk, O Arjuna, soaring high in the sky, upon spotting a dove, plunges its entire body down to seize it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें ना घनगर्जनासरिसा। मयूर बोबांडे आकाशा । ज्ञाता ज्ञेय देखोनि तैसा । धांबचि घे॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ nā ghanagarjanāsarisā| mayūra bobāṃḍe ākāśā | jñātā jñeya dekhoni taisā | dhāṃbaci ghe|| 84||
verses.meaning: Just as a peacock, hearing the thunder, cries out to the sky, so too the knower, seeing the knowable, becomes still.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ज्ञान ज्ञेय ज्ञाता। हे त्रिविध गा पंडुसुता । होयचि कर्मा समस्तां । प्रवृत्ति येथ ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jñāna jñeya jñātā| he trividha gā paṃḍusutā | hoyaci karmā samastāṃ | pravṛtti yetha || 85 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O son of Pandu, the knowledge, the knowable, and the knower—these three—are indeed the impetus for all actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तेंचि ज्ञेय विपायें । जरी ज्ञातयातें प्रिय होये। तरी भोगावया न साहे। क्षणही विलंबु॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teṃci jñeya vipāyeṃ | jarī jñātayāteṃ priya hoye| tarī bhogāvayā na sāhe| kṣaṇahī vilaṃbu|| 86||
verses.meaning: But if that very knowable (Brahman) becomes dear to the knower, then even a moment's delay in experiencing it becomes unbearable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी अवचटें। तेंचि विरुद्ध होऊनि भेटे । तरी युगांत वाटे । सांडावया ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī avacaṭeṃ| teṃci viruddha hoūni bheṭe | tarī yugāṃta vāṭe | sāṃḍāvayā || 87||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, if by chance, that very thing turns adverse and confronts you, then even the end of an eon seems too short to abandon it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्याळा कां हारा। वरपडा जालेया नरा। हरिखु आणि दरारा। सरसाचि उठी॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: vyāḻā kāṃ hārā| varapaḍā jāleyā narā| harikhu āṇi darārā| sarasāci uṭhī|| 88||
verses.meaning: When a snake appears to a person as a garland, both joy and fear arise simultaneously.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ज्ञेय प्रियाप्रियें। देखिलेनि ज्ञातया होये। मग त्याग स्वीकारीं वाहे । व्यापारातें ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jñeya priyāpriyeṃ| dekhileni jñātayā hoye| maga tyāga svīkārīṃ vāhe | vyāpārāteṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Just as the knower, upon perceiving what is desirable and undesirable, then engages in the actions of acceptance or rejection.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ रागी प्रतिमल्लाचा । गोसांबी सर्वदळाचा । रथु सांडूनि पायांचा। होय जैसा॥ ४९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha rāgī pratimallācā | gosāṃbī sarvadaḻācā | rathu sāṃḍūni pāyāṃcā| hoya jaisā|| 490||
verses.meaning: There, the charioteer, enraged at his opponent, abandons his chariot and fights on foot, like a warrior who has lost his mount.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ज्ञातेपणें जें असे तें ये कर्ता ऐसिये दशे। जेवितें बेसलें जेसें। रंधन करूं॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jñātepaṇeṃ jeṃ ase teṃ ye kartā aisiye daśe| jeviteṃ besaleṃ jeseṃ| raṃdhana karūṃ||91||
verses.meaning: Just as a knowledgeable person, when it comes to action, is like one who sits down to eat after having cooked the meal himself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां भंवरेंचि केला मळा। बरकलुचि झाला अंकसळा। नाना देवो रिगाला देउळा-। चिया कामा॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ bhaṃvareṃci kelā maḻā| barakaluci jhālā aṃkasaḻā| nānā devo rigālā deuḻā-| ciyā kāmā|| 92||
verses.meaning: Or, as if a garden was made by bees, or a temple was built by gods, so too did the divine enter into the work of the temple.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा ज्ञेयाचिया हांवा। ज्ञाता इंद्रियांचा मेळावा । डड श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी राहाटवी तेथ पांडवा । कर्ता होय ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā jñeyāciyā hāṃvā| jñātā iṃdriyāṃcā meḻāvā | ḍaḍa śrījñāneśvarī rāhāṭavī tetha pāṃḍavā | kartā hoya || 93 ||
verses.meaning: Similarly, for the sake of the knowable, the knower, who is the assembly of the senses, becomes the doer, O Pandava, in the workings of Shri Dnyaneshwari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आपण होउनी कर्ता । ज्ञाना आणी करणता । तेथें ज्ञेयचि स्वभावतां। कार्य होय ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi āpaṇa hounī kartā | jñānā āṇī karaṇatā | tetheṃ jñeyaci svabhāvatāṃ| kārya hoya || 94||
verses.meaning: And when the Self becomes the doer, bringing knowledge into action, then the knowable naturally becomes the effect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा ज्ञानाचिये निजगती । पालटु पडे गा सुमती । डोळ्यांची शोभा रातीं । पालटे जैसी ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jñānāciye nijagatī | pālaṭu paḍe gā sumatī | ḍoḻyāṃcī śobhā rātīṃ | pālaṭe jaisī || 95||
verses.meaning: Just as the beauty of the eyes changes at night, so too does the true nature of knowledge undergo a transformation, O wise one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां अदृष्ट जालिया उदासु । पालटे श्रीमंताचा विलासु । पुनिवेपाठीं शीतांशु । पालटे जैसा॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ adṛṣṭa jāliyā udāsu | pālaṭe śrīmaṃtācā vilāsu | punivepāṭhīṃ śītāṃśu | pālaṭe jaisā|| 96||
verses.meaning: Just as an unseen misfortune can overturn the splendor of a rich man, so too does the moon's coolness diminish after the full moon.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा चाळितां करणें । ज्ञाता वेष्टिजे कर्तेपणें। तेथिंचीं तियें लक्षणें । ऐक आतां ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā cāḻitāṃ karaṇeṃ | jñātā veṣṭije kartepaṇeṃ| tethiṃcīṃ tiyeṃ lakṣaṇeṃ | aika ātāṃ || 97||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when the senses are engaged, the Knower (the Self) becomes enveloped by the sense of doership. Now, listen to the characteristics of that state.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी बुद्धि आणि मन। चित्त अहंकार हन। हें चतुर्विध चिन्ह। अंतःकरणाचें॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī buddhi āṇi mana| citta ahaṃkāra hana| heṃ caturvidha cinha| aṃtaḥkaraṇāceṃ|| 98||
verses.meaning: Thus, intellect (buddhi), mind (manas), consciousness (chitta), and ego (ahamkara) - these four are the distinguishing characteristics of the inner instrument (antahkarana).

verses.shloka_devanagari: बाह्य त्वचा श्रवण। चक्षु रसना घ्राण । हें पंचविध जाण । इंद्रियें गा॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: bāhya tvacā śravaṇa| cakṣu rasanā ghrāṇa | heṃ paṃcavidha jāṇa | iṃdriyeṃ gā|| 99||
verses.meaning: The outer skin, hearing, sight, taste, and smell—these five are known as the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ आंतुलें तंव करणें। कर्ता कर्तव्या घे उमाणें। मग तैं जरी जाणें। सुखा येतें ॥ ५००॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha āṃtuleṃ taṃva karaṇeṃ| kartā kartavyā ghe umāṇeṃ| maga taiṃ jarī jāṇeṃ| sukhā yeteṃ || 500||
verses.meaning: Then, the inner faculties, the doer, and the deed are all measured. Only then does one experience true happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी बाहेरीलें तियेंही । चश्षुरादिकें दाहाही । उठौनि लवलाही । व्यापारा सूये ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī bāherīleṃ tiyeṃhī | caśṣurādikeṃ dāhāhī | uṭhauni lavalāhī | vyāpārā sūye || 1||
verses.meaning: Then, the ten external senses, such as the eyes, quickly rise and engage in their respective activities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तो इंद्रियकदंबु। करविजे तंब राबु। जंव कर्तव्याचा लाभु। हातासि ये॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga to iṃdriyakadaṃbu| karavije taṃba rābu| jaṃva kartavyācā lābhu| hātāsi ye|| 2||
verses.meaning: Then that multitude of senses is made to work diligently until the fruit of action is attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना तें कर्तव्य जरी दुःखें। फळेल ऐसें देखे। तो लावी त्यागमुखें। तियें दाहाही ॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā teṃ kartavya jarī duḥkheṃ| phaḻela aiseṃ dekhe| to lāvī tyāgamukheṃ| tiyeṃ dāhāhī || 3||
verses.meaning: Even if that action, though painful, appears to bear fruit, he renounces it through detachment, dedicating it to the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग फिटे दुःखाचा ठावो । तंव राहाटवी रात्रिदिवो। विकणवातें कां राबो। जयापरी॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga phiṭe duḥkhācā ṭhāvo | taṃva rāhāṭavī rātridivo| vikaṇavāteṃ kāṃ rābo| jayāparī|| 4||
verses.meaning: Then the abode of sorrow vanishes, just as the day and night revolve, or as the wind blows, or as the sun shines.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेनि त्याग स्वीकारीं। वाहातां इंद्रियांची धुरी । ज्ञातयातें अवधारीं। कर्ता म्हणिपे॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseni tyāga svīkārīṃ| vāhātāṃ iṃdriyāṃcī dhurī | jñātayāteṃ avadhārīṃ| kartā mhaṇipe|| 5||
verses.meaning: In the same way, by accepting renunciation, and by controlling the senses, the one who knows is considered the doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कर्तयाच्या सर्व कर्मी । आउतांचिया परी क्षमी । म्हणौनि इंद्रियांतें आम्ही । करणें म्हणों ॥ ६ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kartayācyā sarva karmī | āutāṃciyā parī kṣamī | mhaṇauni iṃdriyāṃteṃ āmhī | karaṇeṃ mhaṇoṃ || 6 ||
verses.meaning: And in all actions of the doer, the senses are like instruments, hence we call the senses 'instruments'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हेचि करणेंवरी। कर्ता क्रिया ज्या उभारी । तिया व्यापे तें अवधारीं। कर्म एथ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi heci karaṇeṃvarī| kartā kriyā jyā ubhārī | tiyā vyāpe teṃ avadhārīṃ| karma etha|| 7||
verses.meaning: And whatever the doer undertakes through action, that which is pervaded by it is known as karma here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सोनाराचिया बुद्धी लेणें। व्यापे चंद्रकरीं चांदणें। कां व्यापे वेल्हाळपणें । वेली जैसी ॥ ८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: sonārāciyā buddhī leṇeṃ| vyāpe caṃdrakarīṃ cāṃdaṇeṃ| kāṃ vyāpe velhāḻapaṇeṃ | velī jaisī || 8 ||
verses.meaning: Just as the gold ornament is pervaded by the goldsmith's intellect, or moonlight pervades the moon, or a creeper pervades with its grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना प्रभा व्यापे प्रकाशु। गोडिया इक्षुरसु। हें असो अवकाशु। आकाशीं जैसा॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā prabhā vyāpe prakāśu| goḍiyā ikṣurasu| heṃ aso avakāśu| ākāśīṃ jaisā|| 9||
verses.meaning: Just as various lights pervade the illumination, or the sweetness pervades sugarcane juice, or space pervades the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें कर्तयाचिया क्रिया । व्यापले जें धनंजया। तें कर्म गा बोलावया । आन नाहीं ॥ ५१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ kartayāciyā kriyā | vyāpale jeṃ dhanaṃjayā| teṃ karma gā bolāvayā | āna nāhīṃ || 510||
verses.meaning: Just as, O Dhananjaya, the action of the doer is pervaded, that alone is called Karma; there is no other way to describe it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं कर्ता कर्म करण या तिहींचेंही लक्षण । सांगितलें तुज विचक्षण-। शिरोमणी ॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ kartā karma karaṇa yā tihīṃceṃhī lakṣaṇa | sāṃgitaleṃ tuja vicakṣaṇa-| śiromaṇī || 11||
verses.meaning: Thus, the characteristics of the doer, the action, and the instrument have been explained to you, O crest-jewel among the discerning.

verses.shloka_devanagari: 'एथ ज्ञाता ज्ञान ज्ञेय। हें कर्माचें प्रवृत्तित्रय। तैसेंचि कर्ता करण कार्य । हा कर्मसंचयो ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: 'etha jñātā jñāna jñeya| heṃ karmāceṃ pravṛttitraya| taiseṃci kartā karaṇa kārya | hā karmasaṃcayo || 12||
verses.meaning: Here, the knower, knowledge, and the known are the three impulses of action. Similarly, the doer, the means, and the deed are the accumulation of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वन्हीं ठेविला असे धूमु। आथी बीजीं जेबीं द्रुमु। कां मनीं जोडे कामु । सदा जैसा ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: vanhīṃ ṭhevilā ase dhūmu| āthī bījīṃ jebīṃ drumu| kāṃ manīṃ joḍe kāmu | sadā jaisā || 13||
verses.meaning: Just as smoke is inherent in fire, or a tree is inherent in its seed, or desire is always present in the mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा कर्ता क्रिया करणीं। कर्माचें आहे जिंतवणीं। सोनें जैसें खाणी । सुवर्णाचिये ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā kartā kriyā karaṇīṃ| karmāceṃ āhe jiṃtavaṇīṃ| soneṃ jaiseṃ khāṇī | suvarṇāciye || 14||
verses.meaning: Just as gold is inherently present in a mine, so too is the doer (Karta) inherently present in the act of doing (Kriya) and the instrument (Karani), and is the very essence of the action (Karma).

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि हें कार्य मी कर्ता । ऐसें आथि जेथ पंडुसुता । तेथ आत्मा दूरी समस्तां । क्रियांपासीं ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni heṃ kārya mī kartā | aiseṃ āthi jetha paṃḍusutā | tetha ātmā dūrī samastāṃ | kriyāṃpāsīṃ || 95||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O son of Pandu, where there is the thought, "I am the doer of this action," there the Self is entirely distant from all actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यालागीं पुढतपुढती। आत्मा वेगळाचि सुमती। आतां असो हे किती। जाणतासि तूं॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yālāgīṃ puḍhatapuḍhatī| ātmā vegaḻāci sumatī| ātāṃ aso he kitī| jāṇatāsi tūṃ|| 16||
verses.meaning: Therefore, again and again, the Self is indeed distinct, O wise one. But let this be; how much more do you need to know?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी सांगितलें जें ज्ञान। कर्म कर्ता हन। ते तिन्ही तिहीं ठायीं भिन्न । गुणीं आहाती ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī sāṃgitaleṃ jeṃ jñāna| karma kartā hana| te tinhī tihīṃ ṭhāyīṃ bhinna | guṇīṃ āhātī || 17||
verses.meaning: But the knowledge that has been spoken of, the action, and the doer—these three are distinct in their respective places, residing within the gunas (qualities of nature).

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ज्ञाना कर्मा कर्तया। पातेजों नये धनंजया । जे दोनी बांधती सोडावया। एकचि प्रौढ॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jñānā karmā kartayā| pātejoṃ naye dhanaṃjayā | je donī bāṃdhatī soḍāvayā| ekaci prauḍha|| 18||
verses.meaning: Therefore, O Dhananjaya, one should not rely on knowledge, action, or the doer, for these two (knowledge and action) bind, and only one (the Self) is capable of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें सात्त्विक ठाउवें होये । जे गुणभेदु सांगों पाहे। जो सांख्यशास्त्रीं आहे। उवाइला॥१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ sāttvika ṭhāuveṃ hoye | je guṇabhedu sāṃgoṃ pāhe| jo sāṃkhyaśāstrīṃ āhe| uvāilā||19||
verses.meaning: That which is considered Sattvic is what seeks to explain the distinctions of the Gunas, as expounded in the Samkhya Shastra.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें विचारक्षीरसमुद्र। स्वबोधकुमुदिनीचंद्र । ज्ञानडोळसां नरेंद्र । शास्त्रांचा जें॥ ५२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ vicārakṣīrasamudra| svabodhakumudinīcaṃdra | jñānaḍoḻasāṃ nareṃdra | śāstrāṃcā jeṃ|| 520||
verses.meaning: That which is the ocean of milk of deliberation, the moon for the kumudini flower of self-realization, the king among the wise, and the essence of all scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौं प्रकृतिपुरुष दोनीं। मिसळली दिवोरजनीं। तियें निवडितां त्रिभुवनीं। मार्तंडु जें॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauṃ prakṛtipuruṣa donīṃ| misaḻalī divorajanīṃ| tiyeṃ nivaḍitāṃ tribhuvanīṃ| mārtaṃḍu jeṃ|| 21||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun separates day and night, so too does the spiritual seeker distinguish between Prakriti (nature) and Purusha (consciousness) in the three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ अपारा मोहराशी । तत्त्वांच्या मापी चोविसीं । उगाणा घेऊनि परेशीं। सुरवाडिजे॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha apārā moharāśī | tattvāṃcyā māpī covisīṃ | ugāṇā gheūni pareśīṃ| suravāḍije|| 22||
verses.meaning: Where the immeasurable wealth of the universe, measured by the twenty-four principles, is offered to the Supreme Lord as a tribute.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना तें सांख्यशास्त्र। पढे जयाचें स्तोत्र । तें गुणभेदचरित्र । ऐसें आहे॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā teṃ sāṃkhyaśāstra| paḍhe jayāceṃ stotra | teṃ guṇabhedacaritra | aiseṃ āhe|| 23||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, that Samkhya scripture, whose praise is sung, is indeed the narrative of the distinctions of the Gunas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे आपुलेनि आंगिकें । त्रिविधपणाचेनि अंकें । दृश्यजात तितुकें । अंकित केलें॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: je āpuleni āṃgikeṃ | trividhapaṇāceni aṃkeṃ | dṛśyajāta titukeṃ | aṃkita keleṃ|| 24||
verses.meaning: By its own inherent nature, marked by the three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas), it has imprinted its form upon all that is visible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं सत्त्वरजतमा। तिहींची एवढी असे महिमा । जे त्रैविध्य आदी ब्रह्मा। अंतीं कृमी॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ sattvarajatamā| tihīṃcī evaḍhī ase mahimā | je traividhya ādī brahmā| aṃtīṃ kṛmī|| 25||
verses.meaning: Thus, the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas have such great power that they manifest from the very beginning of creation, even in Brahma, down to the smallest worm at the end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी विश्‍वींची आघवी मांदी । जेणें भेदलेनि गुणभेदीं। पडिली ते तंव आदी । ज्ञान सांगों ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī viś‍vīṃcī āghavī māṃdī | jeṇeṃ bhedaleni guṇabhedīṃ| paḍilī te taṃva ādī | jñāna sāṃgoṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: But the entire universe, which is divided by the distinctions of qualities, has its origin in that knowledge which I shall now explain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे दिठी जरी चोख कौजे। तरी भलतेंही चोख सुजे। तैसें ज्ञानें शुद्धे लाहिजे। सर्वही शुद्ध ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: je diṭhī jarī cokha kauje| tarī bhalateṃhī cokha suje| taiseṃ jñāneṃ śuddhe lāhije| sarvahī śuddha || 27||
verses.meaning: Just as a pure eye perceives everything purely, so too, with pure knowledge, everything is attained in its pure form.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तें सात्त्विक ज्ञान । आतां सांगों दे अवधान । कैवल्यगुणनिधान। श्रीकृष्ण म्हणे ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni teṃ sāttvika jñāna | ātāṃ sāṃgoṃ de avadhāna | kaivalyaguṇanidhāna| śrīkṛṣṇa mhaṇe || 28||
verses.meaning: Therefore, that Sattvic knowledge, now listen attentively, said Shri Krishna, the treasure house of the qualities leading to liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अर्जुना गा तें फुडें। सात्त्विक ज्ञान चोखडें । जयाच्या उदयीं ज्ञेय बुडे । ज्ञातेनिसीं ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī arjunā gā teṃ phuḍeṃ| sāttvika jñāna cokhaḍeṃ | jayācyā udayīṃ jñeya buḍe | jñātenisīṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, that pure Sattvic knowledge, upon whose dawn the knowable merges with the knower.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा सूर्य न देखे आंधारें। सरिता नेणिजती सागरें। कां कवळिलिया न धरे। आत्मच्छाया॥ ५३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā sūrya na dekhe āṃdhāreṃ| saritā neṇijatī sāgareṃ| kāṃ kavaḻiliyā na dhare| ātmacchāyā|| 530||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun does not perceive darkness, rivers do not recognize the ocean, or one cannot grasp their own shadow, so too is the nature of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयापरी जया ज्ञाना। शिवादि तृणावसाना। इया भूतव्यक्ति भिन्ना। नाडळती ॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāparī jayā jñānā| śivādi tṛṇāvasānā| iyā bhūtavyakti bhinnā| nāḍaḻatī || 31||
verses.meaning: In the same way, for one who possesses such knowledge, all these diverse manifestations of beings, from Shiva down to a blade of grass, do not appear as separate entities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेसें हातें चित्र पाहातां। होय पाणियें मीठ धुतां। कां चेवोनि स्वप्ना येतां। जैसें होय॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeseṃ hāteṃ citra pāhātāṃ| hoya pāṇiyeṃ mīṭha dhutāṃ| kāṃ cevoni svapnā yetāṃ| jaiseṃ hoya|| 32||
verses.meaning: Just as a picture seen by hand, or salt dissolving in water, or a dream upon waking, so it becomes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें ज्ञानें जेणें। करितां ज्ञातव्यातें पाहाणें। जाणता ना जाणणें। जाणावें उरे॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jñāneṃ jeṇeṃ| karitāṃ jñātavyāteṃ pāhāṇeṃ| jāṇatā nā jāṇaṇeṃ| jāṇāveṃ ure|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as by knowledge, when one perceives the knowable, the knower and the act of knowing cease to exist, only the known remains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सोनें आटूनि लेणीं।॥ न काढिती आपुलिया आयणी। कां तरंग न घेपती पाणी। गाळूनि जैसें ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ soneṃ āṭūni leṇīṃ||| na kāḍhitī āpuliyā āyaṇī| kāṃ taraṃga na ghepatī pāṇī| gāḻūni jaiseṃ || 34||
verses.meaning: Just as ornaments, once melted, do not lose their inherent gold, or waves, when filtered, do not lose their water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी जया ज्ञानाचिया हाता। न लगेचि दृश्यपथा। तें ज्ञान जाण सर्वथा ४४६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी सात्त्विक गा॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī jayā jñānāciyā hātā| na lageci dṛśyapathā| teṃ jñāna jāṇa sarvathā 446 śrījñāneśvarī sāttvika gā|| 35||
verses.meaning: Similarly, that knowledge which does not perceive any object through the senses is indeed true knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आरिसा पाहों जातां कोडें । जैसें पाहातेंचि कां रिगे पुढें। तैसें ज्ञेय लोटोनि पडे । ज्ञाताचि जें॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: ārisā pāhoṃ jātāṃ koḍeṃ | jaiseṃ pāhāteṃci kāṃ rige puḍheṃ| taiseṃ jñeya loṭoni paḍe | jñātāci jeṃ|| 36||
verses.meaning: When one goes to look in a mirror, just as the seer itself appears before them, so too the knowable recedes, and only the knower remains.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पुढती तेंचि सात्त्विक ज्ञान। जें मोक्षलक्ष्मीचें भुवन। हें असो ऐक चिन्ह। राजसाचें ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: puḍhatī teṃci sāttvika jñāna| jeṃ mokṣalakṣmīceṃ bhuvana| heṃ aso aika cinha| rājasāceṃ || 37||
verses.meaning: Furthermore, that very knowledge is sattvic, which is the abode of the wealth of liberation. Let this be; now listen to the characteristics of the rajasic.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी पार्था परियेस। तें ज्ञान गा राजस। जे भेदाची कांस। धरूनि चाले॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī pārthā pariyesa| teṃ jñāna gā rājasa| je bhedācī kāṃsa| dharūni cāle|| 38||
verses.meaning: Therefore, Arjuna, listen. That knowledge is indeed Rajasic, which proceeds by holding onto the distinction of difference.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विचित्रता भूतांचिया। आपण आंतोनि ठिकरिया। बहु चकै ज्ञातया। आणिली जेणें ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: vicitratā bhūtāṃciyā| āpaṇa āṃtoni ṭhikariyā| bahu cakai jñātayā| āṇilī jeṇeṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: The one who, from within, brought forth the wondrous diversity of beings, astonishing the knower.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें साचा रूपाआड। घालूनि विसराचें 'कवाड। मग स्वप्नाचे काबाड। ओपी निद्रा॥ ५४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ sācā rūpāāḍa| ghālūni visarāceṃ 'kavāḍa| maga svapnāce kābāḍa| opī nidrā|| 540||
verses.meaning: Just as sleep, by placing the door of forgetfulness over the true form, then presents the illusion of a dream.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें स्वज्ञानाचिये 'पौळी-। बाहेरि मिथ्या महीं खळीं । तिहीं अवस्थांचिया वह्याळी । दावी जें जीवा॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ svajñānāciye 'pauḻī-| bāheri mithyā mahīṃ khaḻīṃ | tihīṃ avasthāṃciyā vahyāḻī | dāvī jeṃ jīvā|| 41||
verses.meaning: Just as outside the gateway of self-knowledge, in the illusory world, it is the three states of waking, dream, and deep sleep that manifest to the individual soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अलंकारपणे झांकलें। बाळा सोनें कां वायां गेलें। तेसें नामीं रूपीं दुरावलें। अद्वैत जया॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: alaṃkārapaṇe jhāṃkaleṃ| bāḻā soneṃ kāṃ vāyāṃ geleṃ| teseṃ nāmīṃ rūpīṃ durāvaleṃ| advaita jayā|| 42||
verses.meaning: Just as gold, when fashioned into ornaments, is not lost or wasted, so too the non-dual reality (Brahman) is not diminished or obscured by taking on names and forms.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अवतरली गाडग्यां घडां। पृथ्वी अनोळख जाली मूढां। वन्हि जाला कानडा । दीपत्वासाठी॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: avataralī gāḍagyāṃ ghaḍāṃ| pṛthvī anoḻakha jālī mūḍhāṃ| vanhi jālā kānaḍā | dīpatvāsāṭhī|| 43||
verses.meaning: The earth became unknown to the ignorant, like a pot descending into a well. Fire became a mystery, for the sake of light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां वस्त्रपणाचेनि आरोपें। मूर्खाप्रति तंतु हारपे। नाना मुग्धा पटु लोपे। दाऊनि चित्र॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ vastrapaṇāceni āropeṃ| mūrkhāprati taṃtu hārape| nānā mugdhā paṭu lope| dāūni citra|| 44||
verses.meaning: Just as a fool loses sight of the threads because of the appearance of the cloth, or as a simpleton loses sight of the fabric when shown a painting on it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेशी जया ज्ञाना। जाणोनि भूतव्यक्‍ती भिन्ना। ऐक्यबोधाची भावना । निमोनि गेली ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: teśī jayā jñānā| jāṇoni bhūtavyak‍tī bhinnā| aikyabodhācī bhāvanā | nimoni gelī || 45||
verses.meaning: Similarly, for one who knows that all beings are distinct manifestations, the feeling of oneness with all creation has vanished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग इंधनीं भेदला अनळु। फुलांबवरी परिमळु । कां जळभेदें शकलु। चंद्रु जैसा ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga iṃdhanīṃ bhedalā anaḻu| phulāṃbavarī parimaḻu | kāṃ jaḻabhedeṃ śakalu| caṃdru jaisā || 46||
verses.meaning: Just as fire, though one, appears divided by the fuel it consumes; or fragrance, though one, seems to be in the flowers; or the moon, though one, appears fragmented in different bodies of water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसे पदार्थभेद बहुवस । जाणोनि लहान थोर वेष। आंतलें तें राजस। ज्ञान येथ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taise padārthabheda bahuvasa | jāṇoni lahāna thora veṣa| āṃtaleṃ teṃ rājasa| jñāna yetha|| 47||
verses.meaning: Just as one recognizes the various forms and sizes of objects, so too, the inner knowledge is indeed 'rajasic' (active, passionate).

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां तामसाचेंहि लिंग। सांगेन तें बोळख चांग) डावलावया मातंग-। सदन जेसें॥ ४८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ tāmasāceṃhi liṃga| sāṃgena teṃ boḻakha cāṃga) ḍāvalāvayā mātaṃga-| sadana jeseṃ|| 48 ||
verses.meaning: Now, I will also explain the characteristics of the Tamasic (ignorant) state, which is like a house of an untouchable (Matanga) being set on fire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी किरीटी जें ज्ञान । हिंडे विधीचेनि वस्त्रेंहीन । श्रुति पाठमोरी नग्न । म्हणौनि तया॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī kirīṭī jeṃ jñāna | hiṃḍe vidhīceni vastreṃhīna | śruti pāṭhamorī nagna | mhaṇauni tayā|| 49||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the knowledge that adorns Arjuna, which moves without the covering of creation, and which the Vedas turn their backs on, naked, is for him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरींही शास्त्र बटिकरीं। जें निंदेचे विटाळवरी। बोळविलेंसे डोंगरी । म्लेंच्छधर्माच्या ॥ ५५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerīṃhī śāstra baṭikarīṃ| jeṃ niṃdece viṭāḻavarī| boḻavileṃse ḍoṃgarī | mleṃcchadharmācyā || 550||
verses.meaning: Other scriptures, like maidservants, were sent to the mountains of Mleccha dharma, tainted by condemnation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें गा ज्ञान ऐसें। गुणग्रहें तामसें। घेतलें भवें पिसें । होऊनियां॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ gā jñāna aiseṃ| guṇagraheṃ tāmaseṃ| ghetaleṃ bhaveṃ piseṃ | hoūniyāṃ|| 51||
verses.meaning: Such knowledge, when grasped by the quality of ignorance, becomes a mad delusion, causing fear and confusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें सोयरिकें बाधु नेणें । पदार्थी निषेधु न म्हणे। निरोविलें जैसें सुणें। शून्यग्रामीं ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ soyarikeṃ bādhu neṇeṃ | padārthī niṣedhu na mhaṇe| nirovileṃ jaiseṃ suṇeṃ| śūnyagrāmīṃ || 52||
verses.meaning: That which does not know kinship, nor does it forbid anything in the material world, is like a dog sent into an empty village.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया तोंडीं जें नाडळे। कां खातां जेणें पोळे । तेंचि एक वाळे । येर घेणेचि ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā toṃḍīṃ jeṃ nāḍaḻe| kāṃ khātāṃ jeṇeṃ poḻe | teṃci eka vāḻe | yera gheṇeci || 53||
verses.meaning: That which is stuck in the mouth, or that which burns when eaten, should be avoided. All else can be accepted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं सोनें चोरितां उंदिरु। न म्हणे थरुविथरु । नेणें मांसखाइरु। काळें गोरें॥५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ soneṃ coritāṃ uṃdiru| na mhaṇe tharuvitharu | neṇeṃ māṃsakhāiru| kāḻeṃ goreṃ||54||
verses.meaning: Just as a mouse, when stealing gold, does not distinguish between good and bad, nor does a flesh-eating creature differentiate between black and white.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना वनामाजीं बोहरी। कडसणी जेवीं न करी। कां जीत मेलें न विचारी । बैसतां माशी॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā vanāmājīṃ boharī| kaḍasaṇī jevīṃ na karī| kāṃ jīta meleṃ na vicārī | baisatāṃ māśī|| 55||
verses.meaning: Just as a fly, when it sits, does not distinguish between a living being and a dead one, nor does it discriminate between different kinds of trees in a forest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा वांता कां वाढिळेया। साजुक कां सडलिया। बिवेकु कावळिया। नाहीं जैसा॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā vāṃtā kāṃ vāḍhiḻeyā| sājuka kāṃ saḍaliyā| biveku kāvaḻiyā| nāhīṃ jaisā|| 56||
verses.meaning: Just as a crow cannot distinguish between pure and impure, or between fresh and stale food, so too is a person without discrimination.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें निषिद्ध सांडूनि द्यावें। कां विहित आदरें घ्यावें । हें विषयांचेनि नांवें । नेणेंचि जें ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ niṣiddha sāṃḍūni dyāveṃ| kāṃ vihita ādareṃ ghyāveṃ | heṃ viṣayāṃceni nāṃveṃ | neṇeṃci jeṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: Just as one should abandon what is forbidden, or respectfully accept what is prescribed, the Self does not know these distinctions by the names of worldly objects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेतुलें आड पडे दिठी । तेतुलें घेचि विषयासाठी । मग तें स्त्री-द्रव्य वाटी । शिए्नोदरां ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetuleṃ āḍa paḍe diṭhī | tetuleṃ gheci viṣayāsāṭhī | maga teṃ strī-dravya vāṭī | śienodarāṃ || 58||
verses.meaning: Whatever comes into his sight, he takes it for his sensual pleasures. Then he distributes that woman and wealth to his penis and stomach.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तीर्थातीर्थ हे भाख। उदकीं नाहीं सनोळख। तृषा बोळे तेंचि सुख। वांचूनियां॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tīrthātīrtha he bhākha| udakīṃ nāhīṃ sanoḻakha| tṛṣā boḻe teṃci sukha| vāṃcūniyāṃ|| 59||
verses.meaning: Pilgrimage after pilgrimage, one speaks of holy waters, but in the water itself, there is no recognition. Only when thirst speaks, is there true satisfaction, without which it is meaningless.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचिपरी खाद्याखाद्य। न म्हणे निंद्यानिंद्य। तोंडा आवडे तें मेध्य। ऐसाचि बोधु ॥ ५६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāciparī khādyākhādya| na mhaṇe niṃdyāniṃdya| toṃḍā āvaḍe teṃ medhya| aisāci bodhu || 560||
verses.meaning: In the same way, one does not distinguish between edible and inedible, or between blameworthy and blameless. Whatever the mouth likes is considered pure. Such is the nature of this understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि स्त्रीजात तितुकें । त्वचेंद्रियेंचि बोळखे । तियेविषयीं सोयरिकें ।॥ एकचि बोधु॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi strījāta titukeṃ | tvaceṃdriyeṃci boḻakhe | tiyeviṣayīṃ soyarikeṃ ||| ekaci bodhu|| 61||
verses.meaning: And all women, by their very nature, are known through the sense of touch. In this regard, there is only one understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं स्वार्थी जें उपकरे। 'तयाचि नाम सोयिरें। देहसंबंधु न सरे । जिये ज्ञानीं ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ svārthī jeṃ upakare| 'tayāci nāma soyireṃ| dehasaṃbaṃdhu na sare | jiye jñānīṃ || 62||
verses.meaning: That knowledge which is useful for one's own spiritual benefit, that alone is truly one's kin. The attachment to the body does not cease without such knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि विश्व सकळ। जेणें विषयोचि मानिळें केवळ। तया एक जाण 'फळ। देहभरण॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni viśva sakaḻa| jeṇeṃ viṣayoci māniḻeṃ kevaḻa| tayā eka jāṇa 'phaḻa| dehabharaṇa|| 64||
verses.meaning: For one who considers the entire world to be merely an object of enjoyment, the sole fruit of life is the sustenance of the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आकाशपतिता नीरा। जैसा सिंधूचि येक थारा । तैसें कृत्मजात उदरा-। लागींचि बुझे॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ākāśapatitā nīrā| jaisā siṃdhūci yeka thārā | taiseṃ kṛtmajāta udarā-| lāgīṃci bujhe|| 65||
verses.meaning: Just as all the waters falling from the sky ultimately merge into the ocean, so too all actions are understood to be for the sake of the stomach (sustenance).

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि स्वर्ग नरकु आथी । तया हेतु प्रवृत्ति निवृत्ती) इये आघवियेचि राती। जाणिवेची जें ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni svarga naraku āthī | tayā hetu pravṛtti nivṛttī) iye āghaviyeci rātī| jāṇivecī jeṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: Beyond this, there are heaven and hell, and the reasons for them are action and inaction. All of this is the night of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें देहखंडा नाम आत्मा। ईश्वर पाषाणप्रतिमा। ययापरौति प्रमा। ढळों नेणें ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ dehakhaṃḍā nāma ātmā| īśvara pāṣāṇapratimā| yayāparauti pramā| ḍhaḻoṃ neṇeṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: The body is called the soul, and God is a stone idol. Beyond this, their understanding does not waver.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे पडिलेनि शरीरें। केलेनिसीं आत्मा सरे। मा भोगावया उरे। कोण वेषें॥६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe paḍileni śarīreṃ| kelenisīṃ ātmā sare| mā bhogāvayā ure| koṇa veṣeṃ||68||
verses.meaning: He says, "When the body perishes, the soul is not destroyed. Then, in what form does it remain to experience the fruits of its actions?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना ईश्वरु पाहातां आहे । तो भोगवी हें जरी होये । तरी देवचि खाये । विकूनियां ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā īśvaru pāhātāṃ āhe | to bhogavī heṃ jarī hoye | tarī devaci khāye | vikūniyāṃ || 69||
verses.meaning: If it is believed that God, though unseen, is the one who makes us experience everything, then it is as if God Himself consumes us by selling us off.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गांबींचें देवळेश्‍वर। नियामकचि होती साचार। तरी देशींचे डोंगर। उगे कां असती ॥ ५७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: gāṃbīṃceṃ devaḻeś‍vara| niyāmakaci hotī sācāra| tarī deśīṃce ḍoṃgara| uge kāṃ asatī || 570||
verses.meaning: If the temples of God are truly the regulators of the world, then why do the mountains of this land remain silent and unmoving?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा विपायें देवो मानिजे। तरी पाषाणमात्रचि जाणिजे) आणि आत्मा तंब म्हणिजे । देहातेंचि॥ ७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā vipāyeṃ devo mānije| tarī pāṣāṇamātraci jāṇije) āṇi ātmā taṃba mhaṇije | dehāteṃci|| 71||
verses.meaning: If God is considered to be such, then He is known only as a mere stone; and the Self is then said to be nothing but the body itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरें पापपुण्यादिकें। तें आघवेंचि करोनि लटिकें। हित मानी अग्निमुखें। चरणें जें कां॥७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yereṃ pāpapuṇyādikeṃ| teṃ āghaveṃci karoni laṭikeṃ| hita mānī agnimukheṃ| caraṇeṃ jeṃ kāṃ||72||
verses.meaning: All other actions, whether meritorious or sinful, are considered false. The true welfare is to offer oneself into the fire, which is the act of surrendering to the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे चामाचे डोळे दाविती । जें इंद्रियें गोडी लाविती । तेंचि साच हे प्रतीती। फुडी जया॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: je cāmāce ḍoḻe dāvitī | jeṃ iṃdriyeṃ goḍī lāvitī | teṃci sāca he pratītī| phuḍī jayā|| 73||
verses.meaning: Those who show the eyes of the skin, those senses that create sweetness, that indeed is the true experience, for those who understand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना ऐसी प्रथा। वाढती देखसी पार्था । धूमाची वेली वृथा । आकाशीं जैसी ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā aisī prathā| vāḍhatī dekhasī pārthā | dhūmācī velī vṛthā | ākāśīṃ jaisī || 74||
verses.meaning: Indeed, you will see such a practice growing, O Partha, like a useless vine of smoke in the sky.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कोरडा ना बोला । उपेगा आथी गेला। तो वाढोनि मोडला । भेंडु जैसा॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: koraḍā nā bolā | upegā āthī gelā| to vāḍhoni moḍalā | bheṃḍu jaisā|| 75||
verses.meaning: He who speaks dryly, without substance, is like a bamboo that grows tall but is hollow and easily broken.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना उंसांची कणसें। कां नपुंसकें माणुसें। बन लागलें जैसें । साबरीचें ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā uṃsāṃcī kaṇaseṃ| kāṃ napuṃsakeṃ māṇuseṃ| bana lāgaleṃ jaiseṃ | sābarīceṃ || 76||
verses.meaning: Just as there are many kinds of sugarcane stalks, or as there are eunuchs among people, or as a forest of cactus grows.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी बाळकाचें मन। कां चोराघरींचें धन। अथवा ४४८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी गळास्तन । शेळियेचे ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī bāḻakāceṃ mana| kāṃ corāgharīṃceṃ dhana| athavā 448 śrījñāneśvarī gaḻāstana | śeḻiyece || 77||
verses.meaning: Just as a child's mind, or wealth in a thief's house, or the udder of a sheep, is of no true value or benefit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें जें बायाणें। बोसाळ दिसे जाणणें । तयातें मी म्हणें । तामसज्ञान ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ jeṃ bāyāṇeṃ| bosāḻa dise jāṇaṇeṃ | tayāteṃ mī mhaṇeṃ | tāmasajñāna || 78 ||
verses.meaning: That knowledge which is like a barren woman, appearing to be fruitful but actually empty, that I call Tamasic knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंही ज्ञान इया भाषा । बोलिजे तो भावो ऐसा । जात्यंधाचा कां जैसा। डोळा वाडु॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃhī jñāna iyā bhāṣā | bolije to bhāvo aisā | jātyaṃdhācā kāṃ jaisā| ḍoḻā vāḍu|| 79||
verses.meaning: The knowledge expressed in this language is like giving sight to one born blind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: का बधिराचे नीट कान। अपेया नाम पान। तेसें आडनांव ज्ञान। तामसा तया॥ ५८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kā badhirāce nīṭa kāna| apeyā nāma pāna| teseṃ āḍanāṃva jñāna| tāmasā tayā|| 580||
verses.meaning: Just as a deaf person cannot hear well, or an alcoholic cannot drink anything but liquor, so too, for a tamasic person, knowledge is merely a title, not a true understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो किती बोलावें। तरी ऐसें जें देखावें। तें ज्ञान नोहे जाणावें। डोळस तम॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso kitī bolāveṃ| tarī aiseṃ jeṃ dekhāveṃ| teṃ jñāna nohe jāṇāveṃ| ḍoḻasa tama|| 81||
verses.meaning: Let this be; how much more can be said? Even so, what is seen in this manner, know that it is not true knowledge, but rather a darkness with eyes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं तिहीं गुणीं । भेदलें यथालक्षणीं । ज्ञान श्रोतेशिरोमणी । दाविलें तुज ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ tihīṃ guṇīṃ | bhedaleṃ yathālakṣaṇīṃ | jñāna śroteśiromaṇī | dāvileṃ tuja || 82||
verses.meaning: Thus, the knowledge of how these three Gunas are distinct, each with its own characteristics, has been revealed to you, O crest-jewel among listeners.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां याचि त्रिप्रकारा । ज्ञानाचेनि धनुर्धरा । प्रकाशे होती गोचरा । कर्तयांच्या क्रिया॥८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yāci triprakārā | jñānāceni dhanurdharā | prakāśe hotī gocarā | kartayāṃcyā kriyā||83||
verses.meaning: Now, by the light of this three-fold knowledge, the actions of the doers become evident, O Arjuna, the archer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि कर्म पैं गा। अनुसरे तिहीं भागां। मोहरे जालिया बोघा। तोय जेसें॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni karma paiṃ gā| anusare tihīṃ bhāgāṃ| mohare jāliyā boghā| toya jeseṃ|| 84||
verses.meaning: Therefore, action, indeed, is divided into these three parts, just as water becomes ice when it freezes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंचि ज्ञानत्रयवशें। त्रिविध कर्म जें असे। तेथ सात्त्विक तंव ऐसें। परिसे आधीं ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃci jñānatrayavaśeṃ| trividha karma jeṃ ase| tetha sāttvika taṃva aiseṃ| parise ādhīṃ || 85||
verses.meaning: That very knowledge, through its three aspects, gives rise to three kinds of action. Among these, first hear about the sattvic (pure) action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी स्वाधिकाराचेनि मार्गे) आलें जें मानिलें आंगें। पतित्रतेचेनि परिष्वंगें । प्रियातें जैसें ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī svādhikārāceni mārge) āleṃ jeṃ mānileṃ āṃgeṃ| patitrateceni pariṣvaṃgeṃ | priyāteṃ jaiseṃ || 86 ||
verses.meaning: Just as a devoted wife, through her rightful path, embraces her beloved with her whole being, so too does the soul, through its inherent right, embrace the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सांवळ्या आंगा चंदन । प्रमदालोचनीं अंजन । तैसें अधिकारासी मंडण। नित्यपणें जें ॥८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: sāṃvaḻyā āṃgā caṃdana | pramadālocanīṃ aṃjana | taiseṃ adhikārāsī maṃḍaṇa| nityapaṇeṃ jeṃ ||87||
verses.meaning: Just as sandalwood adorns a dark body, and kohl beautifies a woman's eyes, so too does permanence adorn the state of spiritual authority.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें नित्य कर्म भळें। होय नैमित्तिकीं सावाइलें। सोनयासि जोडलें। सौरभ्य जैसें ॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ nitya karma bhaḻeṃ| hoya naimittikīṃ sāvāileṃ| sonayāsi joḍaleṃ| saurabhya jaiseṃ || 88||
verses.meaning: That daily ritual, when performed with devotion, becomes like a special occasion, just as gold is enhanced by fragrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आंगा जीवाची संपत्ती। वेंचुनि बाळाची करी पाळती। परी जीवें उबगणें हे स्थिती। न पाहे माय॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi āṃgā jīvācī saṃpattī| veṃcuni bāḻācī karī pāḻatī| parī jīveṃ ubagaṇeṃ he sthitī| na pāhe māya|| 89||
verses.meaning: And the mother, spending all her life's wealth, nurtures her child. Yet, she never considers this state of being weary of life.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सर्वस्वें कर्म अनुष्ठी। परी फळ न सूये दिठी। उखिती क्रिया पैठी। ब्रह्मींचि करी॥ ५९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sarvasveṃ karma anuṣṭhī| parī phaḻa na sūye diṭhī| ukhitī kriyā paiṭhī| brahmīṃci karī|| 590||
verses.meaning: Similarly, one performs all actions with complete dedication, yet does not cast an eye on the fruits of those actions. Such an action, performed with the understanding of its true nature, leads one directly into Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि प्रिय आलिया स्वभावें। शंबळ उरे वेंचे ठाउवें। नव्हे तेसें सत्प्रसंगें करावें । पारुषे जरी॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi priya āliyā svabhāveṃ| śaṃbaḻa ure veṃce ṭhāuveṃ| navhe teseṃ satprasaṃgeṃ karāveṃ | pāruṣe jarī|| 91||
verses.meaning: And when the beloved (God) is naturally attained, the remaining (worldly attachments) are known to be spent. Even if it seems difficult, one should engage in good company.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी अकरणाचेनि खेदें। द्वेषातें जिवीं न बांधे । जालियाचेनि आनंदें। फुंजो नेणे॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī akaraṇāceni khedeṃ| dveṣāteṃ jivīṃ na bāṃdhe | jāliyāceni ānaṃdeṃ| phuṃjo neṇe|| 92||
verses.meaning: Therefore, do not bind hatred in your heart due to the sorrow of not achieving something, nor swell with pride due to the joy of achievement.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसऐसिया हातवटिया। कर्म निफजे जें धनंजया । जाण सात्त्विक हें तया । गुणनाम गा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisaaisiyā hātavaṭiyā| karma niphaje jeṃ dhanaṃjayā | jāṇa sāttvika heṃ tayā | guṇanāma gā|| 93||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, know that action which is performed with such a disposition is called sattvic in nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ययावरी राजसाचें। लक्षण सांगिजेल साचें। न करी अवधानाचें। वाणेंपण॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayāvarī rājasāceṃ| lakṣaṇa sāṃgijela sāceṃ| na karī avadhānāceṃ| vāṇeṃpaṇa|| 94||
verses.meaning: Now, the characteristics of the Rajasic (passionate) person will be truly described. Do not be lacking in attention.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी घरीं मातापितरां। धड बोली नाहीं संसारा । येर विश्व भरी आदरा । मूर्खु जैसा॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī gharīṃ mātāpitarāṃ| dhaḍa bolī nāhīṃ saṃsārā | yera viśva bharī ādarā | mūrkhu jaisā|| 95||
verses.meaning: Yet, at home, he speaks not a kind word to his parents or family, but showers the whole world with affection, like a fool.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां तुळशीचिया झाडा। दुरूनि न घापे सिंतोडा। द्राक्षीचिया तरी बुडा। दूधचि लाविजे॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ tuḻaśīciyā jhāḍā| durūni na ghāpe siṃtoḍā| drākṣīciyā tarī buḍā| dūdhaci lāvije|| 96||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not sprinkle water on a Tulsi plant from afar, but rather pours milk directly at the base of a grape vine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी नित्यनैमित्तिकें । कर्मे जियें आवश्यकें । तयांचेविषीं न शके । बैसला उठूं॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī nityanaimittikeṃ | karme jiyeṃ āvaśyakeṃ | tayāṃceviṣīṃ na śake | baisalā uṭhūṃ|| 97||
verses.meaning: Similarly, regarding the daily and occasional duties that are essential, one cannot simply sit idle or rise from them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येरां काम्याचेनि तरी नांवें। देह सर्वस्व आघवें। वेंचितांही न मनवे । बहु ऐसें ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: yerāṃ kāmyāceni tarī nāṃveṃ| deha sarvasva āghaveṃ| veṃcitāṃhī na manave | bahu aiseṃ || 98||
verses.meaning: Even if one were to dedicate their entire being, their very all, to the pursuit of worldly desires, it would still not be enough, for such desires are insatiable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा देवढी वाढी लाहिजे। तेथ मोल देतां न धाइजे । पेरितां पुरें न म्हिणिजे। बीज जेबीं॥९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā devaḍhī vāḍhī lāhije| tetha mola detāṃ na dhāije | peritāṃ pureṃ na mhiṇije| bīja jebīṃ||99||
verses.meaning: When the divine growth is desired, it cannot be bought with any price, nor can it be said that the seeds sown are sufficient, for it is a matter of divine grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां परिसु आलिया हातीं। लोहालागीं सर्वसंपत्ती। वेंचितां ये उन्नती । साधकु जैसा॥ ६००॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ parisu āliyā hātīṃ| lohālāgīṃ sarvasaṃpattī| veṃcitāṃ ye unnatī | sādhaku jaisā|| 600||
verses.meaning: Just as the touchstone, upon coming into one's hand, bestows all prosperity upon iron, similarly, a seeker, by expending effort, achieves spiritual upliftment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसीं फळें देखोनि पुढें। काम्यकर्मे दुवाडें। करी परी तें थोकडें। केलेंही मानी॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisīṃ phaḻeṃ dekhoni puḍheṃ| kāmyakarme duvāḍeṃ| karī parī teṃ thokaḍeṃ| keleṃhī mānī|| 1||
verses.meaning: Just as one sees the fruits ahead, and though the desired actions are difficult, one performs them, yet considers what has been done as insignificant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें फळकामुकें। यथाविधि नेटकें।॥ काम्य कौजे तितुकें । क्रियाजात॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ phaḻakāmukeṃ| yathāvidhi neṭakeṃ||| kāmya kauje titukeṃ | kriyājāta|| 2||
verses.meaning: With that desire for fruit, all those actions, performed properly and meticulously, are considered as desire-driven rituals.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि तयाही केलियाचें। तोंडीं लावी दोंडीचें। कर्मी या नांवपाटाचें। वाणें सारी॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi tayāhī keliyāceṃ| toṃḍīṃ lāvī doṃḍīceṃ| karmī yā nāṃvapāṭāceṃ| vāṇeṃ sārī|| 3||
verses.meaning: And even after all that effort, the fruit of their actions is like a mere mouthful of a small, insignificant portion, as if they are given a meager share of a small plate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा भरे कर्माहंकारी। मग पिता अथवा गुरु। ते न मनी काळज्वरु। औषध जैसें॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā bhare karmāhaṃkārī| maga pitā athavā guru| te na manī kāḻajvaru| auṣadha jaiseṃ|| 4||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when filled with the ego of action, one disregards even a father or a guru, just as a feverish patient rejects medicine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेनि साहंकारें। फळाभिलाषियें नरें। कौजे गा आदेरें। जें जें कांहीं ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseni sāhaṃkāreṃ| phaḻābhilāṣiyeṃ nareṃ| kauje gā ādereṃ| jeṃ jeṃ kāṃhīṃ || 5||
verses.meaning: In the same way, a person driven by ego and desire for results performs whatever actions they undertake with great enthusiasm.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तेंही करणें बहुवसा । वळघोनि करी सायासा । जीवनोपावो कां जैसा। कोल्हाटियांचा ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī teṃhī karaṇeṃ bahuvasā | vaḻaghoni karī sāyāsā | jīvanopāvo kāṃ jaisā| kolhāṭiyāṃcā || 6||
verses.meaning: But even that action, being mostly for the sake of livelihood, becomes a burden, like the efforts of a fox to find food.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एका कणालागीं उंदिरी। आसका उपसे डोंगरु । कां शेवाळोद्देशें दर्दुरु। समुद्रु डहुळी ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: ekā kaṇālāgīṃ uṃdirī| āsakā upase ḍoṃgaru | kāṃ śevāḻoddeśeṃ darduru| samudru ḍahuḻī || 7||
verses.meaning: A mouse, desiring a single grain, digs up a mountain. Or a frog, seeking moss, stirs up the ocean.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं भिकेपरतें न लाहे । तऱही गारुड़ी सापु वाहे। काय कौजे शीणुचि होये। गोडु येकां॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ bhikeparateṃ na lāhe | taṟahī gārur̤ī sāpu vāhe| kāya kauje śīṇuci hoye| goḍu yekāṃ|| 8||
verses.meaning: Just as a snake charmer carries a snake, even though it brings no benefit beyond begging, what good can come from such a strenuous effort for some?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो परमाणूचेनि लाभें। पाताळ लंघिती बोळंबे। तैसें स्वर्गसुखलो भें । विचंबणें जें॥९॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso paramāṇūceni lābheṃ| pātāḻa laṃghitī boḻaṃbe| taiseṃ svargasukhalo bheṃ | vicaṃbaṇeṃ jeṃ||9||
verses.meaning: Just as a tiny particle, by its very nature, can traverse the netherworld, so too is the enticement of heavenly pleasures a mere delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें काम्य कर्म सक्‍्लेश। जाणावें येथ राजस । आतां चिन्ह परिस । तामसाचें॥ ६१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ kāmya karma sak‍leśa| jāṇāveṃ yetha rājasa | ātāṃ cinha parisa | tāmasāceṃ|| 610||
verses.meaning: Know that such desire-driven actions are Rajasic, causing distress. Now, listen to the characteristics of Tamasic actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तें गा तामस कर्म । जें निंदेचें काळें धाम । निषेधाचें जन्म। साच जेणें॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī teṃ gā tāmasa karma | jeṃ niṃdeceṃ kāḻeṃ dhāma | niṣedhāceṃ janma| sāca jeṇeṃ|| 11||
verses.meaning: That action is indeed born of Tamas, which is the dark abode of censure and the very origin of prohibition.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें निपजविल्यापाठीं। कांहींच न दिसे दिठी। रेघ काढिलिया पोटीं । तोयाचे जेवीं ॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ nipajavilyāpāṭhīṃ| kāṃhīṃca na dise diṭhī| regha kāḍhiliyā poṭīṃ | toyāce jevīṃ ||92||
verses.meaning: Just as a line drawn on water leaves no trace, so too, after creation, nothing remains visible.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां कांजी घुसळलिया। कां राखोंडी फुंकलिया । कांहीं न दिसे गाळिलिया । वाळुघाणा॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ kāṃjī ghusaḻaliyā| kāṃ rākhoṃḍī phuṃkaliyā | kāṃhīṃ na dise gāḻiliyā | vāḻughāṇā|| 13||
verses.meaning: Just as churning gruel, or blowing on ashes, or sifting sand yields nothing, so too is it with worldly pursuits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना उपणिलिया भूंस। कां विंधिळलिया आकाश । नाना मांडिलिया पाश। वारयासी ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā upaṇiliyā bhūṃsa| kāṃ viṃdhiḻaliyā ākāśa | nānā māṃḍiliyā pāśa| vārayāsī || 14||
verses.meaning: Just as one cannot churn the earth, or pierce the sky, or set a snare for the wind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें आवघेंचि जैसें। वांझें होऊनि नासे। जें केलिया पाठीं तैसें। वायांचि जाय॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ āvagheṃci jaiseṃ| vāṃjheṃ hoūni nāse| jeṃ keliyā pāṭhīṃ taiseṃ| vāyāṃci jāya|| 15||
verses.meaning: Just as a barren woman's efforts come to naught, so too all actions performed without true understanding are ultimately wasted.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ४५० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी एऱ्हवीं नरदेहाही येवढें। धन आटणीये पडे । जें कर्म निफजवितां मोडे । जगाचें सुख॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: 450 śrījñāneśvarī eṟhavīṃ naradehāhī yevaḍheṃ| dhana āṭaṇīye paḍe | jeṃ karma niphajavitāṃ moḍe | jagāceṃ sukha|| 16||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, even in this human body, such wealth is wasted, that by performing actions that destroy the world's happiness, one's own spiritual progress is hindered.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा कमळवनीं फांसु। काढिलिया कांटसु। आपण झिजे नाशु।॥ कमळां करी॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā kamaḻavanīṃ phāṃsu| kāḍhiliyā kāṃṭasu| āpaṇa jhije nāśu||| kamaḻāṃ karī|| 17||
verses.meaning: Just as a thorn, when removed from a lotus pond, itself wears away and perishes, yet it harms the lotuses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां आपण आंगें जळे। आणि नागवी जगाचे डोळे। पतंगु जैसा सळें। दीपाचेनि॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ āpaṇa āṃgeṃ jaḻe| āṇi nāgavī jagāce ḍoḻe| pataṃgu jaisā saḻeṃ| dīpāceni|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as a moth, by sacrificing itself in the lamp, extinguishes its light and blinds the world, so too does ignorance operate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सर्वस्व वायां जावो। वरी देहाही होय घावो। परी पुढिलां अपाबो। निफजविजे जेणें ॥१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sarvasva vāyāṃ jāvo| varī dehāhī hoya ghāvo| parī puḍhilāṃ apābo| niphajavije jeṇeṃ ||19||
verses.meaning: Even if one's entire being is wasted, and the body is wounded, one should still strive to bring about the well-being of others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मासी आपणयातें गिळवी। परी पुढीला वांती शिणवी। तें 'कश्मळ आठवी । आचरण जें॥ ६२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: māsī āpaṇayāteṃ giḻavī| parī puḍhīlā vāṃtī śiṇavī| teṃ 'kaśmaḻa āṭhavī | ācaraṇa jeṃ|| 620||
verses.meaning: Just as a fish swallows its own young, but then vomits them out in distress, so too is the conduct that is remembered as 'impure' or 'defiled'.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंही करावया दोषें। मज सामर्थ्य असे कीं नसे। हेंही पुढील तैसें। न पाहतां करी॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃhī karāvayā doṣeṃ| maja sāmarthya ase kīṃ nase| heṃhī puḍhīla taiseṃ| na pāhatāṃ karī|| 21||
verses.meaning: Whether I have the power to commit such faults or not, I do not consider that either, but simply act.

verses.shloka_devanagari: केवढा माझा उपावो। करितां कोण प्रस्तावो। केलियाही आवो। काय येथ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kevaḍhā mājhā upāvo| karitāṃ koṇa prastāvo| keliyāhī āvo| kāya yetha|| 22||
verses.meaning: What is the extent of my effort? What is the point of my proposal? Even if I make a sound, what is there to gain from it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: इये जाणिवेची सोये । अविवेकाचेनि पायें । पुसोनियां होये । साटोप कर्मी ॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: iye jāṇivecī soye | avivekāceni pāyeṃ | pusoniyāṃ hoye | sāṭopa karmī || 23||
verses.meaning: By the grace of this knowledge, the feet of ignorance are wiped away, and one becomes engaged in purposeful action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपुला वसौटा जाळुनी । बिसाटे जैसा वन्ही । कां स्वमर्यादा गिळोनि। सिंधु उठी॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpulā vasauṭā jāḻunī | bisāṭe jaisā vanhī | kāṃ svamaryādā giḻoni| siṃdhu uṭhī|| 24||
verses.meaning: Just as fire consumes its own dwelling, or the ocean rises, swallowing its own boundaries.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग नेणे बहु थोडें। न पाहे मागें पुढें। मार्गामार्ग येकवढें । करीत चाळे॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga neṇe bahu thoḍeṃ| na pāhe māgeṃ puḍheṃ| mārgāmārga yekavaḍheṃ | karīta cāḻe|| 25||
verses.meaning: Then, knowing very little, not looking back or forward, he considers all paths as one and acts playfully.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें कृत्याकृत्य सरकटित। आपपर नुरवित। कर्म होय तें निचित । तामस जाण॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ kṛtyākṛtya sarakaṭita| āpapara nuravita| karma hoya teṃ nicita | tāmasa jāṇa|| 26||
verses.meaning: That action which is performed without distinguishing between what should and should not be done, and without differentiating between oneself and others, is certainly known as Tamasic.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी गुणत्रयभिन्ना। कर्माची गा अर्जुना । हे केली विवंचना । उपपत्तींसीं॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī guṇatrayabhinnā| karmācī gā arjunā | he kelī vivaṃcanā | upapattīṃsīṃ|| 27||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, thus have I explained with reasoning how actions are differentiated by the three Gunas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ययाचि कर्मा भजतां। कर्माभिमानिया कर्ता । तो जीवुही त्रिविधता । पातळा असे॥ २८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yayāci karmā bhajatāṃ| karmābhimāniyā kartā | to jīvuhī trividhatā | pātaḻā ase|| 28 ||
verses.meaning: Now, the doer who performs these actions with the pride of being the doer, that very individual soul also attains a threefold nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चतुराश्रमबशें। एकु पुरुषु चतुर्धा दिसे। कर्तया त्रैविध्य तैसें। कर्मभेदें ॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: caturāśramabaśeṃ| eku puruṣu caturdhā dise| kartayā traividhya taiseṃ| karmabhedeṃ || 29||
verses.meaning: Just as a single person appears in four forms according to the four stages of life (ashramas), similarly, the doer (Kartā) appears in three ways due to the distinctions in actions (karma).

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी तयां तिहींआंतु। सात्त्विक तंब प्रस्तुतु। सांगेन दत्तचित्तु| आकर्णी तूं॥ ६३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī tayāṃ tihīṃāṃtu| sāttvika taṃba prastutu| sāṃgena dattacittu| ākarṇī tūṃ|| 630||
verses.meaning: Among these three, I will now explain the Sattvic (pure) type to you, so listen with a concentrated mind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी फळोहेशें सांडिलिया। वाढिती जेवी सरळिया। शाखा कां चंदनाचिया। बावन्नया॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī phaḻoheśeṃ sāṃḍiliyā| vāḍhitī jevī saraḻiyā| śākhā kāṃ caṃdanāciyā| bāvannayā|| 39||
verses.meaning: Just as the branches of a sandalwood tree grow straight and tall when they are not burdened by the desire for fruit, so too does spiritual growth flourish when actions are performed without attachment to their outcomes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां न फळतांही सार्थका। जैसिया नागलतिका। तैसिया करी नित्यादिकां। क्रिया जो कां॥३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ na phaḻatāṃhī sārthakā| jaisiyā nāgalatikā| taisiyā karī nityādikāṃ| kriyā jo kāṃ||32||
verses.meaning: Just as a creeper, even without bearing fruit, is considered fruitful, so too are the daily rituals and actions performed by one who is steadfast.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी 'फळशून्यता। नाहीं तया विफळता। पैं फळासीचि पांडुसुता। फळें कायिसी॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī 'phaḻaśūnyatā| nāhīṃ tayā viphaḻatā| paiṃ phaḻāsīci pāṃḍusutā| phaḻeṃ kāyisī|| 33||
verses.meaning: But the absence of fruit does not mean failure. O son of Pandu, what fruits can there be for the fruit itself?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आदेरें करी बहुवसें। परी कर्ता मी हें नुमसे। वर्षाकाळींचे जैसें । मेघवृंद ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ādereṃ karī bahuvaseṃ| parī kartā mī heṃ numase| varṣākāḻīṃce jaiseṃ | meghavṛṃda || 34||
verses.meaning: And though I perform many actions, I do not consider myself the doer, just like the clouds during the rainy season.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि परमात्मलिंगा । समर्पावयाजोगा । कर्मकलापु पैं गा। निपजावया॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci paramātmaliṃgā | samarpāvayājogā | karmakalāpu paiṃ gā| nipajāvayā|| 35||
verses.meaning: In the same way, all actions are performed as an offering to the Supreme Lingam (the ultimate reality).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया काळातें नुलंघणें। देशशुद्द्िही साधणें। कां शास्त्रांच्या वाती पाहणें। क्रियानिर्णयो॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā kāḻāteṃ nulaṃghaṇeṃ| deśaśuddihī sādhaṇeṃ| kāṃ śāstrāṃcyā vātī pāhaṇeṃ| kriyānirṇayo|| 36||
verses.meaning: In that period, one should not transgress; one should also achieve purity of place, or examine the scriptures to determine the correct actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वृत्ती करणें येकवळा। चित्त जावों न देणें फळा। नियमांचिया सांखळा । वबाहणें सदा॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: vṛttī karaṇeṃ yekavaḻā| citta jāvoṃ na deṇeṃ phaḻā| niyamāṃciyā sāṃkhaḻā | vabāhaṇeṃ sadā|| 37||
verses.meaning: To make the mind one-pointed, not allowing the consciousness to chase after the fruits of action, and always binding it with the chains of spiritual discipline.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा निरोधु साहावयालागीं। धैर्याचिया चांगचांगी । जिंतवणी जिती आंगीं । वाहे जो कां॥ ३८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā nirodhu sāhāvayālāgīṃ| dhairyāciyā cāṃgacāṃgī | jiṃtavaṇī jitī āṃgīṃ | vāhe jo kāṃ|| 38 ||
verses.meaning: To endure this restraint, one must possess the strength of unwavering courage, which conquers all obstacles within oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आत्मयाचिये आवडी । कर्मे करितां वरपडीं। देहसुखाचिये परवडीं । येबों न लाहे ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi ātmayāciye āvaḍī | karme karitāṃ varapaḍīṃ| dehasukhāciye paravaḍīṃ | yeboṃ na lāhe || 39||
verses.meaning: And when actions are performed with love for the Self, one does not get entangled in the pursuit of bodily pleasures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आळस निद्रा दुऱ्हावे। क्षुधा न बाणवे। सुरवाडु न पावे। आंगाचा ठावो॥ ६४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āḻasa nidrā duṟhāve| kṣudhā na bāṇave| suravāḍu na pāve| āṃgācā ṭhāvo|| 640||
verses.meaning: Lethargy and sleep disappear; hunger does not arise; the body does not experience pleasure.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंव अधिकाधिक । उत्साहो धरी आगळीक । सोनें जैसें पुटीं तुक । तुटलिया कसी ॥४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃva adhikādhika | utsāho dharī āgaḻīka | soneṃ jaiseṃ puṭīṃ tuka | tuṭaliyā kasī ||49||
verses.meaning: Then, with increasing enthusiasm, it takes on a unique brilliance, just as gold, when tested on a touchstone, shines more brightly after being refined.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी आवडी आथी साच। तरी जीवितही सलंच। आगीं घालितां रोमांच) देखिजती सतिये॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī āvaḍī āthī sāca| tarī jīvitahī salaṃca| āgīṃ ghālitāṃ romāṃca) dekhijatī satiye|| 42||
verses.meaning: If there is true love, then life itself is a small thing. When a devoted wife enters the fire, one can see her hairs standing on end, not from fear, but from intense devotion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मा आत्मयायेवढीया प्रिया । वालभेला जो धनंजया । देहही सिदतां तया। काय खेदु होईल॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mā ātmayāyevaḍhīyā priyā | vālabhelā jo dhanaṃjayā | dehahī sidatāṃ tayā| kāya khedu hoīla|| 43||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, if even my own soul, which is so dear to me, were to perish, what sorrow would that cause me?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि विषयसुरवाडु तुटे। जंब जंब देहबुद्धि आटे। तंव तंव आनंदु दुणबटे। कर्मी जया॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni viṣayasuravāḍu tuṭe| jaṃba jaṃba dehabuddhi āṭe| taṃva taṃva ānaṃdu duṇabaṭe| karmī jayā|| 44||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the enjoyment of worldly pleasures ceases. As the identification with the body diminishes, so too does the joy of the one who performs actions double.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि जो कर्म करी) आणि कोणे एके अवसरीं । तें ठाके ऐसी परी। बाहे जरी ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni jo karma karī) āṇi koṇe eke avasarīṃ | teṃ ṭhāke aisī parī| bāhe jarī || 45||
verses.meaning: When one performs actions in this manner, and at some point, if those actions cease, then what happens?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी कडाडीं लोटला गाडा । तो आपणपें न मनी अवघडा। तैसा ठाकलेनिही थोडा। नोहे जो कां॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī kaḍāḍīṃ loṭalā gāḍā | to āpaṇapeṃ na manī avaghaḍā| taisā ṭhākalenihī thoḍā| nohe jo kāṃ|| 46||
verses.meaning: Just as a cart, once set in motion, does not consider any obstacle difficult, so too, the one who has attained this state is not diminished even by a small hindrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी आदरिलें। अव्यंग सिद्धी गेलें। तरी तेंही जिंतिलें। मिरवू नेणें ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī ādarileṃ| avyaṃga siddhī geleṃ| tarī teṃhī jiṃtileṃ| miravū neṇeṃ || 47||
verses.meaning: Even if one achieves perfect spiritual realization, they do not boast about it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: इया खुणा कर्म करितां। देखिजे जो पंडुसुता । तयातें म्हणिपे तत्त्वतां। सात्त्विक कर्ता ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: iyā khuṇā karma karitāṃ| dekhije jo paṃḍusutā | tayāteṃ mhaṇipe tattvatāṃ| sāttvika kartā || 48||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, the one who performs actions with these characteristics is truly called a sattvic doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां राजसा कर्तेया। बोळखणें हें धनंजया । जे अभिलाषा जगाचिया। वसौटा तो॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ rājasā karteyā| boḻakhaṇeṃ heṃ dhanaṃjayā | je abhilāṣā jagāciyā| vasauṭā to|| 49||
verses.meaning: Now, O Arjuna, know this about the doer who is of the 'rajasic' quality: he is the abode of all worldly desires.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा गांबींचिया कश्मळा। उकरडा होय येकवळा। कां स्मशानी अमंगळा । आघवयांचि॥ ६५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā gāṃbīṃciyā kaśmaḻā| ukaraḍā hoya yekavaḻā| kāṃ smaśānī amaṃgaḻā | āghavayāṃci|| 650||
verses.meaning: Just as all the impurities from a village gather in one heap, or all inauspicious things collect in a cremation ground.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयापरी जो अशेषा । विश्वाचिया अभिलाषा । 'पायपाखाळणिया दोषां। घरटा जाला ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāparī jo aśeṣā | viśvāciyā abhilāṣā | 'pāyapākhāḻaṇiyā doṣāṃ| gharaṭā jālā || 51||
verses.meaning: In the same way, whoever desires the entire universe, becomes a home for the sin of washing feet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि फळाचा लागु । देखे जिये असलगु । तिये कर्मी चांगु । रोहो मांडी ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni phaḻācā lāgu | dekhe jiye asalagu | tiye karmī cāṃgu | roho māṃḍī || 52||
verses.meaning: Therefore, in actions where one sees no attachment to the fruit, a good seed of karma is sown.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आपण जालिये जोडी । उपखों नेदी कवडी । क्षणक्षणा कुरोंडी। जीवाची करी॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi āpaṇa jāliye joḍī | upakhoṃ nedī kavaḍī | kṣaṇakṣaṇā kuroṃḍī| jīvācī karī|| 53||
verses.meaning: And when one's own pair of senses and mind becomes a foe, it does not allow even a moment of peace, constantly gnawing at the soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: 'कृपणु चित्तीं ठेवा आपुला । तैसा दक्षु पराविया माळा । बकु जैसा खुतला । मासेयासी ॥ ५९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: 'kṛpaṇu cittīṃ ṭhevā āpulā | taisā dakṣu parāviyā māḻā | baku jaisā khutalā | māseyāsī || 594||
verses.meaning: Just as a miser guards his wealth, or a vigilant gardener protects his flowerbeds, or a heron patiently waits to catch fish, so too should one guard their spiritual practice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि गोंबी गेलिया जवळी । झगटलिया अंग फाळी। ४५२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी फळे तरी आंतु पोळी । बोरांटी जैसी ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi goṃbī geliyā javaḻī | jhagaṭaliyā aṃga phāḻī| 452 śrījñāneśvarī phaḻe tarī āṃtu poḻī | borāṃṭī jaisī || 55||
verses.meaning: And if the fruit is rotten inside, it's like a thorny berry, even if it looks good from the outside.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें मने वाचा कायें । भलतया दुःख देतु जाये । स्वार्थु साधितां न पाहे। पराचें हित॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ mane vācā kāyeṃ | bhalatayā duḥkha detu jāye | svārthu sādhitāṃ na pāhe| parāceṃ hita|| 56||
verses.meaning: Similarly, one who inflicts pain upon others through mind, speech, or body, and does not consider the well-being of others while pursuing their own self-interest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवींचि आंगें कर्मी । आचरणें नोहे क्षमी । न निघे मनोधर्मी । अरोचकु ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃci āṃgeṃ karmī | ācaraṇeṃ nohe kṣamī | na nighe manodharmī | arocaku || 57||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the body, by its very nature, does not become capable of performing actions, nor does the mind, by its inherent disposition, become averse to them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कनकाचिया फळा । आंतु माज बाहेरी मोळा । तैसा सबाह्य दुबळा । शुचित्वें जो॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kanakāciyā phaḻā | āṃtu māja bāherī moḻā | taisā sabāhya dubaḻā | śucitveṃ jo|| 58||
verses.meaning: Just as a fruit made of gold is outwardly beautiful but inwardly hollow, so too is one who is outwardly pure but inwardly weak.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कर्मजात केलिया । फळ लाहे जरी धनंजया । तरी हरिखें जगा यया । वांकुलिया वाये ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi karmajāta keliyā | phaḻa lāhe jarī dhanaṃjayā | tarī harikheṃ jagā yayā | vāṃkuliyā vāye || 59||
verses.meaning: And if, Arjuna, the fruits of actions were to be obtained through mere performance, then this world would be filled with joyful celebrations.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अथवा जें आदरिलें। हीनफळ होय केलें। तरी शोके तेणें जिंतिळें। धिक्कारों लागे॥ ६६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: athavā jeṃ ādarileṃ| hīnaphaḻa hoya keleṃ| tarī śoke teṇeṃ jiṃtiḻeṃ| dhikkāroṃ lāge|| 660||
verses.meaning: Or if the chosen endeavor yields poor results, then sorrow conquers the mind, leading to self-reproach.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कर्मी राहाटी ऐसी । जयातें होती देखसी । तोचि जाण त्रिशुद्धीसी। राजस कर्ता ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: karmī rāhāṭī aisī | jayāteṃ hotī dekhasī | toci jāṇa triśuddhīsī| rājasa kartā || 61||
verses.meaning: Know that the one whose actions are driven by such a nature is, without a doubt, a Rajasic doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां यया पाठीं येरू। जो कुकर्माचा आगरु । तोही करूं गोचरु । तामस कर्ता॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yayā pāṭhīṃ yerū| jo kukarmācā āgaru | tohī karūṃ gocaru | tāmasa kartā|| 62||
verses.meaning: Now, after this, we shall also reveal the one who is a repository of evil deeds, the Tamasic doer.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी मियां लागलिया कैसें। पुढील जळत असे। हें नेणिजे हुताशें। जियापरी॥ ६३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī miyāṃ lāgaliyā kaiseṃ| puḍhīla jaḻata ase| heṃ neṇije hutāśeṃ| jiyāparī|| 63 ||
verses.meaning: Just as fire does not know what it burns, so too, I do not know how I have become attached to this world, and how it is burning me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं शस्त्रें मियां तिखटें । नेणिजे कैसेनि निवटे । कां नेणिजे काळकूटें। आपलें केलें॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ śastreṃ miyāṃ tikhaṭeṃ | neṇije kaiseni nivaṭe | kāṃ neṇije kāḻakūṭeṃ| āpaleṃ keleṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: How is it that sharp weapons do not cut me? Or how is it that deadly poison does not affect me?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा पुढीलया आपुलया । घातु करीत धनंजया । आदरी वबोखटिया। क्रिया जो कां॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā puḍhīlayā āpulayā | ghātu karīta dhanaṃjayā | ādarī vabokhaṭiyā| kriyā jo kāṃ|| 65||
verses.meaning: Just as, O Dhananjaya, a person who engages in evil deeds brings about their own future destruction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिया करितांही वेळीं। काय जालें हें न सांभाळी। चळला वायु वाहटुळी। चेष्टे तैसा ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyā karitāṃhī veḻīṃ| kāya jāleṃ heṃ na sāṃbhāḻī| caḻalā vāyu vāhaṭuḻī| ceṣṭe taisā || 66||
verses.meaning: Even then, at that very moment, what happened, he does not comprehend. Like a whirlwind, the wind moves, just as it pleases.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं 'करणिया आणि जया । मेळु नाहीं धनंजया। तो पाहुनी पिसेया। कैंची त्राय ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ 'karaṇiyā āṇi jayā | meḻu nāhīṃ dhanaṃjayā| to pāhunī piseyā| kaiṃcī trāya || 67||
verses.meaning: O Dhananjaya, if one's actions and intentions are not aligned, how can such a person, who is like a madman, be saved?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि इंद्रियांचे बोगरिलें। चरोनि राखे जो जियालें। बेलातळीं लागलें। गोचिड जैसें ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi iṃdriyāṃce bogarileṃ| caroni rākhe jo jiyāleṃ| belātaḻīṃ lāgaleṃ| gociḍa jaiseṃ || 68||
verses.meaning: And just as a tick, having fed on the senses, clings to the bel tree, so too does the soul remain attached to the body, sustained by the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हांसया रुदना वेळु । नेणतां आदरी बाळु । राहाटे उच्छंखळु । तयापरी ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: hāṃsayā rudanā veḻu | neṇatāṃ ādarī bāḻu | rāhāṭe ucchaṃkhaḻu | tayāparī || 69||
verses.meaning: Just as a child, unaware of the time for laughter or tears, acts unrestrainedly, so too is the ignorant person.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो प्रकृती आंतलेपणें । कृत्याकृत्यस्वादु नेणें। फुगे केरें धाळेपणें । उकरडा जैसा ॥ ६७० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo prakṛtī āṃtalepaṇeṃ | kṛtyākṛtyasvādu neṇeṃ| phuge kereṃ dhāḻepaṇeṃ | ukaraḍā jaisā || 670 ||
verses.meaning: One who, from within their nature, does not discern between right and wrong actions, swells with pride and arrogance, much like a garbage heap.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि मान्याचेनि नांवें । ईश्वराही परी न खालवे । स्तब्धपणें न मनवे । डोंगरासी ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni mānyāceni nāṃveṃ | īśvarāhī parī na khālave | stabdhapaṇeṃ na manave | ḍoṃgarāsī || 71 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, even God cannot be moved by the name of a revered one, nor can a mountain be made to think by remaining still.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि मन जयाचें विषकल्लोळीं। राहाटी फुडी चोरिली। दिठी कौर ते बोली । पण्यांगनेची ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi mana jayāceṃ viṣakalloḻīṃ| rāhāṭī phuḍī corilī| diṭhī kaura te bolī | paṇyāṃganecī || 72||
verses.meaning: And whose mind, like a prostitute's gaze, is fixed on the tumultuous waves of poison, its conduct stolen by deceitful words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना कपटाचें। देहचि वळिलें तयाचें । तें जिणें कीं जुंबाराचें। टिटेघर॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā kapaṭāceṃ| dehaci vaḻileṃ tayāceṃ | teṃ jiṇeṃ kīṃ juṃbārāceṃ| ṭiṭeghara|| 73||
verses.meaning: Indeed, his very body is fashioned from deceit; his life is like a gambler's den.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नोहे तयाचा प्रादुर्भावो। तो साभिलाष भिल्लांचा गांबो। म्हणौनि नये येवो जावों। तया वाटा॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nohe tayācā prādurbhāvo| to sābhilāṣa bhillāṃcā gāṃbo| mhaṇauni naye yevo jāvoṃ| tayā vāṭā|| 74||
verses.meaning: That is not its manifestation. It is a village of covetous hunters. Therefore, one should not go or come by that path.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आणिकांचें निकें केळें। विरु होय जया आलें। जैसें अपेय पया मिनळें। लवण करी॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi āṇikāṃceṃ nikeṃ keḻeṃ| viru hoya jayā āleṃ| jaiseṃ apeya payā minaḻeṃ| lavaṇa karī|| 75||
verses.meaning: And for others, what is good becomes bad, just as salt, when mixed with milk, makes it undrinkable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां हींब ऐसा पदार्थ । घातलिया आगीआंतु। तेचि क्षणीं धडाडितु। अग्नि होय ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ hīṃba aisā padārtha | ghātaliyā āgīāṃtu| teci kṣaṇīṃ dhaḍāḍitu| agni hoya || 76||
verses.meaning: Just as ice, when placed into fire, instantly becomes fire itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना सुद्रव्यें गोमटीं । जालिया शरीरीं पैठीं। होऊनि ठाती किरीटी। मळुचि जेवीं ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā sudravyeṃ gomaṭīṃ | jāliyā śarīrīṃ paiṭhīṃ| hoūni ṭhātī kirīṭī| maḻuci jevīṃ || 77||
verses.meaning: Just as various beautiful and delicious foods, upon entering the body, ultimately become mere waste, O Kiriti (Arjuna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें पुढिलाचें बरवें । जयाच्या भीतरीं पावे। आणि विरुद्धचि आघवें। होऊनि निगे॥७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ puḍhilāceṃ baraveṃ | jayācyā bhītarīṃ pāve| āṇi viruddhaci āghaveṃ| hoūni nige||78||
verses.meaning: Just as the well-being of others enters within him, and all that is contrary to it departs from him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो गुण घे दे दोख। अमृताचें करी विख। दूध पाजिलिया देख। व्याळु जैसा॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo guṇa ghe de dokha| amṛtāceṃ karī vikha| dūdha pājiliyā dekha| vyāḻu jaisā|| 79||
verses.meaning: Just as a snake, when fed milk, turns it into poison, so too does a wicked person transform good qualities into faults.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि ऐहिकीं जियावें। जेणें परत्रा साच यावें। तें उचित कृत्य पावे। अवसरीं जिये॥ ६८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi aihikīṃ jiyāveṃ| jeṇeṃ paratrā sāca yāveṃ| teṃ ucita kṛtya pāve| avasarīṃ jiye|| 680||
verses.meaning: And one should live in this world in such a way that one attains the next world; that appropriate action should be taken at the right time.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां जया आपैसी। निद्रा ये ठेविली ऐसी । दुर्व्यबहारीं जैसी । विटाळें ळोटे॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ jayā āpaisī| nidrā ye ṭhevilī aisī | durvyabahārīṃ jaisī | viṭāḻeṃ ḻoṭe|| 81||
verses.meaning: Then, just as sleep comes naturally, or as one is naturally drawn to bad conduct, so too does one become defiled.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं द्राक्षरसा आग्नरसा। वेळे तोंड सडे वायसा। कां डोळे फुटती दिवसा। डुडुळाचे॥८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ drākṣarasā āgnarasā| veḻe toṃḍa saḍe vāyasā| kāṃ ḍoḻe phuṭatī divasā| ḍuḍuḻāce||82||
verses.meaning: Just as a crow cannot enjoy the taste of grape juice or sugarcane juice, and an owl's eyes are blinded by daylight, so too are those who are not spiritually inclined unable to grasp the true essence of spiritual knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा 'कल्याणकाळु पाहे। तैं तयातें आळसु खाये । ना प्रमादीं तरी होये। तो म्हणे तैसें ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā 'kalyāṇakāḻu pāhe| taiṃ tayāteṃ āḻasu khāye | nā pramādīṃ tarī hoye| to mhaṇe taiseṃ || 83||
verses.meaning: Just as one who awaits an auspicious time is consumed by laziness, or becomes negligent, so he speaks.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेवींचि सागराच्या पोटीं । जळे अखंड आगिठी । तैसा विषादु वाहे गांठीं । जिवाचिये जो॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jevīṃci sāgarācyā poṭīṃ | jaḻe akhaṃḍa āgiṭhī | taisā viṣādu vāhe gāṃṭhīṃ | jivāciye jo|| 84||
verses.meaning: Just as a fire burns ceaselessly within the ocean, so too does sorrow reside perpetually within the heart of the living being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ळेंडोराआगीं धूमावधि । कां अपाना आंगीं दुर्गंधि। तैसा जो जीवितावधि। विषादें केला॥ ८५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ḻeṃḍorāāgīṃ dhūmāvadhi | kāṃ apānā āṃgīṃ durgaṃdhi| taisā jo jīvitāvadhi| viṣādeṃ kelā|| 85 ||
verses.meaning: Just as smoke is inherent in fire, or a foul odor in flatulence, so too is sorrow inherent in life, made so by poison.
