verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कल्पांताचिया पारा। वेगळेंही जो वीरा। सूत्र धरी व्यापारा। साभिलाषा॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kalpāṃtāciyā pārā| vegaḻeṃhī jo vīrā| sūtra dharī vyāpārā| sābhilāṣā|| 86||
verses.meaning: And even beyond the end of the cosmic cycle, He, the valiant one, holds the thread of all activities, driven by desire.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा जगाही परौती। शुचा वाहे पैं चित्तीं। करितां विषीं हातीं। तृणही न लगे॥८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā jagāhī parautī| śucā vāhe paiṃ cittīṃ| karitāṃ viṣīṃ hātīṃ| tṛṇahī na lage||87||
verses.meaning: Indeed, beyond the world, the mind carries purity. Even when engaging with worldly objects, it does not cling to even a blade of grass.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा जो लोकाआंतु। पापपुंजु मूर्त । देखसी तो अव्याहतु। तामसु कर्ता॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jo lokāāṃtu| pāpapuṃju mūrta | dekhasī to avyāhatu| tāmasu kartā|| 88||
verses.meaning: Thus, whoever you see among people as a personified heap of sins, know that he is an unhindered doer of Tamas (ignorance/darkness).

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं कर्म कर्ता ज्ञान। या तिहींचे त्रिधा चिन्ह। दाविले तुज सुजन-। चक्रवर्ती ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ karma kartā jñāna| yā tihīṃce tridhā cinha| dāvile tuja sujana-| cakravartī || 89||
verses.meaning: Thus, action, the doer, and knowledge—these three distinct characteristics have been revealed to you, O best among the wise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां अविद्येचिया गांबीं। मोहाची वेढूनि मदवी । संदेहाचीं आघवीं । लेऊनि लेणीं ॥ ६९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ avidyeciyā gāṃbīṃ| mohācī veḍhūni madavī | saṃdehācīṃ āghavīṃ | leūni leṇīṃ || 690||
verses.meaning: Now, in the womb of ignorance, adorned with the intoxication of delusion and all the ornaments of doubt.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आत्मनिश्चयाची बरव। जया आरिसां पाहे सावयव । तिये बुद्धीचीही धांव । त्रिधा असे॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātmaniścayācī barava| jayā ārisāṃ pāhe sāvayava | tiye buddhīcīhī dhāṃva | tridhā ase|| 91||
verses.meaning: The beauty of self-realization, which is fully reflected in the mirror of the intellect, that intellect itself has a threefold nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा सत्त्वादि गुणीं इहीं । कायी एक तिहीं ठायीं। न कीजेचि येथ पाहीं । जगामाजी ॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā sattvādi guṇīṃ ihīṃ | kāyī eka tihīṃ ṭhāyīṃ| na kījeci yetha pāhīṃ | jagāmājī || 92||
verses.meaning: Indeed, what is it that these three qualities (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas) do not accomplish in this world?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आगी न वसतां 'पोटीं। कवण काष्ठ असे सृष्टीं। तैसें तें कैचें दृश्यकोटीं। त्रिविध जें नोहे ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āgī na vasatāṃ 'poṭīṃ| kavaṇa kāṣṭha ase sṛṣṭīṃ| taiseṃ teṃ kaiceṃ dṛśyakoṭīṃ| trividha jeṃ nohe || 93||
verses.meaning: Which wood in this world does not contain fire within itself? Similarly, how can there be any visible creation that is not of the three types (sattva, rajas, tamas)?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि तिहीं गुणीं । बुद्धी केली त्रिगुणीं। धृतीसिही वांटणी । तैसीचि असे॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni tihīṃ guṇīṃ | buddhī kelī triguṇīṃ| dhṛtīsihī vāṃṭaṇī | taisīci ase|| 94||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the intellect, being influenced by the three Gunas, also becomes threefold. Similarly, the steadfastness (Dhriti) also gets divided in the same manner.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंचि येक वेगळालें। यथा चिन्हीं अळंकारलें। ४५४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी सांगिजैल उपाइलें। भेदळेपणें ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃci yeka vegaḻāleṃ| yathā cinhīṃ aḻaṃkāraleṃ| 454 śrījñāneśvarī sāṃgijaila upāileṃ| bhedaḻepaṇeṃ || 95 ||
verses.meaning: That very one, uniquely adorned with distinct characteristics, will be explained in the Shri Dnyaneshwari through various means, in its manifold aspects.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी बुद्धि धृति इयां। दोहीं भागांमाजीं धनंजया । आधीं रूप बुद्धीचिया। भेदासि करूं॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī buddhi dhṛti iyāṃ| dohīṃ bhāgāṃmājīṃ dhanaṃjayā | ādhīṃ rūpa buddhīciyā| bhedāsi karūṃ|| 96||
verses.meaning: But, O Dhananjaya, between these two divisions of intellect and fortitude, let us first understand the distinctions of intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी उत्तमा मध्यमा निकृष्टा । संसारासि गा सुभटा । प्राणियां येतिया वाटा । तिनी आथी ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī uttamā madhyamā nikṛṣṭā | saṃsārāsi gā subhaṭā | prāṇiyāṃ yetiyā vāṭā | tinī āthī || 97||
verses.meaning: Thus, O brave one, for all beings entering the path of worldly existence, there are three types: the excellent, the mediocre, and the inferior.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे अकरणीय ( करणीय ) काम्य निषिद्ध। ते हे मार्ग तिन्ही प्रसिद्ध । संसारभयें सबाध। जिवां ययां॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: je akaraṇīya ( karaṇīya ) kāmya niṣiddha| te he mārga tinhī prasiddha | saṃsārabhayeṃ sabādha| jivāṃ yayāṃ|| 98||
verses.meaning: That which is not to be done (or to be done), desirable, or forbidden - these three paths are well-known. They trouble beings with the fear of worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि अधिकारें मानिलें। जें विधीचेनि बोघें आलें। तें येकचि येथ भलें। नित्य कर्म ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni adhikāreṃ mānileṃ| jeṃ vidhīceni bogheṃ āleṃ| teṃ yekaci yetha bhaleṃ| nitya karma || 99||
verses.meaning: Therefore, that which is accepted as authoritative, that which comes from the understanding of the scriptures, that alone is good here, the daily ritual.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंचि आत्मप्राप्तिकळ। दिठी सूनि केवळ। कीजे जैसें कां जळ। सेविजे ताहनें ॥७००॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃci ātmaprāptikaḻa| diṭhī sūni kevaḻa| kīje jaiseṃ kāṃ jaḻa| sevije tāhaneṃ ||700||
verses.meaning: That very fruit of Self-realization, when seen with the inner eye, is consumed just as water is drunk by one who is thirsty.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येतुलेनि तें कर्म। सांडी जन्मभय विषम। करूनि दे सुगम। मोक्षसिव्द्रि॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetuleni teṃ karma| sāṃḍī janmabhaya viṣama| karūni de sugama| mokṣasivdri|| 9||
verses.meaning: Through this, one abandons the dreadful fear of rebirth, making the attainment of liberation easy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें कर्म करी तो भला। संसारभयें सांडिला । करणीयत्वें आला । मुमुक्षञभागा॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ karma karī to bhalā| saṃsārabhayeṃ sāṃḍilā | karaṇīyatveṃ ālā | mumukṣañabhāgā|| 2||
verses.meaning: One who performs actions in this manner is truly blessed, for they have cast aside the fears of worldly existence and have attained the state of a seeker of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ जे बुद्धि ऐसा। बळिया बांधे भरंवसा । मोक्षु ठेविला ऐसा। जोडेल येथ॥३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha je buddhi aisā| baḻiyā bāṃdhe bharaṃvasā | mokṣu ṭhevilā aisā| joḍela yetha||3||
verses.meaning: Where the intellect, with such strength, places its trust, it will attain liberation, which is kept here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि निवृत्तीचि मांडिली । सूनि प्रवृत्तितळीं। इये कर्मी बुडकुळी। द्यावी कौं ना॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni nivṛttīci māṃḍilī | sūni pravṛttitaḻīṃ| iye karmī buḍakuḻī| dyāvī kauṃ nā|| 4||
verses.meaning: Therefore, having established the path of renunciation and placed it beneath the path of action, should one then immerse oneself in these actions or not?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तृषार्ता उदकें जिणें। कां पुरीं पडलिया पोहणें । अंधकूपीं गती किरणें । सूर्याचेनि॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tṛṣārtā udakeṃ jiṇeṃ| kāṃ purīṃ paḍaliyā pohaṇeṃ | aṃdhakūpīṃ gatī kiraṇeṃ | sūryāceni|| 5||
verses.meaning: Just as water is the life for the thirsty, or swimming for those fallen into a flood, so too are the sun's rays the path for those in a dark well.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना पथ्येंसीं औषध लाहे। तरी रोगें दाटलाही जिये । कां मीना जिव्हाळा होये। जळाचा जरी ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā pathyeṃsīṃ auṣadha lāhe| tarī rogeṃ dāṭalāhī jiye | kāṃ mīnā jivhāḻā hoye| jaḻācā jarī || 6||
verses.meaning: Even if a person is severely afflicted by illness, they can recover with various remedies and medicines. Similarly, a fish thrives only when it is in water.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी तयाच्या जीविता । नाहीं जेवीं अन्यथा । तैसें कर्मी इये वर्ततां। जोडेचि मोक्षु॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī tayācyā jīvitā | nāhīṃ jevīṃ anyathā | taiseṃ karmī iye vartatāṃ| joḍeci mokṣu||7||
verses.meaning: Just as there is no other way for life to exist, so too, by acting in this manner, liberation is attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें 'करणीयाचिया कडे। जें ज्ञान आथी चोखडें। आणि अकरणीय हें फुडें। ऐसें जाण॥८॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ 'karaṇīyāciyā kaḍe| jeṃ jñāna āthī cokhaḍeṃ| āṇi akaraṇīya heṃ phuḍeṃ| aiseṃ jāṇa||8||
verses.meaning: This is the pure knowledge that discerns what is to be done and what is not to be done.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जीं तियें काम्यादिकें। संसारभयदायकें । अकृत्यपणाचें आंबुखें। पडिलें जयां॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jīṃ tiyeṃ kāmyādikeṃ| saṃsārabhayadāyakeṃ | akṛtyapaṇāceṃ āṃbukheṃ| paḍileṃ jayāṃ|| 9||
verses.meaning: Those who are entangled in desires and other worldly attachments, which are the cause of fear in this cycle of birth and death, have fallen into the mire of unrighteousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तियें कर्मी अकार्यी । जन्ममरणसमयीं। प्रवृत्ति 'पळवी पायीं। मागिलींचि ॥ ७१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiyeṃ karmī akāryī | janmamaraṇasamayīṃ| pravṛtti 'paḻavī pāyīṃ| māgilīṃci || 710||
verses.meaning: In those actions, even in the time of birth and death, the tendency of past deeds follows closely behind.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आगीमाजीं न रिघवे। अथावीं न घलवे। धगधगीत नागवे। शूळ जेवीं॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ āgīmājīṃ na righave| athāvīṃ na ghalave| dhagadhagīta nāgave| śūḻa jevīṃ|| 11||
verses.meaning: Just as one cannot enter a blazing fire, nor can one touch a red-hot trident, so too is the nature of this spiritual truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां काळियानाग धुंधुवातु । देखोनि न घालवे हातु। न वचवे खोपेआंतु। वाघाचिये॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ kāḻiyānāga dhuṃdhuvātu | dekhoni na ghālave hātu| na vacave khopeāṃtu| vāghāciye|| 12||
verses.meaning: Just as one cannot put their hand into a furious Kalia serpent's mouth, nor enter a tiger's den.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें कर्म अकरणीय । देखोनि महाभय। उपजे निःसंदेह। बुद्धी जिये॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ karma akaraṇīya | dekhoni mahābhaya| upaje niḥsaṃdeha| buddhī jiye|| 13||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when one perceives action as non-action, a great fear undoubtedly arises in the intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वाढिलें रांधूनि विखें। तेथें जाणिजे मृत्यु न चुके । तेवीं निषेधीं कां देखे। बंधातें जे॥१४॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāḍhileṃ rāṃdhūni vikheṃ| tetheṃ jāṇije mṛtyu na cuke | tevīṃ niṣedhīṃ kāṃ dekhe| baṃdhāteṃ je||14||
verses.meaning: If poison is served after being cooked, one knows that death is inevitable. Similarly, how can one not see bondage in forbidden actions?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग बंधभयभरितीं। तियें निषिद्धीं प्राप्ती। विनियोगु जाणे निवृत्ती । कर्माचिये ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga baṃdhabhayabharitīṃ| tiyeṃ niṣiddhīṃ prāptī| viniyogu jāṇe nivṛttī | karmāciye || 15||
verses.meaning: Then, filled with the fear of bondage, those forbidden actions are attained. Nivritti alone knows the proper application of karma.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेनि कार्याकार्यविवेकी । जे प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिमापकीं। खरा कुडा पारखीं। जियापरी॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseni kāryākāryavivekī | je pravṛttinivṛttimāpakīṃ| kharā kuḍā pārakhīṃ| jiyāparī|| 16||
verses.meaning: Just as a discerning person distinguishes between good and bad, or a jeweler identifies genuine from fake, so too does one discern between right and wrong action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी कृत्याकृत्यशुद्धी। बुझे जे निरवधी । सात्त्विक म्हणिपे बुद्धी। तेचि तूं जाण॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī kṛtyākṛtyaśuddhī| bujhe je niravadhī | sāttvika mhaṇipe buddhī| teci tūṃ jāṇa|| 17||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the intellect that understands without limit what is to be done and what is not to be done, know that to be of the Sattvic quality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि बकाच्या गांवीं । घेपे क्षीरनीर सकलवी। कां अहोरात्रींची गोंबी । आंधळें नेणे॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi bakācyā gāṃvīṃ | ghepe kṣīranīra sakalavī| kāṃ ahorātrīṃcī goṃbī | āṃdhaḻeṃ neṇe|| 18||
verses.meaning: Just as a crane cannot discern milk from water, so too a blind person cannot comprehend the difference between day and night.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जया फुलाचा मकरंदु फावे। तो काष्ठें कोरूं धांवे । परी भ्रमरपणा नव्हे । अव्हांटा जेवीं ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayā phulācā makaraṃdu phāve| to kāṣṭheṃ korūṃ dhāṃve | parī bhramarapaṇā navhe | avhāṃṭā jevīṃ || 99||
verses.meaning: Just as a bee, drawn to the nectar of a flower, would never carve wood, so too is the path of devotion distinct from mere ritualistic actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसीं इयें कार्याकार्ये । धर्माधर्मरूपें जियें। तियें न चोजवितां जाये। जाणती जे कां॥ ७२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tesīṃ iyeṃ kāryākārye | dharmādharmarūpeṃ jiyeṃ| tiyeṃ na cojavitāṃ jāye| jāṇatī je kāṃ|| 720||
verses.meaning: Those who know without being told what is right and wrong, what is dharma and adharma, they truly understand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा डोळांबीण मोतियें। घेतां पाडु मिळे विपायें। न मिळणें तें आहे। ठेविलें तेथें॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā ḍoḻāṃbīṇa motiyeṃ| ghetāṃ pāḍu miḻe vipāyeṃ| na miḻaṇeṃ teṃ āhe| ṭhevileṃ tetheṃ|| 29||
verses.meaning: Oh, the pearls in the Domal tree are rarely found when sought. What is unattainable is kept there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अकरणीय अवचटें । नोडवे तरीच लोटे । एऱ्हवीं जाणें एकवटें । दोन्ही जे कां॥२२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ akaraṇīya avacaṭeṃ | noḍave tarīca loṭe | eṟhavīṃ jāṇeṃ ekavaṭeṃ | donhī je kāṃ||22||
verses.meaning: Similarly, that which is not to be done, if it is not encountered by chance, then it is avoided. Otherwise, both are known as one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते गा बुद्धि चोखविषीं। जाण येथ राजसी । अक्षत टाकिली जैसी । मांदियेवरी॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: te gā buddhi cokhaviṣīṃ| jāṇa yetha rājasī | akṣata ṭākilī jaisī | māṃdiyevarī|| 23||
verses.meaning: That intellect, know this, is Rajasic, which is like throwing unbroken rice on a heap of dirt.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि राजा जिया वाटा जाये। ते चोरांसि आडव होये। कां राक्षसां दिवो पाहे। राति होऊनि॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi rājā jiyā vāṭā jāye| te corāṃsi āḍava hoye| kāṃ rākṣasāṃ divo pāhe| rāti hoūni|| 24||
verses.meaning: And just as the path taken by a king becomes an obstacle for thieves, or as night becomes a day for demons.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना निधानचि निदैवा। होये कोळसयाचा उडवा । पैं असतें आपणपें जीवा । नाहीं जालें॥ २५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā nidhānaci nidaivā| hoye koḻasayācā uḍavā | paiṃ asateṃ āpaṇapeṃ jīvā | nāhīṃ jāleṃ|| 25 ||
verses.meaning: Numerous treasures are useless to an unfortunate person, just as a heap of coal is useless. Similarly, the true self, which is always present, is not realized by the individual soul.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें धर्मजात तितुकें । जिये बुद्धीसी पातकें। साच तें लटिकें। ऐसेंचि बुझे॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ dharmajāta titukeṃ | jiye buddhīsī pātakeṃ| sāca teṃ laṭikeṃ| aiseṃci bujhe|| 26||
verses.meaning: Similarly, all that is considered righteousness, to that intellect, is sin. What is true, it understands as false.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते आघवेचि अर्थ) करूनि घाली अनर्थ। गुण ते ते व्यवस्थित । दोषचि मानी॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: te āghaveci artha) karūni ghālī anartha| guṇa te te vyavasthita | doṣaci mānī|| 27||
verses.meaning: All those virtues, when interpreted incorrectly, lead to disaster. He considers all those well-established qualities as faults.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना श्रुतिजातें। अधिष्ठूनि केलें सरतें। तेतुलेंही उपरतें। जाणे जे बुन्दि॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā śrutijāteṃ| adhiṣṭhūni keleṃ sarateṃ| tetuleṃhī uparateṃ| jāṇe je bundi|| 28||
verses.meaning: Indeed, all the Vedas, having established their authority, have concluded their discourse. Yet, even that much is known to be superficial by the intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते कोणातेंही न पुसतां। तामसी जाणावी पंडुसुता । रात्री काय धर्मार्था। साच करावी॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: te koṇāteṃhī na pusatāṃ| tāmasī jāṇāvī paṃḍusutā | rātrī kāya dharmārthā| sāca karāvī|| 29||
verses.meaning: O son of Pandu, know that those who do not consult anyone are of a tamasic nature. What good can be truly accomplished for dharma or artha during the night?

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं बुद्धीचे भेद। तिन्ही तुज विशद । सांगितले स्वबोध-। कुमुदचंद्रा ॥ ७३० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ buddhīce bheda| tinhī tuja viśada | sāṃgitale svabodha-| kumudacaṃdrā || 730 ||
verses.meaning: Thus, the three types of intellect, O moon to the kumud flowers of self-knowledge, have been clearly explained to you.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां ययाची बुद्धिवृत्ती । निष्टंकिला कर्मजातीं। खांदु मांडिजे धृती। त्रिविधा तया॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ yayācī buddhivṛttī | niṣṭaṃkilā karmajātīṃ| khāṃdu māṃḍije dhṛtī| trividhā tayā|| 31||
verses.meaning: Now, the intellect of such a person, having become detached from all actions, firmly establishes itself in the three kinds of steadfastness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये धृतीचेही विभाग। तिन्ही यथालिंग। सांगिजती चांग। अवधान देई॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye dhṛtīcehī vibhāga| tinhī yathāliṃga| sāṃgijatī cāṃga| avadhāna deī|| 32||
verses.meaning: Now, the three divisions of that very steadfastness, according to their characteristics, will be well explained. Pay attention.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी उदेलिया दिनकरु । चोरीसि थोके अंधारु । कां राजाज्ञा अव्यवहारु । कुंठवी जेवीं॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī udeliyā dinakaru | corīsi thoke aṃdhāru | kāṃ rājājñā avyavahāru | kuṃṭhavī jevīṃ|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun's rising dispels darkness, or a king's command halts unlawful acts.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना पवनाचा साटु। वाजीनलिया नीटु। आंगेंसीं बोभाटु। सांडिती मेघ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā pavanācā sāṭu| vājīnaliyā nīṭu| āṃgeṃsīṃ bobhāṭu| sāṃḍitī megha|| 34||
verses.meaning: When the wind blows strongly, the clouds, like a frightened horse, scatter and cry out.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां अगस्तीचेनि दर्शनें । सिंधु घेऊनी ठाती मौने। चंद्रोदयीं कमळवनें। मिठी देती ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ agastīceni darśaneṃ | siṃdhu gheūnī ṭhātī maune| caṃdrodayīṃ kamaḻavaneṃ| miṭhī detī || 35||
verses.meaning: Just as the oceans fall silent upon beholding Agasti, and lotus groves blossom at the moon's rise, so too do these things occur naturally.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो पाबो उचलिला । मदमुख न ठेविती खालां । गर्जोनि पुढां जाला । सिंहु जरी ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso pābo ucalilā | madamukha na ṭhevitī khālāṃ | garjoni puḍhāṃ jālā | siṃhu jarī || 36||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Even if a lion, roaring, comes forward, will a mad elephant put its foot down?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा जो धीरु । उठलिया अंतरु । मनादिकें व्यापारु । सांडिती उभी ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā jo dhīru | uṭhaliyā aṃtaru | manādikeṃ vyāpāru | sāṃḍitī ubhī || 37||
verses.meaning: Similarly, when such steadfastness arises within, the activities of the mind and senses cease completely.

verses.shloka_devanagari: डइद्रियां विषयांचिया गांठी । अपैसया सुटती किरीटी। मन मायेच्या पोटीं । रिगती दाही ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ḍaidriyāṃ viṣayāṃciyā gāṃṭhī | apaisayā suṭatī kirīṭī| mana māyecyā poṭīṃ | rigatī dāhī || 38||
verses.meaning: O Kiriti, the knots of the senses with their objects spontaneously unravel, and the mind, along with the ten senses, enters the womb of Maya.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अधोर्ध्व गूढें काढी । प्राण नवांची पेंडी । बांधोनि घाली उडी । मध्यमेमाजीं ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: adhordhva gūḍheṃ kāḍhī | prāṇa navāṃcī peṃḍī | bāṃdhoni ghālī uḍī | madhyamemājīṃ || 39||
verses.meaning: The yogi, by drawing the upward and downward breaths, binds them into a single bundle and plunges them into the Sushumna Nadi.

verses.shloka_devanagari: संकल्पविकल्पांचें लुगडें। सांडूनि मन उघडें। बुद्धि मागिळेकडे । उगीचि बेसे॥ ७४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṃkalpavikalpāṃceṃ lugaḍeṃ| sāṃḍūni mana ughaḍeṃ| buddhi māgiḻekaḍe | ugīci bese|| 740||
verses.meaning: Shedding the garment of thoughts and doubts, the mind becomes naked and sits silently, turning towards the intellect.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसी धैेर्यराजें जेणें । मन प्राण करणें । स्वचेष्टांचीं संभाषणे । सांडविजती ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisī dhaieryarājeṃ jeṇeṃ | mana prāṇa karaṇeṃ | svaceṣṭāṃcīṃ saṃbhāṣaṇe | sāṃḍavijatī || 41 ||
verses.meaning: Such is the king of fortitude, by whom the mind and vital breath are made to abandon their own activities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आघवींचि सडीं । ध्यानाच्या आंतुल्या मढीं। कोंडिजती निरवडी। योगाचिये॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga āghavīṃci saḍīṃ | dhyānācyā āṃtulyā maḍhīṃ| koṃḍijatī niravaḍī| yogāciye|| 42||
verses.meaning: Then all the senses, within the sanctuary of meditation, become confined without effort, through the practice of Yoga.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी परमात्मया चक्रवर्ती। उगाणिती जंव हातीं। तंव लांचु न घेतां धृती। धरिजती जिया॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī paramātmayā cakravartī| ugāṇitī jaṃva hātīṃ| taṃva lāṃcu na ghetāṃ dhṛtī| dharijatī jiyā|| 43||
verses.meaning: But when the emperor of the Supreme Self is invoked by hand, then patience is held without taking any bribe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते गा धृती येथें। सात्त्विक हें निरुतें। आईक अर्जूनातें। श्रीकांतु म्हणे॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: te gā dhṛtī yetheṃ| sāttvika heṃ niruteṃ| āīka arjūnāteṃ| śrīkāṃtu mhaṇe|| 44||
verses.meaning: Lord Krishna said to Arjuna, "Now listen, Arjuna, I will tell you about the steadfastness that is truly sattvic."

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि होऊनियां शरीरी । स्वर्गसंसाराच्या दोहीं घरीं । नांदे जो पोटभरी । त्रिवर्गोपायें ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi hoūniyāṃ śarīrī | svargasaṃsārācyā dohīṃ gharīṃ | nāṃde jo poṭabharī | trivargopāyeṃ || 45 ||
verses.meaning: And having taken a body, he dwells contentedly in both abodes of heaven and worldly life, by means of the three-fold pursuits (Dharma, Artha, Kama).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो मनोरथांच्या सागरीं। धर्मार्थकामांच्या तारुवावरी । जेणें धेर्यबळें करी । क्रिया वणिज॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to manorathāṃcyā sāgarīṃ| dharmārthakāmāṃcyā tāruvāvarī | jeṇeṃ dheryabaḻeṃ karī | kriyā vaṇija|| 46||
verses.meaning: He, with the strength of his unwavering resolve, engages in the commerce of actions, navigating the ocean of desires upon the ship of Dharma, Artha, and Kama.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें कर्म भांडवला सूये। तयाची चौगुणी येती पाहे। येवढें सायास साहे। जया धृती॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ karma bhāṃḍavalā sūye| tayācī cauguṇī yetī pāhe| yevaḍheṃ sāyāsa sāhe| jayā dhṛtī|| 47||
verses.meaning: The effort made in performing actions, when undertaken with unwavering resolve, yields a fourfold return.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते गा धृती राजस पार्था येथ परियेस। आतां आइक तामस। तिसरी जे कां॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: te gā dhṛtī rājasa pārthā yetha pariyesa| ātāṃ āika tāmasa| tisarī je kāṃ|| 48||
verses.meaning: O Partha, you have now heard about the steadfastness of the passionate (Rajasic) nature. Now listen to the third, which is of the ignorant (Tamasic) nature.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सर्वाधमें गुणें। जयाचें का रूपा येणें। कोळसा काळेपणें। घडला जैसा॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sarvādhameṃ guṇeṃ| jayāceṃ kā rūpā yeṇeṃ| koḻasā kāḻepaṇeṃ| ghaḍalā jaisā|| 49||
verses.meaning: Just as charcoal is formed by its inherent blackness, so too, all dharmas and qualities come into being through Him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अहो प्राकृत आणि हीनु। तयाही कीं गुणत्वाचा मानु। परी न म्हणिजे पुण्यजनु। राक्षसु काई ॥ ७५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aho prākṛta āṇi hīnu| tayāhī kīṃ guṇatvācā mānu| parī na mhaṇije puṇyajanu| rākṣasu kāī || 750||
verses.meaning: Even if someone is ordinary and lowly, and possesses good qualities, they are not called a virtuous person. What then of a demon?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं ग्रहांमाजीं इंगुळु । तयातें म्हणिजे मंगळु। तैसा तमीं धसाळु। गुणशब्दु हा॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ grahāṃmājīṃ iṃguḻu | tayāteṃ mhaṇije maṃgaḻu| taisā tamīṃ dhasāḻu| guṇaśabdu hā|| 51||
verses.meaning: Just as among the planets, the red one is called Mars, so too, in the darkness of ignorance, this word 'guna' (quality) is a stumbling block.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे सर्वदोषांचा वबसौटा । तमचि कामऊनि सुभटा । उभारिला आंगवठा । जया नराचा ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: je sarvadoṣāṃcā vabasauṭā | tamaci kāmaūni subhaṭā | ubhārilā āṃgavaṭhā | jayā narācā || 52||
verses.meaning: He who has burnt away all faults, and by doing so, has built up the spiritual body of that person.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो आळसु सूनि असे कांखे। म्हणौनि निद्रे कहीं न मुके । पापें पोषितां दुःखें॥ न सांडिजे जेवीं ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: to āḻasu sūni ase kāṃkhe| mhaṇauni nidre kahīṃ na muke | pāpeṃ poṣitāṃ duḥkheṃ|| na sāṃḍije jevīṃ || 53||
verses.meaning: Just as a lazy person carries a burden under their arm and therefore never escapes sleep, similarly, one does not abandon sins even when nourished by sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि देहधनाचिया आवडी । सदा भय तयातें न सांडी। वबिसंबूं न सके धोंडीं। काठिण्य जैसें ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi dehadhanāciyā āvaḍī | sadā bhaya tayāteṃ na sāṃḍī| vabisaṃbūṃ na sake dhoṃḍīṃ| kāṭhiṇya jaiseṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: And due to the attachment to the body and wealth, fear never leaves them, just as a stone cannot abandon its hardness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पदार्थजातीं स्नेहो। बांधे म्हणौनि तो शोकें ठावो। केळा न शके पाप जावों। कृतघ्नौनि जैसें ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi padārthajātīṃ sneho| bāṃdhe mhaṇauni to śokeṃ ṭhāvo| keḻā na śake pāpa jāvoṃ| kṛtaghnauni jaiseṃ || 55||
verses.meaning: And because of attachment to material things, sorrow takes hold, just as sin cannot be removed from an ungrateful person.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि असंतोष जीवेंसीं। धरूनि ठेला अहर्निशीं। म्हणौनि मैत्री तेणेंसीं । विषादें केली ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi asaṃtoṣa jīveṃsīṃ| dharūni ṭhelā aharniśīṃ| mhaṇauni maitrī teṇeṃsīṃ | viṣādeṃ kelī || 56||
verses.meaning: And because of this constant dissatisfaction with life, he befriended sorrow.

verses.shloka_devanagari: लसणातें न सांडी गंधी । कां अपथ्यशीळातें व्याधी । तैसी केली मरणावधी । विषादें तया ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: lasaṇāteṃ na sāṃḍī gaṃdhī | kāṃ apathyaśīḻāteṃ vyādhī | taisī kelī maraṇāvadhī | viṣādeṃ tayā || 57||
verses.meaning: Just as garlic does not lose its strong smell, or a sick person does not abandon their unhealthy habits, so too did he cling to sorrow until his death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि वयसा वित्तकामु। ययांचा वाढवी संभ्रमु। म्हणौनि मदें आश्रमु। तोचि केला॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi vayasā vittakāmu| yayāṃcā vāḍhavī saṃbhramu| mhaṇauni madeṃ āśramu| toci kelā|| 58||
verses.meaning: And because of age, wealth, and desire, their confusion increases, therefore, they have made intoxication their abode.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आगीतें न सांडी तापु। सळातें जातीचा सापु। कां जगाचा वैरी वासिपु। अखंडु जैसा ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āgīteṃ na sāṃḍī tāpu| saḻāteṃ jātīcā sāpu| kāṃ jagācā vairī vāsipu| akhaṃḍu jaisā || 59||
verses.meaning: Just as fire does not abandon its heat, a snake does not abandon its inherent venom, or Vasuki (the king of serpents) does not abandon his eternal enmity towards the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी शरीरातें काळु। न विसंबे कवणे वेळु। तैसा आथी अढळु। तामसीं मदु ॥ ७६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī śarīrāteṃ kāḻu| na visaṃbe kavaṇe veḻu| taisā āthī aḍhaḻu| tāmasīṃ madu || 760||
verses.meaning: Just as death does not forget the body at any time, so too is the unwavering intoxication of Tamas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं पांचही हे निद्रादिक। तामसाच्या ठाई दोख। जिया धृती देख। धरिलें आहाती ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ pāṃcahī he nidrādika| tāmasācyā ṭhāī dokha| jiyā dhṛtī dekha| dharileṃ āhātī || 61||
verses.meaning: Thus, these five, sleep and the like, are faults inherent in Tamas, which are held by such a resolve.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये गा धृती नांवें । तामसी येथ हें जाणावें । म्हणितलें तेणें देवें। जगाचेनि॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye gā dhṛtī nāṃveṃ | tāmasī yetha heṃ jāṇāveṃ | mhaṇitaleṃ teṇeṃ deveṃ| jagāceni|| 62||
verses.meaning: That is called Tamasic steadfastness, know this, said the Lord of the universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं त्रिविध जे बुद्धि। कीजे कर्मनिशचयो आधि। तो धृती या सिन्दि। नेइजो येथ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ trividha je buddhi| kīje karmaniśacayo ādhi| to dhṛtī yā sindi| neijo yetha|| 63||
verses.meaning: Thus, the intellect, which is of three kinds, first determines the action. This is called 'Dhriti' (steadfastness) here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सूर्ये मार्ग गोचरु होये। आणि तो चालती कौर पाये। परी चालणें तें आहे। धैर्ये जेवीं॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: sūrye mārga gocaru hoye| āṇi to cālatī kaura pāye| parī cālaṇeṃ teṃ āhe| dhairye jevīṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun illuminates the path, making it visible, and one walks with their feet, yet the act of walking itself is sustained by patience and perseverance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी बुद्दि कर्मातें दावी। ते 'करणसामग्री निफजवी। परी निफजावया होआवी। धीरता जे॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī buddi karmāteṃ dāvī| te 'karaṇasāmagrī niphajavī| parī niphajāvayā hoāvī| dhīratā je|| 65||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the intellect reveals actions and brings forth the means to perform them, but for these to manifest, there must be patience.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते हे गा तुजप्रति। सांगितली त्रिविध धृति। यया कर्मत्रया निष्पत्ति। जालिया मग॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: te he gā tujaprati| sāṃgitalī trividha dhṛti| yayā karmatrayā niṣpatti| jāliyā maga|| 66||
verses.meaning: Thus, I have explained to you the three types of steadfastness, by which the three kinds of actions are accomplished.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ फळ जें एक निफजे। सुख जयातें म्हणिजे । तेंही त्रिविध जाणिजे। कर्मबशें ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha phaḻa jeṃ eka niphaje| sukha jayāteṃ mhaṇije | teṃhī trividha jāṇije| karmabaśeṃ || 67||
verses.meaning: Here, the one fruit that is produced, which is called happiness, that too is known to be threefold due to the influence of actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी फळरूप तें सुख। त्रिगुणी भेदलें देख । विवंचूं आतां चोख । चोखीं बोलीं ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī phaḻarūpa teṃ sukha| triguṇī bhedaleṃ dekha | vivaṃcūṃ ātāṃ cokha | cokhīṃ bolīṃ || 68||
verses.meaning: That fruit-like happiness, however, is seen to be divided by the three Gunas. Let us now clearly consider this in pure words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी चोखी ते कैसी सांगें। पैं घेवों जातां बोलबगें। कानींचियेही लागे। हातींचा मळु ॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī cokhī te kaisī sāṃgeṃ| paiṃ ghevoṃ jātāṃ bolabageṃ| kānīṃciyehī lāge| hātīṃcā maḻu || 69||
verses.meaning: But how can I explain its purity? If one tries to grasp it with words, even the dirt from one's hands clings to the ears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जयाचेनि अव्हेरें। अबधानही होय बाहिरें। तेणें आइक हो आंतरें। ४५८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी जीवाचेनि जीवें ॥ ७७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jayāceni avhereṃ| abadhānahī hoya bāhireṃ| teṇeṃ āika ho āṃtareṃ| 458 śrījñāneśvarī jīvāceni jīveṃ || 770||
verses.meaning: Therefore, listen with your whole heart, with the very life of your being, to that which, if neglected, even attention itself becomes external.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें म्हणौनि देवो । त्रिविधा सुखाचा प्रस्तावो। मांडला तो निर्वाहो। निरूपित असे॥७१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ mhaṇauni devo | trividhā sukhācā prastāvo| māṃḍalā to nirvāho| nirūpita ase||719||
verses.meaning: Having said this, the Lord then expounded upon the three kinds of happiness, and that exposition is now being narrated.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणे सुखत्रयसंज्ञा। सांगों म्हणौनि प्रतिज्ञा बोलिलो तें प्राज्ञा! ऐक आतां॥७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇe sukhatrayasaṃjñā| sāṃgoṃ mhaṇauni pratijñā bolilo teṃ prājñā! aika ātāṃ||72||
verses.meaning: I said I would explain the three kinds of happiness, and I made that promise, O wise one! Now listen.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सुख तें गा किरीटी। दाविजेल तुज दिठी। जें आत्मयाचिये भेटी। जीवासि होय॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sukha teṃ gā kirīṭī| dāvijela tuja diṭhī| jeṃ ātmayāciye bheṭī| jīvāsi hoya|| 73||
verses.meaning: Then, O Kiriti, I will show you that happiness which the soul experiences upon meeting the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मात्रेचेनि मापें । दिव्यौषध जैसें घेपे। कां कथिलाचें कीजे रूपें। रसभावनीं ॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī mātreceni māpeṃ | divyauṣadha jaiseṃ ghepe| kāṃ kathilāceṃ kīje rūpeṃ| rasabhāvanīṃ || 74||
verses.meaning: Just as a divine medicine is taken in measured doses, or as base metal is transformed into gold through alchemical processes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना लवणाचें जळु। होआवया दोनि चार वेळु। देऊनि सांडिजती ढाळु। तोयाचे जेबीं ॥ ७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā lavaṇāceṃ jaḻu| hoāvayā doni cāra veḻu| deūni sāṃḍijatī ḍhāḻu| toyāce jebīṃ || 75||
verses.meaning: Just as a handful of salt is dissolved in water, and the water is then discarded, so too are the various forms of the world dissolved and discarded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं जालेनि सुखलेशें । जीवु भाविलिया अभ्यासें । जीवपणाचें नासे । दुःख जेथें ॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ jāleni sukhaleśeṃ | jīvu bhāviliyā abhyāseṃ | jīvapaṇāceṃ nāse | duḥkha jetheṃ || 76||
verses.meaning: In the same way, when the soul, through spiritual practice, experiences even a trace of this bliss, the suffering of its individual existence is destroyed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें येथ आत्मसुख । जालें असे त्रिगुणात्मक । तेंही सांगों एकेक। रूप आतां॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ yetha ātmasukha | jāleṃ ase triguṇātmaka | teṃhī sāṃgoṃ ekeka| rūpa ātāṃ|| 77||
verses.meaning: That very bliss of the Self, which has become threefold due to the three Gunas, I shall now explain, each form one by one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां चंदनाचें बुड । सर्पी जैसें दुवाड। कां निधानाचें तोंड । विवसिया जेवीं ॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ caṃdanāceṃ buḍa | sarpī jaiseṃ duvāḍa| kāṃ nidhānāceṃ toṃḍa | vivasiyā jevīṃ || 78||
verses.meaning: Now, just as a snake is an adversary to the base of a sandalwood tree, or as a treasure's entrance is to a foolish person.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा स्वर्गीचें गोमटें। आडव यागसंकटें। कां बाळपण दासटें। त्रासकाळें ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā svargīceṃ gomaṭeṃ| āḍava yāgasaṃkaṭeṃ| kāṃ bāḻapaṇa dāsaṭeṃ| trāsakāḻeṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: Indeed, the beauty of heaven is obstructed by the troubles of sacrificial rituals, or childhood is afflicted by the distress of suffering.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें असो दीपाचिये सिद्धी। अबघड धू आधीं | नातरी तो औषधीं। जिभेचा ठावो ॥ ७८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ aso dīpāciye siddhī| abaghaḍa dhū ādhīṃ | nātarī to auṣadhīṃ| jibhecā ṭhāvo || 780||
verses.meaning: Let this be. Just as a lamp's light cannot be obscured by smoke, or a medicine cannot be tasted by the tongue, so too is the nature of the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयापरी पांडवा । जया सुखाचा रिगावा। विषम तेथ मेळावा । यमदमांचा॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāparī pāṃḍavā | jayā sukhācā rigāvā| viṣama tetha meḻāvā | yamadamāṃcā|| 81||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, for those who seek the abode of such bliss, the difficult path of self-restraint and spiritual discipline becomes their gathering place.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देत सर्वस्नेहा मिठी । आंगीं ऐसें वैराग्य उठी । स्वर्गसंसारा कांटी। काढितचि॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: deta sarvasnehā miṭhī | āṃgīṃ aiseṃ vairāgya uṭhī | svargasaṃsārā kāṃṭī| kāḍhitaci|| 82||
verses.meaning: Embracing all love, such detachment arises within, that it uproots the thorns of heaven and worldly existence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विवेकश्रवणें खरपुसें । जेथ त्रताचरणें कर्कशें। करितां जाती भोकसे । बुल्धयादिकांचे ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: vivekaśravaṇeṃ kharapuseṃ | jetha tratācaraṇeṃ karkaśeṃ| karitāṃ jātī bhokase | buldhayādikāṃce || 83 ||
verses.meaning: Through the sharp and intense practice of discrimination and listening to spiritual teachings, and by undertaking severe penances, the impurities and defects of the intellect and other faculties are removed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुषुम्नेचेनि तोंडें। गिळिजे प्राणापानाचे लोंढे । बोहणियेसीचि येवढें। भारी जेथ॥८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: suṣumneceni toṃḍeṃ| giḻije prāṇāpānāce loṃḍhe | bohaṇiyesīci yevaḍheṃ| bhārī jetha||84||
verses.meaning: Through the mouth of the Sushumna, the surging currents of Prana and Apana are swallowed. This is the great burden that comes with the very beginning of spiritual practice.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें सारसांही विघडतां। होय वबोहाहूनि वत्स काढितां। ना भणंगु दवडितां। भाणयावरुनी ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ sārasāṃhī vighaḍatāṃ| hoya vabohāhūni vatsa kāḍhitāṃ| nā bhaṇaṃgu davaḍitāṃ| bhāṇayāvarunī || 85||
verses.meaning: Just as a swan is distressed when separated from its mate, or a calf when taken from its mother, or a beggar when driven away from the food he is about to receive.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं मायेपुढौनि बाळक । काळें नेतां एकुलतें एक। होय कां उदक। तुटतां मीना॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ māyepuḍhauni bāḻaka | kāḻeṃ netāṃ ekulateṃ eka| hoya kāṃ udaka| tuṭatāṃ mīnā|| 86||
verses.meaning: Just as a fish suffers when water is removed, so does a mother when her only child is taken away by death.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें विषयांचें घर। इंद्रियां सांडितां थोर। युगांतु होय तें बीर । विराग साहाती ॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ viṣayāṃceṃ ghara| iṃdriyāṃ sāṃḍitāṃ thora| yugāṃtu hoya teṃ bīra | virāga sāhātī || 87||
verses.meaning: When the senses abandon their attachment to worldly objects, a great spiritual dissolution occurs, which the brave ascetics endure.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा जया सुखाचा आरंभु। दावी काठिण्याचा क्षोभु। मग क्षीराब्धीं लाभु। अमृताचा जैसा॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā jayā sukhācā āraṃbhu| dāvī kāṭhiṇyācā kṣobhu| maga kṣīrābdhīṃ lābhu| amṛtācā jaisā|| 88||
verses.meaning: Just as the churning of the milk ocean, initially arduous, ultimately yielded the nectar of immortality, so too does the path to true happiness, though seemingly difficult at the outset, ultimately bestow the highest bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पहिलया वैराग्यगरळा। धैर्यशंभु बोडवी गळा । तरी ज्ञानामृतें सोहळा । पाहे जेथें ॥८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: pahilayā vairāgyagaraḻā| dhairyaśaṃbhu boḍavī gaḻā | tarī jñānāmṛteṃ sohaḻā | pāhe jetheṃ ||89||
verses.meaning: First, the poison of dispassion, swallowed by the Shiva of courage, then behold the celebration with the nectar of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं कोलिताही कोपे ऐसें। द्राक्षांचे हिरवेपण असे। तें परिपाकीं कां जैसें। माधुर्य आते ॥ ७९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ kolitāhī kope aiseṃ| drākṣāṃce hiravepaṇa ase| teṃ paripākīṃ kāṃ jaiseṃ| mādhurya āte || 790||
verses.meaning: Just as the greenness of grapes, which might seem unappealing, transforms into sweetness upon ripening.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें वैराग्यादिक तैसें । पिकलिया आत्मप्रकाशें। मग बैराग्येंसींही नाशे । अविद्याजात ॥ ९१९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ vairāgyādika taiseṃ | pikaliyā ātmaprakāśeṃ| maga bairāgyeṃsīṃhī nāśe | avidyājāta || 919 ||
verses.meaning: When such dispassion and other virtues ripen through the light of self-realization, then even dispassion itself, along with all ignorance, is destroyed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां सागरीं गंगा जैसी । आत्मीं मीनल्या बुद्धि तैसी। अद्ठयानंदाची आपैसी। खाणी उघडे॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ sāgarīṃ gaṃgā jaisī | ātmīṃ mīnalyā buddhi taisī| adṭhayānaṃdācī āpaisī| khāṇī ughaḍe|| 92||
verses.meaning: Just as the Ganges merges into the ocean, so too does the intellect merge into the Self. Then, spontaneously, the mine of supreme bliss opens up.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें स्वानुभवविश्रामें । बैराग्यमूळ जें परिणमे। तें सात्त्विक येणें नामें। बोलिजे सुख॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ svānubhavaviśrāmeṃ | bairāgyamūḻa jeṃ pariṇame| teṃ sāttvika yeṇeṃ nāmeṃ| bolije sukha|| 93||
verses.meaning: Such is the bliss that culminates in detachment, rooted in the repose of self-realization, and it is known by the name of Sattvic (pure) happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि विषषयेंद्रियां। मेळु होतां धनंजया । जें सुख जाय थडिया । सांडूनि दोन्ही ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi viṣaṣayeṃdriyāṃ| meḻu hotāṃ dhanaṃjayā | jeṃ sukha jāya thaḍiyā | sāṃḍūni donhī || 94||
verses.meaning: And when the senses meet their objects, O Dhananjaya, the joy that transcends both the senses and their objects, that is the true joy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अधिकारिया रिगतां गांबो। होय जैसा उत्साहो। कां रिणावरी विवाहो । विस्तारिला ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: adhikāriyā rigatāṃ gāṃbo| hoya jaisā utsāho| kāṃ riṇāvarī vivāho | vistārilā || 95||
verses.meaning: Just as a person of authority, upon entering a village, is met with great enthusiasm, or as a wedding celebration expands with joy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना रोगिया जिभेपासीं । केळें गोड साखरेंसीं । कां बचनागाची जैसी। मधुरता पहिली ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā rogiyā jibhepāsīṃ | keḻeṃ goḍa sākhareṃsīṃ | kāṃ bacanāgācī jaisī| madhuratā pahilī || 96||
verses.meaning: Just as a banana tastes sweet with sugar to many sick people, or as the aconite plant initially tastes sweet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पहिलें संवचोराचें मैत्र । हाटभेटीचें कलत्र। कां लाघवियाचे विचित्र। विनोद ते॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pahileṃ saṃvacorāceṃ maitra | hāṭabheṭīceṃ kalatra| kāṃ lāghaviyāce vicitra| vinoda te|| 97||
verses.meaning: First, the friendship of a thief, the wife met in a market, or the strange and amusing tricks of a magician.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें विषयेंद्रियदोखीं। जें सुख जीवातें पोखी। मग उपडिला खडकोौं। हंसु जैसा॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ viṣayeṃdriyadokhīṃ| jeṃ sukha jīvāteṃ pokhī| maga upaḍilā khaḍakoauṃ| haṃsu jaisā|| 98||
verses.meaning: Just as a swan, when its wings are plucked, is unable to fly, so too is the soul unable to experience true happiness when it is entangled in the pleasures of the senses.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी जोडी आघवी आटे । जीविताचा ठाय फिटे । सुकृताचियाही सुटे । धनाची गांठी ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī joḍī āghavī āṭe | jīvitācā ṭhāya phiṭe | sukṛtāciyāhī suṭe | dhanācī gāṃṭhī || 99||
verses.meaning: Similarly, all accumulated wealth perishes, the very foundation of life crumbles, and even the knot of merit (sukrut) loosens, along with all riches.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिक भोगिलें जें कांहीं। तें स्वप्न तैसें होय नाहीं । मग हानिच्याचि घाई। लोळावें उरे॥ ८००॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇika bhogileṃ jeṃ kāṃhīṃ| teṃ svapna taiseṃ hoya nāhīṃ | maga hānicyāci ghāī| loḻāveṃ ure|| 800||
verses.meaning: Whatever else was experienced, that becomes like a dream, non-existent. Then, only the agony of loss remains to wallow in.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें आपत्ती जें सुख। ऐहिकीं परिणमे देख । परत्रीं कीर विख। होऊनि परते॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ āpattī jeṃ sukha| aihikīṃ pariṇame dekha | paratrīṃ kīra vikha| hoūni parate|| 1||
verses.meaning: Such is the nature of adversity that it transforms into happiness in this world, but in the afterlife, it surely returns as poison.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे इंद्रियजाता लळा। दिधलिया धर्माचा मळा। जाळूनि भोगिजे सोहळा । विषयांचा जेथ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: je iṃdriyajātā laḻā| didhaliyā dharmācā maḻā| jāḻūni bhogije sohaḻā | viṣayāṃcā jetha|| 2||
verses.meaning: Where the garden of righteousness, cultivated with affection for the senses, is burnt down, and the festivities of worldly pleasures are enjoyed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ पातकें बांधिती थावो। तियें नरकीं देती ठावो। जेणें सुखें हा अपावो। परत्री ऐसा॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha pātakeṃ bāṃdhitī thāvo| tiyeṃ narakīṃ detī ṭhāvo| jeṇeṃ sukheṃ hā apāvo| paratrī aisā|| 3||
verses.meaning: There, sins take root, and they lead one to hell. Such pleasures, in the afterlife, become a cause for ruin.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं नामें विष महुरें। परी मारूनि अंतीं खरें। तैसें आदि जें गोडिरें। अंतीं कडू॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ nāmeṃ viṣa mahureṃ| parī mārūni aṃtīṃ khareṃ| taiseṃ ādi jeṃ goḍireṃ| aṃtīṃ kaḍū|| 4||
verses.meaning: Just as poison, though sweet at first, ultimately kills, so too that which initially seems pleasant turns bitter in the end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पार्था तें सुख साचें । वळिलें आहे रजाचें। म्हणौनि न शिवें तयाचें । आंग कहीं ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: pārthā teṃ sukha sāceṃ | vaḻileṃ āhe rajāceṃ| mhaṇauni na śiveṃ tayāceṃ | āṃga kahīṃ || 5||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, that happiness is truly born of Rajas (passion/activity), and therefore, its true nature never touches the self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि अपेयाचेनि पानें। अखाद्याचेनि भोजनें । स्वैरस्त्रीसंनिधानें । होय जें सुख॥६॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi apeyāceni pāneṃ| akhādyāceni bhojaneṃ | svairastrīsaṃnidhāneṃ | hoya jeṃ sukha||6||
verses.meaning: And the pleasure that arises from drinking what is forbidden, from eating what is inedible, and from the company of a wanton woman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां पुढीलांचेनि मारें। नातरी परस्वापहारें। जें सुख अवतरे । ४६० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी भाटांच्या बोलीं ॥७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ puḍhīlāṃceni māreṃ| nātarī parasvāpahāreṃ| jeṃ sukha avatare | 460 śrījñāneśvarī bhāṭāṃcyā bolīṃ ||7||
verses.meaning: Or by the blows of others, or by the theft of another's property, the happiness that arises, 460 In the words of Shri Dnyaneshwari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें आलस्यावरी पोखिजे। निद्रेमाजीं जें देखिजे। जयाच्या आद्यंतीं भुलिजे। आपुली वाट॥८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ ālasyāvarī pokhije| nidremājīṃ jeṃ dekhije| jayācyā ādyaṃtīṃ bhulije| āpulī vāṭa||8||
verses.meaning: That which is nourished by laziness, that which is seen in sleep, that which causes one to forget their own path from beginning to end.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें गा सुख पार्था । तामस जाण सर्वथा हें बहु न सांगोंचि जे कथा। असंभाव्य हे ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ gā sukha pārthā | tāmasa jāṇa sarvathā heṃ bahu na sāṃgoṃci je kathā| asaṃbhāvya he || 9||
verses.meaning: O Partha, know that such happiness is entirely born of ignorance. I will not elaborate much on this, as its story is inconceivable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें कर्मभेदें मुदलें। फळसुखही त्रिधा जालें। तें हें यथागमें केलें गोचर तुज ॥ ८१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ karmabhedeṃ mudaleṃ| phaḻasukhahī tridhā jāleṃ| teṃ heṃ yathāgameṃ keleṃ gocara tuja || 810||
verses.meaning: Thus, due to the distinctions in actions, the happiness derived from their fruits also becomes threefold. This has been revealed to you according to the scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें कर्ता कर्म कर्मफळ। ये त्रिपुटी येकी केवळ। वांचूनि कांहींचि नसे स्थूल-। सूक्ष्मीं इये॥ ११॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ kartā karma karmaphaḻa| ye tripuṭī yekī kevaḻa| vāṃcūni kāṃhīṃci nase sthūla-| sūkṣmīṃ iye|| 11||
verses.meaning: The doer, the deed, and the fruit of the deed—these three are fundamentally one. Apart from this unity, nothing exists in the gross or subtle realms.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि हे तंव त्रिपुटी । तिहीं गुणीं इहीं किरीटी । गुंफिली असे पटीं। तांतुवीं जैसी ॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi he taṃva tripuṭī | tihīṃ guṇīṃ ihīṃ kirīṭī | guṃphilī ase paṭīṃ| tāṃtuvīṃ jaisī || 12||
verses.meaning: And this triad, O Kiriti, is woven by these three Gunas, like threads in a cloth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि प्रकृतीच्या अवलोकीं। न बंधिजे इहीं सत्त्वादिकीं। तैसी स्वर्गी ना मृत्युलो कीं । आथी वस्तु॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni prakṛtīcyā avalokīṃ| na baṃdhije ihīṃ sattvādikīṃ| taisī svargī nā mṛtyulo kīṃ | āthī vastu|| 13||
verses.meaning: Therefore, that Reality is not bound by the observation of Prakriti, nor by these qualities like Sattva. Such a Reality exists neither in heaven nor on earth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कैंचा लोंबेबीण कांबळा । मातियेवीण मोदळा । कां जळेंबीण कल्लोळा । होणें आहे॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kaiṃcā loṃbebīṇa kāṃbaḻā | mātiyevīṇa modaḻā | kāṃ jaḻeṃbīṇa kalloḻā | hoṇeṃ āhe|| 14||
verses.meaning: How can there be a blanket without wool? How can there be a sweetmeat without flour? Or how can there be waves without water?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें न होनि गुणाचें । सृष्टीची रचना रचे । ऐसें नाहींचि गा साचें। प्राणिजात॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ na honi guṇāceṃ | sṛṣṭīcī racanā race | aiseṃ nāhīṃci gā sāceṃ| prāṇijāta|| 15||
verses.meaning: It is not that the creation of the world is formed without qualities. Indeed, there is no such thing as a living being that is not composed of qualities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यालागीं हें सकळ| तिहीं गुणांचेंचि केवळ। घडलें आहे निखिळ। ऐसें जाण॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yālāgīṃ heṃ sakaḻa| tihīṃ guṇāṃceṃci kevaḻa| ghaḍaleṃ āhe nikhiḻa| aiseṃ jāṇa|| 16||
verses.meaning: Therefore, know that all this creation is entirely made up of these three Gunas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गुणीं देवां त्रयी लाविली । गुणीं लोकीं त्रिपुटी पाडिली । चतुर्वर्णा घातली । सिनानीं उळिगें ॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: guṇīṃ devāṃ trayī lāvilī | guṇīṃ lokīṃ tripuṭī pāḍilī | caturvarṇā ghātalī | sinānīṃ uḻigeṃ || 17||
verses.meaning: The Gunas (qualities of nature) have created the trinity of gods. The Gunas have divided people into three classes. They have also established the four varnas (social orders) with their respective duties and services.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेचि चारी वर्ण । पुससी जरी कोण कोण। तरी जयां मुख्य ब्राह्मण । धुरेचे कां॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teci cārī varṇa | pusasī jarī koṇa koṇa| tarī jayāṃ mukhya brāhmaṇa | dhurece kāṃ|| 18||
verses.meaning: If you ask who these four varnas are, then the Brahmins are considered the foremost among them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येर क्षत्रिय वैश्य दोन्ही। तेही ब्राह्मणाच्याचि मानिजे मानीं॥ जे ते बैदिकविधानीं। योग्य म्हणौनि॥१९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yera kṣatriya vaiśya donhī| tehī brāhmaṇācyāci mānije mānīṃ|| je te baidikavidhānīṃ| yogya mhaṇauni||19||
verses.meaning: The other two varnas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, are also considered to be within the Brahminical fold, because they too are deemed worthy of Vedic rituals.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चौथा शूद्रु जो धनंजया । वेदीं लागु नाहीं तया । तऱही वृत्ति वर्णत्रया-। अधीन तयाची ॥ ८२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: cauthā śūdru jo dhanaṃjayā | vedīṃ lāgu nāhīṃ tayā | taṟahī vṛtti varṇatrayā-| adhīna tayācī || 820||
verses.meaning: The fourth, O Dhananjaya, is the Shudra, who has no right to the Vedas. Nevertheless, his conduct is subservient to the three varnas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तिये वृत्तीचिया जवळिका। वर्णा ब्राह्मणादिकां। शूद्रही कौं देखा। चौथा जाला॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tiye vṛttīciyā javaḻikā| varṇā brāhmaṇādikāṃ| śūdrahī kauṃ dekhā| cauthā jālā|| 21||
verses.meaning: Due to the proximity of this mental state, the Brahmins and other varnas, and even the Shudras, all become one, as if a fourth state has emerged.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा फुलाचेनि सांगातें। तांतु तुरंबिजे श्रीमंतें। तैसें द्विजसंगें शूद्रातें। स्वीकारी श्रुती ॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā phulāceni sāṃgāteṃ| tāṃtu turaṃbije śrīmaṃteṃ| taiseṃ dvijasaṃgeṃ śūdrāteṃ| svīkārī śrutī || 22||
verses.meaning: Just as a thread, by association with a flower, is adorned by the wealthy, so too does the Shruti (Vedas) accept a Shudra (a person of the fourth varna) through association with a Brahmin (a person of the first varna).

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसैसी गा पार्था। हे चातुर्वर्ण्यव्यवस्था । करूं आतां कर्मपथा। यांचिया रूपा॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisaisī gā pārthā| he cāturvarṇyavyavasthā | karūṃ ātāṃ karmapathā| yāṃciyā rūpā|| 23||
verses.meaning: Thus, Arjuna, I have now established the system of the four varnas (social orders) as the very form of the path of action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिहीं गुणीं ते वर्ण चारी । जन्ममृत्यूंचिये कातरी । चुकोनियां ईश्वरी । पैठे होती ॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jihīṃ guṇīṃ te varṇa cārī | janmamṛtyūṃciye kātarī | cukoniyāṃ īśvarī | paiṭhe hotī || 24||
verses.meaning: Through these virtues, all four varnas, escaping the scissors of birth and death, attain entry into the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिये आत्मप्रकृतीचे इहीं। गुणीं सत्त्वादिकीं तिहीं । कर्मे चौघां चहूं ठाई । वांटिली वर्णा॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiye ātmaprakṛtīce ihīṃ| guṇīṃ sattvādikīṃ tihīṃ | karme caughāṃ cahūṃ ṭhāī | vāṃṭilī varṇā|| 25||
verses.meaning: From the very nature of the Self, these three qualities - Sattva and others - have distributed actions among the four varnas, each in its own place.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसें बापें जोडिलें लेका । वांटिले सूर्ये मार्ग पांथिकां । नाना व्यापार सेवकां। स्वामी जैसें ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaiseṃ bāpeṃ joḍileṃ lekā | vāṃṭile sūrye mārga pāṃthikāṃ | nānā vyāpāra sevakāṃ| svāmī jaiseṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: Just as a father accumulates for his son, or the sun illuminates the path for travelers, or a master provides for his servants.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी प्रकृतीच्या गुणीं । जया कर्माची वेल्हावणी । केली आहे वर्णी । चहूं इहीं ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī prakṛtīcyā guṇīṃ | jayā karmācī velhāvaṇī | kelī āhe varṇī | cahūṃ ihīṃ || 27||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the actions that are performed due to the qualities of Prakriti (nature), and which are described by the four varnas (social orders).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ सत्त्वें आपल्या आंगीं । समीननिमीन भागीं। दोघे केळे नियोगी। ब्राह्मण क्षत्रिय॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha sattveṃ āpalyā āṃgīṃ | samīnanimīna bhāgīṃ| doghe keḻe niyogī| brāhmaṇa kṣatriya|| 28||
verses.meaning: There, by their inherent nature, the Brahmin and Kshatriya, in equal measure, are both appointed to their respective duties.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि रज परी सात्त्विक । तेथ ठेविळे बैश्य लोक। रजचि तमभेसक। तेथ शूद्र ते गा॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi raja parī sāttvika | tetha ṭheviḻe baiśya loka| rajaci tamabhesaka| tetha śūdra te gā|| 29||
verses.meaning: And where the Rajas quality is pure and sattvic, there are placed the Vaishya people. Where Rajas is mixed with Tamas, there are the Shudras.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा येकाचि प्राणिवृंदा। भेदु चतुर्वर्णधा। गुणींचि प्रबुद्धा । केला जाण॥ ८३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā yekāci prāṇivṛṃdā| bhedu caturvarṇadhā| guṇīṃci prabuddhā | kelā jāṇa|| 830||
verses.meaning: Thus, among all living beings, the distinction of the four varnas (social orders) is understood to be based on their inherent qualities and attributes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आपुलें ठेविलें जैसें। आइतेंचि दीपें दिसे। गुणभिन्न कर्म तैसें। शास्त्र दावी॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga āpuleṃ ṭhevileṃ jaiseṃ| āiteṃci dīpeṃ dise| guṇabhinna karma taiseṃ| śāstra dāvī|| 31||
verses.meaning: Just as a lamp reveals what is already present, so too do the scriptures illuminate actions that are distinct due to their inherent qualities.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेंचि आतां कोण कोण। वर्णविहिताचें लक्षण। हें सांगों ऐक श्रवण-। सौभाग्यनिधी ॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃci ātāṃ koṇa koṇa| varṇavihitāceṃ lakṣaṇa| heṃ sāṃgoṃ aika śravaṇa-| saubhāgyanidhī || 32||
verses.meaning: Now, I will describe the characteristics of that which is to be described, so listen, O treasure of fortunate ears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सर्वेद्रियांचिया वृत्ती । घेऊनि आपुल्या हातीं। बुद्धि आत्मया मिळे येकांतीं । प्रिया जैसी ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sarvedriyāṃciyā vṛttī | gheūni āpulyā hātīṃ| buddhi ātmayā miḻe yekāṃtīṃ | priyā jaisī || 33||
verses.meaning: Just as a beloved meets her lover in solitude, so too does the intellect, taking hold of all the senses' functions, unite with the Self in seclusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा बुद्धीचा उपरमु । तया नाम म्हणिपे शमु। तो गुण गा उपक्रमु। जया कर्माचा ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā buddhīcā uparamu | tayā nāma mhaṇipe śamu| to guṇa gā upakramu| jayā karmācā || 34||
verses.meaning: Such a turning away of the intellect is called 'Shama'. This quality is the beginning of any action.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि बाहोंद्रियांचें धेंडे । पिटूनि बिधीचेनि दंडें। नेदिजे अधर्माकडे। कहींचि जावों॥३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi bāhoṃdriyāṃceṃ dheṃḍe | piṭūni bidhīceni daṃḍeṃ| nedije adharmākaḍe| kahīṃci jāvoṃ||35||
verses.meaning: And the senses, like unruly children, are disciplined with the rod of righteous conduct, so that they never stray towards unrighteousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो पैं गा शमा बिरजा। दमु गुण जेथ दुजा। आणि स्वधर्माचिया बोजा । जिणें जें 'कां॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: to paiṃ gā śamā birajā| damu guṇa jetha dujā| āṇi svadharmāciyā bojā | jiṇeṃ jeṃ 'kāṃ|| 36||
verses.meaning: That very peace, which is free from the blemish of duality, and which lightens the burden of one's own dharma, is indeed the true victory.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सटवीचिये रातीं। न विसंबिजे जेवीं वाती। तैसा ईश्‍वरनिर्णयो चित्तीं । वाहणें सदा ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: saṭavīciye rātīṃ| na visaṃbije jevīṃ vātī| taisā īś‍varanirṇayo cittīṃ | vāhaṇeṃ sadā || 37||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not forget a lamp on the night of Saptami, so too should the conviction of God's existence always be carried in the heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया नाम तप। तें तिजया गुणाचें रूप। आणि शौचही निष्पाप। द्विविध जेथ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā nāma tapa| teṃ tijayā guṇāceṃ rūpa| āṇi śaucahī niṣpāpa| dvividha jetha|| 38||
verses.meaning: That name is penance, it is the very form of her qualities, and purity is also sinless, of two kinds there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मन भावशुद्धी भरलें। आंग क्रिया अळंकारिलें। ऐसें सबाह्य जियालें। साजिरें जें कां॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: mana bhāvaśuddhī bharaleṃ| āṃga kriyā aḻaṃkārileṃ| aiseṃ sabāhya jiyāleṃ| sājireṃ jeṃ kāṃ|| 39||
verses.meaning: When the mind is filled with purity of intention, and the body is adorned with virtuous actions, such a being, alive both internally and externally, is truly beautiful.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया नाम शौच पार्था। तो कर्मी गुण जये चौथा । आणि पृथ्वीचिया परी सर्वथा । सर्व जें साहाणें ॥ ८४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā nāma śauca pārthā| to karmī guṇa jaye cauthā | āṇi pṛthvīciyā parī sarvathā | sarva jeṃ sāhāṇeṃ || 840||
verses.meaning: O Partha, that name is purity, that is the fourth quality in action, and like the earth, it is the endurance of everything.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते गा क्षमा पांडवा। गुण जेथ पांचवा । स्वरांमाजीं सुहावा। पंचमु जैसा ॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: te gā kṣamā pāṃḍavā| guṇa jetha pāṃcavā | svarāṃmājīṃ suhāvā| paṃcamu jaisā || 41||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, that forgiveness is the fifth quality, just as the fifth note is the most pleasing among the musical notes.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि वांकडेनि बोघेंसीं। गंगा वाहे उजूचि जैसी। कां पुटीं बळला ऊंसीं। गोडी जैसी ॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi vāṃkaḍeni bogheṃsīṃ| gaṃgā vāhe ujūci jaisī| kāṃ puṭīṃ baḻalā ūṃsīṃ| goḍī jaisī || 42||
verses.meaning: Just as the Ganga flows straight despite its crooked banks, or sweetness resides within the twisted sugarcane, so too does true understanding emerge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा विषमांहि जीवां-। लागीं उजुकारु बरवा। तें आर्जव गा साहावा । जेथींचा गुण ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā viṣamāṃhi jīvāṃ-| lāgīṃ ujukāru baravā| teṃ ārjava gā sāhāvā | jethīṃcā guṇa || 43||
verses.meaning: Similarly, even in adverse situations, a straightforward and gentle approach is beneficial for all beings. That humility and simplicity are the qualities that truly endure.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पाणियें प्रयत्ने माळी। अखंड जचे झाडामुळीं। परी तें आघवेंचि फळीं। जाणे जेवीं ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pāṇiyeṃ prayatne māḻī| akhaṃḍa jace jhāḍāmuḻīṃ| parī teṃ āghaveṃci phaḻīṃ| jāṇe jevīṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: Just as a gardener diligently waters the roots of a tree, yet all that effort culminates in the fruit, so too is the ultimate outcome.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें शास्त्राचारें तेणें । ईश्वरूचि येकु पावणें। हें फुडें ४६२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी जें कां जाणणें। तें येथ ज्ञान ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ śāstrācāreṃ teṇeṃ | īśvarūci yeku pāvaṇeṃ| heṃ phuḍeṃ 462 śrījñāneśvarī jeṃ kāṃ jāṇaṇeṃ| teṃ yetha jñāna || 45||
verses.meaning: Similarly, through the practices prescribed by the scriptures, one attains only God. This is the knowledge that is to be understood here.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें गा कर्मी जिये। सातवा गुण होये । आणि विज्ञान हें पाहें। एवंरूप॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ gā karmī jiye| sātavā guṇa hoye | āṇi vijñāna heṃ pāheṃ| evaṃrūpa|| 46||
verses.meaning: That indeed is the seventh quality in action, and behold, this is the form of spiritual knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी सत्त्वशुद्धीचिये वेळे । शास्त्रे कां ध्यानबळें । ईश्‍वरतत्त्वींचि मिळे । निष्टंकबुद्धी ॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī sattvaśuddhīciye veḻe | śāstre kāṃ dhyānabaḻeṃ | īś‍varatattvīṃci miḻe | niṣṭaṃkabuddhī || 47||
verses.meaning: When the mind is purified by sattva, through scriptures or the power of meditation, the intellect becomes firmly fixed in the essence of God.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें विज्ञान बरवें । गुणरत्न जेथ आठवें। आणि आस्तिक्‍्य जाणावें। नववा गुण॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ vijñāna baraveṃ | guṇaratna jetha āṭhaveṃ| āṇi āstik‍ya jāṇāveṃ| navavā guṇa|| 48||
verses.meaning: This knowledge is excellent, where the jewel of virtues is remembered, and faith should be known as the ninth quality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं राजमुद्रा आधथिलिया। प्रजा भजे भलतया। तेवीं शास्त्रें स्वीकारिलिया । मार्गमात्रातें ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ rājamudrā ādhathiliyā| prajā bhaje bhalatayā| tevīṃ śāstreṃ svīkāriliyā | mārgamātrāteṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: Just as subjects obey anyone who holds the royal seal, so too do people follow any path that is accepted by the scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आदरें जें कां मानणें । तें आस्तिक्य मी म्हणें। तो नववा गुण जेणें। कर्म तें साच ॥ ८५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādareṃ jeṃ kāṃ mānaṇeṃ | teṃ āstikya mī mhaṇeṃ| to navavā guṇa jeṇeṃ| karma teṃ sāca || 850||
verses.meaning: That which is respectfully accepted, that I call faith. That is the ninth quality, by which actions become true.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं नवही शमादिक । गुण जेथ निर्दोष। तें कर्म जाण स्वाभाविक । ब्राह्मणाचें ॥५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ navahī śamādika | guṇa jetha nirdoṣa| teṃ karma jāṇa svābhāvika | brāhmaṇāceṃ ||51||
verses.meaning: Thus, where the nine qualities like tranquility are faultless, know that to be the natural action of a Brahmin.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो नवगुणरत्नाकरु। या नवरत्नांचा हारु। न फेडित ले दिनकरु । प्रकाशु जैसा॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: to navaguṇaratnākaru| yā navaratnāṃcā hāru| na pheḍita le dinakaru | prakāśu jaisā|| 52||
verses.meaning: He is an ocean of nine virtues, a garland of nine gems. Just as the sun never sheds its light, so too does He remain eternally radiant.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना चांपा चांपौळी पूजिला । चंद्रु चंद्रिका धवळला । कां चंदनु निजें चर्चिला । सौरभ्यें जेबीं॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā cāṃpā cāṃpauḻī pūjilā | caṃdru caṃdrikā dhavaḻalā | kāṃ caṃdanu nijeṃ carcilā | saurabhyeṃ jebīṃ|| 53||
verses.meaning: Just as a variety of Champaka flowers are worshipped, or the moon is brightened by moonlight, or sandalwood is naturally fragrant, so too is the divine essence inherently manifest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं नवगुणटिकलग। लेणें ब्राह्मणाचें अव्यंग कहींचि न संडी आंग । ब्राह्मणाचे ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ navaguṇaṭikalaga| leṇeṃ brāhmaṇāceṃ avyaṃga kahīṃci na saṃḍī āṃga | brāhmaṇāce || 54||
verses.meaning: Just as the ninefold virtues are the unblemished ornament of a Brahmin, they never leave the Brahmin's being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां उचित जें क्षत्रिया । तेंहीं कर्म धनंजया । सांगों ऐक प्रज्ञेचिया । भरोबरी ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ ucita jeṃ kṣatriyā | teṃhīṃ karma dhanaṃjayā | sāṃgoṃ aika prajñeciyā | bharobarī || 55||
verses.meaning: Now, Arjuna, listen with full understanding, I will tell you what is proper for a Kshatriya to do.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी भानु हा तेजें। नापेक्षी जेवीं विरजे। कां सिंहें न पाहिजे। जावळिया॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī bhānu hā tejeṃ| nāpekṣī jevīṃ viraje| kāṃ siṃheṃ na pāhije| jāvaḻiyā|| 56||
verses.meaning: Just as the sun does not depend on a lamp for its radiance, or a lion does not need a cub to prove its strength.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा स्वयंभ जो जीवें लाठु। सावायेंबीण उद॒भटु । तें शौर्य गा जेथ श्रेष्ठु| पहिला गुण ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā svayaṃbha jo jīveṃ lāṭhu| sāvāyeṃbīṇa uda̱bhaṭu | teṃ śaurya gā jetha śreṣṭhu| pahilā guṇa || 57||
verses.meaning: Such is the self-born, who is naturally mighty, spontaneously manifested, and whose valor is supreme, being the foremost quality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि सूर्याचेनि प्रतापें। कोडिही नक्षत्र हारपे। ना तो तरी न लोपे। सचंद्रीं तिहीं ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi sūryāceni pratāpeṃ| koḍihī nakṣatra hārape| nā to tarī na lope| sacaṃdrīṃ tihīṃ || 58||
verses.meaning: And by the sun's radiance, countless stars vanish, yet the moon, along with them, does not truly disappear.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेनि आपुले प्रौढिंगुणें। जगा या विस्मयो देणें । आपण तरी न क्षोभणें । कायसेनही ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseni āpule prauḍhiṃguṇeṃ| jagā yā vismayo deṇeṃ | āpaṇa tarī na kṣobhaṇeṃ | kāyasenahī || 59||
verses.meaning: In the same way, by one's own profound qualities, one should astonish the world, yet oneself remain undisturbed by anything.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें प्रागल्भ्यरूप तेजा । जिये कर्मी गुण दुजा । आणि धीरु तो तिजा। जेथींचा गुण॥ ८६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ prāgalbhyarūpa tejā | jiye karmī guṇa dujā | āṇi dhīru to tijā| jethīṃcā guṇa|| 860||
verses.meaning: That brilliance, that splendor, is the first quality. The second quality is the action itself, and the third quality is the steadfastness that arises from it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरि पडलिया आकाश बुद्धीचे डोळे मानस। झांकी ना तें परियेस। धैर्य जेथें ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: vari paḍaliyā ākāśa buddhīce ḍoḻe mānasa| jhāṃkī nā teṃ pariyesa| dhairya jetheṃ || 61||
verses.meaning: Listen, even if the intellect's eyes and the mind are covered by the sky falling upon them, that which remains unshaken is fortitude.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पाणी हो कां भलतेतुकें । परी तें जिणौनि पद्य फांके। कां आकाश उंचिया जिंके । आवडे तयातें ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pāṇī ho kāṃ bhalatetukeṃ | parī teṃ jiṇauni padya phāṃke| kāṃ ākāśa uṃciyā jiṃke | āvaḍe tayāteṃ || 62||
verses.meaning: And even if the water is of any amount, the lotus still emerges victorious from it. Or, just as the sky conquers all heights, so too does it please the one who desires it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं विविध अवस्था । पातलिया जिणोौनि पार्था । प्रज्ञाफळ तया अर्था । वेझ देणें जें॥६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ vividha avasthā | pātaliyā jiṇoauni pārthā | prajñāphaḻa tayā arthā | vejha deṇeṃ jeṃ||63||
verses.meaning: Thus, O Partha, having overcome various states, the fruit of wisdom is to give meaning to them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें दक्षत्व गा चोख। जेथ चौथा गुण देख। आणि झुंज अलौकिक । तो पांचवा गुण॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ dakṣatva gā cokha| jetha cauthā guṇa dekha| āṇi jhuṃja alaukika | to pāṃcavā guṇa|| 64||
verses.meaning: That skill is truly pure, where the fourth quality is seen, and the extraordinary battle is the fifth quality.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आदित्याचीं झाडें। सदा सन्मुख सूर्याकडे । तेवीं समोर शत्रूपुढें। होणें जें कां ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādityācīṃ jhāḍeṃ| sadā sanmukha sūryākaḍe | tevīṃ samora śatrūpuḍheṃ| hoṇeṃ jeṃ kāṃ || 65||
verses.meaning: Just as trees always face the sun, so too should one stand resolutely before an enemy.

verses.shloka_devanagari: माहेवणी प्रयत्नेंसी । चुकविजे सेजे जैसी। रिपू पाठी नेदिजे तैसी। समरांगणीं ॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: māhevaṇī prayatneṃsī | cukavije seje jaisī| ripū pāṭhī nedije taisī| samarāṃgaṇīṃ || 66||
verses.meaning: Just as one carefully avoids a bed of thorns, so too should one not turn their back on an enemy in battle.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हा क्षत्रियाचेया आचारीं। पांचवा गुणेंद्रु अवधारी । चहूं पुरुषार्था शिरीं । भक्ति जैसी ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: hā kṣatriyāceyā ācārīṃ| pāṃcavā guṇeṃdru avadhārī | cahūṃ puruṣārthā śirīṃ | bhakti jaisī || 67||
verses.meaning: In the conduct of a Kshatriya, know that the fifth virtue is devotion, just as devotion is supreme among the four human pursuits.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि जालेनि फुलें फळें। शाखिया जैसीं मोकळे । कां उदार परिमळें । पद्याकरु ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi jāleni phuleṃ phaḻeṃ| śākhiyā jaisīṃ mokaḻe | kāṃ udāra parimaḻeṃ | padyākaru || 68||
verses.meaning: Just as branches become laden with flowers and fruits, or a lotus pond becomes generous with its fragrance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नाना आवडीचेनि मापें । चांदिणें भलतेणें घेपे । पुढिलांचेनि संकल्पें। तैसें जें देणे॥ ६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nānā āvaḍīceni māpeṃ | cāṃdiṇeṃ bhalateṇeṃ ghepe | puḍhilāṃceni saṃkalpeṃ| taiseṃ jeṃ deṇe|| 69||
verses.meaning: Just as moonlight can be gathered in vessels of various shapes and sizes according to one's desire, so too is the giving (of spiritual experience) in accordance with the recipient's intention.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें उमप गा दान। जेथ सहावें गुणरत्न। आणि आज्ञे एकायतन। होणें जें कां॥ ८७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ umapa gā dāna| jetha sahāveṃ guṇaratna| āṇi ājñe ekāyatana| hoṇeṃ jeṃ kāṃ|| 870||
verses.meaning: That is indeed a great gift, where the six virtues are the jewels, and it becomes the abode of commands.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पोषूनि अवयव आपुले। करविजती मानविले। तेवीं पालणें लो भविलें । जग जें भोगणें ॥७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: poṣūni avayava āpule| karavijatī mānavile| tevīṃ pālaṇeṃ lo bhavileṃ | jaga jeṃ bhogaṇeṃ ||71||
verses.meaning: Just as one nourishes one's own limbs and makes them perform desired actions, so too does the Lord sustain and delight the world, which is His own enjoyment.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया नाम ईशवरभावो। जो सर्वसामर्थ्याचा ठावो। तो गुणांमाजीं रावो। सातवा जेथ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā nāma īśavarabhāvo| jo sarvasāmarthyācā ṭhāvo| to guṇāṃmājīṃ rāvo| sātavā jetha|| 72||
verses.meaning: That Name is the very essence of God, the abode of all power, the king among all qualities, the seventh where it resides.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें जें शौर्यादिकीं। इहीं सात गुणविशेखीं । अळंकृत सप्तक्रखीं । आकाश जैसें ॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ jeṃ śauryādikīṃ| ihīṃ sāta guṇaviśekhīṃ | aḻaṃkṛta saptakrakhīṃ | ākāśa jaiseṃ || 73||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky is adorned with the seven great sages (Saptarishi), so too is the soul adorned with these seven special qualities, such as valor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सप्तगुणीं विचित्र। कर्म जें जगीं 'पवित्र। ते सहज जाण क्षात्र। क्षत्रियाचें ॥७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ saptaguṇīṃ vicitra| karma jeṃ jagīṃ 'pavitra| te sahaja jāṇa kṣātra| kṣatriyāceṃ ||74||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the actions in the world that are considered sacred and are characterized by seven qualities, know them to be naturally Kshatriya, belonging to a warrior.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना ना क्षत्रिय नव्हे नरु । तो सत्त्वसोनयाचा मेरु । म्हणौनि गुणस्वर्गा आधारु । सातां इयां ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā nā kṣatriya navhe naru | to sattvasonayācā meru | mhaṇauni guṇasvargā ādhāru | sātāṃ iyāṃ || 75 ||
verses.meaning: He is not merely a Kshatriya; he is a mountain of pure sattva (goodness), and thus, he is the very foundation of the seven heavens of virtues.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी सप्तगुणार्णवीं। परिवारली बरवी । हे क्रिया नव्हे पृथ्वी । भोगीतसे तो॥७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī saptaguṇārṇavīṃ| parivāralī baravī | he kriyā navhe pṛthvī | bhogītase to||76||
verses.meaning: Otherwise, surrounded by the seven oceans of qualities, this is not an action of the earth; it is he who experiences it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां गुणांचे सातांही ओघीं। हे क्रिया ते गंगा जगीं। तया महोदधीचिया आंगीं । विलसे जैसी ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ guṇāṃce sātāṃhī oghīṃ| he kriyā te gaṃgā jagīṃ| tayā mahodadhīciyā āṃgīṃ | vilase jaisī || 77||
verses.meaning: Just as the Ganga, with its seven streams of virtues, flows into the great ocean, so too does this action shine forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी हें बहु असो देख । शौर्यादि गुणात्मक । कर्म गा नैसर्गिक । क्षत्रजातीसी ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī heṃ bahu aso dekha | śauryādi guṇātmaka | karma gā naisargika | kṣatrajātīsī || 78 ||
verses.meaning: But let this be enough; know that valor and other such qualities are the natural actions of the Kshatriya caste.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां वैश्याचिये जाती । उचित जे महामती। तें ऐकें गा निरुती। क्रिया सांगों ॥ ७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ vaiśyāciye jātī | ucita je mahāmatī| teṃ aikeṃ gā nirutī| kriyā sāṃgoṃ || 79||
verses.meaning: Now, listen carefully, O great-minded one, to the actions I shall describe, which are appropriate for the Vaishya caste.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी भूमि बीज नांगरु। यया भांडवलाचा आधारु । घेऊनि लाभु अपारु । मेळवणें जें ॥ ८८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī bhūmi bīja nāṃgaru| yayā bhāṃḍavalācā ādhāru | gheūni lābhu apāru | meḻavaṇeṃ jeṃ || 880||
verses.meaning: Just as the earth, seeds, and plough are the capital, by utilizing them, immense profit is gained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना कृषी जिणें । गोधनें राखोनि वर्तणें। कां समर्धीची विकणें। महर्षी बस्तु॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā kṛṣī jiṇeṃ | godhaneṃ rākhoni vartaṇeṃ| kāṃ samardhīcī vikaṇeṃ| maharṣī bastu|| 81||
verses.meaning: Or, indeed, living by farming, or tending cattle, or selling the possessions of great sages.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येतुलाचि पांडवा । बैश्यातें कर्माचा मेळावा। हा वैश्यजातिस्वभावा-। आंतुळा जाण॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetulāci pāṃḍavā | baiśyāteṃ karmācā meḻāvā| hā vaiśyajātisvabhāvā-| āṃtuḻā jāṇa|| 82||
verses.meaning: O Pandava, this much is the gathering of actions for a Vaishya. Know that this is inherent in the nature of the Vaishya caste.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि बैश्य क्षत्रिय ब्राह्मण । हे द्विजन्मे तिन्ही वर्ण। ययांचें जें शुश्रूषण। तें शूट्रकर्म॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi baiśya kṣatriya brāhmaṇa | he dvijanme tinhī varṇa| yayāṃceṃ jeṃ śuśrūṣaṇa| teṃ śūṭrakarma|| 83||
verses.meaning: And the Vaishyas, Kshatriyas, and Brahmins – these three twice-born varnas – to serve them is the duty of the Shudra.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं द्विजसेवेपरौतें । धांबणें नाहीं शूद्रातें। एवं चतुर्वर्णोचितें । दाविलीं करमें॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ dvijaseveparauteṃ | dhāṃbaṇeṃ nāhīṃ śūdrāteṃ| evaṃ caturvarṇociteṃ | dāvilīṃ karameṃ|| 84||
verses.meaning: Indeed, for Shudras, there is no greater support than serving the twice-born (Brahmins). Thus, the duties appropriate for all four varnas have been shown.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ४६४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी आतां इयेचि विचक्षणा। वेगळालिया वर्णा। उचित जैसें करणां। शब्दादिक॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: 464 śrījñāneśvarī ātāṃ iyeci vicakṣaṇā| vegaḻāliyā varṇā| ucita jaiseṃ karaṇāṃ| śabdādika|| 85||
verses.meaning: Now, in this very discernment, just as words and other things are appropriate for different castes, so too are actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नातरी जळदच्युता। पाणिया उच्ति सरिता । सरितेसी पंडुसुता । सिंधु उचितु॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: nātarī jaḻadacyutā| pāṇiyā ucti saritā | saritesī paṃḍusutā | siṃdhu ucitu|| 86||
verses.meaning: Just as a cloud is naturally drawn to water, and a river to the ocean, so too, O son of Pandu, is the ocean the natural destination for the river.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें वर्णाश्रमवशें । जें करणीय आलें असे। गोरेया आंगा जैसें । गोरेपण॥ ८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ varṇāśramavaśeṃ | jeṃ karaṇīya āleṃ ase| goreyā āṃgā jaiseṃ | gorepaṇa|| 87||
verses.meaning: Just as fairness is inherent to a fair body, so too are actions that arise naturally from one's varna (social class) and ashrama (stage of life).

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया स्वभावविहिता कर्मा । शास्त्राचेनि मुखें वीरोत्तमा। प्रवर्तावयालागीं प्रमा। अढळ कौजे॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā svabhāvavihitā karmā | śāstrāceni mukheṃ vīrottamā| pravartāvayālāgīṃ pramā| aḍhaḻa kauje|| 88||
verses.meaning: O best among warriors, for the performance of actions prescribed by one's own nature, through the mouth of the scriptures, a firm and unwavering प्रमाण (authoritative injunction) is established.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं आपुलेंचि रत्न थितें। घेपे पारखियाचेनि हातें। तैसें स्वकर्म आपेतें। शास्त्रें करावीं ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ āpuleṃci ratna thiteṃ| ghepe pārakhiyāceni hāteṃ| taiseṃ svakarma āpeteṃ| śāstreṃ karāvīṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Just as one's own jewel, though present, is taken by the hands of a stranger, so too should one perform their own prescribed duties as ordained by the scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसी दिठी असे आपुलिया ठायीं । परी दीपेंबीण भोग नाहीं । मार्गु न लाहतां काई। पाय असतां होय॥ ८९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisī diṭhī ase āpuliyā ṭhāyīṃ | parī dīpeṃbīṇa bhoga nāhīṃ | mārgu na lāhatāṃ kāī| pāya asatāṃ hoya|| 890||
verses.meaning: Just as sight resides within oneself, yet without a lamp, there is no experience of seeing; similarly, what good are feet if one cannot find the path?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि ज्ञातिवशें साचारु। सहज असे जो अधिकारु। तो आपुलाल्िया शास्त्रें गोचरु । आपण कोजे॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jñātivaśeṃ sācāru| sahaja ase jo adhikāru| to āpulāliyā śāstreṃ gocaru | āpaṇa koje|| 91||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the true right, which is naturally inherited, should be understood by oneself through one's own scriptures.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग घरींचाचि ठेवा । जेवीं डोळ्यां दावी दिवा। तरी घेतां काय पांडवा। आडळु असे॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga gharīṃcāci ṭhevā | jevīṃ ḍoḻyāṃ dāvī divā| tarī ghetāṃ kāya pāṃḍavā| āḍaḻu ase|| 92||
verses.meaning: Just as a lamp reveals the treasure within one's own home, what obstruction could there be, O Pandava, in taking it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें स्वभावें भागा आलें। वरी शास्त्रें खरें केलें। तें विहित जो आपुलें) आचरे गा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ svabhāveṃ bhāgā āleṃ| varī śāstreṃ khareṃ keleṃ| teṃ vihita jo āpuleṃ) ācare gā|| 93||
verses.meaning: Thus, what has naturally come to one's lot, and what the scriptures have affirmed as true, that prescribed duty one should perform.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी आळसु सांडुनी। फळकाम दवडुनी। आंगें जीवें मांडुनी । तेथेंचि भरु ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī āḻasu sāṃḍunī| phaḻakāma davaḍunī| āṃgeṃ jīveṃ māṃḍunī | tetheṃci bharu || 94||
verses.meaning: Therefore, abandoning laziness, casting aside the desire for fruits of action, and dedicating oneself wholeheartedly, one should immerse oneself completely in that (divine work).

verses.shloka_devanagari: बोघीं पडिलें पाणी। नेणें आनानी वाहणी । तैसा जाय आचरणीं। व्यवस्थौनी ॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: boghīṃ paḍileṃ pāṇī| neṇeṃ ānānī vāhaṇī | taisā jāya ācaraṇīṃ| vyavasthaunī || 95||
verses.meaning: Just as water poured into a riverbed naturally flows along its course, so too does a person of wisdom act in accordance with established principles.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अर्जुना जो यापरी | तें विहित कर्म स्वयें करी। तो मोक्षाच्या ऐलद्वारीं। पैठा होय ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: arjunā jo yāparī | teṃ vihita karma svayeṃ karī| to mokṣācyā ailadvārīṃ| paiṭhā hoya || 96||
verses.meaning: Arjuna, one who thus performs their prescribed duties spontaneously, enters the very threshold of liberation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें अकरणा आणि निषिद्धा। न वचेचि कांहीं संबंधा । म्हणौनि भवा विरुद्धा। मुकला तो॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ akaraṇā āṇi niṣiddhā| na vaceci kāṃhīṃ saṃbaṃdhā | mhaṇauni bhavā viruddhā| mukalā to|| 97||
verses.meaning: Therefore, he is freed from the cycle of worldly existence, as he does not engage in forbidden actions or those that are not prescribed.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि काम्यकर्मांकडे। न परतेचि जेथ कोडें। तेथ चंदनाचेही खोडे। न लेचि तो॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kāmyakarmāṃkaḍe| na parateci jetha koḍeṃ| tetha caṃdanācehī khoḍe| na leci to|| 98||
verses.meaning: And where there is no desire for worldly actions, there one does not even wear sandalwood paste.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येर नित्य कर्म तंव। फळत्यागें वेंचिलें सर्व। म्हणौनि मोक्षाची शींब। ठाकूं लाहे ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yera nitya karma taṃva| phaḻatyāgeṃ veṃcileṃ sarva| mhaṇauni mokṣācī śīṃba| ṭhākūṃ lāhe || 99||
verses.meaning: When all regular actions are performed without desire for their fruits, then the boundary of liberation can be reached.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसेंनि शुभाशुभीं संसारीं। सांडिला तो अवधारीं। वैराग्यमोक्षद्वारीं। उभा ठाके॥ ९००॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃni śubhāśubhīṃ saṃsārīṃ| sāṃḍilā to avadhārīṃ| vairāgyamokṣadvārīṃ| ubhā ṭhāke|| 900||
verses.meaning: Thus, having abandoned both good and bad in worldly existence, he stands at the threshold of liberation through dispassion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें सकळ भाग्याची सीमा । मोक्षलाभाची जें प्रमा। नाना कर्ममार्गश्रमा । शेवटु जेथ॥ १॥
