verses.meaning: Similarly, when one forgets that 'I am Brahman,' then the world itself becomes filled with Brahman. But if even this understanding is abandoned, then the very state of being Brahman also dissolves.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा मोडतु मांडतु ब्रह्मे । तो दुःखें देहाचिये सीमे। मी अर्जुन येणें नामें। उभा ठेला ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā moḍatu māṃḍatu brahme | to duḥkheṃ dehāciye sīme| mī arjuna yeṇeṃ nāmeṃ| ubhā ṭhelā || 52||
verses.meaning: Thus, Brahma, who creates and destroys, is bound by the limits of the body due to suffering. I, Arjuna, stand here by this name.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग कांपतां 'करतळीं॥ दडपूनि रोमावळी। पुलिका स्वेदजळीं। जिरऊनियां॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga kāṃpatāṃ 'karataḻīṃ|| daḍapūni romāvaḻī| pulikā svedajaḻīṃ| jiraūniyāṃ|| 53||
verses.meaning: Then, trembling, with the hair on the palms pressed down, the goosebumps dissolved in the sweat.

verses.shloka_devanagari: प्राणक्षोभें डोळतया। आंगा आंगचि टेंकया। सूनि स्तंभु चाळया। भुलौनियां ॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: prāṇakṣobheṃ ḍoḻatayā| āṃgā āṃgaci ṭeṃkayā| sūni staṃbhu cāḻayā| bhulauniyāṃ || 54||
verses.meaning: When the vital breath is disturbed, the body itself touches the body, and the pillar is shaken, as if deluded.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नेत्रयुगुळाचेनि वबोतें। आनंदामृताचें भरितें। बोसंडत तें मागुतें। काढूनियां॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: netrayuguḻāceni vaboteṃ| ānaṃdāmṛtāceṃ bhariteṃ| bosaṃḍata teṃ māguteṃ| kāḍhūniyāṃ|| 55||
verses.meaning: With the overflowing joy of the eyes, the nectar of bliss surges forth, and then it is drawn back in.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विविधा औओत्सुक्‍यांची दाटी। चीप दाटत होती कंठीं।॥ ते करूनियां पैठी । हृदयामाजीं ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: vividhā auotsuk‍yāṃcī dāṭī| cīpa dāṭata hotī kaṃṭhīṃ||| te karūniyāṃ paiṭhī | hṛdayāmājīṃ || 56||
verses.meaning: A multitude of eager desires crowded and choked the throat, but he made them enter and settle in his heart.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वाचेचें वितुळणें। सांवरूनि प्राणें। अक्रमाचें श्‍वसणें । ठेऊनि ठायीं ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāceceṃ vituḻaṇeṃ| sāṃvarūni prāṇeṃ| akramāceṃ ś‍vasaṇeṃ | ṭheūni ṭhāyīṃ || 57||
verses.meaning: Restraining the outward expression of speech, and holding the breath in its natural state, one should fix the mind on the unmanifest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग अर्जुन म्हणे काय देवो। पुसताति आवडे मोहो। तरी तो सकुटुंब गेला जी ठावो। घेऊनि आपुला॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga arjuna mhaṇe kāya devo| pusatāti āvaḍe moho| tarī to sakuṭuṃba gelā jī ṭhāvo| gheūni āpulā|| 58||
verses.meaning: Then Arjuna said, "What shall I give? They ask with love, but he has gone with his whole family, taking his place."

verses.shloka_devanagari: पासीं येऊनि दिनकरें। डोळ्यांतें आंधारें। पुसिजे हें कायि सरे। कोणे गांबीं ॥ ५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāsīṃ yeūni dinakareṃ| ḍoḻyāṃteṃ āṃdhāreṃ| pusije heṃ kāyi sare| koṇe gāṃbīṃ || 59||
verses.meaning: If the sun itself were to approach, could darkness ever ask it to remove the darkness from its eyes? How could such a thing be possible?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा तूं श्रीकृष्णराया । आमुचिया डोळयां। गोचर हेंचि कायिसया। न पुरे तंव॥ १५६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā tūṃ śrīkṛṣṇarāyā | āmuciyā ḍoḻayāṃ| gocara heṃci kāyisayā| na pure taṃva|| 1560||
verses.meaning: O Lord Krishna, why is it that merely seeing You with our eyes is not enough for us?

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरी लोभें मायेपासूनी । तें सांगसी तोंड भरूनी। जें कायिसेनिही करूनी । जाणू नये ॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: varī lobheṃ māyepāsūnī | teṃ sāṃgasī toṃḍa bharūnī| jeṃ kāyisenihī karūnī | jāṇū naye || 61||
verses.meaning: Out of love, you will speak to me fully of that which cannot be known by any means.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां मोह असे कीं नाहीं। हें ऐसें जी पुससी काई । कृतकृत्य जाहलों पाहीं। तुझेपणें ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ moha ase kīṃ nāhīṃ| heṃ aiseṃ jī pusasī kāī | kṛtakṛtya jāhaloṃ pāhīṃ| tujhepaṇeṃ || 62||
verses.meaning: Now, whether there is delusion or not, why do you ask such a question? Behold, I have become fulfilled through your grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गुंतलो होतों अर्जुनगुणें। तो मुक्‍त जालों तुझेपणें।॥ आतां पुसणें सांगणें । दोन्ही नाहीं ॥६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: guṃtalo hotoṃ arjunaguṇeṃ| to muk‍ta jāloṃ tujhepaṇeṃ||| ātāṃ pusaṇeṃ sāṃgaṇeṃ | donhī nāhīṃ ||63||
verses.meaning: I was entangled in the qualities of Arjuna, but through You, I have become liberated. Now, there is no need for questioning or explaining.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मी तुझेनि प्रसादें। 'लाधलेनि आत्मबोधें। मोहाचे तया कांदे । नेदीच उरों॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: mī tujheni prasādeṃ| 'lādhaleni ātmabodheṃ| mohāce tayā kāṃde | nedīca uroṃ|| 64||
verses.meaning: Through your grace, having attained self-realization, I will not allow the roots of delusion to remain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां करणें का न करणें। हें जेणें उठी दुजेपणें। तें तूं बांचूनि नेणें। सर्वत्र गा॥ ६५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ karaṇeṃ kā na karaṇeṃ| heṃ jeṇeṃ uṭhī dujepaṇeṃ| teṃ tūṃ bāṃcūni neṇeṃ| sarvatra gā|| 65 ||
verses.meaning: Now, whether to act or not to act, this duality that arises, You alone know it, O Lord, for You are everywhere.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येविषयीं माझ्या ठायीं । संदेहाचें नुरेचि कांहीं । त्रिशुद्धी कर्म जेथ नाहीं । तें मी जालों॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeviṣayīṃ mājhyā ṭhāyīṃ | saṃdehāceṃ nureci kāṃhīṃ | triśuddhī karma jetha nāhīṃ | teṃ mī jāloṃ|| 66||
verses.meaning: Regarding this, there is no doubt left in me. I have become that which is completely devoid of the three kinds of actions.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तुझेनि मज मी पावोनी। कर्तव्य गेलें निपटूनी । परी आज्ञा तुझी वांचोनि। आन नाहीं प्रभो॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: tujheni maja mī pāvonī| kartavya geleṃ nipaṭūnī | parī ājñā tujhī vāṃconi| āna nāhīṃ prabho|| 67||
verses.meaning: By Your grace, I have attained myself, and all my duties have ceased. Yet, without Your command, there is nothing else, O Lord.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां जें दृश्य दृश्यातें नाशी । जें दुजें द्वैतातें ग्रासी। जें एक परी सर्वदेशीं। बसबी सदा॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ jeṃ dṛśya dṛśyāteṃ nāśī | jeṃ dujeṃ dvaitāteṃ grāsī| jeṃ eka parī sarvadeśīṃ| basabī sadā|| 68 ||
verses.meaning: For that which destroys the seen within the seen, that which consumes the duality of the other, that which is one yet establishes itself everywhere eternally.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचेनि संबंधें बंधु फिटे। जयाचिया आशा आस तुटे । जें भेटलया सर्व भेटे। आपणपांचि॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāceni saṃbaṃdheṃ baṃdhu phiṭe| jayāciyā āśā āsa tuṭe | jeṃ bheṭalayā sarva bheṭe| āpaṇapāṃci||69||
verses.meaning: By whose association all bonds are broken, by whose hope all desires are severed, by meeting whom everything is met, and one's own self is realized.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें तूं गुरुलिंग जी माझें।॥ जें येकलेपणींचें विरजें। जयालागीं बोलांडिजे। अद्वैतबोधु ॥ १५७०॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ tūṃ guruliṃga jī mājheṃ||| jeṃ yekalepaṇīṃceṃ virajeṃ| jayālāgīṃ bolāṃḍije| advaitabodhu || 1570||
verses.meaning: You are that Guru-Lingam to me, which is the renunciation of loneliness, for which the knowledge of non-duality is transcended.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आपणचि होऊनि ब्रह्म सारिजे कृत्याकृत्यांचे काम । मग कौजे का निःसीम । सेवा जयाची ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: āpaṇaci hoūni brahma sārije kṛtyākṛtyāṃce kāma | maga kauje kā niḥsīma | sevā jayācī || 71 ||
verses.meaning: When one becomes Brahman oneself, the distinction between what is to be done and what is not to be done ceases. Then, why should one praise the boundless service of that (Brahman)?

verses.shloka_devanagari: गंगा सिंधु सेवूं गेली । पावतांचि समुद्र जाळी । तेवीं भक्तां सेळ दिधली । निजपदाची ॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: gaṃgā siṃdhu sevūṃ gelī | pāvatāṃci samudra jāḻī | tevīṃ bhaktāṃ seḻa didhalī | nijapadācī || 72||
verses.meaning: Just as the Ganga, upon reaching the ocean, merges into it, so too the devotee, upon attaining the divine abode, merges with the Self.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो तूं माझा जी निरुपचारु । श्रीकृष्णा सेव्य सद्गुरु । मा ब्रह्मतेचा उपकारु । हाचि मानीं ॥७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: to tūṃ mājhā jī nirupacāru | śrīkṛṣṇā sevya sadguru | mā brahmatecā upakāru | hāci mānīṃ ||73||
verses.meaning: You are my unblemished, pure, and holy Sadguru, O Shri Krishna. I consider this the greatest favor of Brahman-realization.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जें मज तुम्हां आड। होतें भेदाचें कवाड तें फेडोनि केलें गोड। सेवासुख॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: jeṃ maja tumhāṃ āḍa| hoteṃ bhedāceṃ kavāḍa teṃ pheḍoni keleṃ goḍa| sevāsukha|| 74||
verses.meaning: The barrier of separation that stood between you and me, I have removed it, making the joy of service sweet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी आतां तुझी आज्ञा) सकळदेवाधिदेवराज्ञा। करीन देई अनुज्ञा। भलतियेविषयीं ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī ātāṃ tujhī ājñā) sakaḻadevādhidevarājñā| karīna deī anujñā| bhalatiyeviṣayīṃ || 75 ||
verses.meaning: Therefore, now, by your command, O King of all Gods, I shall act. Grant me permission in all matters.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया अर्जुनाचिया बोला । देवो नाचे सुखें भुलला । म्हणे विश्‍वफळा जाला । 'फळ हा मज॥ ७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā arjunāciyā bolā | devo nāce sukheṃ bhulalā | mhaṇe viś‍vaphaḻā jālā | 'phaḻa hā maja|| 76||
verses.meaning: At these words of Arjuna, God danced, enchanted with joy, saying, "This fruit has become a fruit for Me, the fruit of the universe!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: उणेनि उमचला सुधाकरु । देखुनी आपल्मा कुमरु । मर्यादा क्षीरसागरु । विसरेचिना ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: uṇeni umacalā sudhākaru | dekhunī āpalmā kumaru | maryādā kṣīrasāgaru | visarecinā || 77||
verses.meaning: When the moon, a child of the ocean, rises, the ocean does not forget its own boundaries, even upon seeing its offspring.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें संवादाचिया बहुलां। लग्न दोघांचियां आंतुला । लागलें देखोनि जाला । निर्भर संजयो ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ saṃvādāciyā bahulāṃ| lagna doghāṃciyāṃ āṃtulā | lāgaleṃ dekhoni jālā | nirbhara saṃjayo || 78 ||
verses.meaning: Seeing such a great wedding of conversation between the two, Sanjaya became completely satisfied.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें उचंबळलेपणें। संजय धूतराष्ट्रातें म्हणें। जी कैसें बादरायणें । रक्षिलों दोघे ॥ ९१५८० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ ucaṃbaḻalepaṇeṃ| saṃjaya dhūtarāṣṭrāteṃ mhaṇeṃ| jī kaiseṃ bādarāyaṇeṃ | rakṣiloṃ doghe || 91580 ||
verses.meaning: With that surge of emotion, Sanjaya said to Dhritarashtra, "O master, how Vyasa protected both of us!"

verses.shloka_devanagari: आजि तुमतें अवधारा । नाहीं चर्मचक्षूही ४९८ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी संसारा। कीं ज्ञानदृष्टिव्यबहारा। आणिलेती ॥ १५८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āji tumateṃ avadhārā | nāhīṃ carmacakṣūhī 498 śrījñāneśvarī saṃsārā| kīṃ jñānadṛṣṭivyabahārā| āṇiletī || 1581||
verses.meaning: Listen to me today, you who have been brought into this worldly existence, not by the eyes of the flesh, but by the eye of knowledge.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि रथींचिये राहाटी । घेई जो घोडेयासाठीं । तया आम्हां या गोष्टी । गोचरा होती ॥ ८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi rathīṃciye rāhāṭī | gheī jo ghoḍeyāsāṭhīṃ | tayā āmhāṃ yā goṣṭī | gocarā hotī || 82||
verses.meaning: And for us, who are like charioteers, taking care of the horses, these matters become clear and understandable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वरी जुंझाचें निर्वाण। मांडलें असे दारुण। दोहीं हारी आपण। हारपिजे जैसें॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: varī juṃjhāceṃ nirvāṇa| māṃḍaleṃ ase dāruṇa| dohīṃ hārī āpaṇa| hārapije jaiseṃ|| 83||
verses.meaning: It is as if a terrible battle has been arranged, and in both armies, one loses oneself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येवढा जिये सांकडां। कैसा अनुग्रहो पैं गाढा । जे ब्रह्मानंदु उघडा । भोगवीतसे॥ ८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yevaḍhā jiye sāṃkaḍāṃ| kaisā anugraho paiṃ gāḍhā | je brahmānaṃdu ughaḍā | bhogavītase|| 84||
verses.meaning: In such a difficult situation, how profound is this grace, that it openly allows one to experience the bliss of Brahman.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें संजय बोलिला । परी न द्रवे येरु उगला । चंद्रकिरणीं शिवतला। पाषाणु जैसा॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ saṃjaya bolilā | parī na drave yeru ugalā | caṃdrakiraṇīṃ śivatalā| pāṣāṇu jaisā|| 85||
verses.meaning: Sanjaya spoke thus, but Dhritarashtra remained unmoved, like a stone untouched by moonlight.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे देखोनि तयाची दशा । मग करीचिना सरिसा। परी सुखें जाला पिसा। बोलतसे॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: he dekhoni tayācī daśā | maga karīcinā sarisā| parī sukheṃ jālā pisā| bolatase|| 86||
verses.meaning: Seeing this state of his, he then does not make it equal, but happily becomes mad and speaks.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भुलविला हर्षवेगें ॥ म्हणौनि धृतराष्ट्रा सांगे। एऱ्हवीं नव्हे तयाजोगें। हें कौर जाणे ॥८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhulavilā harṣavegeṃ || mhaṇauni dhṛtarāṣṭrā sāṃge| eṟhavīṃ navhe tayājogeṃ| heṃ kaura jāṇe ||87||
verses.meaning: Thus, out of sheer joy, Sanjaya narrated the events to Dhritarashtra. Otherwise, Dhritarashtra was not worthy of hearing such a profound discourse; this was known to all Kauravas.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणे पैं कुरुराजा। ऐसा बंधुपुत्र तो तुझा । बोलिला तें अधोक्षजा । गोड जाळें॥ ८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇe paiṃ kururājā| aisā baṃdhuputra to tujhā | bolilā teṃ adhokṣajā | goḍa jāḻeṃ|| 88||
verses.meaning: Then, O King of the Kurus, this son of your brother, what he said to Lord Adhokshaja, became sweet (to Him).

verses.shloka_devanagari: अगा पूर्वापर सागर। हा नामासीचि सिनार। येर आघवें तें नीर। एक जैसें ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: agā pūrvāpara sāgara| hā nāmāsīci sināra| yera āghaveṃ teṃ nīra| eka jaiseṃ || 89||
verses.meaning: Oh, the ocean of past and future is nothing but a name. All else is water, just the same.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसा श्रीकृष्ण पार्थ ऐसें । हें आंगाचिपासीं दिसे । मग संवादीं जी नसे। कांहींचि भेदु॥ १५९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: tesā śrīkṛṣṇa pārtha aiseṃ | heṃ āṃgācipāsīṃ dise | maga saṃvādīṃ jī nase| kāṃhīṃci bhedu|| 1590||
verses.meaning: Thus, Shri Krishna and Arjuna are seen as one and the same; there is no difference between them in their dialogue.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं दर्पणाहूनि चोखें। दोन्ही होती सन्मुखें। तेथ येरीं येर देखे। आपणपें जैसें ॥९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ darpaṇāhūni cokheṃ| donhī hotī sanmukheṃ| tetha yerīṃ yera dekhe| āpaṇapeṃ jaiseṃ ||91||
verses.meaning: Just as a clear mirror, when placed before another, perfectly reflects the other, so too does the self perceive itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा देवेंसीं पंडुसुतु । आपणपें देवीं देखतु। पांडवेंसीं देखे अनंतु। आपणपें पार्थी ॥९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā deveṃsīṃ paṃḍusutu | āpaṇapeṃ devīṃ dekhatu| pāṃḍaveṃsīṃ dekhe anaṃtu| āpaṇapeṃ pārthī ||92||
verses.meaning: Just as the son of Pandu saw himself in the Lord, so too the infinite Lord saw Himself in Pandu's son.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देव देवो भक्‍तालागीं। जिये विवरूनि देखे आंगीं। येरु तियेचेही भागीं। दोन्ही देखे ॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: deva devo bhak‍tālāgīṃ| jiye vivarūni dekhe āṃgīṃ| yeru tiyecehī bhāgīṃ| donhī dekhe || 93||
verses.meaning: God, for the devotee, is seen and experienced within their very being. And in that very experience, both the devotee and God become one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणिक कांहींच नाहीं। म्हणौनि करिती काई । दोघे येकपणें पाहीं । नांदताती ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇika kāṃhīṃca nāhīṃ| mhaṇauni karitī kāī | doghe yekapaṇeṃ pāhīṃ | nāṃdatātī || 94||
verses.meaning: There is nothing else; therefore, what can they do? See, the two reside as one.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां भेदु जरी मोडे । तरी प्रश्‍नोत्तर कां घडे। ना भेदुचि तरी जोडे । संवादसुख कां॥ ९५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ bhedu jarī moḍe | tarī praś‍nottara kāṃ ghaḍe| nā bheduci tarī joḍe | saṃvādasukha kāṃ|| 95 ||
verses.meaning: If the distinction between us were to dissolve now, how could there be a question and answer? And if there were no distinction, how could the joy of dialogue arise?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें बोलतां दुजेपणें । संबादीं द्वैत गिळणें । तें ऐकिलें बोलणें । दोघांचें मियां॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ bolatāṃ dujepaṇeṃ | saṃbādīṃ dvaita giḻaṇeṃ | teṃ aikileṃ bolaṇeṃ | doghāṃceṃ miyāṃ|| 96||
verses.meaning: When speaking like this, duality is swallowed in the conversation. I have heard the conversation of these two.

verses.shloka_devanagari: उटूनि दोन्ही आरसे । वबोडविलीया सरिसे। कोण कोणा पाहातसे। कल्यपाबें पां॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: uṭūni donhī ārase | vaboḍavilīyā sarise| koṇa koṇā pāhātase| kalyapābeṃ pāṃ|| 97||
verses.meaning: When two mirrors are placed facing each other, who sees whom? Similarly, who sees whom in the illusion of the world?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां दीपासन्मुखु। ठेविळया दीपकु। कोण कोणा अर्थिकु। कोण जाणें ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ dīpāsanmukhu| ṭheviḻayā dīpaku| koṇa koṇā arthiku| koṇa jāṇeṃ || 98||
verses.meaning: Or, if a lamp is placed in front of another lamp, who is the giver and who is the receiver? Who can tell?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना ना अकापुढें अर्कु। उदयळिया आणिकु। कोण म्हणे प्रकाशकु । प्रकाश्य कवण॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā nā akāpuḍheṃ arku| udayaḻiyā āṇiku| koṇa mhaṇe prakāśaku | prakāśya kavaṇa|| 99||
verses.meaning: When the sun itself rises, who would call another light-giver, and what would be illuminated?

verses.shloka_devanagari: हें निर्धारू जातां फुडें । निर्धारासि ठक पडे । ते दोघे जाळे येवढे। संबादें सरिसे॥ १६००॥
verses.shloka_iast: heṃ nirdhārū jātāṃ phuḍeṃ | nirdhārāsi ṭhaka paḍe | te doghe jāḻe yevaḍhe| saṃbādeṃ sarise|| 1600||
verses.meaning: When this determination progresses, the determination itself is deceived. Both become equal in their conversation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी मिळतां दोन्ही उदकें। माजीं 'लवण वारूं ठाके। कीं तयासींही निमिखें। तेंचि होय ॥ १॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī miḻatāṃ donhī udakeṃ| mājīṃ 'lavaṇa vārūṃ ṭhāke| kīṃ tayāsīṃhī nimikheṃ| teṃci hoya || 1||
verses.meaning: When two waters meet, the salt that was separating them disappears, and in an instant, it becomes one with them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसे श्रीकृष्ण अर्जुन दोन्ही । संबादले तें मनीं । धरितां मजही वानी । तेंचि होतसे ॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: taise śrīkṛṣṇa arjuna donhī | saṃbādale teṃ manīṃ | dharitāṃ majahī vānī | teṃci hotase || 2||
verses.meaning: Just as the conversation between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, when contemplated, makes one realize that I am also the same.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें म्हणे ना मोटकें। तंब हिरोनि सात्त्विकें । आठव नेल्म नेणों कें। संजयपणाचा॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ mhaṇe nā moṭakeṃ| taṃba hironi sāttvikeṃ | āṭhava nelma neṇoṃ keṃ| saṃjayapaṇācā|| 3||
verses.meaning: He did not even say this much, but the sattvic nature completely took away the memory of his role as Sanjaya, as if he didn't know where it went.

verses.shloka_devanagari: रोमांच जंब फरके। तंव तंव आंग सुरके। स्तंभ स्वेदांतें जिंके। एकला कंपु॥ ४॥
verses.shloka_iast: romāṃca jaṃba pharake| taṃva taṃva āṃga surake| staṃbha svedāṃteṃ jiṃke| ekalā kaṃpu|| 4||
verses.meaning: As the hair stands on end, the body shivers, and a solitary tremor conquers both rigidity and perspiration.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अट्ठयानंदस्पर्शे । दिठी रसमय जाली असे। ते अश्रु नव्हती जैसें । द्रवत्वचि ॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aṭṭhayānaṃdasparśe | diṭhī rasamaya jālī ase| te aśru navhatī jaiseṃ | dravatvaci || 5||
verses.meaning: By the touch of supreme bliss, the sight has become imbued with rasa (divine essence). Those are not tears, but rather liquid bliss itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: नेणों काय न माय पोटीं । नेणों काय गुंफे कंठीं । वागर्था पडत मिठी । उससांचिया ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: neṇoṃ kāya na māya poṭīṃ | neṇoṃ kāya guṃphe kaṃṭhīṃ | vāgarthā paḍata miṭhī | usasāṃciyā || 6||
verses.meaning: I do not know what is contained within the womb, nor what is entwined around the neck. The meaning of words is embraced by sighs.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना सात्त्विकां आठां। चाचरु मांडतां उमेठा। संजयो जालासे चोहटां। संवादसुखाचा॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā sāttvikāṃ āṭhāṃ| cācaru māṃḍatāṃ umeṭhā| saṃjayo jālāse cohaṭāṃ| saṃvādasukhācā|| 7||
verses.meaning: Indeed, when the eight sattvic emotions are fully manifested, it is as if a marketplace of the joy of dialogue has been established.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तया सुखाची ऐसी जाती । जे आपणचि धरी शांती। मग पुढती देहस्मृती। लाधली तेणें ॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayā sukhācī aisī jātī | je āpaṇaci dharī śāṃtī| maga puḍhatī dehasmṛtī| lādhalī teṇeṃ || 8||
verses.meaning: Such is the nature of that bliss, that it itself embraces peace. Then, through that peace, the remembrance of the body is attained again.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेव्हां बैसतेनि आनंदें । म्हणें जी जें उपनिषदें। नेणती तें व्यासप्रसादें। ऐकिले मियां ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevhāṃ baisateni ānaṃdeṃ | mhaṇeṃ jī jeṃ upaniṣadeṃ| neṇatī teṃ vyāsaprasādeṃ| aikile miyāṃ || 9||
verses.meaning: Then, with overflowing joy, he says, "That which even the Upanishads do not fully comprehend, I have heard through the grace of Vyasa."

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐकतांचि ते गोठी । ब्रह्मत्वाची पडिली मिठी । मीतूंपणेंसीं सृष्टो। विरोनि गेलळी॥ १६१०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aikatāṃci te goṭhī | brahmatvācī paḍilī miṭhī | mītūṃpaṇeṃsīṃ sṛṣṭo| vironi gelaḻī|| 1610||
verses.meaning: As soon as that truth was heard, the embrace of Brahman fell, and the duality of 'I' and 'you,' along with the entire creation, dissolved.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे आघवेचि का योग। जया ठाया येती मार्ग। तयाचें वाक्य सवंग। केलें मज व्यासें ॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: he āghaveci kā yoga| jayā ṭhāyā yetī mārga| tayāceṃ vākya savaṃga| keleṃ maja vyāseṃ || 99||
verses.meaning: All these yogas, all these paths, converge at one place. Vyasa has made it easy for me to speak of that very place.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अहो अर्जुनाचेनि मिषें। आपणपेंचि दुजें ऐसें। नटोनि आपणया उद्देशें। बोलिलें जें देव ॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: aho arjunāceni miṣeṃ| āpaṇapeṃci dujeṃ aiseṃ| naṭoni āpaṇayā uddeśeṃ| bolileṃ jeṃ deva || 92||
verses.meaning: Indeed, through the guise of Arjuna, the Lord Himself, appearing as if another, spoke for His own instruction.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ कीं माझें श्रोत्र। पाटाचें जालें जी पात्र। काय वानूं स्वतंत्र । सामर्थ्य श्रीगुरूचें ॥ १३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha kīṃ mājheṃ śrotra| pāṭāceṃ jāleṃ jī pātra| kāya vānūṃ svataṃtra | sāmarthya śrīgurūceṃ || 13||
verses.meaning: Or perhaps my ear has become a vessel for the flow of knowledge. How can I independently describe the power of my revered Guru?

verses.shloka_devanagari: राया हें बोलतां विस्मित होये । तेणेंचि मोडावला ठाये। रलीं कीं रत्नकिळा ये। झांकोळित जैसी ॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: rāyā heṃ bolatāṃ vismita hoye | teṇeṃci moḍāvalā ṭhāye| ralīṃ kīṃ ratnakiḻā ye| jhāṃkoḻita jaisī || 94||
verses.meaning: The king, upon hearing this, was astonished. He was overwhelmed, just as the brilliance of a jewel is overshadowed by its own radiance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: हिमवंतींचीं सरोवरें । चंद्रोदयीं होती काश्मीरें। मग सूर्यागमीं माघारें। द्रवत्ब ये ॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: himavaṃtīṃcīṃ sarovareṃ | caṃdrodayīṃ hotī kāśmīreṃ| maga sūryāgamīṃ māghāreṃ| dravatba ye || 15||
verses.meaning: The lakes in the Himalayas, which appear like Kashmir during moonrise, revert to their liquid state at sunrise.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा शरीराचिया स्मृती । तो संबादु संजय चित्तीं। धरी आणि पुढती । तेंचि होय॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā śarīrāciyā smṛtī | to saṃbādu saṃjaya cittīṃ| dharī āṇi puḍhatī | teṃci hoya|| 16||
verses.meaning: Similarly, Sanjay held that conversation in his mind, remembering the body, and then it happened again.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग उठोनी म्हणे नृपा। श्रीहरीचिया विश्वरूपा । देखिलया उगा कां पां। ५०० श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी असों लाहसी॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga uṭhonī mhaṇe nṛpā| śrīharīciyā viśvarūpā | dekhilayā ugā kāṃ pāṃ| 500 śrījñāneśvarī asoṃ lāhasī|| 17||
verses.meaning: Then, rising, the king said, "O Lord, having seen the cosmic form of Shri Hari, why do you remain silent?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: न देखणेनि जें दिसे। नाहींपणेंचि जें असे । विसरें आठवे तें कैसें। चुकऊं आतां॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: na dekhaṇeni jeṃ dise| nāhīṃpaṇeṃci jeṃ ase | visareṃ āṭhave teṃ kaiseṃ| cukaūṃ ātāṃ|| 18||
verses.meaning: That which is seen without seeing, that which exists in its non-existence, how can one remember it through forgetting? Let us now avoid this error.

verses.shloka_devanagari: देखोनि चमत्कारु। कौजे तो नाहीं पैसारु। मजहीसकट महापूरु। नेत आहे॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: dekhoni camatkāru| kauje to nāhīṃ paisāru| majahīsakaṭa mahāpūru| neta āhe|| 19||
verses.meaning: Behold this miracle! There is no escape from it. The great flood is carrying me away along with everything else.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसा श्रीकृष्णार्जुन-। संवादसंगमीं स्नान। करूनि देतसे तिळदान। अहंतेचें ॥ १६२०॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisā śrīkṛṣṇārjuna-| saṃvādasaṃgamīṃ snāna| karūni detase tiḻadāna| ahaṃteceṃ || 1620||
verses.meaning: Thus, by bathing in the confluence of the dialogue between Shri Krishna and Arjuna, one offers the sesame seeds of ego as a donation.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ असंवबरें आनंदें। अलौकिकही कांहीं स्फुंदे। श्रीकृष्ण म्हणे सदगदें। वेळोवेळां॥ २१॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha asaṃvabareṃ ānaṃdeṃ| alaukikahī kāṃhīṃ sphuṃde| śrīkṛṣṇa mhaṇe sadagadeṃ| veḻoveḻāṃ|| 21||
verses.meaning: Then, with uncontainable joy, and with some extraordinary inspiration, Shri Krishna spoke repeatedly, overwhelmed with emotion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या अवस्थांची कांहीं । कौरवांतें परी नाहीं । म्हणौनि रायें तें कांहीं। कल्पावें जंव॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā avasthāṃcī kāṃhīṃ | kauravāṃteṃ parī nāhīṃ | mhaṇauni rāyeṃ teṃ kāṃhīṃ| kalpāveṃ jaṃva|| 22||
verses.meaning: These states of being, however, are not like the Kauravas. Therefore, the king (Dhritarashtra) should not imagine anything about them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तंब जाला सुखलाभु। आपणपां करूनि स्वयंभु। बुझाविला अवष्टंभु। संजयें तेणें॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṃba jālā sukhalābhu| āpaṇapāṃ karūni svayaṃbhu| bujhāvilā avaṣṭaṃbhu| saṃjayeṃ teṇeṃ|| 23||
verses.meaning: Thus, Sanjaya, by his own divine insight, became self-manifested, and dispelled the obstruction of ignorance.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ कोणी येकी अवसरी । होआवी ते करूनि दुरी। रावो म्हणे संजया परी। कैशी तुझी गा॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha koṇī yekī avasarī | hoāvī te karūni durī| rāvo mhaṇe saṃjayā parī| kaiśī tujhī gā|| 24||
verses.meaning: At some point, one must distance themselves from such things. The King then asks Sanjaya, "How is your understanding?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें तूंतें येथें व्यासें। बैसविलें कासया उद्देशें। अप्रसंगामाजीं ऐसें। बोलसी काई॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ tūṃteṃ yetheṃ vyāseṃ| baisavileṃ kāsayā uddeśeṃ| aprasaṃgāmājīṃ aiseṃ| bolasī kāī|| 25||
verses.meaning: Why then did Vyasa seat you here with such an intention? Why do you speak thus on an irrelevant topic?

verses.shloka_devanagari: रानींचें राउळा नेलिया। दाही दिशा मानी सुनिया । कां रात्री होय पाहलया । निशाचरां ॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: rānīṃceṃ rāuḻā neliyā| dāhī diśā mānī suniyā | kāṃ rātrī hoya pāhalayā | niśācarāṃ || 26||
verses.meaning: When the queen is taken to the temple, the ten directions become desolate, or when night turns into dawn, it is so for the night-prowlers.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जो जेथिंचें गौरव नेणे । तयासि तें भिंगुळवाणें । म्हणौनि अप्रसंगु तेणें । म्हणावा कीं तो ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jo jethiṃceṃ gaurava neṇe | tayāsi teṃ bhiṃguḻavāṇeṃ | mhaṇauni aprasaṃgu teṇeṃ | mhaṇāvā kīṃ to || 27||
verses.meaning: That which one does not understand or appreciate, appears insignificant or frightening to them. Therefore, one might consider it irrelevant or simply beyond their comprehension.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग म्हणे सांगें प्रस्तुत । उदयलेंसे जें उत्कळित । तें कोणासि बा रे जैत। देईल शेखीं ॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga mhaṇe sāṃgeṃ prastuta | udayaleṃse jeṃ utkaḻita | teṃ koṇāsi bā re jaita| deīla śekhīṃ || 28||
verses.meaning: Then he said, "Tell me, this rising, surging phenomenon, to whom will it ultimately grant victory?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: एऱ्हवीं विशेषें बहुतेक । आमुचें ऐसें मानसिक । जे दुर्योधनाचे अधिक । प्रताप सदा॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: eṟhavīṃ viśeṣeṃ bahuteka | āmuceṃ aiseṃ mānasika | je duryodhanāce adhika | pratāpa sadā|| 29||
verses.meaning: In fact, it is mostly our mental disposition, which is more inclined towards the pride and power of Duryodhana.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि येरांचेनि पाडें। दळही यांचें देव्हडें। म्हणौनि जैत फुडें। आणील ना तें॥ १६३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi yerāṃceni pāḍeṃ| daḻahī yāṃceṃ devhaḍeṃ| mhaṇauni jaita phuḍeṃ| āṇīla nā teṃ|| 1630||
verses.meaning: And compared to others, their army is small. Therefore, how can they achieve victory?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आम्हां तंव गमे ऐसें। मा तुझें ज्योतीष कैसें। तें नेणों संजया असे। तैसें सांग पां॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: āmhāṃ taṃva game aiseṃ| mā tujheṃ jyotīṣa kaiseṃ| teṃ neṇoṃ saṃjayā ase| taiseṃ sāṃga pāṃ|| 31||
verses.meaning: To us, it seems like this. But what is your astrology like? We do not know, Sanjaya, so please tell us as it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: यया बोला संजयो म्हणे। जी येरयेरांचें मी नेणें। परी आयुष्य तेथें जिणें। हें फुडें कौं गा॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: yayā bolā saṃjayo mhaṇe| jī yerayerāṃceṃ mī neṇeṃ| parī āyuṣya tetheṃ jiṇeṃ| heṃ phuḍeṃ kauṃ gā|| 32||
verses.meaning: Sanjaya said, "I do not know about the others, but where there is life, there is existence, is it not so?"

verses.shloka_devanagari: चंद्रु तेथें चंद्रिका । शंभु तेथें अंबिका । संत तेथें बिवेका। असणें कों जी॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: caṃdru tetheṃ caṃdrikā | śaṃbhu tetheṃ aṃbikā | saṃta tetheṃ bivekā| asaṇeṃ koṃ jī|| 33||
verses.meaning: Just as moonlight resides with the moon, and Ambika with Shambhu, so too does Viveka (discrimination/wisdom) reside with the saints.

verses.shloka_devanagari: राबो तेथें कटक। सौजन्य तेथें सोयरीक । वन्हि तेथें दाहक। सामर्थ्य कीं ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: rābo tetheṃ kaṭaka| saujanya tetheṃ soyarīka | vanhi tetheṃ dāhaka| sāmarthya kīṃ || 34||
verses.meaning: Where there is a king, there is an army. Where there is kindness, there is kinship. Where there is fire, there is burning. Such is the nature of power.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दया तेथें धर्मु। धर्म तेथें सुखागमु। सुखीं पुरुषोत्तमु। असे जैसा ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: dayā tetheṃ dharmu| dharma tetheṃ sukhāgamu| sukhīṃ puruṣottamu| ase jaisā || 35||
verses.meaning: Where there is compassion, there is righteousness; where there is righteousness, there is the arrival of happiness; and in happiness, the Supreme Being resides.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वसंतु तेथें वनें। वन तेथें सुमनें । सुमनीं पालिंगनें । सारंगांची ॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: vasaṃtu tetheṃ vaneṃ| vana tetheṃ sumaneṃ | sumanīṃ pāliṃganeṃ | sāraṃgāṃcī || 36||
verses.meaning: Wherever there is spring, there are forests. Wherever there are forests, there are flowers. And in the flowers, there are bees embracing them.

verses.shloka_devanagari: गुरु तेथ ज्ञान । ज्ञानीं आत्मदर्शन । दर्शनीं समाधान। आथी जेसें॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: guru tetha jñāna | jñānīṃ ātmadarśana | darśanīṃ samādhāna| āthī jeseṃ|| 37||
verses.meaning: Where there is a Guru, there is knowledge. In knowledge, there is self-realization. In self-realization, there is contentment, just as it is.

verses.shloka_devanagari: भाग्य तेथ विलासु। सुख तेथ उल्लासु। हें असो तेथ प्रकाश । सूर्य जेथें ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: bhāgya tetha vilāsu| sukha tetha ullāsu| heṃ aso tetha prakāśa | sūrya jetheṃ || 38||
verses.meaning: Where there is good fortune, there is enjoyment. Where there is happiness, there is delight. Moreover, where the sun is, there is light.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें सकल पुरुषार्थ । जेणें स्वामी का सनाथ। तो श्रीकृष्णरावो जेथ। तेथ लक्ष्मी॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ sakala puruṣārtha | jeṇeṃ svāmī kā sanātha| to śrīkṛṣṇarāvo jetha| tetha lakṣmī|| 39||
verses.meaning: Just as all human endeavors find their fulfillment and purpose through a master, so too, wherever Lord Krishna, the sovereign, is present, there resides Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity and fortune.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि आपलेनि कांतेंसीं। ते जगदंबा जयापासीं । अणिमादिकीं काय दासी । नव्हती तयातें ॥ १६४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi āpaleni kāṃteṃsīṃ| te jagadaṃbā jayāpāsīṃ | aṇimādikīṃ kāya dāsī | navhatī tayāteṃ || 1640||
verses.meaning: And with her beloved, the Mother of the Universe, by his side, are not even the Siddhis like Anima and others his humble servants?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कृष्ण विजयस्वरूप निजांगें। तो राहिला असे जेणें भागें। तैं जयो लागेवेगें। तेथेंचि आहे॥ ४१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṛṣṇa vijayasvarūpa nijāṃgeṃ| to rāhilā ase jeṇeṃ bhāgeṃ| taiṃ jayo lāgevegeṃ| tetheṃci āhe|| 41||
verses.meaning: Krishna, who is the embodiment of victory, resides in that very place where victory is swiftly attained.

verses.shloka_devanagari: विजयो नामें अर्जुन विख्यातु। विजयस्वरूप श्रीकृष्णनाथु । श्रियेसीं विजय निश्‍चितु । तेथेंचि असे॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: vijayo nāmeṃ arjuna vikhyātu| vijayasvarūpa śrīkṛṣṇanāthu | śriyesīṃ vijaya niś‍citu | tetheṃci ase|| 42||
verses.meaning: Arjuna is renowned by the name Vijaya (victorious). Lord Krishna is the embodiment of victory. Where these two are, there is certainly prosperity and victory.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचिये देशींच्या झाडीं । कल्पतरूतें होडी। न जिणावें कां येवढीं।॥ मायबापें असतां॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāciye deśīṃcyā jhāḍīṃ | kalpatarūteṃ hoḍī| na jiṇāveṃ kāṃ yevaḍhīṃ||| māyabāpeṃ asatāṃ|| 43||
verses.meaning: When one's parents are present, why should the trees in their land not surpass even the wish-fulfilling trees of heaven?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ते पाषाणही आघवे। चिंतारत्नें कां नोहावे। तिये भूमिके कां न यावें । सुवर्णत्व ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: te pāṣāṇahī āghave| ciṃtāratneṃ kāṃ nohāve| tiye bhūmike kāṃ na yāveṃ | suvarṇatva || 44 ||
verses.meaning: Why should not those very stones become wish-fulfilling gems? Why should not that ground turn into gold?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचिया गांबींचिया। नदी अमृतें बाहाविया। नवल कायि राया। विचारीं पां॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāciyā gāṃbīṃciyā| nadī amṛteṃ bāhāviyā| navala kāyi rāyā| vicārīṃ pāṃ|| 45||
verses.meaning: What wonder is it, O King, that rivers of nectar flow from the very roots of such a tree? Reflect upon this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाचे बिसाट शब्द। सुखें म्हणों येती वेद। सदेह सच्चिदानंद। कां न व्हावे ते॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāce bisāṭa śabda| sukheṃ mhaṇoṃ yetī veda| sadeha saccidānaṃda| kāṃ na vhāve te|| 46||
verses.meaning: His powerful words, spoken with ease, become the Vedas themselves. Why should such a one not be the embodied सच्चिदानंद (Sat-chit-anand)?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पैं स्वर्गापवर्ग दोन्ही । इयें पदें जया अधीनीं। तो श्रीकृष्ण बाप जननी । कमळा जया॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: paiṃ svargāpavarga donhī | iyeṃ padeṃ jayā adhīnīṃ| to śrīkṛṣṇa bāpa jananī | kamaḻā jayā|| 47||
verses.meaning: Indeed, both heaven and liberation are under the control of the one whose father is Shri Krishna and whose mother is Kamala (Lakshmi).

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जिया बाहीं उभा। तो लक्ष्मीयेचा वल्लभा । तेथें सर्वसिद्धी स्वयंभा। येर मी नेणें ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jiyā bāhīṃ ubhā| to lakṣmīyecā vallabhā | tetheṃ sarvasiddhī svayaṃbhā| yera mī neṇeṃ || 48||
verses.meaning: Therefore, the one in whose arms He stands, the beloved of Lakshmi, all perfections naturally manifest there; I know no other truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि समुद्राचा मेघु। उपयोगें तयाहूनि चांगु। तैसा पार्थी आजि लागु। आहे तये॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi samudrācā meghu| upayogeṃ tayāhūni cāṃgu| taisā pārthī āji lāgu| āhe taye|| 49||
verses.meaning: And just as a cloud is more beneficial than the ocean, so too, Arjuna, is the benefit derived from her today.

verses.shloka_devanagari: 'कनकत्वदीक्षागुरू। लोहा परिसु होय कौरू। परी जगा पोसिता व्यवहारू । तेंचि जाणें ॥ १६५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: 'kanakatvadīkṣāgurū| lohā parisu hoya kaurū| parī jagā positā vyavahārū | teṃci jāṇeṃ || 1650||
verses.meaning: Just as a guru initiates a disciple into the gold-making process, transforming iron into gold, similarly, the true essence of worldly affairs lies in sustaining the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथ गुरुत्वा येतसे उणें । ऐसें झणें कोण्ही म्हणे । बन्हि प्रकाश दीपपणें । प्रकाशी आपुला॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetha gurutvā yetase uṇeṃ | aiseṃ jhaṇeṃ koṇhī mhaṇe | banhi prakāśa dīpapaṇeṃ | prakāśī āpulā|| 51||
verses.meaning: Lest anyone should think that the Guru's greatness is diminished, understand that just as a lamp illuminates itself by its own light, so too does the Guru's inherent brilliance shine forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा देवाचिया शक्‍ती । पार्थु देवासीचि बहुती। परी माने इये स्तुती । गौरव असे ॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā devāciyā śak‍tī | pārthu devāsīci bahutī| parī māne iye stutī | gaurava ase || 52||
verses.meaning: Similarly, Arjuna, though empowered by God, is considered great due to this praise, which bestows honor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पुत्र मी सर्वगुणीं। जिणावा हे बापा शिराणी। तरी ते शाडू्गपाणी। फळा आली ॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi putra mī sarvaguṇīṃ| jiṇāvā he bāpā śirāṇī| tarī te śāḍūgapāṇī| phaḻā ālī || 53||
verses.meaning: And if a son, endowed with all virtues, surpasses his father, then indeed, the bearing of such a son has borne fruit.

verses.shloka_devanagari: किंबहुना ऐसा नृपा। पार्थ जालासे कृष्णकृपा । तो जयाकडे साक्षेपा। रीति आहे॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kiṃbahunā aisā nṛpā| pārtha jālāse kṛṣṇakṛpā | to jayākaḍe sākṣepā| rīti āhe|| 54||
verses.meaning: Indeed, O King, Arjuna has become such, by the grace of Krishna, that he is the very embodiment of righteousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तोचि गा विजयासि ठावो। येथ तुज कोण संदेहो। तेथ न ये तरी वाबो। विजयोचि होय ॥ ५५॥
verses.shloka_iast: toci gā vijayāsi ṭhāvo| yetha tuja koṇa saṃdeho| tetha na ye tarī vābo| vijayoci hoya || 55||
verses.meaning: That indeed is the abode of victory. What doubt can you have in this? If one does not reach there, then victory itself becomes futile.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जेथ श्री तेथे श्रीमंतु| जेथ तो पंडूचा सुतु। तेथ विजय समस्तु। अभ्युदयो ५०२ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी तेथ॥५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jetha śrī tethe śrīmaṃtu| jetha to paṃḍūcā sutu| tetha vijaya samastu| abhyudayo 502 śrījñāneśvarī tetha||56||
verses.meaning: Therefore, wherever there is prosperity, there is the prosperous one; wherever there is the son of Pandu, there is complete victory and all-round success. Thus says Shri Dnyaneshwari.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जरी व्यासाचेनि साचें। धिरे (मानी ) मन तुमचें। तरी या बोलाचें। ध्रुवचि माना ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jarī vyāsāceni sāceṃ| dhire (mānī ) mana tumaceṃ| tarī yā bolāceṃ| dhruvaci mānā || 57||
verses.meaning: If your mind truly finds solace in Vyasa's words, then consider these words as the ultimate truth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जेथ तो श्रीवल्लभु। जेथ भक्‍तकदंबु। तेथ सुख आणि लाभु । मंगळाचा ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: jetha to śrīvallabhu| jetha bhak‍takadaṃbu| tetha sukha āṇi lābhu | maṃgaḻācā || 58||
verses.meaning: Where that beloved Lord is, where the multitude of devotees is, there is happiness and the gain of auspiciousness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: या बोला आन होये। तरी व्यासाचा अंकु न वाहें। ऐसें गाजोनि बाहें। उभिलीं तेणें ॥५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yā bolā āna hoye| tarī vyāsācā aṃku na vāheṃ| aiseṃ gājoni bāheṃ| ubhilīṃ teṇeṃ ||59||
verses.meaning: If these words bring joy, then Vyasa's lineage will not be diminished. Thus, with such proclamation, they stood forth.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं भारताचा आवांका । आणूनि एलोका येका । संजयें कुरुनायका। दीधल्म हातीं ॥ १६६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ bhāratācā āvāṃkā | āṇūni elokā yekā | saṃjayeṃ kurunāyakā| dīdhalma hātīṃ || 1660||
verses.meaning: Thus, Sanjay, having brought the entire scope of the Bharata war into a single vision, placed it in the hands of the Kaurava king.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जैसा नेणों केवढा वन्ही। परी गुणाग्रीं ठेऊनी। आणिजे सूर्याची हानी। निस्तरावया॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: jaisā neṇoṃ kevaḍhā vanhī| parī guṇāgrīṃ ṭheūnī| āṇije sūryācī hānī| nistarāvayā|| 61||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not know the full extent of the fire, yet by placing a small spark at the tip of a wick, one can bring about the destruction of the sun, to overcome it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसें शब्दब्रह्म अनंत। जाळे सवालक्ष भारत । भारताचें शतें सात। सर्वस्व गीता ॥ ६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: teseṃ śabdabrahma anaṃta| jāḻe savālakṣa bhārata | bhāratāceṃ śateṃ sāta| sarvasva gītā || 62||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the infinite Shabda-Brahma (Vedic knowledge) became the one hundred and twenty-five thousand verses of the Mahabharata. Of these seven hundred verses of the Mahabharata, the Gita is the essence of all.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तयाही सातां शतांचा । इत्यर्थु हा ह्लोक शेषींचा । व्यासशिष्य संजयाचा। पूर्णोद्गारु जो॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tayāhī sātāṃ śatāṃcā | ityarthu hā hloka śeṣīṃcā | vyāsaśiṣya saṃjayācā| pūrṇodgāru jo|| 63||
verses.meaning: This verse, the last of the seven hundred, is the complete utterance of Sanjaya, the disciple of Vyasa.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येणें येकेंचि शलोकें । राहे तेणें असकें । अविद्याजाताचें निकें । जिंतलें होय ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yeṇeṃ yekeṃci śalokeṃ | rāhe teṇeṃ asakeṃ | avidyājātāceṃ nikeṃ | jiṃtaleṃ hoya || 64||
verses.meaning: By this one verse alone, all the suffering caused by ignorance is overcome.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसे शलोक शतें सात। गीतेचीं पदें आंगें वाहत। पद्यें म्हणो कीं परमामृत। गीताकाशींचें ॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: aise śaloka śateṃ sāta| gītecīṃ padeṃ āṃgeṃ vāhata| padyeṃ mhaṇo kīṃ paramāmṛta| gītākāśīṃceṃ || 65||
verses.meaning: Thus, these seven hundred verses, the very essence of the Gita, flow forth. Should I call them poems, or the supreme nectar from the sky of the Gita?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं आत्मराजाचिये सभे। गीते बोडवले हे खांबे । मज शलोक प्रतिभे। ऐसे येत॥६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ ātmarājāciye sabhe| gīte boḍavale he khāṃbe | maja śaloka pratibhe| aise yeta||66||
verses.meaning: Or, in the assembly of the King of Self, these pillars are the Gita, and to me, each verse appears as a divine inspiration.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं गीता हे सप्तशती । मंत्रप्रतिपाद्य भगवती । मोहमहिषा मुक्‍ती। आनंदली असे॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ gītā he saptaśatī | maṃtrapratipādya bhagavatī | mohamahiṣā muk‍tī| ānaṃdalī ase|| 67||
verses.meaning: Just as the Bhagavati (Divine Mother) in the Saptashati, who is glorified by mantras, rejoices upon liberating devotees from the demon of delusion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि मनें कायें वाचा जो सेवकु होईल इयेचा। तो स्वानंदसाप्राज्याचा । चक्रवर्ती करी ॥ ६८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni maneṃ kāyeṃ vācā jo sevaku hoīla iyecā| to svānaṃdasāprājyācā | cakravartī karī || 68||
verses.meaning: Therefore, whoever serves this (knowledge/path) with mind, body, and speech, will be made the emperor of the kingdom of self-bliss.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं अविद्यातिमिररोखें। श्लोक सूर्यातें पैजा जिंके । ऐसे प्रकाशिले गीतामिषें । रायें श्रीकृष्णें ॥६९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ avidyātimirarokheṃ| śloka sūryāteṃ paijā jiṃke | aise prakāśile gītāmiṣeṃ | rāyeṃ śrīkṛṣṇeṃ ||69||
verses.meaning: Or, as if to challenge the sun of the Shlokas (verses) with the darkness of ignorance, Lord Shri Krishna illuminated them in the guise of the Gita.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं शलोकाक्षरद्राक्षलता । मांडब जाळी आहे गीता । संसारपथश्रांता । विसंबावया ॥ १६७० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ śalokākṣaradrākṣalatā | māṃḍaba jāḻī āhe gītā | saṃsārapathaśrāṃtā | visaṃbāvayā || 1670 ||
verses.meaning: Or, the Gita is like a trellis of grapevines, formed by the letters of the shlokas, for those weary travelers on the path of worldly existence to rest.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं सभाग्यसंतीं भ्रमरीं। केले ते शलोककल्हारीं। श्रीकृष्णाख्यसरोबरीं। सासिन्नळी हे॥७१॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ sabhāgyasaṃtīṃ bhramarīṃ| kele te śalokakalhārīṃ| śrīkṛṣṇākhyasarobarīṃ| sāsinnaḻī he||71||
verses.meaning: Or, the fortunate bees of saints have made these verses, like lotus stalks, in the lake named Shri Krishna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौं शलोक नव्हती आन । गमे गीतेचें महिमान । वाखाणिते बंदिजन । उदंड जैसे॥ ७२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauṃ śaloka navhatī āna | game gīteceṃ mahimāna | vākhāṇite baṃdijana | udaṃḍa jaise|| 72||
verses.meaning: How can one describe the glory of the Gita? It is as if the bards are endlessly praising it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौं एलोकांचिया आवारा। सात शतें करूनि सुंदरा। सर्वागम गीतापुरा। वसो आले॥ ७३॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauṃ elokāṃciyā āvārā| sāta śateṃ karūni suṃdarā| sarvāgama gītāpurā| vaso āle|| 73||
verses.meaning: The Bhagavad Gita, the essence of all scriptures, came to reside in the beautiful abode of the seven hundred verses, like a divine cowherd.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौं निजकांता आत्मया। आवडी गीता मिळावया। शलोक नव्हती बाह्या। पसरु का जो॥ ७४॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauṃ nijakāṃtā ātmayā| āvaḍī gītā miḻāvayā| śaloka navhatī bāhyā| pasaru kā jo|| 74||
verses.meaning: How could the Lord, the very Self, out of love for the Gita, spread out these verses externally, as if they were not already within?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कौं गीताकमळींचे भृंग) कीं हे गीतासागरतरंग। कौं हरीचे तुरंग। गीतारथींचे ॥७५॥
verses.shloka_iast: kauṃ gītākamaḻīṃce bhṛṃga) kīṃ he gītāsāgarataraṃga| kauṃ harīce turaṃga| gītārathīṃce ||75||
verses.meaning: Are they the bees of the lotus of the Gita? Or are they the waves of the ocean of the Gita? Or are they the steeds of Hari, for the chariot of the Gita?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं श्लोक सर्वतीर्थ संघातु। आला श्रीगीतेगंगेआंतु। जे अर्जुन नरसिंहस्थु। जाला म्हणौनि॥७६॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ śloka sarvatīrtha saṃghātu| ālā śrīgītegaṃgeāṃtu| je arjuna narasiṃhasthu| jālā mhaṇauni||76||
verses.meaning: Or, the confluence of all holy places has come into the Ganga of the Srimad Bhagavad Gita, because Arjuna has become the Narasimha (man-lion) within it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कीं नोहे हे शलोकश्रेणी। अचिंत्यचित्तचिंतामणी । कीं निर्विकल्पां लावणी । कल्पतरूंची ॥ ७७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kīṃ nohe he śalokaśreṇī| aciṃtyacittaciṃtāmaṇī | kīṃ nirvikalpāṃ lāvaṇī | kalpatarūṃcī || 77||
verses.meaning: Or is this not a series of verses, but an inconceivable wish-fulfilling gem for the mind? Or is it a planting of wish-fulfilling trees for those beyond conceptual thought?

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसिया शतें सात शलोकां। 'परि आगळा येकयेका। आतां कोण वेगळिका | वानावा पां॥ ७८॥
verses.shloka_iast: aisiyā śateṃ sāta śalokāṃ| 'pari āgaḻā yekayekā| ātāṃ koṇa vegaḻikā | vānāvā pāṃ|| 78||
verses.meaning: Thus, there are seven hundred such verses, each one excelling the other. Now, which one should I describe as distinct?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तान्ही आणि पारठी। इया कामधेनूतें दिठी। सूनि जैसिया गोठी। कीजती ना॥७९॥
verses.shloka_iast: tānhī āṇi pāraṭhī| iyā kāmadhenūteṃ diṭhī| sūni jaisiyā goṭhī| kījatī nā||79||
verses.meaning: Just as a calf and a heifer, though both are offspring of a cow, are not treated with the same reverence as the wish-fulfilling cow (Kamadhenu) itself, so too are certain distinctions made.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दीपा आगिलु मागिलु। सूर्यु धाकुटा बडीलु। अमृतसिंधु खोलु। उथळु कायसा॥ १६८०॥
verses.shloka_iast: dīpā āgilu māgilu| sūryu dhākuṭā baḍīlu| amṛtasiṃdhu kholu| uthaḻu kāyasā|| 1680||
verses.meaning: Can a lamp illuminate the front and back of the sun? Can the sun be called small or big? Can the ocean of nectar be called deep or shallow?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसे पहिळे सरते। एलोक न म्हणावे गीते । जुनीं नवीं पारिजातें। आहाती काई॥ ८१॥
verses.shloka_iast: taise pahiḻe sarate| eloka na mhaṇāve gīte | junīṃ navīṃ pārijāteṃ| āhātī kāī|| 81||
verses.meaning: Similarly, the Gita is not to be called old or new, just as the Parijat flowers are neither old nor new.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि शलोका पाडु नाहीं। हें कीर समर्थ काई। येथ वाच्य वाचकही । भागु न धरी॥८२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi śalokā pāḍu nāhīṃ| heṃ kīra samartha kāī| yetha vācya vācakahī | bhāgu na dharī||82||
verses.meaning: And there is no need to compose verses. What is the use of that? Here, neither the expressed nor the expresser holds any sway.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे इये शास्त्री येकु। श्रीकृष्णचि वाच्य वाचकु । हें प्रसिद्ध जाणे लोकु । भलताही ॥ ८३॥
verses.shloka_iast: je iye śāstrī yeku| śrīkṛṣṇaci vācya vācaku | heṃ prasiddha jāṇe loku | bhalatāhī || 83||
verses.meaning: Indeed, in these scriptures, Shri Krishna alone is the subject and the speaker. This truth is well-known even to ordinary people.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथें अर्थे तेंचि पाठें।॥ जोडे येवढेनि धटें। वाच्यबाचक येकवटें। साधितें शास्त्र ॥८४॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetheṃ arthe teṃci pāṭheṃ||| joḍe yevaḍheni dhaṭeṃ| vācyabācaka yekavaṭeṃ| sādhiteṃ śāstra ||84||
verses.meaning: Here, the meaning itself is the lesson. With such firmness, the expressed and the expresser become one, which is what the scriptures accomplish.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि मज कांहीं। समर्थनीं आतां विषय नाहीं। गीता जाणा हे वाडूमयी। श्रीमूर्ति प्रभूची ॥ ८५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni maja kāṃhīṃ| samarthanīṃ ātāṃ viṣaya nāhīṃ| gītā jāṇā he vāḍūmayī| śrīmūrti prabhūcī || 85||
verses.meaning: Therefore, there is no need for me to elaborate further. Know that this Gita is the embodiment of the Lord's divine form, expressed through words.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शास्त्र वाच्यें अर्थे फळे। मग आपण मावळे तैसें नव्हे हें सगळें । परब्रह्मचि ॥ ८६॥
verses.shloka_iast: śāstra vācyeṃ arthe phaḻe| maga āpaṇa māvaḻe taiseṃ navhe heṃ sagaḻeṃ | parabrahmaci || 86||
verses.meaning: The scriptures reveal the meaning, and then they themselves disappear. This entire phenomenon is not like that; it is the Supreme Brahman itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कैसा विशवाचिया कृपा। करूनि महानंद सोपा । अर्जुनव्याजें रूपा। आणिल्य देवें॥८७॥
verses.shloka_iast: kaisā viśavāciyā kṛpā| karūni mahānaṃda sopā | arjunavyājeṃ rūpā| āṇilya deveṃ||87||
verses.meaning: How the Lord, through the grace of the universe, made the great bliss easy to attain, bringing it into form through the guise of Arjuna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चकोराचेनि निमित्तें। तिन्ही भुवनें संतप्तें। निवविलीं कळावंतें। चंद्र जेबीं॥८८॥
verses.shloka_iast: cakorāceni nimitteṃ| tinhī bhuvaneṃ saṃtapteṃ| nivavilīṃ kaḻāvaṃteṃ| caṃdra jebīṃ||88||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon, for the sake of the chakora bird, cools the three worlds with its artistry, so too does the divine cool the universe.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां गौतमाचेनि मिषें। कळिकाळज्वरितोहेशों। पाणिढाळु गिरीशें । गंगेचा केला ॥ ८९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ gautamāceni miṣeṃ| kaḻikāḻajvaritoheśoṃ| pāṇiḍhāḻu girīśeṃ | gaṃgecā kelā || 89||
verses.meaning: Or, was it that Lord Shiva, under the pretext of Gautama, poured forth the Ganga to alleviate the fever of the Kali Yuga?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें गीतेचें हें दुभतें। वत्स करूनि पार्थातें। दुभीनली जगापुरतें । श्रीकृष्ण गाय ॥ १६९०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ gīteceṃ heṃ dubhateṃ| vatsa karūni pārthāteṃ| dubhīnalī jagāpurateṃ | śrīkṛṣṇa gāya || 1690||
verses.meaning: Just as the Gita's milk, with Partha as the calf, was milked by the cow Lord Krishna for the entire world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: येथें जीवें जरी नाहाळ। तरी हेंचि कीर होआल। नातरी पाठमिषें तिंबाल। जीभचि जरी ॥ ९१॥
verses.shloka_iast: yetheṃ jīveṃ jarī nāhāḻa| tarī heṃci kīra hoāla| nātarī pāṭhamiṣeṃ tiṃbāla| jībhaci jarī || 91||
verses.meaning: Even if the tongue does not taste it, this is what will happen. Otherwise, it will be soaked in the pretext of the back, if it is the tongue itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तरी लोह एके अंशें। झगटलिया परिसें। येरीकडे अपैसें। सुवर्ण होय ॥ ९२॥
verses.shloka_iast: tarī loha eke aṃśeṃ| jhagaṭaliyā pariseṃ| yerīkaḍe apaiseṃ| suvarṇa hoya || 92||
verses.meaning: Just as a piece of iron, by merely touching the philosopher's stone, spontaneously transforms into gold.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसी पाठाची ते वाटी। एलोकपाद लावा ना जंब वोठीं। तंव ब्रह्मतेची पुष्टी । येईल आंगा॥ ९३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisī pāṭhācī te vāṭī| elokapāda lāvā nā jaṃba voṭhīṃ| taṃva brahmatecī puṣṭī | yeīla āṃgā|| 93||
verses.meaning: Just as by repeatedly reciting the sacred text, one's lips become accustomed to uttering the divine name, so too, by constant practice, the strength of Brahman will manifest within the body.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना येणेंसीं मुख वांकडें। करूनि ठाकालळ कानवडें। तरी कानींही घेतां पडे । तेचि लेख॥ ९४॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā yeṇeṃsīṃ mukha vāṃkaḍeṃ| karūni ṭhākālaḻa kānavaḍeṃ| tarī kānīṃhī ghetāṃ paḍe | teci lekha|| 94||
verses.meaning: If you turn your face away in displeasure and cover your ears, still, whatever you hear will be considered as if you have accepted it.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जे हे श्रवणें पाठें अर्थे। गीता नेदी मोक्षाआरौतें। जैसा समर्थ दाता कोणातें। नास्ति न म्हणे॥ ९५॥
verses.shloka_iast: je he śravaṇeṃ pāṭheṃ arthe| gītā nedī mokṣāārauteṃ| jaisā samartha dātā koṇāteṃ| nāsti na mhaṇe|| 95||
verses.meaning: One who studies the Gita through listening and recitation, and understands its meaning, will not be denied liberation, just as a generous donor never says no to anyone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि जाणतया सवा । गीताचि येकी सेवा । काय कराल आघवां । शास्त्री येरी ॥ ९६॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni jāṇatayā savā | gītāci yekī sevā | kāya karāla āghavāṃ | śāstrī yerī || 96||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for those who truly know, the Gita alone is the supreme service. What need is there then for all other scriptures?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि कृष्णार्जुनीं मोकळी । गोठी चावळिली जे निराळीं। ते श्रीव्यासें केळी करतळीं। घेवों ये ऐसी ॥ ९७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi kṛṣṇārjunīṃ mokaḻī | goṭhī cāvaḻilī je nirāḻīṃ| te śrīvyāseṃ keḻī karataḻīṃ| ghevoṃ ye aisī || 97||
verses.meaning: And the unique conversation between Krishna and Arjuna, which was so profound, Vyasa made it as accessible as a fruit held in the palm of one's hand.

verses.shloka_devanagari: बाळकातें वोरसें। माय जें ५०४ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी जेवऊं बैसे। तैं तया ठाकती तैसे। घांस करी ॥ ९८॥
verses.shloka_iast: bāḻakāteṃ voraseṃ| māya jeṃ 504 śrījñāneśvarī jevaūṃ baise| taiṃ tayā ṭhākatī taise| ghāṃsa karī || 98||
verses.meaning: Just as a mother lovingly feeds her child, preparing morsels that are easy for the child to eat.

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां अफाटा समीरणा। आपैतेंपण शाहाणा । केलें जैसें विंजणा । निर्मूनियां॥ ९९॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ aphāṭā samīraṇā| āpaiteṃpaṇa śāhāṇā | keleṃ jaiseṃ viṃjaṇā | nirmūniyāṃ|| 99||
verses.meaning: Or, just as a fan is created to make the vast wind appear to have a form and be manageable.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें शब्दें जें न लभे। तें घडूनियां अनुष्टभें। स्त्रीशूद्रादि प्रतिभे। सामाविलें॥ १७०० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ śabdeṃ jeṃ na labhe| teṃ ghaḍūniyāṃ anuṣṭabheṃ| strīśūdrādi pratibhe| sāmāvileṃ|| 1700 ||
verses.meaning: That which cannot be attained through mere words, was composed in the Anushtubh meter, and thus made accessible to the intellect of women, Shudras, and others.

verses.shloka_devanagari: स्वातीचेनि पाणियें।॥ न होती जरी मोतियें। तरी अंगीं सुंदरांचिये। का शोभतीं तियें ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: svātīceni pāṇiyeṃ||| na hotī jarī motiyeṃ| tarī aṃgīṃ suṃdarāṃciye| kā śobhatīṃ tiyeṃ || 9||
verses.meaning: If pearls were not formed by the waters of the Swati constellation, then how would they adorn the bodies of beautiful women?

verses.shloka_devanagari: नादु वाद्या न येतां। तरी कां गोचरु होता । फुलें न होतां घेपता । आमोदु केवीं॥ २॥
verses.shloka_iast: nādu vādyā na yetāṃ| tarī kāṃ gocaru hotā | phuleṃ na hotāṃ ghepatā | āmodu kevīṃ|| 2||
verses.meaning: If sound does not come from an instrument, how can it be perceived? If there are no flowers, how can fragrance be experienced?

verses.shloka_devanagari: गोडीं न होतीं पक्वान्ने, तरी कां फावती रसनें। दर्पणावीण नयनें। नयनु कां दिसे॥ ३॥
verses.shloka_iast: goḍīṃ na hotīṃ pakvānne, tarī kāṃ phāvatī rasaneṃ| darpaṇāvīṇa nayaneṃ| nayanu kāṃ dise|| 3||
verses.meaning: If there were no delicious dishes, how would the tongue taste them? Without a mirror, how would the eye see itself?

verses.shloka_devanagari: द्रष्टा श्रीगुरुमूर्ती। न रिगता दृश्यपंथीं। तरी कां ह्या उपास्ती। आकळता तो॥४॥
verses.shloka_iast: draṣṭā śrīgurumūrtī| na rigatā dṛśyapaṃthīṃ| tarī kāṃ hyā upāstī| ākaḻatā to||4||
verses.meaning: If the Seer, the form of the Guru, does not enter the path of the seen, then how can He be grasped through this devotion?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें वस्तु जें असंख्यात। तया संख्या शतें सात। न होती तरी कोणा येथ। फावों शकतें॥ ५॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ vastu jeṃ asaṃkhyāta| tayā saṃkhyā śateṃ sāta| na hotī tarī koṇā yetha| phāvoṃ śakateṃ|| 5||
verses.meaning: Just as the innumerable cannot be counted as seven hundred, so too, who can truly grasp it here?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मेघ सिंधूचें पाणी वाहे । तरी जग तयातेंचि पाहे। कां जें उमप तें नोहे। ठाकतें कोण्हा ॥ ६॥
verses.shloka_iast: megha siṃdhūceṃ pāṇī vāhe | tarī jaga tayāteṃci pāhe| kāṃ jeṃ umapa teṃ nohe| ṭhākateṃ koṇhā || 6||
verses.meaning: Just as the clouds carry the ocean's water, yet the world looks to them, for the ocean's vastness is immeasurable and cannot be contained by anyone.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि वाचा जें न पवे। तें हे श्‍लोक न होते बरवे । तरी कानें मुखें फावे। ऐसें कां होतें ॥ ७॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi vācā jeṃ na pave| teṃ he ś‍loka na hote barave | tarī kāneṃ mukheṃ phāve| aiseṃ kāṃ hoteṃ || 7||
verses.meaning: And that which words cannot reach, these verses would not have been beautiful. Then how could it be attained through ears and mouth?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि श्रीव्यासाचा हा थोरु । विश्वा जाळा उपकारु । जे श्रीकृष्णउक्ती आकारु । ग्रंथाचा केळला॥ ८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni śrīvyāsācā hā thoru | viśvā jāḻā upakāru | je śrīkṛṣṇauktī ākāru | graṃthācā keḻalā|| 8||
verses.meaning: Therefore, this great favor of Shri Vyasa has spread throughout the world, that he gave the form of a scripture to the words of Shri Krishna.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि तोचि हा मी आतां। श्रीव्यासाचीं पदें पाहतां पाहतां। आणिला श्रवणपथा । मऱ्हाठिया ॥ ९॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi toci hā mī ātāṃ| śrīvyāsācīṃ padeṃ pāhatāṃ pāhatāṃ| āṇilā śravaṇapathā | maṟhāṭhiyā || 9||
verses.meaning: And it is I, now, who, by contemplating the verses of Shri Vyasa, have brought them to the Marathi ear.

verses.shloka_devanagari: व्यासादिकांचे उन्मेख। राहाटती जेथ साशंक । तेथ मीही रंक येक। वाचाळी करीं ॥ १०॥
verses.shloka_iast: vyāsādikāṃce unmekha| rāhāṭatī jetha sāśaṃka | tetha mīhī raṃka yeka| vācāḻī karīṃ || 10||
verses.meaning: Where even great sages like Vyasa hesitate and are filled with doubt, there I, a humble and poor one, am attempting to speak.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी गीता ईश्वरु भोळा । ले व्यासोक्तिकुसुममाळा। तरी माझिया दूर्बादळा। ना न म्हणे कौं५८€११॥ आणि क्षीरसिंधूचिया तटा। पाणिया येती गजघटा। तेथ काय मुरकुटा। वारिजत असे॥ १२॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī gītā īśvaru bhoḻā | le vyāsoktikusumamāḻā| tarī mājhiyā dūrbādaḻā| nā na mhaṇe kauṃ58€11|| āṇi kṣīrasiṃdhūciyā taṭā| pāṇiyā yetī gajaghaṭā| tetha kāya murakuṭā| vārijata ase|| 12||
verses.meaning: The Gita is a garland of flowers, the words of Vyasa, offered to the simple God. Why would He refuse my humble offering of durva grass? When herds of elephants come to the shore of the ocean of milk to drink, does the ocean ever refuse a small fish?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पांख फुटे पांखिरूं। नुडे तरी नभींच स्थिरू । गगन आक्रमी सत्वरू। तो गरुडही तेथ॥ ९१३॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṃkha phuṭe pāṃkhirūṃ| nuḍe tarī nabhīṃca sthirū | gagana ākramī satvarū| to garuḍahī tetha|| 913||
verses.meaning: When a bird's wings sprout, it doesn't just stay still in the sky. It swiftly traverses the heavens, like an eagle there.

verses.shloka_devanagari: राजहंसाचें चालणें। भूतळीं जालिया शाहाणें। आणिकें काय कोणें । चालावेंचिना ॥ १४॥
verses.shloka_iast: rājahaṃsāceṃ cālaṇeṃ| bhūtaḻīṃ jāliyā śāhāṇeṃ| āṇikeṃ kāya koṇeṃ | cālāveṃcinā || 14||
verses.meaning: If the swan's gait is considered wise on earth, does it mean no one else should walk?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी आपुलेनि अवकाशें। अगाध जळ घेपे कलशें। चुळीं चूळपणा ऐसें। भरूनि न निघे॥ १५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī āpuleni avakāśeṃ| agādha jaḻa ghepe kalaśeṃ| cuḻīṃ cūḻapaṇā aiseṃ| bharūni na nighe|| 15||
verses.meaning: Just as a small pot can hold an immense amount of water within its own space, yet a mere handful cannot contain it, so too is the nature of the divine.

verses.shloka_devanagari: दिवटीच्या आंगीं थोरी । तरी ते बहु तेज धरी । वाती आपुलिया परी । आणीच कीं ना॥ १६॥
verses.shloka_iast: divaṭīcyā āṃgīṃ thorī | tarī te bahu teja dharī | vātī āpuliyā parī | āṇīca kīṃ nā|| 16||
verses.meaning: Just as a torch, by its very nature, holds great brilliance, so too does the wick, in its own way, bring forth light, does it not?

verses.shloka_devanagari: जी समुद्राचेनि पैसें । समुद्री आकाश आभासे । थिल्लरीं थिल्लराऐसें। बिंबेचि पैं॥ १७॥
verses.shloka_iast: jī samudrāceni paiseṃ | samudrī ākāśa ābhāse | thillarīṃ thillarāaiseṃ| biṃbeci paiṃ|| 17||
verses.meaning: Just as the sky appears in the ocean according to its vastness, so too does it reflect in a small puddle according to its size.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेवीं व्यासादिक महामती । वावरों येती इये ग्रंथी, मा आम्ही ठाकों हे युक्‍ती। न मिळे कीर॥ १८॥
verses.shloka_iast: tevīṃ vyāsādika mahāmatī | vāvaroṃ yetī iye graṃthī, mā āmhī ṭhākoṃ he yuk‍tī| na miḻe kīra|| 18||
verses.meaning: In the same way, great sages like Vyasa have delved into these scriptures, so how can we, with our limited intellect, comprehend this profound wisdom? It is indeed unattainable for us.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जिये सागरीं जळचरें। संचरती मंदराकारें। तेथ देखोनि शफरें येरें। पोहों न लाहती॥ १९॥
verses.shloka_iast: jiye sāgarīṃ jaḻacareṃ| saṃcaratī maṃdarākāreṃ| tetha dekhoni śaphareṃ yereṃ| pohoṃ na lāhatī|| 19||
verses.meaning: In that ocean where aquatic creatures move like Mount Mandara, seeing them, other small fish cannot swim.

verses.shloka_devanagari: अरुण आंगाजवळिके । म्हणौनि सूर्यातें देखे। मा भूतळींची न देखे । मुंगी काई ॥ १७२० ॥
verses.shloka_iast: aruṇa āṃgājavaḻike | mhaṇauni sūryāteṃ dekhe| mā bhūtaḻīṃcī na dekhe | muṃgī kāī || 1720 ||
verses.meaning: The sun is seen because of the proximity of Arun (the charioteer of the sun god). But does an ant on the ground not see it?

verses.shloka_devanagari: यालागीं आम्हां प्राकृतां। देशिकारें बंधें गीता। म्हणणें हें अनुचिता। कारण नोहे॥ २९॥
verses.shloka_iast: yālāgīṃ āmhāṃ prākṛtāṃ| deśikāreṃ baṃdheṃ gītā| mhaṇaṇeṃ heṃ anucitā| kāraṇa nohe|| 29||
verses.meaning: Therefore, for us ordinary people, to call the Gita a 'regional' or 'local' composition is not inappropriate.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि बापु पुढां जाये। ते घेत पाउलाची सोये। बाळ ये तरी न लाहे। पाबों कायी॥ २२॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi bāpu puḍhāṃ jāye| te gheta pāulācī soye| bāḻa ye tarī na lāhe| pāboṃ kāyī|| 22||
verses.meaning: And when the father walks ahead, the child follows in his footsteps. But if the child does not even try, how can he ever reach?

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा व्यासाचा मागोवा घेतु। भाष्यकारातें बाट पुसतु। अयोग्यही मी न पवतु। कें जाईन॥ २३॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā vyāsācā māgovā ghetu| bhāṣyakārāteṃ bāṭa pusatu| ayogyahī mī na pavatu| keṃ jāīna|| 23||
verses.meaning: Just as I follow in Vyasa's footsteps, seeking guidance from the commentators, how can I, being unworthy, ever attain that path?

verses.shloka_devanagari: आणि पृथ्वी जयाचिया क्षमा । नुबगे स्थावरजंगमा । जयाचेनि अमृतें चंद्रमा । निवबी जग॥ २४॥
verses.shloka_iast: āṇi pṛthvī jayāciyā kṣamā | nubage sthāvarajaṃgamā | jayāceni amṛteṃ caṃdramā | nivabī jaga|| 24||
verses.meaning: And the earth, whose forgiveness does not tire of the animate and inanimate, and by whose nectar the moon cools the world.

verses.shloka_devanagari: जयाचें आंगिक असिकें । तेज लाहोनि अर्के । आंधाराचें सावाइकें । लोटिजत आहे॥ २५॥
verses.shloka_iast: jayāceṃ āṃgika asikeṃ | teja lāhoni arke | āṃdhārāceṃ sāvāikeṃ | loṭijata āhe|| 25||
verses.meaning: From whose body, the sun, having received its radiance, is pushing away the darkness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: समुद्रा जयाचें तोय। तोया जयाचें माधुर्य। माधुर्या सौंदर्य। जयाचेनि॥ २६॥
verses.shloka_iast: samudrā jayāceṃ toya| toyā jayāceṃ mādhurya| mādhuryā sauṃdarya| jayāceni|| 26||
verses.meaning: The ocean's water, the water's sweetness, and the sweetness's beauty all belong to Him.

verses.shloka_devanagari: पवना जयाचें बळ। आकाश जेणें पघळ ज्ञान जेणें उज्ज्वळ। चक्रवर्ती ॥ २७॥
verses.shloka_iast: pavanā jayāceṃ baḻa| ākāśa jeṇeṃ paghaḻa jñāna jeṇeṃ ujjvaḻa| cakravartī || 27||
verses.meaning: The one whose strength is the wind, by whom the sky is expanded, by whom knowledge shines brightly, the sovereign emperor.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वेद जेणें सुभाष। सुख जेणें सोल्लास। हें असो रूपस। विश्‍व जेणें॥ २८॥
verses.shloka_iast: veda jeṇeṃ subhāṣa| sukha jeṇeṃ sollāsa| heṃ aso rūpasa| viś‍va jeṇeṃ|| 28||
verses.meaning: The Vedas are made beautiful by it, and happiness is made joyful by it. Let this be the beautiful form by which the universe exists.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो सर्वोपकारी समर्थ । सद्गुरु श्रीनिवृत्तिनाथु। राहाटत असे मजहीआंतु । रिघोनियां॥ २९ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: to sarvopakārī samartha | sadguru śrīnivṛttināthu| rāhāṭata ase majahīāṃtu | righoniyāṃ|| 29 ||
verses.meaning: That all-beneficent and capable Sadguru, Shri Nivruttinath, resides and operates within me.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां आयती गीता जगीं । मी सांगें मऱ्हाठिया भंगीं। येथ कें बिस्मयालागीं। ठावो आहे॥ १७३०॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ āyatī gītā jagīṃ | mī sāṃgeṃ maṟhāṭhiyā bhaṃgīṃ| yetha keṃ bismayālāgīṃ| ṭhāvo āhe|| 1730||
verses.meaning: Now, the Gita, which is readily available in the world, I will explain in Marathi. Where then is there room for wonder?

verses.shloka_devanagari: श्रीगुरूचेनि नांवें माती । डोंगरीं जयापासीं होती। तेणें कोळियें त्रिजगतीं। येकवद केळी॥ ३१॥
verses.shloka_iast: śrīgurūceni nāṃveṃ mātī | ḍoṃgarīṃ jayāpāsīṃ hotī| teṇeṃ koḻiyeṃ trijagatīṃ| yekavada keḻī|| 31||
verses.meaning: In the name of the Guru, the earth that was once scattered on the mountains, that very earth, through the Guru's grace, became unified in all three worlds.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चंदनें वेधलीं झाडें । जालीं चंदनाचेनि पाडें । वसिष्ठें मानिली कीं भांडें। भानूसीं शाटी॥ ३२॥
verses.shloka_iast: caṃdaneṃ vedhalīṃ jhāḍeṃ | jālīṃ caṃdanāceni pāḍeṃ | vasiṣṭheṃ mānilī kīṃ bhāṃḍeṃ| bhānūsīṃ śāṭī|| 32||
verses.meaning: Trees touched by sandalwood become sandalwood themselves. Similarly, did Vashistha ever consider the sun as a mere pot?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मा मी तंब चित्ताथिला। आणि श्रीगुरु ऐसा दादुला। जो दिठीवेनि आपुला। बैसवबी पदीं ॥ ३३॥
verses.shloka_iast: mā mī taṃba cittāthilā| āṇi śrīguru aisā dādulā| jo diṭhīveni āpulā| baisavabī padīṃ || 33||
verses.meaning: I am but a mere child, and the Guru is like a loving father who, with his mere glance, establishes me at his feet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधींचि देखणी दिठी। वरी सूर्य पुरवी पाठी । तैं न दिसे ऐसी गोठी । केंही आहे ॥ ३४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhīṃci dekhaṇī diṭhī| varī sūrya puravī pāṭhī | taiṃ na dise aisī goṭhī | keṃhī āhe || 34||
verses.meaning: When the eye is already endowed with sight, and the sun further illuminates its path, is there any object that remains unseen?

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि माझे नित्य नवे। इवासोच्छासही प्रबंध होआवे । श्रीगुरुकृपा काय नोहे। ज्ञानदेवो म्हणे ॥ ३५॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni mājhe nitya nave| ivāsocchāsahī prabaṃdha hoāve | śrīgurukṛpā kāya nohe| jñānadevo mhaṇe || 35||
verses.meaning: Therefore, my life is ever new, and even my breathing becomes a spiritual discourse. What is not possible through the grace of the Guru? So says Dnyandev.

verses.shloka_devanagari: याकारणें मियां। श्रीगीतार्थु मऱ्हाठिया। केला लोकां यया । दिठीचा विषो॥ ३६॥
verses.shloka_iast: yākāraṇeṃ miyāṃ| śrīgītārthu maṟhāṭhiyā| kelā lokāṃ yayā | diṭhīcā viṣo|| 36||
verses.meaning: For this reason, I have made the meaning of the Srimad Bhagavad Gita, in Marathi, an object of sight for these people.

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी मऱ्हाठे बोल रंगें। कवळितां पैं गीतांगें। तें गातयाचेनि पांगें। येकाढतां नोहे ॥ ३७॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī maṟhāṭhe bola raṃgeṃ| kavaḻitāṃ paiṃ gītāṃgeṃ| teṃ gātayāceni pāṃgeṃ| yekāḍhatāṃ nohe || 37||
verses.meaning: But when the Marathi language, with its vibrant expressions, embraces the limbs of the Gita, it does not become one with the singer's limited understanding.

verses.shloka_devanagari: म्हणौनि गीता गावों म्हणे । तैं गाणिबें होती लेणें। ना मोकळे तरी उणें। गीताही आणित ॥ ३८॥
verses.shloka_iast: mhaṇauni gītā gāvoṃ mhaṇe | taiṃ gāṇibeṃ hotī leṇeṃ| nā mokaḻe tarī uṇeṃ| gītāhī āṇita || 38||
verses.meaning: Therefore, when the Gita is sung, it becomes an adornment. Otherwise, if it is not sung, it is incomplete, even the Gita itself.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सुंदर आंगीं लेणें न सूये। तें तो मोकळा श्वृंगारु होये। ना लेइलें तरी आहे। ५०६ श्रीज्ञानेश्वरी तैसें के उचित ॥ ३९॥
verses.shloka_iast: suṃdara āṃgīṃ leṇeṃ na sūye| teṃ to mokaḻā śvṛṃgāru hoye| nā leileṃ tarī āhe| 506 śrījñāneśvarī taiseṃ ke ucita || 39||
verses.meaning: Just as ornaments do not suit a beautiful body, for its natural beauty is its adornment, and even without them, it remains beautiful; similarly, what is truly appropriate?

verses.shloka_devanagari: कां मोतियांची जैसी जाती । सोनयाही मान देती। नातरी मानवती। अंगेंचि सडीं ॥ १७४०॥
verses.shloka_iast: kāṃ motiyāṃcī jaisī jātī | sonayāhī māna detī| nātarī mānavatī| aṃgeṃci saḍīṃ || 1740||
verses.meaning: Just as pearls, by their very nature, lend value to gold, or rather, they are inherently esteemed for their own being.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना ना गुंफिलीं कां मोकळीं। उणीं न होती परिमळीं। वबसंतागमींचीं वाटोळीं। मोगरीं जैसीं ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā nā guṃphilīṃ kāṃ mokaḻīṃ| uṇīṃ na hotī parimaḻīṃ| vabasaṃtāgamīṃcīṃ vāṭoḻīṃ| mogarīṃ jaisīṃ || 49||
verses.meaning: Whether strung together or left loose, they do not diminish in fragrance, just like the jasmine buds that appear in spring.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसा गाणिवेतें मिरवी । गीतेवीणही रंगु दावी। तो लाभाचा प्रबंधु ओंबीं। केला मियां॥ ४२॥
verses.shloka_iast: taisā gāṇiveteṃ miravī | gītevīṇahī raṃgu dāvī| to lābhācā prabaṃdhu oṃbīṃ| kelā miyāṃ|| 42||
verses.meaning: Just as a skilled musician, even without a song, can create a delightful atmosphere, so too have I composed this work, which is a source of great spiritual gain.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें आबालसुबोधें। ओवीयेचेनि प्रबंधें। ब्रह्मरससुस्वादें । अक्षरें गुंथिली ॥ ४३॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ ābālasubodheṃ| ovīyeceni prabaṃdheṃ| brahmarasasusvādeṃ | akṣareṃ guṃthilī || 43||
verses.meaning: With that, for the easy understanding of all, through the composition of this Ovi, letters were strung together, imbued with the sweet taste of Brahman's essence.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आतां चंदनाच्या तरुवरीं । परिमळालागीं फुलवरी । 'पारुखणें जियापरी । लागेना कीं ॥ ४४॥
verses.shloka_iast: ātāṃ caṃdanācyā taruvarīṃ | parimaḻālāgīṃ phulavarī | 'pārukhaṇeṃ jiyāparī | lāgenā kīṃ || 44||
verses.meaning: Just as one does not need to search for fragrance in a sandalwood tree, for it is inherent, so too is the divine essence within.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेसा प्रबंधु हा श्रवणीं । लागतखेंवो समाधि आणी । ऐकिलियाही वाखाणी । काय व्यसन न लवी ॥ ४५॥
verses.shloka_iast: tesā prabaṃdhu hā śravaṇīṃ | lāgatakheṃvo samādhi āṇī | aikiliyāhī vākhāṇī | kāya vyasana na lavī || 45||
verses.meaning: Such is the profound discourse that upon hearing it, one immediately attains a state of deep meditation. Even after hearing it, one continues to contemplate and praise it. What addiction could be more compelling than this?

verses.shloka_devanagari: पाठ करितां व्याजें। पांडित्यें येती वेषजे। तें अमृतातें नेणिजे । फावलिया ॥ ४६॥
verses.shloka_iast: pāṭha karitāṃ vyājeṃ| pāṃḍityeṃ yetī veṣaje| teṃ amṛtāteṃ neṇije | phāvaliyā || 46||
verses.meaning: Even if one recites scriptures with the intention of showing off their scholarship, they will not understand the true essence of the nectar of immortality, even if it is readily available.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसेंनि आइतेपणें । कवित्व जालें हें उपेणें । मनन निदिध्यास श्रवणें । जिंतिलें आतां॥ ४७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃni āitepaṇeṃ | kavitva jāleṃ heṃ upeṇeṃ | manana nididhyāsa śravaṇeṃ | jiṃtileṃ ātāṃ|| 47||
verses.meaning: Thus, through this effortless poetic expression, the practices of contemplation, deep meditation, and listening have now been conquered (or mastered).

verses.shloka_devanagari: हे स्वानंदभोगाची सेळ। भलतयासीचि देईल। सर्वेद्रियां 'पोषवील। श्रवणाकरवीं ॥ ४८॥
verses.shloka_iast: he svānaṃdabhogācī seḻa| bhalatayāsīci deīla| sarvedriyāṃ 'poṣavīla| śravaṇākaravīṃ || 48||
verses.meaning: This joy of self-realization will be given to anyone. It will nourish all senses through the ears.

verses.shloka_devanagari: चंद्रातें आंगवणें । भोगूनि चकोर शाहाणे । परी फावे जैसें चांदिणें। भलतयाही ॥ ४९॥
verses.shloka_iast: caṃdrāteṃ āṃgavaṇeṃ | bhogūni cakora śāhāṇe | parī phāve jaiseṃ cāṃdiṇeṃ| bhalatayāhī || 49||
verses.meaning: Just as the moon is the natural sustenance for the wise chakora bird, so too is moonlight available to all, regardless of their wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तैसें अध्यात्मशास्त्रीं यिये। अंतरंगचि अधिकारिये। परी लोकु वाक॒चातुर्ये । होईल सुखिया ॥ ५०॥
verses.shloka_iast: taiseṃ adhyātmaśāstrīṃ yiye| aṃtaraṃgaci adhikāriye| parī loku vāka̱cāturye | hoīla sukhiyā || 50||
verses.meaning: In the spiritual scriptures, the inner self is indeed the true authority. But people, through their clever words, will find happiness.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ऐसें श्रीनिवृत्तिनाथाचें। गौरव आहे जी साचें। ग्रंथु नोहे हें कृपेचें। वैभव तये ॥ ५१॥
verses.shloka_iast: aiseṃ śrīnivṛttināthāceṃ| gaurava āhe jī sāceṃ| graṃthu nohe heṃ kṛpeceṃ| vaibhava taye || 51||
verses.meaning: Such is truly the glory of Shri Nivruttinath. This is not merely a text, but the very opulence of his grace.

verses.shloka_devanagari: क्षीरसिंधुपरिसरीं । शक्तीच्या कर्णकुहरीं । नेणों कै श्रीत्रिपुरारीं । सांगितलें जें॥ ५२॥
verses.shloka_iast: kṣīrasiṃdhuparisarīṃ | śaktīcyā karṇakuharīṃ | neṇoṃ kai śrītripurārīṃ | sāṃgitaleṃ jeṃ|| 52||
verses.meaning: Perhaps, in the vicinity of the ocean of milk, into the ears of Shakti, Lord Tripurari revealed that which is unknown.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तें क्षीरकल्लोळाआंतु। मकरोदरीं गुप्तु| होता तयाचा हातु । पैठें जालें॥ ५३॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṃ kṣīrakalloḻāāṃtu| makarodarīṃ guptu| hotā tayācā hātu | paiṭheṃ jāleṃ|| 53||
verses.meaning: Just as a hand, though hidden within the belly of a crocodile, can enter the churning milk ocean, so too can the divine reach into the most concealed places.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो मत्स्येंद्र सप्तशृंगी । भग्नावयवा चौरंगी । भेटला कीं तो सर्वांगी । संपूर्ण जाळा॥ ५४॥
verses.shloka_iast: to matsyeṃdra saptaśṛṃgī | bhagnāvayavā cauraṃgī | bheṭalā kīṃ to sarvāṃgī | saṃpūrṇa jāḻā|| 54||
verses.meaning: Did Matsyendra, with his broken limbs, meet Chaurangi on the Saptashringi mountain, or was it that Chaurangi became whole and complete?

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग समाधि अव्युत्थया। भोगावी वासना यया । ते मुद्रा श्रीगोरक्षराया । दिधली मीनीं ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga samādhi avyutthayā| bhogāvī vāsanā yayā | te mudrā śrīgorakṣarāyā | didhalī mīnīṃ || 55 ||
verses.meaning: Then, to him who desired to experience the state of unmanifested samadhi, Shri Gorakshanath bestowed the Mudra to Meenanath.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें योगाब्जिनीसरोबरु । विषयविध्वंसैकवीरु । तियें पदीं कां सर्वेश्वर । अभिषेकिला ॥ ५६॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ yogābjinīsarobaru | viṣayavidhvaṃsaikavīru | tiyeṃ padīṃ kāṃ sarveśvara | abhiṣekilā || 56||
verses.meaning: With that, the one who is the sole hero in destroying worldly desires, the one who is like the sun for the lotus of Yoga, was consecrated as the Lord of all in those very feet.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग तिहीं तें शांभव । अट्ठयानंदवैभव । संपादिलें सप्रभव । श्रीगहिनीनाथा ॥ ५७॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga tihīṃ teṃ śāṃbhava | aṭṭhayānaṃdavaibhava | saṃpādileṃ saprabhava | śrīgahinīnāthā || 57||
verses.meaning: Then, through them, the glorious and blissful state of Shiva, the very source of all creation, was attained by Shri Gahininath.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेणें कळिकळितु भूतां। आला देखोनि निरुता। ते आज्ञा श्रीनिवृत्तिनाथा । दिधली ऐसी ॥ ५८॥
verses.shloka_iast: teṇeṃ kaḻikaḻitu bhūtāṃ| ālā dekhoni nirutā| te ājñā śrīnivṛttināthā | didhalī aisī || 58||
verses.meaning: Seeing the intense suffering of beings, Shri Nivruttinath gave this command.

verses.shloka_devanagari: ना आदिगुरु शंकरा-। लागोनि शिष्यपरंपरा। बोधाचा हा संसरा। जाला जो आमुतें॥५९॥
verses.shloka_iast: nā ādiguru śaṃkarā-| lāgoni śiṣyaparaṃparā| bodhācā hā saṃsarā| jālā jo āmuteṃ||59||
verses.meaning: From the primordial Guru Shankara, through the lineage of disciples, this world of spiritual knowledge has come down to us.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तो हा तूं घेऊनि आघवा। कळीं गिळितयां जिवां । सर्व प्रकारीं धांवा । करीं पां वेगीं ॥ १९७६०॥
verses.shloka_iast: to hā tūṃ gheūni āghavā| kaḻīṃ giḻitayāṃ jivāṃ | sarva prakārīṃ dhāṃvā | karīṃ pāṃ vegīṃ || 19760||
verses.meaning: Therefore, you should quickly take all these souls, who are being swallowed by the Kali Yuga, and rush to their aid in every possible way.

verses.shloka_devanagari: आधींच तंव तो कृपाळु । वरी गुरुआज्ञेचा बोलु। जाला जैसा वर्षाकाळु। खवळणें मेघां॥ ६१॥
verses.shloka_iast: ādhīṃca taṃva to kṛpāḻu | varī guruājñecā bolu| jālā jaisā varṣākāḻu| khavaḻaṇeṃ meghāṃ|| 61||
verses.meaning: He was already compassionate, and then the command of the Guru came upon him, like the stirring of clouds at the onset of the rainy season.

verses.shloka_devanagari: मग आर्ताचेनि वोरसें। गीतार्थग्रंथनमिसें । वर्षला शांतरसें। तो हा ग्रंथु॥६२॥
verses.shloka_iast: maga ārtāceni voraseṃ| gītārthagraṃthanamiseṃ | varṣalā śāṃtaraseṃ| to hā graṃthu||62||
verses.meaning: Thus, this scripture, born from the yearning of the distressed, under the guise of expounding the Gita's meaning, pours forth the essence of tranquility.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तेथ पुढां मी बापिया। मांडला आर्ती आपुलिया । कीं यासाठीं येवढिया । आणिलों यशा ॥ ६३॥
verses.shloka_iast: tetha puḍhāṃ mī bāpiyā| māṃḍalā ārtī āpuliyā | kīṃ yāsāṭhīṃ yevaḍhiyā | āṇiloṃ yaśā || 63||
verses.meaning: Then, I, a humble child, presented my heartfelt longing, for this very purpose, to achieve such great success.

verses.shloka_devanagari: एवं गुरुक्रमें लाधलें। समाधिधन जें आपुलें। तें ग्रंथें बोधौनि दिधलें। गोसावी मज ॥ ६४॥
verses.shloka_iast: evaṃ gurukrameṃ lādhaleṃ| samādhidhana jeṃ āpuleṃ| teṃ graṃtheṃ bodhauni didhaleṃ| gosāvī maja || 64||
verses.meaning: Thus, the wealth of samadhi, which is inherently mine, was bestowed upon me by my Guru through this scripture, by imparting its wisdom.

verses.shloka_devanagari: वांचूनि पढे ना वाची। ना सेवाही जाणें स्वामीची । ऐशिया मज ग्रंथाची। योग्यता कें असे॥ ६५॥
verses.shloka_iast: vāṃcūni paḍhe nā vācī| nā sevāhī jāṇeṃ svāmīcī | aiśiyā maja graṃthācī| yogyatā keṃ ase|| 65||
verses.meaning: I neither read nor recite, nor do I know how to serve my Master. How then can I be worthy of this scripture?

verses.shloka_devanagari: परी साचचि गुरुनाथें। निमित्त करूनि मातें। प्रबंधव्याजें जगातें। रक्षिले जाणा॥ ६६॥
verses.shloka_iast: parī sācaci gurunātheṃ| nimitta karūni māteṃ| prabaṃdhavyājeṃ jagāteṃ| rakṣile jāṇā|| 66||
verses.meaning: But truly, the Guru, using me as an instrument, has, through the pretext of this composition, protected the world, know this.

verses.shloka_devanagari: तऱही पुरोहितगुणें। मी बोललों पुरें उणें । तें तुम्हीं माउलीपणें ।॥ उपसाहिजो जी ॥ ६७॥
verses.shloka_iast: taṟahī purohitaguṇeṃ| mī bolaloṃ pureṃ uṇeṃ | teṃ tumhīṃ māulīpaṇeṃ ||| upasāhijo jī || 67||
verses.meaning: Therefore, due to the qualities of a priest, whatever I have spoken, whether complete or incomplete, please bear with it, O Mother, with your motherly compassion.

verses.shloka_devanagari: शब्द कैसा घडिजे । प्रमेयीं कैसें पां चढिजे। अळंकारु म्हणिजे। काय तें नेणें ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.shloka_iast: śabda kaisā ghaḍije | prameyīṃ kaiseṃ pāṃ caḍhije| aḻaṃkāru mhaṇije| kāya teṃ neṇeṃ || 68 ||
verses.meaning: How is a word formed? How does it gain prominence in a proposition? What is an embellishment? I know none of these.

verses.shloka_devanagari: सायिखडेयाचें बाहुलें। चालवित्या सूत्राचेनि चाले। तैसा मातें दाबीत बोले। स्वामी तो माझा ॥ ६९ ॥
